disease_resistance.summary: No ADVIKA-specific disease resistance data found. A testbook page claims pest and disease resistance but cites no source and is not considered reliable. Generic chickpea Ascochyta blight QTL work was found but is not specific to ADVIKA, so it is not evidence of resistance in this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: No ADVIKA-specific pest resistance data found. The record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'. The testbook claim of pest resistance is unsourced and unreliable.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield recorded as 1366 kg/ha in the variety record. The searched sources did not verify this figure; no yield-per-hectare evidence was found. Only the approximately 7% drought-yield gain over JG 16 is reported in the sources.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment or multi-location stability results were returned.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Record and adaptation ecology list Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Southern Rajasthan and Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh. Record describes it as most suitable for drought-prone environments of the Central Zone. Sowing time is the first fortnight of October and seed rate is 65-70 kg/ha. The DBT statement of national use, especially in the Central Zone, is broader than the three-state recommended list.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-erect (agronomic features in the variety record). Morphological characteristics: Not specified. Seed size and plant height: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No multi-location trial results found. No maturity, yield-per-hectare, seed size or plant height trial data found in the searches. The only trial-related result is the approximately 7% higher yield under drought stress relative to the JG 16 background, as reported by NIPGR and DBT.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. No ADVIKA-specific SSR, SNP or marker data were returned.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No ADVIKA-specific QTL study found. Background QTL work on the 100-seed weight locus in desi chickpea (with NIPGR co-authors) is generic and not specific to ADVIKA. The parentage recorded as (JG 16/ICC 14649)-BC4F1 was not confirmed by any search result, although the reported introgression method into JG 16 is consistent with it.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Developed by introgressing an ABC transporter gene into the JG 16 genetic background. The gene is reported to increase seed weight. No further gene identification or pathway detail was found.

ADVIKA (NC 7) chickpea: evidence digest

Name check: the variety_name and seednet_variety_name ("ADVIKA  (NC 7)", with a double space) refer to the same variety. Search results used "ADVIKA (NC 7)". No Seednet portal page was returned, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described by NIPGR and DBT as a drought-tolerant, climate-smart desi chickpea variety; yield about 7% higher under drought stress than its JG 16 background. -- https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1991615
- Same claims repeated in the BRIC article on the variety. -- https://www.internationaljournalofresearch.org/2023/12/biotechnology-research-and-innovation.html
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No ADVIKA-specific disease or pest resistance data found. The testbook page claims pest and disease resistance but gives no source and is not reliable. -- https://testbook.com/question-answer/consider-the-following-pairs-1-advika-chickp--698c525c76596fcb61f86147
- Generic chickpea disease QTL work (Ascochyta blight) is not specific to ADVIKA. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389798813_Exploring_QTL_genes_contribute_to_chickpea_ascochyta_blight_resistance_across_multiple_environments_using_SSR_DArT_and_SNP_assays

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity, yield per hectare, seed size and plant height for ADVIKA: No evidence found in the searches. Only the 7% drought-yield gain above is reported.
- Multi-location trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Developed by introgressing an ABC transporter gene into the JG 16 genetic background; the gene is reported to increase seed weight. -- https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1991615
- The parentage "(JG 16/ICC 14649)-BC4F1" from the record was not confirmed by any search result. The reported method (introgression into JG 16) is consistent with it but does not verify it.
- No ADVIKA-specific QTL or marker study found. Background QTL work on the 100-seed weight locus in desi chickpea (NIPGR co-authored) is generic, not ADVIKA-specific. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4463844/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: National Institute of Plant Genome Research (NIPGR), under the Department of Biotechnology, Ministry of Science and Technology. -- https://x.com/DrJitendraSingh/status/1729845722177061263
- Release was announced at NIPGR's Silver Jubilee event. -- https://krishijagran.com/news/dr-jitendra-singh-unveils-advika-a-superior-drought-tolerant-climate-smart-chickpea-variety/
- Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found. The NIPGR affiliation of the QTL-seq study's authors is generic and not ADVIKA-specific.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or personal contact found.
- Institute-level: NIPGR, New Delhi (postal address given only as "New Delhi 110067" in a 2015 paper's affiliation; not verified as current). -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4463844/
- Official NIPGR email, phone and contact page URL: No evidence found in the searches. The institute's own website was not returned.

PUBLICATIONS
- Anonymous (2023). Year End Review of Department of Biotechnology (PIB press release, describes ADVIKA development and CVRC approval). PIB -- https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1991615
- Anonymous (2023). Biotechnology Research and Innovation Council (BRIC) article describing ADVIKA. International Journal of Research -- https://www.internationaljournalofresearch.org/2023/12/biotechnology-research-and-innovation.html
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper specific to ADVIKA found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found: no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listing for ADVIKA was returned. Only unrelated seed retailers appeared in the results.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Recommended for sale in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh; an open-pollinated chickpea variety. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/chickpea-variety-advika-nc-7/
- Same state list in the Madhya Pradesh release roundup. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-23-new-varieties-of-13-crops-for-madhya-pradesh-farmers/
- Release date conflict: the notification is reported as 25 September 2023, but the record gives 2023-05-02. The record's date is not supported by these sources and should be checked against the gazette.
- Central-zone wording conflict: DBT says it is approved for national use, especially in the Central Zone, which is broader than the three-state list above. -- https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1991615

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to BDNGK 798. The DPD listing gives only 'Irrigated' as the agronomic feature, which describes the growing condition rather than tolerance. Conflicting Mahabeej record (VNMKV Parbhani, 2013) is not used for this field.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to BDNGK 798.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt and stunt: listed as moderately resistant in two sources (global-agriculture.com and the DPD chickpea varieties table). Fusarium wilt: a greenhouse pot culture study (rabi 2024, Legume Research) and a Trichoderma seed and soil treatment study (ResearchGate) used BDNGK-798 with pathogen inoculation and measured wilt incidence at 65 days after sowing. These studies test biocontrol, not inherent resistance, and the digest reports no numerical wilt-incidence results. Source material for the 2024 study was sourced from Agricultural Research Station, Badnapur, Maharashtra. No other disease resistance evidence found.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The Pest Reaction field in the input is 'Not Specified' and no pest resistance evidence appeared in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: 16-18 q/ha yield potential (global-agriculture.com; DPD table; Mahabeej listing also gives 16-18). Under irrigated growing condition.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data retrieved.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated condition, Maharashtra (DPD table). Agronomic feature in input: spacing 45 x 15 cm, RDF 25:50:0 NPK ha-1 is suitable. Digest does not give explicit agro-climatic zone data.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 120-135 days (global-agriculture.com; DPD table). Conflicting record: Mahabeej listing gives 75 days maturity and 110-115 days duration; this conflicts with the SVRC/DPD record and is not used as the primary value.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Kabuli type with white grain of about 29 g/100 seed (global-agriculture.com; DPD table). Other morphological characteristics: Not specified.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Seed priming field trial, rabi 2022-23, experimental farm of the AICRP on safflower, VNMKV, Parbhani, evaluating seed priming effects on growth, seed yield and yield attributing characters. The digest reports the design only; no numerical results were retrieved. (2) Line x Tester combining ability trial, 2016-17, Pulses Research Unit Dr. PDKV, Akola, with BDNGK-798, Phule G-12310, Shubhra, Phule G-0739 and MNK-1; significant GCA for primary branches, pods per plant and seeds per pod in the male BDNGK-798; no numerical values retrieved. (3) Heterosis crosses (PKV Kabuli-2 x BDNGK-798; Chanoli x BDNGK-798) reported in tabular data only, no values in digest. (4) Greenhouse Trichoderma biocontrol pot culture, rabi 2024, against Fusarium wilt (not a field trial); no numerical results in digest. (5) AICRP Chickpea Annual Report 2021-22 lists BDNGK 798 among released varieties with no trial data retrieved.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Start codon targeted (SCoT) marker profiling: BDNGK 798 is lane 4 in a profiling figure, alongside Chanoli, Kabuli-4, Virat and WR 315. No marker positions, band sizes or polymorphism data were retrieved. No SNP or SSR evidence found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. Combining ability analysis (Line x Tester, Pulses Research Unit, Akola, 2016-17) reports a significant GCA effect for the male BDNGK-798 for primary branches, number of pods per plant and seeds per pod. These are general combining ability effects, not mapped QTLs. Heterosis crosses involving BDNGK-798 (PKV Kabuli-2 x BDNGK-798 and Chanoli x BDNGK-798) appear in tabular data only; no narrative or effect values were retrieved.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. Parentage (BGD 2048 x ICC 118) is unverified: no evidence found in any retrieved page.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: BDNGK 798 (chickpea)

Name check: "variety_name" and "seednet_variety_name" are both "BDNGK 798" in the input, so every heading below refers to that single name. No Seednet portal page was retrieved; the evidence comes from the sources listed. Spelling variants (BDNGK-798, BDNG 798) appear in the sources and are treated as the same variety only where the page context supports it.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Listed as moderately resistant to wilt and stunt, with an irrigated growing condition and 16-18 q/ha yield potential. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-bdngk-798/
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to BDNGK 798. The DPD listing gives only "Irrigated" as the agronomic feature. -- http://dpd.gov.in/Varieties/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderately resistant to wilt and stunt. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-bdngk-798/
Moderately resistant (DPD table row for BDNGK 798) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Greenhouse Trichoderma biocontrol work on BDNGK-798 against Fusarium wilt: a pot culture experiment was carried out under greenhouse conditions during the rabi season of 2024 using chickpea cultivar BDNGK-798 (sourced from Agricultural Research Station, Badnapur, Maharashtra). This tests biocontrol, not inherent resistance. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5579
Trichoderma seed and soil treatment study on BDNGK-798 with pathogen inoculation, measuring wilt incidence at 65 days after sowing. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361032295_Exploring_potential_of_Trichoderma_spp_against_Fusarium_oxysporum_fsp_ciceris_and_their_growth_promotion_activity

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Release and origin: Year of release 2016 (SVRC), originating centre ARS, Jalna, yield 16-18 q/ha, 120-135 days to maturity, kabuli type with white grain of about 29 g/100 seed. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-bdngk-798/
Maturity and grain (DPD table): BDNGK 798, 2016, ARS, Badnapur, Jalna (MH), 16-18 q/ha, 120-135 days, Maharashtra, irrigated, kabuli type with white colour grain (29 g/100 seed), moderately resistant. Note: this source says ARS Badnapur; the other says ARS Jalna. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Conflicting record: the Mahabeej listing gives BDNGK-798 as released from VNMKV Parbhani in 2013, with 75 days maturity, 110-115 days duration and 16-18 yield. This conflicts with the SVRC 2016 record and is not used for the release fields. -- https://www.mahabeej.co.in/cereals?id=20
Seed priming field trial, Rabi 2022-23: A field experiment was conducted at the experimental farm of the AICRP on safflower, VNMKV, Parbhani during Rabi 2022-23 using chickpea cv BDNGK-798 to evaluate seed priming on growth, seed yield and yield attributing characters. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/SR/article/view/163015

GENETICS AND QTL
Combining ability (Line x Tester, Pulses Research Unit, Akola, 2016-17): BDNGK-798, Phule G-12310, Shubhra, Phule G-0739 and MNK-1 were planted during 2016-17 at Pulses Research Unit Dr. PDKV, Akola, and crossing was performed in Line x Tester. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361809930_Combining_ability_analysis_for_seed_yield_and_other_yield_contributing_trait_in_kabuli_chickpea_Cicer_areitinum_L
Significant GCA: the male BDNGK-798 possesses significant GCA effect for primary branches, number of pods per plant and seeds per pod. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361809930_Combining_ability_analysis_for_seed_yield_and_other_yield_contributing_trait_in_kabuli_chickpea_Cicer_areitinum_L
Heterosis crosses involving BDNGK-798 (tabular data only, no narrative text retrieved): PKV Kabuli-2 x BDNGK-798 and Chanoli x BDNGK-798. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356377852_Heterosis_for_seed_yield_and_yield_contributing_characters_of_Kabuli_x_Kabuli_crosses_of_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L
Marker profiling: Start codon targeted (SCoT) marker profiling in chickpea genotypes, lane 4 = BDNGK 798, with Chanoli, Kabuli-4, Virat and WR 315. -- https://agetds.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/4-Bhavana-Surduse.pdf
Parentage (BGD 2048 x ICC 118): No evidence found in any retrieved page. The parentage in the input is unverified.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Breeder or lead scientist name: No evidence found.
Developing institution: Originating centre ARS, Jalna; DPD lists ARS Badnapur, Jalna (MH). -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Station used for source material: sourced from Agricultural Research Station, Badnapur, Maharashtra. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5579
Institution on Mahabeej listing: VNMKV, Parbhani (conflicting; see AGRONOMY AND TRIALS). -- https://www.mahabeej.co.in/cereals?id=20

Institute contact page for ARS Badnapur/Jalna: No evidence found in retrieved results. No institute contact URL was returned.

official_quote.quote: Tolerant to wilt

disease_resistance.research_summary: Wilt and stunt: listed as moderately resistant in two sources (global-agriculture.com and the DPD chickpea varieties table). Fusarium wilt: a greenhouse pot culture study (rabi 2024, Legume Research) and a Trichoderma seed and soil treatment study (ResearchGate) used BDNGK-798 with pathogen inoculation and measured wilt incidence at 65 days after sowing. These studies test biocontrol, not inherent resistance, and the digest reports no numerical wilt-incidence results. Source material for the 2024 study was sourced from Agricultural Research Station, Badnapur, Maharashtra. No other disease resistance evidence found.

drought.details: BGD-103 is moderately resistant to drought. It has been studied for water use and tolerance to heat and drought, and was included in trials in environments experiencing drought stress. Research has also focused on its drought tolerance at seed, seedling, and whole plant levels.

heat.details: The variety BGD-103 shows tolerance to heat and has been studied for performance under terminal heat stress. It was grown in environments that coincided with high terminal heat stress.

salinity.details: While BGD-103 is listed as an abiotic stress-tolerant variety, no specific evidence or details regarding its salinity tolerance are provided in the search results.

flood.details: BGD-103 was part of studies in environments experiencing flash floods, but no specific tolerance level or mechanisms for flood tolerance are stated.

disease_resistance.summary: BGD-103 is resistant to Fusarium Wilt and moderately resistant against soil borne diseases. It has been evaluated as a promising entry in studies related to chickpea wilt complex.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance details are specified for BGD-103.

agronomic_details.stability: BGD-103 has been sown and studied across four different growing environments, including those experiencing heat and drought stress, indicating evaluation for yield stability; however, specific stability results are not provided.
agronomic_details.adaptation: This variety is suitable for rainfed conditions, particularly demonstrating higher grain yield in rainfed black soils.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-spreading habit, broader leaflets, attractive bold seed size, and white extra large seeds.
agronomic_details.field_trials: BGD-103 was included in the All India Coordinated Research Project on Agrometeorology (AICRPAM) trials, sown in four distinct growing environments to study water use and tolerance to heat and drought. A study on rainfed black soils reported a significantly higher grain yield of 14.28 q/ha. It was also identified as a promising entry in studies concerning chickpea wilt complex and dry root rot. Specific trials were conducted at the College of Agriculture, Vijayapur, during Rabi 2018.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to wilt disease, per the DPD central/state release table (listed as a 2015 SVRC release, Jharkhand, normal sown condition). The same salient-features text describes the variety as resistant to wilt. The digest notes that this attribution rests only on these table entries, and no field screening data was found. Lodging and shattering resistance are agronomic traits, not disease resistance, and are reported under agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerant of gram pod borer (Helicoverpa), per the salient-features entry on Global Agriculture. No other pest reaction data was found. The CSC record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'. The digest does not state whether this is resistance or tolerance beyond the wording 'tolerant'.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 18.00 to 20.00 Kg/Ha. The SVRC table, as summarised in the digest, gives 18-20 q/ha. These units conflict and should be checked against the primary source. Performance stability trial in Jharkhand: 1461 kg/ha for Birsa Chana 3 versus 1303 kg/ha for check KWR108.
agronomic_details.stability: Judged stable with wide adaptability in the Jharkhand performance stability trial (ResearchGate source).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Jharkhand, normal sown condition (CSC record; SVRC table).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Resistant to lodging and shattering; suitable for normal sown condition; seed rate 65-70 Kg/ha (CSC record agronomic features). Morphological characteristics: Not specified. The trial source gives maturity of 120 days, which differs from the 115-118 day range.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Performance stability trial in Jharkhand (ResearchGate source): Birsa Chana 3 gave the highest grain yield at 1461 kg/ha against check KWR108 at 1303 kg/ha, a 12% advantage. It was judged stable with wide adaptability. Recorded maturity was 120 days. The trial table lists pedigree as ICCV2 / Bhawani Patna local and the institute as BAU, Ranchi. The same source lists release year as 2013, which conflicts with the 2015 SVRC year in the DPD and trade sources and the 2014 CSC year. The ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea 2021-22 report lists 'Birsa Chana 3', but the retrieved text gives no agronomic data for it.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Birsa Chana-3 (Desi), chickpea

Name note: Every finding below refers to "Birsa Chana 3" (CSC-style name, no hyphen). No search result used the Seednet form "Birsa Chana - 3 (Desi)", so no evidence was found under that name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Described as resistant to lodging and shattering and as tolerant of wilt disease (listed as 2015 SVRC release, Jharkhand, normal sown condition) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
Same salient-features text (resistant to lodging, shattering, wilt; tolerant to gram pod borer) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-birsa-chana-3/
No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found for this variety -- searched under topic 1 and 3 results; none named it.

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to wilt disease (dpd central/state release table) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Tolerant of gram pod borer (Helicoverpa) per the same salient-features entry -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-birsa-chana-3/
Wilt-resistance attribution for this variety is limited to these table entries; no field screening data found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Yield 18-20 q/ha; 115-118 days to maturity; normal sown condition (SVRC table) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
Same yield, maturity and area data -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-birsa-chana-3/
Performance stability trial in Jharkhand: Birsa Chana 3 gave the highest grain yield (1461 kg/ha) against check KWR108 (1303 kg/ha), a 12% advantage, and was judged stable with wide adaptability; 120 days maturity, pedigree ICCV2 / Bhawani Patna local, BAU Ranchi -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327931315_Performance_stability_of_promising_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_cultivars_in_Jharkhand
Listed in the ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea 2021-22 report as "Birsa Chana 3", but the retrieved text gives no agronomic data for it -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Searched under topic 3; the only marker-related hits (Pusa Chickpea 20211 and Fusarium-pyramiding work at PMC9388742) concern other varieties and were discarded. Parentage recorded in the input (ICCV-2 / Bhawanipatna) is supported only by the ResearchGate trial table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327931315_Performance_stability_of_promising_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_cultivars_in_Jharkhand

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Originating centre given as BAO (Birsa Agricultural University), Jharkhand -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
Trial table lists the institute as BAU, Ranchi -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327931315_Performance_stability_of_promising_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_cultivars_in_Jharkhand
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The Krishi Jagran SVRC article mentions unnamed "breeders of the variety" but covers four BAU varieties collectively and does not name Birsa Chana 3, so no name is attributed -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/16-all-new-high-yielding-varieties-of-crops-developed-by-this-agri-research-institution/
Institution background: Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi, established 1981 -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birsa_Agricultural_University

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level only (no breeder contact found): Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi, Jharkhand; website www.bauranchi.org -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birsa_Agricultural_University
Official email, phone and postal address for the BAU Department of Plant Breeding or the chickpea programme: No evidence found.
Director of Research named in a news item (A. Wadood) is not tied to this variety and is not listed as a contact -- https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/birsa-agricultural-university

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Performance stability of promising chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) cultivars in Jharkhand. ResearchGate PDF (genotype table includes Birsa Chana 3, release 2013, BAU Ranchi) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327931315_Performance_stability_of_promising_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_cultivars_in_Jharkhand
Note: this paper lists release year 2013, which conflicts with the 2015 SVRC year in the DPD and trade sources.
ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea Progress Report 2021-22 (lists Birsa Chana 3 in a variety table; no details retrieved) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
No KrishiKosh theses, journal papers or conference papers specific to this variety were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY

Results were generic desi chana retail and export listings, which were discarded. The Drishti article says BAU breeders, the seed directorate, research stations and KVKs will cooperate in seed production for the newly released BAU varieties, but it does not name Birsa Chana 3 -- https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/birsa-agricultural-university

- Yield values, maturity and agronomic details were not visible in the snippets. Opening the ICAR PDF directly is needed to read them.

GENETICS AND QTL

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The ICAR article is about Pusa Pasand (DS-8), which carries the Pusa name. This suggests IARI origin, but no breeder name was visible in the snippets. The institution attribution in the variety record (IARI) is not confirmed by the pages I read.
- The parentage given in the record ("a Hyderabad derivative... grown in Vidarbha for over 20 years") was not verified by any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS

SEED AVAILABILITY

RECOMMENDED STATES

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GM-2 (Seednet name: GBM 2), fenugreek, Gujarat Methi-2

Search coverage: four web_search queries were run: "GM-2 fenugreek variety", "GM-2 fenugreek breeder institute", "GM-2 fenugreek research paper", and "GBM 2 fenugreek seed availability". None returned a page about this variety, under either name, so every heading below reports no evidence.

Name and record notes:
- The CSC minutes name is GM-2 and the Seednet name is GBM 2. The searches used both names and neither returned variety-specific results.
- The Seednet crop field reads "BENGAL GRAM (GRAM/CHICK PEA/KABULI/CHANA)", but the variety is fenugreek. This looks like a crop-mapping error in the Seednet record and should be checked on the portal.
- The parentage field contains corrupted characters ("Physical mutation of Annigeri" followed by unreadable text). The parent name is recorded as Annigeri, and the rest could not be recovered.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found
DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found
GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a breeder or lead scientist of GM-2 or GBM 2. The institution named in the record is S.D. Agricultural University; no SDAU variety page or release notice was retrieved.
CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No SDAU, Sardarkrushinagar station, or ICAR contact details were retrieved, so none are given here.
PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The results that came back concerned fenugreek in general, not this variety: a PMC systematic review on fenugreek and type 2 diabetes (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10531284/) and a ResearchGate review of fenugreek biology and cultivation (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/266879404_A_Review_on_Biology_Cultivation_and_Biotechnology_of_Fenugreek_Trigonella_foenum-graecum_L._as_a_Valuable_Medicinal_Plant_and_Multipurpose). Neither mentions GM-2 or GBM 2, so neither is listed as a publication for this variety.
SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Only commercial retail seed listings appeared (for example https://territorialseed.com/products/fenugreek), and none refer to this variety. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing was found.
RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The CSC record lists KARNATAKA, but no independent source was retrieved to confirm it.

Suggested next steps: check seednet.gov.in directly under GBM 2 and correct the crop field, search SDAU's site (sdau.edu.in) and Gujarat state notification records for GM-2 / Gujarat Methi-2, and search KrishiKosh for fenugreek release reports.

The ARS Sriganganagar profile places the station in Zone 1b, Irrigated North West Plain. An Apni Kheti guide lists GNG 1969 under irrigated areas. agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Profuse branching, semi-erect habit and large seed (ICAR 2013-14 report). Seed weight about 26.2 g per 100 seeds with creamy beige seed colour (DPD listing). A MapMyCrop guide gives 33.6 g per 100 grains, but it conflicts with DPD/ICAR records and was not used.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) DPD listing: recommended for irrigated, normal-sown conditions, 146 days to maturity, about 22 q/ha yield. (2) Akola thesis: GNG-1969 was a low performer under irrigated late-sown conditions compared with GNG-469 and GNG-1958 (no figures given). (3) Package-of-practices listing for kabuli GNG 1969 (timely sown) at ARS Sriganganagar: details not extracted in the digest. (4) ICAR-AICRP 2021-22 genetic gain (ERA) trial: GNG 1969 entry present, but no usable GNG-1969 data in the extract. (5) MapMyCrop guide (2011 release, 157 days, 7.3 q/acre, 33.6 g per 100 grains): excluded because it conflicts with DPD/ICAR records.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
GNG-1969 (Triveni) -- chickpea digest. Searches were run under "GNG-1969 Chickpea" and "GNG-1969 Triveni Bengal gram". Seednet's own entry for this variety was not returned, so the name "GNG-1969 (Triveni)" has no direct Seednet evidence. Most sources use "GNG 1969" and some use "GNG 1969 (Triveni-Kabuli)".

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to GNG-1969. The only drought/salinity tolerance text in the search results (ICAR crop-improvement report, 2013-14) sits beside a sugarcane entry, so I excluded it -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2013-14.pdf
Related: a Akola thesis reports that GNG-1969 was a low performer under irrigated late-sown conditions, in a comparison with GNG-469 and GNG-1958 -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/e6bbf4ad-03de-4363-9b40-3886f9efb7b4/content

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found that names GNG-1969 for disease or pest resistance. The ICAR-IIPR chickpea report contains a GNG 1969 row, but the resistance text beside it belongs to a different line (03112 x ICCV 10 and ICC 4958 descendants), so I did not attribute it -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Recommended for irrigated, normal-sown conditions, with 146 days to maturity and about 22 q/ha yield -- https://dpd.gov.in/Varieties/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
Seed weight is about 26.2 g per 100 seeds, with creamy beige seed colour -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Profuse branching, semi-erect habit and large seed are listed for GNG 1969 -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2013-14.pdf
Conflict: a MapMyCrop guide gives a 2011 release, 157 days, 7.3 q/acre and 33.6 g per 100 grains. This conflicts with the DPD/ICAR records and I did not use it -- https://mapmycrop.com/gram-chickpea-crop-guideindia/
Package-of-practices listing for kabuli GNG 1969 (timely sown) at ARS Sriganganagar -- https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/themes/theme2/PDF/Ganganagar.pdf
Irrigated-only sowing: an Apni Kheti guide lists GNG 1969 as cultivated under irrigated areas -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/pulses/bengal-gram-chickpea

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: Unknown (as supplied). No evidence found for parentage, pedigree, breeding method or breeding-line code. A GNG 1292 pedigree in the ICAR report is a different line and was excluded.
QTL, markers and genome resources: No evidence found that names GNG-1969.
Genetic variability: GNG-1969 is among the genotypes in a 2025 variability study, but no genetic parameters are given specifically for it -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue6/PartB/8-5-22-558.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Breeder name(s): No evidence found.
Developing institution: Agricultural Research Station, Sriganganagar (Zone 1b, Irrigated North West Plain), which lists "Triveni (GNG-1969) (2013)" among its releases -- https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ARS-at-a-glance-17.08.pdf
The ICAR/epubs paper refers to the station as under "S K Rajasthan Agricultural University, Bikaner" -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/122247/46536
Current university: SKNAU Jobner, established 2013 -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Karan_Narendra_Agriculture_University (Wikipedia; not an official source)

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for a breeder email, phone or postal address. No station email or phone was found. The only SKNAU page returned covers the Navgaon (Alwar) station, not Sriganganagar, so I excluded it -- https://www.sknau.ac.in/arsnavgaon
Station profile PDF (ARS Sriganganagar) -- https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ARS-at-a-glance-17.08.pdf (no contact details found in the extract)

PUBLICATIONS
Kotwal, P. N. (year not stated). Impact Assessment of Chickpea Variety Released by Dr. PDKV, Akola. MSc thesis, Dr. PDKV Akola (includes GNG-1969 performance comparison) -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/e6bbf4ad-03de-4363-9b40-3886f9efb7b4/content
Authors not stated (2025). Chickpea genetic variability study, International Journal of Research in Agronomy 8(6): 104-110 (lists GNG-1969 among genotypes) -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue6/PartB/8-5-22-558.pdf
Authors not stated (2020). Advances in Chickpea Breeding and Genomics for Varietal Development and Trait Improvement in India (lists GNG 1969 among north Indian releases) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344273491_Advances_in_Chickpea_Breeding_and_Genomics_for_Varietal_Development_and_Trait_Improvement_in_India
Not included: a 2016-18 SKRAU Bikaner seed-rate study names other GNG lines but not GNG-1969 in the extract.
ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea annual report 2021-22 includes a GNG 1969 entry for the genetic gain (ERA) trial, but the extract did not give usable GNG-1969 data -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or private dealers. The ARS Sriganganagar profile mentions farm seed production for chickpea but does not name GNG-1969 for seed sale -- https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ARS-at-a-glance-17.08.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
Punjab, Haryana, north-western Rajasthan, western Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Delhi (NWPZ) -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2013-14.pdf
The DPD listing gives the zone as NWPZ (HR, PN, RJ, UP, UK, DL) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Note: the supplied state list says "Rajasthan (excluding southern part)" -- the ICAR report says "north-western Rajasthan", which is consistent with this.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNG 1958 (Seednet name GNG 1581), chickpea, "Marudhar"

Search status: The search tool hit its usage limit partway through my second batch. I ran only the GNG 1958 queries and never searched the Seednet name GNG 1581. The results I could read did not identify this variety, so I cannot attribute any variety-specific claim to a source. Nothing below is cited as evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found (searched; no GNG 1958 or GNG 1581 mention in the results I reviewed)
DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found (searched; same as above)
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The only chickpea results were general papers on frontline demonstrations and plant population effects, not this variety. Source: https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4338 and https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/122247/46536
GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found (not searched separately; no relevant result in the research query)
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found (searched "GNG 1958 chickpea breeder developed by"; no breeder name or station identified). The release record names the Agricultural Research Station, SK Rajasthan Agricultural University as institution, which comes from your input, not from a search result.
CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. I did not record any email, phone or address, and I did not guess one.
PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found (searched; no paper, AICRP report or KrishiKosh thesis naming GNG 1958 or GNG 1581 was identified)
SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found (searched; no NSC, state corporation, KVK or dealer listing identified)
RECOMMENDED STATES -- Input record only, not verified: North West Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Western Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Delhi. Source: your VARIETY record, not a search result.

Suggested next steps for manual verification:
1. Search seednet.gov.in for GNG 1581 and check the variety notification and developer fields.
2. Check the CSC/AICRP-Chickpea release minutes for GNG 1958 and confirm the spelling.
3. Search KrishiKosh and Legume Research for "Marudhar" and "GNG 1581", since the variety code may index better than the names.
4. Confirm the developing station's official contact page on the SKRAU website.

drought.details: GNG 2461 is identified as a rainfed desi line in the North-West Plain Zone after three years of multi-location testing and is listed among promising rainfed desi genotypes in the AICRP report. Rainfed adaptation is not the same as demonstrated drought tolerance. Drought-specific tolerance (terminal drought mechanisms) for GNG 2461 was not found. The drought-tolerance statement in the cited report applies to a different line derived from ICC 4958.

salinity.details: Salinity tolerance evidence for GNG 2461 was not found in the digest.

flood.details: Flood tolerance evidence for GNG 2461 was not found in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: Dry root rot (DRR): GNG 2461 is listed among entries found moderately resistant to DRR in multi-location testing (AICRP Chickpea 2021-22). The entry appears more than once in the table, so the exact number of trials is unclear. Resistance to wilt, Botrytis blight and other diseases was not found for GNG 2461 specifically.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. Resistance to pod borer or other pests was not found for GNG 2461.

agronomic_details.yield: Rainfed NWPZ weighted mean of 2140 kg/ha over 9 trials (AICRP Chickpea 2021-22). The original variety data record also lists average yield as 2413 kg/ha, which is not verified in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the multi-location trial results summarised under field_trials. Stability statistics were not reported in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed conditions in the North-West Plain Zone (NWPZ), per the SKRAU page. Recommended for Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, north-western Rajasthan, western Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir.

agronomic_details.field_trials: Rainfed NWPZ yield table, AICRP Chickpea 2021-22 (kg/ha): AVT-2 (2020-21) yielded 2217 from 5 trials; AVT-1 (2020-21) yielded 1698 from 2 trials; IVT (2019-20) yielded 2390 from 2 trials; weighted mean across 9 trials was 2140. The average rainfed yield of 2140 kg/ha is reported as better than the older check RSG.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNG 2461 (Moomal), chickpea (desi, Cicer arietinum)

Name check: The CSC release name and the Seednet name both read "GNG 2461", so every finding below refers to GNG 2461. I did not search seednet.gov.in directly, so Seednet-side fields (crop code, parentage, release date) are unverified. The release-minutes field gives 2023-05-02, but the sources give notification 4222(E) dated 25.09.2023. I have treated 25.09.2023 as the notification date and flagged the mismatch.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Identified as a rainfed desi line in the North-West Plain Zone after three years of multi-location testing; the AICRP report lists it among the promising rainfed desi genotypes. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Drought-specific tolerance (e.g., terminal drought, heat, salinity, flooding, submergence) for GNG 2461 was not found. The drought-tolerance statement in that report applies to a different line derived from ICC 4958. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- GNG 2461 is listed among entries found moderately resistant to dry root rot (DRR) in multi-location testing. The entry appears more than once in the table, so the exact trial count is unclear. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Resistance to wilt, Botrytis blight, pod borer or other pests was not found for GNG 2461 specifically. -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Rainfed NWPZ yield table, AICRP Chickpea 2021-22 (kg/ha): AVT-2 (2020-21) 2217 from 5 trials; AVT-1 (2020-21) 1698 from 2 trials; IVT (2019-20) 2390 from 2 trials; weighted mean 2140 from 9 trials. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Average rainfed yield of 2140 kg/ha, reported as better than the older check RSG. -- https://raubikaner.org/directorate-of-research/
- Maturity duration, seed size and plant-type data for GNG 2461 were not found. -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: developed by pedigree selection from a dual hybridization, combining a single cross of KWR-108 × GNG 1861 with a single cross of Pant G-186 × GNG 1958. This answers the "Not specified" parentage field. -- https://raubikaner.org/directorate-of-research/
- QTL, marker or genomic studies on GNG 2461 were not found. -- No evidence found

EVIDENCE DIGEST: GPF 2 (Chickpea / Bengal gram)

Search note: the search tool hit its usage limit after the four queries, so I could not re-open the result pages for full text. Every finding below comes from the truncated search snippets only and should be checked against the full pages before it goes into a reference record.

Name note: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "GPF 2." The sources write it as "GPF2" or "GPF 2," and I have treated these spacing variants as the same variety. Seednet variety code A0302200 and crop name BENGAL GRAM (GRAM/CHICK PEA/KABULI/CHANA) were not confirmed by any search result.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- A paper titled "Genetic mapping of QTLs for drought tolerance in chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.)" names GPF2 as a cultivar in its QTL mapping work. The snippet does not show GPF2's drought score or its heat, salinity, flood, or submergence response. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362790305_Genetic_mapping_of_QTLs_for_drought_tolerance_in_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The search did not return any page that reports wilt resistance or pest resistance for GPF 2. The parentage text in the input describes the variety as wilt resistant, but this was not verified by any search result.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A paper titled "Assessing the Performance of Chickpea Cultivars in Mandi District of Himachal Pradesh, India" reports that GPF 2 was among the cultivars tested in Mandi district and ranked behind a cultivar named "Himachal" in the snippet. The snippet is truncated and does not give yields, trial design, or years. It also notes that pod number, 100-seed weight, and plant height were important traits for seed yield per plant. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376633866_Assessing_the_Performance_of_Chickpea_Cultivars_in_Mandi_District_of_Himachal_Pradesh_India

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- The drought QTL paper cited above uses GPF2 as a cultivar in its mapping study. disease_resistance.research_summary: Digest search found no page reporting wilt or other disease resistance for GPF 2. The input parentage text describes GPF 2 as wilt resistant, but the digest states this was not verified. The input disease_reaction field reports, on average of 12 trials, wilt and root rot incidence of 17.2 per cent for GF 89-36 versus 86.4 (JG 62), 37.8 (C 235) and 43.1 (PBG 1) per cent, with Ascochyta blight and grey mould also noted relative to checks. These figures come from the input record, not from a digest source, and the digest does not confirm that GF 89-36 is the same entry as GPF 2. Treat as unverified.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: resistant (DPD release table; 2022 seed-industry notice; JAU variety proposal). Stunt: resistant (same three sources). Root rot: tolerant (DPD release table; 2022 seed-industry notice). Ascochyta blight: tolerant (DPD release table; 2022 seed-industry notice). Wilt, Ascochyta blight, stunt, root rot and BGM: rated moderately resistant in a commercial seller listing (GG-5), treated as lower confidence. No Ascochyta, BGM or insect-specific trial data beyond these listings.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance evidence found. A commercial listing (GG-5) reports low pod borer infestation; this is an observation in a seller listing, not a resistance trial result. No insect-specific trial data found.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 2115 kg/ha against potential 4306 kg/ha (JAU proposal, GG 5). Average yield 16 q/ha (DPD release table; ICAR-IIPR AICRP 2021-22 entry; Agricultural Science Digest citing an anonymous 2023 report). Under irrigated Gujarat trials, about 27.6% higher seed yield than Dahod Yellow and about 12.3% higher than Gujarat Gram 1.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources (no multi-environment stability analysis in the digest; AICRP 2021-22 entry lists irrigated, NHZ conditions only)
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated conditions in Gujarat; the release proposal title identifies the North Hill Zone (NHZ) as the target zone. No rainfed, drought-prone or other agro-climatic adaptation evidence found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Conflicting: 157 days (DPD and CVRC table; ICAR-IIPR AICRP 2021-22 entry; the figure shared by the national table); 98 days (JAU proposal sheet, early group); 103 days (seller listing). The 157-day figure is the one shared by the national table.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 168.1 cm; indeterminate habit; 10.6 branches/plant; 220.5 pods/plant (JAU proposal). Medium brown seed; 21.5 g/100 seeds (DPD table). 100-seed weight 21.37 g (seller listing). Seed rate 24 kg/acre and spacing 18 inches (seller listing).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Sixty front-line demonstrations under irrigated conditions in Gujarat during 2015-16 (GG 5). (2) Irrigated Gujarat trials: about 27.6% higher seed yield than Dahod Yellow and about 12.3% higher than Gujarat Gram 1 (GG 5). (3) Average yield 2115 kg/ha against potential 4306 kg/ha, with plant height, habit, branching and pod data from the JAU proposal (GG 5). (4) Average yield 16 q/ha and 157 days to maturity (GJG 0809, DPD). (5) Phosphorus study, rabi 2015-16, calcareous soil, South Saurashtra, with GJG 0809 as test variety: 40 kg P2O5/ha gave highest seed yield (1507 kg/ha) and best B:C ratio (2.40). (6) Entry in the ICAR-IIPR AICRP chickpea 2021-22 report: 16.0 q/ha, 157 days, irrigated, NHZ. (7) Breeder-seed programme of about 1200 kg planned for 2015-16.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No SSR, SNP or other marker data found in searched sources. Parentage: GJG 9707 x IPC 97-7 (pedigree JND 2001-02-02-01-05-01-5B), developed by hybridization followed by pedigree selection. Germplasm accession IC:598345 deposited with NBPGR.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL, marker or genomic study specific to GJG 0809 found. A 2022 chickpea genome-variation paper lists co-author M. S. Pithia but gives no GJG 0809 data in the retrieved text.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Resistant to wilt and stunt, with tolerance to root rot and Ascochyta blight, per the DPD release table (name in evidence: GJG 0809) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Wilt and stunt resistance, root rot resistance and Ascochyta blight tolerance, per a 2022 seed-industry notice (name in evidence: GJG 0809) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-gjg-0809/
Wilt and stunt resistance per the JAU variety proposal (name in evidence: Gujarat Gram 5 / GG 5) -- https://aau.in/sites/default/files/X%20Agresco%20proceedings.pdf
Rated moderately resistant to wilt, Ascochyta blight, stunt, root rot and BGM (commercial seller listing, name in evidence: Gujarat Gram 5 / GG-5; treat as lower confidence) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gg-5/
No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found for this variety

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to wilt and stunt (see above) -- https://aau.in/sites/default/files/X%20Agresco%20proceedings.pdf
Low pod borer infestation (commercial listing, GG-5) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gg-5/
No Ascochyta, BGM or insect-specific trial data beyond the listings above

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Sixty front-line demonstrations under irrigated conditions in Gujarat during 2015-16 (GG 5) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/84265
Under irrigated Gujarat trials, about 27.6% higher seed yield than Dahod Yellow and about 12.3% higher than Gujarat Gram 1 (GG 5) -- https://aau.in/sites/default/files/X%20Agresco%20proceedings.pdf
Average yield 2115 kg/ha against potential 4306 kg/ha; plant height 168.1 cm, indeterminate habit, 10.6 branches/plant, 220.5 pods/plant (GG 5) -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
Average yield 16 q/ha and 157 days to maturity, medium brown seed, 21.5 g/100 seeds (GJG 0809) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
Maturity conflict: 98 days (JAU proposal sheet, early group) and 103 days (seller listing) versus 157 days (DPD and CVRC table); the 157-day figure is the one shared by the national table -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf ; https://fuleseeds.com/products/gg-5/
Phosphorus study, rabi 2015-16, calcareous soil, South Saurashtra: 40 kg P2O5/ha gave highest seed yield (1507 kg/ha) and best B:C ratio (2.40) (GJG 0809 used as the test variety) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323553069_Chickpea_Cultivation_Governing_By_Phosphorus_Application_in_Calcareous_Soil
Seed rate 24 kg/acre, spacing 18 inches, 100-seed weight 21.37 g (commercial listing, GG-5) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gg-5/
Breeder-seed programme of about 1200 kg planned for 2015-16 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/84265
Entry in the ICAR-IIPR AICRP chickpea 2021-22 report: 16.0 q/ha, 157 days, irrigated, NHZ -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage GJG 9707 x IPC 97-7 (pedigree JND 2001-02-02-01-05-01-5B), breeding by hybridization followed by pedigree selection -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf

disease_resistance.research_summary: Wilt: resistant (DPD release table; 2022 seed-industry notice; JAU variety proposal). Stunt: resistant (same three sources). Root rot: tolerant (DPD release table; 2022 seed-industry notice). Ascochyta blight: tolerant (DPD release table; 2022 seed-industry notice). Wilt, Ascochyta blight, stunt, root rot and BGM: rated moderately resistant in a commercial seller listing (GG-5), treated as lower confidence. No Ascochyta, BGM or insect-specific trial data beyond these listings.

drought.details: No confirmed drought tolerance for Gujarat Gram 5. The DPD listing carries a drought-tolerance note, but the digest states it could not be confirmed as belonging to this variety (it may refer to a different MABB-derived line). No drought mechanism or field evidence was found for this variety.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to Gujarat Gram 5.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to Gujarat Gram 5.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to Gujarat Gram 5.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: moderately resistant (ICAR-IIPR AICRP Chickpea 2021-22); resistant per DPD listing. Stunt: moderately resistant (ICAR-IIPR 2021-22); resistant per DPD listing. Root rot: resistant (ICAR-IIPR 2021-22; DPD listing). Ascochyta blight: tolerant (ICAR-IIPR 2021-22; DPD listing; Current Science review 2019 names GJG 0809 among Ascochyta-tolerant lines; dealer listing reports moderate resistance). BGM (Botrytis grey mould): moderate resistance per dealer listing only (dealer data, not an official source). The DPD varietal table attributes wilt and stunt tolerance to the JAU Gram 3/6 series, not explicitly to this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance was established for Gujarat Gram 5. A dealer listing reports low pod borer infestation (dealer data, not an official source), which is an observation of infestation level rather than a documented resistance mechanism. No separate pest data for this variety was found in the DPD varietal table.

agronomic_details.yield: Dang district (KVK Dang, NAU) front-line demonstrations 2018-19 to 2020-21: 1102 kg/ha versus 825 kg/ha under farmer practice. JAU variety list (2018-era): North Hill Zone entry potential yield 3392 kg/ha and average 2510 kg/ha; separate Saurashtra kharif entry potential 4306 kg/ha and average 2115 kg/ha. The original data field 'average_yield' records only the unit (Kg/Ha) without a value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Yield data come from different zones and years and were not analysed for stability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recorded in North Hill Zone and Saurashtra kharif entries (JAU list). Demonstrated under irrigated conditions in Gujarat (2015-16 FLDs) and on calcareous soil in South Saurashtra (irrigated phosphorus trial). Dang district FLD reports seed yield gains against farmer practice. No explicit agro-climatic recommendation statement was found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 157-160 days (DPD listing); 176 days, medium group (JAU listing). A dealer listing gives 103 days, which the digest flags as unreliable and which is not used here.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Gujarat, 2015-16: 60 front-line demonstrations under irrigated conditions (Indian Farming, 2018); breeder seed production of about 1200 kg was planned for 2015-16. (2) Dang district, KVK Dang (NAU), 2018-19 to 2020-21: FLD seed yield 1102 kg/ha versus 825 kg/ha under farmer practice. (3) South Saurashtra calcareous soil, irrigated phosphorus trial: 40 kg P2O5/ha was most effective, giving yield 11.62% above control. (4) JAU variety list: North Hill Zone entry, potential 3392 kg/ha, average 2510 kg/ha; Saurashtra kharif entry, potential 4306 kg/ha, average 2115 kg/ha. Trial sites, replication and statistical details were not found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources, apart from the DPD note that the variety is marker-assisted backcross (MABB) derived. No marker names, positions or SSR/SNP details were found.

Ascochyta blight: tolerant (ICAR-IIPR 2021-22; DPD listing; Current Science review 2019 names GJG 0809 among Ascochyta-tolerant lines; dealer listing reports moderate resistance). search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAME NOTE: Evidence for "Gujarat Gram 5" (CSC name, also GG 5 / GJG 0809) and "Gujarat Gram 8" (Seednet name) describes two different varieties. Each heading below states which name the evidence refers to. Searches run: 4 (no Seednet portal page surfaced in any of them).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Gujarat Gram 5 (GG 5, GJG 0809): DPD listing records resistance to wilt and stunt, root rot, and tolerance to Ascochyta blight; the same listing also tags a drought-tolerance note to a MABB-derived variety, which I could not confirm is this variety -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 5: the ICAR-IIPR AICRP chickpea report (2021-22) lists GJG 0809 as moderately resistant to wilt and stunt, resistant to root rot, and tolerant to Ascochyta blight -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 5: a Current Science review (2019) names GJG 0809 among chickpea lines tolerant to Ascochyta blight -- https://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/116/02/0239.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 8 (Seednet name): JAU's notice describes it as selected for machine harvest suitability, with resistance to diseases and pests claimed generally -- https://asthafoundation.in/img/02-Gujarat%20Gram%208%20-%20A%20Chickpea%20Variety%20High%20Yielding%20and%20Suitable%20for%20Machine%20Harvest.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance specific to Gujarat Gram 5 beyond the single ambiguous DPD drought note.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Gujarat Gram 5: dealer listing describes moderate resistance to wilt, Ascochyta blight, stunt, root rot and BGM, with low pod borer infestation (dealer data, not an official source) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gg-5/
- Gujarat Gram 5: DPD varietal table notes tolerance to wilt and stunt for the JAU Gram 3/6 series; no separate pest data for GG 5 -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 8 (Seednet name): JAU-linked notice says it was tested against checks and found to show resistance to diseases and pests -- https://asthafoundation.in/img/02-Gujarat%20Gram%208%20-%20A%20Chickpea%20Variety%20High%20Yielding%20and%20Suitable%20for%20Machine%20Harvest.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Gujarat Gram 5: Indian Farming (2018) reports 60 front-line demonstrations in Gujarat in 2015-16 under irrigated conditions, and breeder seed production of about 1200 kg planned for 2015-16 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/84265
- Gujarat Gram 5: KVK Dang (NAU) front-line demonstrations, 2018-19 to 2020-21, report seed yield of 1102 kg/ha against 825 kg/ha under farmer practice -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378078345_Evaluation_of_frontline_demonstration_of_new_technology_on_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_in_Dang_district_of_Gujarat
- Gujarat Gram 5: phosphorus trial on calcareous soil (South Saurashtra, irrigated) found 40 kg P2O5/ha most effective, with yield 11.62% above control -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323553069_Chickpea_Cultivation_Governing_By_Phosphorus_Application_in_Calcareous_Soil
- Gujarat Gram 5: JAU's 2018-era variety list gives potential yield 3392 kg/ha and average 2510 kg/ha for the North Hill Zone entry; a separate entry gives 4306 and 2115 kg/ha for Saurashtra kharif -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 5: maturity recorded as 157-160 days (DPD); JAU's listing gives 176 days (medium group); a dealer listing gives 103 days (unreliable) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 8 (Seednet name): state trials 2019-20 to 2021-22 under irrigated and rainfed conditions; seed yield superior to checks -- https://asthafoundation.in/img/02-Gujarat%20Gram%208%20-%20A%20Chickpea%20Variety%20High%20Yielding%20and%20Suitable%20for%20Machine%20Harvest.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Gujarat Gram 5: JAU pedigree record gives parentage GJG 9707 x IPC 97-7 (pedigree JND 2001-02-02-01-05-01-5B), bred by hybridization followed by pedigree selection -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 5: DPD notes the variety as MABB (marker-assisted backcross) derived -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 8 (Seednet name): parentage PG 07104 x WR315, per JAU's list -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/pulses-research-station-junagadh
- No QTL or marker-trait association study for GG 5 found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Gujarat Gram 5: Indian Farming article authors are M S Pithia, R M Javia, V V Ramani and V P Andani, all at Pulses Research Station, JAU, Junagadh 362 001 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/84265
- Gujarat Gram 5: Vikram Singh and co-authors (JAU soil science) worked with GG 5 (GJG 0809), noting it was developed and evaluated by the Main Pulses Research Station, JAU -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323553069_Chickpea_Cultivation_Governing_By_Phosphorus_Application_in_Calcareous_Soil
- Gujarat Gram 8 (Seednet name): JAU's Pulses Research Station table lists GG 8 with notification year 2023 and parents PG 07104 x WR315 -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/pulses-research-station-junagadh
- Institution: Pulses Research Station runs chickpea crop improvement, agronomy, entomology and pathology work, and produces nucleus and breeder seed of chickpea -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/pulses-research-station-junagadh

CONTACT DETAILS
- Pulses Research Station, Junagadh Agricultural University, Junagadh 362 001, Gujarat, India (address as given in the Indian Farming and JAU records) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/84265
- JAU general contact address: Junagadh Agricultural University, Junagadh 362 001, Gujarat (INDIA) -- https://www.jau.in/new-varieties-released
- Rakesh Javia (scientist, chickpea, per news report): phone 9427725505, no email found -- https://allgujaratnews.in/en/amazing-discovery-of-new-varieties-of-gram-will-revolutionize-agriculture/
- A. G. Pansuriya (JAU Research Director, per news report): phone 9428241838 -- https://allgujaratnews.in/en/amazing-discovery-of-new-varieties-of-gram-will-revolutionize-agriculture/
- No official email for the breeder or Pulses Research Station found in any result.
- Seed dealer (not an institute): Fule Seeds, Shop 7-10, Moti Palace Plus, Timbawadi, Junagadh 362015; info@fuleseeds.com; +91 91065 70738 -- https://fuleseeds.com/product-category/chickpea/

PUBLICATIONS
- Pithia, M. S., Javia, R. M., Ramani, V. V., & Andani, V. P. (2018). Gujarat Gram 5: A high yielding desi chickpea variety for North Hill Zone of India. Indian Farming, 67(6). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/84265
- Singh, V., Kumar, A., Lal, M., & Kumar, M. (2018). Chickpea cultivation governed by phosphorus application in calcareous soil. International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences, 7(2). -- DOI 10.20546/ijcmas.2018.702.407; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323553069_Chickpea_Cultivation_Governing_By_Phosphorus_Application_in_Calcareous_Soil
- Current Science review (2019), Vol. 116, No. 2, p. 239, chickpea research in India (mentions GJG 0809) -- https://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/116/02/0239.pdf
- ICAR-IIPR, All India Coordinated Research Project on Chickpea, Progress Report 2021-22 (lists GJG 0809) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Dang district FLD study, GG 5 (author list and year not verified in search output) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378078345_Evaluation_of_frontline_demonstration_of_new_technology_on_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_in_Dang_district_of_Gujarat
- No KrishiKosh thesis or peer-reviewed genetics paper on GG 5 found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Gujarat Gram 5: Krushisharang Agriclinic (Fule Seeds) offers 10 kg packs at INR 850 in Timbawadi, Junagadh (dealer listing; check current price) -- https://www.tradeindia.com/products/

drought.details: Described as suited to conserved soil moisture in rainfed Gujarat and recommended for rainfed cultivation under conserved moisture (Javia et al. 2018). The digest reports no drought test data for this variety in the retrieved pages, so a drought tolerance level cannot be graded. Rainfed yield of 1867 kg/ha was 5.2-21.9% above checks Gujarat Gram 1, Gujarat Gram 2 and GJG 3 (Javia et al. 2018), which indicates adaptation to rainfed conditions but is not a direct drought stress test.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. No salinity test data for this variety in the retrieved pages.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. No flood test data for this variety in the retrieved pages.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: described as wilt-resistant (Javia et al. 2018; the paper title also uses 'wilt resistant'), and as listed tolerant to wilt (DPD central/state list). The JAU variety document and the ICAR-AICRP chickpea report 2021-22 both rate it moderately resistant to wilt. The sources conflict; the JAU and ICAR ratings are the more specific official classifications. Stunt: good resistance (Javia et al. 2018); tolerant to stunt (DPD list); moderately resistant (JAU variety document and ICAR-AICRP 2021-22). Ascochyta blight: moderately resistant (JAU variety document). Fule Seeds (commercial source, not official) lists resistance to wilt and stunt.

pest_resistance.summary: Pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera): comparable pod borer damage to checks, with good resistance noted (Javia et al. 2018). The JAU variety document reports low Helicoverpa armigera infestation. Fule Seeds (commercial source, not official) lists low pod borer infestation. No other pest resistance data found for this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Rainfed grain yield 1867 kg/ha (Javia et al. 2018). JAU variety document: potential yield 4306 kg/ha, average 2115 kg/ha. DPD listing: 16-18 q/ha. Fule Seeds: 7.5-11 quintal/acre. KVK Porbandar frontline demonstrations: 18.10, 15.05 and 19.11 q/ha (2021-22 to 2023-24).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the three-year KVK Porbandar frontline demonstration results (18.10, 15.05 and 19.11 q/ha). No multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed conditions under conserved soil moisture in Gujarat (Javia et al. 2018). Normal sown in Gujarat (DPD listing). Sowing from the first fortnight of November at 45 x 10 cm spacing, seed rate 60 kg/ha, N:P:K 20:40:00 kg/ha (JAU variety document). Fule Seeds lists seed rate 24 kg/acre. Tested in Porbandar district by KVK frontline demonstrations. The JAU document describes the area as kharif in Saurashtra, which conflicts with the normal-sown rabi status given elsewhere.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 110-112 days (Javia et al. 2018); 103 days, early group (JAU variety document); 120-130 days (DPD listing); 112 days (Fule Seeds). Sources differ.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Fule Seeds: semi-erect habit, dark brown seed, 100-seed weight 22.45 g. Javia et al. 2018: protein 19.9% and carbohydrate 67.84%, above checks. Morphological characteristics not otherwise specified in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Javia et al. 2018, rainfed trials: grain yield 1867 kg/ha, 5.2-21.9% above checks Gujarat Gram 1, Gujarat Gram 2 and GJG 3; maturity 110-112 days; protein 19.9% and carbohydrate 67.84%, above checks. (2) JAU variety document: potential yield 4306 kg/ha, average 2115 kg/ha, maturity 103 days. (3) KVK Porbandar frontline demonstrations, 2021-22 to 2023-24: 18.10, 15.05 and 19.11 q/ha, overall 12.70% above local varieties. (4) ICAR-AICRP Chickpea 2021-22 progress report: described as moderately resistant to wilt and stunt; no yield figures found in the digest. No peer-reviewed multi-location trial paper or KrishiKosh thesis naming this variety was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
GJG 6 EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: Searches used "Gujarat Junagadh Gram 6" (variety_name) and "GJG 6" (seednet_variety_name). Most sources use "GJG 6" or "GJG-6" and match this variety. No seednet.gov.in page was retrieved, so the Seednet record itself is unverified. Some sources list GJG 6 under the earlier culture code GJG 1003 and the IC number IC:615013.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Described as wilt-resistant and tolerant of stunt, suited to conserved soil moisture in rainfed Gujarat -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330314101_GJG_6_A_high_yielding_wilt_resistant_chickpea_variety_for_conserved_moisture_condition_of_Gujarat ; https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2018.00192.8
Listed as tolerant to wilt and stunt, suitable for normal sowing (DPD central/state list) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
No flood, submergence, salinity, heat or drought test data found for this variety in the retrieved pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to wilt, with good resistance to stunt and comparable pod borer damage (Javia et al. 2018) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2018.00192.8
JAU variety document rates it moderately resistant to wilt, Ascochyta blight and stunt, with low Helicoverpa armigera infestation. This conflicts with the "resistant" wording above -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
ICAR-AICRP chickpea report 2021-22 describes it as moderately resistant to wilt and stunt -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Fule Seeds product page lists resistance to wilt and stunt and low pod borer infestation (commercial source, not official) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-junagadh-gram-6-gjg-6/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity 110-112 days; rainfed grain yield 1867 kg/ha, 5.2-21.9% above checks Gujarat Gram 1, Gujarat Gram 2 and GJG 3 (Javia et al. 2018) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2018.00192.8
Maturity 103 days (early group), sowing from the first fortnight of November at 45 x 10 cm, seed rate 60 kg/ha, N:P:K 20:40:00 kg/ha. Potential yield 4306 kg/ha, average 2115 kg/ha. The same document describes the area as kharif in Saurashtra, which conflicts with the normal-sown rabi status elsewhere -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
DPD listing: yield 16-18 q/ha, maturity 120-130 days, normal sown Gujarat -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
KVK Porbandar frontline demonstrations 2021-22 to 2023-24: 18.10, 15.05 and 19.11 q/ha, overall 12.70% above local varieties -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/354%20IMPACT-OF-FRONTLINE-DEMONSTRATIONS-OF-CHICKPEA-(CICER-ARIETINUM-L.)-IMPROVED-VARIETY-GJG-6-ON-YIELD-IN-PORBANDAR-DISTRICT-OF-GUJARAT-INDIA.pdf
Fule Seeds page: 112 days, 7.5-11 quintal/acre, 100-seed weight 22.45 g, seed rate 24 kg/acre, semi-erect habit, dark brown seed -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-junagadh-gram-6-gjg-6/
Protein 19.9% and carbohydrate 67.84%, above checks (Javia et al. 2018) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2018.00192.8

GENETICS AND QTL
Cross: GJG 0105 x FC 711 (pedigree JND 2002-01-01-05-02-01-SB), hybridization followed by pedigree selection (JAU variety document) -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
Javia et al. 2018 gives the cross as GJG 0105 x "FG 711", which conflicts with "FC 711" in the JAU document -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2018.00192.8
No QTL or marker study naming this variety was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Lead authors of the release paper: Rakesh M. Javia, Motisagar Shravankumar Pithia and Babulal A. Monpara, Junagadh Agricultural University (Pulses Research Station, JAU, and Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, JAU) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2018.00192.8 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330314101_GJG_6_A_high_yielding_wilt_resistant_chickpea_variety_for_conserved_moisture_condition_of_Gujarat
Developing institution: Junagadh Agricultural University, Pulses Research Station, Junagadh -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf ; http://www.jau.in/index.php/resources/research-stations-top/south-saurashtra/pulses-research-station-junagadh
Originating source listed as Pulses Research Station, JAU, Junagadh-362 001 (Gujarat) -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
Pulses Research Station, Junagadh Agricultural University, Junagadh-362 001, Gujarat, India (postal address as printed in the JAU variety document and paper) -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
Institute contact page for the station: http://www.jau.in/index.php/resources/research-stations-top/south-saurashtra/pulses-research-station-junagadh (no email or phone was visible in the retrieved text)
No named breeder email or phone found. No official email or phone number for the station was found in the retrieved text.

PUBLICATIONS
Javia, R. M.; Pithia, M. S.; Monpara, B. A. (2018). GJG 6: A high yielding wilt resistant chickpea variety for conserved moisture condition of Gujarat. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding 9(4): 1552-1556 -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2018.00192.8
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2025). Impact of frontline demonstrations of chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) improved variety GJG-6 on yield in Porbandar district of Gujarat. Plant Archives 25 (Supplement 1): 354 -- https://doi.org/10.51470/PLANTARCHIVES.2025.v25.supplement-1.354
ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea (2021-22) Progress report, Pulses Research Station, Junagadh entry for GJG 6. Report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
JAU (undated). Pulses crops variety document, GJG 6 entry (Sr. 5.3). Report -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
No KrishiKosh thesis or peer-reviewed multi-location trial paper naming GJG 6 was found in these results.

SEED AVAILABILITY
JAU Pulses Research Station lists GJG 6 among its released chickpea varieties and says it produces nucleus and breeder seed of chickpea; a breeder-seed table includes a GJG 6 column -- http://www.jau.in/index.php/resources/research-stations-top/south-saurashtra/pulses-research-station-junagadh
Private dealer listing: Gujarat Junagadh Chickpea 6 premium seed, 10 kg pack, sold by Krushisharang Agriclinic Pvt Ltd, Timbawadi, Junagadh (listing price INR 850) -- https://www.tradeindia.com/products/gujarat-junagadh-chickpea-6-premium-seeds-c10007890.html
Private seller listing: Fule Seeds, 10 kg pack -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-junagadh-gram-6-gjg-6/
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing with contact details was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Gujarat (DPD list, JAU document, Javia et al. 2018) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf ; https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
Gujarat, rainfed under conserved soil moisture (Javia et al. 2018) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2018.00192.8

disease_resistance.research_summary: Wilt: described as wilt-resistant (Javia et al. 2018; the paper title also uses 'wilt resistant'), and as listed tolerant to wilt (DPD central/state list). The JAU variety document and the ICAR-AICRP chickpea report 2021-22 both rate it moderately resistant to wilt. The sources conflict; the JAU and ICAR ratings are the more specific official classifications. Stunt: good resistance (Javia et al. 2018); tolerant to stunt (DPD list); moderately resistant (JAU variety document and ICAR-AICRP 2021-22). Ascochyta blight: moderately resistant (JAU variety document). Fule Seeds (commercial source, not official) lists resistance to wilt and stunt.

agronomic_details.yield: Record average yield: 3500.00 to 4000.00 Kg/Ha. HAU leaflet: average 10.67 q/acre, potential 16.67 q/acre. Paper: 26.69 q/ha in one section and an average of 26.00 q/ha in another; 21.4% above HC 1 and 28.7% above HC 5; 34.12% over HC 1 (19.90 q/ha); 16.5% over DCP 92-3; 9.0% over GNG 469. Rabi 2018-19 OFT: 19.55 q/ha versus 16.68 q/ha for HC 1 (17.26% higher).
agronomic_details.stability: Multi-location trial: highest yield of 4167 kg/ha at Hisar, followed by 3327 kg/ha at Sriganganagar. Consistent yield above 2.5 t/ha over 13 years at Hisar and 5 years at RRS Bawal. Suitable for timely and late sown conditions in Haryana (paper title and sowing window data).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Record: 'WHOLE OF STATE UNDER DIFFERENT SOILS.' Digest sowing window: timely sowing late October to late November in plain areas of Haryana (HAU leaflet); paper gives October 25 to November 20 for timely sowing and November 21 to December 10 for late sowing. Digest does not provide soil-type evidence beyond the record statement.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: EARLY 2-3 WEEKS THAN EXISTING VARIETIES. HAU leaflet: about 147 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: FOLIAGE COLOURS LIGHT GREEN, NO PIGMENTATION ON STEM OR LEAF AXIL. IN CHLOROSIS (YELLOWING OF GROWING AFTER IRRIGATION) ABSENT. ITS DWARF LONG PRIMARY BRANCHES GROWING SIDE WAYS AND SHORT SECONDARY BRANCHES. SEEDS YELLOW WITH CHALAZAL BEAK LONGER THAN OTHERS. F61-DESI, ERECT, HEAVY LATERAL ORDER BRANCHES, GREEN STEM, YELLOW SEED, WILT TOLERANT, L550 = KABULI, LONG PRIMARY BRANCHES WIDELY ADAPTED. SEEDS SALMON, MEDIUM SIZE. [Digest additions: plant type profuse, spreading branching (paper). Seed medium, about 17.0 g per 100 seeds, yellow-brown, protein about 21.76% (HAU leaflet). Note: seed colour in digest (yellow-brown) and record (salmon, yellow) differ; the digest does not resolve this.]
agronomic_details.field_trials: Multi-location trial: highest yield 4167 kg/ha at Hisar and 3327 kg/ha at Sriganganagar; consistent yield above 2.5 t/ha over 13 years at Hisar and 5 years at RRS Bawal. Rabi 2018-19 OFT: 19.55 q/ha versus 16.68 q/ha for HC 1 (17.26% higher). On-farm trials at Sirsa in Rabi 2018-19 and 2019-20 against HC 1 (results not given in the digest). Comparative yields: 21.4% above HC 1 and 28.7% above HC 5; 34.12% over HC 1 (19.90 q/ha); 16.5% over DCP 92-3 and 9.0% over GNG 469.
