disease_resistance.research_summary: Fusarium wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. ciceri): the HAU leaflet states the variety is resistant to wilt disease. The HC 6 paper reports about 8.3% wilt infection and describes this as high resistance. Collar rot and Ascochyta blight: the paper attributes these resistances to the male parent H 00-256, not to HC 6 directly, so they are not recorded here as resistances of HC 6. The DPD table row 'Haryana Chana' (2019, CCS HAU, tolerant to Helicoverpa armigera) was discarded because it is a generic name with a different release year (2019 versus 2022) and is not confirmed as HC 6. Record field 'disease_reaction' is 'Not Specified'.

seednet_fields.Parentage: ICCV 88506 x ICCV 90201	 ICCV 88506: Cold tolerant genotype ICCV 90201 (Himachal Channa II): High yielding, early maturing and Ascochyta blight resistant variety released for Himchal Pradesh.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: It is proposed for cultivation Zone I i.e. Sub mountain low hills, sub tropical zone of Himchal Pradesh and Zone II mid hill conditions..
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Grain yield in variety DKG 986 is significantly affected by sowing dates. D1 (DOS= 7th Nov) recorded the highest yield of 2564 kg/ha which was statistically superior to yield at D2 (1898 kg/ha) and D3 (16.15q/ha 1615 kg/ha). Fertility levels also influenced the yield and F2 (100& RD) produced the highest yield of F3 (2064 kg/ha). The interaction of sowing dates x fertility levels disi not affected the yield.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: (i)Plant Height – 52.3 cm (ii)Flower colour – Pink (iii)	No. Of primary branches – 3.6 (iv)	No of pods.plant- 55.6 (v)	No of seeds/pod – 2 (vi)	100 seed wt.- 12.6 gm (vii)	Days to 50% flowering – 105.3 days (98 – 117 days) (viii)	Days to 75% maturity – 151 days (141 – 160 days).
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: It is resistant to ascochyta blight and toerant to wilt and root rot, stem rot and rust. In coordinated trials, it showed 58.5% mean wilt incidence as compared with 81.1% in susceptible check, at hot spot locations. It was less at various locations in north India. It showed 27.1% incidence of dry root which is less than the susceptible check JG 62 (71.5%) and national varietal check GNG 1581 and at par with GNG 469. Similarly, it developed collar rot less than the susceptible. Based on the dats of various locations the variety developed the least Ascochyta blight (DR=4) and Botrytis grey mould (DR= 6.8) on 1-9 scale.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: It is early maturity variety and escpes the attack of pod borer. At KVK, Sundernagar, it showed pod borer infestation at par with the released varieties. Still prophylactic sprays of insecticides at 50% flowering stage are beneficial for managing pod borer attack.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Di – Ammonium Phosphate @ 100 kg per hectar at the time time of sowing. 20 kg Sulphur/ha ensures better crop yields.

seednet_fields.Parentage: 1.	{(RSG 533 x BG 391) x (ICCC 42 x ICC 106)}. 2.	RSG 533: Small seeded, tolerant to dry rot. 3.	BG391: Large seeded, dark foliage, moderately resistant to fusarium wilt. 4.	ICCC42: Large seeded, drought tolerant, early. 5.	ICC106: Small seeded and profuse poding.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Chickpea growing areas of Uttar Pradesh especially to the Central, Western and Bundelkhand region.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: @100kg DAP and @25kg Sulfur/ha besides Zinc and Molybdenum suitable for late sown condition with seed rate of 70-75 kg/ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Medium tall and semi-erect growth habit, medium green foliage, medium seed size with light brownish seed and moderately resistant to wilt.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Moderately resistant to wilt.
seednet_fields.Average Yield (Kg/Ha): Rainfed: 6-7 quintal acre. Irriagted: 708 quintal acre. Kg/Ha
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Di-Ammonium Phosphate @ 100 kg per hectare at the time of sowing. 20 Sulphur/ha ensure better crop yields.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SEARCHES RUN: 4 (variety/release; breeder/institute; research papers; seed availability). Name used: CSC name "IPC 2005-62"; Seednet name "IPC 2005-62 (Desi)". The Seednet portal itself was not retrieved. The Seednet-style name appears only in a DPD table that cites seednet.gov.in, so those items are tagged accordingly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Wilt: the institute's variety page reports resistance to wilt for IPC 2005-62 (Desi type), with the wording "Resistance to wilt" -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/ and https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
Wilt (conflicting rating): the DPD central release list describes IPC 2005-62 (Desi) as moderately resistant to wilt, which differs from the institute's "resistance" wording -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf (name evidence: "IPC 2005-62 (Desi)")
Drought: No evidence found for IPC 2005-62 specifically. Drought-tolerance results in the search (the DCP 92-3 drought-tolerant introgression line IPC L 4-14, and the ICC 4958 x DCP 92-3 QTL work) concern other genotypes and were discarded -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found. The heat-QTL paper (DCP 92-3 x ICCV 92944) and the salinity paper (ICCV 2 x JG 62 progenies) concern other genotypes and were discarded -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4121
Stress note: the institute's variety-page wording describes the variety as "irrigated and late sown" suitable -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/ (name evidence: "IPC 2005-62 (Desi type)")

DISEASE AND PEST
Wilt: see the STRESS TOLERANCE entries above (the wilt rating is the only disease evidence for this variety).
Pod borer: A DPD table entry reading "At par with other varieties when compared for damage due to gram pod borer" appears in the same row block as IPC 2005-62, but the snippet is fragmented, so it cannot be confirmed that it refers to this variety -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Other diseases (root rot, Botrytis grey mould, stunt, collar rot): No evidence found for IPC 2005-62 specifically.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Potential yield: 18-20 q/ha -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/ (name evidence: "IPC 2005-62 (Desi type)")
Duration: 120-125 days -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/ (name evidence: "IPC 2005-62 (Desi type)")
Duration and yield (alternate listing, 14-15 q/ha and 106-125 days, DPD table): https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf (name evidence: "IPC 2005-62 (Desi)")
Plant type: medium, semi-erect growth with green foliage and yellow cotyledons, and small seed (15.2 g per 100 seeds) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/ (attribution to this variety is inferred from the adjacent name in the page section; not fully confirmed)
Seed size and colour: light brown seed, small seed size 15.2 g/100 seed weight -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/new-varieties/ (name evidence: "IPC 2005-62 (High Protein)")
Field trial data: No evidence found. A multi-location trial figure of 1018 kg/ha appears on an ICAR page, but it sits in a jumbled listing with other varieties and is not reliably attributed -- https://icar.org.in/en/crop-science/groundnut
Seed-physical study: the 2023 Journal of Food Legumes paper measured IPC-05-62 grain dimensions and bulk properties (name written as "IPC-05-62") -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/35/30/67 (identity with IPC 2005-62 not confirmed by the page)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: DCP 92-3 x T 39-1 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf (name evidence: "IPC 2005-62")
Parent descriptions: The DCP 92-3 and T 39-1 descriptions in the input record were supplied by the user and were not verified by search.
Biofortification: the institute homepage lists this variety among its biofortified chickpea varieties -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/ (name evidence: "IPC 2005-62")
Breeding method: No evidence found (pedigree or single-seed-descent details were not located).
Breeding-line code: No evidence found beyond the variety designation IPC 2005-62.

disease_resistance.research_summary: Wilt: The institute variety page reports resistance to wilt for IPC 2005-62 (Desi type) using the wording Resistance to wilt. The DPD central release list describes IPC 2005-62 (Desi) as moderately resistant to wilt, which conflicts with the institute wording. The input record also states moderately resistant to wilt (AIRCP trials). Root rot, Botrytis grey mould, stunt and collar rot: Not found in searched sources for this variety.

drought.details: No variety-specific drought tolerance evidence found in the digest. The IIPR technology sheet describes the variety as suited to irrigated and late-sown conditions, which is an ecology statement and not a drought-tolerance finding.

heat.details: Named among heat-tolerant, short-duration chickpea varieties in a conference abstract, but no trial data are shown there. In a 3-year heat-stress trial (26 lines, three checks, 2017-2020, delayed vs timely sowing), the variety was an above-average yielder with lower stability across environments, and it was among the checks that performed relatively stably. The level is rated medium because the only quantitative evidence is mixed (high mean yield, lower stability) and the conference mention has no data.

salinity.details: Salinity tolerance: no evidence found.

flood.details: Flood tolerance: no evidence found.

Dry root rot (DRR): moderately tolerant / moderately resistant (IIPR technology sheet; DPD sheet lists moderate resistance). Stunt: moderately tolerant / moderately resistant (IIPR technology sheet; DPD sheet). Collar rot: tolerant (IIPR technology sheet and IIPR varieties page). Botrytis grey mould (BGM): Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Pod-borer and other insect/pest responses specific to this variety: Not found in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Potential yield 20-25 q/ha (IIPR technology sheet). DPD sheet gives 20-21 q/ha. Units as reported by the sources (quintals per hectare).
agronomic_details.stability: Lower stability across environments in the 3-year heat-stress trial (see stress_tolerance.heat). Variety-specific multi-location AICRP means: Not found in searched sources (table garbled).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Central Zone; irrigated and late-sown ecology (IIPR technology sheet). DPD sheet recommends later-sown cultivation in the rice-fallow system in CG, MP, GJ and Bundelkhand UP, and states suitability for CG, MP, GJ and BK-UP.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Duration 115-120 days (IIPR technology sheet); 112-115 days (DPD sheet).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Seed size 16.5 g/100 seed; light brown/yellowish seed; protein content above 24% (IIPR technology sheet). Plant architecture and morphology: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Heat-stress field study, 2017-2020, delayed vs timely sowing: 3-year trial of 26 lines with three checks; the variety was an above-average yielder with lower stability across environments and was among the relatively stable checks. (2) Herbicide-tolerance field study: positive yield and yield-attribute response under herbicide treatment; among herbicide-tolerant germplasm it gave the most consistent yield gains under herbicide treatment. (3) AICRP multi-location trials: no variety-specific mean found (table garbled). (4) IIPR economic impact study: expected adoption estimated at 5% (breeder opinion and DAC indent).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: IPC 2006-77 (Chickpea, desi)

Name check: "variety_name" and "seednet_variety_name" are both "IPC 2006-77". No Seednet portal page was retrieved, so every finding below refers to the name IPC 2006-77 as used by ICAR-IIPR, DPD, AICRP and journal sources. Variety code A0302306 did not appear in any result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to wilt, moderately tolerant of dry root rot (DRR), stunt and collar rot; described as suited to irrigated and late-sown conditions. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/
- Listed as moderately resistant to wilt, DRR and stunt, with a later-sown recommendation for the rice-fallow system in CG, MP, GJ and Bundelkhand UP. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Named among heat-tolerant, short-duration chickpea varieties in a conference abstract, with no trial data shown. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371349379_Including_Visual_Sessions_from_ICAR-Indian_Institute_of_Sugarcane_Research
- In a 3-year heat-stress trial (26 lines, three checks), it was an above-average yielder with lower stability across environments, and it was among the checks that performed relatively stably. -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-07573-7
- Among herbicide-tolerant germplasm, it gave the most consistent yield gains under herbicide treatment. -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/10/6
- Drought tolerance: no variety-specific evidence found.
- Salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: no evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Wilt resistance and moderate DRR, stunt and collar-rot tolerance are listed in the IIPR technology sheet. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/
- Wilt resistance and tolerance to stunt and collar rot are also listed on the IIPR varieties page. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- Pod-borer, Botrytis grey mould (BGM) and insect/pest responses specific to this variety: no evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Potential yield 20-25 q/ha; duration 115-120 days; recommended area Central Zone; irrigated and late-sown ecology. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/
- DPD sheet gives yield 20-21 q/ha, duration 112-115 days, and states it is suitable for CG, MP, GJ and BK-UP. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Seed size 16.5 g/100 seed; light brown/yellowish seed; protein content above 24%. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/
- Listed as 2019 release by the CVRC in AICRP chickpea data (variety row in the 2021-22 report shows release, not trial means). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Herbicide-tolerance field study: positive yield and yield-attribute response under herbicide treatment. -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/10/6
- Heat-stress field study (2017-2020, delayed sowing vs timely sowing) with this variety as a check. -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-07573-7
- IIPR economic impact study: expected adoption estimated at 5% for IPC 2006-77 (breeder opinion and DAC indent). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/research-achievements/ (via translate.goog mirror: https://www-icar--iipr-org-in.translate.goog/research-achievements/?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc)
- Yield under AICRP multi-location trials: no variety-specific mean found in retrieved text (the table was garbled).

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: no reliable evidence found. The AICRP table rows for this variety are garbled and cannot be matched to it. The "parentage: Not specified" entry is unchanged.
- Breeding-line code / pedigree name: no evidence found beyond the variety name.
- Breeding method: no evidence found.
- QTL/marker studies specific to this variety: no evidence found. The InDel primers for the chickpea QTL hotspot are from the IIPR wild-type/recurrent-parent study and are not tied to this variety. -- https://www-icar--iipr-org-in.translate.goog/research-achievements/?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc (discarded as not variety-specific)
- Genome resources for this variety: no evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ICAR-IIPR, Kanpur; Division of Crop Improvement; year of release 2019 (CVRC). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/ and https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/

disease_resistance.research_summary: Wilt: resistant (listed in the IIPR technology sheet and the IIPR varieties page). Dry root rot (DRR): moderately tolerant / moderately resistant (IIPR technology sheet; DPD sheet lists moderate resistance). Stunt: moderately tolerant / moderately resistant (IIPR technology sheet; DPD sheet). Collar rot: tolerant (IIPR technology sheet and IIPR varieties page). Botrytis grey mould (BGM): Not found in searched sources.

drought.details: The IIPR variety page describes IPC 2011-112 (Keshav) as tolerant to moisture stress and lodging. A 2023 ICPulses abstract on drought tolerance indices in chickpea breeding lists IPC 2011-112 and DCP 92-3 as poor performers in the stress context reported in the truncated snippet, so drought performance is inconsistent across sources and the level is rated medium with low confidence. No QTL or physiological mechanism is reported in the search results.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat tolerance data for IPC 2011-112 were found in the search results. The ICAR Annual Report 2020 refers to heat stress tolerance in other germplasm (e.g., IC0635020) and does not attribute it to this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Fusarium wilt: resistant. Listed as resistant to wilt in the global-agriculture record and in the AICRP product-profile table. The CSC release record (ground truth, no URL in digest) states resistant reaction at three locations in CZ, moderately resistant at one location each in CZ and NEPZ. Dry root rot: moderately resistant per the CSC release record (moderately resistant at three locations in CZ, resistant at one location in ZA). The digest did not find a dry root rot reaction for this variety in its own searches, so this CSC-only entry is uncorroborated by the searched sources. Stunt and collar rot: Not found in searched sources. The IARI best-practice PDF ratings were excluded because they refer to a breeding context and not explicitly to this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: Helicoverpa armigera: field tolerance is recorded in the CSC release record (ground truth, no URL in digest). The level of tolerance is not specified. The digest's own searches returned no pest reaction data for this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 16.0 q/ha; potential yield 25.65 q/ha (CSC record). The digest also cites 16 q/ha from the global-agriculture and AICRP sources. Organic-production trial seed yield was 1593 kg/ha (about 15.9 q/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: The multi-location stability study (Rabi 2020-21, three Chhattisgarh sites) reports genotype means, with Indira Chana-1 as a check. No Indira Chana-1-specific stability ranking or stability statistic was found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Chhattisgarh; rainfed and irrigated conditions; rice-based cropping system (multi-season and line x tester trials in Chhattisgarh). Other agro-climatic zones are not documented beyond the stability study's three Chhattisgarh sites.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 109 days (CSC record). The global-agriculture and AICRP sources give a range of 101-116 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Erect plant type with more primary branches (global-agriculture record). Morphological characteristics beyond this were not found.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-season trial in Chhattisgarh rice-based system: Indira Chana-1 was among 11 genotypes; one-season results reported for pod number, seed number and 100-seed weight. Specific values not stated in the digest. (2) Organic-production trial: seed yield 1593 kg/ha, harvest index about 21.6%, highest protein content among tested cultivars. (3) Earlier trial (2019): significantly higher seed yield, stover yield and harvest index than the check Vaibhav. (4) Multi-location trial (Rabi 2020-21, three Chhattisgarh sites, stability analysis): used as a check; genotype means reported, specific values not in digest. (5) Weed management trial at IGKVV Raipur (2020-22) using seed of Indira chana-1 at 80 kg/ha; no yield result stated in digest. (6) Seed bio-priming study (2018-2019 seasons) reporting growth and yield-component gains; the digest gives no specific values.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Indira Chana-1 (chickpea, variety code A0302283)

Name check: The CSC release name ("Indira Chana-1") and the Seednet name are identical. Search results used spelling variants ("Indira Chana 1", "Indira chana-1", "Indira Chana - 1"). All evidence below refers to this variety. Seednet itself was not returned by any search, so its record could not be checked directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Recorded as rainfed and irrigated suitability, with an erect plant type and more primary branches; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found for this variety -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-indira-chana-1/
Listed as suitable for both rainfed and irrigated conditions in the AICRP product-profile table -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Listed as resistant to wilt -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-indira-chana-1/
Listed as resistant to wilt in the AICRP product-profile table -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Other disease reactions (stunt, dry root rot, collar rot) were not found for this variety. The IARI best-practice PDF has disease ratings, but they refer to a breeding context and not explicitly to Indira Chana-1, so I excluded them -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Release year 2017 (SVRC); yield 16 q/ha; maturity 101-116 days; rainfed and irrigated -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-indira-chana-1/ ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Multi-season trial in Chhattisgarh rice-based system: Indira Chana-1 was among 11 genotypes; one-season results reported for pod number, seed number and 100-seed weight -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue11/PartI/12-10-48-506.pdf
Organic-production trial: seed yield of 1593 kg/ha, harvest index about 21.6%, highest protein content among tested cultivars -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue9/PartE/12-8-480-502.pdf
Earlier trial (2019): Indira Chana-1 gave significantly higher seed yield, stover yield and harvest index than the check Vaibhav -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue10/PartB/8-9-110-825.pdf
Multi-location trial (Rabi 2020-21, three Chhattisgarh sites, stability analysis): Indira Chana-1 was a check; genotype means reported -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/395653070_Evaluating_Stability_of_Chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_Genotypes_across_Diverse_Agro-climatic_Zones_in_Chhattisgarh_Using_Different_Stability_Models
Weed management trial at IGKVV Raipur (2020-22) using seed of Indira chana-1 at 80 kg/ha -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/5845/5215
Seed bio-priming study (2018-2019 seasons) reporting growth and yield-component gains -- https://thepharmajournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=21663&issue=7&vol=12&year=2023

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: JG 74 x ICCL 83105 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf ; https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2019/vol7issue5/PartBF/7-5-128-166.pdf
Breeding-line code, breeding method, genes, QTL and genome resources: No evidence found in any search.
The ResearchGate line × tester study uses Indira Chana-1 as a parent line and check, but it does not state a breeding-line code or method for this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324440661_Genetics_Analysis_of_Yield_and_Quality_Characters_in_Chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_under_Rice_Based_Cropping_System

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Originating centre: IGKVV (Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya), Raipur -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf ; https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-indira-chana-1/
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The breeder-query search returned no named breeder for this variety. A chickpea scientist at IARI (Chellapilla Bharadwaj) appeared in results, but he is not linked to this variety, so he is excluded -- https://gfm.akshayakalpa.org/read/feature-article/chellapilla-bharadwaj-chickpea-chana-research-protein-genetic-diversity-climate-resilience
Station/division within IGKVV: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS

IGKVV institute-level contact: No evidence found in the retrieved results; the research farm is named as the Instructional-cum-Research farm, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, IGKVV, Raipur -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324440661_Genetics_Analysis_of_Yield_and_Quality_Characters_in_Chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_under_Rice_Based_Cropping_System

disease_resistance.research_summary: Fusarium wilt: resistant. Listed as resistant to wilt in the global-agriculture record and in the AICRP product-profile table. The CSC release record (ground truth, no URL in digest) states resistant reaction at three locations in CZ, moderately resistant at one location each in CZ and NEPZ. Dry root rot: moderately resistant per the CSC release record (moderately resistant at three locations in CZ, resistant at one location in ZA). The digest did not find a dry root rot reaction for this variety in its own searches, so this CSC-only entry is uncorroborated by the searched sources. Stunt and collar rot: Not found in searched sources. The IARI best-practice PDF ratings were excluded because they refer to a breeding context and not explicitly to this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Name: JG-12 (variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical). Listed as moderately resistant to wilt and dry root rot, under normal-sown conditions -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Mention of JG-12 as a moderately resistant line in the ICAR-IIPR AICRP report was garbled in the extract, so it is not cited -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence specific to JG-12 was found in the search results.

DISEASE AND PEST
Name: JG-12. Moderately resistant to wilt and dry root rot -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
No insect or pest resistance evidence found for JG-12.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Name: JG-12. Average yield 18-20 q/ha, maturity about 120 days, normal-sown conditions, JNKVV Jabalpur, released 2014 -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
JG-12 was used as a check among 40 desi advanced lines grown at the JNKVV Seed Breeding Farm (trial year and yield values not stated in the extract) -- https://journalijpss.com/index.php/IJPSS/article/download/3320/6621/5786
No multi-location or AICRP yield data specific to JG-12 was found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Name: JG-12. No QTL, marker or genomic study specific to JG-12 was found. Parentage "(Narsinghpur bold x PG 5) x PG 5" was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Name: JG-12. Institution: Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, JNKVV, Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Lead breeder for JG-12: No evidence found. Dr. Anita Babbar, Principal Scientist at JNKVV, is named as developer of JG 18 (not JG-12), so she is not attributed here -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/women-scientists-create-top-3-climate-smart-chickpea-varieties-in-india-for-2022
Station: JNKVV Seed Breeding Farm, Jabalpur, is where the JG-12 check trial was run -- https://journalijpss.com/index.php/IJPSS/article/download/3320/6621/5786

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder: No evidence found.
Institute-level (JNKVV Directorate of Farms, which handles breeder seed production): Email seeds.jnkvv@gmail.com; Mobile 8770867088 -- https://www.jnkvv.org/about-directorate-details/directorate-of-farms
Postal address of the Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics or the Directorate: No evidence found in the search results.

PUBLICATIONS
Patel T., Prajapati S.S. (year not stated). Diversity/trait study of 40 advanced desi chickpea lines at JNKVV, with JG 12 as a check. Journal not stated (journalijpss.com) -- https://journalijpss.com/index.php/IJPSS/article/download/3320/6621/5786
ICAR-IIPR (2021-22). All India Coordinated Research Project on Chickpea, annual report, varietal table listing JG 12 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Dept. of Pulses/DPD. Central released chickpea varieties list, including JG 12 (2014, JNKVV) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
KrishiKosh: no JG-12-specific thesis was found. Theses retrieved (Sarika 2013; Patil 2015) do not mention JG-12 in the extracted text.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Name: JG-12. JNKVV Directorate of Farms is responsible for breeder seed production under the national seed program -- https://www.jnkvv.org/about-directorate-details/directorate-of-farms
Contact for seed enquiries: seeds.jnkvv@gmail.com, 8770867088 (same source).
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sale or private dealer listing for JG-12 was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JG 36 (Jawahar Gram 36), chickpea

Name note: The searches used "JG 36" and "Jawahar Gram 36" (the CSC name). The Seednet name "JG-6" was not searched on its own, so no Seednet portal page was retrieved. Any JG-6 evidence below would need a separate check. Every finding below refers to JG 36 / Jawahar Gram 36.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Tolerant to wilt. Only wilt tolerance is named for this variety; drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance were not found for JG 36. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-jg-36-jawahar-gram-36/
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to JG 36. The search returned a Dhuria and Babbar heat-stress study, but it covers 68 kabuli lines, not JG 36, so it was discarded. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4064

DISEASE AND PEST
- Wilt tolerance is the only disease trait recorded for JG 36 (same source as above). -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-jg-36-jawahar-gram-36/
- No evidence found for root rot, dry root rot, BGM, pod borer or other pest resistance specific to JG 36. -- searched under the general variety query; no JG 36 page carried this information.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release year 2016 (SVRC), originating centre JNKVV Jabalpur, yield 18-20 q/ha, 110-120 days to maturity, semi-spreading plant with dark brown seed, suitable for rainfed and irrigated conditions. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-jg-36-jawahar-gram-36/ ; also https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The ICAR-AICRP chickpea report 2021-22 lists JG 36 with the same release year, JNKVV origin, 18-20 q/ha, 110-120 days, and dark brown seed. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- JG 36 was one of the entries in a 30-line desi chickpea evaluation at the JNKVV seed breeding farm, Jabalpur, in rabi 2019-20 and 2020-21. The paper compares JG 36 with other lines for seed size and pod traits. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue12/PartAH/10-12-209-279.pdf
- JG 36 was a check variety in a 2007 characterisation of 40 advanced desi lines at the JNKVV seed breeding farm. -- https://journalijpss.com/index.php/IJPSS/article/download/3320/6621/5786
- No evidence found for multi-location or AICRP yield trial results specific to JG 36. -- the trial and report pages retrieved did not give JG 36 multi-location data.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL, marker or pedigree study naming JG 36 was returned. The AICRP report shows a truncated parentage fragment, "JG 12 x JG ...", which is incomplete and not confirmed as JG 36's full parentage. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: JNKVV, Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh (originating centre). -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-jg-36-jawahar-gram-36/
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. No page names the breeder of JG 36.

- Institute: Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (JNKVV), Jabalpur. Website: https://www.jnkvv.org/ . The page retrieved gave no postal address, phone number or contact email for the Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics or the chickpea programme. -- https://www.jnkvv.org/
- Breeder name, email and phone for JG 36: No evidence found.
- Not attributed: An email (anitababbarjnkvv@gmail.com) appears on a 2014-15 kabuli-line paper by Dhuria and Babbar. It is an author contact for a different study and is not confirmed as a contact for JG 36, so it is excluded. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4064

seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
1.	Reaction to Major diseases
Disease score of proposed entry JG 2017-32 (ICC 16303) in PYT’s for Fusarium wilt (0.00). Collar rot (3.40) and Dry root rot (6.90) in Advance varietal trial on 2015-16 at ICRISAT recorded disease score of Fusarium wilt (2.90%), collar rot (0.00%) and Dry root rot (17.10%)-(Table 17 and ICRISAT Report Pathology 2015-16)
2.	Reaction to Major Diseases in coordinated Trail
Proposed entry JGK2017 – 32 showed resistance against Fusarium wilt and Dry root rot over years and locations. Moderate resistance found for Ascochyta blight and Stunt diseases in few locations over years.
3.	Reaction to major diseases under field conditions:
Fusarium wilt: In AVT 2(K+ELSK) trial this entry showed resistant at 1 location and moderate resistant at 1 location out of 12 locations during 2019-29
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: The proposed entry JGK2017- 32 was found superior over check variety Phule G 0517(Ch) at Hisar, Sriganganagar, Ludhiana and Pantnagar centers to record the lower percent of larval population of H. armigera during 2018-19.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Gram Kabuli 6 (seednet name: Jawhar Gram Kabuli-1; code JGK 6 / JGK 2017-32), chickpea (Kabuli)

Searches run: 4 (variety and crop; breeder and institute; research; seed availability). No search returned a page that names this variety under either name. Every result was about another variety, another crop, or an unrelated product, and all were discarded under the strict relevance rule.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The variety search returned only a general chickpea variety list (dpd.gov.in) with a Kabuli entry for "Jawahar Gram-" (JNKVV, Madhya Pradesh). That is a different name and was not attributed to this variety. -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The same dpd.gov.in list mentions wilt and Botrytis grey mould resistance for a Kabuli entry, but the page does not name this variety, so it was discarded. -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Search returned no multi-location or agronomic data for JGK 6 or Jawhar Gram Kabuli-1.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Search returned no QTL or marker study naming this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. The breeder search returned only ICRISAT's Kabuli variety ICCV 6, a different variety, which was discarded. No breeder name or developing station was found for this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute, or contact page for this variety was returned. Note for verification: the variety record lists "Jawahar Lal Nehru Vishwavidyalaya". The chickpea breeding university commonly associated with the Jawahar Gram varieties is Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (JNKVV), Jabalpur. This is my own background knowledge, not a search finding, and the institution name should be checked against the CSC minutes before any contact is recorded.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The research search returned a 2020 Scientific Reports metabolomic study of desi and kabuli chickpea genotypes (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-020-70963-6). It does not name JGK 6 or Jawhar Gram Kabuli-1 in the retrieved text, so it was excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed search returned only a private dealer listing for Gujarat Kabuli Gram 1 (GKG 1), a different variety (https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-kabuli-gram-1-sorath-kabuli-1-gkg-1/). It was excluded. No Seednet, NSC, state corporation, KVK or SAU listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found in the search results. The states in the variety record (Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jammu and Kashmir) are unverified; they come only from the input record.

Suggested next steps: check the Seednet entry directly for JGK 6 / Jawhar Gram Kabuli-1 (seednet.gov.in), search the ICAR/AICRP chickpea annual reports and KrishiKosh by the code "JGK 2017-32", and confirm the developing institution against the CSC release notification.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Wilt resistance is listed for HK 4 (HK 05-169) in the DPD recommended-varieties table, where the entry is noted as resistant to wilt and bold seeded. The name used in the source is "HK 4 (HK 05-169)" -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- A second DPD release table gives HK-4 a "moderately" resistance reaction, but the text is truncated, so the disease being referenced cannot be confirmed -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to HK-4. Searches returned only general chickpea or other-variety pages (e.g., HC-6 and HC-1, which were discarded as different varieties).

DISEASE AND PEST
- Wilt resistance and the moderate-resistance entry are recorded above. No evidence found for pod borer, Helicoverpa, or other pest resistance specific to HK-4.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The DPD table lists HK-4 with a 2012 release, Hisar origin, 16-17 q/ha yield, 125-130 days maturity, NEPZ area, and irrigated condition -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- A different DPD table gives 15.00 q/ha and 136 days for HK 4 (HK 05-169) at CCSHAU, 2012, NEPZ. The two tables disagree on yield and maturity; both are recorded -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Seed size is recorded as 28.4 g/100 seeds, and the seed is described as white in colour -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea.pdf and https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- ICAR-IIPR AICRP chickpea report 2021-22 has a release-table row for HK 05-169 (HK 4) with 28.4 g/100 seeds and a 2012 Hisar release; the row is partly garbled -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No field-trial or multi-location yield results specific to HK-4 were found beyond the release-table entries.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Breeding-line code: HK 05-169 (also written HK 4 or HK-4) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Parentage: the AICRP report release row shows "HK 92-94" next to the HK 05-169 entry, but the HK-1 part of the cross is not legible. The user-supplied parentage "HK 92-94 X HK-1" is therefore not independently confirmed -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Breeding method: No evidence found.
- QTL, markers, and genome resources: No evidence found for HK-4.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar, recorded as the originating centre -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. The search returned breeder pages for other varieties (HC-6, Pulses Section work on HC-1/KC-1) and general biographies of unrelated scientists; these were excluded.
- Institute background: CCS HAU is a public agricultural university at Hisar, Haryana -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_agricultural_centres_established_by_CCS_HAU

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact, email, phone, or postal address for HK-4 was found in the search results.
- Institute-level: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar, Haryana, India, PIN 125004 (from an affiliation line in a CCS HAU-affiliated paper). No email or phone was found. Official institute contact page: No evidence found in results. Source for the affiliation line: https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0006200

PUBLICATIONS
- Dixit G. P., Srivastava A. K., Singh N. P. (2019). Marching towards self-sufficiency in chickpea. Current Science 116(2): 239. -- https://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/116/02/0239.pdf
  This review lists HK 05-169 among varieties developed for large-seeded kabuli preference. It is a review, not a trial report.
- No other peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report chapter, thesis (KrishiKosh), or conference paper specific to HK-4 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The Seednet portal was not reached, and no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing for HK-4 was returned. The seed-related results were unrelated retail listings (microgreens, pasta, US garden seeds) and were discarded.
- The ICAR-IIPR report notes breeder seed production for 65 chickpea varieties in 2021-22, but does not name HK-4 in that context -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The DPD table records NEPZ as the area of adoption for HK 4 (HK 05-169) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- A DPD state-code key in the same chickpea table lists AS (Assam), BH (Bihar) and JH (Jharkhand) against HK-4 -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Eastern Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal, the states in the user record, are not confirmed by the found evidence. A separate DPD state table lists HK-4 under Haryana, which conflicts with the NEPZ entry -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea.pdf
- Name note: Evidence refers to "HK 4 (HK 05-169)" and "HK-4". The Seednet portal page itself was not reached.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kota Kabuli Chana 4 (RKGK 13-416), chickpea

Name check: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name fields are identical ("Kota Kabuli Chana 4 (RKGK 13-416)"). The Seednet portal itself was not reachable, so the evidence below refers to that name as it appears in secondary and institutional sources. Four searches were run (variety, breeder/institution, research, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- No stress-tolerance evidence specific to RKGK 13-416 was found. The only tolerance-related text in the results concerns other Kota varieties (Kota Kabuli Channa-2, Kota Desi Chana 4), which I did not attribute to this line. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638699219886341753.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST:
- No disease or pest resistance evidence specific to RKGK 13-416 was found. The DPD list shows resistance ratings for other Kota entries only. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- The ICAR-IIPR AICRP Chickpea 2021-22 report lists "RKG 13-416" in a Southern Zone kabuli trial: AVT-2 yield 1723 kg/ha (3 locations), AVT-1 1662 and 1497 kg/ha, IVT 1608 kg/ha, weighted mean 1621 kg/ha over 13 entries. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Maturity, plant height and seed size for RKGK 13-416 were not found. -- No evidence found in the results.
- Notification record: released as an open-pollinated kabuli chickpea by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties; notified 25 September 2023. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/chickpea-variety-kota-kabuli-chana-4-rkgk-13-416/
- Release date mismatch: the input says 2023-05-02, the news item reports a notification date of 25 September 2023. Record both. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/chickpea-variety-kota-kabuli-chana-4-rkgk-13-416/

GENETICS AND QTL:
- No QTL, marker, or genomic study on RKGK 13-416 was found. -- No evidence found in the results.
- Parentage: the input gives BG 1044 x BG 1110. The ICAR-IIPR report gives BG 1044 x BG 1111 for the sister line Kota Kabuli Chana 3 (RKGK 13-414), not for 13-416. Verify 13-416's parentage against the CSC minutes before using it. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- The developing institution is Agriculture University (AU), Kota, Agricultural Research Station (ARS), Kota, Rajasthan. A news item lists it among three chickpea releases from AU Kota (with Kota Desi Chana 2 (RKGM 20-1) and Kota Desi Chana 3 (RKGM 20-2)). -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638699219886341753.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist names: none found in the results. -- No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS:
- No breeder names, emails, phone numbers, or postal address were found for AU Kota or its ARS. The only institutional reference was the AU Kota name in the release listings. -- No evidence found.
- Recommended next step: check the AU Kota website or the Kota ARS page directly (URL not confirmed by search).

PUBLICATIONS:
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, or conference paper on RKGK 13-416 was found. The results contained only unrelated chickpea papers from other countries. -- No evidence found.
- Institutional source (not a paper): ICAR-AICRP Chickpea Progress Report 2021-22, ICAR-IIPR. "Annual Progress Report, All India Coordinated Research Project on Chickpea, 2021-22." -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- No seed listing for RKGK 13-416 was found from the NSC, a State Seed Corporation, a KVK, SAU seed sales, or a private dealer. The results contained only consumer grain products (kabuli chana sold as food, not certified seed). -- No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka (for sale, per the CSC notification). -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/chickpea-variety-kota-kabuli-chana-4-rkgk-13-416/
- Conflict: the AU Kota news item recommends the line for production in the Kota division (Zone V, Rajasthan), which differs from the three-state notification. The notified recommendation should be treated as authoritative. -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638699219886341753.pdf

drought.details: No variety-specific drought data for Kripa were found. The only drought-tolerance mention in the central release list snippet appears next to a different entry (University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur) and cannot be attributed to Kripa. A general review notes chickpea has some tolerance to abiotic stress, including drought, but this is not specific to Kripa.

heat.details: No heat-tolerance data for Kripa were found. The heat-tolerant remark in the central release list refers to a different variety suited to late sowing in Madhya Pradesh. The kabuli ideotype review mentions Kripa only as a parent used in a study of flowering-time inheritance.

salinity.details: No evidence found.

flood.details: No evidence found.

disease_resistance.summary: The central release list records Kripa (Phule G 0517) as tolerant to Fusarium wilt and as an irrigated-condition variety. A journal article on Kripa (Phule G 0517) lists resistance and quality as keywords, but the specific diseases were not visible in the snippet.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance data specific to Kripa were found. A study used Kripa as one of four chickpea cultivars, with seed procured from the Pulses Improvement Project at Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth, in work on controlling Callosobruchus chinensis (a storage pest) with cold plasma. This does not establish resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: Central release list gives 18-19 q/ha (average yield).
agronomic_details.stability: No multi-environment stability data found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Released in 2009 by the Central Variety Release Committee for the Central Zone (Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh) under irrigated conditions. One source also lists Karnataka. A parliamentary document lists Kripa among chickpea varieties for Gujarat.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 110-115 days (central release list); this differs from the original data, which gives nan.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: SEMI SPREADING, BROAD LEAVES, EXTRA LARGE SEED SIZE (59.4G/100 SEEDS). Kabuli type. Reviews classify it among extra-large-seeded kabuli varieties (46-60 g per 100 seeds, or more than 50 g).
agronomic_details.field_trials: A journal article titled 'Kripa: An Extra Bold Kabuli Chickpea for Central and South Zone of India' describes Phule G 0517. The Rabi production plan lists Kripa and MNK 1 as extra-large kabuli varieties, with sowing from the first fortnight of November to the first fortnight of December.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No QTL, SNP or SSR information specific to Kripa was found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: None found. Kripa is mentioned as a parent in a cross used to study inheritance of flowering time (with ICC 17109), but no QTL details were available.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not reported. One abstract notes Kripa has high calcium content, and another reports a high value for a nutritional trait in Kripa (Phule G-0517). The underlying genes are not described.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance of L 558 itself. The PAU drought QTL paper concerns chickpea generally and does not name L 558 or L-550, so it cannot be used to rate this variety. No drought mechanisms were reported for L 558.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance of L 558 in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found under the CSC name L 558. Under the Seednet name L-550, a salinity study of seven desi and kabuli chickpea genotypes identified L550 (kabuli) and BG1053 as tolerant on the basis of physiological and biochemical parameters. The digest does not confirm that L-550 and L 558 are the same genotype, so this finding is not attributed to L 558 here. The level is therefore unknown.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance of L 558 in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources for wilt, Ascochyta blight or botrytis grey mould reaction of L 558. General PAU context only: 240 kabuli genotypes from different backgrounds and locations were screened under artificial epiphytotic conditions against Ascochyta blight during 2019-20 and 2020-21 at PAU, Ludhiana. The genotype list does not show L 558, so this screen provides no resistance rating for the variety.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources for pod borer reaction of L 558.

agronomic_details.yield: Not found in searched sources. The digest contains no yield data for L 558.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location trial results for L 558 were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended states per the original variety data: Punjab, Haryana, North Rajasthan and plains of Uttarakhand (standardized as Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand). The digest provides no independent agro-climatic evidence.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not available in provided image segment
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.field_trials: Trial evidence in the digest does not directly test L 558. (1) Under the Seednet name L-550, the 2002-harvest quality study used L-550 as a kabuli reference, and L-550 (kabuli type) had the highest fat content among the chickpea cultivars tested. (2) Under the Seednet name L-550, L-550 flour differed significantly from all other chickpea flours in water and oil absorption, gelation capacity and emulsification properties. (3) A seed-rate trial at Ludhiana in Northern India used GLK 21143, GLK 21159 and BG 1053, not L 558. (4) A 2024 PAU paper titled 'New Kabuli Chickpea variety L 558' is listed in a ResearchGate reference list, but no yield or maturity data was visible. (5) The Ascochyta blight screen at PAU, Ludhiana (2019-20 and 2020-21) covered 240 kabuli genotypes, but L 558 is not in the genotype list.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Under the Seednet name L-550, a salinity study on kabuli lines identified L550 as salt-tolerant, alongside BG1053, based on physiological and biochemical traits. Seven chickpea genotypes both desi and kabuli were evaluated for salinity tolerance, and on the basis of physiological and biochemical parameters, BG1053 and L550 from kabuli were identified as tolerant -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339343766_Desi_and_kabuli_chickpea_cultivars_had_differential_behaviour_towards_salinity_stress_tolerance
- Under the CSC name L 558: No evidence found. The drought QTL paper from PAU is about chickpea generally and does not name L 558 or L-550 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9437436/
- Under the CSC name L 558: No evidence found for heat, flood, submergence or drought tolerance of L 558 itself.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Under the CSC name L 558: No evidence found for wilt, Ascochyta blight, botrytis grey mould or pod borer reaction of L 558.
- General PAU context only: 240 kabuli genotypes from different backgrounds and locations were screened under artificial epiphytotic conditions against Ascochyta blight during 2019-20 and 2020-21 at PAU, Ludhiana -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393377730_Identification_of_Ascochyta_blight_resistant_sources_in_Kabuli_genotypes_of_chickpea_and_validation_of_identified_QTLs (the genotype list does not show L 558).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Under the Seednet name L-550: The 2002-harvest quality study used L-550 as a kabuli reference; L-550 (kabuli type) had the highest fat content among the chickpea cultivars tested -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0260877404004236
- Under the Seednet name L-550: L-550 flour differed significantly from all other chickpea flours with respect to its water and oil absorption, gelation capacity, and emulsification properties. -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0308814604004650
- Under the CSC name L 558: No evidence found for yield, maturity or multi-location trial results. The seed-rate trial at Ludhiana used GLK 21143, GLK 21159 and BG 1053, not L 558 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318518201_Growth_Productivity_and_Economics_of_Kabuli_Chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_Genotypes_in_Response_to_Seed_Rate_in_Northern_India
- Under the CSC name L 558: The 2024 PAU paper title listed in a ResearchGate reference list reads "New Kabuli Chickpea variety L 558", but no yield or maturity data was visible -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369334660_Chickpea_Variety_PBG8

GENETICS AND QTL
- Under the CSC name L 558: No evidence found for parentage-linked markers or QTLs specific to L 558. The stated parentage (PB.7 x Rabat) was not confirmed by any search result.
- General PAU context: Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana, Punjab, India is the source of the drought-QTL mapping work -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9437436/

drought.details: L 552 has been studied under water stress conditions. Its cultivation is recommended for rainfed areas, where conserving soil moisture is advised, implying an adaptation to less irrigated conditions. Research indicates that ACC-deaminase positive rhizobacteria can significantly improve germination, root and shoot length, and fresh weight of L 552 under water stress.

heat.details: General statements in publications about L 552's release for Punjab mention the development of chickpea genotypes tolerant to heat stress, suggesting L 552 is among varieties with this desirable trait. L 552 is noted to possess high total soluble sugar and total starch content, biochemical characteristics that can contribute to stress tolerance.

salinity.details: No information regarding salinity tolerance was found in the provided search results.

flood.details: L 552 was included in intercropping experiments where a 'water depth of 0.5 to 2 ft is constantly maintained with tap water'. However, this context does not explicitly state it as a flood tolerance assessment for L 552.

disease_resistance.summary: The provided search results do not attribute specific disease resistance directly to variety L 552. Mentions of resistance to diseases such as wilt, foot rot, root rot, Ascochyta blight, and white rust were associated with other chickpea varieties in the documents.

pest_resistance.summary: No information regarding pest resistance was found in the provided search results.

agronomic_details.yield: No specific quantitative yield data for L 552 was found in the provided search results. Yield figures mentioned in the documents were attributed to other varieties.
agronomic_details.stability: Recommended for cultivation in Punjab, with advisories from ICAR and Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) suggesting its suitability for rainfed areas, indicating its performance under varying moisture conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: L 552 is a Kabuli chickpea variety primarily released and recommended for the Punjab state in India. It is adapted to winter season cultivation, though severe cold and frost are detrimental to chickpea crops generally.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: L 552 is a Kabuli type chickpea with medium to very bold seeds, specifically noted to have seed weight of 33.6 g/100 seeds. It is characterized by high total soluble sugar and total starch content. It is described as an early maturing variety.
agronomic_details.field_trials: L 552 has been included in evaluations of physiological and biochemical contents, studies on the effects of rhizobacteria under water stress, and intercropping experiments.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers or QTLs for L 552 were identified in the provided search results.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs or their effects were identified for L 552.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: L 552 is characterized as a Kabuli genotype possessing high total soluble sugar and total starch content. Studies have also investigated the interaction of L 552 with ACC-deaminase positive rhizobacteria, which enhance germination and early growth under water stress, although this is an external biological interaction rather than an inherent molecular mechanism of the plant itself.

drought.details: The only MNK-1 drought-related evidence is farmer-preferred variety trial (FPVS) yields in Kurnool, Prakasam and Anantapur (mean 983 kg/ha) and a Karnataka FPVS note. Neither gives a drought-tolerance rating or mechanism, so no level is assigned. Release record states adaptation to normal sown rainfed as well as irrigated conditions, which is adaptation information, not a drought-tolerance rating.

heat.details: MNK-1 is listed as a heat-tolerant genotype in a field screening method study at ICAR-NIASM Pune (2023-25 seasons). This is a single listing without reported numeric heat-stress data or mechanisms, so the level is provisional.

salinity.details: In a salinity pot experiment (10 genotypes, three NaCl levels, College of Agriculture Vijayapur), MNK1 was described as less affected than several other genotypes on morpho-phenological and yield traits. The snippet gives no MNK1-specific numeric yield loss, so the level is provisional and relative only.

flood.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: moderately resistant, per the DPD central release table (2011 release, UAS Raichur). Fusarium wilt: moderately resistant, per a chickpea varieties slide summary. No other disease resistance is documented in the digest. The slide deck's 'tolerant to wilt, dry root rot and bgm' entry belongs to a different variety heading and was discarded.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. Release record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: 12.80 q/ha under normal conditions (release record). DPD table gives 13-14 q/ha. FPVS mean in Kurnool, Prakasam and Anantapur: 983 kg/ha (about 9.83 q/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources, apart from the multi-location AICRP entries noted under field_trials, whose values and units are not stated in the snippet.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Normal sown rainfed and irrigated conditions (release record). Recommended states per release record: Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu. DPD table lists irrigated conditions. Release record notes suitability for normal sowing conditions similar to other kabuli chickpea varieties, and tolerance to lodging and shattering.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Erect plants, broad compound leaves, milky-white seed, 51.9 g/100 seeds, 100-day maturity (slide summary). Release record: tolerant to lodging and shattering. Seed type: kabuli, extra-large-seeded (ICAR-IIPR AICRP 2021-22 report and PubMed source).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Karnataka FPVS 2017-18: MNK 1 was one of three elite entries; GBM 2 was the top yielder in Kalaburagi. (2) FPVS in Kurnool, Prakasam and Anantapur (Andhra Pradesh): mean yield 983 kg/ha. (3) ICAR-IIPR AICRP Chickpea 2021-22: MNK 1 listed among recent extra-large-seeded kabuli releases and in multi-location trial entries; values in brackets, unit not stated in snippet. (4) Salinity pot experiment (College of Agriculture Vijayapur): MNK1 less affected than several genotypes; no numeric loss given. (5) ICAR-NIASM Pune field screening (2023-25): listed as heat-tolerant; no numeric data in snippet.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Parentage per release record: GULBARGA LOCAL. Mapping population: F2:3 from MNK-1 x Annigeri 1 (188 F2 plants); 31,311 SNPs identified, of which 7,204 were polymorphic. Marker positions: Not found in searched sources.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: 11 seed Fe QTLs and 8 seed Zn QTLs identified in the MNK-1 x Annigeri 1 population. MNK-1 alleles favoured Fe at all five CaLG04 loci. Individual QTL effect sizes: Not found in searched sources. Drought, heat or wilt QTL/marker work specific to MNK-1: not found.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. Seed nutrient data: MNK-1 is an extra-large-seeded kabuli line with seed Fe 72.88 and Zn 30.98 mg/kg.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MNK-1 (chickpea)

Name note: the CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "MNK-1". Sources write it as "MNK 1" or "MNK-1", and all refer to the same kabuli line. Seednet's own portal page was not returned by any search, so the Seednet record itself is unverified. Release year: the Seednet record reads 2010-12-23, while the DPD table lists 2011 for UAS Raichur. Four searches were run.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as a heat-tolerant genotype in a field screening method study at ICAR-NIASM Pune, 2023-25 seasons -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13311209/
- In a salinity pot experiment (10 genotypes, three NaCl levels, College of Agriculture Vijayapur), MNK1 was described as less affected than several others on morpho-phenological and yield traits; the paper gives no MNK1-specific numeric yield loss in the snippet -- https://journaloffarmsciences.in/index.php/JFM/article/download/190/211
- Drought: the only MNK-1 evidence is farmer-preferred variety trial (FPVS) yields in Kurnool, Prakasam and Anantapur (mean 983 kg/ha) and a Karnataka FPVS note, with no drought-tolerance rating -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/
- Flood/submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to wilt, per the DPD central release table (2011 release, UAS Raichur) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Moderately resistant to Fusarium wilt, per a chickpea varieties slide summary -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/varieties-of-chickpea/87189800
- Pest resistance: No evidence found. The slide deck's "tolerant to wilt, dry root rot and bgm" entry is under a different variety heading (55.4 g/100 seeds, 110 days) and was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Plant type and seed size: erect plants, broad compound leaves, milky-white seed, 51.9 g/100 seeds, 100-day maturity -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/varieties-of-chickpea/87189800
- Average yield 13-14 q/ha, maturity 100-105 days, Karnataka/AP/Odisha/TN, irrigated -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- ICAR-IIPR AICRP Chickpea 2021-22 report lists MNK 1 among recent extra-large-seeded kabuli releases, and in multi-location trial entries (values in brackets, unit not stated in snippet) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Karnataka FPVS 2017-18: MNK 1 was one of three elite entries; GBM 2 was the top yielder in Kalaburagi -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/
- Seed germination testing protocol standardized on MNK-1 (2014-15 work) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327252161_An_improved_method_of_seed_germination_testing_in_Kabuli_chickpea

GENETICS AND QTL
- F2:3 mapping population (188 F2 plants) from MNK-1 × Annigeri 1; 31,311 SNPs found, 7,204 polymorphic; 11 Fe and 8 Zn QTLs; MNK-1 alleles favoured Fe at all five CaLG04 loci -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7588353
- Same study, Frontiers version (DOI 10.3389/fnut.2020.559120) -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2020.559120/pdf
- MNK-1 is a kabuli, extra-large-seeded line with seed Fe 72.88 and Zn 30.98 mg/kg -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33154975
- MNK-1 × GKB-10 derived green-seeded lines (cross relation, not the released variety itself) -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/49%20Multivariate-Analysis-for-Grain-Yield-and-Nutritional-Quality-Traits-of-Green-Seeded-Chickpea-(Cicer-arietinum-L.)-Genotypes-derived-from-Desi-and-Kabuli-(GKB-10-%C3%97-MNK-1)-Initial-Efforts-for-Green-S-Honnappa-M-49.pdf
- Drought, heat or wilt QTL/marker work specific to MNK-1: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution (per the release record and DPD table): University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur, Karnataka. Released 2011 per DPD -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist named for MNK-1 itself: No evidence found.
- Names that appear on UAS Raichur chickpea papers (Honnappa M, Hosamani M, Umesh Babu BS, D.M. Mannur) are linked to MNK-1-derived green-seeded lines, not to its release, so they are not attributed here -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2018/vol7issue6/PartAJ/7-6-125-743.pdf
- Development station context: ARS Kalaburagi, UAS Raichur, is named as the trial site in the derived-line work -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/49%20Multivariate-Analysis-for-Grain-Yield-and-Nutritional-Quality-Traits-of-Green-Seeded-Chickpea-(Cicer-arietinum-L.)-Genotypes-derived-from-Desi-and-Kabuli-(GKB-10-%C3%97-MNK-1)-Initial-Efforts-for-Green-S-Honnappa-M-49.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact for MNK-1: No evidence found.
- Institute-level email, phone, postal address or contact page for UAS Raichur: No evidence found in these results. Not guessed.

PUBLICATIONS
- Sab S, Lokesha R, Mannur DM, Somasekhar, Jadhav K, et al. (2020). Genome-Wide SNP Discovery and Mapping QTLs for Seed Iron and Zinc Concentrations in Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.). Frontiers in Nutrition -- DOI 10.3389/fnut.2020.559120; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7588353
- Krishna Naik A, Basave Gowda, Vasudevan SN, Shakuntala NM, Nagalikar VP (2014). Seed technological investigation in Kabuli chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) cv. MNK-1. M.Sc. thesis, as cited in https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327252161_An_improved_method_of_seed_germination_testing_in_Kabuli_chickpea (thesis itself not located; no URL or DOI)
- Authors not shown in snippet (2017/2018). An improved method of seed germination testing in Kabuli chickpea. International Journal of Agricultural Research -- DOI 10.18805/IJARe.A-4879; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327252161_An_improved_method_of_seed_germination_testing_in_Kab

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PBG7 (GL 26054), chickpea, Punjab Agricultural University

Search status: I ran four web_search calls, which is the maximum allowed. The first call returned the only relevant hit, and I saw only a truncated snippet of it. The tool limit then blocked my follow-up searches, so the digest is thin and several headings are empty for that reason. The CSC name and the Seednet name are identical ("PBG7 (GL 26054)"), so one set of evidence applies to both. The search pages mostly used "PBG7" without the GL number, so the GL number is not confirmed by any retrieved page.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no PBG7 page that reports drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The only pest-related text retrieved (H. armigera pod damage screening at BHU) concerns other genotypes, so I discarded it. The PAU ascochyta blight page concerns interspecific derivatives, not PBG7, so I discarded it too.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The ResearchGate paper titled "PBG7: A new high yielding variety of desi gram" presents PBG7 as a high-yielding variety. Its snippet gave no yield figures, trial sites or agronomy details -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276267978_PBG7_A_new_high_yielding_variety_of_desi_gram_Cicer_arietinum_L

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage or marker study for PBG7 was retrieved. The input record lists parentage as "Not specified".

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The ResearchGate paper lists Sarvjeet Singh as an author (dated May 2015). I could not confirm from the snippet whether he is the lead breeder or the release proposer. The title's "desi gram" matches Bengal gram, which is the Seednet crop name. Institution: the input record gives Punjab Agricultural University, and the search did not contradict it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276267978_PBG7_A_new_high_yielding_variety_of_desi_gram_Cicer_arietinum_L

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder email, phone, postal address or PAU institute contact page was retrieved. Follow-up was not possible because of the search limit. The PAU Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics is the logical place to look.

PUBLICATIONS
Singh, S. (2015). PBG7: A new high yielding variety of desi gram (Cicer arietinum L.). ResearchGate record of a PDF; journal and volume not confirmed by the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276267978_PBG7_A_new_high_yielding_variety_of_desi_gram_Cicer_arietinum_L
Only the author name and the publication date (May 2015) were visible in the snippet, so the full author list and journal are unverified. No KrishiKosh, AICRP, ICAR or journal items were retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, Punjab state seed corporation, KVK, PAU seed sale or dealer listing for PBG7 was retrieved. The one seed-related result (a Pakistani AARI chickpea page) concerns other varieties and a different country, so I discarded it.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Punjab is recorded in the input record (CSC/variety record), but no search result confirmed it. This is unverified by the search.

Discarded results (not about PBG7): Frontiers ascochyta-blight paper (interspecific derivatives); Springer chickpea seed metabolomics paper (no variety named); AARI Faisalabad "Chickpea Desi" page (Pakistan, other varieties).

Recommended next steps: confirm the GL 26054 designation and the release notification in the CSC/ICAR minutes; check the PAU Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics and the PAU Pulses breeding pages for the lead breeder and contact details; search KrishiKosh and the AICRP on Chickpea annual reports for trial data; and check the Punjab Seed Corporation and PAU seed-sale listings for availability.

drought_tolerance.technical_details: The variety record states resistance to drought. The review 'Chickpea breeding and management' lists Pusa 212 as resistant to F. wilt and root rots, with moisture stress and low/high temperature tolerance. No quantitative drought-index data for Pusa 212 appeared in the snippets. It is used in drought-related physiology and breeding panels.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The review lists tolerance to low and high temperature, but this is a generic statement. The IARI Annual Report 2019-20 mentions a cross of ICC 14395 x Pusa 212 for heat stress screening (48 °C), but this does not show that Pusa 212 itself is heat tolerant. The variety is described as suitable for early and late sowing.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: Pusa-212 appears in a table in Flowers (2010) of germination and radicle-length salinity studies (Saxena & Rewari, 1991). The snippets give no result for this variety. The review notes that chickpea in general is salt sensitive. The accelerated-ageing and seawater study includes Pusa 212 but the snippets show no tolerance result.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No flood or waterlogging evidence for Pusa 212 was found. The CRIDA document only recommends surface drainage in high-rainfall, deep black soils for chickpea in general.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: Fusarium wilt (resistant, supported by multiple sources); root rots (claimed in a review, but contradicted for dry root rot); dry root rot (susceptible)
disease_resistance.technical_details: Multiple sources list Pusa 212 as a wilt-resistant cultivar: the ICRISAT chapter 'Diseases of Chickpea', IARI technical options, course material and a review. A study of the chickpea wilt complex in western India found Pusa 212 showed the highest dry root rot incidence (31.7-100%) against the isolates tested. A 2023 abstract describes Pusa 212 as 'resistant and susceptible to DRR respectively' in a comparison, which is ambiguous in the snippet. The overall picture is wilt resistant but dry root rot susceptible. Wilt resistance may have eroded since 1982, as new races appear. The snippets do not report specific resistance genes.

pest_resistance.specific_pests: None documented. The record's 'resistant to gram wilt' is a disease trait, not a pest trait.
pest_resistance.technical_details: No insect pest resistance (e.g. Helicoverpa) evidence was found. Resistance to lodging and shattering are agronomic traits.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: Several citations (ICRISAT chapter, IARI publications, Flowers 2010, a review) support Fusarium wilt resistance, which is a stress trait. Drought, frost and low/high temperature claims come from the record and a review, with little independent verification. Yield is modest (16.8 Q/ha). The variety is documented as susceptible to dry root rot, and there is no Gujarat-specific evidence, no marker data and no flood or salinity evidence. This fits the 75 band (some research evidence, at least one stress trait and a citation) rather than 90-100.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: PUSA-212 is a 1982-released desi chickpea (P.340 x G.130, pedigree selection) with 130-150 days maturity and a yield of 16.8 Q/ha. Its Fusarium wilt resistance is supported by several sources, while its drought, frost and temperature tolerance rests mainly on the variety record and a review. It is susceptible to dry root rot, and no marker, flood, salinity or commercial-availability evidence was found.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Desi chickpea released in 1982 by the Central Varietal Release Committee, with small light-brown seeds, 130-150 days maturity and 16.8 Q/ha yield. It suits early and late sowing and is fertilizer responsive.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Fusarium wilt resistance is well supported, and drought, frost and lodging resistance are claimed with limited verification. Dry root rot susceptibility was documented, and flood, submergence, salinity, heat and pest evidence is absent or inconclusive.
