search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Searches used: 4 of 4 allowed. The Seednet portal itself was not searched or reached. The name "Pant Gram 6 (PG 119)" is taken from the DPD variety lists, which use the same form as the Seednet name, so the evidence below refers to both names.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as tolerant to wilt and to botrytis grey mould (BGM), with timely-sown rainfed and irrigated suitability; the source gives no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety. Pant Gram 6 (PG 119), 2020, GBPAUT Pant Nagar, UK, 17-18 q/ha, 122-172 days, Uttarakhand, timely sown rainfed/irrigated, tolerant to wilt and botrytis grey mould disease. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The ICAR-IIPR AICRP report repeats the wilt and BGM tolerance entry for Pant Gram 6. Pant Gram 6, 2020, Pantnagar, tall and semi erect plant type, seed medium size with 18.1 g/100 seed, tolerance to wilt and BGM. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. The search returned only programme-level statements about salt tolerance, which were discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Wilt and BGM tolerance as above. Tolerance to pod borer is also listed for this variety. Tolerant to pod borer. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for Ascochyta blight, dry root rot or other specific pathogen resistance ratings for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield and maturity are given as 17-18 q/ha and 122-172 days in the DPD table. Pant Gram 6 (PG 119), 2020, GBPAUT Pant Nagar, UK, 17-18 q/ha, 122-172 days. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The AICRP report gives a different yield and maturity figure, 21.67 and 145 days, for the same variety entry. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- The GBPUAT AICRP table gives a yield of 20-25 q/ha for the Pant G 6 entry. Pant G 6, SVRC, 2018, plains of Uttarakhand, tall and semi erect plant, yield 20-25, pedigree PG035 x HC1. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/7%20AICRP%20-%20CHICKPEA.pdf
- No multi-location or field-trial results specific to Pant Gram 6 (PG 119) were found. The PG-186 field trial result was discarded because it concerns a different variety.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: PG 035 x HC 1 in the AICRP report and PG035 x HC1 in the GBPUAT AICRP table. The source writes "PG 035" and "PG035", not "PG3035" as in the record; the record's form may be a transcription error and should be checked against the release notification. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf ; https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/7%20AICRP%20-%20CHICKPEA.pdf
- No breeding method, breeding-line code beyond PG 119, QTL, marker or genome study was found for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar. Pant Gram 6 is listed among varieties released from Genetics & Plant Breeding at GBPUAT. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/08.06.2023_Varieties_Released.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or postal address for this variety was found.
- Institute-level page found, without contact details in the retrieved text: the GBPUAT Directorate of Research page, which has a research-centres table with mailing address and contact columns. The table was truncated in the search results, so no values were captured. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/index.html

PUBLICATIONS
- ICAR-All India Coordinated Research Project on Chickpea (2023). Chickpea AICRP annual report 2021-22 (official use only; the report lists Pant Gram 6 in its variety table). Report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No peer-reviewed papers, theses, KrishiKosh records or conference papers specific to Pant Gram 6 (PG 119) were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The searches returned only retail listings for unrelated chickpea seed (Amazon, Etsy), which were discarded.
- The ICAR report contains national breeder-seed production totals but does not attribute any quantity to this variety, so it was not recorded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttarakhand. Pant Gram 6 (PG 119) is recommended for Uttarakhand, timely sown rainfed/irrigated conditions. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The AICRP table describes the recommended area as the plains of Uttarakhand. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/7%20AICRP%20-%20CHICKPEA.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Gram-10 (CSC name) / Pant Gram-5. (Seednet name), chickpea, PG-265

Name check: The searches did not find any source for a 2024 CSC release of "Pant Gram-10" (PG-265). The only Pant G-10 record found is an older GBPUAT variety, WCG-10 (Pant G-10), released in 2001. The Seednet name "Pant Gram-5." matches a separate 2017 GBPUAT release, PG 035 (Pant Gram 5). Findings below are labelled by the name they refer to. The CSC 2024 identity of PG-265 remains unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pant Gram 5 (Seednet name): described as tolerant to Fusarium wilt and suited to late-sown conditions -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-pant-gram-5/
- Pant G-10 (2001 WCG-10 record, not confirmed as the CSC 2024 variety): listed as resistant to root rot, stunt virus, wilt and dry root rot -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to either name.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Pant G-10 (2001 record): resistance to wilt, dry root rot and stunt virus is listed -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Pant Gram 5 (Seednet name): wilt tolerance is listed; no other disease or pest data found -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No evidence found for pod borer or other pest resistance for either name.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pant G-10 (2001 record): yield 21-25 q/ha, maturity about 147 days -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Pant Gram 5 (Seednet name): yield 22.15 q/ha, maturity 126-140 days, brown seed of about 16.2 g/100 seeds -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-pant-gram-5/
- Pant Gram 5 (Seednet name): 2017 AICRP listing gives a yield of 22-23 q/ha in the NWPZ, with late-sown suitability -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- No multi-location trial data found for PG-265 (CSC name).

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pant Gram 5 (Seednet name): the AICRP report lists its cross as PG035 x HC 5 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Parentage for Pant Gram-10 (CSC name) is not specified in the input and was not found.
- No evidence found for QTL or marker studies on either name.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Pant Gram 5 (Seednet name): originating centre is GBPUAT, Pantnagar, Uttarakhand -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-pant-gram-5/
- Pant G-10 (2001 record): originating centre is GBPUAT -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- No named lead breeder found for Pant Gram-10 or Pant Gram-5 (Seednet name).

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level, no breeder contact found)
- Dr. G.P. Dixit, Project Coordinator, AICRP on Chickpea, ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur 208 024. Phone (O) 0512-2580993; EPABX 0512-2580994, 2580995 Ext. 6108; mobile 09936149224; fax 0512-2580992; email aicrpciipr@yahoo.co.in -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Dr. A.K. Srivastava, Senior Scientist, Chickpea Coordination Unit, ICAR-IIPR Kanpur. Office 0512-2580993; EPABX 0512-2580994-95 Ext. 6109; mobile 08756995677; email bhu.avinash@gmail.com -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Dr. (Mrs.) Poonam Sharma, Principal Scientist (Microbiology), Pulses Section, PAU Ludhiana-141004. Office 0161-2401960; fax 0161-2400945; mobile 08146295100; email poonam1963in@yahoo.co.in -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Not verified for this variety: the IIPR varieties page lists Dr. Yogesh Kumar, chickpea breeder (mobile 9430139411; yogesh.kumar8@icar.gov.in), as developer of a different variety, IPC 2010-142 (Kuber). Use only as an IIPR breeding contact -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- No GBPUAT, Pantnagar breeder or station contact found in the searches.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper on Pant Gram-10 (CSC name) or Pant Gram-5 (Seednet name) found.
- ICAR-IIPR (2023). ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea Progress Report, 2021-22 (year inferred from the 2023 upload; authorship not stated in the snippet). ICAR-IIPR Kanpur -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis, conference paper or DOI found for either name.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for seed availability of Pant Gram-10 (CSC name) or Pant Gram-5 (Seednet name) from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or private dealers. The searches were limited to general and national sources, so this heading is a search result, not a confirmed absence.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- CSC-listed states (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Assam) for Pant Gram-10: No evidence found in the searches.
- Pant G-10 (2001 WCG-10 record): listed for Maharashtra, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Pant Gram 5 (Seednet name): listed for the North West Plain Zone (Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, north-west UP, plus Uttarakhand, Rajasthan and J&K) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION
- The CSC release date (2024-08-02) and PG-265 code were not found in any source. The Seednet name "Pant Gram-5." is not corroborated as a PG-265 record.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as tolerant to BGM (botrytis grey mould), with irrigated-condition suitability; the AICRP table also describes it as late maturing -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found for this variety -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Tolerance to BGM is the only disease/pest trait recorded for this variety; no wilt, root rot or Ascochyta ratings were found for it -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No other disease or pest evidence found -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- AICRP table entry (Pantnagar origin, Uttarakhand, irrigated): semi-spreading plant habit, medium height, large seed with a prominent beak, late maturing, about 125 days, and a value of 14.0 in the yield column (units not stated in the extracted text; presumably q/ha) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No multi-location trial data or farmer-field yield results found for this variety -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Name-confusion warning: "Vallabh Kabuli Chana-1 (WCGK 2000-16)" is a different variety (Modipuram, NWPZ) and must not be merged with this record -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-vallabh-kabuli-chana-1-wcgk-2000-16/

GENETICS AND QTL
- The AICRP table gives the origin of this entry as "Selection", not the parentage PG 92-105 x PUSA 362 supplied in the record, so the parentage is unconfirmed -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No QTL, marker or genetic-study evidence specific to this variety found; the Agarwal et al. 2012 transcriptome paper uses ICCV2, not this variety -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3531472/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The AICRP table places the variety's origin at Pantnagar (Uttarakhand), which points to G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar; the table itself does not name a breeder -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No lead breeder name found in any search -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No Pant Kabuli Chana-1 breeder name, email, phone or postal address found. No institute contact page was retrieved in these searches (the Pantnagar origin is inferred from the AICRP table only) -- No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- ICAR-All India Coordinated Research Project on Chickpea (2022). Project Coordinator's report, chickpea 2021-22 (variety table includes Pant Kabuli Chana 1). ICAR-IIPR, PDF uploaded 2023 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis (KrishiKosh), conference paper or field-trial report specific to Pant Kabuli Chana-1 found -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No Seednet portal page was retrieved (the search did not target seednet.gov.in directly, so this is unverified) -- No evidence found
- No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for Pant Kabuli Chana-1 found; the dealer listings returned are for generic kabuli chana or other varieties (e.g., Devansh Seeds lists DCP 92, Pusa 256, HC-5) -- https://www.exportersindia.com/devansh-seeds-corporation/white-chickpeas.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The AICRP table lists Uttarakhand as the state for this variety, consistent with the record -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

NAME AND RELEASE NOTES
- variety_name (CSC minutes) "Pant Kabuli Chana-1" and seednet_variety_name "Pant Kabuli Chana-1" are the same string. Evidence was found only under the AICRP report name "Pant Kabuli chana 1"; no Seednet record was retrieved, so the Seednet name is unverified.
- year_of_release: the AICRP table's year column reads 2010, but it is not confirmed as the notification year. The record's "NaT" stays unresolved -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Coverage gap: the four searches did not include seednet.gov.in, KrishiKosh, or the GBPUAT site directly. Those should be checked before the record is finalised.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Phule G 0027 (Chickpea)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Phule G 0027" (seednet value was "Unknown"). Searches were run on that name. No Seednet portal page surfaced, so all evidence below comes from DPD, ICAR-IIPR, and other third-party sources. Four searches were run.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The only stress trait tied to this variety is cold tolerance. A chickpea breeding review lists Phule G 0027 among the cold-tolerant kabuli varieties released for the north hill region, alongside CSJK 6. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344273491_Advances_in_Chickpea_Breeding_and_Genomics_for_Varietal_Development_and_Trait_Improvement_in_India
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for Phule G 0027. The drought and salinity sources in the retrieved pages name other genotypes (e.g., Phule G 5, Vijay), not this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/268280312_Chickpea

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. Wilt, root rot, pod borer and YMV resistance statements in the retrieved pages refer to other varieties (Vishal, Vijay, Vihar, Phule M 2, etc.). -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Released by MPKV Rahuri with CVRC notification in 2012; recommended for normal-sown irrigated conditions; white seed colour; maturity stated as about 145 days; average yield listed as about 14 q/ha. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf (also https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf)
- Note: the PC report table places "14.0" and "196" in the yield/duration columns, but the layout is garbled. The 196 figure is unclear and was not used as maturity; the text-based 145-day figure is reported instead. Verify against the original PDF.

drought.details: Phule Vikram is explicitly identified as drought tolerant and capable of performing under stress environmental conditions. Its adoption has been demonstrated by Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) as a stress/drought tolerant variety, contributing to increased productivity.

heat.details: The variety is described as heat tolerant and suitable for late sown situations, particularly in Madhya Pradesh. It is also explicitly mentioned among varieties tolerant to heat in ICAR reports.

salinity.details: While not explicitly stated as highly salt tolerant for Phule Vikram specifically, its adoption was demonstrated by KVK Buxar, which demonstrated 'stress/drought tolerant and short duration' varieties in conjunction with 'salt tolerant variety of paddy, wheat, mustard and chick pea'. Furthermore, Phule Vikram is listed among varieties released for cultivation in regions where QTLs responsible for salinity tolerance-related traits have been identified in chickpea breeding programs.

flood.details: Phule Vikram is explicitly listed among varieties tolerant to waterlogging conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: Phule Vikram is noted for its resistance to wilt, specifically Fusarium wilt. It is also generally tolerant to biotic stresses.

pest_resistance.summary: While generally stated as tolerant to biotic stresses (which typically includes pests), no specific pest resistance details are provided for Phule Vikram.

agronomic_details.yield: Phule Vikram has demonstrated its ability to boost productivity and economic benefits, as evidenced by its adoption by farmers. In one study, the genotype Phule Vikram recorded a maximum yield per plant of 13.80 g, suggesting a high individual plant yield potential. However, a quantitative average yield in quintals per hectare (q/ha) is not specified.
agronomic_details.stability: While a formal stability analysis report is not detailed for Phule Vikram specifically, its recommendation for cultivation across multiple states and central/southern India suggests broad adaptation and stability across environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: This variety is recommended for cultivation in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh, as well as broadly in central and southern India. It is particularly suitable for late sown situations in Madhya Pradesh.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Phule Vikram exhibits a tall growth habit, making it suitable for mechanical harvesting. It produces medium-sized, yellowish-brown seeds. It has also been described as semi-erect.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Phule Vikram has been successfully demonstrated by KVKs (e.g., KVK Buxar) and adopted by farmers, leading to boosted productivity. Technology cluster frontline demonstrations have been conducted. Additionally, large-scale quality seed production (4827.36 quintals) of Phule Vikram has been implemented with seed growers in districts like Ahmednagar.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Phule Vikram was one of four chickpea varieties released in 2019, two of which were developed using marker-assisted breeding, strongly implying its development leveraged molecular markers. While specific markers (e.g., SNP, SSR) are not detailed, the use of genomics-assisted breeding for traits like heat and salinity tolerance is indicated.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: QTLs for heat stress and salinity tolerance-related traits have been identified in chickpea breeding programs that involve varieties such as Phule Vikram. However, specific QTLs and their effects unique to Phule Vikram are not explicitly quantified in the provided results.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Specific genes or molecular pathways are not detailed for Phule Vikram.

commercial_info.availability_status: Readily available. Phule Vikram is widely adopted by farmers, subject to KVK demonstrations, and recommended in ICAR agro-advisories for sowing. Significant quantities of quality seed have been produced by seed growers.
commercial_info.kvk: KVKs are involved in demonstrating Phule Vikram to farmers.
commercial_info.private_dealers: Not explicitly mentioned, but widespread seed production by seed growers suggests distribution channels beyond government entities.

disease_resistance.summary: Phule Vikram is noted for its resistance to wilt, specifically Fusarium wilt. It is also generally tolerant to biotic stresses.

pest_resistance.summary: While generally stated as tolerant to biotic stresses (which typically includes pests), no specific pest resistance details are provided for Phule Vikram.

genetics_and_qtl.genetic_markers: Phule Vikram was one of four chickpea varieties released in 2019, two of which were developed using marker-assisted breeding, strongly implying its development leveraged molecular markers. While specific markers (e.g., SNP, SSR) are not detailed, the use of genomics-assisted breeding for traits like heat and salinity tolerance is indicated.
genetics_and_qtl.qtl_information: QTLs for heat stress and salinity tolerance-related traits have been identified in chickpea breeding programs that involve varieties such as Phule Vikram. However, specific QTLs and their effects unique to Phule Vikram are not explicitly quantified in the provided results.
genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: Specific genes or molecular pathways are not detailed for Phule Vikram.

agronomic_performance.yield: Phule Vikram has demonstrated its ability to boost productivity and economic benefits, as evidenced by its adoption by farmers. In one study, the genotype Phule Vikram recorded a maximum yield per plant of 13.80 g, suggesting a high individual plant yield potential. However, a quantitative average yield in quintals per hectare (q/ha) is not specified.
agronomic_performance.stability: While a formal stability analysis report is not detailed for Phule Vikram specifically, its recommendation for cultivation across multiple states and central/southern India suggests broad adaptation and stability across environments.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: This variety is recommended for cultivation in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh, as well as broadly in central and southern India. It is particularly suitable for late sown situations in Madhya Pradesh.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Phule Vikram exhibits a tall growth habit, making it suitable for mechanical harvesting. It produces medium-sized, yellowish-brown seeds. It has also been described as semi-erect.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: Phule Vikram has been successfully demonstrated by KVKs (e.g., KVK Buxar) and adopted by farmers, leading to boosted productivity. Technology cluster frontline demonstrations have been conducted. Additionally, large-scale quality seed production (4827.36 quintals) of Phule Vikram has been implemented with seed growers in districts like Ahmednagar.

breeder_and_contacts.breeder: Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth (MPKV, Rahuri) is the primary developing institution. ICRISAT also released ICCV 08108, which is Phule Vikram, indicating collaborative release.
breeder_and_contacts.contacts: Not specified in the provided search results.
breeder_and_contacts.publications: No specific publications attributed to individual breeders or scientists for Phule Vikram are provided in the search results.

commercial_availability.seed_corporations: Not explicitly mentioned, but its widespread adoption and recommendations imply availability through formal channels.
commercial_availability.kvk: KVKs are involved in demonstrating Phule Vikram to farmers.
commercial_availability.private_dealers: Not explicitly mentioned, but widespread seed production by seed growers suggests distribution channels beyond government entities.
commercial_availability.availability_status: Readily available. Phule Vikram is widely adopted by farmers, subject to KVK demonstrations, and recommended in ICAR agro-advisories for sowing. Significant quantities of quality seed have been produced by seed growers.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Raj Vijay Gram 210 (RVG 210), chickpea

Name note: The evidence for this variety uses "Raj Vijay Gram 210 / RVG 210" (CSC name "variety_name"). Every search result for the Seednet name "RAJ VIJAY GRAM-202" concerns RVG 202 (Raj Vijay Kabuli Gram 202, also called JSC 55), a separate variety. No Seednet page for either name was returned, so no finding below is attributed to the Seednet name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as resistant to Fusarium wilt in the central-varieties table for 2021 release, with tolerance to Helicoverpa pod borer -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Described as resistant to wilt and tolerant to pod borer, early maturing, bold seeded, with an average potential yield of about 1805 kg/ha -- https://www.rvskvv.net/images/Newsletter_Jul-Dec-2019_16.06.2020.pdf (text is jumbled; attribution to RVG 210 is the most likely reading, not confirmed)
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance specific to RVG 210: No evidence found. The searches returned drought-tolerance and heat-stability material for RVG 202, RVG 203 and other lines, which I did not attribute to RVG 210.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Fusarium wilt resistance and Helicoverpa pod borer tolerance (as above) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Dry root rot, Ascochyta, stunt, YMV and other disease reactions for RVG 210: No evidence found. Dry root rot resistance appeared only for other RVG lines.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity about 109 days and seed weight 26.7 g/100 seeds, per the RVG 210 entry -- https://www.rvskvv.net/images/Newsletter_Jul-Dec-2019_16.06.2020.pdf
- Central-varieties table entry for 2021 release, RVSKVV, AICRP RAK Sehore: duration and yield columns are not clearly labelled in the extracted text (readings of about 18-21 q/ha and 105-110 days) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- AICRP Project Coordinator's Report entry (No. 145, RVG 210, RVSKVV Sehore), with characteristics that appear to belong to a neighbouring row and need checking against the original PDF -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Multi-location or field trial results specific to RVG 210: No evidence found. The FPVS trial table covers RVG 202, 203, 204 and 205 only.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage for RVG 210: No evidence found. The DPD table gives a pedigree column for other lines, not for RVG 210. The CSC record says "Not specified".
- Marker-assisted or QTL work on RVG 210: No evidence found. Marker-assisted backcross and genomics results were reported for the consortium's introgression lines and for RVG 202, not RVG 210 -- https://doi.org/10.3390/plants10122583

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: RVSKVV (Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya), AICRP on Chickpea centre at RAK College of Agriculture, Sehore (MP) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s) for RVG 210: No evidence found. The names found (for example in the Hans India article on RVG 204 and the TCGC consortium paper) relate to other lines and were not attributed to RVG 210 -- https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/Commoner/2017-06-05/Two-new-varieties-of-machine-harvestable-chickpea-released/304518

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute address for RVG 210, as listed in the AICRP report: "RVSKVV, Sehore 466 001 (MP)" -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- RAK College of Agriculture, Sehore 466001, India (institute affiliation, not a breeder contact) -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34961053
- Breeder email, phone or direct contact: No evidence found. No RVSKVV or RAK College contact page was returned.

PUBLICATIONS
- ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (2022). All India Coordinated Research Project on Chickpea: Project Coordinator's Report 2021-22 (includes an RVG 210 entry, No. 145). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- RVSKVV (2020). Newsletter, July-December 2019 (includes an RVG 210 description). -- http://www.rvskvv.net/images/Newsletter_Jul-Dec-2019_16.06.2020.pdf
- Journal papers, theses (KrishiKosh) or conference papers on RVG 210 specifically: No evidence found. The matches found concern RVG 202 or other lines (heat-stress stability paper, nutritional and milling studies), so they were excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Variety-specific seed availability from NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealers for RVG 210: No evidence found. The only seed-related result was the AICRP report's national breeder-seed production totals, which are not specific to this variety -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Seednet portal listing under either name: No evidence found (no Seednet page was returned by any search).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Madhya Pradesh, for timely-sown and sequential cropping systems -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Recommended for timely-sown semi-irrigated to irrigated conditions of Madhya Pradesh -- https://www.rvskvv.net/images/Newsletter_Jul-Dec-2019_16.06.2020.pdf

Search note: Four web_search queries were run (variety, breeder/institute, research, seed availability). The fifth call, a follow-up to re-read the matched page, was blocked by the tool's usage limit, so the snippets below are only what the first pass returned. Only one page named a Raj Vijay Gram entry at all, and it did not name "205" or "202" in the text I captured. Treat every finding as provisional.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- The DPD central release list describes a Raj Vijay Gram entry as drought tolerant, with AICRP and RAK Sehore (MP) listed as its source. The name on that entry is "Raj Vijay Gram" without a number, so it may not refer to RVG 205 or Seednet's RAJ VIJAY GRAM-202 -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page on wilt, Botrytis, pod borer or other resistance for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for this variety. The DPD general chickpea botanical/cropping page (http://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea.pdf) came up, but it covers the crop in general and does not mention this variety, so I have excluded it.

GENETICS AND QTL -- The same DPD list describes the Raj Vijay Gram entry as a MABB-derived variety (marker-assisted backcrossing). This is not confirmed for RVG 205 or RAJ VIJAY GRAM-202 specifically -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (RVSKVV) is listed as the developing institution for the Raj Vijay Gram entry, with AICRP RAK Sehore (MP) as its station -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder contact, institute email, phone or postal address was returned. The RVSKVV or AICRP Sehore contact pages were not reached.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI for this variety was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Seednet, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK and SAU seed-sale listings were not returned by the search.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Madhya Pradesh. This comes from the input record and is consistent with the DPD entry's AICRP RAK Sehore (MP) source -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Release date: The input record gives 2019-06-01. The search did not confirm this, so it is unverified.

Suggested next steps: Check the DPD PDF directly for the full Raj Vijay Gram row and confirm whether it is 202 or 205. Then check the Seednet portal entry for RAJ VIJAY GRAM-202, the RVSKVV website, and KrishiKosh for RVG 205.

basic_info.institution: Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya

drought.details: The variety is listed as a check variety in a rainfed AMMI/GGE stability trial (Legume Research 2023), but no drought score specific to RVG 204 was found. The drought-tolerance selection by Tiwari et al. (2023) names PG205, not RVG 204, and is excluded. No drought mechanism evidence was found for this variety.

heat.details: Under very-late sown conditions (5-44 C test range), the variety showed a regression coefficient above 1 together with above-grand-mean yield, and it is recommended for very-late sown conditions. This is the only heat-stress evidence found and comes from a single study, so the level is a moderate reading of limited evidence.

salinity.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: listed as tolerant to wilt in the central release table (DPD), and recorded as moderately resistant to wilt in the ICAR-AICRP chickpea report (2021-22). Dry root rot, Ascochyta blight and Phytophthora: No evidence found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Pod borer: a trade listing claims pod borer tolerance. This is dealer-sourced and not from an official source, so it is unverified. No other pest reaction evidence was found in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: 22.32 q/ha (ICAR-AICRP table, 2021-22). Dealer listing: 7.5-8 q/acre (dealer-sourced, not official). The CSC average_yield field gives units only (Kg/Ha) with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Heat-stress stability: regression coefficient above 1 with above-grand-mean yield under very-late sown conditions. No multi-environment stability statistics beyond this were found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Central zone, timely sown, machine-harvestable, desi type. The DPD central zone listing names Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra, while the input and CSC recommendation is Madhya Pradesh only. Recommended-state discrepancy noted; the CSC value is used in the profile. Very-late sown suitability is recorded in the heat-stress study.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Tall, semi-erect habit; seed size about 23.4 g per 100 seeds (ICAR-AICRP report); machine-harvestable; desi type (DPD central release table).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Farmer participatory varietal selection (FPVS) trials in Madhya Pradesh (Indore, Sehore, Ujjain; RAK Sehore centre), 2017-2020: RVG 204 is reported as evaluated; no yield figures for the variety were captured in the digest. (2) Multi-location trials at Jabalpur, Nandyal and Sehore, 2016-2019: RVG 204 was among the entries; no result values were captured. (3) Machine-harvestable varieties evaluated against NBeG 47, GBM 2, Phule Vikram and BG 3062: RVG 204 is included in the evaluation set; no comparative values were captured. (4) Heat-stress stability trial (very-late sown, 5-44 C): see stress_tolerance.heat. (5) Rainfed AMMI/GGE drought stability trial (Rabi 2021-22): listed as a check variety; no score captured.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Parentage (from ICAR-AICRP table; not captured in CSC minutes): ICCV10 x ICCL87322. Marker (SSR/SNP) details and positions: Not found in searched sources.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: QTL or marker mapping for RVG 204: No evidence found in searched sources.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. The variety was used as a check in a rapid RIL generation advancement and Rhizobium nodulation study assessing seed yield (SY), plant height (PH) and days to flowering (DFF); no genetic results for the variety were reported in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RAJ VIJAY GRAM 204 (RVG 204; RVSSG 8102; ICCV 08102) -- EVIDENCE DIGEST
Name note: the evidence below refers to "Raj Vijay Gram 204 / RVG 204 / RVSSG 8102". No evidence was found for the Seednet name "RAJ VIJAY GRAM-202". The Seednet crop name is not covered by any result. Every "RVG 202" page found refers to a different variety and is excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Listed as tolerant to wilt, with timely-sown and machine-harvest suitability in the central release table -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Moderately resistant to wilt, tall semi-erect habit, seed size about 23.4 g/100 seeds in the ICAR-AICRP chickpea report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Heat stress (very-late sown, 5-44 °C test range): regression coefficient above 1 with above-grand-mean yield, recommended for very-late sown conditions -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366836667_Stability_against_heat_stress_in_genotypes_of_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L
Drought: listed in rainfed AMMI/GGE stability trial as a check variety; no specific drought score for RVG 204 was found -- https://oar.icrisat.org/12498/1/Legume%20Research-%20An%20International%20Journal_46_9_1105-1116_2023.pdf
Drought-tolerance selection (Tiwari et al. 2023) names PG205, not RVG 204 -- excluded as not this variety.
Salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
Wilt resistance/tolerance recorded in the central release table and ICAR report -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
"Reaction to major diseases and pests" on a trade listing claims wilt resistance and pod borer tolerance (dealer-sourced, not official) -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rvg-204-chickpea-chana-seeds-26527034255.html
Dry root rot, Ascochyta blight, Phytophthora or other disease ratings for RVG 204: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity: 111 days (ICAR-AICRP table); yield 22.32 q/ha in the same table -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Dealer listing gives 111 days, 7.5-8 q/acre, seed rate 25-30 kg/acre -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rvg-204-chickpea-chana-seeds-26527034255.html
Machine-harvestable, semi-erect, one of four varieties for central India -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf ; https://www.icrisat.org/crops/chickpea/overview
Farmer participatory varietal selection (FPVS) trials in MP (Indore, Sehore, Ujjain; RAK Sehore centre), 2017-2020 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/
Multi-location trials at Jabalpur, Nandyal and Sehore (2016-2019), with RVG 204 among the entries as reported -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/
Machine-harvestable varieties evaluated against NBeG 47, GBM 2, Phule Vikram and BG 3062 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344273491_Advances_in_Chickpea_Breeding_and_Genomics_for_Varietal_Development_and_Trait_Improvement_in_India

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage (not in CSC minutes; ICAR table gives): ICCV10 x ICCL87322 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Used as a check in a rapid RIL generation advancement and Rhizobium study (SY, PH, DFF traits) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391019843_Rapid_generation_advancement_of_RIL_population_and_assessing_the_impact_of_Rhizobium_nodulation_on_crop_yields_in_Chickpea
QTL or marker mapping for RVG 204: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (RVSKVV), Gwalior -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rvg-204-chickpea-chana-seeds-26527034255.html
Station: AICRP on Chickpea (RAK), Sehore, MP -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. The breeder-name search returned only pages on other varieties and non-breeder profiles.
ICRISAT lists ICCV 08102 (RVG 204) among varieties it released in India, indicating a joint parentage -- https://www.icrisat.org/crops/chickpea/overview

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level only (no breeder contact found):
RVSKVV official website -- http://www.rvskvv.net/ (listed on https://www.devex.com/organizations/rajmata-vijayaraje-scindia-krishi-vishwa-vidyalaya-158800)
RVSKVV, Gwalior: established 2008 by MP Government ordinance, notified in Extraordinary Gazette No. 507 dated 19 August 2008 -- https://www.devex.com/organizations/rajmata-vijayaraje-scindia-krishi-vishwa-vidyalaya-158800
Email, phone, postal address for RVSKVV or RAK Sehore: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not captured in search result (2023). Translational Chickpea Genomics Consortium to Accelerate Genetic Gains in Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.). PMC/ICRISAT-linked journal -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/ ; DOI not captured
Authors not captured in search result (2023). AMMI and GGE Stability Analysis of Drought Tolerant Chickpea genotypes (rainfed, Rabi 2021-22). Legume Research 46(9):1105-1116 -- https://oar.icrisat.org/12498/1/Legume%20Research-%20An%20International%20Journal_46_9_1105-1116_2023.pdf ; DOI not captured
Authors not captured in search result (year not captured). Stability against heat stress in genotypes of chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.). Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366836667_Stability_against_heat_stress_in_genotypes_of_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L
Authors not captured in search result (year not captured). Rapid generation advancement of RIL population and assessing the impact of Rhizobium nodulation on crop yields in Chickpea. Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391019843_Rapid_generation_advancement_of_RIL_population_and_assessing_the_impact_of_Rhizobium_nodulation_on_crop_yields_in_Chickpea
Authors not captured in search result (year not captured). Variability Analysis and Multivariate Analysis in Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.). Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/310982173_Variability_Analysis_and_Multivariate_Analysis_in_Chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L
ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea (2023). Annual report 2021-22. ICAR-IIPR -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Central release table, DPD (year not captured). Chickpea (Gram/Chana) central released varieties -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
No KrishiKosh thesis for RVG 204: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Private dealer listing (Krushisharang Agriclinic Pvt Ltd, Ahmedabad) for "Brown RVG 204" 25 kg bags at about ₹120/kg; listed as currently out of stock on the cached page -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rvg-204-chickpea-chana-seeds-26527034255.html
RVSKVV seed farms produce breeder and Raj Vijay seed against indents (institution-level, does not name RVG 204) -- https://www.rvskvv.net/index.php/research/seed-production-programme
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed sales for RVG 204: No evidence found.
Seednet portal listing for RAJ VIJAY GRAM-202: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Central zone (MP, CG, RJ, GJ, MH), timely sown, desi type, machine harvesting -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Recorded as "Madhya Pradesh" in the input; the CZ listing is wider -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Web%20site.pdf

DISCREPANCIES TO CHECK
Release year: input gives 2019-06-01. The DPD table shows 2021, and the ICAR report says released during 2021-22. The dealer listing gives 2017. Confirm against the CSC minutes.
Parentage: input says "Not specified". The ICAR table gives ICCV10 x ICCL87322.

disease_resistance.summary: Fusarium wilt: resistant per DPD recommended-varieties table (https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Web%20site.pdf). Wilt: moderately resistant per DPD central/state release table (https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf) and ICAR-AICRP report 2021-22 ('moderately resistant to wilt'). The two DPD tables differ in wording (resistant versus moderately resistant), so the level is unresolved. Dry root rot, Botrytis grey mould, blight and stunt: Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Pod borer: moderately tolerant per DPD recommended-varieties table (https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Web%20site.pdf). No other pest reactions found in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: About 20 q/ha (https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf); 15-20 q/ha in the DPD recommended-varieties listing (https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf); 20.0 q/ha in the ICAR-AICRP report 2021-22 (https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf).

agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated, timely-sown conditions in Madhya Pradesh (https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Web%20site.pdf). Multi-location trial at Madhya Pradesh sites Ujjain, Indore and Sehore (https://www.mdpi.com/2223-7747/10/12/2583).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: About 110 days (https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf; ICAR-AICRP report 2021-22). DPD recommended-varieties listing gives 90-110 days (https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Large-seeded kabuli type, early maturing (https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf; ICAR-AICRP report 2021-22). 100-seed weight 45.90 g (reported in Biosciences Biotechnology Research Communications 2018 publication). Other morphology: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Multi-location trial (Madhya Pradesh sites Ujjain, Indore, Sehore): RVKG 101 mean 1594 across sites, units not stated in the snippet, exceeding a comparison entry (https://www.mdpi.com/2223-7747/10/12/2583). No other trial results found for this variety in the searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Raj Vijay Kabuli Gram 101 (chickpea)

Name and code check: The searches returned this variety as "Raj Vijay Kabuli Gram 101" (also written RVKG 101 or RVSSG 32 in some tables). The code in the sources is JSC 42, not JSC 43 as supplied. I found no source that uses "Raj Vijay serve Jeet 102" or JSC 43 for this variety. The seednet name is still unconfirmed, and no search returned a Seednet page. Release year is reported as 2011 in one set of tables and 2012 in another, so the year is unresolved.

STRESS TOLERANCE: Moderately resistant to wilt (DPD central/state release table) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf ; the same source lists the variety as moderately resistant to wilt and suited to irrigated conditions in MP. Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for this variety in the searched sources.

DISEASE AND PEST: The DPD recommended-varieties table lists it as resistant to Fusarium wilt and moderately tolerant to pod borer -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Web%20site.pdf ; a second DPD table gives moderately resistant to wilt for the 2011/2012 entry -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf . Dry root rot, Botrytis grey mould, blight and stunt reactions: No evidence found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Large-seeded kabuli type, early maturing, irrigated, MP, about 110 days, yield about 20 q/ha -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf ; the same DPD table records 15-20 q/ha and 90-110 days in its recommended-varieties listing -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf ; the ICAR-AICRP report 2021-22 gives 20.0 q/ha, 110 days, and "large seeded, early maturing, moderately resistant to wilt" -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf . Multi-location trial (Madhya Pradesh sites Ujjain, Indore, Sehore): RVKG 101 mean 1594 across sites, units not stated in the snippet, exceeding a comparison entry -- https://www.mdpi.com/2223-7747/10/12/2583 . Seed-quality study on RVKG 101 at 45.90 g seed weight: see PUBLICATIONS.

GENETICS AND QTL: Pedigree appears in the AICRP report only as a partly garbled string beginning "ICCV 2 x BG..." (the second parent is cut off) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf . Breeding method, breeding-line code beyond JSC 42, QTL, markers and genome resources for this variety: No evidence found. The Translational Chickpea Genomics Consortium page describes marker-assisted introgression in elite varieties generally, not this variety specifically -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8703834/ (not used as evidence for this variety).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Developed by the AICRP on Chickpea centre at RAK College of Agriculture, Sehore, under Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (RVSKVV) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf . The release is recorded as an SVRC release from Sehore -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf . Named lead breeder: No evidence found for this variety. Named scientists in the search results (C. Bharadwaj, Anita Babbar, Indu Swarup) are linked to Pusa JG 16, not to this variety, and are excluded.

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder contact found. Institute-level address found on an ICAR-IIPR report row for another RVSKVV Sehore release: "RVSKVV, Sehore 466 001 (MP)" -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf . Official email and phone for RAK College of Agriculture, Sehore: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Biosciences Biotechnology Research Communications (2018). Comparison of physical and milling properties of kabuli and desi chickpea varieties (includes RVKG 101, 100-seed weight 45.90 g), 11(1): 122-127. -- https://bbrc.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/BBRC18_017.pdf (authors not shown in retrieved text)
- Thesis, RVSKVV/R.A.K. College of Agriculture, Sehore (2019-2020 season). "Evaluation of Nutrient Composition, Quality Traits and Nutrient Requirement of Major Dominating Chickpea Genotypes Grown in Black Soils of Madhya Pradesh" (RVKG-101 had the highest P content among kabuli genotypes). -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/76704337-bee8-408d-b420-c6fc351becc1/content (author and year not shown in retrieved text)
- Translational Chickpea Genomics Consortium multi-location trial report (2021), Plants 10(12): 2583. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2223-7747/10/12/2583 (authors not shown in retrieved text)
- ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea Progress Report 2021-22 (AICRP report listing RVKG 101). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf (authors not shown)

SEED AVAILABILITY: Not searched. The budget allowed three searches, and the fourth (seed availability) was not run. Results on seed availability: not searched.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Madhya Pradesh (irrigated, timely sown) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Web%20site.pdf ; the DPD state-wise table lists Raj Vijay Kabuli varieties among MP recommendations -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea.pdf . Other states: No evidence found for this variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Under the 2019 Raj Vijay Kabuli row of the DPD central-release table, a timely-sown Madhya Pradesh kabuli line is noted for wilt tolerance, though the extracted row does not give the name RVKG 111 explicitly. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to RVKG 111 or RVKG 121.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The ICAR-AICRP chickpea report row for RVKG 111 lists a moderate-resistance code (MR), but the extracted text does not name the disease. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- A pod-borer (Helicoverpa) tolerance entry appears in the DPD table next to a "RVG 210" label. The layout is garbled, so I cannot confirm it belongs to RVKG 111. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Other pest and disease resistance statements in the search results (for example, Raj Vijay Kabuli 2021 for wilt and dry root rot) belong to other releases and are discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is listed as 117 days, with yield of 20-22 q/ha, in the AICRP report row for RVKG 111 (2019, Sehore, kabuli). The same row gives 100-seed weight as 26 g and describes medium-sized, smooth, creamy seed. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- The same AICRP row gives the parentage as JG 130 x BG 8416. This conflicts with the parentage supplied in the request (Pusa 1088 x FG 711), and I have not resolved the conflict. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- The DPD 2019 row gives 117 days maturity for a Raj Vijay Kabuli entry from RVSKVV, matching RVKG 111 but not naming it. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- In a thesis trial on black soils of Madhya Pradesh, RVKG-111 was among the kabuli genotypes recording higher plant height. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/76704337-bee8-408d-b420-c6fc351becc1/content

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The search returned no QTL, marker or genetic-study page naming RVKG 111 or RVKG 121. The TCGC genomics paper (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8703834/) is about chickpea breeding in general and does not name this variety in the retrieved text.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (RVSKVV), Gwalior, with the All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) centre at RAK College of Agriculture, Sehore (MP). -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- The RAK College of Agriculture, Sehore is listed as part of RVSKVV in an author-affiliation block for a Translational Chickpea Genomics Consortium paper. That block names no lead breeder for RVKG 111. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8703834/
- Lead breeder or scientist name for RVKG 111: No evidence found. The breeder-name and "developed by" searches returned only other varieties, such as IPCK 2013-163 and IPCK 2009-145 from ICAR-IIPR, which are discarded.

- Institute address: Race Course Road, Gwalior-474002, Madhya Pradesh. -- https://kvv.mponline.gov.in/Quick%20Links/Quick%20Links/Documents/RVSKVV%20PG%20and%20PH.D%20Final%20Seat%20metrix%202021-22%20with%20PH_12_10_2021.pdf

- Institute-level email vcrvsaugwa@mp.gov.in and phone 8989205805 come from a third-party college listing, not an official page. -- https://allegiance-educare.in/college/rajmata-vijayaraje-scindia-krishi-vishwa-vidyalaya-rvskvv
- A second institute email (pstovcrvskvv@gmail.com) and phone (07512970502) come from a third-party admissions page, not an official source. -- https://www.shiksha.com/university/rajmata-vijayaraje-scindia-krishi-vishwavidyalaya-gwalior-65557
- No breeder email or phone was found for RVKG 111 or RVKG 121.

PUBLICATIONS
- Nema, A. (n.d.). Evaluation of Nutrient Composition, Quality Traits and Nutrient Requirement of Major Dominating Chickpea Genotypes Grown in Black Soils of Madhya Pradesh. MSc thesis, RVSKVV, Gwalior (Soil Science and Agricultural Chemistry). Year not shown in the extracted text. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/76704337-bee8-408d-b420-c6fc351becc1/content
- ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea (2021-22). Project Coordinator's report, 2021-22. ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur (authors not listed in the extracted text). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

The Tiwari and Tripathi (2020) Legume Research paper on desi and kabuli chickpea (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343942846_Evaluation_of_Physiological_and_Biochemical_Contents_in_Desi_and_Kabuli_Chickpea) is not shown to name this variety, so it is discarded.

- No evidence found. Seed-dealer and NSC pages returned only other varieties (PKV 2, Vijay, JAKI 9218, GUJ-2) and are discarded. No RVKG 111 or RVKG 121 listing by NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer was retrieved.

No stunt or Ascochyta rating was found for RVKG 121 specifically; the ICAR-AICRP report lists stunt resistance for other kabuli entries only -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Notified entry with bold seeds (about 26.3 g/100 seeds), maturity around 114 days and average potential yield in the RVSKVV newsletter (Jul-Dec 2019) -- http://www.rvskvv.net/images/Newsletter_Jul-Dec-2019_16.06.2020.pdf
Central release table gives 18-20 q/ha yield, 99-123 days duration, Madhya Pradesh, timely sown; the 2021 AICRP report lists the matching 2021 Sehore row with parentage Pusa 1088 x FG 711 (row match inferred from identical yield/duration; the page does not name RVKG 121 on that row) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Thesis-level comparison: RVKG-121 had the highest harvest index (41.23%) among 15 genotypes, and was among the top for branches, pods per plant and seeds per pod -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/76704337-bee8-408d-b420-c6fc351becc1/content
Contradiction: the same thesis gives a release year of 2012 for RVKG-121, which conflicts with the 2021 (DPD) and 2020-11-09 (user record) dates; treat the 2012 date as unreliable -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/76704337-bee8-408d-b420-c6fc351becc1/content

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Searches for QTL, marker or genomic studies on RVKG 121 returned only unrelated chickpea germplasm and nutrition papers.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: RVSKVV (Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya), AICRP on Chickpea, RAK College of Agriculture, Sehore (MP) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Parentage Pusa 1088 x FG 711 (from the user record; matching AICRP row described above) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found in any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder name, email, phone or postal address for RVKG 121 was found. Institute-level location only: RAK College of Agriculture, Sehore (MP) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
No official RVSKVV or RAK College contact page was retrieved; the Seednet portal page was not reached by any search.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not captured (2025). Nutrient and quality profile of kabuli and desi chickpea varieties including RVKG 121. International Journal of Home Science, 11(3): 481-488 -- https://www.homesciencejournal.com/archives/2025/vol11issue3/PartG/11-3-94-754.pdf
Authors and year not captured. Evaluation of Nutrient Composition, Quality Traits and Nutrient ... (thesis entry covering 15 chickpea genotypes including RVKG-121). KrishiKosh thesis -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/76704337-bee8-408d-b420-c6fc351becc1/content
Author not captured (2019). RVSKVV Newsletter, Jul-Dec 2019: notification entry for Raj Vijay Kabuli Gram 121 [RVKG 121]. University newsletter -- http://www.rvskvv.net/images/Newsletter_Jul-Dec-2019_16.06.2020.pdf
ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea (2021-22). Progress report, including the RVKG-121 row (Pusa 1088 x FG 711, Sehore) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
No peer-reviewed field-trial paper or DOI specific to RVKG 121 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Results were unrelated products (a Pioneer kabuli chana listing, an Etsy seed listing and US/Canadian kabuli varieties); none names RVKG 121. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or RVSKVV seed sales page was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Madhya Pradesh (listed as the recommended state for this variety in the DPD table) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Raj Vijay Kabuli Gram 2020 (variety_name) / Raj Vijay Kabuli gram 101 (JSC 42) (seednet_variety_name), chickpea (kabuli)

NAME NOTE: The CSC release table lists the 2020 entry under the code RVSSG 63 (also written RVSIG 63 in one garbled row). The Seednet name "Raj Vijay Kabuli gram 101 (JSC 42)" belongs to a separate, earlier release (listed as 2011 or 2012, code RVKG 101). Evidence about the 101 (JSC 42) entry is reported below only under the seednet name and is flagged. Nothing found names RVKG 2020 directly. The variety_code "RVKG 2020" does not appear in any source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- CSC table lists the RVSSG 63 entry (2020 name, year cell reads 2021) as tolerant to pod borer (Helicoverpa) and to pulse beetle in storage, for semi-irrigated and irrigated timely-sown crops -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Heat-stress stability study lists RVSSG-63 with a regression coefficient below one and a lower-than-grand-mean yield, read as stable under normal and mid-late sowing but not high-yielding; no explicit heat tolerance claim -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366836667_Stability_against_heat_stress_in_genotypes_of_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L
- Stability in phenology and yield under varied temperatures (25 genotypes) was reported, but the retrieved text does not confirm RVSSG 63 among the named genotypes -- No evidence found for RVSSG 63 specifically; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366614322_Stability_in_Phenology_Yield_and_Yield_Attributes_of_Chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_Genotypes_under_Various_Temperature_Conditions
- Drought, flood, submergence, salinity: No evidence found for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- RVSSG 63 entry (CSC table): moderately resistant to chickpea stunt -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- RVSSG 63 entry (CSC table): tolerant to pod borer and pulse beetle in storage -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Raj Vijay Kabuli gram 101 (JSC 42) entry (Seednet name, 2011/2012 release, NOT confirmed for 2020): moderately resistant to wilt; resistant to Fusarium wilt and moderately tolerant to pod borer -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Wilt, dry root rot, Botrytis grey mould, Ascochyta blight for RVSSG 63: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- CSC table row for the RVSSG 63 entry gives 20-23 q/ha yield and 105-165 days maturity, but row alignment is garbled; treat as unverified -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- ICAR-IIPR AICRP chickpea report (2021-22) row for the 2020 entry (RVSSG 63): reports a yield figure near 16.37 q/ha and 147 days, large seed (100-seed weight about 39.5 g), NWPZ timely sown; the row is garbled and column mapping is uncertain -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Raj Vijay Kabuli gram 101 (JSC 42) entry (Seednet name): reports 1500-1800 kg/ha, 109 days, 40.6 g/100 seed, recommended for timely-sown irrigated kabuli areas of Madhya Pradesh; not confirmed for the 2020 release -- https://www.rvskvv.net/index.php/research/significant-achievements
- Multi-location or FPVS trials naming this variety: No evidence found (national TCGC/FPVS results name other lines) -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8703834/

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage ICCV 2 x BG 256 is attributed to Raj Vijay Kabuli Gram 101 (JSC 42), the Seednet-name entry, not to the 2020 RVSSG 63 release -- https://www.rvskvv.net/index.php/research/significant-achievements and https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- The AICRP report row for the 2020 entry shows "JSC 52 x" as parentage, which is garbled and conflicts with the ICCV 2 x BG 256 record; unresolved -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- QTL, marker, or MAS studies for this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution per CSC table: RVSKVV (Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya), AICRP on Chickpea at RAK College of Agriculture, Sehore (MP) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found in any retrieved source; search results gave only unrelated individuals (e.g., Rajeev Kumar Varshney, whose work is not linked to this variety) and those are excluded.
- Station: RAK College of Agriculture, Sehore -- https://rvskvv.net/index.php/academics/institutions-1/254-college-of-agriculture-sehore

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: RVSKVV official site -- https://www.rvskvv.net/
- College of Agriculture, Sehore (RAK), Echhawar Road

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Raj Vijay Kabuli Gram 151 (variety code RVKG 151 / RVSSG 37), chickpea

Name handling: The sources I found name this variety as "Raj Vijay Kabuli Gram 151" (RVKG 151 or RVG 151) in the dpd.gov.in and ICAR-IIPR tables. The Seednet name "Raj Vijay Kabuli gram 101 (JSC 42)" refers to a different variety (Gram 101) in every source I found. Gram 101 findings appear below only under the Seednet heading and are labelled as Gram 101.

Mismatch to resolve: The parentage "ICCV2 X BG 256" in the input matches the ICAR-IIPR table entry for Gram 101, not Gram 151. For Gram 151, the same table lists "Dollar x Kripa." Please check the parentage against the CSC minutes before relying on either.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Gram 151 is listed as tolerant to wilt (Fusarium) in the dpd central-release table. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; http://dpd.gov.in/Varieties/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Gram 151 was found. The only stress-related wilt note for Gram 101 is "moderately resistant to wilt." -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Gram 151 is described as tolerant to wilt, with no other disease or pest resistance listed. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Gram 101 (not 151): moderately resistant to wilt. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Gram 151 is an extra-large-seeded kabuli, sown timely under irrigated conditions, with a duration of about 113 days. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The AICRP report gives 100-seed weight of 54.3 g, a 113-day duration, a yield of 20-21 q/ha, normal sowing, and medium-tall, spreading growth habit for RVKG 151. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- The dpd central table lists yield 17-18 q/ha for Gram 151. This conflicts with the 20-21 q/ha in the AICRP report. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Gram 101 (Seednet name): large-seeded kabuli, early maturing, about 110 days, yield about 20 q/ha, irrigated. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No multi-location trial results specific to Gram 151 were found. The multi-location trial result in the search (Pakistani/Moroccan/Chinese kabuli germplasm) names other varieties and was discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker or genetic study for Gram 151 was found.
- Parentage for Gram 151 in the AICRP table: Dollar x Kripa. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Parentage for Gram 101 in the AICRP table: ICCV 2 x BG 256. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Gram 151 was released by Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (RVSKVV) through its AICRP on Rabi Pulses (RAK) at Sehore, Madhya Pradesh. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- No lead breeder or scientist name for Gram 151 was found in any search result. -- No evidence found (breeder name searched)
- Gram 101 was released by the same institution and centre. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone, postal address or institute contact page URL for Gram 151 or RVSKVV was found in the search results. -- No evidence found
- Institute-level identifiers available from the sources: "RVSKVV, AICRP RAK, Sehore (MP)." Use the RVSKVV and AICRP-RAK websites to find contact details; they were not in the results. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report entry beyond the 2021-22 report, thesis (KrishiKosh), or conference paper naming Gram 151 was found. The research search returned chickpea papers on other varieties and germplasm, which were discarded. -- No evidence found
- AICRP/ICAR Chickpea Project Coordinator's report (2021-22), which contains the Gram 151 variety entry: ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea (2023). Chickpea varietal table. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No seed source (NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or dealer) naming Gram 151 was found. The seed-related pages returned were for other varieties or other states and were discarded. -- No evidence found

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Gram 151 is listed for Madhya Pradesh, timely-sown and irrigated conditions. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Year of release: 2019 per the dpd and AICRP tables. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Gram 101 (Seednet name): released 2011 or 2012 for Madhya Pradesh, with the release year differing between tables. -- http://dpd.gov.in/Varieties/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf ; https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

drought.details: The IIAU entry describes GJGK 1617 as moderately tolerant to drought. No drought mechanism (root traits, osmotic adjustment, biomass or yield-under-stress data) was found in the digest. The ICAR-IIPR report describes the variety as suitable for timely-sown irrigated conditions in the North West Plain Zone and released for the West Central Zone including Gujarat; this is a irrigated-condition recommendation and does not itself establish drought tolerance. Seednet-name evidence for Sorath Kabuli 2 (GKG 2) describes irrigated recommendation and is a different variety, so it was not used for this rating.

heat.details: No evidence found in the digest on heat tolerance for GJGK 1617.

salinity.details: No evidence found in the digest on salinity tolerance for GJGK 1617.

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest on flood tolerance for GJGK 1617.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to white rust and stag head; moderately resistant to downy mildew (IIAU entry). Good resistance to stunt disease (dealer listing, not a research source). No peer-reviewed field disease screening for GJGK 1617 was found; wilt and Ascochyta data in the digest relate to other varieties and were not used.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to major insect pests as listed in the JAU/IIAU entry. Low pod borer damage reported in a dealer listing (not a research source). No further pest screening data found.

agronomic_details.yield: Sources conflict. IIAU entry: about 13.83 q/ha average seed yield and 12-15 q/ha under recommended practices. ICAR-IIPR report: 17-18 q/ha. Dealer listing: 7.5-11 quintal/acre (approximately 18.6-27.2 q/ha on conversion; the dealer figure is high relative to research sources and unverified). IIAU entry also gives 5345 kg/ha, which the digest flags as a mixed-crop brochure error (kharif transplanted entry, treated as unverified).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Multi-location AICRP (Junagadh) trial data for this variety were not retrieved.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for timely-sown irrigated conditions in the North West Plain Zone per ICAR-IIPR report; released for the West Central Zone including Gujarat (ICAR-IIPR report). The IIAU kharif transplanted recommendation conflicts with rabi chickpea sources and is treated as an error until verified.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 139-144 days (IIAU entry); 100-115 days (ICAR-IIPR report). The two sources conflict and the CSC record states Not specified.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 89-107 cm; profuse branching; 17-23 sympodia; long staple (26.8 mm); seed size 42.6 g/100 seeds (IIAU entry); 43.5 g/100 seeds (ICAR-IIPR report); 43.5 g test weight (dealer listing); dal recovery 67.45%, protein 23.60%, iron 63.78 ppm, zinc 35.40 ppm (dealer listing). Kabuli type.
agronomic_details.field_trials: IIAU entry: 12-15 q/ha under recommended practices; about 13.83 q/ha average seed yield. ICAR-IIPR chickpea progress report 2021-22: 17-18 q/ha, 100-115 days, released for West Central Zone including Gujarat, suitable for timely-sown irrigated conditions in North West Plain Zone. Dealer listing: 7.5-11 quintal/acre, with the quality traits noted above (not a research trial). No multi-location AICRP trial data for GJGK 1617 found.
