search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Gujarat Kabuli Gram 1 (Sorath Kabuli 1), chickpea, GJGk 1617

Searches run: 4 web_search queries (variety/release, breeder/institution, research/publications, seed availability). Name check: the CSC name "Gujarat Kabuli Gram 1 (Sorath Kabuli 1)" matches the GKG 1 sources below. The Seednet name "Sorath Kabuli 2 (Gujarat Kabuli Gram 2)" refers to GKG 2, a different variety per JAU's 2023 recommendations, so Seednet-name evidence is listed separately.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderately tolerant to drought; GJGK 1617 is described as a kabuli variety with ~13.83 q/ha average seed yield and 139-144 days maturity -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- Source entry also states yield 5345 kg/ha, released for Gujarat (kharif, transplanted); this conflicts with the other sources and appears to be a mixed-crop brochure entry -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- Suitable for timely-sown irrigated conditions in the North West Plain Zone; released for the West Central Zone including Gujarat; 17-18 q/ha, 100-115 days -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Seednet-name evidence (GKG 2): recommended to farmers under irrigated conditions as an early-maturing kabuli variety -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//research_accomplishments_and_recommendations_2023_20251219_764.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to white rust and stag head; moderately resistant to downy mildew -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- Good resistance to stunt disease with low pod borer damage (dealer listing, not a research source) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-kabuli-gram-1-sorath-kabuli-1-gkg-1/
- Moderately resistant to major insect pests (as listed in the JAU entry) -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- No peer-reviewed field disease screening for GJGK 1617 found (wilt/Ascochyta data appear only for other varieties) -- No evidence found beyond the above

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Plant height 89-107 cm, profuse branching, 17-23 sympodia, long staple (26.8 mm); 12-15 q/ha under recommended practices -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- Seed size 42.6 g/100 seeds (IIAU entry); 43.5 g/100 seeds (ICAR-IIPR report); 43.5 g test weight (dealer listing) -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf ; https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-kabuli-gram-1-sorath-kabuli-1-gkg-1/
- Dealer listing: 7.5-11 quintal/acre yield, dal recovery 67.45%, protein 23.60%, iron 63.78 ppm, zinc 35.40 ppm -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-kabuli-gram-1-sorath-kabuli-1-gkg-1/
- Multi-location trial data (AICRP, Junagadh) not retrieved for this variety -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: cross ICC 14195P3 x ICCV 92337 (ICAR-IIPR report; the same report also prints ICCV93337) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Parentage in the CSC record is "Not specified"; the cross above is the only parentage found
- QTL or marker studies for this variety -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Pulses Research Station, Junagadh Agricultural University (JAU), Junagadh, Gujarat -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/pulses-research-station-junagadh
- Station established 1965-66 as a small research scheme; the station page lists GKG 1 among its chickpea varieties -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/pulses-research-station-junagadh
- Lead breeder name(s) -- No evidence found. The IIAU entry mentions JAU officials (Research Director, PG Dean, Registrar) as acknowledgements only, not as breeders.
- Release year: 2022-10-26 in the input record; the dealer listing says 2023 -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-kabuli-gram-1-sorath-kabuli-1-gkg-1/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder names, emails, phone numbers: No evidence found
- Institute-level contact: JAU Pulses Research Station page (no email, phone or postal address appeared in the retrieved text) -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/pulses-research-station-junagadh
- Recommend verifying contact details directly on the JAU site; I did not find an official email or phone for this station in the retrieved results.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2023). Chickpea progress report 2021-22, ICAR-IIPR (AICRP chickpea) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (n.d.). Pulses/Field crop variety release brochure, Indian Agricultural Universities Association (IAUA) News -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2023). Research Accomplishments and Recommendations 2023, Junagadh Agricultural University (covers GKG 2 recommendation) -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//research_accomplishments_and_recommendations_2023_20251219_764.pdf
- Peer-reviewed papers, theses (KrishiKosh) and conference papers specific to GJGK 1617 -- No evidence found
- Not used as variety evidence: Frontiers in Genetics 2022 (wilt pyramiding, 10.3389/fgene.2022.924287) and Poonia et al. FLD papers, which are not about this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Dealer listing for Sorath Kabuli 1 / GKG 1 (Fule Seeds) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-kabuli-gram-1-sorath-kabuli-1-gkg-1/
- Seednet (seednet.gov.in) listing, NSC, State Seed Corporation (GSSC), KVK or SAU seed-sales records for GKG 1 -- No evidence found
- Seednet-name variety (GKG 2 / Sorath Kabuli 2): seed production figures are in the allgujaratnews report -- https://allgujaratnews.in/en/amazing-discovery-of-new-varieties-of-gram-will-revolutionize-agriculture/

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Gujarat (CSC record; ICAR-IIPR report and IIPR zone text list Gujarat within the West Central Zone with Rajasthan, MP, UP Bundelkhand and Maharashtra) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Kharif transplanted recommendation in the IIAU entry conflicts with the rabi chickpea sources and should be treated as an error until verified -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf

drought.details: No search result reports drought tolerance for BL 44. Berseem is described only generally as a winter hardy, short-duration crop with high water requirement, which suggests limited drought tolerance for the crop overall. This is not variety-specific evidence.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat tolerance data found. Berseem is described as winter hardy. The Apni Kheti page gives a sowing temperature of 25-27°C and a harvesting temperature of 15-20°C for the crop in general.

salinity.details: A Scribd crop document says berseem can be grown in saline-sodic soils. This is a crop-level statement, and no BL 44-specific salinity evaluation was found.

flood.details: No flood tolerance data for BL 44 in the results.

disease_resistance.summary: No BL 44-specific disease reaction found. The Apni Kheti page reports resistance to stem rot and root rot, and immunity to downy mildew, for other listed berseem varieties; the snippets attribute these to the varieties described near BL 43 and Bundel Berseem 3, not clearly to BL 44. These findings should not be transferred to BL 44.

pest_resistance.summary: No BL 44-specific pest reaction found.

agronomic_details.yield: In a 2022 comparative trial reported in The Pharma Journal, BL-44 gave a green fodder yield of 435.1 q/ha, compared with 469.1 q/ha for BL-43. The other figures in the snippet (74.9 for BL-44 versus 83.0 for BL-43; 2.90 versus 3.13; 0.50 versus 0.55) are unlabelled and probably dry matter yield and economic parameters, but the snippet does not say which.
agronomic_details.stability: Not reported across environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The recommended area covers Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Jharkhand, Bihar, Eastern Uttar Pradesh and Odisha, per the CSC data. No agro-climatic zone detail was found.

drought.details: Specific drought tolerance for BL-43 is not detailed. However, berseem (Egyptian clover) in general is recognized for its drought tolerance, with breeding programs aiming to select drought-tolerant genotypes under water stress conditions. It is described as being among the most drought-tolerant cover crops that produce significant biomass.

heat.details: Specific heat tolerance for BL-43 is not detailed. Berseem (Egyptian clover) breeding programs aim to select heat-tolerant and late-maturing lines. While it can show increased antioxidant activity under elevated temperatures as a coping mechanism, some reports indicate it is less heat-tolerant than certain other vetch varieties.

salinity.details: Specific salinity tolerance for BL-43 is not detailed. Berseem (Egyptian clover) can be cultivated in saline-sodic soils, and studies have identified ecotypes with salinity and alkalinity tolerance. Research has also evaluated the salt tolerance of various berseem cultivars and explored methods to enhance it.

flood.details: Specific flood tolerance for BL-43 is not detailed. While research mentions extreme climatic events like heavy rainfall threatening crops and studies on flood tolerance for other species, no direct information on berseem's flood tolerance is provided.

drought.details: No search result gives drought data for Bundel Berseem-9 (JHB-20-1). The official record lists stress reaction as NONE. Only crop-level statements exist. Some sources describe berseem as drought tolerant (ICRISAT field manual; a study-material PDF). The FAO Egyptian clover document mentions screening berseem accessions for drought tolerance. Another source (core.ac.uk crop production text) says Egyptian clover is less drought tolerant than alfalfa. The Tejveer Singh et al. review mentions drought-tolerant lines being identified. None of this can be attributed to this variety. Its tetraploid origin implies no specific drought advantage.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat data. The FAO document says a major objective of berseem breeding is to select heat-tolerant and late-maturing lines (crop-level objective only). Berseem is a winter-season crop.

salinity.details: No variety-specific data. Crop-level sources say berseem tolerates relatively high salt concentrations (FAO hay crops chapter). The FAO Egyptian clover document refers to screening ecotypes for salinity and alkalinity tolerance. A study note says Bundel Berseem-3 shows tolerance to soil alkalinity, which is a different variety.

flood.details: No variety-specific data. Sources conflict at crop level: FAO says berseem thrives on heavy, moist soils and tolerates waterlogging, while a study-material PDF says the crop does not tolerate waterlogging.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bundel Berseem Single Cut-1 (JBSC-1), berseem (Trifolium alexandrinum)

Name note: The CSC name "Bundel Berseem Single Cut-1" and the Seednet name "JBSC-1" both appear in the sources below. Each line states which name its page uses. Four searches were run.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Under a water-withdrawal trial, the single-cut JBSC-1 gave the highest dry-matter water use efficiency among the varieties tested at the 10-day interval. This is a water-use result, not a formal drought-tolerance rating. Name used: JBSC-1 -- https://publications.rmsi.in/index.php/rma/article/view/1158
- No evidence found for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance under either name.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found under either name. The search returned only generic berseem pages.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity: 110 days to 50% flowering and 165 days from seedling to seed maturity; described as early maturing. Name used: Bundel Berseem Single Cut-1 -- https://www.leafconagro.com/berseem-variety-jbsc-1-bundel-berseem-single-cut-1/
- Yield: green fodder 38.3 t/ha and dry matter 5.98 t/ha (single cut). Name used: Bundel Berseem Single Cut-1 -- https://www.leafconagro.com/berseem-variety-jbsc-1-bundel-berseem-single-cut-1/
- Quality: average CP 18.41%, IVDMD 58.20%, NDF 47.43%, ADF 32.37%. Name used: Bundel Berseem Single Cut-1 -- https://www.leafconagro.com/berseem-variety-jbsc-1-bundel-berseem-single-cut-1/
- Agronomic traits: tall, single cut, bold-seeded, self-compatible, suited to hay. Name used: JBSC-1 -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=166
- Phosphorus trial (2016): JBSC-1 was one of seven genotypes at 60, 80 and 100 kg P2O5/ha. Dry-matter and crude-protein figures are reported; JBSC-1 yielded 614.78 in the first column, with units not clearly stated in the snippet. Name used: JBSC-1 -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2016/06/40-43.pdf
- Seed-production table: JBSC-1, released 2018, from EC 318954, IGFRI Jhansi, with a 150–200 figure in the table (units not stated in the snippet). Name used: JBSC-1 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11336856/

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: selection from exotic collection EC-318954 introduced from Germany. Recurrent selection was used. Cross-pollinated, with more than 85% outcrossing. Name used: Bundel Berseem Single Cut-1 -- https://www.leafconagro.com/berseem-variety-jbsc-1-bundel-berseem-single-cut-1/
- The seed-production review gives the same origin (EC 318954 from Germany). Name used: JBSC-1 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11336856/
- No QTL, marker or genomic evidence found under either name.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Grassland and Fodder Research Institute (IGFRI), Jhansi. Name used: JBSC-1 -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=166 and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11336856/
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. The authors of the 2025 water-use paper are IGFRI and other ICAR staff, but the paper does not name a breeder for this variety, so they are not attributed as breeders.

CONTACT DETAILS

VARIETY NAME CHECK
Searches were run under both names. Evidence for "Jawahar Barley 1" (JB-110) is barley. Evidence for the Seednet name "JAWAHAR BARSEEM-1" is berseem (Egyptian clover, Trifolium alexandrinum), a different crop. The parentage in the record (Chhindwara government dairy farm) matches the berseem JB-1 selection, not a barley line. The record mixes the two, so the barley entry needs checking against the CSC/Seednet records before use.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No barley-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data found for Jawahar Barley 1 -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf (notification list only)
- Berseem: general statements that berseem varieties carry tolerance to frost, cold, and salinity, plus stem rot and root rot, but these are not specific to JB-1 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11336856/

DISEASE AND PEST
- No disease or pest resistance data found for Jawahar Barley 1 (barley) -- searched, none found.
- Berseem: the same PMC review lists stem rot, root rot, and fall armyworm as biotic stresses that berseem varieties are developed against; no JB-1 scores given -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11336856/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Barley: no yield, maturity, or trial data found for Jawahar Barley 1.
- Berseem JB-1: green fodder yield of 700–750 q/ha and high regeneration potential, recorded in a table of 1982 release -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11336856/
- Berseem JB-1: a forage comparison trial in Anand, Gujarat reports dry matter and quality values for JB-1 -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/168-175.pdf

heat.details: No heat-tolerance data for JB 07-15 or JB-05-09 were found. Crop-level note only: berseem germination needs about 13-15.5 C and growth slows in severe cold. This is not variety-specific and does not establish heat tolerance.

salinity.details: The digest states that berseem in general tolerates salinity. No variety-specific salinity evidence was found for JB 07-15 or JB-05-09, so the variety level is recorded as unknown. Crop-level statement only.

flood.details: No flood-tolerance data were found for JB 07-15 or JB-05-09.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease-resistance evidence was found for JB 07-15. JB-5 (a different 2005 release, not JB 07-15) is listed with resistance to stem rot. Berseem breeding targets root rot and stem rot resistance at crop level only, not tied to any variety. Do not attribute JB-5 stem rot resistance to JB 07-15.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest-resistance evidence was found for JB 07-15. The digest reports weed pressure (Cichorium intybus and Chenopodium album reducing green fodder and seed yield by roughly 25-35%), but this is not tied to any variety and is not pest resistance. No insect or other pest data were found.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Not found in searched sources for JB 07-15 beyond the ground-truth recommended states listed in the variety profile. Digest reports JB-05-09 was recommended for Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand, which applies to that variety, not JB 07-15.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified for JB 07-15. JB-05-09 (different variety) is listed as tolerant of lodging with medium duration.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) JB-05-09 at CCS HAU Hisar, rabi 2017-18: 687 q/ha green fodder and 93 q/ha dry matter, at par with other entries. (2) JB-05-09 grown in an AICRP-style field trial at Jabalpur under standard practice; weeds were mainly dicots (source cited is a rice biostimulant paper, so the source-to-claim link is unclear). (3) AICRP multi-location herbicide trial at Jabalpur, Rahuri and Urulikanchan (2012-15); variety not named in retrieved text, so JB 07-15 cannot be linked. (4) 2023-24 AICRP phosphorus trial at Urulikanchan (Pune) with four promising genotypes and two checks; genotype names not in retrieved text, so JB 07-15 is not confirmed. (5) JB 07-15: no yield, trial, or maturity data found under this name.

Breeding-method context only: JB-5 was developed by recurrent selection from colchicine-treated material (polyploidy breeding, 2005). JB-05-09 was selected from an irradiated population of JB-1. These are breeding origins of other varieties, not JB 07-15. Berseem is largely self-incompatible with a narrow genetic base, which limits seed set (crop-level).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- JB-05-09 (Seednet name "Jawahar Berseem 05-9"): listed as tolerant of lodging, with medium duration. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11336856/
- JB-5 (2005 release, a different variety): listed with resistance to stem rot. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11336856/
- Berseem in general: germination needs about 13-15.5 °C, growth slows in severe cold, and the crop tolerates salinity. No drought, heat, or submergence data for JB 07-15 or JB-05-09 were found. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/1cb43291-2445-43cf-8aa4-a0de39dd90ab/content ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trifolium_alexandrinum
- JB 07-15 (CSC name): no stress-tolerance evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- JB-5: resistance to stem rot. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11336856/
- Berseem breeding targets: root rot and stem rot resistance (crop-level, not variety-specific). -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2405844024117665 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382916858_Quality_seed_production_scenario_of_Egyptian_clover_Trifolium_alexandrinum_in_India_A_24-year_retrospective_analysis
- Weed pressure: weeds such as Cichorium intybus and Chenopodium album reduce green fodder and seed yield by roughly 25-35%, but this was not tied to either variety. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1665&context=igc
- JB 07-15: no disease or pest evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- JB-05-09: 650-680 q/ha green fodder; recommended for Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11336856/
- JB-5: 550-580 q/ha green fodder. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11336856/
- JB-05-09 at CCS HAU Hisar, rabi 2017-18: 687 q/ha green fodder and 93 q/ha dry matter, at par with other entries. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/1cb43291-2445-43cf-8aa4-a0de39dd90ab/content
- JB-05-09 was grown in an AICRP-style field trial at Jabalpur using standard practice; weeds were mainly dicots. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380720265_Effect_of_biostimulants_on_growth_and_yield_of_rice
- AICRP multi-location herbicide trial at Jabalpur, Rahuri and Urulikanchan (2012-15); variety not named in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339377005_Effect_of_different_herbicides_on_weed_control_efficiency_fodder_and_seed_yields_of_berseem_Trifolium_alexandrinum_L_in_central_India
- 2023-24 AICRP phosphorus trial at Urulikanchan (Pune) with four promising genotypes and two checks; genotype names not in retrieved text, so JB 07-15 is not confirmed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/395199382_Growth_Forage_Yield_and_Quality_of_Berseem_Trifolium_alexandrinum_L_Genotypes_under_Different_Phosphorus_Levels
- JB 07-15: no yield, trial, or maturity data found under this name.

GENETICS AND QTL
- JB-05-09: selected from an irradiated population of JB-1. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11336856/
- JB-5: recurrent selection from colchicine-treated material; polyploidy breeding, 2005. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11336856/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331017277_Genetic_Improvement_of_Berseem_Trifolium_alexandrinum_in_India_Current_Status_and_Prospects
- Berseem is largely self-incompatible with a narrow genetic base, which limits seed set. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382916858_Quality_seed_production_scenario_of_Egyptian_clover_Trifolium_alexandrinum_in_India_A_24-year_retrospective_analysis
- No QTL or marker study for JB 07-15 or JB-05-09 was found. -- (search returned none)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution for all JNKVV varieties: Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (JNKVV), Jabalpur. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/1cb43291-2445-43cf-8aa4-a0de39dd90ab/content
- JB-5 was bred at JNKVV in 2005; JB-05-09 was notified in 2019. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331017277_Genetic_Improvement_of_Berseem_Trifolium_alexandrinum_in_India_Current_Status_and_Prospects ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11336856/
- Coordinating program: AICRP on Forage Crops, linked to ICAR-IGFRI Jhansi, established 1970. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339377005_Effect_of_different_herbicides_on_weed_control_efficiency_fodder_and_seed_yields_of_berseem_Trifolium_alexandrinum_L_in_central_India ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380720265_Effect_of_biostimulants_on_growth_and_yield_of_rice
- Lead breeder names for JB 07-15 or JB-05-09: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS

PUBLICATIONS

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: ANANTHA (Groundnut)

Name note: The input gives variety_name "ANANTHA" and seednet_variety_name "Unknown". No search returned a Seednet page, so every finding below refers to the name "Anantha" as it appears in the source, not to a confirmed Seednet record. The search also returned "Anantha Jyoti" (ICGV 91114), a different name, and "Ananta" planters and kernel graders; I have excluded all of these as unverified for this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Anantha was one of several groundnut genotypes tested for drought tolerance at the ICAR-Directorate of Groundnut Research Regional Research Station, Anantapur, over the 2017 to 2019 rainy seasons, and it sat close to the centre of the pod-yield biplot, which indicates stable performance -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-38581-0
The same paper says some Indian groundnut cultivars are reported as drought tolerant, but that such claims had not been confirmed in drought hot spots, which is why the Anantapur trial was run -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-38581-0

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searched; no page names Anantha with a disease or pest reaction. The DAC national table lists other varieties' resistances only -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Aparajita (Clitoria ternatea), JGCT-2013-3 (Titli)

Search note: 4 web_search queries were run, the maximum allowed. Results were dominated by herbal-medicine pages, and none of them documented this variety's release. Every heading below reports what was found or that nothing was found. Name note: "Aparajita" is the CSC release-minute name and "Aprajita" is the Seednet name. The evidence below refers to the plant species or to unrelated Aparajita material unless stated otherwise. No result mentioned JGCT-2013-3 or Titli.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for the cultivar. Only a tissue-culture study on acid stress in butterfly pea was returned, and it does not concern this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376057823_Tolerance_Level_of_Butterfly_Pea_Clitoria_ternatea_L_to_Stress_Acidity_Through_Tissue_Culture_Technique

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for multi-location or AICRP trials of this variety. The only related ICAR material is a DMAPR, Anand (Gujarat) report on flower-colour and petal-type polymorphism in Aparajita, which describes accession variation and does not report yield or trial performance. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JMAP/article/view/25996

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for QTL or marker studies of this variety. The flower-colour polymorphism paper above is the closest morphological-variation study. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JMAP/article/view/25996

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No breeder name, developing scientist, or ICAR-IGFRI variety page was found. The input record names ICAR-IGFRI, Jhansi as the institution, but no search result confirmed that attribution. The results that mention Aparajita came from DMAPR Anand and ICAR-CTCRI Thiruvananthapuram, which are not the listed institution. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/61419

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, or postal address appeared in the results. The IGFRI contact page was not retrieved and should be checked directly before the record is finalised.

PUBLICATIONS
Bishoyi, A. K., & Geetha, K. A. (2012). Polymorphism in flower colour and petal type in Aparajita (Clitoria ternatea). Open Access Journal of Medicinal and Aromatic Plants, 3, 212-214 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JMAP/article/view/25996 (The ICAR listing gives 2013 as the year and the citing paper gives 2012. The year needs verification.)
Raju, S. (year not shown in snippet). Assessment of chemical diversity in Clitoria ternatea accessions by an improved and validated HPTLC method. Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences, 86(9) -- https://doi.org/10.56093/ijas.v86i9.61419 (ICAR-CTCRI; a chemical-diversity study, not a variety-performance study.)

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No Seednet, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, or SAU listing was found for "Aprajita" or "Aparajita". The only seed results were commercial okra (bhindi) retailers, which are unrelated to this forage legume. -- https://www.kulanursery.com/seed-store/p/indian-okra-seeds

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No external source confirmed the list. The only support is the input record: Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, south Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. This is unverified.

DATA-QUALITY FLAGS FOR REVIEWER
1. The Seednet record lists this variety under "BHINDI (OKRA)", which conflicts with the crop (Clitoria ternatea). This is probably a crop-mapping error on the portal and should be corrected or confirmed on seednet.gov.in.
2. The release date (2018-08-10) and the parentage ("Not specified") come only from the input record.
3. Searches did not reach seednet.gov.in, icar.org.in, KrishiKosh, or IGFRI pages directly. A targeted follow-up search on those domains is recommended.

disease_resistance.summary: Yellow vein mosaic disease (YVMV): GAO-5 is described as resistant to YVMV compared with the checks GO 2 and Pusa Sawani. This is evidence for GAO-5 (the Seednet name), not confirmed for GAO 7 or AOL 12-52. The GAO-5 release area is described as the YVMV-prone area of Gujarat. No other disease data were found.

pest_resistance.summary: Sucking pests: GAO-5 is reported to have a low population of sucking pests compared with the checks GO 2 and Pusa Sawani. This is the only pest evidence found, it applies to GAO-5 rather than GAO 7 or AOL 12-52, and no data were found for GAO 7 or AOL 12-52.

agronomic_details.yield: Not available for GAO 7 or AOL 12-52. For GAO-5, the release notice reports an average yield of 141 q/ha, with green fruit yield 36% and 56% higher than the checks GO 2 and Pusa Sawani respectively.
agronomic_details.stability: AOL-12-52 x GJO-3 (a hybrid combination, not the variety itself) showed above-average stability in a multi-environment AMMI study. No stability data were found for GAO 7 or AOL 12-52 alone.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The GAO-5 release is for the YVMV-prone area of Gujarat. The input states (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Odisha) are not supported by any evidence in the digest for this variety. The Chhattisgarh, Orissa and Andhra Pradesh list found in the search belongs to Shitla Jayoti, a different variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) GAO-5 release trial: average yield of 141 q/ha reported in the release notice. (2) GAO-5 versus checks: 36% higher green fruit yield than GO 2 and 56% higher than Pusa Sawani. (3) AOL-12-52 general combining ability: significant and desirable GCA for yield per plant and related traits in a South Gujarat study. (4) Line x tester study: AOL-12-52 used as a parent, with significant general and specific combining ability effects. (5) AOL-12-52 x GJO-3 multi-environment AMMI trial: above-average stability. (6) Silicic acid foliar-spray field trial at the Main Vegetable Research Station, Anand, in which GAO-5 was used as a check cultivar. No trial was found that tests GAO 7 directly.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: I searched both names. The evidence covers Gujarat Anand Okra-5 (GAO-5), the Seednet name. I found no release record for "AOL 12-52 Gujarat Anand Okra 7 (GAO 7)" or its release year. AOL 12-52 appears only as a parent in hybrid studies. The input's year_of_release ("NaT") is not a valid date and could not be verified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- GAO-5 is described as resistant to yellow vein mosaic disease (YVMV) compared with checks -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-okra-5-0
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for GAO-5 or AOL 12-52 were found. The heat-tolerance claims I found refer to the hybrid Anand Kranti, not this variety -- https://urbanacres.in/revolutionary-okra-variety-boosts-gujarat-yield/

DISEASE AND PEST
- GAO-5 is reported to have a low population of sucking pests and to be resistant to YVMV compared with the checks GO 2 and Pusa Sawani -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-okra-5-0
- For GAO-5 this is the only pest or disease evidence found. No data were found for GAO 7 or AOL 12-52.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- GAO-5 reported an average yield of 141 q/ha in its release notice and gave 36% and 56% higher green fruit yield than the checks GO 2 and Pusa Sawani -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-okra-5-0
- AOL-12-52 showed significant and desirable general combining ability for yield per plant and related traits in a South Gujarat study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333508586_Combining_ability_studies_for_various_horticultural_traits_in_okra_Abelmoschus_esculentus_L_Moench_under_South-Gujarat_conditions
- AOL-12-52 x GJO-3 showed above-average stability in a multi-environment AMMI study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323937760_Genotype_x_Environment_Interaction_and_Stability_Analysis_for_Earliness_Seed_Yield_and_Fruit_Yield_in_Okra_Using_the_Additive_Main_Effect_and_Multiplicative_Interaction_AMMI
- GAO-5 was used as a check cultivar in a silicic acid foliar-spray field trial at the Main Vegetable Research Station, Anand -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue2/PartZ/8-2-306-538.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- AOL-12-52 is listed as a parent in a line x tester combining-ability study, with significant general and specific combining ability effects -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333508586_Combining_ability_studies_for_various_horticultural_traits_in_okra_Abelmoschus_esculentus_L_Moench_under_South-Gujarat_conditions
- A 2026-dated paper from AAU's Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding (Pravallika et al.) covers DNA markers and hybrid performance in okra. It does not name GAO 7 in the snippet, so its link to this variety is unconfirmed -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41798224/
- No QTL or marker study specific to GAO 7, AOL 12-52 or GAO-5 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The developing institution is Anand Agricultural University (AAU), Anand, Gujarat. The GAO-5 release entry is held by the Main Vegetable Research Station, Anand -- https://aau.in/college-menu/251/236
- Scientists named in AAU okra work are V. I. Joshi and K. B. Kathiria. Their paper is on Anand Komal (GAO 8), not GAO 7 or AOL 12-52 -- https://journalijpss.com/index.php/IJPSS/article/view/4901
- No lead breeder was named for GAO 7 or AOL 12-52.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Main Vegetable Research Station, Anand Agricultural University, Anand 388110, Gujarat. The office phone number was truncated in the search result and could not be recovered -- https://aau.in/college-menu/251/236
- Anand Agricultural University general site (institute-level contact): https://www.aau.in
- No breeder email or phone was found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Joshi, V. I., and Kathiria, K. B. et al. (2024). Assessing High-yielding Variety Anand Komal for Dual-season Cultivation of Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus L. Moench) in Middle Gujarat Agro Climatic Condition. International Journal of Plant & Soil Science -- https://doi.org/10.9734/ijpss/2024/v36i84901 (full author list not confirmed)
- Pravallika, P. L. N., Pandya, M. P., Sakure, A., Joshi, R., and Kumar, S. (year not shown). Integrating nutrient profiling, biochemical traits, and DNA markers for yield improvement in Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus). PubMed -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41798224/
- Combining ability studies for various horticultural traits in okra under South-Gujarat conditions (authors and year not confirmed). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333508586_Combining_ability_studies_for_various_horticultural_traits_in_okra_Abelmoschus_esculentus_L_Moench_under_South-Gujarat_conditions
- Genotype x Environment Interaction and Stability Analysis for Earliness, Seed Yield and Fruit Yield in Okra Using AMMI (authors and year not confirmed). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323937760_Genotype_x_Environment_Interaction_and_Stability_Analysis_for_Earliness_Seed_Yield_and_Fruit_Yield_in_Okra_Using_the_Additive_Main_Effect_and_Multiplicative_Interaction_AMMI
- Journal of Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry 2019; 8(2): 1552-1558 (silicic acid trial using GAO 5). Phytojournal -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue2/PartZ/8-2-306-538.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP/ICAR report specific to GAO 7 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Gujarat Farm Seeds Private Limited, 101 Jemsons House, Near Laxmi Cinema, Cross Roads, Anand 388001 (private dealer). Listed as a seller of okra seed; GAO-5 or GAO 7 is not named. Managing Director listed as Sagar Shah -- https://www.tradeindia.com/gujarat-farm-seeds-private-limited-35275535/
- The indiamart listing offers Komal Gold okra seed; it is not identified as GAO-5 or GAO 7 -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/okra-bhindi-seeds-komal-gold-21389526755.html
- AAU offers the hybrid Anand Kranti at a subsidised rate. This is not GAO 7 -- https://urbanacres.in/revolutionary-okra-variety-boosts-gujarat-yield/
- No Seednet, NSC, state seed corporation or KVK listing for GAO-5 or GAO 7 was found. Seednet was not directly searched.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- GAO-5 was released for the YVMV-prone area of Gujarat -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-okra-5-0
- The GAO-5 release list gives 2011 (42nd SSSC) -- https://aau.in/variety_released
- The AAU crop-variety list gives notification 421/2016 dated 29/12/2016 for GAO-5. This conflicts with the 2011 release year and needs checking -- https://aau.in/college-menu/251/236
- The states in the input (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Orissa) are not supported by any evidence for this variety. The Chhattisgarh/Orissa/Andhra Pradesh list I found is for Shitla Jayoti, a different variety -- https://www.vantikatech.com/2020/02/improved-varieties-of-okra-bhindi.html?m=1

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Gujarat Okra / Gujarat Okra-2 (okra, Abelmoschus esculentus)

Search status: the search budget ran out after 4 queries, so several headings rest on thin evidence. The snippets I could read were short, and I did not open the full pages.

Name note: the CSC name is "Gujarat Okra" and the Seednet name is "Gujarat Okra-2". The only source I found calls the material "Gujarat Okra Hybrid-2 (GOH-2)", so it is unclear whether that refers to the same entry. Findings below are attributed to the name used in each source.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searched, but no stress-tolerance data (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) appeared for Gujarat Okra or Gujarat Okra-2.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Searched, but no disease or pest resistance data appeared.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Partial. A Junagadh University (JAU) characteristics document lists "Gujarat Okra Hybrid-2 (GOH-2)" and describes its pods as green, tender and attractive. No maturity, yield or trial data was found in the snippet. -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//vrs_imp_charactristics_of_varities_20260512_1553.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Searched, but no parentage, hybrid cross details or marker studies were found. The input record also gives parentage as "Not specified".

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Partial. The JAU Vegetable Research Station, Junagadh, is listed as a JAU research unit alongside the Research, Training & Testing Centre (RTTC) and Cotton Research Station, Khapat. No breeder or scientist name was found. -- http://www.jau.in/index.php/2-init-content/research/103-vegetable-research-station

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level only. No breeder contact was found. The station page confirms the station's name and location (Junagadh) but no email, phone or postal address appeared in the snippet. Obtain these from the JAU contact page or the Vegetable Research Station page at the URL above.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. One ResearchGate result on sowing time in okra varieties under Jalandhar conditions came up, but the snippet did not show that Gujarat Okra or Gujarat Okra-2 was among the varieties tested, so I have not listed it. No DOI or report for this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Weak. An IndiaMART listing from Vraj Agri Seeds (Sanand, Gujarat) offers "hybrid and OP okra seeds" at ₹1000/kg. The snippet does not name Gujarat Okra-2, so this does not confirm availability of the variety. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/hybrid-and-op-okra-seeds-24126622855.html
No official seed source (NSC, Gujarat State Seed Corporation, JAU seed sales, Seednet listing) was checked, because the search budget was exhausted.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Input record only, not verified by search. The CSC-style list gives: West Bengal, Assam, Uttarakhand, Orissa, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu. No source confirming this list was found.

RELEASE -- Input record only: year of release 2008-10-07, institution Junagadh Agricultural University Vegetable Research Station, variety code Hybrid-2. No notification or gazette source was found to verify these.

heat.details: Heat tolerance up to about 40 °C was reported by AAU scientists in controlled and field conditions. This claim comes from a news article (urbanacres.in), not an official AAU release, so it is treated as medium confidence. The plant is also described as short-statured with short internodes, which is reported to make it less prone to wind damage (AAU and news sources); wind damage is not one of the stress categories requested, so this is noted here only for context.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. No salinity tolerance evidence was found.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. No flood tolerance evidence was found.

disease_resistance.summary: Yellow vein mosaic disease (YVMV) and enation leaf curl disease (ELCV/OLCV) field prevalence was reported as lower than in the checks GJOH 4, GAO 5 and Pusa Sawani. This is a comparative field observation, not a formal resistance rating. Formal resistance rating for YVMV or OLCV: No evidence found.

pest_resistance.summary: Damage from jassid, whitefly and shoot and fruit borer was reported as lower than in the checks GJOH 4, GAO 5 and Pusa Sawani. No formal resistance rating was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 140 q/ha (AAU sources). A news article reports 16,500 kg/ha (165 q/ha), which differs from the AAU figure. In middle Gujarat trials the mean was 163 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Yield advantage was reported in two sets of trials: across Gujarat (20.00, 23.12 and 30.08 per cent higher than GJOH 4, GAO 5 and Pusa Sawani) and in middle Gujarat (30.59, 38.02 and 55.70 per cent higher than the same checks). No broader multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Gujarat under kharif season and irrigated conditions. The short stature is reported to make the plant less prone to wind damage. Adaptation or ecology details beyond this: Not available.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not available (no evidence found in searched sources)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: 9. Ten fruits weight (g): 137, 10. Stem colour: a. Seedling Stage: Green, b. Maturity stage: Reddish, 11. Leaf shape: Deeply lobbed
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Across Gujarat: fruit yield 20.00, 23.12 and 30.08 per cent higher than GJOH 4, GAO 5 and Pusa Sawani. (2) Middle Gujarat: yield 30.59, 38.02 and 55.70 per cent higher than GJOH 4, GAO 5 and Pusa Sawani, at a mean of 163 q/ha. (3) Disease and pest field observations: YVMV, ELCV, jassid, whitefly and shoot and fruit borer damage lower than the same checks (see disease and pest sections). (4) Quality traits: mucilage 28.51 g/kg and chlorophyll-a 0.400 mg/g, both higher than the checks. (5) Fruit description: dark green, tender and smooth with a narrow acute apex; leaf margins strongly serrated. Maturity, sowing and seed rate for this hybrid: No evidence found. Note: the record lists sowing season kharif, spacing 60 cm x 30 cm, fertilizer 100-50-50 NPK kg/ha and seed rate 8-10 kg/ha, but these are not confirmed for variety 205 by the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Gujarat Okra Hybrid 205 (okra)

Search budget note: the 4-search limit was reached. Searches 1 and 4 used the same query, so the topic 3 research query ran once and the seed query was not run separately. Topics with no hits are marked "No evidence found" below. The release-minutes name and the Seednet name were both checked. The Seednet name "Gujarat Okra Hybrid-2" appears only in a Junagadh (JAU) document, which describes a different hybrid (GOH 2), so no Seednet evidence for variety code 205 was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Plant is short-statured with short internodes, and the reduced height is described as making it less prone to wind damage -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-okra-hybrid-205-anand-kranti ; https://urbanacres.in/revolutionary-okra-variety-boosts-gujarat-yield/
- Heat tolerance up to about 40 °C was reported by AAU scientists in controlled and field conditions. This comes from a news article, not an official AAU release -- https://urbanacres.in/revolutionary-okra-variety-boosts-gujarat-yield/
- Drought, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST:
- Field prevalence of yellow vein mosaic disease and enation leaf curl disease was reported as lower than in the checks GJOH 4, GAO 5 and Pusa Sawani -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-detail/27577
- Jassid, whitefly and shoot and fruit borer damage was reported as lower than in the same checks -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-detail/27577
- Formal resistance rating for YVMV or OLCV: No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Release year 2023; area of release Gujarat, kharif season, irrigated condition; average yield 140 q/ha; originating centre MVRS, Anand -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-okra-hybrid-205-anand-kranti ; https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-detail/27577
- Fruit yield was 20.00, 23.12 and 30.08 per cent higher than GJOH 4, GAO 5 and Pusa Sawani across Gujarat -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-detail/27577
- In middle Gujarat, yield was 30.59, 38.02 and 55.70 per cent higher than the same checks, at a mean of 163 q/ha -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-detail/27577
- Fruits are dark green, tender and smooth with a narrow acute apex; leaf margins are strongly serrated -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-okra-hybrid-205-anand-kranti
- Higher mucilage (28.51 g/kg) and chlorophyll-a (0.400 mg/g) than the checks -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-detail/27577
- Maturity, sowing and seed rate for this hybrid: No evidence found
- Alternative names reported in news: "Anand Kranti" and "Gujarat Shankar Bhinda 205"; reported yield 16,500 kg/ha -- https://urbanacres.in/revolutionary-okra-variety-boosts-gujarat-yield/

GENETICS AND QTL:
- Parentage conflict: the parentage supplied in the record (JNDOH-02-2 from KS-404 x HRB-108-2) matches the JAU hybrid "Gujarat Okra Hybrid 2 (GOH 2)", not the AAU hybrid 205. Treat the parentage as unverified for variety 205 -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/FVegetableCropsVR.pdf
- No AAU source for variety 205 gives its parentage or breeding method
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- Developing institution: Anand Agricultural University, Main Vegetable Research Station (MVRS), Anand -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-detail/27577
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found on the pages retrieved
- Junagadh (JAU, Vegetable Research Station) is the developer of GOH 2, which has the same parentage as the record. It is not the developer of variety 205 -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/FVegetableCropsVR.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS:
- Main Vegetable Research Station, Anand Agricultural University, Anand 388110 (Gujarat) -- https://aau.in/college-menu/251/236
- Phone: office (02692) 290251; farm (02692) 261817 -- https://aau.in/college-menu/251/236
- Email: rsmvrs@aau.in -- https://aau.in/college-menu/251/236
- Named breeder contact: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS:
- No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, theses or conference papers for variety 205 were found in the search results. Peer-reviewed or report items: No evidence found
- Release-related source: the AAU page mentions the Indian Council of Agricultural Research, New Delhi, but the page does not identify a specific report -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-okra-hybrid-205-anand-kranti

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- AAU said it would sell seed of this hybrid at roughly Rs 2,500/kg, below typical private hybrid prices. The article is about 855 days old, so the price may be out of date -- https://urbanacres.in/revolutionary-okra-variety-boosts-gujarat-yield/
- Seednet listing for code 205: No evidence found
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing: No evidence found beyond the AAU price statement

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- Gujarat, kharif, irrigated conditions -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-okra-hybrid-205-anand-kranti
- Year of release reported as 2023. The record's year field is NaT, and no CSC minutes were found to confirm it -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-detail/27577

salinity.details: No evidence of salinity tolerance for NBH-180. The salt-tolerance mention in the BUAT document is a fruit-crop review citation, not about this hybrid.

flood.details: No evidence found. The waterlogging mention in the SKUAST-J report is general context and not specific to NBH-180.

disease_resistance.summary: NBH-180 is not reported as resistant to any disease. The SKUAST-J AICRP (Vegetable Crops) okra resistant trial evaluated eight entries, with Arka Anamika and NBH-180 as checks. The retrieved snippets do not give disease reaction scores for NBH-180. The ResearchGate review lists NBH-180 among 13 okra hybrids, but the 'moderately tolerant to YVMD and OELCD' note appears next to an IIVR germplasm entry, not NBH-180.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance data for NBH-180 found in the results.

agronomic_details.yield: In a 2019 varietal evaluation (Chemical Science/Chemi Journal), NBH-180 yielded 153.74 q/ha. This was statistically at par with the top hybrid NBH-225 (166.83 q/ha) and Mahabeej-333 (160.49 q/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not assessed across environments in the retrieved material. NBH-180 is repeatedly used as a check or comparator, including in AICRP trials at SKUAST-J and evaluations at BUAT, which suggests it is a benchmark hybrid.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The recommended states span peninsular, central and eastern India (tropical and sub-tropical regions). No agro-climatic zone details found in the results.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: Used as a check with Arka Anamika in the AICRP okra resistant trial at SKUAST-J (2016-17). Evaluated alongside Mona-002, VNR-999 and DOV-1 in BUAT trials that recorded days to first flowering and related traits. Compared in a 2019 hybrid/variety evaluation, where it ranked among the top yielders.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Nirmal-433 (variety_name, CSC minutes; crop: cotton; code NACH-433) / Nirmal-147 (seednet_variety_name; Seednet crop: BHINDI (OKRA))

Search scope: 4 web searches were run (release/variety, Seednet, breeder/contact, research/trials). The searches did not return any page that describes NACH-433 or Nirmal-147 directly. Findings below are either institution-level or from unrelated products, and are labelled as such.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Nirmal-433/NACH-433: No evidence found. Searched under the variety query and the NACH-433 research query; no page described drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for this variety.
Nirmal-147 (Seednet, bhindi/okra): No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
Nirmal-433/NACH-433: No evidence found for resistance to any disease or pest.
Nirmal-147 (Seednet, bhindi/okra): Unrelated okra product pages only. A retail okra listing describes a different "Nirmal" okra hybrid as early and prolific, with no resistance data -- https://www.amazon.com/Nirmal-Okra-Seeds-India-Seed/dp/B08XPP1K5F (not verified as Nirmal-147). A separate okra seed listing for an unrelated variety notes tolerance to YVMV and powdery mildew -- https://seedsofindia.com/products/komal-okra (different variety, not Nirmal-147).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Nirmal-433/NACH-433: No evidence found for maturity, yield or trial results.
Nirmal-147 (Seednet, bhindi/okra): No evidence found beyond the retail listing above, which gives an early-maturity claim of about 38-40 days -- https://www.amazon.com/Nirmal-Okra-Seeds-India-Seed/dp/B08XPP1K5F (unverified for Nirmal-147).
Context only (not variety-specific): the AICRP on Cotton annual report for 2024-25 is coordinated by ICAR-CICR Nagpur -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Nirmal-433/NACH-433: No evidence found. No parentage was found, and the record lists parentage as not specified.
Nirmal-147: No evidence found.
Context only: general cotton QTL studies exist, but none involve NACH-433 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3830114/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Nirmal-433/NACH-433: No breeder or scientist name was found. Institution (company-level): Nirmal Seeds Pvt. Ltd. (NSPL) was established in 1988 at Pachora, Jalgaon district, Maharashtra, and its mandate includes developing hybrids and varieties -- https://www.indiamart.com/nirmal-seeds-pvt-ltd/aboutus.html
Sister NACH-series cotton names from the same company (not the target variety): NACH-6 (Navinya-6) was notified for extra-long fine staple arboreum cotton for the central and south zones, and NACH-12 (Ambika) was described as going for AICRP notification -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/seeds-6506575312.html
Nirmal-147 (Seednet): No evidence found for a Seednet entry or breeder under this name.

CONTACT DETAILS
Nirmal-433/NACH-433: No breeder contact found. Institute-level contacts only:
- Corporate and Register Office: Bhadgaon Road, Pachora, Dist-Jalgaon, Maharashtra, India - 424201 -- https://nirmalseedsindia.com/contact-us/
- Jalgaon office listing names "Pradeep Sapkal (Executive)" with the location Jalgaon, Maharashtra -- https://www.indiamart.com/nirmal-seeds-pvt-ltd/aboutus.html
- A Patna seller listing names "Pankaj Kumar" as seller contact -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/seeds-6506575312.html
- No official email or phone number was found for NSPL in these results.
Nirmal-147 (Seednet): No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Nirmal-433/NACH-433: No evidence found. No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, theses (KrishiKosh) or conference papers mentioning this variety were returned.
Nirmal-147: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Nirmal-433/NACH-433: No seller listing for this cotton variety was found. The only Nirmal seed listings were for okra (bhindi), which is a different crop. A seed retailer lists "Nirmal Seeds Okra (Bhindi)" -- https://www.desikheti.com/collections/buy-okra-seeds-online-at-best-price
A cotton hybrid under the company's Nirmal brand, Nirmal Solar 76 (NCH-4341 BG II), was found; it is a different hybrid and not NACH-433 -- https://kisancenter.com/product/nirmal-nch-4341-cotton-seeds-solar-76-bg2/218062
Nirmal-147 (Seednet): No evidence found on Seednet or any state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer page.
Name discrepancy: the record lists crop as cotton but Seednet lists the same variety name under bhindi (okra). No evidence was found to resolve this.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Nirmal-433/NACH-433: No evidence found. The states in the record (Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Gujarat) could not be verified by these searches.
Nirmal-147 (Seednet): No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The "Nirmal -18 cotton variety" search returned no page on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety. Results were a YouTube video comparing "NIRMAL CHAYA" with a Pakistani BS18 (different variety) -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mqm6m0geuRs

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The same search returned no disease or pest resistance data for NACH-18 or Nirmal -18. The YouTube result above concerns a different variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. The company product-performance page (https://nirmalseedsindia.com/product-performance/) appeared in results, but the retrieved text showed only generic bio-product performance entries and did not name NACH-18 or Nirmal -18. Not confirmed for this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL
Not searched. The tool limit was reached before the genetics/QTL query could run.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. The "Nirmal-147 bhindi okra" search returned only consumer okra seed listings (Amazon, eBay, desikheti.com) and an unrelated Wikipedia biography of Dilbagh Singh Athwal. None names a breeder, institute or station for this variety, so none are attributed to it.
Institution lead only (not evidence of breeder): Nirmal Seeds India, the company site, https://nirmalseedsindia.com/ and https://nirmalseedsindia.com/product-performance/ .
Note: Seednet lists Nirmal-147 under BHINDI (OKRA), while the release record lists cotton. This conflict is unresolved; the okra pages found do not confirm the Seednet entry either way.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No email, phone or postal address for this variety or for Nirmal Seeds Pvt. Ltd. was extracted from the results. The Nirmal Cotton Private Limited address (Panipat, Haryana, https://www.nirmalcotton.com/) belongs to an unrelated yarn company and is discarded. The company site, https://nirmalseedsindia.com/, may carry a contact page; it was not checked.

PUBLICATIONS
Not searched. The tool limit was reached before the research/publications query (papers, AICRP reports, KrishiKosh theses) could run. No citations are recorded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for NACH-18 or Nirmal -18. The cotton-query results included an IndiaMart listing from Nirmal Seeds Private Limited (https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/seeds-6506575312.html), but it names NACH-6 (Navinya-6), a different variety, so it is discarded. The Nirmal Solar 76 NCH-4341 listing (https://kisancenter.com/product/nirmal-nch-4341-cotton-seeds-solar-76-bg2/218062) is a different hybrid and is also discarded. The dedicated seed-availability query (NSC, SAU, KVK, dealers) was not run.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. None of the retrieved pages confirmed the recommended states (Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu). These appear only in the input record, not in any search result.

SEARCH LOG
Four web_search calls were made. Two were the same "Nirmal -18 cotton variety" query (one duplicated by error), one was the Nirmal-147 okra/breeder query, and one was the Nirmal -18 cotton query retried. The research and seed-availability queries were not run because the tool limit was reached. Coverage is therefore incomplete: no publications, genetics, or seed-availability evidence was obtained, and the official Indian sources (seednet.gov.in, ICAR, KrishiKosh, AICRP) were not reached. A follow-up session is needed for queries 3 and 4 and for direct checks of seednet.gov.in and the CSC release notification.

drought_tolerance.technical_details: The drought and water-stress snippets are generic advice or refer to other crops or varieties. The IARI 2022 drought snippet does not name Pusa Kranti as tolerant. No okra-specific drought evidence was found.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The KVK Kishtwar snippet says 'This variety is tolerant to heat and susceptible to major diseases'. It appears in the Pusa Kranti entry, which describes fruits as 'stocky, oblong, dark purple', so it refers to brinjal, not okra. It cannot be applied to okra.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: No variety-specific salinity data. The snippets concern cabbage, rice, or generic soil notes. The Sher-e-Bangla thesis mentions GA treatment of Pusa Kranti in pots, but that is not a salinity tolerance finding.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: Only generic advice to avoid waterlogging (okra cannot tolerate it). No varietal evidence.

submergence_tolerance.technical_details: The submergence-tolerant varieties mentioned in the BAU advisory are paddy (MTU), not okra.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: None verified for okra. The 'susceptible to major diseases' statement likely refers to brinjal. Okra yellow vein mosaic virus (YVMV) resistance is not documented in the results.
disease_resistance.technical_details: No resistance mechanisms or genes identified.

pest_resistance.technical_details: The CBSE Agriculture textbook states 'Punjab Barsati and Pusa Kranti have tolerance to jassid attack' in the context of the okra pest section. This is a textbook statement, not a primary trial. No resistance genes are given.

stress_tolerance_analysis.overall_stress_tolerance: no (insufficient evidence). Only jassid tolerance is weakly supported, and no abiotic stress evidence specific to okra was found.
key_stress_attributes: Jassid tolerance (textbook-level statement, CBSE Agriculture)

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety has several citations: ICAR advisories, the BAU advisory, a CBSE textbook and the TNAU checklist. The only stress-related claim for okra is jassid tolerance, from a textbook. Many snippets confuse okra with brinjal (also called Pusa Kranti), so heat tolerance and disease susceptibility cannot be attributed to okra. There is no Gujarat-specific recommendation, no yield data and no abiotic stress evidence. This fits the 60 tier (citations but weak stress traits).

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Listed in ICAR and state advisories; reported jassid tolerance; dwarf, spreading habit (crop attribution uncertain); no verified abiotic stress data
dashboard_data.state_acronyms: Not specified (BR is mentioned in an advisory only)
dashboard_data.seasons: Kharif (ICAR Kharif advisories); also appears in Rabi advisory lists, though the crop is unclear

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Pusa Kranti (okra) appears in many ICAR and university recommendation lists, with a textbook note of jassid tolerance. Evidence for drought, heat, salinity, flood or disease resistance is absent, and several snippets are really about brinjal's Pusa Kranti. Evidence quality is low and Gujarat suitability is unverified.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Pusa Kranti is a long-listed okra variety (probably IARI-bred) described as dwarf and spreading, but release year, parentage, yield and maturity are not documented in the results. Brinjal data under the same name must be excluded.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: The only okra-specific stress trait is jassid tolerance (CBSE textbook). Abiotic stress tolerance is unknown, and the 'heat tolerant, disease susceptible' statement refers to brinjal. Overall stress tolerance is not demonstrated.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Search note: The search quota ran out after four queries, so the second round of checks (breeder page, contacts, seed sources) could not be completed. Findings come from result snippets only, and I did not open the full pages. Name mapping: "Rajalaxmi" (CSC name) is the name the evidence refers to throughout. "Rajlaxmi" (Seednet name) was searched once, under okra, and matched nothing relevant.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found in snippets. The only tolerance-related text is a NRRI-table fragment that mentions "salinity" next to other varieties, not Rajalaxmi. Not verified.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found specific to Rajalaxmi. A table fragment on the ICAR-CRRI page lists a blast-related entry, but it is not clearly attributed to Rajalaxmi. Not verified. -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Rajalaxmi is listed as a hybrid, irrigated type, with a release year of 2006 and duration of about 135 days. The ResearchGate table shows Rajalaxmi (Hybrid), Irrigated, with numeric columns (5.8, 135, 4.3) whose headings were not visible, so yield values are unconfirmed. -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338966196_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Parentage is not stated in any source, and the hybrid status suggests a cross, but the parents are unknown.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The ICAR-CRRI released-varieties page is titled as a list of varieties developed by ICAR-NRRI, Cuttack, 1968-2019, and includes Rajalaxmi. This suggests NRRI as the developing institution, but the snippet does not state Rajalaxmi's breeder directly. Breeder name: not found. -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338966196_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder, email, phone, or address found. Institute contact page not retrieved. The institute appears to be ICAR-National Rice Research Institute, Cuttack, but its contact details must be obtained from the institute's own website.

PUBLICATIONS -- S.R. Das (2012). Rice in Odisha. IRRI Technical Bulletin 16 (Rice in Odisha, i T B 2012 No. 16) -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf. This names Rajalaxmi among hybrids grown in Odisha. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis was found in the snippets. Remaining items: not searched (quota exhausted).

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The okra query returned only an unrelated private okra seed listing (Advanta Raadhika), which does not relate to this record.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Orissa (Odisha) and Assam. The ICAR-CRRI released-varieties table lists "Orissa, Assam" for Rajalaxmi. This matches the CSC record, which says Orissa is already notified and Assam was recommended as an extension. -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/

DATA DISCREPANCIES TO FLAG
- Release year: the CSC record gives 2010-10-10, while the NRRI/CRRI table gives 2006. Needs checking against the CSC minutes.
- Crop: Seednet lists the entry under BHINDI (OKRA), but every source found identifies Rajalaxmi as a rice hybrid. The Seednet entry appears to be misfiled and should be corrected or verified on the portal.
- Type: the sources describe Rajalaxmi as a hybrid, while the CSC record does not state this.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Uttara (variety_name and seednet_variety_name both "Uttara"; crop "sugarcane" in the release record, but Seednet lists crop "BHINDI (OKRA)")

Search coverage: four web_search queries were run (variety/release, breeder/institution, research papers, seed availability). None returned any page that mentions a variety called Uttara. The evidence below is therefore mostly "No evidence found." The sugarcane/okra crop conflict cannot be resolved from these results, so the record should not be finalised until the variety's crop and developing station are confirmed from the CSC minutes or the Seednet entry.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for Uttara (searched "Uttara sugarcane variety"; results were IISR varietal release lists without Uttara) -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/pages/varietiesreleased.jsp

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for Uttara (the only disease-related hit, a sugarcane red rot article on Academia.edu, concerns cultivar Co 0238, not Uttara) -- https://www.academia.edu/Documents/in/Sugarcane_Cultivation

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for Uttara in sugarcane or okra trial results. The IISR release page lists sugarcane varieties by region but not Uttara -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/pages/varietiesreleased.jsp

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for Uttara

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found naming a breeder or developing station for Uttara. The "Regional Agricultural Research Station" in the record is not identified in any result. Institute-level background for the sugarcane body only: Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research, Lucknow, established 1952 -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Sugarcane_Research (this is not confirmed as Uttara's developer)

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. Institute-level contact for the sugarcane candidate only (unverified for Uttara): IISR, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/pages/varietiesreleased.jsp (no email or phone was extracted from the results)

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for Uttara. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI matching the variety was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for Uttara. The only okra-seed hit was a commercial retail listing for generic Indian desi okra, not a variety named Uttara -- https://www.etsy.com/listing/989761541/free-shipping-40-indian-desi-okra-seeds

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found for Andhra Pradesh. The recorded state is unverified.

Next steps: check seednet.gov.in directly for variety code H0704117 to resolve the crop (sugarcane vs. okra); check the CSC minutes for the 18 January 2013 release; and check Andhra Pradesh SAU/ANGRAU or Regional Agricultural Research Station records. These sources were not reachable with the search budget used.

agronomic_details.yield: Official salient-features table: potential yield 25-26 q/ha. Field results: 20.7 q/ha average (KVK Malkangiri front-line demonstration); 18.8 q/ha in the same demonstration against 8.6 q/ha for the local check; 17.6 q/ha at Ganjam-II (Berhampur) against 11.68 q/ha for Budha Mandia.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources (no multi-environment stability analysis in digest; results come from individual demonstrations and trials).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Demonstrations and trials reported from rainfed and organic conditions in the South Eastern Ghat Zone of Odisha (Malkangiri, Berhampur/Ganjam) and Koraput. Recommended states: Odisha, Bihar, Chhattisgarh (list truncated). Formal agro-climatic fit not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 110-115 days (official salient-features table); 110 days (KVK Malkangiri demonstration); 105-115 days (KVK Ganjam-I FLD 2023-24).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Brown seed (reported in KVK Malkangiri demonstration). The DHAN compendium entry for plant height, ear type, finger number and grain colour is not attributed here because the digest states that source mixes this entry with another line.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) KVK Malkangiri front-line demonstration: average yield 20.7 q/ha; 110-day maturity (variety named Arjun, OEB-526). (2) Same KVK Malkangiri demonstration: 18.8 q/ha for Arjun against 8.6 q/ha for the local check; moderate blast resistance and brown seed also reported. (3) Ganjam-II (Berhampur) demonstration: 17.6 q/ha against 11.68 q/ha for Budha Mandia; the Odisha yield assessment reports higher yield and drought-tolerance traits (fragmentary; no drought trial data). (4) KVK Ganjam-I FLD 2023-24 (Ragi Arjuna, OEB 526): 105-115 days; 5.0 q/ha FLD area record. (5) KVK Koraput report: Kalinga-601 outperformed OEB-526 on yield attributes. (6) Pink stem borer screening at CPR Berhampur included OEB 526; resistance rating not given in excerpt.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: ARJUNA (OEB-526), crop: millet (finger millet/ragi)

Name check: The CSC name ARJUNA and the Seednet name Arjuna (crop BITTER GOURD) are not the same crop. Every source that names OEB-526 treats it as a finger millet (ragi) variety from OUAT Bhubaneswar. The only bitter gourd hit is a private hybrid called "Arjuna," which has no link to OEB-526. It is listed separately below and is not attributed to this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
(evidence for: ARJUNA / OEB-526, finger millet)
- Rated moderately resistant to leaf, neck and finger blast -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- A KVK Malkangiri demonstration reports the same moderate resistance to leaf, neck and finger blast, plus brown seed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388368171_Growth_productivity_quality_and_profitability_of_organic_finger_millet_under_cultivar_and_nutrient_management_options (also https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359893120_A_COMPARATIVE_STUDY_ON_YIELD_PERFORMANCE_OF_FINGER_MILLET_VARIETIES_UNDER_RAINFED_CONDITIONS_IN_SOUTH_EASTERN_GHAT_ZONE_OF_ODISHA)
- An Odisha yield assessment says the variety showed higher yield and drought-tolerance traits; the excerpt is fragmentary and gives no drought trial data -- https://e-planet.co.in/images/Publication/vol-23-1/Yield%20assessment.pdf
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast (leaf, neck, finger): moderately resistant, as above -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- Pink stem borer (Sesamia inferens) screening at CPR Berhampur lists OEB 526 among tested genotypes, but the excerpt does not give its resistance rating -- https://www.entomoljournal.com/archives/2018/vol6issue6/PartM/6-6-63-795.pdf
- Stalk rot, leaf/finger blast beyond the above, and other pests: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- KVK Malkangiri front-line demonstration: 110-day maturity, average yield 20.7 q/ha (variety named Arjun, OEB-526) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359893120_A_COMPARATIVE_STUDY_ON_YIELD_PERFORMANCE_OF_FINGER_MILLET_VARIETIES_UNDER_RAINFED_CONDITIONS_IN_SOUTH_EASTERN_GHAT_ZONE_OF_ODISHA
- Same demonstration: 18.8 q/ha for Arjun, against 8.6 q/ha for the local check -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388368171_Growth_productivity_quality_and_profitability_of_organic_finger_millet_under_cultivar_and_nutrient_management_options
- Ganjam-II (Berhampur) demonstration: 17.6 q/ha, against 11.68 q/ha for Budha Mandia -- https://e-planet.co.in/images/Publication/vol-23-1/Yield%20assessment.pdf
- Official salient-features table: 110-115 days maturity, 25-26 q/ha potential yield -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- KVK Ganjam-I FLD 2023-24 (Ragi "Arjuna", OEB 526): 105-115 days, 5.0 q/ha FLD area record -- https://kvkganjam.org/public/uploads/document_6901924a3944e8.19551751.pdf
- KVK Koraput report: a comparison in which Kalinga-601 outperformed OEB-526 on yield attributes -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388368171_Growth_productivity_quality_and_profitability_of_organic_finger_millet_under_cultivar_and_nutrient_management_options (KVK Koraput PDF: http://kvkkoraput.org/upload/menu_13052025014125.pdf)
- Plant height 105-110 cm, semi-compact ears, 8-9 fingers, white grain (DHAN small millet compendium, which mixes this entry with another line): -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
- Bitter gourd (Seednet crop): No evidence found for OEB-526. The ACSEN "Arjuna" bitter gourd hybrid page is a different product (see SEED AVAILABILITY).

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The parentage conflict is recorded under BREEDER AND INSTITUTION.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: OAUT/OUAT, Bhubaneswar, 2011 release, pedigree SDFM 30 x PE 244 -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- Conflicting record: the DHAN compendium gives a pure-line selection from NAU Waghai, Gujarat, state release 2009, and attributes the notification to the AICSMIP PCU at GKVK Bangalore -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.
- Station: the Pulse Research Station, Berhampur, is described as supplying breeder and foundation seed of new varieties for the district, but the excerpt does not name Arjuna -- https://kvkganjam.org/public/uploads/document_6901924a3944e8.19551751.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level email (from a TNAU page, not an OUAT page): ouatmain@hotmail.com -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/ragi/institutions_schemes.html
- Institute fax (same source): 91-674-2397780
- Postal address (same source): Orissa University of Agriculture & Technology, Bhubaneswar-751003, Orissa, India
- Corresponding author email on a KVK Ganjam-II paper on this variety (author, not breeder): sasmitapriyadarshini@ouat.ac.in -- https://e-planet.co.in/images/Publication/vol-23-1/Yield%20assessment.pdf
- Breeder email/phone: No evidence found.
- Official OUAT contact page URL: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
