search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Dragon (NMH-1247), maize

Name note: The CSC/IIMR listing uses "Dragon (NMH-1247)". The Seednet name "DRAGON" with crop "BITTER GOURD" was not confirmed by any search result. Every page that names Dragon describes it as a maize hybrid, so the evidence below refers to the maize hybrid under both names. Seednet's crop assignment is unverified and should be checked on the portal.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No Dragon-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found. The company listing gives only a general "tolerance to major diseases" claim (see DISEASE AND PEST). -- https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/

DISEASE AND PEST
- The company describes Dragon NMH-1247 as tolerant to major diseases, with no named pathogens or ratings. -- https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/
- No pest resistance evidence specific to Dragon found. Nuziveedu's general R&D statements on downy mildew and fall armyworm were not attributed to Dragon, so they are excluded. -- https://www.exportersindia.com/nuziveeduseeds/seeds.htm ; https://www.accesstoseeds.org/index/south-southeast-asia/company-scorecards/nuziveedu-seeds/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Company listing: crop matures in 80 days, is sold as high-quality silage with high protein, and has a tall plant with a big, well-filled cob. -- https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/
- A third-party seller listing describes a long maturity, medium cob placement, semi-dent golden-yellow grain, and tip filling. This conflicts with the 80-day company figure. -- https://www.exportersindia.com/nuziveeduseeds/seeds.htm
- CSC/IIMR cultivar table gives a yield value of 9.9 for this variety, with the unit not stated in the table. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
- No multi-location trial data, AICRP report entry, or field-trial result for Dragon found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. Searches returned only unrelated maize QTL papers (none naming NMH-1247 or Dragon). Parentage is not specified in the input and was not found in any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Nuziveedu Seeds Limited, Hyderabad, listed as a private developer in the CSC/IIMR table. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
- No named lead breeder or scientist found for Dragon. The company's Wikipedia entry names M. Prabhakara Rao as a key person, but nothing links him to Dragon, so this is not attributed. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuziveedu_Seeds
- No development station found. The company's Guntur and Ahmedabad entities were not used, because the sources do not tie them to Dragon's development.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Company address (third-party listing of Nuziveedu Seeds, Hyderabad): Nsl Icon, Road No 12, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, Andhra Pradesh, Pin-500034, Telangana. Listed by a directory, not verified on the official site. -- https://www.exportersindia.com/nuziveeduseeds/seeds.htm
- Phone numbers on the same directory listing: Sales +91-9953717914; Support +91-9700318318. Not verified against the official site. -- https://www.exportersindia.com/nuziveeduseeds/seeds.htm
- No official email, no breeder contact, and no institute contact page URL for Dragon found. Official company site: https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/
- Excluded: Ahmedabad and Guntur Nuziveedu-named listings are similarly named entities and are not used here.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. Searches of journal and KrishiKosh-type sources returned no paper, thesis or report naming Dragon or NMH-1247. The IIMR cultivar table is a listing, not a publication.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Company product page lists Dragon NMH-1247 as a Nuziveedu maize product. -- https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/
- Directory listing offers Dragon (NMH 1247) hybrid maize seed from Nuziveedu Seeds, Hyderabad. -- https://www.exportersindia.com/nuziveeduseeds/seeds.htm
- No dealer, KVK, state seed corporation or SAU sales listing for Dragon found. Other Nuziveedu maize listings (Danvir 1368, Winner NMH-8352, Bond NMH-007) are different varieties and are excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- CSC/IIMR release table: Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and Western Uttar Pradesh. Notification entry is gazette 112(E) dated 13-01-2016, which differs from the 2015-10-12 release date given in the input. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
- Company page gives a much wider list: Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Delhi, Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamilnadu, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh. This conflicts with the CSC list and should be resolved against the gazette notification. -- https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/

drought.details: No drought tolerance is documented for Dheeraj in the sources found. It is released as a water-use-efficient Spanish bunch type suited to irrigated kharif and rabi cultivation. The RARS table credits 'drought tolerant' to Dharani, not Dheeraj. A 2022 KVK Kalikiri paper reports a yield shortfall in 2019-20 attributed to water shortage during crop growth. Water-use efficiency is not the same as drought tolerance, so no level is assigned.

heat.details: A secondary agri-news article lists heat tolerance for Dheeraj, but the digest states this is not confirmed by a primary source. No primary evidence found.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance documented in the sources found.

flood.details: No flood tolerance documented in the sources found.

disease_resistance.summary: No resistance documented. Stem rot: Dheeraj was used as a susceptible parent (with TCGS 1694, TCGS 2245, Kadiri-6 and Narayani) in a line x tester inheritance study of stem rot resistance, which implies susceptibility; this is an inference, not a direct screening result. No evidence found for resistance to rust, leaf spot, bud necrosis (PBND/PSND) or aflatoxin specific to this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: No resistance documented. No evidence found for resistance to leaf miner, thrips or white grub specific to this variety. The only pest material found is a root grub management study at RARS, which does not name Dheeraj.

agronomic_details.yield: Chittoor district on-farm and front-line demonstrations (2016-17 to 2019-20): mean 22.7 q/ha for Dheeraj versus 18.0 q/ha for Kadiri 6. Seasonal yields reported as kharif 2.37 t/ha and rabi 3.44 t/ha. A 2019-20 yield shortfall attributed to water shortage is noted in the KVK paper. The irrigation-schedule trial reports Kadiri Lepakshi at 3607 kg/ha as outyielding Dheeraj; the Dheeraj value is not given in the digest. RARS yield values are not legible.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the single 2019-20 water-shortage shortfall reported by the KVK paper. No multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated kharif and rabi cultivation (RARS release description). Tested in Chittoor district (Western Mandals). The digest's name check notes that the Seednet entry is Heera under BITTER GOURD; no evidence was used for that entry, and all findings refer to groundnut Dheeraj (TCGS 1073).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 105-110 days (RARS comparison table; Chittoor demonstrations report 105-110 days)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Spanish bunch type (RARS release description). In a morpho-physiological study of 20 genotypes, Dheeraj had the greatest plant height; the full genotype list was not captured. Other morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Chittoor district OFTs/FLDs, 2016-17 to 2019-20: mean yield 22.7 q/ha vs 18.0 q/ha for Kadiri 6; B:C ratio 2.1 vs 1.7; maturity 105-110 days; kharif 2.37 t/ha, rabi 3.44 t/ha. (2) Irrigation-schedule trial (IW/CPE 1.0, 0.8, 0.6) with TAG-24, Dheeraj, Kadiri Lepakshi and Kadiri Chitravathi: Dheeraj was outyielded by Kadiri Lepakshi (3607 kg/ha); Dheeraj's own yield not reported in the digest. (3) RARS Tirupati comparison table: maturity 105-110 days and water-use-efficiency notes; yield columns not interpretable. (4) Morpho-physiological study of 20 genotypes: Dheeraj had the greatest plant height. (5) Genetic enhancement review: Dheeraj TCGS-1073 listed in a table with trait values not legible.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. No QTL or marker study naming this variety was found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. Dheeraj appears as a parent in an F6 RIL population (TAG 24, Dheeraj and Visishta crossed with ICGV 181024) in a high-oleic breeding programme at the Groundnut Breeding Section, RARS Tirupati. No QTL effects were reported. A stem rot inheritance study used Dheeraj as a susceptible parent (see disease_resistance), but no genetic parameters for Dheeraj are reported in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. The high-oleic programme refers to ahfad2 genes affecting oil profile in advanced breeding lines, but the digest does not report Dheeraj-specific genotype or allele data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Name check: the Seednet entry is "Heera" under BITTER GOURD. I had no search budget left to search "Heera", so every finding below refers to groundnut "Dheeraj" (TCGS 1073). Some sources spell it "Dheraj" or "Dhiraj"; "Dhiraj 101" (Gujarat, stem-rot selection) is a different variety and was discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Released by RARS Tirupati as a water-use-efficient Spanish bunch type suited to irrigated kharif and rabi cultivation; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance is documented for it in the sources found. The RARS table credits "drought tolerant" to Dharani, not Dheeraj -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/varieties/groundnut1.pdf
- A 2022 KVK Kalikiri paper describes it as water-use efficient and reports a yield shortfall in 2019-20 attributed to water shortage during crop growth -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/special-issue?year=2022&vol=11&issue=1S&ArticleId=10127 ; https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Salient-features-of-Dheeraj-TCGS-1073-and-Kadiri-6_tbl1_363744348
- A secondary agri-news article lists "heat tolerance" for it, but this is not confirmed by a primary source -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits

DISEASE AND PEST
- Stem rot: used as a susceptible parent (with TCGS 1694, TCGS 2245, Kadiri-6, Narayani) in a line x tester inheritance study of stem rot resistance, which implies susceptibility -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00029-w
- No evidence found for resistance to rust, leaf spot, bud necrosis (PBND/PSND), leaf miner, thrips, white grub or aflatoxin specific to this variety. The only pest material found is a root grub management study at RARS, which does not name Dheeraj -- https://www.entomoljournal.com/archives/2019/vol7issue3/PartAA/9-2-167-578.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Chittoor district on-farm and front-line demonstrations (2016-17 to 2019-20): mean yield 22.7 q/ha against 18.0 q/ha for Kadiri 6; B:C 2.1 vs 1.7; 105-110 days maturity; kharif 2.37 t/ha and rabi 3.44 t/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363744348_Performance_of_groundnut_var_Dheeraj_in_Western_Mandals_of_Chittoor_dt ; https://www.thepharmajournal.com/special-issue?year=2022&vol=11&issue=1S&ArticleId=10127
- Irrigation-schedule trial (IW/CPE 1.0, 0.8, 0.6) with TAG-24, Dheeraj, Kadiri Lepakshi and Kadiri Chitravathi: Dheeraj was outyielded by Kadiri Lepakshi (3607 kg/ha) -- https://agris.fao.org/search/en/providers/122664/records/64b529416e070f62ec8394d9
- RARS Tirupati comparison table lists maturity 105-110 days and water-use-efficiency notes for Dheeraj; column meanings are not clear enough to report yield values -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/varieties/groundnut1.pdf
- Morpho-physiological study: Dheeraj had the greatest plant height among 20 genotypes (genotype list not fully captured) -- https://sasapjas.org/evaluation-of-morpho-physiological-traits-in-groundnut-arachis-hypogaea-l-genotypes/

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL or marker study naming this variety was found.
- Parent in a high-oleic breeding programme: F6 RILs from crosses of TAG 24, Dheeraj and Visishta with ICGV 181024, developed at Groundnut Breeding Section, RARS Tirupati -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387532763_Effect_of_ahfad2_genes_on_oil_profile_of_advanced_breeding_lines_in_groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L
- Stem rot inheritance crosses (see DISEASE AND PEST) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00029-w
- Genetic enhancement review lists "Dheraj TCGS-1073" from ANGRAU, Tirupati in a table, but the table row is not legible enough to read its trait values -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Tirupati, via its Groundnut Breeding Section -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/varieties/groundnut1.pdf
- Release: State Varietal Release Committee, ANGRAU, listed in the 2018-19 annual report as a state-level release of TCGS 1073 -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/Annual%20Report%20%20-%202018-2019%20(1).pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The second search returned only unrelated Dhiraj 101 and Badami pages. Named people in the sources (M Reddi Kumar, Sahaja Deva, C. Suvarna, K. Viswanath) are a professor, a KVK SMS, and stem-rot inheritance co-authors, not confirmed developers of Dheeraj -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363744348_Performance_of_groundnut_var_Dheeraj_in_Western_Mandals_of_Chittoor_dt

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. P. Rajasekhar, RARS Tirupati, phone 9989625209, email adr.rarstpt@angrau.ac.in. Listed as the contact for Dheeraj seed on the RARS list. He is not identified as the breeder -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Seed_Production_Targets/balance%20of%20seed%2010.11.22.pdf
- Institute-level address (S.V. Agricultural College, Tirupati-517 502, Andhra

disease_resistance.summary: Moderate tolerance to the rhizome rot and wilt complex in ginger, with a 29.3% disease reduction relative to a local susceptible check (UBKV research summary; the same finding appears on the UBKV news page). Leaf spot and leaf blotch tolerance was not attributed to Mohini: the digest ties it to TCP-129, a turmeric line (Uttar Rangini), and this was excluded.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found. Searches returned no insect pest resistance data for Mohini.

agronomic_details.yield: About 14 t/ha, as claimed by UBKV, compared with 6-10 t/ha for generally marketed ginger. Trial conditions were not stated.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: Genotype collected from Morolpara, Alipurduar district, West Bengal; selected in West Bengal and tested at national level. Recommended mainly for West Bengal, Odisha, Kerala and Himachal Pradesh, apart from other ginger-growing states.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) UBKV reports a yield of about 14 t/ha against 6-10 t/ha for marketed ginger; trial conditions not stated. (2) Dry recovery of 21.7% against 16-20% for marketed ginger. (3) Oleoresin 4.13% and essential oil 1.31% reported for Mohini. (4) Natural sweet aroma reported. (5) Ginger GCP-49 (IC-0614552), Mohini, went through CVT trials and was released at the 27th AICRP workshop at NRCSS Rajasthan. (6) The Terai Zone RRS 2017-18 report recommends GCP-49 for national release as UBKV Aada-1 (popular name Mohini), and the proposal was sent to the Central Variety Release Committee. (7) Field agronomy trials of ginger at RRS Terai Zone used the local variety, not Mohini, so they are not Mohini trial results.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Moderate tolerance to the rhizome rot and wilt complex, with 29.3% disease reduction relative to a local susceptible check -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/news/ginger-variety-release-notification/
Moderate tolerance to rhizome rot and wilt complex is also reported in the UBKV research summary -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/news/ginger-variety-release-notification/ (same finding; duplicate page)
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. Searches 1 to 4 returned no data on these traits for Mohini.

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderate tolerance to rhizome rot and wilt complex (29.3% disease reduction over local susceptible check) -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/news/ginger-variety-release-notification/
Leaf spot and leaf blotch tolerance: NOT attributed to Mohini. The UBKV pages tie this trait to TCP-129, a turmeric line (Uttar Rangini), so it was discarded -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/research/
Insect pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
High yield of about 14 t/ha, compared with 6-10 t/ha for generally marketed ginger (UBKV's own claim; trial conditions not stated) -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/news/ginger-variety-release-notification/
Dry recovery of 21.7%, compared with 16-20% for marketed ginger -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/news/ginger-variety-release-notification/
Oleoresin 4.13% and essential oil 1.31% reported for Mohini -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/news/ginger-variety-release-notification/
Natural sweet aroma reported -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/news/ginger-variety-release-notification/
Genotype collected from Morolpara, Alipurduar district; selection done in West Bengal and tested at national level -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/news/ginger-variety-release-notification/
Ginger GCP-49 (IC-0614552), Mohini, went through CVT trials and was released at the 27th AICRP workshop at NRCSS Rajasthan -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/GPB_Annual_Report_2017-18.pdf
Terai Zone RRS 2017-18 report: GCP-49 recommended for national release as UBKV Aada-1 (popular name Mohini); proposal sent to Central Variety Release Committee -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/RRSTZ-2017-2018.pdf
Field agronomy trials of ginger at RRS Terai Zone used the local variety, not Mohini -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/RRSTZ-2017-2018.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Searches 1 to 4 returned no marker, QTL, parentage or genetic-diversity study for Mohini. Parentage is "Not specified" in the input and no source gave it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed by Dr. Soumendra Chakraborty (Associate Professor, UBKV) with horticulturist Prof. Suchand Datta, pathologist Dr. Anamika Debnath and technical assistant Mr Murari Roy -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/news/ginger-variety-release-notification/
Earlier contributors named: Dr. Sekhar Bandyopadhyay, Prof Jagadish Chandra Jana, Dr. Surajit Khalko, Prof. B.C. (list cut off in source) -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/news/ginger-variety-release-notification/
Developing institution: Uttar Banga Krishi Viswavidyalaya (UBKV), Pundibari, Cooch Behar, West Bengal; work under the AICRP on Spices (2014-15 to 2016-17) project on ginger germplasm, funded by ICAR -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/Bio-data-Dr-Soumendra-Chakraborty_24March21.pdf
Dr. Moumita Chakraborty is listed beside the variety-development entry in the GPB annual report; her role is not stated -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/GPB_Annual_Report_2017-18.pdf
AICRP on Spices co-operator listing names "Mohini (Ginger)" among released varieties in a staff profile; this is a list entry, not a breeding record -- https://spices.res.in/staff/detail/dr-akshitha-h-j
Notification: Gazette of India, 16 January 2018, Department of Agriculture, Cooperation and Farmers' Welfare (notification REGD. D.L.-33004/99) -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/news/ginger-variety-release-notification/
Note on dates: the CSC year_of_release (2017-09-18) differs from the Gazette date (16 Jan 2018); the sources do not explain the 2017 date, which probably refers to the AICRP workshop recommendation.
Note on names: "variety_name" and "seednet_variety_name" are both "Mohini" and the same evidence applies to both. The seednet crop field says "BITTER GOURD", which conflicts with the ginger evidence; the ginger evidence was used.

CONTACT DETAILS
Dr. Soumendra Chakraborty, breeder, UBKV: email soumendra1@gmail.com, mobile 9474092958, address UBKV, Pundibari, Coochbehar, West Bengal 736165 -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/GPB_Annual_Report_2017-18.pdf (the layout places this email and phone beside his name; mapping is inferred)
Two other UBKV Breeding/GPB contacts listed in same annual report, names not clearly mapped to emails/phones: arup_skr@rediffmail.com (9474016823) and kundu.avijit78@gmail.com (9433678323) -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/GPB_Annual_Report_2017-18.pdf
Institute-level contact, UBKV: registrar@ubkv.ac.in; address P.O. Pundibari, Cooch Behar, West Bengal 736165 -- https://www.collegeduniyabharat.com/university/uttar-banga-krishi-vishwavidyalaya/ (third-party aggregator; not the official site)
Institute-level phone: +91 3582 270143 (third-party aggregator) -- https://findmycollege.com/colleges/uttar-banga-krishi-vishwavidyalaya-ubkv-cooch-behar-528 ; 03582-270012 and 9593943726 also given by third parties -- https://coochbehar.gov.in/public-utility/uttar-banga-krishi-viswavidyalaya/
Official university site: https://www.ubkv.ac.in/research/ (no direct contact details seen on the page captured)

PUBLICATIONS
Chakraborty, S. et al. (2018 approx.). Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding Annual Report 2017-18. UBKV, Pundibari -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/GPB_Annual_Report_2017-18.pdf (authors not stated; report lists Mohini release and breeder seed multiplication)
Regional Research Station (Terai Zone) Annual Report 2017-2018. UBKV, Directorate of Research -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/RRSTZ-2017-2018.pdf

Peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports on Mohini trials, KrishiKosh theses, and conference papers specifically on Mohini: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
UBKV states that breeder seed multiplication of Mohini has been taken up by the University farm -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/news/ginger-variety-release-notification/
Seed multiplication of Mohini (UBKV AADA-I) is listed in the GPB annual report -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/GPB_Annual_Report_2017-18.pdf
Seednet portal listing: No evidence found. Searches did not retrieve a Seednet page for Mohini (under either name).
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or private dealer listings for Mohini ginger: No evidence found. An IndiaMART listing for "Hybrid Ginger Seeds (Mohini)" from Agri Mitra Services, Indore (https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/hybrid-ginger-seeds-mohini-25460304812.html) was DISCARDED: it describes a hybrid, not the UBKV variety, and is a similarly named commercial product.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Recommended mainly for West Bengal, Odisha, Kerala and Himachal Pradesh, apart from other ginger-growing states -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/news/ginger-variety-release-notification/
Notified for national release throughout India in ginger-growing states -- https://www.ubkv.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/GPB_Annual_Report_2017-18.pdf
CSC input states (Kerala, Odisha, Himachal Pradesh, West Bengal) match the UBKV news page.

drought_tolerance.technical_details: No variety-specific drought data. The general cucurbit chapter says bitter gourd is sensitive to water stress and needs irrigation.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The croplibrary.com page says bitter gourd in general tolerates 35-40°C with adequate soil moisture. This is a crop-level claim from a non-peer-reviewed site and is not specific to this variety.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence found.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: The cucurbit chapter snippet mentions that a gourd is more tolerant to waterlogging than ridge gourd. The snippet is truncated and the gourd is not identified as bitter gourd. No variety-specific data.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: Alternaria leaf blight: classed Resistant with a mean disease incidence of 4.5% in a varietal screening (ScienceDirect). A PPV&FR compendium snippet mentions 'Resistant to Fusarium wilt', but its attribution to this variety is not clear from the snippet. The PAU 'resistant to root knot nematode and virus diseases' snippet appears next to the Punjab Kareli-1 entry and probably describes the neighbouring variety, Punjab Jhaar Karela-1, so it is not attributed here.
disease_resistance.technical_details: The Alternaria result comes from a field screening and is not tied to any identified resistance gene. No gene or mechanism information was found.

pest_resistance.specific_pests: None documented for this variety. The fruit fly is noted as the most destructive pest of bitter gourd in general.
pest_resistance.technical_details: No variety-specific pest reaction data.

stress_tolerance_analysis.overall_stress_tolerance: no (only a single biotic-stress evidence point, Alternaria leaf blight resistance. No abiotic stress evidence.)
key_stress_attributes: Resistant to Alternaria leaf blight (4.5% incidence), ScienceDirect study

agronomic_performance.yield_potential: About 70 q/acre per PAU Progressive Farming, which is roughly 17,300 kg/ha (conversion: 70 q/acre x 100 kg x 2.471 acres/ha). The input record leaves the unit blank. Another PAU snippet quotes 35 q/acre, but it appears to refer to Punjab Jhaar Karela-1.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Not specified. PAU describes a warm, humid-climate crop that is sensitive to frost and low temperatures.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Long vines. Leaves are green, smooth and serrated (PAU package of practices). The fruit description is truncated.
agronomic_performance.field_trial_results: Only the single Alternaria screening. No multi-location trial data and no Gujarat trials.
agronomic_performance.farmer_adoption: Listed among recommended bitter gourd varieties in PAU publications and on popular farming sites. No adoption data.

breeder_and_development_info.research_publications: The Alternaria leaf blight fungicide study (ScienceDirect, S1658077X21001120) evaluates this variety as one of the varieties tested. No variety-development paper was found.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: There are citations, namely PAU publications, the PPV&FR compendium and a peer-reviewed Alternaria screening in ScienceDirect. Stress-trait evidence is weak: there is one disease resistance result and no abiotic tolerance data. The 75 band needs at least one stress trait with a citation, which could arguably apply to the Alternaria result, but the evidence is limited to a single biotic trait. It also comes from a screening of a Punjab-released variety, with no Gujarat or hot, semi-arid zone testing. The score therefore sits at 60, with an upside to 75 if the Alternaria evidence is judged sufficient. The release year is inconsistent across sources (2009 vs 2015).

dashboard_data.key_attributes: PAU variety. Long vines. About 70 q/acre. Resistant to Alternaria leaf blight.
dashboard_data.seasons: Not specified (warm-season crop; PAU treats it as a spring-summer and rainy-season crop, which is unconfirmed in the snippets)

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Punjab Kareli-1 is a PAU-developed bitter gourd variety, listed with a yield of about 70 q/acre and classed as resistant to Alternaria leaf blight (4.5% incidence). No abiotic stress tolerance, genetic marker, breeder or Gujarat-specific data were found. Evidence quality is low to moderate, and the release year conflicts between sources (2009 vs 2015).
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: PAU bitter gourd variety with long vines and green, serrated leaves. Yield is about 70 q/acre (about 17,300 kg/ha). Maturity, parentage and recommended states are not specified, and no Gujarat trials were found.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: The only documented stress trait is resistance to Alternaria leaf blight. There is no evidence for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance, and no pest resistance data. Suitability for Gujarat's climate stresses is unproven.

drought_tolerance.technical_details: Pusa Vishesh is listed in a Jammu (SKUAST) contingency plan for drought and delayed transplanting, and in a review of climate-resilient vegetables (ResearchGate 2025) where the snippet lists it next to drought/heat traits. The snippets do not say that Pusa Vishesh itself was tested for or shown to be drought tolerant. The general bitter gourd sources (growables.org, eagri.org) say bitter gourd does not tolerate drought or water stagnation. The IARI 2022 report mentions drought-tolerant material, but the snippet does not link it to this variety.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: Pusa Vishesh is described as a spring-summer variety. The IARI Annual Report 2019 mentions heat-stress expression studies (48 °C) that include Pusa Vishesh as a genotype. The snippet does not state the outcome. Heat tolerance is therefore not confirmed.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: No variety-specific salinity data found. The salt-tolerance results in the snippets (melatonin in bitter melon) are general and do not involve this variety.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence. Bitter gourd is generally reported to be intolerant of water stagnation. The 2012 agromet bulletin recommends Pusa Vishesh for sowing, not for flood conditions.

submergence_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence. The submergence-tolerant varieties in the 2012 bulletin (Jalashree, Jalkuwari) are rice varieties, not bitter gourd.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: ToLCNDV: Pusa Vishesh was used as a parent (DBGS-2 × Pusa Vishesh) to build populations for genetic study of ToLCNDV. This does not show resistance, and the snippet does not say it is a susceptible or resistant parent. No other disease data found.
disease_resistance.technical_details: No resistance genes or mechanisms were reported for this variety.

pest_resistance.specific_pests: Root-knot nematode (Meloidogyne incognita): Pusa Vishesh was found susceptible in a germplasm screening (The Pharma Journal 2022).
pest_resistance.technical_details: Susceptibility reported in screening. No resistance mechanism or gene is known.

stress_tolerance_analysis.overall_stress_tolerance: no (not demonstrated; the evidence is indirect and unconfirmed, and one source shows nematode susceptibility)

genetic_and_molecular_profile.genetic_markers: No QTL, SNP or SSR markers specific to Pusa Vishesh were found. It was included in a genetic diversity and population structure study (PMC10574847) as a released variety in sub-cluster V, with light-green to glossy green fruits.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.molecular_mechanisms: None established. The IARI 2019 report includes gene expression studies under heat stress that use Pusa Vishesh, but details are not in the snippet.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.breeding_techniques: Described as a selection from a local collection (eagri, vikaspedia), so conventional selection. Also used as a parent in crosses such as DBGS-2 × Pusa Vishesh. The ISVS review describes it as an inbred line.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.genetic_background: Selection from a local collection; formal parentage not specified

agronomic_performance.farmer_adoption: Widely recommended in state and national advisories and variety checklists. It is among the reference varieties maintained by PPV&FRA. No direct farmer feedback found.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: There are multiple citations (peer-reviewed, IARI reports, ICAR advisories), which meets the 60 threshold. It does not reach 75 because no stress trait is clearly shown for this variety: the drought/heat links are indirect or unconfirmed, and nematode susceptibility is documented. Yield data are also absent, and there is no Gujarat-specific evidence.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: IARI selection from a local collection; spring-summer and rainy season use; medium-long (15-20 cm) glossy green smooth fruits; nematode susceptible; stress tolerance unconfirmed
dashboard_data.state_acronyms: Not specified (JK mentioned in an advisory)

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Pusa Vishesh is an IARI bitter gourd variety selected from a local collection, with medium-long glossy green fruits, suited to spring-summer and rainy season cultivation and widely listed in advisories and checklists. Evidence for drought or heat tolerance is indirect and unconfirmed, and it was reported susceptible to root-knot nematode. Citation coverage is moderate, but variety-specific stress, yield and Gujarat data are lacking.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: IARI-bred, selection from a local collection; spring-summer/rainy season; fruits 15-20 cm, glossy green, smooth. Maturity, release year and absolute yield are not documented in the results.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No direct evidence of drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Nematode susceptibility is documented, and ToLCNDV resistance is not established. Overall stress tolerance is unconfirmed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Recently released varieties (CoS 16233 among them) are described as having good yield, pest and disease resistance, and better ratoonability. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found for this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/404703870_Ratoon_Management_Present_Status_and_Future_Prospects_for_Increasing_Sugarcane_Productivity_in_Subtropical_India

DISEASE AND PEST -- CoS 16233 (Roshan) is listed among the new red rot-resistant varieties approved in a medium/late maturity group. -- https://www.cmv360.com/tractors/news/7-new-red-rot-resistant-sugarcane-varieties-approved
DISEASE AND PEST -- Insect-pest resistance: No evidence found. The 2024 ratoon paper's general claim of pest resistance is not tied to a specific trait score.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Maturity: CoS 16233 (Roshan) appears under medium and late maturing varieties; the ratoon paper also calls it a mid-late variety. -- https://www.cmv360.com/tractors/news/7-new-red-rot-resistant-sugarcane-varieties-approved ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/404703870_Ratoon_Management_Present_Status_and_Future_Prospects_for_Increasing_Sugarcane_Productivity_in_Subtropical_India
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Yield: The news piece gives a higher yield of up to 600 quintals per acre for the approved group as a whole, not a variety-specific figure. -- https://www.cmv360.com/tractors/news/7-new-red-rot-resistant-sugarcane-varieties-approved
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Trial data: No variety-specific AICRP trial yields were found. A table in the ratoon paper lists a CoS16233 row with unlabeled numbers that cannot be read as yield. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/404703870_Ratoon_Management_Present_Status_and_Future_Prospects_for_Increasing_Sugarcane_Productivity_in_Subtropical_India

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Parentage was not found for this variety, and no QTL or marker study was returned.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Breeder names: No evidence found. The search returned breeder information only for other varieties (CoS15233, Bismil/CoSha 17231, Co 16030), which were discarded.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing bodies: The news article attributes the development to ICAR and IISR Lucknow. This conflicts with the UP state-council attribution in the next line and is only a secondary news claim. -- https://www.cmv360.com/tractors/news/7-new-red-rot-resistant-sugarcane-varieties-approved
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution context: UPCSR, Shahjahanpur, is the nodal agency that supervises various levels of breeder seed cane production. This is an institutional role, not a breeding credit. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/404703870_Ratoon_Management_Present_Status_and_Future_Prospects_for_Increasing_Sugarcane_Productivity_in_Subtropical_India

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute address (institute-level): UPCSR-Sugarcane Research Institute, Shahjahanpur-242001, UP, India. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/404703870_Ratoon_Management_Present_Status_and_Future_Prospects_for_Increasing_Sugarcane_Productivity_in_Subtropical_India
CONTACT DETAILS -- Email: Sudhir.Shukla@icar.gov.in (corresponding author, Sudhir Shukla, of the ratoon management review that mentions CoS 16233). This is the review's corresponding author, not a confirmed breeder of this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/404703870_Ratoon_Management_Present_Status_and_Future_Prospects_for_Increasing_Sugarcane_Productivity_in_Subtropical_India
CONTACT DETAILS -- Phone, official institute contact page: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS -- Authors not shown in retrieved text (n.d.). Ratoon Management: Present Status and Future Prospects for Increasing Sugarcane Productivity in Subtropical India. ResearchGate (mentions CoS 16233 as a recently released variety) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/404703870_Ratoon_Management_Present_Status_and_Future_Prospects_for_Increasing_Sugarcane_Productivity_in_Subtropical_India
PUBLICATIONS -- No variety-specific peer-reviewed paper, thesis (KrishiKosh), AICRP annual report or DOI was found. The Co 16030 and CoPb 14185 papers were discarded as other varieties.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Seed cane is allotted at the State level by the Cane Commissioner, Govt of Uttar Pradesh. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/404703870_Ratoon_Management_Present_Status_and_Future_Prospects_for_Increasing_Sugarcane_Productivity_in_Subtropical_India

drought.details: No drought tolerance evidence specific to Smarak was found. The Frontiers source describes Smarak as suitable for kharif rainfed and summer irrigated conditions but does not claim drought tolerance. Lodging resistance (short, woody stem) is a plant trait and is not evidence of drought tolerance. The only waterlogging/stress literature returned did not name Smarak.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. No heat tolerance evidence specific to Smarak was returned.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. No salinity tolerance evidence specific to Smarak was returned.

flood.details: Not flood tolerant per the digest; no flood-specific evidence for Smarak was found. The Frontiers source describes suitability for kharif rainfed and summer irrigated conditions, not flood tolerance. The general sesame waterlogging literature does not name Smarak.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerance to Macrophomina (charcoal rot) is listed for SMARAK (OSC 560) in the DOD entry. The DOD variety table gives the Smarak row (2012) a tolerance profile of leaf curl, phyllody, Macrophomina, Cercospora and capsule borer. These are tolerance (not immunity) ratings from a single government listing. The two DOD entries (Smarak 2012 and SMARAK (OSC 560) 2015) may refer to the same variety; the digest does not settle this. No independent field validation was found.

pest_resistance.summary: Capsule borer: listed as tolerant in the DOD variety table (Smarak 2012 row). Stored-grain pest (Corcyra cephalonica, rice moth): a study found the white-seeded Smarak more vulnerable to infestation than the black-seeded Prachi, indicating susceptibility rather than resistance. No resistance to other pests was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Conflicting figures. rkb-odisha lists an average yield of 12.0 q/ha (approximately 1200 kg/ha). DOD gives a yield potential of 800-900 kg/ha. The digest does not reconcile these. In a multi-varietal organic trial in the Gangetic plains of West Bengal, the Smarak-based T-7 treatment gave 1765 kg/ha seed yield (see field_trials).

agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Short and woody stem, resistant to lodging; height about 120 cm (Frontiers 2025). agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) On-farm trial, KVK Angul, 2024: Smarak was one of three technology options against Nali rasi. (2) Multi-varietal trial under organic management, Gangetic plains of West Bengal: treatment T-7, statistically comparable to T-5 (1375 kg/ha), gave the highest seed yield (1765 kg/ha) from the Smarak variety, with 52.64% oil content. (3) OUAT Central Farm, Rabi 2014-15: five varieties (Uma, Amrit, Smarak, Prachi, Nirmala) were tested with growth regulators NAA, GA3 and IAA. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SEARCH NOTE: Four web_search calls were run. Searches 1 to 3 covered SMARAK / OSC 560 (sesame). Search 4 covered "Sara" bitter gourd (Seednet name). The Seednet name returned nothing relevant.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Smarak (OSC-560) is a sesame variety resistant (short and woody stem) to lodging, reaching a height of 120 cm and maturing in 80–85 days. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/sustainable-food-systems/articles/10.3389/fsufs.2025.1565401/full
- Smarak is described as suitable for kharif rainfed and summer irrigated conditions, not for drought or flood tolerance specifically. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/sustainable-food-systems/articles/10.3389/fsufs.2025.1565401/full
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Smarak. The searches returned only general sesame waterlogging literature (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9120847/), which does not name Smarak.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Smarak is listed as Shubra, Smarak, Subhra (OSC-2007), Smarak (OSC 560) for Odisha; the DOD entry gives it a tolerance profile of tolerance to leaf curl, phyllody, Macrophomina, Cercospora and capsule borer (table row "Smarak · 2012"). -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Sesame.aspx
- Separate DOD entry for SMARAK (OSC 560) lists it as tolerant to Macrophomina (charcoal rot). -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx
- Stored-grain pest: in a study of Corcyra cephalonica, the white-seeded Smarak was found to be more vulnerable to rice moth infestation than the black-seeded Prachi. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343393036_Management_of_Corcyra_cephalonica_Stain_by_botanicals_and_its_effect_of_infestation_on_stored_sesamum_seeds ; also https://www.ijcmas.com/9-7-2020/Soumya%20B.%20Babu,%20et%20al.pdf
- Note: the DOD listing gives Smarak 2012 and SMARAK (OSC 560) 2015. The two entries may be the same variety recorded with different years; the evidence does not settle this.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration and yield: Smarak (OSC 560) is listed at 80 days duration, 12.0 q/ha average yield and 50% oil. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/oilseed-crops-in-odisha/sesame/
- DOD gives 800–900 kg/ha yield potential and 48–52% oil content for SMARAK (OSC 560). Figures conflict with the rkb-odisha figures and are not reconciled here. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx
- Shattering: the plant avoids shattering through synchronous maturity, with visual cues for timely harvest. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/sustainable-food-systems/articles/10.3389/fsufs.2025.1565401/full
- On-farm trial (KVK Angul, 2024): Smarak was one of three technology options against Nali rasi; the text says Smarak, Subhra and Kalinga sesame 3-1 gave 24.5, 16.2 and 12.3% higher seed yield than farmer practice, but the mapping of percentages to varieties is ambiguous in the source. -- https://www.kvkangul.org/on-farm-testing/
- Multi-varietal trial, organic management, Gangetic West Bengal: The T-7 treatment, statistically comparable to treatment T-5 (1375 kg/ha), produces the highest seed yield (1765 kg/ha) from the Smarak variety of sesame. Oil content recorded at 52.64%. -- https://www.switchon.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Multi-varietal-trial-on-Sesamum-under-organic-management-in-the-Gangetic-plains-of-West-Bengal-1.pdf
- OUAT Central Farm trial, Rabi 2014-15, five varieties (Uma, Amrit, Smarak, Prachi, Nirmala) with growth regulators NAA, GA3 and IAA. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/abstractview.php?ID=5135&vol=6-11-2017&SNo=215

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL, marker or genetic-study result naming Smarak or OSC 560 was returned. The only genetics material found is general sesame breeding (https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_15), which does not mention Smarak.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Released centre: OUAT, Bhubaneswar. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx
- Institutional role: the AICRP on Sesame at OUAT has a mandate covering development, evaluation and release of sesame varieties, and produces breeder seed of Amrit, Smarak and Subhra. -- https://ouat.nic.in/research_stations
- Developing station: AICRP on Sesame, OUAT, Dhenkanal, Odisha (cited as a co-author affiliation for the 2025 Frontiers paper). -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/sustainable-food-systems/articles/10.3389/fsufs.2025.1565401/full
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The searches did not name a lead breeder or scientist for Smarak. The OUAT sesame research chapter lists Swapan K. Tripathy, Jayashree Kar and Dibyabharati Sahu in OUAT sesame breeding work, but this is general sesame work and is not attributed to Smarak. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_15

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder-level contact for Smarak was found.
- Institute-level, general sesame contact (not specific to Smarak): Swapan K Tripathy Email: swapankumartripathy@mail.com http://www.ouat.nic.in/ -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_15
- OUAT Bhubaneswar postal address and phone: No evidence found in the search results.
- Seednet "Sara" contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in results (2025). Sustainability of rice–sesame cropping systems: evaluating tillage and nutrient interactions in the eastern plateau and hills of the Indian sub-continent. Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/sustainable-food-systems/articles/10.3389/fsufs.2025.1565401/full (authors not visible in retrieved text; only institutional affiliations: ICAR-IIOR Hyderabad, TNAU, OUAT AICRP Sesame Dhenkanal, ANGRAU)
- Authors not shown in results (2017). Effect of Plant Growth Regulators on Morpho-Physiological and Yield Parameters of Some Sesame (Sesamum indicum L.) Cultivars. IJCMAS -- https://www.ijcmas.com/abstractview.php?ID=5135&vol=6-11-2017&SNo=215
- Authors not shown in results (year not shown). Management of Corcyra cephalonica Stain. by botanicals and its effect of infestation on stored sesamum seeds. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343393036_Management_of_Corcyra_cephalonica_Stain_by_botanicals_and_its_effect_of_infestation_on_stored_sesamum_seeds
- Authors not shown in results (year not shown). Biology and Morphometry of Corcyra cephalonica Stain in ... IJCMAS, OUAT Bhubaneswar (2018-19 study) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-7-2020/Soumya%20B.%20Babu,%20et%20al.pdf
- Authors not shown in results (year not shown). Performance of sesamum varieties under rainfed upland conditions in the N-E ghat zone of Odisha. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328073756_Performance_of_sesamum_varieties_under_rainfed_upland_conditions_in_the_N-E_ghat_zone_of_Odisha (Smarak not clearly named in the retrieved text; OSC 560 appears in the tables)
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP annual report naming Smarak was found in the searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK sales or private dealer listing for Smarak was found in the searches. The OUAT AICRP breeder-seed production mandate (https://ouat.nic.in/research_stations) is the only seed-supply evidence. Seednet availability: No evidence found (the Seednet portal was not reached).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Odisha. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx ; https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Sesame.aspx
- The DOD table gives the release year as 2015 for SMARAK (OSC 560). The CSC minutes release date is 2014-10-20, and the PPV&FR certificate dates are 2017 and 2018 (https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumforextantnotified-nov-2021.pdf). These dates are not reconciled.

SEEDNET NAME CHECK ("Sara", BITTER GOURD)
- No evidence found. The search returned only commercial bitter gourd hybrids (e.g., trueleafmarket.com, vnrseeds.com) and general bitter gourd pages. None names "Sara" and none is a sesame variety. Nothing was attributed to this record on that basis.

SHANTI (mesta, JBM 71) evidence digest

Search budget: 4 web_search calls used (the maximum). Results were checked only from the first five hits per query, and none of the hits concerned this variety. Every heading below therefore reads "No evidence found" unless noted. The Seednet name "Shanta" is listed under bitter gourd, which does not match the mesta record. The variety name "SHANTI" and the crop "mesta" also returned no matching sources, so the two names could not be reconciled from the evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found (searched; no hits on SHANTI/JBM 71 mesta stress data)
DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found (searched; no hits)
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found (searched; no hits)
GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found (searched; no hits)
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for the lead breeder or scientist of SHANTI at Jute Research Station, OUAT. The OUAT research-station page (https://ouat.nic.in/research_stations) came up, but the portion returned did not mention the Jute Research Station or this variety.
CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone or address was retrieved. Institute-level contact for OUAT was not captured in the retrieved text; the OUAT site (https://ouat.nic.in) is the starting point for a manual lookup.
PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No papers, AICRP reports, KrishiKosh theses or conference papers matched SHANTI/JBM 71 mesta.
SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for mesta variety SHANTI. The only Seednet-name hit, "Shanta", returned a private seller page for a bitter gourd variety, which is a different crop and variety (https://seedsofindia.com/products/bitter-gourd-shanghai). It should not be attributed to this record.
RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The CSC record states Odisha, but no independent source confirmed it.

Suggested next steps (outside the search cap): check the CSC release notification for the exact mesta variety name and code; query the Seednet portal under the mesta crop filter, not bitter gourd; and check the ICAR-CRIJAF / Jute Research Station, OUAT (Odisha) publications and annual reports directly.

RELEASE/NOTIFICATION: BCKV lists this white jute (C. capsularis) as Sweta (BCCC 1), notified under CVRC S.O. No. 1379(E) dated 27.03.2018 -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en ; the gazette index lists S.O 1379(E) on 27/03/2018 as a seed variety notification -- https://seednet.gov.in/SeedGO/Index.htm
RELEASE DATE DISCREPANCY: The input gives 2018-01-20, but the gazette notification date is 27 March 2018. Verify before use.
NAME SPELLING: The source uses "Sweta"; the input uses "Shweta." The BCCC 1 code matches.
BREEDER/INSTITUTION: Developed and applicant listed as BCKV, under the AINP on Jute and Allied Fibres -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en ; AINP achievements summary (one white jute, BCCC 1, identified 2012-17) -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/ainp-on-jute-and-allied-fibre-en
YIELD: Fibre yield of 27.5 q/ha reported -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en ; AINP report gives about 0.53% yield gain over checks (possibly a typo for 5.3%) and fibre quality W5 vs W6 in checks -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/ainp-on-jute-and-allied-fibre-en
FIBRE QUALITY: Tenacity 15 g/tex and fineness 1.66 tex reported -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
DISEASE RESISTANCE: Reported tolerance to stem rot -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
PEST RESISTANCE: Reported tolerance to semi-looper and BHC (Bihar hairy caterpillar) -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Swetha (NLR 40024), rice

Name note: The CSC minutes name is "Swetha" and the Seednet name is also "Swetha". The Seednet crop field reads "BITTER GOURD", which conflicts with rice. The evidence below refers to rice, and the crop mismatch should be checked on the Seednet record. Searches run: 4 (variety, breeder/institute, NLR 40024 code, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as a short-duration variety for early kharif with blast and lodging tolerance -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf
- The IRRI Rice Research Notes article describes it as medium-duration with multiple tolerances, which conflicts with the short-duration description above. Its full text was not accessible in the snippet, so the specific tolerances could not be confirmed -- https://zenodo.org/records/7000090

DISEASE AND PEST
- Under gall midge monitoring at the station, NLR 40024 showed 18.16% deadheart/gall incidence, versus 28.35% in NLR 34242 and 7.03% in NLR 34449 -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf
- The Zenodo keyword list tags the release with disease resistance and pest resistance, but the specific pathogens and pests were not visible -- https://zenodo.org/records/7000090

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Mean yield in organic-treatment trials was 6064 kg/ha for NLR 40024, the highest among the entries tested (next was NLR 34242 at 5735 kg/ha). Trial year and location are not stated in the snippet -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf
- Recommended for early kharif plantings in the Southern Zone in the Kharif 2014 package of practices -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/package%20of%20practices/Rice.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found (searched; no QTL, marker, or parentage information was returned). Parentage is "Not specified" in the input record.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Listed among 25 varieties developed and released from the research station, with release year 2012 in that list (the input record gives 2013-01-18) -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf
- The IRRI note lists N. D. Majumder, G. Francis, R. M. Balachandran and P. V. Zachariah as authors, but the snippet is truncated, so this should be verified against the PDF before use. Source: https://zenodo.org/records/7000090
- Institutional conflict: the IRRI note says the variety was released in Kerala, while the NLR code and the rarstpt.org list point to an Andhra Pradesh station (Nellore/Tirupati, ANGRAU). Verify which institute developed it. The input's "Agriculture Research Station" field is too generic to identify the station.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder-level contact found. No official email, phone, or postal address for the station or its division was returned in the search results. Institute contact page: not found. Recommended next step: ANGRAU (Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University) main site or the Regional Agricultural Research Station page on rarstpt.org.

PUBLICATIONS
- Majumder, N. D.; Zachariah, G.; Francis, R. M.; Balachandran, P. V. (year not confirmed). Swetha: a new, medium-duration variety with multiple tolerance released in Kerala, India. International Rice Research Notes (IRRI) -- https://zenodo.org/records/7000090 (verify author list and year against the PDF)

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, or SAU seed sales. The only commercial hit was a consumer product "Swetha" Seeraga Samba rice brand, which is unrelated to this variety -- https://www.jamoona.com/en-be/products/telugu-5kg-samba-rice-seeraga

RECOMMENDED STATES

EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: the variety_name "Vishwas" and seednet_variety_name "Vishwas (NUL-7)" both appear in the evidence below. The CSC/DPD table lists it as "Vishwas (NUL-7)"; seller pages use "Vishwas NUL-7" or "NUL-7 (Vishwas)". All findings refer to this variety, and I checked each page for both names and for black gram. I did not run a separate search on seednet.gov.in, so no Seednet page is cited.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Tolerant of YMV (yellow mosaic virus) and powdery mildew, per seller listings -- https://agrosiaa.com/products/detail/nirmal-black-gram-vishwas-nul-7-2-kg
- Same YMV and powdery mildew tolerance claim, as a seller spec -- https://www.indiamart.com/sanjaybrothers/black-gram-seeds.html
- The DPD table records resistance to MYMV and powdery mildew for NUL-7 -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Drought: NUL 7 Viswas was one of several black gram genotypes in a PEG-induced drought screen at seedling stage, with germination and seedling growth recorded. The snippet does not give a clear tolerance rating for this variety, so no drought-tolerance conclusion is drawn -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4535
- Heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistance to MYMV and powdery mildew (see above) -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf

An insect-succession paper from Odisha mentions NUL-7 (Vishwas) only as a trial entry, with no resistance finding -- https://environmentandecology.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/MS11-Biodiversity-and-Succession-of-Insects-of-Blackgram.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS

VARIANT NOTE: The record gives "SG 1 White Long" as the release-minutes name and "White long" as the Seednet name. The crop is blackgram in the record but BITTER GOURD on Seednet. None of the four searches returned a page naming this variety for either crop. The only "SG 1" hit is a snake gourd variety, which is a different crop. Under the strict-relevance rule, every heading below is "No evidence found" unless noted.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches for "SG 1 White Long" with blackgram or bitter gourd returned only other varieties (blackgram T 9, CO 5, MDU 1, VBN series; bitter gourd CO 1, Coimbatore Long White, MDU 1, Priyanka, Priya). None of these is this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Blackgram pages on yellow mosaic and pod borer resistance concern other releases (e.g., MDU 1, https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/2014/Blackgram.pdf). Those are not this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Nothing on duration, yield, or trials for SG 1 White Long. Bitter gourd yield tables list other varieties (https://subsistencefarming.in/en/bitter-gourd-farming/). Those are not this variety.

processing_metadata.data_gap_note: None of the 50 provided search results mention ADT 54 or any rice variety with the code AD 09493 (IET 24249). The results concern black gram (Vigna mungo) and pulse crops, where the ADT designation refers to different varieties (for example, ADT 4 and ADT 5 black gram). The parentage 'T9/ADT-2 PANT U.14' in the CSC record closely resembles text in the results describing black gram ADT 4, so it must not be attributed to ADT 54 without confirmation. All ADT 54-specific fields are reported as unknown or not available. Verification requires rice-specific sources such as the TNAU Aduthurai rice research station, the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University variety release records, or the ICAR Rice Varietal Release documentation.

agronomic_details.yield: Mean grain yield of 6334 kg/ha across 242 trials (Pushpa et al., EJPB 2020). This is 9.4% above ADT 43 (5788 kg/ha, 112 days) and 14.0% above CO 51 (5562 kg/ha, 112 days). The supplied reference value of 1500.00 to 2000.00 Kg/Ha conflicts with this digest finding and was not used to override it.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the mean across 242 trials. A seed vigour study lists ADT 53 among 12 rice varieties with high seed vigour potential; this is not a yield stability analysis.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Kuruvai (June-July sowing) in Tiruchirappalli (Tamil Nadu crop practice guide). Kuruvai/Kodai in delta districts and Sornavari/Navarai in other districts, including northeastern districts (Tamil Nadu crop practice guide and press summary). The supplied adaptation note refers to summer irrigated sowings (April-May) in the Cauvery Delta zone; the digest does not confirm or contradict this.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 70 To 70Days (supplied reference value). Conflicts with digest findings of 110-115 days (Pushpa et al., EJPB 2020) and 105-110 days (TNAU Aduthurai station page), which describe it as a short-duration culture.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Non-lodging, compact plant type with well-exerted panicles (EJPB article 1094). search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: ADT 53 (rice)
Searches run: 4 of 4 allowed. The search tool returned no results for "ADT-5" or for the Seednet name, so every finding below refers to the name "ADT 53" (release-minute name, variety code AD07073/IET 23955).

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to ADT 53. The only trait recorded is a non-lodging, compact plant type with well-exerted panicles -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1094

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to ADT 53. The Tamil Nadu advisory lists ADT 53 as a recommended kuruvai variety but gives no resistance data -- https://www.tnpscthervupettagam.com/currentaffairs-detail/tps-5-rice-variety?cat=tamilnadu-news

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Released 2019 by TNAU as a short-duration culture of 110-115 days (Pushpa et al., EJPB 2020) -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/EJPB/article/view/3314
-- Mean grain yield of 6334 kg/ha across 242 trials, 9.4% above ADT 43 (5788 kg/ha, 112 days) and 14.0% above CO 51 (5562 kg/ha, 112 days) -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/EJPB/article/view/3314
-- TNAU Aduthurai station page gives duration 105-110 days, yield 6334 kg/ha, and "alternate for ADT 43" -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-aduthurai/varieties-released/
-- Press summaries report milling 62% and head rice 65%, with zinc and iron content noted; the variety is described as suited to parboiling as an alternative to ADT 43 -- https://www.tnpscthervupettagam.com/currentaffairs-detail/new-paddy-variety ; https://www.tnpscthervupettagam.com/currentaffairs-detail/tps-5-rice-variety?cat=tamilnadu-news
-- Seed vigour study lists ADT 53 among 12 rice varieties with high seed vigour potential -- https://journalijecc.com/index.php/IJECC/article/view/3332
-- Tamil Nadu crop practice guide lists ADT 53 for Kuruvai (June-July) sowing in Tiruchirappalli and for Sornavari/Navarai seasons in northeastern districts -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/01_Rice.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- Pedigree-derived from the cross ADT 43 / JGL 384 (Pushpa et al., EJPB 2020) -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1094
-- CONFLICT: the supplied parentage ("pureline selection from Kanpur blackgram") is not supported by this source and appears to be wrong for a rice variety. No QTL or marker study was found -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1094

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: Tamil Nadu Rice Research Institute (TRRI), Aduthurai, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-aduthurai/varieties-released/
-- Contributing authors (EJPB 2020): R. Pushpa, R. Saraswathi, D. Sassikumar, R. Chandirakala, R. Suresh, B. Meenakumari, K. Chozan, S. Suresh, A. Karthikeyan, V. Ravi. The paper does not state which of these is the lead breeder -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2020.1101.018
-- No evidence found for a named lead breeder in the institute's variety list -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-aduthurai/varieties-released/

-- Seed-stock list also names: Agricultural Research Station, Paramakudi, 04564-222139; KVK Tindivanam, 04147-250001 / 90470 42517, kvktvm@tnau.ac.in; Rice Research Station, Tirur (phone not captured) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf

drought.details: Tolerant to moisture stress and considered drought tolerant. It can be suitable for dry land ecosystems, though protective life-saving irrigation may be required under severe stress. Morphological characterization indicates narrow leaves, which have been observed to be drought tolerant in most cases.

heat.details: While studies on the effect of temperature on urdbean phenological behavior involving ADT-6 exist, specific heat tolerance levels for ADT 6 are not detailed.

salinity.details: Tolerant to salt affected soils and salinity. ADT 6 has been included in studies investigating black gram genotypes under salinity stress at the vegetative stage.

flood.details: General information states urdbean has more tolerance to water logging conditions than mungbean, but specific flood tolerance for ADT 6 is not provided.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV/YMV), Urdbean Leaf Crinkle Virus (LCV), Leaf Curl Virus (LCV), and Stem Necrosis. Moderately resistant to Anthracnose and Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB). It is also known to be tolerant to root-knot nematode.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistant to stem fly and shows moderate resistance to pod borer. It is also tolerant to root knot nematode.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield ranges from 655 kg/ha (6.55 q/ha) to 7-8 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Information on stability across diverse environments is not explicitly provided, but its suitability for rice fallow conditions across multiple states suggests adaptability within this specific cropping system.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Highly suitable for rice fallow conditions, particularly for the December-January season in the Cauvery Delta Zone of Tamil Nadu. It is also advised for sowing in the Chithiraipattam (Summer Irrigated) season in districts of Tamil Nadu including Thanjavur, Thiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Cuddalore, Villupuram, Tiruchirappalli, and Perambalur. It is also practiced in rice fallow systems in Odisha, West Bengal, and Chhattisgarh.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Characterized by narrow leaves and pubescence.
agronomic_details.field_trials: ADT 6 has been included in various field trials and experiments, including those testing black gram varieties under different irrigation regimes and in FRBD design experiments for Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus resistance.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: ADT 6 was included in studies for morphological characterization and genetic diversity. It exhibits narrow leaves, which are associated with drought tolerance. It is also used in studies to investigate black gram genotypes under salinity stress.

disease_resistance.summary: DBGV-5 was used as a local check variety in field trials for Yellow Mosaic Disease (YMD) screening under natural conditions. It was not listed among the cultivars exhibiting resistance to YMD (Pratap urd-1, Uttara, PU-31, IPU-2-43), implying susceptibility or a lack of strong resistance (Result 5). DBGV-5 has also been utilized as a parent (LGB 752 × DBGV 5) in crosses to unravel the inheritance of Powdery Mildew Disease (PMD) resistance in blackgram, with F2 populations showing Mendelian segregation patterns for resistance (Result 7). However, its specific resistance level to PMD is not explicitly stated.

agronomic_details.adaptation: DBGV-5 is suitable for early or late sown conditions and intercropping situations (Original Data).

agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Erect and determinate growth habit, ovate leaf shape, black non-hairy smooth pods, and large seeds (Original Data). It is also resistant to lodging and shattering (Original Data). It has been identified as an early flowering type (Result 8).
agronomic_details.field_trials: DBGV-5 has been evaluated as a local check variety in field trials for screening Yellow Mosaic Disease (YMD) under natural conditions (Result 5). Data on various traits related to assimilate partitioning have been recorded for DBGV-5 in studies (Result 9).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (e.g., SNP, SSR) or their positions linked to specific traits for DBGV-5 are provided. However, genetic diversity analysis using morphological and molecular markers has been conducted on blackgram, with DBGV-5 being an identified genotype in such studies (Result 8).
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: The inheritance of Powdery Mildew Disease (PMD) resistance involving DBGV-5 as a parent (LGB 752 × DBGV 5) showed F1 resistance and F2 populations segregating in a 9:3:3:1 ratio, indicating significant Mendelian inheritance patterns for PMD resistance (Result 7). No specific QTLs are identified.

disease_resistance.summary: Powdery mildew (Erysiphe polygoni): BDU-12 was reported as moderately resistant in a natural epiphytotic screen and listed among the moderately resistant genotypes. Mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV): in a 2018 summer screen at ARS Bidar, a row showed a score of 2 and an MR (moderately resistant) rating; the snippet is partly garbled, so this rating is not fully reliable. A companion MYMV screen (ResearchGate listing) names BDU-12, but its category placement is unclear. Cercospora leaf spot: no BDU-12 evidence found. The DU-1 (UAS Dharwad, 2013) entry is susceptible to cercospora leaf spot and powdery mildew, but this is a separate line of evidence and is not confirmed to be BDU-12.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. A study of sucking pests (aphids, jassids) on blackgram at ARS Bidar evaluated seed dressings (imidacloprid, thiamethoxam) but does not name BDU-12, so no pest resistance evidence for BDU-12 was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Not found in searched sources for BDU-12 per-hectare yield in a multi-location trial. CSC record lists average yield as Not Available. A diversity study ranks BDU-12 highly for grain yield per plant and grain yield per hectare, but no numeric values were reported in the digest. DU-1 national table figures (about 14-15 q/ha) refer to the Dharwad DU-1 and are not attributed to BDU-12.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Not found in searched sources for BDU-12 varietal adaptation. The ARS Bidar station is in Zone-1 (north-eastern transition zone) of Karnataka with a blackgram mandate; this describes the station location, not confirmed varietal adaptation.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not found in searched sources. CSC record lists maturity_days as Not Available. The DU-1 duration (80-85 days) is for the Dharwad DU-1 and is not confirmed for BDU-12.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources. Pods per plant and pod length were ranked highly in a diversity study (see field_trials), but no morphological description was found.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Genetic diversity study of blackgram quantitative traits: BDU-12 ranked highly for pods per plant, pod length, grain yield per plant and grain yield per hectare. Year and trial details are not clear from the snippet. (2) Summer 2018 MYMV screen at ARS Bidar: score of 2 with MR rating; snippet partly garbled. (3) Natural epiphytotic powdery mildew screen: BDU-12 listed as moderately resistant. (4) Companion MYMV screen (ResearchGate listing): BDU-12 named, category unclear. (5) No multi-location maturity or yield trial for BDU-12 was found. (6) Bidar 2016-17 and 2017-18 kharif trials concern pest control, not varietal agronomy, and do not evaluate BDU-12 yield.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: BDU-12 (CSC name) / DU-1 (Seednet name), blackgram

Search note: four web_search queries were run (BDU-12 variety; BDU-12 breeder/Bidar institute; BDU-12 research papers; DU-1 Seednet). The search snippets gave no release notification, maturity, yield, or parentage for BDU-12, and no breeder names or contact details.

Name note: The evidence below refers to BDU-12 unless marked DU-1. The DU-1 items are a separate line of evidence. A 2013 UAS Dharwad release is also called DU-1, and it is not confirmed to be the same material as BDU-12.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- BDU-12 was reported as moderately resistant to powdery mildew (Erysiphe polygoni) in a natural epiphytotic screen, and was listed among the moderately resistant genotypes -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298342748_Screening_of_blackgram_genotypes_under_natural_epiphytotic_condition_for_powdery_mildew_disease_resistance_Erysiphae_polygoni_DC
- The DU-1 (UAS Dharwad, 2013) entry is described as susceptible to cercospora leaf spot and powdery mildew -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for BDU-12 were found in the results.

DISEASE AND PEST
- BDU-12 appeared in a 2018 summer MYMV screen at ARS Bidar, with a row showing a score of 2 and an MR (moderately resistant) rating. The snippet is partly garbled, so the rating is not fully reliable -- http://www.plantarchives.org/article/9-%20Screening%20of%20Blackgram%20genotypes%20against%20Mungbean%20Yellow%20Mosaic%20Virus%20(MYMV)%20disease.pdf
- A companion MYMV screen (ResearchGate listing) names BDU-12 among genotypes in the screen, but its category placement is unclear -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396464324_SCREENING_OF_BLACKGRAM_GENOTYPES_AGAINST_MUNGBEAN_YELLOW_MOSAIC_VIRUS_MYMV_DISEASE
- Sucking pests (aphids, jassids) on blackgram at ARS Bidar were studied with seed dressings (imidacloprid, thiamethoxam). BDU-12 is not named -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue4/PartAD/8-4-298-864.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A genetic diversity study of blackgram quantitative traits ranked BDU-12 highly for pods per plant, pod length, grain yield per plant and grain yield per hectare. Year and trial details are not clear from the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/315459088_Genetic_diversity_analysis_in_blackgram_L_Hepper_based_on_quantitative_traits
- No BDU-12 maturity duration or yield per hectare in a multi-location trial was found. DU-1 is listed in a national state-release table with 80-85 day duration and about 14-15 q/ha yield, but this is the Dharwad DU-1, not confirmed as the same variety -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- A Bidar-based study of 2016-17 and 2017-18 kharif trials is about pest control, not varietal agronomy -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue4/PartAD/8-4-298-864.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker, or genetic-mapping study on BDU-12 was found. The only genetic material found is the diversity analysis above -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/315459088_Genetic_diversity_analysis_in_blackgram_L_Hepper_based_on_quantitative_traits

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The Agricultural Research Station, Bidar (University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur, Karnataka) is the developing station. It lists TAU-1 and DU-1 as blackgram varieties it identified -- https://uasraichur.karnataka.gov.in/new-page/About+ARS+Bidar/en
- The station is in Zone-1 (north-eastern transition zone) of Karnataka, with a mandate covering blackgram -- https://uasraichur.karnataka.gov.in/new-page/About+ARS+Bidar/en
- Breeder names for BDU-12: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Agricultural Research Station, Bidar-585401, Karnataka, India, with UAS Raichur as parent university -- http://www.plantarchives.org/article/9-%20Screening%20of%20Blackgram%20genotypes%20against%20Mungbean%20Yellow%20Mosaic%20Virus%20(MYMV)%20disease.pdf (address); https://uasraichur.karnataka.gov.in/new-page/About+ARS+Bidar/en (institute page)
- Named contacts (name, role, email, phone): No evidence found. The ARS Bidar institute page was retrieved, but no email or phone appeared in the snippet.

PUBLICATIONS
- Hadimani, A.; Konda, C.R.; Nidagundi, J.M.; Patil, R. (year not confirmed in snippet). Genetic diversity analysis in blackgram [(L.) Hepper] based on quantitative traits. Research paper, UAS Raichur -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/315459088_Genetic_diversity_analysis_in_blackgram_L_Hepper_based_on_quantitative_traits
- Authors not confirmed (Sidramappa et al. are cited in the MYMV paper). (2018 season). Screening of blackgram genotypes against Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV) disease. Journal article, ARS Bidar -- http://www.plantarchives.org/article/9-%20Screening%20of%20Blackgram%20genotypes%20against%20Mungbean%20Yellow%20Mosaic%20Virus%20(MYMV)%20disease.pdf
- Shobharani, M.; Sunilkumar, N.M.; Sidramappa; Biradar, A. (2019). Field evaluation of imidacloprid and thiamethoxam against sucking insect pests of blackgram. Phytojournal, vol. 8(4) -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue4/PartAD/8-4-298-864.pdf
- Powdery mildew screening of blackgram genotypes under natural epiphytotic conditions (Erysiphe polygoni). Authors and year not confirmed in the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298342748_Screening_of_blackgram_genotypes_under_natural_epiphytotic_condition_for_powdery_mildew_disease_resistance_Erysiphae_polygoni_DC
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports, and DOI-level records for BDU-12: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seed sources for BDU-12 (UAS Raichur, ARS Bidar seed unit, NSC, KVK, private dealers): No evidence found.
- DU-1 is listed on the national urdbean variety compilation drawn from Seednet, but no seller or stock information was found -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- BDU-12 (CSC record): Karnataka, per the variety record given. No independent notification or state-recommendation source was found.
- DU-1 (Seednet and national table): the Dharwad DU-1 is listed under Gujarat, with a Karnataka listing in a separate table. The state listing for this name is inconsistent across sources -- http://dpd.gov.in/Urdbean.PDF

drought.details: DU-1 is tolerant to moisture stress and can withstand extremes of soil water stress. It is listed among stress-tolerant black gram genotypes.

heat.details: No specific information regarding DU-1's heat tolerance was found.

salinity.details: While attempts to incorporate salt tolerance in black gram are mentioned, and DU-1 is listed in a document related to adopting salt tolerant crops, direct evidence for DU-1's salt tolerance is not specified.

flood.details: Urdbean (blackgram) generally exhibits more tolerance to waterlogging conditions than mungbean, suggesting DU-1, as an urdbean variety, shares this characteristic.

disease_resistance.summary: DU-1 shows moderate resistance to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV), Leaf Crinkle Virus (LCV), anthracnose, and Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB). It is also listed as resistant or moderately resistant to charcoal rot caused by Macrophomina phaseolina.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific information regarding pest resistance was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields vary: 14-15 quintals per hectare (1400-1500 kg/ha) in central release documents for Gujarat. In specific trials, it was a top-yielding genotype with 1024 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: DU-1 exhibited stable performance across locations.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for Kharif, Rabi, and Summer seasons, and suitable for rice fallows. It is considered an 'all season' variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: DU-1 is characterized by high yield, bold seeds, and erect growth.
agronomic_details.field_trials: DU-1 was part of field trials conducted at Pantnagar during Kharif 2000-2001 and screened for resistance to charcoal rot. It has also been included in studies on adoption levels of recommended cultivation practices.
