EVIDENCE DIGEST: Ghantasala Minumu 1 / Ghantasala Mimumu 1 (GBG 1), Black gram (Vigna mungo)

Name note: The CSC name is "Ghantasala Minumu 1" and the Seednet name is "Ghantasala Mimumu 1 (GBG 1)". No page used either full name. The evidence below refers to "GBG 1" (also written GBG-1), listed under ARS Ghantasala. Pages about TBG 104 / Tirupati Minumu-1 (ARS Tirupati, 2017), PDF-Akola, KKM 1, ADT 6, LBG 752, and commercial seed listings for other varieties were discarded as different varieties.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to GBG 1. Searches returned only general black gram pages. -- https://www.agrifarming.in/black-gram-and-green-gram-varieties-for-kharif-and-rabi-seasons (checked; no GBG 1 stress data)

DISEASE AND PEST
- The central release table lists GBG 1 (2019, ARS Ghantashala) with a resistance note to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic (MYMV). The extracted text is fragmented, so treat it as a single-source table entry. -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for other disease or pest resistance (e.g., powdery mildew, root-knot nematode, pod borer) for GBG 1. -- n/a

- Maturity is listed as 70-75 days, and the yield column reads 13-14 with no unit in the extract (probably q/ha, not confirmed). -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf

- A research paper on black gram performance in Andhra Pradesh mentions trial sites at Ghantasala (rabi 2017-18), but the snippet does not confirm that GBG 1 was among the entries. BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- GBG 1 is attributed to ARS (Agricultural Research Station) Ghantasala, Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), released 2019. -- https://knowledge.desikheti.com/popular-black-gram-seed-varieties-in-india-complete-information/ ; http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf

disease_resistance.summary: Yellow mosaic disease (YMD): resistant under natural field conditions (AAU release notice; IAUA release notice; AAU/AGRESCO records; Pulse Research Station recommendation listing describing YMD resistance with better seed quality). The paper states the variety was developed for YMD resistance because local checks T-9 and GU-1 are highly susceptible to yellow mosaic in short-duration crops. Mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV): listed as resistant in one national listing (dpd.gov.in table entry GUJARAT 2022 ANAND URDBEAN 4). A seed vendor listing also states resistance against yellow mosaic virus disease. No other disease resistance found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No specific pest resistance was found for this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Kharif seed yield 1005 kg/ha (19.08% above T-9 and 23.92% above GU-1 in middle Gujarat). Summer seed yield 864 kg/ha (22.21% above T-9 and 23.42% above GU-1 in middle Gujarat). Average yield 961 kg/ha across seasons. Release notice range given as 3.5 to 4.5 q/acre (original data).
agronomic_details.stability: Average yield 961 kg/ha across seasons. Consistent superiority over T-9 and GU-1 reported for both kharif and summer in middle Gujarat. No multi-location stability analysis found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Middle Gujarat agro-climatic zone; suitable for kharif and summer seasons.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Medium (AAU/AGRESCO record, not stated in days). Conflicting day figures: 95-100 days (Fule Seeds vendor page) versus 65-75 days (IAUA notice). Seed rate of 7.5-8 kg/acre given by the vendor page.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-erect habit, medium maturity, hairy pods with 6-7 seeds, dull black seed. Quality: 24.66% protein, 55.58% carbohydrate, Fe 49.97 mg/kg, Zn 29.28 mg/kg.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Kharif seed yield trial in middle Gujarat: 1005 kg/ha, 19.08% above T-9 and 23.92% above GU-1. (2) Summer seed yield trial in middle Gujarat: 864 kg/ha, 22.21% above T-9 and 23.42% above GU-1. (3) Multi-season trials: average 961 kg/ha, tested as JAUG 2. (4) Proposed for summer and kharif recommendation to farmers of middle Gujarat at the 17th AGRESCO meeting. Trial location details beyond middle Gujarat, and trial years, not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: Searches used "Gujarat Anand Urdbean 4" (release-minutes name, also written GAU 4 / Shyamal). The Seednet name "Gujarat Urdbean 3 (GU-3: Anjani)" returned only a different blackgram variety from NAU Navsari (released 2020), so no evidence was kept for that name, and it is not attributed to this variety below.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Resistant to yellow mosaic disease under natural field conditions; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-urdbean-4-shayamal
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Described as resistant to yellow mosaic disease (YMD) in the AAU release notice; no other stress tolerance stated -- https://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Developed for YMD resistance because local checks T-9 and GU-1 are highly susceptible to yellow mosaic in short-duration crops -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354004319_Study_about_GAU_4_A_New_High_Yielding_Ymv_Resistant_Urdbean_Variety
- [Seednet name GU-3 Anjani] No evidence found for this variety

DISEASE AND PEST
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] YMD resistance reported in multiple AAU and AGRESCO records; no specific pest resistance found -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-urdbean-4-shayamal ; https://aau.in/college-menu/507
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Resistant to yellow mosaic in the Pulse Research Station recommendation listing (2021 release, YMD resistant with better seed quality) -- https://aau.in/college-menu/507
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Listed as resistant to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV) in one national listing -- https://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf (search result 23-9 item; the table entry labelled GUJARAT 2022 ANAND URDBEAN 4)
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Seed vendor listing states resistance against yellow mosaic virus disease -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gau-4-shyamal/
- [Seednet name GU-3 Anjani] No evidence found for this variety

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Kharif seed yield 1005 kg/ha, 19.08% above T-9 and 23.92% above GU-1 in middle Gujarat -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-urdbean-4-shayamal
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Summer seed yield 864 kg/ha, 22.21% above T-9 and 23.42% above GU-1 in middle Gujarat -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-urdbean-4-shayamal
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Average yield 961 kg/ha across seasons; tested as JAUG 2 in trials -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354004319_Study_about_GAU_4_A_New_High_Yielding_Ymv_Resistant_Urdbean_Variety
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Agronomic traits: semi-erect habit, medium maturity, hairy pods with 6-7 seeds, dull black seed -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-urdbean-4-shayamal
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Maturity conflict: AAU/AGRESCO record medium maturity (not in days); a vendor page gives 95-100 days and seed rate 7.5-8 kg/acre, which conflicts with the 65-75 day figure in the IAUA notice -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gau-4-shyamal/ ; https://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Proposed for summer and kharif recommendation to farmers of middle Gujarat at the AGRESCO meeting -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Quality: 24.66% protein, 55.58% carbohydrate, Fe 49.97, Zn 29.28 mg/kg -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-urdbean-4-shayamal

GENETICS AND QTL
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] DNA fingerprinting with SRAP markers against T-9 and GU-1 checks; no QTL or marker-trait mapping found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354004319_Study_about_GAU_4_A_New_High_Yielding_Ymv_Resistant_Urdbean_Variety
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Pedigree conflict: the supplied parentage (T-9 x NU-00-161, made rabi 2011-12) is not found in any source; the paper says the variety was selected from germplasm GP No. 6 at ARS Jabugam -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354004319_Study_about_GAU_4_A_New_High_Yielding_Ymv_Resistant_Urdbean_Variety

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Developed through selection by Pulse Research Station, Anand Agricultural University, Vadodara; released by the state variety release committee in 2021 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354004319_Study_about_GAU_4_A_New_High_Yielding_Ymv_Resistant_Urdbean_Variety
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Lead named scientist: Kalpeshkumar Vithalbhai Patel, Assistant Research Scientist, Pulse Research Station, AAU, working on pigeonpea, greengram and blackgram improvement; the profile also places him at Regional Research Station, Anand, which conflicts with the Pulse Research Station listing -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Kalpeshkumar-Patel
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Co-authors of the 2021 paper: H.C. Parmar, H.P. Patel, V.B. More, Vishal B. Kundaria, B.N. Patel (all Pulse Research Station, AAU) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354004319_Study_about_GAU_4_A_New_High_Yielding_Ymv_Resistant_Urdbean_Variety
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Originating centre in national table: Research Scientist, Pulse Research Station, AAU, Vadodara -- https://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- [Seednet name GU-3 Anjani] The only matching record names NAU Navsari for a different variety; not attributed -- http://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Kalpeshkumar Vithalbhai Patel (corresponding author), email kvpatel@aau.in -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354004319_Study_about_GAU_4_A_New_High_Yielding_Ymv_Resistant_Urdbean_Variety
- Address from the paper: Pulse Research Station, Anand Agricultural University, Vadodara 389003, Gujarat, India -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354004319_Study_about_GAU_4_A_New_High_Yielding_Ymv_Resistant_Urdbean_Variety

- Institute website: www.aau.in (Anand Agricultural University) -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anand_Agricultural_University
- No phone number found for the station or the breeder
- Not used: arsderol@aau.in (Agricultural Research Station, Derol, a different station) -- https://aau.in/college-menu/457

PUBLICATIONS
- Patel, K.V., Parmar, H.C., Patel, H.P., More, V.B., Kundaria, V.B., Patel, B.N. (2021). Study about GAU 4: A New High Yielding YMV Resistant Urdbean Variety. International Journal of Plant & Soil Science 33(17): 227-235 -- DOI 10.9734/IJPSS/2021/v331730567 (DOI as printed: 10.9734/IJPSS/2021/v33i173 0567; spacing removed)
- Combined AGRESCO of SAUs and Kamdhenu, 17th meeting proceedings, item 17.1.1.7 "Proposal for release of Urdbean variety Gujarat Anand Urdbean 4 (GAU 4: Shyamal)" (year not shown in the snippet) -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
- No other peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper found

SEED AVAILABILITY

- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or AAU seed-sales listing found in the search results
- [Seednet name GU-3 Anjani] No evidence found for this variety; the seed listings found refer to other Gujarat urdbean lines

RECOMMENDED STATES

- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] AGRESCO recommendation for farmers of middle Gujarat, summer and kharif -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf

official_quote.quote: Resistant to YMD under natural field condition

disease_resistance.research_summary: Yellow mosaic disease (YMD): resistant under natural field conditions (AAU release notice; IAUA release notice; AAU/AGRESCO records; Pulse Research Station recommendation listing describing YMD resistance with better seed quality). The paper states the variety was developed for YMD resistance because local checks T-9 and GU-1 are highly susceptible to yellow mosaic in short-duration crops. Mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV): listed as resistant in one national listing (dpd.gov.in table entry GUJARAT 2022 ANAND URDBEAN 4). A seed vendor listing also states resistance against yellow mosaic virus disease. No other disease resistance found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Powdery mildew: resistant up to the podding stage per the central release table (2015 release by IGKV Raipur for Chhattisgarh kharif and summer). Powdery mildew resistance is also reported in a Pulses review and a DPD summer-pulses table. Yellow mosaic virus (YMV): listed as resistant in an IGKV publication table (IGKV/Pub./T.bl./2014/18), but this reads as a single row and the YMV claim requires verification. No other disease resistance found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: No resistance to MYMV, bruchids, or other pests specific to this variety found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAME NOTE: Evidence below uses "Indira Urd Pratham" (CSC/release-table name) and "INDIRA URD PRATHAM (RU 03-14)" (Seednet name). Searches did not reach the Seednet portal. Where a source uses the code RU 03-14, the Seednet name is implied. A Gurudev listing uses "RU 07 08", which conflicts with RU 03-14.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to powdery mildew up to the podding stage, per the central release table, which records 2015 release by IGKV Raipur for Chhattisgarh kharif and summer -- https://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found in the searches.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Listed as resistant to yellow mosaic and powdery mildew in an IGKV publication table (IGKV/Pub./T.bl./2014/18), which reads as one row, so the YMV claim needs checking -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Girijesh-Sharma/publication/339134315_Improved_Cultivation_Practices_for_Dry_Land_Crops_in_Bastar_Plateau_Agroclimatic_Zone/links/5e3fe2b2a6fdccd965930ca7/Improved-Cultivation-Practices-for-Dry-Land-Crops-in-Bastar-Plateau-Agroclimatic-Zone.pdf
- Powdery mildew resistance is also reported in a Pulses review and a DPD summer-pulses table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348801694_Challenges_in_Pulses_Productivity_and_Agronomic_Opportunities_for_Enhancing_Growth_and_Yield_in_Blackgram_Vigna_mungo_L_Hepper_A_Review ; http://www.dpd.gov.in/2.%20Summer%20Pulses%20(English).pdf
- Resistance to MYMV, bruchids, or other pests specific to this variety: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release-table yield 12-13 q/ha, 70-75 days -- https://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- A private seller's description gives 12-14 q/ha and 70-75 days, which is a non-official source -- https://www.vantikatech.com/2020/04/high-yield-uradblack-gram-variety.html
- Raipur planting-geometry trial (kharif 2013) found Indira Urd Pratham gave the highest seed yield, stover yield and harvest index among four genotypes -- https://www.envirobiotechjournals.com/issues/article_abstract.php?aid=7538&iid=224&jid=3
- Bilaspur integrated nutrient management trial (kharif 2021) used this variety -- https://www.ijcmas.com/11-10-2022/Surabhi%20Patre,%20et%20al.pdf
- Chhattisgarh cluster demonstrations (Bemetara, Bhatapara, Janjgir-Champa and other districts) list "Indira urd 1", not confirmed as this variety -- https://dpd.gov.in/Annual%20Report%20%202023-24%2014.01.2025.pdf
- Multi-location trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Combining-ability study (2020) found this variety the best general combiner for most traits and reported best crosses with it -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-3-2020/Neeraj%20Ankur%20Toppo,%20et%20al.pdf
- Variety-specific QTL or marker studies: No evidence found. The 2022 GWAS on 100 blackgram genotypes (Punjab) does not name this variety in the retrieved text -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9310006/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Released by Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur, Chhattisgarh -- https://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- IGKV is an autonomous research and education body in Chhattisgarh -- https://www.dairyknowledge.in/dkp/link/indira-gandhi-krishi-vishwavidyalaya-igkv
- Lead breeder name(s) and station: No evidence found.

- Breeder names, roles, emails, phones: No evidence found.
- Institute-level postal address, phone, email, or contact page URL for IGKV: No evidence found in the searches. Institute website not retrieved.

- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP annual report entry was found in these searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY

- IndiaMART listing by Gurudev (Tikamgarh) for "RU 07 08" certified seed, 8 kg pack, 75-day duration; code conflicts with RU 03-14 -- https://dir.indiamart.com/impcat/urad-seeds.html
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU seed sales: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Chhattisgarh, for kharif and summer seasons -- https://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Release year is 2015 in the release table and Pulses report, but a 2016 date appears in a separate DPD table -- http://www.dpd.gov.in/2.%20Summer%20Pulses%20(English).pdf
- Listed in the Plant Authority registered-varieties compendium as "Indira Urd Pratham (RU 3-14)" -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compediumforallcategoryuptonov-2021.pdf
- Parentage: Not specified in any retrieved source.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: ICAR- Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur- 208024 (UP).
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Kharif season in entire Madhya Pradesh.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Kharif season (I)	15 Kg N + 40 Kg P2O5 + 20 Kg S per ha. (II)	Timely sown conditions. (III)	Seed rate 12-15 Kg/ha. (IV)	30 X 10 cm inter and intra-row spacing. (V)	Tolerant to pod shattering.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: The variety has market and distinct characters like dark green canopy, prolific bearing, black pods on maturity and medium bold seeds.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Tolerant to drought stress conditions.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to yellow mosaic virus, cercospora leaf spot, anthracnose, leaf crinklr, powdery mildew.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Tolerant to major insect-pest under field conditions.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 10-15 kg N + 40-45 kg P2O5 + 20 kg S as basal application. 20 kg Zn can also be applied.

drought.details: This variety, consistently identified as blackgram (urdbean) in search results, is tolerant to moisture stress and drought stress. It is also noted for its tolerance to combined stress of drought and salinity. The developing institution, ICAR-IIPR, is involved in QTLs identification for drought tolerance.

heat.details: This variety, consistently identified as blackgram (urdbean) in search results, has been identified as a relatively heat tolerant genotype. The Division of Crop Improvement at ICAR-IIPR (the developing institution) focuses on the development of heat tolerant varieties, including QTLs identification for heat tolerance.

salinity.details: This variety, consistently identified as blackgram (urdbean) in search results, is tolerant to combined stress of drought and salinity.

flood.details: Urdbean (blackgram), the crop consistently identified for this variety in search results, generally exhibits more tolerance to water logging conditions than mungbean. IPU 10-26 is explicitly associated with waterlogging tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: This variety, consistently identified as blackgram (urdbean) in search results, is resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV). It exhibits moderate resistance to Leaf Crinkle Virus (LCV), anthracnose, and Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB). It is also resistant to Urdbean Leaf Crinkle Virus (ULCV) and rust.

pest_resistance.summary: This variety, consistently identified as blackgram (urdbean) in search results, is highly tolerant to leaf folder. General resistance to insect-pests is also noted in context with this variety's release.

agronomic_details.yield: This variety, consistently identified as blackgram (urdbean) in search results, has a potential yield of 10-12 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: In Urdbean Initial Varietal Trials conducted in 2013-14, IPU 10-26 proved superior by 2.58 (unit not specified) as a test entry.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for the Kharif season in Madhya Pradesh. As a blackgram variety, it is noted as relatively heat tolerant. Its phenological behavior (including days to flowering) is influenced by temperature and photoperiod, and it was screened for photo insensitivity.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Seeds are brown in colour.
agronomic_details.field_trials: IPU 10-26 was a test entry in the Urdbean Initial Varietal Trial during 2013-14. It was also included in screenings for days to flowering and photo insensitivity in Vigna mungo (blackgram).

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: ICAR- Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur- 208024 (UP).
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Kharif season in entire Madhya Pradesh.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Kharif season (I)	15 Kg N + 40 Kg P2O5 + 20 Kg S per ha. (II)	Timely sown conditions. (III)	Seed rate 12-15 Kg/ha. (IV)	30 X 10 cm inter and intra-row spacing. (V)	Tolerant to pod shattering.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: The variety has market and distinct characters like dark green canopy, prolific bearing, black pods on maturity and medium bold seeds.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Tolerant to drought stress conditions.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to yellow mosaic virus, cercospora leaf spot, anthracnose, leaf crinklr, powdery mildew, bacterial leaf blight and web blight.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Tolerant to major insect-pest under field conditions.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 10-15 kg N + 40-45 kg P2O5 + 20 kg S as basal application. 20 kg Zn can also be applied.

drought.details: Tolerant to moisture stress and combined stress of drought and salinity. It has been tested for drought stress conditions at the seedling stage through PEG (Polyethylene glycol).

heat.details: While general abiotic stress (including heat) research is mentioned alongside IPU 13-1, specific heat tolerance for this variety is not explicitly stated in the provided results.

salinity.details: Tolerant to combined stress of drought and salinity.

flood.details: While urdbean generally has tolerance to waterlogging, specific tolerance for IPU 13-1 to flood or waterlogging conditions is not explicitly stated.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV). Moderately resistant to Leaf Crinkle Virus (LCV), anthracnose, and Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB). It is part of the development of disease-resistant urdbean cultivars.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance for IPU 13-1 is detailed, though it is a modern variety, and Integrated Crop Management (ICM) is practiced with it.

agronomic_details.yield: No quantitative average yield in standard units (e.g., quintals/hectare) is available from the search results. Some demonstration results indicate a figure of '1.98' (units unclear).
agronomic_details.stability: Not specified
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for Kharif season cultivation in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Main-stem pod bearing variety.
agronomic_details.field_trials: IPU 13-1 has been part of Cluster Frontline Demonstrations (CFLD) by KVKs (e.g., KVK Datia, KVK Mahoba, KVK Saharanpur) and included in Action Plans for pulse production in Uttar Pradesh. It has also been used in research studies evaluating growth parameters.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: IPU 13-1 has been included in molecular diversity analysis among different isolates.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs identified.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: IPU 13-1 is characterized as a main-stem pod bearing urdbean variety, a significant plant type for accommodating greater yield potential.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: listed as resistant to wilt in the DPD variety listing (main disease tolerance on record). Yellow mosaic virus (YMV): reported as resistant in three sources, namely the DPD listing, a ResearchGate review (described as whitefly-transmitted disease) and an indiacustomercare-independent exam resource that lists LBG 752 among resistant varieties with Pant Urd-19 and KU-96-3. CONFLICT: a KVK Garikapadu demonstration sheet calls LBG-752 'YMV susceptible' in one treatment, while another entry in the same sheet calls PU31/LBG 752 'highly resistant to YMV'. agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for LBG 752. Multi-location or AICRP yield trial data: No evidence found. LBG-20 (a parent) was stable across environments for branch number in a dual-season trial, which is not a yield stability measure for LBG 752.

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Farmer-level demonstration on YMV tolerance and IPM at Garikapadu (KVK), with LBG 752 as the farmers' practice variety; the sheet contains the conflicting YMV susceptible/highly resistant entries described under disease_resistance. (3) 2023 Krishna district adoption study: adoption constraints identified as lack of knowledge, extension and timely seed availability; no yield results reported. (4) Multi-location or AICRP yield trial: No evidence found. (5) Dual-season trial of parent LBG-20 for branch number only; not a trial of LBG 752.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Photo-insensitive, so it can be sown across seasons -- https://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf (the URL is http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf)
Listed as resistant to wilt and yellow mosaic virus, which are the main disease tolerances on record -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The 2019 genetic divergence study at RARS Lam (LBG 752 used as a check) and the 2023 Krishna district adoption study do not report stress scores for this variety -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2022/vol11issue2/PartAD/11-2-118-932.pdf ; https://ideas.repec.org/a/ags/ajaees/367470.html

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to yellow mosaic virus (YMV), described as whitefly-transmitted -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348801694_Challenges_in_Pulses_Productivity_and_Agronomic_Opportunities_for_Enhancing_Growth_and_Yield_in_Blackgram_Vigna_mungo_L_Hepper_A_Review
Resistant to YMV and listed among resistant varieties with Pant Urd-19 and KU-96-3 -- https://indianagriexam.com/courses/general-agriculture-for-competitive-exams/lesson/cultivation-of-urd-bean-black-gram-module-22/
CONFLICT: A KVK Garikapadu demonstration sheet calls LBG-752 "YMV susceptible" in one treatment, while another entry calls PU31/LBG 752 "highly resistant to YMV" -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/KVK/KVK,%20Garikapadu%20activities.pdf
Pest resistance (pod borer, whitefly, aphids, thrips): No evidence found specific to LBG 752 -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/KVK/KVK,%20Garikapadu%20activities.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Potential yield 18-20 q/ha, duration 75-80 days, "All Seasons" in Andhra Pradesh -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
Yield of about 2000 kg/ha in 75-80 days (differs from the 18-20 q/ha figure above) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348801694_Challenges_in_Pulses_Productivity_and_Agronomic_Opportunities_for_Enhancing_Growth_and_Yield_in_Blackgram_Vigna_mungo_L_Hepper_A_Review
Farmer-level demonstration (YMV tolerance and IPM) in Garikapadu, with LBG 752 as the farmers' practice variety -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/KVK/KVK,%20Garikapadu%20activities.pdf
Adoption, constraints (lack of knowledge, extension and timely seed availability) in Krishna district -- https://ideas.repec.org/a/ags/ajaees/367470.html
Multi-location or AICRP yield trial data for LBG 752: No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage LBG 402 x LBG 20, bred by pedigree method -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Blackgram.pdf
LBG 402 (Prabhava) is photo-sensitive and wilt-resistant, which helps explain the wilt tolerance of the cross -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Blackgram.pdf
LBG-20 was stable across environments for branch number in a dual-season trial -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4523
QTL, marker or RAPD study on LBG 752: No evidence found. The RAPD paper found covers other black gram lines (PU-31 and accessions) -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5383788/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Lam, Guntur, Andhra Pradesh 522 034 -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf ; https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Blackgram.pdf

The chickpea source (https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf) lists a "LAM ANGRAU 2010, 15 q, wilt and YMV" row that appears to be this black gram entry misfiled under chickpea. Seednet name "Lam Minumu-752" matches "LBG 752 (Lam Minumu 752)" in the central release list; the name "Lam Minumu 752" was searched under both crops. The release-minutes name is therefore evidence under "LBG 752 / Lam Minumu 752", not chickpea.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Mash 391 (variety_name) / MASH-1 (seednet_variety_name), blackgram (Vigna mungo)

Search status: The search tool hit its usage limit after one usable query ("Mash 391 blackgram variety"), so only one search returned results. The later queries (breeder, research papers, seed availability) were not run. The only result returned was about a different blackgram variety (PU-31, Kathua district, J&K) and was discarded under the strict relevance rule. Every heading below therefore reflects that single unrelated search, and the gaps need a rerun before this record is used.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The one search returned only PU-31 yield-gap material, which is a different variety.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. Not searched successfully.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The only trial-related result concerned PU-31, not Mash 391 or MASH-1.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. Not searched successfully.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The record gives institution as "Not specified" and parentage as "A selection from local material of Punjab developed in early fifties" (supplied variety record, no URL). No breeder name was found on the web.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder or institute contact was located. A search for the breeder or institute was not completed.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. Not searched successfully. No authors, titles, DOIs or URLs were located for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. Not searched successfully (the seed-availability query was blocked by the limit).

RECOMMENDED STATES: Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Orissa and Tamil Nadu -- supplied variety record only (CSC release data as given in the input; not confirmed by any web source). Year of release recorded as 2010-12-23 (CSC/Seednet input field; not web-verified).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Mash 479 is reported resistant to MYMV, powdery mildew, bacterial leaf spot (BLS) and urdbean leaf crinkle virus (LCV) -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Mash 479 in any search result.

DISEASE AND PEST
Mash 479 is described as a disease-resistant kharif urdbean -- https://oar.icrisat.org/6556/
Mash 479 is listed as resistant to MYMV, PM, BLS and LCV, with a KUG 479 code in the same table -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
Pest resistance (whitefly, stem fly, bruchids, aphids): No evidence found for Mash 479.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Mash 479 is listed with a yield of 10-12 q/ha, a duration of 82-85 days (the table column is ambiguous), spring-season suitability and the NWPZ zone -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
Note: the release-minutes date is 2010-12-23, while this source gives 2011. Confirm against the CSC minutes.
Multi-location or field-trial results specific to Mash 479: No evidence found.
Mash 479 appears as a reference point in a protein-content table (25.25%, citing Sandhu et al. 2012) -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full
Agronomy package for Mash 479 specifically: No evidence found. Generic blackgram agronomy pages do not name it.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage ("selection from local Punjab material, similar to Mash-1"): No evidence found in any search result. The only related source is the Frontiers review, which lists Mash 479 in a quality table but does not state its parentage -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full
QTL, marker or GWAS studies naming Mash 479: No evidence found. The PAU GWAS paper (Singh et al. 2022) is about a 100-genotype panel and does not name Mash 479 in the retrieved text -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9310006/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: PAU Ludhiana is listed as the originating centre -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
Breeding paper authors: J S Sandhu, R K Gill, I Singh, S Singh, S K Gupta (2012). Their affiliations were not shown in the retrieved record, so they are not confirmed as the lead breeders -- https://oar.icrisat.org/6556/
The PAU GWAS paper (Singh et al. 2022) lists PAU Ludhiana departments but does not name Mash 479 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9310006/

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for PAU Ludhiana's pulses programme appeared in any result. The ICRISAT repository record lists no contact details.

PUBLICATIONS
Sandhu, J S; Gill, R K; Singh, I; Singh, S; Gupta, S K (2012). Mash 479, a disease resistant variety of kharif urdbean. Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding 72(1): 109 -- https://oar.icrisat.org/6556/
Singh, L; Dhillon, G S; Kaur, S; et al. (2022). Genome-wide Association Study for Yield and Yield-Related Traits in Diverse Blackgram Panel (Vigna mungo L. Hepper). Frontiers in Genetics -- DOI 10.3389/fgene.2022.849016. Included as context only; it does not name Mash 479 in the retrieved text.
Also reference-listed in: Frontiers in Plant Science review (2023), "Genetics, genomics, and breeding of black gram" -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full
No field-trial, AICRP report or KrishiKosh thesis specific to Mash 479 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for Mash 479 or KUG 479 was returned. A generic grower's guide lists "Mash-479" among varieties but gives no seed source -- https://www.roysfarm.com/growing-black-gram/

RECOMMENDED STATES
Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand (the NWPZ zone) are listed for Mash 479 -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
A second table lists KUG-479 under Punjab and Uttarakhand/UP, consistent with the above -- http://dpd.gov.in/Urdbean.PDF
The release record says "Western Uttar Pradesh and Plains of Uttarakhand," which is narrower than the NWPZ notation. Both forms are noted here.

MASH-48 (SEEDNET NAME) EVIDENCE
Searches for the Seednet name returned "Mash 48" and "Mash-48" in general variety lists, without a variety code, release year or breeder. These pages are the only matches for the Seednet name:
- "Mash 48" listed as popular in Haryana, Madhya Pradesh and Punjab -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/xml
- "Mash-48" in a list of varieties -- https://indiaagronet.com/indiaagronet/crop%20info/black_gram.htm
Identity with Mash 479 / KUG 479 is not confirmed. These may refer to a different or older line. Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) pages were not returned by any search.

disease_resistance.summary: Mash 1190: No disease resistance evidence found; the DPD table resistance column is blank. Mash 114 (linkage unconfirmed): a 2006-era press report states resistance to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV); this is unverified and not from a peer-reviewed source. General context only: major black gram threats include MYMV, urdbean leaf crinkle virus, Cercospora leaf spot and powdery mildew.

pest_resistance.summary: Mash 1190: No pest resistance evidence found; the DPD table resistance column is blank. Mash 114: no variety-specific pest resistance found. The farm-advice page states yellow mosaic is spread by whitefly; this is general crop advice, not variety-specific. General context: whitefly, bruchids and others are major black gram pests.

agronomic_details.yield: Mash 1190: Not available; the yield cell is not legible in the extracted DPD text. Mash 114 (linkage unconfirmed): average yield 3.7 q/acre (farm-advice page).
agronomic_details.stability: Mash 114 (linkage unconfirmed): out-yielded the check Mash 338 by 39.45% across 14 multi-location trials. Stability across environments beyond these trial results is not found in searched sources for either entry.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Mash 1190: Listed for NWPZ (Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand) in the DPD table. Mash 114: Punjab-focused farm advice; no separate state recommendation found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Mash 1190: 70-80 days per DPD table (input field reads 'Not available in provided image segment'). Mash 114 (linkage unconfirmed): about 85 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: a) Leaflets are narrow and dark green, b) Stem and pods are less hairy. Mash 114 (linkage unconfirmed): dwarf, short-duration kharif variety with 6-7 bold black seeds per pod.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Mash 1190: No trial result specific to this entry was found; the DPD table gives maturity and region only. Mash 114 (linkage unconfirmed): (1) 14 multi-location trials, 39.45% over check Mash 338; (2) PAU breeding trials, 45.2% more yield than Mash 338 and 20% more in agronomic trials (press report). The 45.2% and 39.45% figures differ and the sources do not reconcile them. Management data (not trial results): kharif seed rate 7-8 kg/acre; summer seed rate 19-20 kg/acre; seed treatment with a fungicide then Rhizobium at 2 g/kg.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Mash 1190 (variety_name, CSC minutes) / Mash 114 (seednet_variety_name, Seednet portal)

Name note: The Mash 1190 (SUG 1190) entry comes from the DPD central-release table. The Mash 114 entries come from the review, press and farm-advisory pages. I did not reach the Seednet portal, so no Seednet record was verified. No source I found explicitly links Mash 1190 and Mash 114 as the same entry. The input's parentage (Mash 338 x RBI-1) matches the Mash 114 descriptions below, so treat that link as unconfirmed.

Release year: the input says 2022-10-26, but the DPD table lists Mash 1190 with year 2023 -- https://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Mash 1190: No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance -- http://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Mash 114: No stress-tolerance findings specific to this variety were found in the sources reviewed. The review covers black gram stresses in general and says breeding needs more diverse material for stress resistance -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/

DISEASE AND PEST
- Mash 1190: The DPD table gives a days-to-maturity and region for this entry but its resistance column is blank. No disease or pest resistance evidence found -- http://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Mash 114: A 2006-era news report says it is resistant to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV) -- https://www.oneindia.com/2006/06/15/pau-launches-two-new-high-yielding-maize-varieties-1150360564.html
- Mash 114: The farm-advice page says yellow mosaic is spread by whitefly. This is general crop advice, not variety-specific -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/pulses/mash-urd
- General context: major black gram threats include MYMV, urdbean leaf crinkle virus, Cercospora leaf spot, powdery mildew, and whitefly, bruchids and others -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Mash 1190: Listed as a PAU Ludhiana variety with 70-80 days to maturity. Its yield cell is not legible in the extracted text, so no yield figure is recorded -- http://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Mash 114: Described as a dwarf, short-duration kharif variety ready in about 85 days, with 6-7 bold black seeds per pod and average yield of 3.7 q/acre -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/pulses/mash-urd
- Mash 114: Kharif seed rate 7-8 kg/acre; summer seed rate 19-20 kg/acre; seed treatment with a fungicide then Rhizobium at 2 g/kg -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/pulses/mash-urd
- Mash 114: Across 14 multi-location trials it out-yielded the check Mash 338 by 39.45% -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full
- Mash 114: In PAU breeding trials it gave 45.2% more yield than Mash 338, and 20% more in agronomic trials (press report) -- https://www.oneindia.com/2006/06/15/pau-launches-two-new-high-yielding-maize-varieties-1150360564.html
- Mash 114: Its breeding-trial figure (45.2%) differs from the 39.45% multi-location figure above. The sources do not reconcile the two.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Mash 114: Developed from an interspecific cross between black gram and rice bean -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full
- Mash 114: Listed among genotypes with high Fe content (97.9 ppm, Singh et al. 2017) in the nutritional-quality table -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/
- General context: rice-bean traits (pod number, seed weight and MYMD resistance) have been introgressed into black gram -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/
- General QTL study: MYMV resistance QTLs were identified and validated in blackgram. It is not specific to Mash 1190 or Mash 114 -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4459
- Mash 1190: No QTL or marker study found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Mash 1190: Originating centre is listed as PAU Ludhiana, under the ICAR AICRP on MULLaRP source -- http://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Mash 114: Described as released by Punjab Agricultural University -- https://blackgram.in/
- Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found for either name. No institute breeder page was found.
- AICRP on MULLaRP coordinating centre: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4459

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Punjab Agricultural University, Ferozepur Road, PAU Gate 2, Ludhiana, Punjab 140004 (address as listed by NDDB) -- https://nddb.coop/farmer/animal-nutrition/state-wise-list-of-seeds-producer-supplier
- Institute website: www.pau.edu -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_Agricultural_University
- Director (Seeds) office phones, 2019 listing: 94640-37325, 98159-65404, 98724-28072. Dated; verify before use -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=4304
- Official email: No evidence found
- Breeder names, roles, phones and emails: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- Singh et al. (2013). Mash 114 multi-location trial results (14 locations, 39.45% over Mash 338). Full title and journal not captured -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full
- Authors not captured (2023). Genetics, genomics, and breeding of black gram [Vigna mungo (L.) Hepper]. Frontiers in Plant Science -- DOI 10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/
- Vadivel K., Manivannan N., Mahalingam A., Satya V.K., Vanniarajan C., Ragul S. (2023). search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Urd 7 (black gram / urd bean)

Name handling: The CSC-style name "Pant Urd 7" and the Seednet name "Pant Urd-7" both appear in the sources. The DPD compilation lists it as "Pant U 7" with code "PU 10-16". All evidence below refers to that same entry. Only the DPD compilation names this variety in the crop context. The Seednet portal itself was not reachable in these searches.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No variety-specific evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The DPD table gives no stress information for this entry. -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- The DPD compilation lists "Pant U 7" (year 2020, GBPUA&T, code PU 10-16, Pantnagar) with the salient feature "MYMV and PM resistant", meaning resistance to mungbean yellow mosaic virus and powdery mildew. -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- No independent screening data naming Pant Urd 7 were found. The MYMIV screening paper on ResearchGate names PANT URD-19, not Pant Urd 7, so it was discarded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/349219356_Urdbean

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The DPD row gives yield 8-9 q/ha and maturity 80-85 days. Column alignment was inferred from the table header and is not confirmed by a release notification. -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Pant Urd-7 was grown as a test crop in a soil-test-based fertilizer prescription study on Mollisol of Uttarakhand. The page gives no author, year or journal, and it reports nutrient requirements per quintal of urd grain, not varietal yield. -- https://gbpuat-in.academia.edu/Departments/Agriculture/Documents

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- No evidence found. Parentage and breeding method for Pant Urd 7 were not specified in any source. "PU 10-16" is the only breeding-line code found, from the DPD compilation. -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- The 2024 black gram genetics and breeding review does not name Pant Urd 7, so it was not used. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10822891/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUA&T), Pantnagar, which the DPD compilation lists as the originating centre. -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- No breeder name for Pant Urd 7 was found. The 2021 GBPUAT newsletter names Panwar, Verma and Arora, but it is about Pant Urd 12, so those names were not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/26.07.2021_Issue-13_COA_Pantnagar_Newsletter.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder or variety-specific contact was found. Institute-level details from the GBPUAT newsletter: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar 263145, Uttarakhand. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/26.07.2021_Issue-13_COA_Pantnagar_Newsletter.pdf
- Institute website as listed on Wikipedia: gbpuat.ac.in, with the same Pantnagar 263145 postal code. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G._B._Pant_University_of_Agriculture_and_Technology
- Conflicting postal code: a stakeholder listing gives Pantnagar, Udham Singh Nagar 244923. The 263145 code is supported by two sources and is the more likely one. -- https://www.space4water.org/stakeholder/govind-ballabh-pant-university-agriculture-and-technology-pantnagar
- No email or phone number for the institute, the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, or the pulses programme was found in these results.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or conference paper naming Pant Urd 7 was found. Results for the Pant Urd 31, Pant U-35, Pant U-8/U-9 and Pant Urd 12 papers were discarded because they name other varieties.
- Partial item (author and year unknown): Soil Test Crop Response based fertilizer prescription for Urd grown on Mollisol of Uttarakhand. Source: GBPUAT document page, with Pant Urd-7 as test crop. -- https://gbpuat-in.academia.edu/Departments/Agriculture/Documents

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The fourth search returned only general GBPUAT seed-brand statements ("Pantnagar Seeds") and a breeder-seed demand note for other varieties (Pant Urd 10, Pant Urd 12). Neither names Pant Urd 7, so neither was used. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/research/From%20seed%20to%20transformation.pdf
- No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale listing for Pant Urd 7 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttarakhand, kharif season, per the DPD compilation. The compilation's central-versus-state placement of this row is unclear, and no CSC release notification was found to confirm it. -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf

Search limits: Four searches were run. The official Seednet, ICAR and KrishiKosh pages were not reached, so the Seednet record, the CSC minutes and any breeder contact remain unverified and should be checked directly on those portals.

Search note: the four allowed web_search queries were run. The retrieved pages refer to "Pant U 8" and "Pant U-8" (the form used in the dpd.gov.in table and the Pantnagar food-science papers). No page used the seednet form "Pant Urd-8" or the code "PU 11-14". Every finding below refers to the "Pant U 8 / Pant U-8" spelling, which I have matched to this variety on the basis of the same name, crop and institution.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for Pant U 8 specifically. The only stress-tolerance text in the results is general black gram crop advice (drought and heat tolerance, frost susceptibility) that does not name this variety -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/black-gram-ppt-black-gram-also-known-as-urad-or-urd-bean-is-an-important-pulse-crop-grown-in-india/271676749

DISEASE AND PEST
Partial, unconfirmed: the central release table lists Pant U 8 with a resistance note that is cut off in the retrieved text ("Res."), so the specific disease or pest is not recoverable -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
Not applicable: the resistance statements for Pant Urd-19, Pant U-30, Pant Urd-9/10 and Pant U-84 in other pages refer to different varieties and were excluded -- https://indianagriexam.com/courses/general-agriculture-course-for-for-competitive-exams/lesson/cultivation-of-urd-bean-black-gram-module-22/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Central release table entry for Pant U 8: year 2020, GBPUA&T, maturity 80-85 days, yield column reads 9-10 (units not labelled in the retrieved text, most likely q/ha), Uttarakhand, kharif season -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
No field-trial, multi-location or AICRP result for Pant U 8 was found -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage, breeding-line code, breeding method and genome/marker data for Pant U 8: No evidence found. The breeding-method review hits concern Pant U 26, Pant U 30 and Pant U-84 and were excluded -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327386671_Realization_of_facts_and_profiteering_of_black_gram_through_different_breeding_methods

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution (from the central release table): G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUA&T), Pantnagar -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
Crop Research Centre (CRC), G.B. Pant University, Pantnagar, is named as the source of the Pant U-8 seed used in a food-quality study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/349865866_Product_formulation_from_black_gram_and_its_evaluation_for_nutritional_and_sensory_quality
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact was found. No GBPUA&T institute email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL appeared in any retrieved result. No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Kanth, A. and others (2021). Product formulation from black gram and its evaluation for nutritional and sensory quality. Journal publication (ResearchGate record; journal not confirmed in retrieved text) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/349865866_Product_formulation_from_black_gram_and_its_evaluation_for_nutritional_and_sensory_quality
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2021). Nutritional quality evaluation of improved varieties of black gram (Phaseolus mungo). The Pharma Innovation Journal 10(1) -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue1/PartC/10-1-7-834.pdf
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2021). Nutritional quality evaluation of improved varieties of black gram (Phaseolus mungo) (ResearchGate record). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348417799_Nutritional_quality_evaluation_of_improved_varieties_of_black_gram_Phaseolus_mungo
Note: these two papers compare Pant U-8, Pant U-9, Pant U-31 and Pant U-35 for nutrition and sensory traits. They contain no agronomic, stress or genetic data for Pant U 8.
No peer-reviewed agronomy, breeding, AICRP or KrishiKosh thesis for Pant U 8 was found -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The only seed listings in the results were generic black gram listings, and the named varieties (Pant Urad-9, Pant Urad-10) are not Pant U 8 -- https://kvssl.com/products/black-gram/
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for Pant U 8 was found -- No evidence found

RECOMMENDED STATES
Uttarakhand (kharif season) -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf

drought.details: Tolerant to combined stress of drought and salinity.

heat.details: No specific evidence of heat tolerance for Pant Urd 9 was found in the provided results. While abiotic stresses including heat are mentioned generally, direct tolerance for this variety is not specified.

salinity.details: Tolerant to combined stress of drought and salinity. Mentioned in the context of improving yield of salt tolerant sugarcane, but Pant Urd 9 is listed alongside.

flood.details: No specific evidence for flood tolerance (waterlogging) for Pant Urd 9 was found.

disease_resistance.summary: Pant Urd 9 exhibits resistance to Mung bean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV), Powdery Mildews, and Urdbean Leaf Crinkle Virus (ULCV).

pest_resistance.summary: Agro-advisories list Pant Urd 9 as an improved variety that is tolerant or resistant to insect pests. However, it has been noted that plant mortality can be caused by insect pest attacks in experiments using this variety.

agronomic_details.field_trials: Pant Urd 9 has been utilized in experiments focusing on nutrition and weed management practices. It is also listed among varieties undergoing farmer field evaluation.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NOTE: Pant Urd 10 (CSC name) and Pant Urd 12 (Seednet name) are both black gram (Vigna mungo, urd bean), not chickpea. The "chickpea" field in the input appears to be wrong and I did not search chickpea. No evidence I found links Pant Urd 10 and Pant Urd 12 as the same variety, so the two names are reported separately below. The search budget ran out after 4 web_search calls, so breeder, contact and publication coverage is incomplete.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance under either name. The search returned general black gram pages and other varieties. (Searched under Pant Urd 10 and Pant Urd 12.)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Pant Urd 10 (CSC table row): listed as resistant to MYMV and powdery mildew, with the note "(PU 10-23)" and LCV listed in the same row; the table layout makes the exact pairing ambiguous. -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Pant Urd 12: the 2021 Pantnagar newsletter describes it as disease resistant and reports reactions to important diseases and insect pests, but the snippet does not name the specific diseases. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/26.07.2021_Issue-13_COA_Pantnagar_Newsletter.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pant Urd 10 (CSC table row): 80-85 days duration and 12-13 q/ha yield, with the table noting Pant Urd 10 as kharif and released in 2019 by GBPUA&T. The 2019 year conflicts with the input release date of 2018-08-10. -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Urd 11 / Pant Urd 12 (blackgram, PU 13-05, GBPUAT)

Search status: four web_search queries were run, which is the maximum allowed. A fifth query was refused by the tool limit. The first batch's full result objects were not kept in session state, so I could not re-read them. Nothing below is verified against a primary release notification, Seednet listing, or institute page for this variety.

Naming: "Pant Urd 11" (CSC release-minutes name) and "Pant Urd 12" (Seednet name) were both searched. No result tied either name to this variety, so no evidence is attributed to either name.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searched under both names; no result described drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No result gave MYMV, anthracnose, or other disease or pest reaction for this variety. The only resistance-related hit concerned a different variety, VBN 11 -- http://www.researchgate.net/publication/375642257_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_VBN_11_-A_new_high_yielding_and_MYMV_disease_resistant_blackgram_variety (not a match; excluded).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for this variety. One unrelated Pantnagar spacing trial (kharif 2000-01 urd bean, wider spacing and pod numbers) was returned: https://saulibrary.edu.bd/daatj/public/uploads/Done%2019-10396.pdf (not about Pant Urd 11; excluded).

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The MYMV inheritance study in the VBN 11 result is for a different variety and is excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No breeder name, developing station, or institute page for Pant Urd 11/12 was returned. The institution given in the input is G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology; this was not confirmed by any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No name, email, phone, address or contact-page URL was retrieved for GBPUAT or for this variety's breeding programme.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, report, thesis or KrishiKosh record was retrieved that names Pant Urd 11 or Pant Urd 12.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The fourth search was not run as a seed-specific query. The Seednet name "Pant Urd 12" returned only a generic blackgram slideshow: https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/black-gram-ppt-black-gram-also-known-as-urad-or-urd-bean-is-an-important-pulse-crop-grown-in-india/271676749 (not a seed source; excluded).

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Only partial. The input lists Uttarakhand as the recommended state, but no search result confirmed this. The Department of Pulses central-release list was returned, with its visible entries including Pant U 8 (2020): http://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf. Its visible snippet did not show a Pant Urd 11 or Pant Urd 12 row, so the list should be checked directly for the entry and its notified zone.

Next steps for a complete record: open the dpd.gov.in list and find the Pant Urd 11 row; search seednet.gov.in for "Pant Urd 12"; check GBPUAT's Pantnagar pulses/breeding pages and KrishiKosh for the variety; and check the CSC or AICRP-MULLaRP annual reports for the 2023 release.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: TJU 130 (Trombay Jawahar Urd 130), blackgram

Name note: The search found no source that uses "variety_name" or "seednet_variety_name" for this line. Every TJU 130 hit below is a list entry or a related-post link. Nothing I found confirms the CSC release minutes, the Seednet listing, or the 2023-05-02 release date.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Krishak Jagat's variety pages list TJU 130 by name but give no stress data for it. Its only TJU 130 mention is a related-post link on other urdbean notification pages -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/urdbean-variety-black-gram-adt-7-ad-tr-bg-14003/
- No TJU 130-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data was found in any search result. The Vikaspedia Cercospora-resistant entries name Jawahar urd-2 and Jawahar urd-3, which are different JNKVV lines, not TJU 130 -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/blackgram-and-greengram?lgn=en

DISEASE AND PEST
- No TJU 130-specific disease or pest resistance data was found. The only resistance material in the results is wild Trombay blackgram (INGR10133) and TU94-2, which were studied for yellow mosaic and bruchid resistance; neither is TJU 130 -- https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.11.09.374041.full.pdf
- Vikaspedia lists yellow mosaic, powdery mildew, stem fly and Cercospora resistant varieties, but TJU 130 does not appear among them -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/blackgram-and-greengram?lgn=en

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No TJU 130 yield, maturity, or multi-location trial data was found. The national yield figure (585 kg/ha) and state-wise yield ranges are general crop statistics, not variety data -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf (not verified for this variety; see also https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf for an unrelated 2024-25 blackgram entry with 130-135 day maturity, which is not identified as TJU 130)
- No TJU 130 field-trial result was found. Multi-location blackgram testing under AICPIP is described generally -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/

GENETICS AND QTL
- No TJU 130 genetic or marker study was found. The parentage given in the brief (KU 96-3 x RIL 68) was not confirmed by any search result.
- General blackgram genetics and breeding review, with BARC authorship and mutation-breeding context; does not mention TJU 130 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/
- GWAS for yield traits in a 100-genotype panel (PAU, 2022); no TJU 130 entry -- https://doi.org/10.3389/fgene.2022.849016

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The breeding programme that produced Trombay urdbean mutant lines sits in BARC's Nuclear Agriculture and Biotechnology Division (NABT). A BARC e-book lists urdbean mutants registered with NBPGR, but does not name TJU 130 -- https://www.barc.gov.in/ebooks/9788196745349/complete.pdf
- A BARC/World Vegetable Center review names Souframanien Jegadeesan (BARC, Mumbai) as an author on blackgram breeding. No source links him to TJU 130 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/
- JNKVV (Jabalpur) is the second listed institution. Its Directorate of Farms runs Breeder Seed Production under the National Seed Production Programme. The page does not mention TJU 130 -- https://www.jnkvv.org/about-directorate-details/directorate-of-farms
- Breeder/lead scientist names for TJU 130: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- JNKVV Directorate of Farms (institute-level contact, listed on the official JNKVV page): Mobile 8770867088; Email seeds.jnkvv@gmail.com -- https://www.jnkvv.org/about-directorate-details/directorate-of-farms
- BARC NABT Division: no contact details found in the results. Postal address: not found.
- Individual breeder contact (email, phone): No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No TJU 130-specific publication was found in any search.
- Jegadeesan, S.; Somta, P. et al. (2023). Genetics, genomics, and breeding of black gram [Vigna mungo (L.) Hepper]. Frontiers in Plant Science -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full (general review, not TJU 130-specific; the PMC copy is at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/)
- Singh, L.; Dhillon, G. S.; Kaur, S. et al. (2022). Genome-wide Association Study for Yield and Yield-Related Traits in Diverse Blackgram Panel (Vigna mungo L. Hepper). Frontiers in Genetics -- https://doi.org/10.3389/fgene.2022.849016 (no TJU 130 entry)
- Mishra, P. (2020). Effect of integrated nutrient management on growth, development and yield of blackgram. JNKVV thesis, KVK Rewa; variety not identified -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/f6e32525-0a7b-48d3-8691-28af74225652/content
- Patidar, R. (2005). Heterosis and Combining Ability Analysis for Seed Yield and Its Component Traits in Blackgram. M.Sc. thesis, JNKVV, Jabalpur. Found only as a citation inside a ResearchGate document, not in KrishiKosh; no URL -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327386671_Realization_of_facts_and_profiteering_of_black_gram_through_different_breeding_methods

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The search returned only non-Indian bean seed vendors and irrelevant pages. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, JNKVV seed sale, or Seednet listing for TJU 130 was found. This search was run once, so availability is unverified.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The brief lists Madhya Pradesh. No source confirmed this for TJU 130. Krishak Jagat's TJU 130 link appears only as a related post on pages for other urdbean varieties -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/urdbean-variety-black-gram-adt-7-ad-tr-bg-14003/
- Madhya Pradesh is named as a major blackgram-growing state, a general statistic that does not establish recommendation for TJU 130 -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/blackgram-and-greengram?lgn=en

Searches run: 4 (variety and release; breeder and institution; research and publications; seed availability). Unresolved: TJU 130 release notification, parentage, maturity, yield, stress tolerance, breeder names and direct contacts, and seed sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: TRCRU-22 (blackgram / urd bean)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "TRCRU-22", so every finding below refers to the same name. Search coverage was limited: only 4 searches ran, and the returned snippets were short. Several headings have no usable evidence, and I could not open the full pages.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found under this heading (no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data retrieved).

DISEASE AND PEST -- In a screening of blackgram genotypes against Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV), TRCRU-22 recorded the lowest PDI and the minimum per cent disease, while the susceptible check TAU-1 had the highest PDI; the snippet did not state the final resistance class -- http://www.plantarchives.org/article/9-%20Screening%20of%20Blackgram%20genotypes%20against%20Mungbean%20Yellow%20Mosaic%20Virus%20(MYMV)%20disease.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for yield, maturity, or agronomic performance of TRCRU-22 specifically. A dual-season stability study in blackgram (Legume Research) came up in the search, but the retrieved snippet did not confirm that TRCRU-22 was among its genotypes -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4523 (unverified relevance)

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found (no parentage, marker, or QTL data retrieved; the input lists parentage as "Not specified").

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for the lead breeder or scientist names. The input record names the University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur (Karnataka) and the Nuclear Agriculture and Biotechnology Division, BARC, as the institutions. No search result confirmed this.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, address, or contact-page URL was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS --
Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Screening of Blackgram genotypes against Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV) disease. Plant Archives (journal name inferred from the site domain) -- http://www.plantarchives.org/article/9-%20Screening%20of%20Blackgram%20genotypes%20against%20Mungbean%20Yellow%20Mosaic%20Virus%20(MYMV)%20disease.pdf
No other TRCRU-22-specific publication was confirmed.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-availability search returned only generic black gram storage and market pages, with no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listings. Seednet was not reached.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The input record lists Karnataka and Maharashtra. No search result confirmed this. The CSC release notification and its date were not retrieved; the input gives a release date of 2022-10-26.

PROCESS NOTE: The search budget was 4 queries. A fifth call, made in an attempt to re-read the snippets in full, was refused by the tool's usage limit. The digest is therefore built from the truncated snippets of the first four searches. Before relying on this record, check seednet.gov.in, the ICAR CSC notification, the UAS Raichur and BARC pages, and KrishiKosh directly.

drought.details: No drought trial data for TU 40 was found in the searched sources. No mechanism or evidence is reported.

heat.details: No heat trial data for TU 40 was found in the searched sources. No mechanism or evidence is reported.

salinity.details: No salinity trial data for TU 40 was found in the searched sources. No mechanism or evidence is reported.

flood.details: A farmer in an agronet article reports the crop stood in water for over two weeks and still yielded well. The article does not state which BARC variety this refers to, so this waterlogging tolerance is unconfirmed and is not attributed to TU 40 here.

disease_resistance.summary: Powdery mildew: TU 40 is listed as a powdery mildew resistance source (disease score 1), with the identifying reference given as Singh et al., 2016a. The Central released variety table also records TU 40 as resistant to powdery mildew. Yellow mosaic virus (YMV): the Deccan Chronicle and agronet pages report TU 40 as resistant to yellow mosaic virus; the digest attributes YMV resistance to TU 40 in these two pages only. No field-level scoring data were found for either disease.

pest_resistance.summary: Bruchids: a ResearchGate abstract names TU 40 among new black gram genotypes with resistance to bruchids (listed with TU 26 and TU 72). This is an abstract-level listing; no scoring data or method details were found. No other pest resistance for TU 40 was found. Seed-treatment and pest-management pages were discarded because they do not name TU 40.

agronomic_details.yield: Central released variety table: 9-10 q/ha (approximately 900-1000 kg/ha). The CSC record gives the average yield unit as Kg/Ha without a value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location trial results specific to TU 40 were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rabi season; listed in the SZ zone in the Central released variety table (Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Odisha). Pilot-scale cultivation reported in Villupuram, Tamil Nadu.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Pilot-scale cultivation in Villupuram, Tamil Nadu, reported by the Deccan Chronicle; no yield or performance data given. (2) A Legume Research heterosis study used TU-40 as a parent and reports desirable seed yield and pod number heterosis for some TU-40 crosses; this is a cross-performance result, not a variety trial. (3) No multi-location trial results specific to TU 40 were found. The farmer waterlogging account is not attributed to TU 40 (see flood).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: A unigene-SSR diversity study places TU-40 in a cluster with TU-72, both from the same cross (TU94-2 x V. mungo var. silvestris). No marker positions were reported for TU 40.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No QTL or marker-trait association for TU 40 was found.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not found in searched sources. Seednet portal listing, NSC and State Seed Corporation listings were not returned by the search engine (seednet.gov.in not reached). The Tamil Nadu state agriculture department procured BARC seed and distributed it to some farmers.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- TU 40 (black gram, BARC Trombay) is reported as resistant to yellow mosaic virus and powdery mildew, and was being grown on a pilot scale in Villupuram, Tamil Nadu -- https://www.deccanchronicle.com/current-affairs/180116/barc-seeds-save-tamil-nadu-pulse-farmers.html
- A farmer quoted in an agronet article says the crop stood in water for over two weeks and still yielded well. The article does not clearly say which BARC variety this refers to, so treat the waterlogging tolerance as unconfirmed for TU 40 -- https://indiaagronet.com/indiaagronet/crop%20info/black_gram.htm
- No drought, heat, salinity or submergence trial data for TU 40 was found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- TU 40 is listed as a powdery mildew resistance source (disease score 1), with the identifying reference given as Singh et al., 2016a -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/ (also https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full)
- A ResearchGate abstract names TU 40 among new black gram genotypes with resistance to bruchids (TU 26, TU 40, TU 72) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327386671_Realization_of_facts_and_profiteering_of_black_gram_through_different_breeding_methods
- YMV resistance is attributed to TU 40 in the Deccan Chronicle and agronet pages above.
- Seed-treatment and pest-management pages were found, but they do not name TU 40 and were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The Central released variety table lists TU 40: released 2013, Trombay Mumbai, yield 9-10 q/ha, 70-75 days, Rabi season, resistant to powdery mildew -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- A Legume Research heterosis study used TU-40 as a parent in crosses and reports desirable seed yield and pod number heterosis for some TU-40 crosses -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4764
- No multi-location trial results specific to TU 40 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: TU-40 was derived from TU 94-2 × wild black gram (V. mungo var. silvestris) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/ (and https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full)
- Unigene-SSR study: TU-40 pedigree recorded as TU94-2 × V. mungo var. silvestris, and TU-40 clusters with TU-72 from the same cross -- https://www.plantbreedbio.org/journal/view.php?doi=10.9787%2FPBB.2017.5.2.88
- Breeding method: mutation and recombination breeding at BARC; the breeding-line code TU-40 is listed in a BARC timeframe document (page reference only) -- https://www.barc.gov.in/group/66_s246.pdf
- Genome resources: black gram is a diploid (2n = 22) self-pollinating crop with a genome of about 574 Mbp (general crop data, not TU 40-specific) -- https://www.plantbreedbio.org/journal/view.php?doi=10.9787%2FPBB.2017.5.2.88
- No QTL or marker-trait association for TU 40 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), Trombay, Mumbai, through its Nuclear Agriculture and Biotechnology Division (NA&BTD) -- https://www.barc.gov.in/group/66_s246.pdf (also https://www.deccanchronicle.com/current-affairs/180116/barc-seeds-save-tamil-nadu-pulse-farmers.html)
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The press and institutional pages name no breeder for TU 40.
- Named BARC scientist (not stated as TU 40 breeder): J. Daniel Chellappa, senior scientist, BARC Technical Coordination Wing, quoted on TU-94-2 and TU-40 seed supply -- https://www.deccanchronicle.com/current-affairs/180116/barc-seeds-save-tamil-nadu-pulse-farmers.html
- Frontiers affiliation list includes BARC, Mumbai, India, as a co-author institution for the black gram review, but this is not TU 40 specific -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full

CONTACT DETAILS
- Official email: No evidence found.
- Phone: No evidence found.
- Postal address: No evidence found. Only the city (Trombay, Mumbai) is given in the sources above.
- Institute-level URL found: https://www.barc.gov.in/ (domain appears in the BARC timeframe PDF at https://www.barc.gov.in/group/66_s246.pdf; no contact page was retrieved).
- Named contact in press: J. Daniel Chellappa, senior scientist, BARC Technical Coordination Wing (no email or phone given) -- https://www.deccanchronicle.com/current-affairs/180116/barc-seeds-save-tamil-nadu-pulse-farmers.html

PUBLICATIONS
- Nair RM, Chaudhari S, Devi N, Shivanna A, Gowda A, Boddepalli VN, Pradhan H, Schafleitner R, Jegadeesan S, Somta P (2024). Genetics, genomics, and breeding of black gram [Vigna mungo (L.) Hepper]. Frontiers in Plant Science -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full (DOI 10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363). TU 40 appears in its powdery mildew resistance table and parentage text.
- Singh et al. (2016a). Cited in the Frontiers review as the source of TU 40 powdery mildew resistance and parentage. Full record not retrieved -- No evidence found for URL or DOI.
- Authors not stated in snippet (year not stated). Heterosis for yield and yield components in black gram [Vigna mungo (L.) Hepper]. Legume Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4764
- Authors not stated in snippet (2017). Cross Species Amplification of Cowpea Derived Unigene-SSR Markers and Diversity Analysis in Black Gram [Vigna mungo (L.) Hepper]. Plant Breeding and Biotechnology -- https://www.plantbreedbio.org/journal/view.php?doi=10.9787%2FPBB.2017.5.2.88 (DOI 10.9787/PBB.2017.5.2.88)
- Central released variety table (DPD, Government of India), TU 40 row. Document, no author -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- KrishiKosh theses and AICRP/ICAR annual reports on TU 40: No evidence found (not returned by the search engine; krishikosh.egranth.ac.in was not reached).

SEED AVAILABILITY
- BARC supplied sample seed of TU-94-2 and TU-40 to the Tamil Nadu agriculture department on request, and planned bulk supply for multiplication in 2015-16 -- https://www.deccanchronicle.com/current-affairs/180116/barc-seeds-save-tamil-nadu-pulse-farmers.html
- The state agriculture department procured BARC seed and distributed it to some farmers, and farmers asked for more -- https://indiaagronet.com/indiaagronet/crop%20info/black_gram.htm
- Seednet portal listing, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listing for TU 40: No evidence found (seednet.gov.in not returned by the search engine).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The Central released variety table gives TU 40's suitable zone as SZ (Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Odisha), for Rabi season -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- The Deccan Chronicle reports pilot cultivation in Villupuram, Tamil Nadu -- https://www.deccanchronicle.com/current-affairs/180116/barc-seeds-save-tamil-nadu-pulse-farmers.html
- The input field "recommended_states_raw" was "Not specified", so the Zone/State list above is from the central release table, not from a gazette notification. No CSC release-minute or Seednet notification text was found.

NAME CHECK
- variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "TU 40", so all evidence above refers to the same name. No separate Seednet page was retrieved to confirm the portal entry.
- Discarded as other varieties or crops: Pant Urd-40, Pant Urd 31, TU-94-2 (MYMV source, separate variety), TAU-1, Trombay Urd entries for other years, Lupin bean and other non-black-gram pages.
