disease_resistance.research_summary: Powdery mildew: TU 40 is listed as a powdery mildew resistance source (disease score 1), with the identifying reference given as Singh et al., 2016a. The Central released variety table also records TU 40 as resistant to powdery mildew. Yellow mosaic virus (YMV): the Deccan Chronicle and agronet pages report TU 40 as resistant to yellow mosaic virus; the digest attributes YMV resistance to TU 40 in these two pages only. No field-level scoring data were found for either disease.

pest_resistance.research_summary: Bruchids: a ResearchGate abstract names TU 40 among new black gram genotypes with resistance to bruchids (listed with TU 26 and TU 72). This is an abstract-level listing; no scoring data or method details were found. No other pest resistance for TU 40 was found. Seed-treatment and pest-management pages were discarded because they do not name TU 40.

drought.details: Rainfed yield of 871 kg/ha is reported, with 23.2% and 25.9% gains over check varieties. No explicit drought-tolerance trial was found in peer-reviewed or institutional sources, so yield performance alone does not establish drought tolerance mechanisms.

heat.details: Only a non-authoritative blog claims heat and drought tolerance. This is not corroborated by ICAR or TNAU sources and is therefore not treated as evidence.

salinity.details: No evidence found.

flood.details: No evidence found.

disease_resistance.summary: Mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV): highly resistant, per the developers' release paper, together with synchronized maturity and determinate habit. Leaf crinkle: resistant, per the release paper. Powdery mildew: moderately resistant, per the release paper. Other diseases (YMV, leaf curl virus, stem necrosis, and a PM entry) appear in the national listing, but that row is garbled in extraction and is UNVERIFIED. Note that the evidence refers to blackgram, not chickpea.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found beyond the disease notes. The release paper states the culture was screened against major insect pests, but results were not retrieved, so no specific pest resistance can be confirmed.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 900 kg/ha, which is 11.9% above check VBN 6 and 13.5% above check CO 6. Irrigated yield 988 kg/ha. Rainfed yield 871 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: No stability analysis across environments found in the evidence.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Listed for the Southern Zone (Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Odisha). TNAU describes suitability for all seasons in Tamil Nadu.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Determinate habit, non-shattering pods, synchronized maturity.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Multilocation trials, adaptive research trials and on-farm trials were included in the evaluation.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CROP MISMATCH: VBN 8 is a blackgram (urdbean, Vigna mungo) variety from TNAU, not a chickpea variety. The chickpea-specific fields in the request (variety code, 2018 release, states) appear to be carried over from a blackgram record, so none of the findings below are chickpea data. -- https://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
RELEASE YEAR CONFLICT: The TNAU Vamban variety list gives 2016, while the national pulses listing gives 2018. Parentage is also recorded differently across sources (VBN 3 x VBG 04-008 in the journal paper; Vamban 3 x VBN 04-008 on the TNAU page). -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/ ; https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1360
DISEASE RESISTANCE (MYMV): Highly resistant to mungbean yellow mosaic virus, with synchronized maturity and determinate habit, per the developers' release paper. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1360
DISEASE RESISTANCE (leaf crinkle and powdery mildew): Resistant to leaf crinkle; moderately resistant to powdery mildew, per the same release paper. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1360
DISEASE RESISTANCE (other): The national listing row for VBN 8 is garbled in extraction but appears to mention YMV, leaf curl virus, and stem necrosis resistance, and a PM entry. Treat as unverified. -- https://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
DROUGHT: Rainfed yield of 871 kg/ha, versus 23.2% and 25.9% gains over check varieties; no explicit drought-tolerance trial found in peer-reviewed or institutional sources. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1360
HEAT: Only a non-authoritative blog claims heat and drought tolerance; not corroborated by ICAR/TNAU sources. -- https://agri.bot/docs/duration-for-vbn-8-black-gram-variety/
SALINITY: No evidence found.
FLOOD / SUBMERGENCE: No evidence found.
PEST RESISTANCE: No evidence found beyond the disease notes above. The release paper says the culture was screened against major insect pests, but results were not retrieved. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1360
QTL / MARKERS: No evidence found.
YIELD AND TRIALS: Average yield of 900 kg/ha, 11.9% and 13.5% above checks VBN 6 and CO 6; irrigated yield of 988 kg/ha; trials included multilocation, adaptive research and on-farm trials. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1360 ; https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/
BREEDER / INSTITUTION: Developed at National Pulses Research Centre, Vamban, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU); released from the NPRC Vamban programme. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/
SEED AVAILABILITY (NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs): No evidence found.
RECOMMENDED STATES: Listed for the Southern Zone (Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Odisha), matching the request; TNAU separately describes suitability for all seasons in Tamil Nadu. -- https://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf ; https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/49th-Research-Highlights-2015-2017.pdf
MATURITY: 65–70 days, determinate with non-shattering pods. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance of VBN 5 (greengram). The TNAU greengram profile covers disease response only.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance of VBN 5 (greengram).

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance of VBN 5 (greengram).

disease_resistance.summary: Mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV): listed as resistant in the TNAU profile for VBN 5. Urdbean leaf crinkle virus (ULCV): listed as resistant in the TNAU profile for VBN 5. Field evidence: in a farmer-field trial at Tiruppur (kharif 2020), VBN 5 showed the lowest MYMV incidence among the entries tested (4.1%), compared with 5.1% for LGG 630 and 5.3% for DGG 1. The trial measured incidence only; it did not establish resistance mechanisms or levels.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The input record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified', and no pest-resistance evidence for VBN 5 appeared in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield of 878 kg/ha as listed by TNAU. In the Tiruppur farmer-field trial (kharif 2020), grain yield was 8.15 q/ha (815 kg/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Evidence comes from a single farmer-field trial location and season; no multi-environment stability data were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Per the input record, suitable for all seasons in both irrigated and rainfed conditions throughout Tamil Nadu except the Nilgiris and Kanyakumari districts. The digest does not independently confirm this adaptation statement.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: EARLY (input record). TNAU lists duration as 70-75 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: PUBESCENT BLACK PODS; PODS COME OUT ABOVE THE CANOPY DURING PODDING STAGE UNDER NORMAL CONDITION; LANCEOLATE LEAVES IN NORMAL CONDITION AND OVATE LEAVES IN DRY CONDITION. TNAU also describes VBN 5 as high-yielding with multiple blooming and non-shattering pods, and 22.85% protein.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Tiruppur farmer-field trial (KVK, TNAU Tiruppur; 7 farms, 5 replications; kharif 2020): VBN 5 recorded 31.8 pods per plant and grain yield of 8.15 q/ha, the highest of the three improved entries. Comparators were LGG 630 at 7.90 q/ha and DGG 1 at 7.20 q/ha. VBN 5 also had the lowest MYMV incidence (4.1%) in this trial. No other trial results for VBN 5 were found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. Parentage conflict: the input record gives VAMBAN 1 X VIGNA MUNGO VAR SILVESTRIS 1. The TNAU greengram page gives VBN(Gg) 2 x ML 1451 for VBN 5. The record's parentage resembles the blackgram entries on the TNAU blackgram page. The parentage must be verified before use.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of VBN 5 (greengram) or VBN 6 (blackgram). The TNAU greengram profile covers disease response only. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Pulses/Vbn%205.html
STRESS TOLERANCE (VBN 5, greengram) -- A TNAU profile lists it as resistant to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV) and urdbean leaf crinkle virus (ULCV) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Pulses/Vbn%205.html

DISEASE AND PEST -- VBN 5 (greengram): TNAU lists resistance to MYMV and ULCV -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Pulses/Vbn%205.html
DISEASE AND PEST -- VBN 5 (greengram), farmer-field trial at Tiruppur, kharif 2020: lowest MYMV incidence among the entries tested (4.1%), against 5.1% for LGG 630 and 5.3% for DGG 1 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375544594_Assessing_the_Performance_of_Latest_Greengram_Varieties_under_Improved_production_Packages_in_Thiruppur_Tamil_Nadu_India
DISEASE AND PEST -- Seed-treatment advice for VBN (Bg) 5 and VBN 6 (blackgram) on the TNAU page: imidacloprid seed treatment against yellow mosaic virus is recommended for several blackgram varieties; the table does not state whether VBN 6 itself is resistant -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/pulses_blackgram.html

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- VBN 5 (greengram): year of release 2022, duration 70–75 days, average yield 878 kg/ha, high-yielding with multiple blooming and non-shattering pods, 22.85% protein -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Pulses/Vbn%205.html
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- VBN 5 (greengram), Tiruppur farmer-field trial (7 farms, 5 replications, kharif 2020): 31.8 pods per plant and grain yield 8.15 q/ha, the highest of three improved entries; LGG 630 gave 7.90 q/ha and DGG 1 gave 7.20 q/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375544594_Assessing_the_Performance_of_Latest_Greengram_Varieties_under_Improved_production_Packages_in_Thiruppur_Tamil_Nadu_India
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- VBN 6 (blackgram, seednet name): TNAU lists parentage, 65–70 day duration and grain yield of 836–882 kg/ha across the VBN 6/7 entries; the table is not clearly separated per variety, so treat these figures as unconfirmed for VBN 6 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/pulses_blackgram.html
PARENTAGE CONFLICT -- The TNAU greengram page gives VBN 5 parentage as VBN(Gg) 2 × ML 1451, not the VAMBAN 1 × Vigna mungo var. silvestris 1 given in the record. The record's parentage resembles the blackgram entries on the TNAU blackgram page. Verify before use -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Pulses/Vbn%205.html

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Searches returned no QTL, marker or molecular-parentage study for VBN 5 or VBN 6.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No breeder or scientist names found for VBN 5 or VBN 6 in the retrieved results. The TNAU page for VBN 5 names the release year and parentage but no breeder. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Pulses/Vbn%205.html
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution per the input record: National Pulses Research Centre, Pudukkottai, under Tamil Nadu Agricultural University. The retrieved pages do not confirm the station; the TNAU blackgram page lists Pudukkottai only as a district in its sowing table. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/pulses_blackgram.html

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address, or institute contact-page URL for National Pulses Research Centre, Pudukkottai, or for the breeding team, appeared in any result. Contact the TNAU Department of Pulses or the NPRC Pudukkottai directly.

PUBLICATIONS -- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not confirmed). Assessing the Performance of Latest Greengram Varieties under Improved Production Packages in Thiruppur, Tamil Nadu, India. Farmer-field trial by KVK, TNAU Tiruppur, kharif 2020; journal not identified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375544594_Assessing_the_Performance_of_Latest_Greengram_Varieties_under_Improved_production_Packages_in_Thiruppur_Tamil_Nadu_India
PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, or KrishiKosh thesis specific to VBN 5 or VBN 6 was found in the searches. The search for research papers returned only the Tiruppur trial above.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- VBN 6 (blackgram, seednet name): listed in TNAU sowing-season recommendations for multiple districts, but no seed supplier, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing was found -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/pulses_blackgram.html
SEED AVAILABILITY -- VBN 5 (greengram): No evidence found for any seed source.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Tamil Nadu (from input record). The TNAU greengram page and the Tiruppur trial confirm Tamil Nadu. The TNAU blackgram page lists VBN 6 for multiple Tamil Nadu districts across seasons. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Pulses/Vbn%205.html ; https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/pulses_blackgram.html

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY: VBN 6 (Black gram / urd). Seednet name is also "VBN 6", so the evidence below refers to the same name under both headings. Where a source is ambiguous, I say so.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV); the source is a paper titled as a high-yielding VBN 6 variety resistant to MYMV, and the snippet is truncated at "highly resistant to" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338281041_Development_of_Yellow_Mosaic_Virus_Resistant_Genotypes_in_Urdbean_TNAU_blackgram_VBN_6_A_high_yielding_blackgram_variety_with_resistant_to_Mungbean_Yellow_Mosaic_Virus
STRESS TOLERANCE -- A slide deck lists VBN 6 as YMV-resistant with a 2011 release year -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshare/black-gram-ppt-black-gram-also-known-as-urad-or-urd-bean-is-an-important-pulse-crop-grown-in-india/271676749 (the table row for VBN 6 is in the snippet; the URL shown is the slideshare page returned by search)
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned no VBN 6-specific tolerance data for these stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST -- MYMV resistance (see above). Leaf crinkle or powdery mildew resistance for VBN 6: No evidence found for this variety. The slide deck mentions YMV resistance only.
DISEASE AND PEST -- Pest tolerance (aphid, stemfly, pod borer) for VBN 6: No evidence found. The aphid, stemfly and pod borer tolerance text in the search results belongs to COBG 653, not VBN 6 -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-1-3-34-36.pdf (discarded for this variety).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Released by the National Pulses Research Centre (NPRC), Vamban; maturity 65-70 days in the TNAU variety table -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/ and https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/pulses_blackgram.html
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Yield: the TNAU variety table gives 850 kg/ha for VBN 6 (rainfed and irrigated columns are not clearly separated in the snippet), and the slide deck gives 850 and 890 kg/ha. The column alignment is unclear, so treat these figures as unverified -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/pulses_blackgram.html ; https://www.slideshare.net/slideshare/black-gram-ppt-black-gram-also-known-as-urad-or-urd-bean-is-an-important-pulse-crop-grown-in-india/271676749
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The TNAU paper describes VBN 6 as shorter in duration with synchronized maturity, and as high-yielding over the checks Vamban 4 and VBN (Bg) 5 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338281041_Development_of_Yellow_Mosaic_Virus_Resistant_Genotypes_in_Urdbean_TNAU_blackgram_VBN_6_A_high_yielding_blackgram_variety_with_resistant_to_Mungbean_Yellow_Mosaic_Virus
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Grain described as medium-sized and black: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338281041_Development_of_Yellow_Mosaic_Virus_Resistant_Genotypes_in_Urdbean_TNAU_blackgram_VBN_6_A_high_yielding_blackgram_variety_with_resistant_to_Mungbean_Yellow_Mosaic_Virus
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Discrepancy: one TNAU-linked table places a 2007 release year and a different parentage on a column that may be VBN 6, while the same table gives 2011 for the column with the Vigna mungo silvestris parentage. The mapping of columns to varieties is unclear, so the release year and yield figures above are not confirmed -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/pulses_blackgram.html

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage: Vamban 1 x Vigna mungo var. silvestris 1 (TNAU sources list it as Vamban 1 x Vigno mungo var. silvestris) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338281041_Development_of_Yellow_Mosaic_Virus_Resistant_Genotypes_in_Urdbean_TNAU_blackgram_VBN_6_A_high_yielding_blackgram_variety_with_resistant_to_Mungbean_Yellow_Mosaic_Virus

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Vallabh Urd-1 (Black gram, Vigna mungo)

Name note: The CSC-style name appears in the sources as "Vallabh Urd 1" or "Vallabh Urd-1". The Seednet form "Vallabh Urd - 1" did not appear in any result, so no evidence here is from Seednet. All findings below refer to this variety under the Vallabh Urd 1 / Urd-1 spelling. Excluded as other varieties or products: Indira Urd-1, Pratap Urd-1, Pant Urd-31, Vallabh Basmati and Vallabh Taramira. The OSTI EMS/gamma-ray double-mutant paper names no variety, so it is excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as tolerant to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV) in the central/state release table, with a 2015 release year -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Identified as broad-based resistant in AICRP trials -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276420920_Production_of_enriched_compost
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found. No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Reported resistance to yellow mosaic virus, Cercospora leaf spot, Macrophomina blight, anthracnose and bacterial leaf spot, with moderate resistance to insects -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276420920_Production_of_enriched_compost
- Reported tolerance to MYMV -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Average yield of about 1,069.2 kg/ha, about 16.29% above the check Uttara, in AICRP trials -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276420920_Production_of_enriched_compost
- Maturity of 70-75 days and yield of 10-11 q/ha in the release table -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- In a plant-spacing trial, a different black gram variety outyielded Vallabh Urd-1 (used as a comparator, not the top entry) -- https://saulibrary.edu.bd/daatj/public/uploads/Done%2019-10396.pdf
- Named as a black gram variety in KVK technology demonstrations under NFSM pulses in rabi 2015-16 -- https://www.isss-india.org/img/Bulletin31.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: derived by gamma-irradiation mutation breeding from Pant Urd 19, a popular variety in western Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276420920_Production_of_enriched_compost
- Breeding-line code: none found. QTL/marker studies specific to this variety: none found. Genome resources specific to this variety: none found. No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel University of Agriculture and Technology (SVPUAT), Meerut, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding -- https://www.svpuat.edu.in/dept-ag-genetics-plant-breeding.php?eid=45c48cce2e2d7fbdea1afc51c7c6ad26
- Central release listed under the department's page with notification 268(E) dated 28.01.2015 -- https://www.svpuat.edu.in/dept-ag-genetics-plant-breeding.php?eid=45c48cce2e2d7fbdea1afc51c7c6ad26
- Listed among the university's black gram varieties (Vallabh Urd-1) -- http://iauaindia.org/UniversityDetails.aspx?id=47
- Lead breeder name: not found in any result. No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder name, email, phone or postal address for this variety was found in the results. No evidence found.
- Institution-level reference only: SVPUAT, Meerut (website domain svpuat.edu.in, from the department page URL above). No email, phone or address was shown in the snippets.

PUBLICATIONS
- SVPUAT (2018-19). Annual Report 2018-19. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel University of Agriculture and Technology, Meerut -- https://www.svpuat.edu.in/annualreport/Annual%20Report%202018-19.pdf (names Vallabh Urd 1 under nucleus seed maintained)
- Authors not shown (n.d.). Production of enriched compost (extension material, SVPUAT, Vallabh Urd 1 section). Journal/report not shown; the ResearchGate title does not match the content -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276420920_Production_of_enriched_compost
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Response of blackgram varieties as affected by different plant spacing. Journal not identified in the snippet -- https://saulibrary.edu.bd/daatj/public/uploads/Done%2019-10396.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP annual report specific to this variety was found. No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY

EVIDENCE DIGEST: TJU 339 (Trombay Jawahar Urd 339), blackgram

Name note: The CSC-style name "TJU 339 (Trombay Jawahar Urd 339)" appears in the ICAR, BARC and Global Agriculture sources below. The Seednet-style name "(Trombay Jawahar Urd 339) TJU 339" did not appear in any result, and no Seednet page was reached, so no evidence in this digest is confirmed under that name. Four queries were run in one batch (within the 3–4 limit). Several headings have thin or no evidence; those are marked.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as a resistant or tolerant line for MYMV, leaf curl virus, Cercospora leaf spot, anthracnose and powdery mildew; no abiotic stress (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) data found -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CROSS-CHECK FLAG: The record lists crop as blackgram, but the Seednet crop name is BOTTLE GOURD, and every GH-22 source found describes a bottle gourd variety. No page tied GH-22 to blackgram. Under the strict relevance rule, the blackgram findings below are "No evidence found." The bottle gourd sources are listed separately at the end for record correction. Both names ("GH-22 (Ghiya Hisar 22)") were searched, and the evidence refers to the same name on both.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches for GH-22 blackgram returned no stress-tolerance data. The only GH-22 variety page found is for bottle gourd (see crop-mismatch section).

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No blackgram GH-22 disease or pest data was returned. Generic blackgram pages (not GH-22) were excluded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for blackgram. The bottle gourd trial data are excluded (see crop-mismatch section).

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The only GH-22 genetics-related result was a generic blackgram GWAS (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9310006/), which does not name GH-22 and was excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a named GH-22 breeder. Institution-level link: a Haryana Kisan Ayog report lists "GH-22" among vegetable varieties released by CCS HAU, Hisar, Haryana, without naming the crop -- https://hkkp.org.in/Reports/Report_on_Horticulture.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No GH-22 breeder contact found. Institute-level contact (acceptable fallback): CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar - 125 004, INDIA; phone 1-800-1803001 -- https://translate.google.com/translate?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.hau.ac.in%2F&hl=hi&sl=en&tl=hi&client=srp (Google Translate proxy of hau.ac.in; the direct institute page was not returned by search). No email or station address was found for GH-22.

PUBLICATIONS -- No blackgram GH-22 publications found. Search returned no GH-22 paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or QTL study. The only GH-22 publication found is for bottle gourd (see crop-mismatch section).

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Seed sellers returned were for generic bottle gourd or unrelated products, not GH-22. No NSC, Haryana Seeds Development Corporation, KVK, or CCS HAU seed listing naming GH-22 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found for blackgram. The record's "Haryana" and release date of 2015-04-07 could not be verified from search results.

CROP-MISMATCH SOURCES (excluded from the blackgram record; retained for correction)
- GH-22: A new bottle gourd variety (short communication, Indian Journal of Vegetable Science-type source; authors, year, and journal name not shown in search result). Reports: 280 q/ha average fruit yield, 125-130 day duration, 750-800 g fruit, and multi-location CVT results (256.1 q/ha over 20 trials, 2010-11 to 2012-13). Breeding institution not stated on the page. -- https://isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/229/212
- Haryana Kisan Ayog horticulture report (see BREEDER AND INSTITUTION above), which lists GH-22 as a CCS HAU vegetable release. -- https://hkkp.org.in/Reports/Report_on_Horticulture.pdf

RECOMMENDATION: Verify the crop field against the CSC release minutes and the Seednet entry. The evidence points to GH-22 being a bottle gourd variety from CCS HAU, Hisar, so the blackgram crop field appears to be an error. The release date and recommended states also need checking against the official notification.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Sourav (CO-58), Jute (Corchorus olitorius)

Name note: The release-minutes name is "Sourav" and the Seednet name is "Sourav (CO-58)". The AICRP list shows it as "CO 58 (Sourav)". No Seednet portal page came back in the searches, so every item below refers to the name "Sourav" or "CO 58/CO-58" in jute sources. Several search hits named a different Sourav (a wheat line, a rice line "CO58", a person, a jute-fabric paper). I discarded those.

STRESS TOLERANCE / DISEASE AND PEST
- AICRP release table lists CO 58 (Sourav), 2010, W.B., notification S.O. 211(E) of 29.01.2010, fibre yield 34 (q/ha, as listed), with resistance to premature flowering, non-shattering pods, better fibre quality and resistance to major pests and diseases. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
- Details-of-varieties table gives the same entry and states the variety is resistant to premature flowering and has better fibre quality. The table does not list specific pathogens for CO 58. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- Improved-technology slide deck repeats the AICRP entry (yield 34 q/ha; resistance to major pests and diseases; non-shattering pods; mid-March sowing). -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546
- No evidence found for named drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to CO 58. The only tolerance wording is generic ("tolerance of abiotic stresses") on the AICRP achievements page for the group. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
- Discarded: wheat "Sourav" drought and heat tolerance papers (different crop) at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341103907_Screening_for_drought_tolerance_in_wheat_genotypes_by_morphological_and_SSR_markers

DISEASE AND PEST
- The AICRP entry names resistance to premature flowering and to "major pest and diseases" without naming specific pests or pathogens. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- No evidence found for named disease or pest resistance (for example stem rot, root rot, anthracnose or yellow mite) specific to CO 58. Those named resistances appear for other AICRP varieties in the same table (e.g., JBO 2003H "Ira"). -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Recommended sowing is mid-March (AICRP entry). -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
- Coastal South Bengal pre-kharif 2023 trial, seven olitorius varieties incl. CO 58: fibre yield of CO 58 was not the top entry (JBO 1 was highest at 28.2 q/ha, and CO 58 was "closely followed"). Table row for CO 58 lists values including 48.3, 374.8, 52.73, 6.75 and 2591.70 without column labels in the extract, so I did not report them as yields. -- https://indianecologicalsociety.com/wp-content/themes/ecology/volume_pdfs/1755055411.pdf
- Coastal South Bengal varietal study (ResearchGate abstract): CO 58 ranked second for stick and biological yield, behind JBO 1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390811461_Varietal_Performance_of_Jute_Corchorus_capsularis_L_Based_on_Crop_Growth_and_Yield_in_the_Coastal_Region_of_South_Bengal
- Note: the ResearchGate paper title says C. capsularis, while the trial text refers to olitorius jute; treat the crop species as unresolved for that study.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage TJ-40 x Tanganyika-1 (from the task record): no evidence found in any search result.
- Breeding-line code: CO 58 is the code given in the AICRP list and the Seednet name. No other line code found. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
- Breeding method, QTL, markers, genome resources: no evidence found for CO 58.
- Discarded: Frontiers hybridization/combining-ability paper on tossa jute (no CO 58 link shown in the retrieved text): https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2025.1499256/full
- Discarded: rice "CO58" (CBMAS14142, QTL qDTY) at https://www.cornous.com/article/journal-of-innovative-agriculture/rice-co58-a-mid-early-duration-aromatic-rice-variety

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety is attributed to CRIJAF (ICAR Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibres, Barrackpore), which developed jute varieties under the AICRP. -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/promising-technologies-of-crijaf-14411.html
- A CRIJAF proceedings paper states the olitorius variety Sourav (CO-58) was being tested for DUS (distinctness, uniformity, stability) to obtain protection. -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/promising-technologies-of-crijaf-14411.html
- A CRIJAF news item (2021) lists CO 58 (Sourav) among relatively recent varieties (developed 2007-08) for replacement of old varieties; this is an institute statement, not a named breeder. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-11/ICAR-News-Jan-Dec%202021.pdf
- Lead breeder name: no evidence found. The search did not return a named breeder for CO 58.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact: no evidence found.
- Institute-level address (from a CRIJAF conference paper; not specific to this variety): Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibres (ICAR), Barrackpore, Kolkata 700 120. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323960530_Sarkar_Debabrata_Pratik_Satya_Chandan_Sourav_Kar_Avijit_Kundu_Avrajit_Chakraborty_Jiban_Mitra_SBChoudhry_Nur_Alam_Mandal_Debajeet_Das_Kanti_Meena_PGKarmakar_ABMandal_MKSinha_BSMahapatra_and_NKSingh_20
- Official email, phone or institute contact page URL: no evidence found in the results. Check https://icar.org.in and the CRIJAF site directly.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, KrishiKosh record or DOI was found that is specifically about CO 58 (Sourav).
- Related item (CO 58 is one of several varieties compared): Binita Dey, Pijush Das, Jayeeta Maji, Chandan Sourav Kar (year not shown in extract). Varietal performance of olitorius jute under coastal soils of West Bengal, Indian Ecological Society. -- https://indianecologicalsociety.com/wp-content/themes/ecology/volume_pdfs/1755055411.pdf (year 2023 per text: pre-kharif 2023 trial)
- Related item: Binita Dey, Pijush Das, Jayeeta Maji, Chandan Sourav Kar (year not shown). Varietal performance of Jute (Corchorus capsularis L.) based on crop growth and yield in the coastal region of South Bengal. ResearchGate. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390811461_Varietal_Performance_of_Jute_Corchorus_capsularis_L_Based_on_Crop_Growth_and_Yield_in_the_Coastal_Region_of_South_Bengal

SEED AVAILABILITY
- CRIJAF sells jute seed under its own trademark and has supplied breeder seed of other varieties; no CO 58 sales record was found. -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/promising-technologies-of-crijaf-14411.html
- Private-dealer listing names "SOURAV (CO-58)" under a "JUTE HYBRIDS" heading. Treat as unverified: CO 58 is an open-pollinated variety, and the listing may be mislabelled. -- https://www.indiaseeds.com/products.html
- No evidence found for NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed sales of CO 58. Seednet listing: not retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- AICRP entry gives state W.B. (West Bengal) as the notifying state. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
- Secondary sources list CO-58 (Sourav) under Assam, Meghalaya and Tripura state lists (these are general guides, not official notifications). -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/a-complete-guide-of-jute-cultivation-in-simple-steps-know-these-unheard-hybrid-jute-varieties/ ; https://cropscultivation.com/jute-cultivation-in-india/
- Recommended-states field in the task record ("Not specified") should be updated to West Bengal (notification) with the secondary-source states flagged as unverified.

SEARCHES RUN: 4 (release/traits; breeder/institute; research papers; seed availability). The Seednet portal was not retrieved and should be checked directly at seednet.gov.in.

- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in Kanchan (IPCK 2009-145) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/new-varieties/

DISEASE AND PEST
- It is moderately resistant to wilt disease. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/new-varieties/
- Same wilt rating in the IIPR varieties page, which also records the gazette notification -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/ (index 4-6)
- No evidence found for stunt, dry root rot, Ascochyta blight, or insect resistance specific to Kanchan.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- It has large seed size (32.2g/100 seed weight) with seed creamy white colour. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/new-varieties/
- It matures in 130-135 days with yield of 18-20 q/ha and suitable for timely sown condition in Western and Central region of Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/new-varieties/
- No Kanchan-specific multi-location trial data found beyond the IIPR summary above.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for parentage, pedigree, marker-assisted work, or QTL studies on Kanchan. The parentage field "Not specified" is unresolved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institute: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur. Listed under Division of Crop Improvement -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/ (index 11-3)
- Lead breeder for Kanchan: No evidence found. The IIPR page gives a breeder only for the neighbouring line IPC 2004-01, and that is not Kanchan.
- Notification: This variety was released in 2022 (Gazette notification No. 1056 (E) dated 06.03.2023. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- Name discrepancy: the IIPR pages describe the line as "Kabuli" in one entry (index 4-4, 20-4) and as "Desi" in another (index 1-3, 20-4). The crop type needs checking before the record is finalised.
- Release-date mismatch: the CSC field says 2022-10-26, but the gazette date is 06.03.2023. The CSC minutes were not located.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Division of Crop Improvement, ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur 208 024 -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/ (index 11-1)
- Breeder name, email, phone: No evidence found for Kanchan. The only breeder contact found is for IPC 2004-01 (Dr. SK Chaturvedi, Principal Scientist & Chickpea Breeder, Mob. 9336214977). The email on that page is truncated ("sushilk.c"), so it cannot be used as recorded -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/ (index 11-6, 11-7)
- Institute contact page URL: No evidence found in the search results.
- Full institute postal address beyond "Kanpur 208 024": No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No Kanchan-specific publication found. No paper, thesis, or conference item naming IPCK 2009-145 or Kanchan chickpea was retrieved.
- Context only: the ICAR-AICRP Chickpea Progress Report 2021-22 (AICRP chickpea report, ICAR-IIPR), which does not mention Kanchan in the retrieved text -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- KrishiKosh: not searched; no evidence retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Chickpea Kanchan (IPCK 2009-145): No evidence found on Seednet, NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, or SAU seed sales.
- Seednet crop "BOTTLE GOURD": the Seednet name "Kanchan" was searched under bottle gourd. The only Kanchan bottle gourd listings are private retail products, for example KANCHAN BOTTLE GOURD ( कंचन लौकी ) product -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/kanchan-bottle-gourd. These do not match the chickpea record, and no Seednet entry was found for chickpea Kanchan.
- Separate varieties not to be conflated with this record: Kashi Kanchan is a bottle gourd variety listed by a seed company -- https://www.vnrseeds.com/variety-list/?vdb=Bottle+Gourd (index 32-7). The ICAR-IIVR page under a bottle gourd URL describes a cowpea variety, Kashi Kanchan -- https://icariivr.org.in/product/bottle-gourd-kashi-kanchan/ (index 37-4). PDKV Kanchan is a Maharashtra chickpea variety released in 2019 -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf (index 16-8).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttar Pradesh only: the gazette-linked entry recommends timely sown conditions in the Western and Central region of Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/new-varieties/ (index 20-8). This matches the input field "Uttar Pradesh".

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME RESOLUTION
- "ALR 2" for coconut: no page uses this exact name for a coconut variety. The closest match is TNAU's "ALR (CN) 2" (coconut, Coconut Research Station, Aliyar Nagar), which the TNAU pages date to 2010, not the 2015-04-07 release date in the record. Treat the link as unverified.
- "ALR 2" as groundnut (ICRISAT PMD_72, TNAU groundnut pages, released 1994) is a different crop and was discarded.
- "PLR 2" (Seednet name, bottle gourd): one TNAU page lists PLR 2 among bottle gourd varieties. No page links it to the coconut release record, so the crop mismatch is unresolved.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- ALR (CN) 2 is described as drought tolerant -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-aliyarnagar/varieties-released/
- The same drought claim appears on the TNAU research-station profile page -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/about_us/abt_us_research_aliyar.html
- No flood, submergence, salinity or heat evidence found for ALR (CN) 2 -- searched via the search 1 and search 3 results; none returned.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for ALR (CN) 2 disease or pest resistance. The TNAU pages that mention resistance (leaf spot, leaf blight, basal stem rot, bud rot, eriophyid mite) refer to ALR (CN) 1 or ALR (CN) 3 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-aliyarnagar/varieties-released/ ; https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/coconut_varieties/coconut_tall_ALR-CN-1.html
- Bottle gourd PLR 2 disease or pest data: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- ALR (CN) 2: selection from Tiptur tall; average yield 109 nuts/palm/year after stabilisation; copra 136 g/nut; copra yield 14 kg/palm/year; oil 64.7% -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-aliyarnagar/varieties-released/ ; https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/about_us/abt_us_research_aliyar.html
- The TNAU page calls it a best substitute for Chowghat Orange Dwarf -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-aliyarnagar/contact-us/ (same varieties page; see https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-aliyarnagar/varieties-released/)
- ALR (CN) 2 trial data (multi-location, AICRP): No evidence found. The AICRP Palms centre page lists ALR (CN) 1, Kalpatharu and ALR (CN) 3 as the station's releases and omits ALR (CN) 2 -- http://www.aicrppalms.res.in/centres_aliya.html
- PLR 2 bottle gourd agronomy: No evidence found beyond the variety name in a TNAU list -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_vegetables_bottlegourd.html
- Maturity for ALR (CN) 2: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for ALR 2 or ALR (CN) 2 genetic, marker or QTL work. The only genomic hits concerned unrelated bottle gourd or other crops.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution for ALR (CN) 2: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coconut Research Station, Aliyar Nagar (642 101, Coimbatore district) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-aliyarnagar/varieties-released/ ; http://www.aicrppalms.res.in/centres_aliya.html
- Lead breeder name for ALR (CN) 2: No evidence found.
- PLR 2 breeder or institution: No evidence found. The TNAU Palur "PLR" code appears only in a seed-extraction scheme and a hybrid scheme, which do not name PLR 2 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/vrs-palur/completed-schemes/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Coconut Research Station, Aliyar Nagar -- 642 101 (Tamil Nadu Agricultural University). Addressed to "The Associate Professor and Head" -- email arsaliar@tnau.ac.in; phone 04253-288722 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-aliyarnagar/contact-us/
- Same station, listed in the TNAU directory as Professor and Head Dr. N. Shoba, Ph.D.: phone 04253-288722, email arsaliar@tnau.ac.in, mobile 9443899677, Fax 04253-288722, Aliyar Nagar-642 101 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/univ_tel_dir_16.06.17.pdf (dated 2017; verify currency)
- Venture-capital scheme contact (Professor and Head, Coconut Research Station, Aliyarnagar-642 101, Coimbatore District; Tel 04253 288722; arsaliar@tnau.ac.in) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_protection/schemes%20&%20services_govt_vcs_crs%20aliyarnagar.html
- PLR 2 (Palur station) contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. Search 3 returned only unrelated items (coconut ethnobotany review, TNAU Coconut Tonic studies, Aliyar soil-series paper), none about ALR 2 or ALR (CN) 2 or PLR 2.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The TNAU page says more than 200,000 seedlings of ALR (CN) 1 were sold to farmers since 2002, and describes strong farmer demand for ALR (CN) 2 seedlings -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-aliyarnagar/varieties-released/
- Seed or seedling sales channel for ALR (CN) 2 (CRS counter, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, private dealers): No evidence found beyond the station contact above.
- PLR 2 bottle gourd seed (TNAU Palur, NSC, dealer): No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- ALR (CN) 2 state recommendation: No evidence found. The record field "Not specified" stands. A krishicode table lists ALR (Cn)-1 for Tamil Nadu only and omits ALR (CN) 2 -- https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/name-of-variety-salient-features_24.html
- PLR 2 recommended states: No evidence found.

The variety is documented in institutional sources (TNAU, seednet, ICAR advisories) as a high-yielding or newly released Tamil Nadu variety, but no yield figure is given, which puts it between the 20 and 40 tiers. A score of 40 reflects that a documented release with qualitative yield claims exists. It is not recommended for Gujarat because no Gujarat adaptation or trial evidence was found.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: PLR 2 is a TNAU bottle gourd selection from the Uchimedu local with round, bottleneck-free fruit, recommended for Tamil Nadu and Puducherry and demonstrated through KVK FLDs. No variety-specific stress, disease or pest tolerance, genetic marker, quantified yield or Gujarat adaptation data were found, and the evidence consists of institutional documents rather than peer-reviewed research. The release year is inconsistent (2019 in TNAU sources versus 2022 in the input).
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Selection from a Tamil Nadu landrace (Uchimedu), with round fruit and no bottleneck, recommended in TNAU and ICAR advisories for Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. Yield and maturity values are not given.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No evidence of drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence, disease or pest tolerance for PLR 2. Stress-related snippets in the results belong to other crops or varieties and should not be attributed to it.

variety_profile.institution: Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana, Punjab (per PPV&FRA journal and PAU sources)
variety_profile.recommended_states: Punjab (released for Punjab in 2014 per PAU); no Gujarat-specific recommendation found
variety_profile.year_of_release: 2022 (supplied record). Search evidence indicates release in 2014 and PPV&FRA registration REG/2016/778. The discrepancy is unresolved, and 2022 may refer to the July 2022 journal listing.

drought_tolerance.technical_details: No variety-specific drought tolerance data found. A snippet from a thesis mentions drought-tolerance selection indices, but this is generic and not attributed to Punjab Barkat. PAU advisories only say to avoid water stress.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The krishikosh thesis snippet mentions temperature and leaf damage in eight bottle gourd genotypes, but it does not state a result for Punjab Barkat. It is used as a parent in the crosses PSPL x Punjab Barkat and Punjab Komal x Punjab Long. No confirmed heat tolerance.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence found.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: The ResearchGate handbook chapter says bottle gourd as a species is more tolerant of waterlogging than ridge gourd. This is a crop-level statement, not a variety-specific one.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: Mosaic disease (moderately resistant)
disease_resistance.technical_details: Several secondary sources (agri-extension and crop-guide websites) report moderate resistance to mosaic disease. No resistance genes or mechanisms are described. These sources largely copy the PAU description and are not primary data.

pest_resistance.technical_details: No pest resistance evidence found. A thesis on screening bottle gourd genotypes for resistance exists, but the snippet gives no result for this variety.

stress_tolerance_analysis.overall_stress_tolerance: no
key_stress_attributes: Moderate resistance to mosaic disease (secondary sources, not confirmed by primary data)

genetic_and_molecular_profile.breeding_techniques: Selection from a local collection or population (per the ResearchGate handbook, 'developed by selection from a...'; the snippet is truncated). Conventional breeding. The variety is also used as a parent in crosses (PSPL x Punjab Barkat).
genetic_and_molecular_profile.genetic_background: Parentage not specified in the record. Developed by selection (details truncated).

agronomic_performance.yield_potential: About 226 q/acre (about 22,600 kg/acre, roughly 55,800 kg/ha by conversion), per secondary sources. The record's unit is only given as 'Kg/Ha'.
agronomic_performance.yield_stability: No multi-environment stability data. A 2019 farmer-field study at Mohali (22 fields, three genotypes) reportedly found Punjab Barkat produced the maximum number of fruits (the snippet is truncated).
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Punjab, suited to spring-summer and rainy season sowing. Not tested in Gujarat according to the evidence.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Vigorous, profusely branched vines. Long, cylindrical, light green fruits.
agronomic_performance.field_trial_results: Mohali farmer-field trial (2019): highest fruit number among three genotypes. The PAU recommended spacing is about 2.5 m x 0.45-0.60 m, with a seed rate of about 2.0 kg/acre.
agronomic_performance.farmer_adoption: Listed among PAU-recommended bottle gourd varieties in Progressive Farming 2024 and in ICAR Kharif Agro-Advisories 2025, which indicates continued use in Punjab. No direct farmer feedback found.

breeder_and_development_info.breeding_institution: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana
breeder_and_development_info.development_timeline: Released for Punjab in 2014. Registered with PPV&FRA as REG/2016/778 and listed in the Plant Variety Journal of July 2022.
breeder_and_development_info.research_publications: PAU Package of Practices for vegetables. The Mohali farmer-field evaluation thesis (2019 study cited). The krishikosh PhD thesis using the variety as a parent. The handbook chapter 'Cucurbits' (2017).

commercial_availability.seed_corporations: Not found. PAU seed is likely sold through its own channels, but this is not confirmed.
commercial_availability.private_dealers: Not found
commercial_availability.availability_status: limited (confirmed in Punjab only; Gujarat availability unknown)

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety has citations: PAU package of practices, a PPV&FRA registration, a thesis with a farmer-field trial, and an ICAR advisory. Its only stress trait is moderate mosaic resistance, which comes from secondary websites. There is no evidence of abiotic stress tolerance and no Gujarat-specific testing, so the score falls in the 'at least one citation, weak on stress traits' band. Yield data exist (about 226 q/acre) but are not independently verified.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Vigorous, profusely branched vines; long, cylindrical, light green fruits; moderately resistant to mosaic; about 226 q/acre; PAU-recommended
dashboard_data.seasons: Spring-summer and rainy (kharif) season sowing in Punjab; the ICAR Kharif advisory 2025 lists it

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Punjab Barkat is a PAU-developed bottle gourd variety released in 2014 (the supplied record says 2022), with vigorous vines, long light-green cylindrical fruits, and a reported yield of about 226 q/acre. Its only documented stress trait is moderate mosaic resistance, from secondary sources. There is no evidence of drought, heat, salinity or flood tolerance, and no Gujarat trials. Evidence quality is moderate for agronomy and low for stress.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: PAU-bred bottle gourd (registered REG/2016/778) with vigorous, branched vines and long cylindrical light-green fruits. Reported yield is about 226 q/acre. Recommended in Punjab, with a high fruit count in Mohali farmer-field trials.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Moderately resistant to mosaic disease per secondary sources. No variety-specific evidence for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance, and no pest resistance data. No genetic markers or QTL were found. It cannot be classed as stress tolerant on current evidence.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME CHECK: The CSC name "Ruchi" (LCK 5021) and the Seednet name "Ruchi" both match linseed sources. The Seednet crop field says "BOTTLE GOURD", which conflicts with linseed. I did not retrieve a Seednet page, so the Seednet crop label should be treated as a probable data-entry error to verify. All evidence below refers to linseed "Ruchi (LCK-5021)".

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Ruchi is listed as a dual-purpose linseed variety with rust and mildew resistance. Ruchi – All Uttar Pradesh. (Rust & Mildew Resistant) -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/research-article/scientific-cultivation-of-dual-purpose-crop-linseed
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance specific to Ruchi: No evidence found. Generic context only: Linseed is fairly resistant to drought -- https://egyankosh.ac.in/bitstream/123456789/88363/1/Unit-8.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Rust and mildew resistance (as above) -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/research-article/scientific-cultivation-of-dual-purpose-crop-linseed
- Pest resistance specific to Ruchi (gall midge, bud fly, wilt, Alternaria): No evidence found. Generic advice: For the control of galmidge, some insecticide should be sprayed at the time of bud formation. -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/research-article/scientific-cultivation-of-dual-purpose-crop-linseed

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Official notification table lists Ruchi (LCK-5021), released 2010 from Kanpur, with a yield potential of 39.84 (printed as Kg/ha, which looks like a unit error and should be verified against the source), oil content listed as 1366 (S) and 1055 (F), and recommended regions as UP except Bundelkhand, Bihar, West Bengal JKD, Assam and NEH -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Maturity duration: No evidence found.
- Multi-location trial results for Ruchi: No evidence found. Generic rabi yield range, not Ruchi-specific: 10 to 15 q/ha of seeds with pure rabi crop under rainfed conditions and 5 to 9 q/ha of seeds under utera conditions. -- https://www.morungexpress.com/linseed-a-potential-dual-purpose-rabi-oilseed-crop

GENETICS AND QTL
- Ruchi-specific genetics, parentage, QTL or marker studies: No evidence found. Parentage remains unrecorded.
- General context: Till date, 102 varieties have been released in the country for different agro-ecologies and most of these varieties are developed either through selections from introductions or hybridizations of intraspecific crosses. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-84200-9_32
- An AFLP diversity study used 45 AICRP genotypes, described as mostly popular varieties, but the retrieved text does not name Ruchi -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0378111914008919

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.
- Developing institution: Not named for Ruchi in the retrieved text. The release centre is listed as Kanpur -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Related context: the AICRP linseed genotype set is draw

seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 110-112 CM, IT IS MEDIUM DURATION VARIETY MATURES IN ABOUT 125 DAYS. PLANTS HAVE THICK STEM AND ERECT PLANT TYPE. THIS NEW AEROBIC RECE VARIETY SAVES WATER UP TO 50% IN SUMMER AND 80-90 IN KHARIF WITH GOOD RAINFALL DISTRIBUTION. DIRECT SEEDED CROP LIKE IN CASE OF RAGE OR MAIZE AND JOWAR IN NON-PUDDLED SITUATION. IT IS DROUGHT AND BLAST DISEASE TOLERANT. PROFUSE ROOTING, HIGH TILLERING AND GRAINS ARE MEDIUM SLENDER. VARIETY IS SUITABLE FOR BOTH KHARIF AND SUMMER SEASONS. IRRIGATION ONCE IN 5-7 DAYS UNTIL FLOWERING AND ONCE IN 3 DAYS AT FLOWERING AND GRAIN FILLING STAGE. THE GRAIN YIELD IS 6T/HA AND FODDER YIELD 6T/HA

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Vardan (IPL 315) is a lentil variety from ICAR-IIPR Kanpur, but the evidence here is thin. I used all four permitted searches. Searches 2 to 4 returned no breeder, contact, peer-reviewed paper, or seed-source pages that name this variety. Seednet name is still unconfirmed.

NAME CHECK
variety_name (CSC minutes): Vardan. seednet_variety_name: Unknown. Searches used "Vardan" and "IPL 315". Every page that names this variety uses "IPL 315" or "Vardan" with IPL 315 in the same row. No Seednet page was found, so the Seednet name remains unconfirmed.

STRESS TOLERANCE
The IIPR varieties page lists IPL 315 as rust-resistant and wilt-tolerant, with large brown seed and orange cotyledons. -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
Rust resistance and wilt tolerance (as above) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/
The IIPR page is the only source found for these traits, and no pest data was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Potential yield 15-20 q/ha and duration 129-138 days (IIPR varieties page) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/
Seed-weight of 2.9 g per 100 seeds (IIPR varieties page) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/
Maturity of 135-140 days and 12-13 q/ha yield in the DPD table, with "2018" and "2019" both given as the release year -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf and http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
No multi-location trial results or AICRP data were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage given as PL 4 x DPL 62 (ResearchGate review table, labelled IPL 315 (Vardan)) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698673_COMPREHENSIVE_STUDY_OF_LENTIL_LENS_CULINARIS_MEDIK_SEED_AND_THEIR_NUTRITIONAL_PROFILE-A_REVIEW
Breeding method, breeding-line code, QTL/marker and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur (IIPR varieties page and DPD table) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/ and https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
The only contact information found is the institute copyright footer: "ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur" (https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/). No official email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL appeared in the retrieved results. Verify these on the IIPR site before use.

PUBLICATIONS
The ResearchGate review (author and year fields not shown in the retrieved text) lists IPL 315 (Vardan) in a variety table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698673_COMPREHENSIVE_STUDY_OF_LENTIL_LENS_CULINARIS_MEDIK_SEED_AND_THEIR_NUTRITIONAL_PROFILE-A_REVIEW
A ResearchGate paper on breeding strategies uses IPL-315 only as one of four check varieties in a 50-genotype trial (rabi 2023-24), so it does not describe this variety itself -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313234111_Breeding_strategies_to_improve_lentil_for_diverse_agro-ecological_environments
No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, KrishiKosh record or AICRP report focused on this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed-related search returned only international seed retailers, which are not relevant to this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Uttar Pradesh (IIPR varieties page; DPD table lists U.P.) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/ and https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
The ResearchGate review table lists "M.P, C.G & Bundelkhand" with a "region of U.P." note. This is ambiguous and needs checking against the source. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698673_COMPREHENSIVE_STUDY_OF_LENTIL_LENS_CULINARIS_MEDIK_SEED_AND_THEIR_NUTRITIONAL_PROFILE-A_REVIEW

GAPS FOR FOLLOW-UP
- Year of release: the sources disagree (2018 and 2019 in the DPD table, 2019 on IIPR, 2010 in the review, which may refer to development). Check the CSC minutes.
- Institution, parentage, and station are partly confirmed. Breeder names, contacts, seed sources and Seednet listing still need a direct check on seednet.gov.in and the IIPR site.

drought.details: No drought-specific evidence was found for Varuna or Varuna-WRR2. The Haryana State Seeds listing describes T-59 (Varuna) as suitable for rainfed areas, which is a general suitability statement rather than a measured drought tolerance result. The same listing also describes T-59 as frost resistant and lodging resistant. Tractor Junction describes T-59 as suited to all climatic conditions. These statements refer to T-59 (the older open-pollinated Varuna), not confirmed for Varuna-WRR2. The digest notes that the research query found no drought-index evidence.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to Varuna or Varuna-WRR2 in the searched research query.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to Varuna or Varuna-WRR2 in the searched research query.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to Varuna or Varuna-WRR2 in the searched research query.

disease_resistance.summary: White rust (Albugo candida): Varuna is documented as susceptible. It was used as the susceptible host in white-rust transformation work and as the susceptible cultivar in a 2014-16 white-rust fungicide trial. Transgenic WRR-gene lines derived from Varuna were characterised as resistant, including resistance to a virulent Ac2V isolate. Varuna-WRR gene lines show higher constitutive defence metabolites and sustained transcriptomic and metabolomic defence responses against A. candida. Naming note: the digest uses both Varuna-WRR2 and Varuna_WRR for the white-rust-resistant derivative, and the source linking them to the variety code is not confirmed. No other disease resistance evidence was found.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for aphid, Alternaria, or other pest resistance in Varuna.

agronomic_details.yield: Haryana State Seeds: 8-10 quintals/acre (T-59 Varuna). Tractor Junction: about 6-8 quintals/acre (T-59 Varuna). Kisaan Helpline: average seed yield 18 quintals/ha. CSAUA&T Kanpur variety-characterisation table lists 1140 (2015-16) falling to 60 (2020-21), with unclear meaning. These figures are not consistent with each other and are not confirmed for Varuna-WRR2. DMH-11 is reported 28% above Varuna in ICAR-DRMR trials, but this figure comes from the promoter and the Biotech Consortium, not an independent multi-location trial.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location AICRP-RM yield data for Varuna-WRR2 was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended states: Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh (Northern Rajasthan standardised to Rajasthan). Haryana State Seeds describes T-59 as suitable for rainfed areas. Tractor Junction describes T-59 as suited to all climatic conditions. Kisaan Helpline describes irrigated conditions. Agro-climatic fit beyond these statements is not specified in the digest.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Haryana State Seeds: 145-150 days. Tractor Junction: 145-150 days. Kisaan Helpline (Hindi): 110-115 days. Sources differ; variety identity for each figure should be checked.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Haryana State Seeds (T-59 Varuna): lodging resistant, non-shattering, frost resistant. Oil content about 39% (Haryana State Seeds and Tractor Junction) and 37% (Kisaan Helpline). Sowing 25 Sep-15 Oct; seed rate 2 kg/acre (Haryana State Seeds) and line sowing 7.5 kg/ha (Kisaan Helpline). Morphological characteristics are not specified in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Haryana State Seeds and Tractor Junction report yield ranges for T-59 Varuna as listed above; these are listing values, not trial results. (2) CSAUA&T Kanpur variety-characterisation table: Varuna (T-59) yield 1140 (2015-16) to 60 (2020-21), meaning unclear. (3) DMH-11 reported 28% above Varuna in ICAR-DRMR trials, sourced from the promoter and Biotech Consortium, not independent. (4) A 2014-16 white-rust fungicide trial used Varuna as the susceptible cultivar. No multi-location AICRP-RM data for Varuna-WRR2 was found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Varuna x Heera doubled-haploid (VH) map with 833 markers. A chromosome-scale genome assembly of Varuna with 18 pseudochromosomes is reported. Marker positions are not available in the digest. Varuna bn 3.6 carries barnase, and barstar sits in EH-2 modbs 2.99 (a transgenic male-sterility system, not a stress marker).
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Varuna x Tumida doubled-haploid population: 20 stable QTL for nine plant architecture traits, with candidate genes mapped to the Varuna and Tumida genome assemblies. No QTL specific to white-rust resistance in Varuna-WRR2 was found beyond the multi-omics study. QTL effect sizes are not available in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: BjuWRR1-mediated resistance to A. candida in Varuna_WRR, with higher constitutive defence metabolites and sustained transcriptomic and metabolomic defence responses (2026 multi-omics study). Candidate genes for plant architecture traits are mapped to the Varuna and Tumida assemblies. Barnase/barstar is a transgenic male-sterility system in bn 3.6.

commercial_info.private_dealers: Tractor Junction and Kisaan Helpline pages reference Varuna varieties; no dealer details were found in the digest. Not found in searched sources for dealers.

disease_resistance.summary: White rust (Albugo candida): Varuna is documented as susceptible. It was used as the susceptible host in white-rust transformation work and as the susceptible cultivar in a 2014-16 white-rust fungicide trial. Transgenic WRR-gene lines derived from Varuna were characterised as resistant, including resistance to a virulent Ac2V isolate. Varuna-WRR gene lines show higher constitutive defence metabolites and sustained transcriptomic and metabolomic defence responses against A. candida. Naming note: the digest uses both Varuna-WRR2 and Varuna_WRR for the white-rust-resistant derivative, and the source linking them to the variety code is not confirmed. No other disease resistance evidence was found.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for aphid, Alternaria, or other pest resistance in Varuna.

genetics_and_qtl.genetic_markers: Varuna x Heera doubled-haploid (VH) map with 833 markers. A chromosome-scale genome assembly of Varuna with 18 pseudochromosomes is reported. Marker positions are not available in the digest. Varuna bn 3.6 carries barnase, and barstar sits in EH-2 modbs 2.99 (a transgenic male-sterility system, not a stress marker).
genetics_and_qtl.qtl_information: Varuna x Tumida doubled-haploid population: 20 stable QTL for nine plant architecture traits, with candidate genes mapped to the Varuna and Tumida genome assemblies. No QTL specific to white-rust resistance in Varuna-WRR2 was found beyond the multi-omics study. QTL effect sizes are not available in the digest.
genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: BjuWRR1-mediated resistance to A. candida in Varuna_WRR, with higher constitutive defence metabolites and sustained transcriptomic and metabolomic defence responses (2026 multi-omics study). Candidate genes for plant architecture traits are mapped to the Varuna and Tumida assemblies. Barnase/barstar is a transgenic male-sterility system in bn 3.6.

agronomic_performance.yield: Haryana State Seeds: 8-10 quintals/acre (T-59 Varuna). Tractor Junction: about 6-8 quintals/acre (T-59 Varuna). Kisaan Helpline: average seed yield 18 quintals/ha. CSAUA&T Kanpur variety-characterisation table lists 1140 (2015-16) falling to 60 (2020-21), with unclear meaning. These figures are not consistent with each other and are not confirmed for Varuna-WRR2. DMH-11 is reported 28% above Varuna in ICAR-DRMR trials, but this figure comes from the promoter and the Biotech Consortium, not an independent multi-location trial.
agronomic_performance.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location AICRP-RM yield data for Varuna-WRR2 was found.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Recommended states: Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh (Northern Rajasthan standardised to Rajasthan). Haryana State Seeds describes T-59 as suitable for rainfed areas. Tractor Junction describes T-59 as suited to all climatic conditions. Kisaan Helpline describes irrigated conditions. Agro-climatic fit beyond these statements is not specified in the digest.
agronomic_performance.maturity_days: Haryana State Seeds: 145-150 days. Tractor Junction: 145-150 days. Kisaan Helpline (Hindi): 110-115 days. Sources differ; variety identity for each figure should be checked.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Haryana State Seeds (T-59 Varuna): lodging resistant, non-shattering, frost resistant. Oil content about 39% (Haryana State Seeds and Tractor Junction) and 37% (Kisaan Helpline). Sowing 25 Sep-15 Oct; seed rate 2 kg/acre (Haryana State Seeds) and line sowing 7.5 kg/ha (Kisaan Helpline). Morphological characteristics are not specified in the digest.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: (1) Haryana State Seeds and Tractor Junction report yield ranges for T-59 Varuna as listed above; these are listing values, not trial results. (2) CSAUA&T Kanpur variety-characterisation table: Varuna (T-59) yield 1140 (2015-16) to 60 (2020-21), meaning unclear. (3) DMH-11 reported 28% above Varuna in ICAR-DRMR trials, sourced from the promoter and Biotech Consortium, not independent. (4) A 2014-16 white-rust fungicide trial used Varuna as the susceptible cultivar. No multi-location AICRP-RM data for Varuna-WRR2 was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY RECORD: Varuna (variety_name) / Varuna (seednet_variety_name), crop mustard (Brassica juncea). Seednet crop name is BOTTLE GOURD; no source supports that.

NAME NOTE: Searches on "Varuna" returned two different lines. Varuna T-59 is the older open-pollinated mustard variety. Varuna-WRR2 / Varuna_WRR is a white-rust-resistant derivative in CGMCP research. Varuna bn 3.6 is a barnase male-sterile GM line. No source linked the 2022-10-26 date to a CSC release of Varuna-WRR2. The date matches the 18-Oct-2022 GEAC release recommendation and the 25-Oct-2022 MoEFCC approval for GM mustard (DMH-11 and parental lines). I could not confirm a Seednet listing; the Seednet portal was not reachable by search.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Haryana State Seeds listing describes T-59 (Varuna) as frost resistant, lodging resistant, non-shattering, and suitable for rainfed areas -- https://haryanaseeds.org.in/products/field-crops/rabi-crops/mustard
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Tractor Junction describes T-59 (Varuna) as suited to all climatic conditions -- https://www.tractorjunction.com/blog/mustard-farming-in-india-varieties-cultivation/
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Varuna's susceptibility to white rust (Albugo candida) is documented; a Varuna-derived white-rust-resistant line (Varuna_WRR) was characterised as resistant -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11033-023-09040-w ; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2026.1918745/full

disease_resistance.research_summary: White rust (Albugo candida): Varuna is documented as susceptible. It was used as the susceptible host in white-rust transformation work and as the susceptible cultivar in a 2014-16 white-rust fungicide trial. Transgenic WRR-gene lines derived from Varuna were characterised as resistant, including resistance to a virulent Ac2V isolate. Varuna-WRR gene lines show higher constitutive defence metabolites and sustained transcriptomic and metabolomic defence responses against A. candida. Naming note: the digest uses both Varuna-WRR2 and Varuna_WRR for the white-rust-resistant derivative, and the source linking them to the variety code is not confirmed. No other disease resistance evidence was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Rice variety "6129" (CSC name) / "6129 (BS- 129) (HRI 152) (IET 18815)" (Seednet name)

Search note: 4 web_search calls were used. The Seednet portal itself did not appear in any result, so Seednet-specific fields could not be checked directly. Results for "Arize 6129", "Arize 6129 Gold", "Sava 7501", and "AICRIP hybrid rice" were excluded as different products or varieties. Name-matched entries are labelled below as "6129 (BS 129 (HRI152 (IET 18815)" (Seednet-style name) or "Hybrid-6129 (IET 18815)" (CSC-style name).

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. Searches returned only general QTL papers on other rice lines (for example, IR64, TDK1, and a heat-tolerant aromatic population), which were excluded.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest resistance data naming this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity listed as 120 days (mid-early), with yield not available, for HRI-152 (IET 18815), 2007, Bayer Bio-Science Hyderabad -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Maturity 115-120 days and yield 6.58 t/ha listed for PA 6129, 2007, Bayer Bio-Science Hyderabad (name variant; the page does not explicitly link PA 6129 to IET 18815) -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Same figures repeated in a Hindi-language list of hybrid paddy released 1994–2021 -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/
- Kerala Agricultural University Research Report 2017 lists PA-6129 among five rice hybrids in an Advanced Variety Trial (early, transplanted) with silicon-solubiliser treatments, compared against the local check Jyothi. Trial yield for PA-6129 specifically was not visible in the snippet (name variant, not confirmed as this variety) -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/research_report_2017.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: No evidence found.
- Breeding method: No evidence found. The name is listed as a hybrid (Hybrid-6129), which indicates a hybrid breeding origin, but the method and parental lines were not found.
- Breeding-line codes found: BS 129, HRI 152, IET 18815 (as listed in the notifications) -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Breeding-line code IET 18815 also appears in the PPV&FR registration compendium as "Hybrid-6129 (IET-18815)" -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumfinal27oct2018.pdf
- QTL, marker, or genome-resource data: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution (the only one found): Bayer Bio-Science, Hyderabad, listed for HRI-152 (IET 18815) and PA 6129 -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Bayer Crop Science is named as developer of the separate product "Arize 6129 Gold", which is excluded from the findings above -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/national-news/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.
- Station or research site: No evidence found beyond the Hyderabad location above.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder name, role, email, and phone: No evidence found.
- Institute-level contact: The searches did not return an official Bayer or Bayer Crop Science contact page. The only location found is the Bayer Bio-Science Hyderabad listing above, with no postal address, email, or phone.
- Official institute page URL: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Kerala Agricultural University (2017). Research Report 2017 (compilation of university trials; the trial listing names PA-6129 among entries; the editor list was not captured). KAU Research Report 2017 -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/research_report_2017.pdf
- PPV&FR Authority (2018). Compendium of Registered Varieties under PPV&FR Act, 2001 (contains an entry "Hybrid-6129 (IET-18815)" at page 71; applicant and certificate details were not visible in the snippet). Compendium -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumfinal27oct2018.pdf
- No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, KrishiKosh theses, or DOI-linked publications found for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Aggarwal Enterprises, Karnal, Haryana (IndiaMART dealer listing): "Hybrid paddy 6129 bayer", 3 kg packet, listed at ₹850 per packet, marked in stock; listing date not shown -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/hybrid-paddy-6129-bayer-23443473048.html
- National Seeds Corporation, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU seed sale listings: No evidence found.
- Seednet availability status: not checked directly (portal not returned by search).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Haryana: notified for "6129 (BS 129 (HRI152 (IET 18815)" under S.O. 268(E) dated 28.01.2015 -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm (also https://krishakjagat.org/national-news/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/)
- All India: "Hybrid-6129 (IET 18815)" under S.O. 1703(E) dated 05.10.2007 -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm (also https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf)
- Punjab, Tamil Nadu, and Pondicherry: listed for HRI-152 (IET 18815) and PA 6129 -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Year of release: the CSC input value "0" is not valid. Evidence shows 2007 (all-India hybrid notification) and 2015 (Haryana notification for the 6129 (BS 129) entry).

csc_fields.meeting_title: Minutes of the 28th meeting of Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties for Horticultural Crops
csc_fields.additional_notes: General regulatory guidelines and conditions for consideration of proposals for release and notification of Horticultural crop & variety by the committee:, 1. Sponsoring Institute/organization should ensure that the proposals are submitted in proper format and must have the required documents viz., acknowledgement certificate regarding submission of seed sample with NBPGR, detailed morphological characters of varieties, AICRP data on disease and pests reaction, source of material and pedigree, package of practices of the cultivar, DNA fingerprinting profile, A-4 size coloured photographs on glossy sheet etc., 2. The committee will not consider any proposal for release or notification in case the copy of proposal is not submitted to respective Director/Project Coordinator., 3. The proposals will be submitted through email (cvrc.hort-agri@gov.in). Five signed original hard copies will be submitted to Deputy Commissioner (Quality Control), DAC&FW, Shastri Bhawan, New Delhi for records., 4. Each sponsoring institution/breeder will make of the proposal., 5. ICAR Institutes, SAUs and other organizations should devise a naming system of the name of Institute followed by crop name and then serial number of variety. Proposals with names of family members, gods and goddesses will not be accepted., 6. RECORD FLAG -- The input lists crop "potato" and Seednet crop "BRINJAL", but the only Arunima entry I found is a sweet potato line from the CTCRI tuber-crop release bulletin. The parentage (brinjal, Digras, Yeotmal) and the Seednet name ARUNA did not appear in any result. Treat the record as unverified until the CSC minutes and Seednet entry are checked. Searches used: (1) release/notification, (2) breeder/institute, (3) research papers, (4) identity check on ARUNA/brinjal. No seed-availability search was run, so that heading has no search behind it.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- The only Arunima entry found is noted for a relatively low incidence of sweet potato weevil; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found for it. -- https://www.ctcri.org/public/publications/2025-11/technical-bulletin_tuber_crop_varieties_in_india.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- Weevil incidence is the only pest note for Arunima. AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The bulletin describes a semi-spreading plant, purplish-red-skinned elliptic tubers with orange flesh, beta-carotene content, and a 90-100 day duration.
