drought_tolerance.technical_details: The IARI Annual Report 2022 snippet mentions Pusa Hybrid-5 near a statement about 'most tolerant to drought stress', but the snippet is truncated. It cannot be shown that the statement refers to this brinjal hybrid. The same report lists a bitter gourd 'Pusa Hybrid-5', so the name may belong to a different crop. Other hits only mention drought generically.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: Climate-smart brinjal review lists Pusa Hybrid 5 among varieties, but the snippet does not state heat tolerance. The PMC 2025 article lists it in a nutraceutical comparison (a quality trait, not a stress trait). The heat-tolerance hits are generic. The agricultural catalogue's 'tolerant to heat' line refers to a different crop (pod yield 18 t/ha).

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: No variety-specific salinity data. Salt-tolerance mentions in the results are generic (ICAR advisory for YAAS-affected lands, transplastomic brinjal in the ISAAA brief).

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No variety-specific flood data. Several sources state brinjal in general cannot tolerate waterlogging and advise avoiding water stagnation. This is a crop-level statement, not a tested trait of this hybrid.

submergence_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence. The 'submergence tolerant' reference in the BASU advisory is about paddy varieties, not brinjal.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: None confirmed. The release record says only that no major disease problem was encountered in the field. A krishisewa listing has 'Tolerant to fruitrot, wilt and blight', but the snippet is ambiguous and may belong to the adjacent variety entry.
disease_resistance.technical_details: The record gives no resistance genes or mechanisms and no screening data.

pest_resistance.specific_pests: None confirmed. The record says only that no major pest problem was seen in the field, which is an observation rather than a resistance trial. Fruit and shoot borer resistance is not documented.
pest_resistance.technical_details: No resistance mechanisms or genes reported.

stress_tolerance_analysis.overall_stress_tolerance: no (not demonstrated). The official record says 'NOT APPLICABLE' for stress reaction, and the search results contain no variety-specific stress data.
key_stress_attributes: None evidence-backed

genetic_and_molecular_profile.breeding_techniques: Conventional F1 hybrid breeding from two good combining lines (heterosis breeding). No marker-assisted selection is documented.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: There are many citations and sources confirming the variety's identity, yield (45-55 t/ha) and recommendation by ICAR/IARI. However, no source gives variety-specific evidence of stress tolerance (drought, heat, salinity, flood, disease or pest). The official stress reaction is 'NOT APPLICABLE', and the drought and heat hits are ambiguous or generic. The 75 and 60 bands require at least one stress trait with a citation or a citation with weak stress traits. Citations exist for yield and adaptation, which would fit 60, but the lack of any stress trait and the absence of Gujarat in the recommended states led to a conservative score. Evidence of agronomic merit is moderate. Score band chosen: 50 (a defensible range is 40-60).

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Long glossy dark purple fruits; F1 hybrid; 45-55 t/ha; 80-85 days to first picking; fertility-responsive; poor in poor soils; no major disease or pest seen in release trials.
dashboard_data.state_acronyms: DL, UP, PB, AP, KL, TN, KA
dashboard_data.seasons: Autumn-winter and spring-summer (Central Gangetic Plains); normal season in southern states; ICAR advisory also mentions a Kharif sowing window of mid-April to end of May.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Pusa Hybrid-5 is an IARI long-fruited brinjal F1 hybrid released in 1992 with high yield (45-55 t/ha) and maturity in 80-85 days, and it is widely listed in ICAR and state advisories. No variety-specific evidence of drought, heat, salinity, flood, disease or pest tolerance was found, and the official stress reaction is 'not applicable'. Evidence is strong for yield and adaptation but weak for stress traits, and the variety is not formally recommended for Gujarat.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Long-fruited, dark purple IARI F1 hybrid yielding 45-55 t/ha, maturing in 80-85 days, responsive to good soil fertility and poor in poor soils. Recommended for Delhi, UP, Punjab, AP and southern states across multiple seasons.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No documented stress tolerance. Release trials noted no major disease or pest problems, but there are no screening data or resistance genes. Generic brinjal waterlogging sensitivity applies. Genetic marker and QTL information is absent.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Ranga (CSC name, sugarcane) / Prangal (Seednet name, listed under BRINJAL)

Searches run: 4 of 4 allowed (release and notification; Prangal on Seednet; breeder; Co V 15-356 research). The seed availability search was not run because the search cap was reached. The Seednet and CSC records conflict on crop: Seednet lists brinjal, while the CSC record and the Co V code point to sugarcane.

STRESS TOLERANCE (Ranga: no evidence found; Prangal: no evidence found)
No page names Ranga or Prangal for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. A RARS Anakapalle waterlogging study tests 16 unnamed pre-release clones, so it is not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/Sugarcane-Clones-Suitable-for-Water-logged-Conditions-of-Andhra-Pradesh-PS-Rao-66.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST (Ranga: no evidence found; Prangal: no evidence found)
A 2025 news report on two new Anakapalle sugarcane varieties says one is red-rot resistant, but neither variety is named, so it is not attributed. -- https://www.etvbharat.com/amp/en/state/andhra-pradesh-anakapalle-agri-research-centre-releases-two-new-sugarcane-varieties-enn26061900957
The sugarcane borer review credits Co 356 with borer resistance. That is a different designation from Co V 15-356, so it is discarded. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10340-024-01750-9

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (Ranga: no evidence found; Prangal: no evidence found)
The same news report gives yield and jaggery figures for the two unnamed varieties, so they are not attributed. -- https://www.etvbharat.com/amp/en/state/andhra-pradesh-anakapalle-agri-research-centre-releases-two-new-sugarcane-varieties-enn26061900957
The AICRP sugarcane page for the Anakapalle station lists its released varieties. None is Ranga. The closest entry is CoA 14321 (Vasista, 2009A 107), released in 2020 with a yield of 135 t/ha. That designation differs from "2009 V 127" in the record, so it is not attributed. -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/anakapalle.htm

GENETICS AND QTL (Ranga: no evidence found; Prangal: no evidence found)
No page on marker, QTL or DNA-fingerprinting work names this variety. The fingerprinting hits concern Swarnamukhi (Co T 10367), a different clone. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346126746_Swarnamukhi_Co_T_10367_-_A_New_Sugarcane_clone_for_Andhra_Pradesh

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (Ranga: no breeder found; Prangal: no evidence found)
The ANGRAU 2020-21 annual report says one sugarcane variety from the university was submitted to the State Variety Release Committee for identification and release. It does not name the variety, so this cannot be linked to Ranga. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/ANGRAU%20AR%20%202020-21.pdf
The developing station for ANGRAU's Anakapalle sugarcane work is the Regional Agricultural Research Station, Anakapalle. This is station-level context only. -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/anakapalle.htm
Ch Mukunda Rao (Associate Director of Research) and D Adilakshmi (Principal Scientist, Sugarcane) are named in a news report about two unnamed Anakapalle varieties. They are not attributed to Ranga. -- https://www.etvbharat.com/amp/en/state/andhra-pradesh-anakapalle-agri-research-centre-releases-two-new-sugarcane-varieties-enn26061900957

CONTACT DETAILS (Ranga: institute-level only; Prangal: no evidence found)
Institute address, from ANGRAU annual report 2020-21: "Lam, Guntur-522 034, Andhra Pradesh, India". No email or phone appeared in the retrieved text. This is an institute-level address only, not a breeder contact. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/ANGRAU%20AR%20%202020-21.pdf
No breeder email or phone was found for Ranga.

PUBLICATIONS (Ranga: no evidence found; Prangal: no evidence found)
No paper, report or thesis names Ranga, Prangal or Co V 15-356. The Swarnamukhi and Co 86032 items are about other clones and varieties and are discarded. No item is listed.

SEED AVAILABILITY (Ranga: not searched; Prangal: no evidence found)
Seed availability was not searched because the search cap was reached. The Prangal search returned only brinjal varieties from TNAU, IIHR (Arka series) and Wikipedia GI pages, none named Prangal. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/ta/aas/brinjal.html ; https://iihr.res.in/varieties-crop-name/brinjal

RECOMMENDED STATES (Ranga: no evidence found; Prangal: no evidence found)
The 2023 central notification list of sugarcane varieties for sale covers Andhra Pradesh, but none of its entries is Ranga. The recorded state "Andhra Pradesh" is therefore unconfirmed for this variety. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-10-new-varieties-of-sugarcane-for-farmers/

drought_tolerance.technical_details: Snippets mention drought only in generic contexts. One grafting snippet says a rootstock is 'resistant to wilt pathogens and tolerant to drought', which refers to the rootstock, not Pusa Hybrid-6. The IARI Annual Report 2022 drought snippet appears next to a bitter gourd entry, so it cannot be attributed to this brinjal hybrid. No direct drought trial of Pusa Hybrid-6 is evident.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The IARI 2018 annual report has a heat tolerance screening item next to the Pusa Hybrid-6 yield figure (44.25 t/ha), but the snippet does not link the two. Other heat-related snippets are generic. The release notes say it suits spring-summer crops only where summers are free of long hot dry winds, which suggests limited tolerance to hot dry conditions.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: A 2025 ScienceDirect study (Plant Physiology and Biochemistry, pii S0981942825001949) lists Pusa Hybrid-6 among genotypes classed as highly tolerant at the germination stage. This is a germination-stage screen only, and the snippets show no field-level salinity data. I rate it medium rather than high because the evidence covers one stage and the full text was not available. Grafting studies cite it as a scion on salt-tolerant rootstocks, which does not show intrinsic tolerance.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No direct evidence for this variety. Sources state that brinjal in general cannot tolerate waterlogging. The waterlogging items in IARI reports concern other crops and germplasm.

submergence_tolerance.technical_details: The submergence snippets concern rice and other crops. The BAU Sabour document that mentions Pusa Hybrid-6 uses it as a yield check in a brinjal hybrid trial, not as a submergence-tolerant entry.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: The official description reports no major disease problems in the field. A 2023 bacterial wilt screening snippet groups Pusa Hybrid-6 with entries other than the resistant Arka Nidhi, which implies it was not resistant (the snippet is truncated).
disease_resistance.technical_details: No resistance genes or mechanisms are documented. The observation of no major disease problems is a field observation, not a resistance claim.

pest_resistance.specific_pests: Fruit and shoot borer (FSB). The ISAAA brief reports Pusa Hybrid-6 as the national check in Bt brinjal trials, with higher damage (mean shoot damage 13.07% and higher fruit damage) than the Bt hybrids (1.51%) and non-Bt counterparts (7.06%).
pest_resistance.technical_details: The release notes recommend routine pest control, particularly in August to October, against FSB. These data show susceptibility to FSB, not resistance.

stress_tolerance_analysis.overall_stress_tolerance: no
key_stress_attributes: Germination-stage salinity tolerance reported in a 2025 study (single-stage evidence)
Susceptible to fruit and shoot borer (national check in Bt brinjal trials)
No documented drought, heat, flood or submergence tolerance

genetic_and_molecular_profile.genetic_markers: None found in the search results.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.molecular_mechanisms: None documented for this hybrid. The salinity study concerns antioxidant enzymes in tolerant genotypes in general.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.breeding_techniques: Conventional F1 hybrid breeding using two good combining lines.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.genetic_background: A ROUND FRUITED F1 HYBRID DEVELOPED BY TWO GOOD COMBINING LINES OF BRINJAL. Some sources describe it as non-spiny, and a protected cultivation manual lists it among parthenocarpic hybrids (unverified).

agronomic_performance.yield_stability: No multi-environment stability analysis was found. Reported yields are consistent across sources: 45 t/ha (eAgri), 450 q/ha (Krishisewa), and 44.25 t/ha in an IARI 2018 trial. Another trial reports 325.51 q/ha as a check.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: RECOMMENDED FOR RLEASE AND CULTIVATION FOR NORTHERN & CENTRAL INDIA. 1. AUTUMN- WINTER CROP ( FROST- FREE WINTER); 2. SPRING-SUMMER CROP (SUMMER FREE OF LONG HOT DRY WINDS). Responsive to normal and higher fertility soils, but not poor soils.

agronomic_performance.field_trial_results: Used widely as a national check in Bt brinjal large-scale trials, and as a check in BAU Sabour hybrid evaluation. IARI 2018 report: 44.25 t/ha. Grafting studies (Kumar et al., 2017) assessed yield and quality of Pusa Hybrid-6 grafted on rootstocks.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: There are multiple citations (a 2025 peer-reviewed study, 2017 grafting work, ICAR and IARI reports) and consistent high yield data of 40-50 t/ha. The only stress trait with research backing is germination-stage salinity tolerance, which is narrow, and FSB susceptibility is documented. Because stress evidence is weak and not field-validated, it falls in the 60 band (citation present, weak on stress traits) instead of 75. The variety is also not officially recommended for Gujarat, and its adaptation notes exclude hot dry wind summers.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Early round purple F1 hybrid, 40-50 t/ha, 85-90 days, germination-stage salinity tolerance reported, FSB susceptible, needs fertile soil
dashboard_data.seasons: Autumn-winter (frost-free) and spring-summer (free of long hot dry winds)

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Pusa Hybrid-6 is an early, round-fruited IARI F1 brinjal hybrid (1991) with consistently reported yields of 40-50 t/ha and wide use as a check variety. The only research-backed stress trait is germination-stage salinity tolerance, while it is susceptible to fruit and shoot borer and no drought, heat, flood or submergence tolerance was found. Yield evidence is strong, stress evidence is weak, and no genetic marker or breeder contact data were located.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Early (85-90 days) round purple F1 hybrid from IARI, released in 1991, yielding 40-50 t/ha. Suited to fertile soils in autumn-winter and spring-summer seasons of northern and central India, and officially recommended for Maharashtra.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Evidence of stress tolerance is limited to germination-stage salinity tolerance in a 2025 screening study. It is susceptible to fruit and shoot borer, and the search results show no direct evidence for drought, heat, flood or submergence tolerance. Overall stress tolerance is unclear and not demonstrated.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance evidence found for Shalimar Brinjal Hybrid-1. Bacterial wilt: no evidence found for this variety. pest_resistance.summary: No resistance to shoot and fruit borer (Leucinodes orbonalis) is supported by the evidence. Shalimar Brinjal Hybrid-1 and Hybrid-2 showed the highest shoot infestation (about 9.1 and 8.7 per cent) and fruit infestation (about 23.1 and 22.0 per cent) among the tested brinjal genotypes, and had higher total sugars and lower total phenols. These findings indicate relatively high infestation, not resistance. No other pest data found in the digest.

It was classed as a public-sector hybrid from SKUAST-Kashmir and grouped in Cluster VI with Pink Long, Baramulla Local Sel-01 and Baramulla Local Sel-02. No yield values were found. (2) Shoot and fruit borer screening: Shalimar Brinjal Hybrid-1 and Hybrid-2 recorded about 9.1 and 8.7 per cent shoot infestation and about 23.1 and 22.0 per cent fruit infestation by Leucinodes orbonalis, the highest among the tested brinjal genotypes, with higher total sugars and lower total phenols. (3) No yield, maturity, spacing or multi-location trial data found.

Bacterial wilt: no evidence found for this variety. The bacterial wilt tolerance results in the Scientific Reports and PMC papers refer to other hybrids (BBSR series crosses), not Shalimar. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12216501

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Shalimar Hybrid-1 was one of 30 pink brinjal genotypes tested at the Experimental Farm, Division of Vegetable Science, SKUAST-J (Jammu), in a genetic divergence study. It was classed as a public-sector hybrid from SKUAST-Kashmir, and was grouped in Cluster VI with Pink Long, Baramulla Local Sel-01 and Baramulla Local Sel-02. No yield values for this hybrid were found in the snippets. -- https://www.genresj.org/index.php/grj/article/download/genresj.FRFO5243/204?inline=1
No yield, maturity, spacing or multi-location trial data for Shalimar Brinjal Hybrid-1 found. -- https://www.genresj.org/index.php/grj/article/download/genresj.FRFO5243/204?inline=1

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found: no parentage, inbred parents, QTL, marker or combining-ability study for Shalimar Brinjal Hybrid-1 was found. Parentage remains "Not specified". The SSR and heterosis papers found (e.g., https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-56612-4) do not include this hybrid in the snippets.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: SKUAST-Kashmir (Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir), per the release metadata and the genetic divergence study. -- https://www.genresj.org/index.php/grj/article/download/genresj.FRFO5243/204?inline=1
Breeder name: No evidence found for the lead breeder or scientist of Shalimar Brinjal Hybrid-1.
Division: Division of Vegetable Science, Faculty of Horticulture, Shalimar Campus, which runs the university's brinjal and other vegetable hybrid programmes. Head of Division named as Prof. Ishfaq Abidi (2026 news report; not confirmed as this hybrid's developer). -- https://kashmirreader.com/2026/07/17/skuast-k-advances-climate-resilient-vegetable-breeding/

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder: No evidence found.
Institute-level: Prof. Ishfaq Abidi, Head, Division of Vegetable Science, Faculty of Horticulture, Shalimar Campus, SKUAST-K (named in news report; no email or phone found) -- https://kashmirreader.com/2026/07/17/skuast-k-advances-climate-resilient-vegetable-breeding/
Email, phone and postal address: No evidence found in the search results. Institute contact page URL: not captured in results; SKUAST-K main site not returned by searches.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not captured (2024 or later, based on cited references). Genetic Resources Journal (GenRes J) -- https://www.genresj.org/index.php/grj/article/download/genresj.FRFO5243/204?inline=1
Authors not captured (year not captured). Biochemical Basis of Resistance in Brinjal Genotypes Against Shoot and Fruit Borer (Leucinodes orbonalis Guenee). Journal/report not captured -- https://www.academia.edu/37770162/Biochemical_Basis_of_Resistance_in_Brinjal_Genotypes_Against_Shoot_and_Fruit_Borer_Leucinodes_Orbonalis_Guenee_
No AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, or peer-reviewed paper dedicated to Shalimar Brinjal Hybrid-1 was found in the search results.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found from NSC, SKUAST-K seed sales, KVKs, or state seed corporations for Shalimar Brinjal Hybrid-1 or the Seednet name. Results were generic private F1 hybrid listings unrelated to this variety (e.g., https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/f1-hybrid-brinjal-seeds-23541045788.html). A Seednet portal search was not run (search budget used).

RECOMMENDED STATES

No independent confirmation found in the search results; the only field context found is SKUAST-J trial material in the Jammu study above -- https://www.genresj.org/index.php/grj/article/download/genresj.FRFO5243/204?inline=1

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: SHRESTHA (JRM-5), Mesta (kenaf/roselle)

Name note: the CSC name is SHRESTHA and the Seednet name is SHRESTHA(JRM-5). The only page that names this variety is a Vikaspedia Mesta page, and it uses "JRM-5 (Shrestha)", so it matches both names. Four searches were run, and the results were thin, so most headings are "No evidence found."

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches for SHRESTHA with Mesta/kenaf returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page on this variety's disease or pest reaction was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for variety-specific yield, maturity or trial data. The only related item is a general Mesta production guide that lists JRM-5 (Shrestha) among recommended varieties, with no agronomic figures for it: https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/commercial-crops/mesta

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found for SHRESTHA's parentage (HC-583 x Pure Green, as supplied in the record) being confirmed by a source. Search results did describe HC-583 as an older, widely grown Mesta variety (released 1963), which is context for one parent only and does not confirm the cross: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/398580799_Mesta_Kudlung_Production_Technology_of_Underutilized_Crop_in_Purulia_District

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No page named a lead breeder, developing institute or station for SHRESTHA. The Bangladesh kenaf/jute review results describe other institutes (BJRI) and other varieties, so they were discarded: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332251444_Varietal_Advances_of_Jute_Kenaf_and_Mesta_Crops_in_Bangladesh_A_Review

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No official institute, division or contact page for SHRESTHA was returned. The record's "institution: not specified" field is consistent with this.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper naming SHRESTHA was returned. The Bangladesh review and Purulia production-technology items are about other varieties or countries and were not attributed to this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No Seednet listing, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer page was returned for SHRESTHA(JRM-5). The Seednet portal was not reachable by search.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Partly supported. The Vikaspedia Mesta page lists JRM-5 (Shrestha) under Andhra Pradesh and Bihar: https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/commercial-crops/mesta. The record's other states (Orissa, Assam, Maharashtra, West Bengal) were not confirmed by any result.

Recommended next step: check the Seednet entry for SHRESTHA(JRM-5) directly, and the ICAR-CRIJAF (Barrackpore) or ICAR-IIJNRM annual reports for the CSC release minutes. Those are the likeliest sources for breeder, parentage and trial data, and they were not reachable with the search tool.

Name note: The CSC name is SUBHRA (OSC 207) and the Seednet name is Shubhra. The evidence below mostly uses the spellings "Subhra," "Shubra," and "SUBHRA (OSC 207)." Several official pages spell it differently, and some entries are ambiguous, so each line says which name the page uses.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for SUBHRA specifically. The DOD page's tolerance note (white seed; tolerant to leaf curl, phyllody, Macrophomina, Cercospora, capsule borer) sits in the row for Smarak, not Subhra. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Sesame.aspx
- The search returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or waterlogging data for Subhra.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for SUBHRA. The only Macrophomina tolerance statement in the DOD characters table is for Smarak (OSC 560), not Subhra. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A Rural Knowledge Bank table lists "Subhra (QSC 207)" with duration 85 days, average yield 9.0 q/ha, and oil content 52%. The name "QSC" appears to be a typo for OSC. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/oilseed-crops-in-odisha/sesame/
- The DOD characters table gives Subhra's yield potential as 800-900 kg/ha and oil content as 48-52%, with OUAT as the releasing centre. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx
- The DOD variety page describes "Shubra" (2012, OUAT, 48-52% oil, 800-900 kg/ha) as golden-yellow, bold-seeded, with delayed shattering, synchronous maturity, and suitability for kharif and summer seasons. The DOD seed-colour description conflicts with the white-seeded note for SUBHRA on another DOD page, so this entry is unresolved. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Sesame.aspx
- No multi-location or field-trial results for SUBHRA were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No pedigree, parentage, marker, or QTL data for SUBHRA or Shubhra appeared. The parentage field is "Not specified" in the record.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

drought.details: No evidence found in the digest for drought tolerance in this variety. The ecology source describes suitability for irrigated and timely-sown conditions only, which is not a drought tolerance claim. The CSC record states that, owing to earliness, the variety escapes terminal moisture stress. This is an escape mechanism, not a tolerance finding, and the digest contains no source for it, so it is not used to assign a level.

heat.details: No evidence found in the digest for heat tolerance in this variety. The CSC record states that, owing to earliness, the variety escapes heat. This is recorded as an escape mechanism from early maturity and is not an independently sourced tolerance finding in the digest.

salinity.details: No evidence found for this variety. Salinity QTL results in the chickpea review concern other lines and were excluded.

flood.details: No evidence found for this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: moderately resistant, as listed by the institute's variety page. A PVS study on Zone-III B (Buxar) lists Shubhra (IPCK 2002-29) among chickpea varieties reported to have stable wilt resistance. Rust: one IIPR listing mentions tolerance to rust and wilt, but the sentence is not clearly tied to Shubhra, so rust resistance is not counted. pest_resistance.summary: Pod borer: the CSC record and one DPD table row state the variety is escaping pod borer. The DPD row layout is ambiguous, so this is not confirmed as resistance from the digest. No other pest resistance found in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Potential yield 20-22 q/ha (ICAR technologies page). Central release table: 22 q/ha. CSC record: average yield 2041 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the farmer-based and PVS evidence listed under field trials. Yield in multi-location AICRP trials beyond the reported entry: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for the Central Zone under irrigated and timely-sown conditions in the rabi season, per the CSC record and the ICAR technologies page. Suitable for normal sown conditions, similar to other kabuli chickpea varieties (CSC record). Recommended states per CSC record: Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Gujarat.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 104-108 days (CSC record). The ICAR technologies page gives duration 105-115 days, and the central release table gives 107 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Central release table: erect plant with light green foliage, large creamy white seed, 33 g per 100 seeds. ICAR technologies page: seed weight 34.0 g per 100 seeds. CSC record: tolerant to lodging and shattering, seed rate 80 kg/ha, very good quality grain, protein 21.8%, sugar 6.8%.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Central release table and AICRP chickpea report (2021-22): 22 q/ha, 107 days, Central Zone, irrigated. (2) Farmer trials at Fatehpur and Jalaun (UP), 2018-19: Shubhra and Ujjawal gave higher yields than RVG 202, and farmers preferred Shubhra as the best kabuli line. (3) Farmer-participatory (FPVS) trials in Uttar Pradesh: rated among the best-performing lines. (4) Zone-III B (Buxar) PVS: identified as promising for grain yield among kabuli genotypes. (5) Milling quality study: among kabuli varieties with better milling properties; soaks in about 1.5 hours with high dal recovery. Yield data from other multi-location trials: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY: Shubhra (IPCK 2002-29), Chickpea (kabuli)
Name note: The CSC/CVRC name is "Shubhra" and the Seednet name is "Shubhra (IPCK 2002-29)". The sources I found use "Shubhra (IPCK 2002-29)" or "IPCK 2002-29 (Shubhra)". One DPD table row reads "Shubra (IPCK 2004-29)", but IIPR assigns IPCK 2004-29 to Ujjawal, so I treat that row as a naming error and did not use it for this variety.
Parentage note: Your input says "L 114 X H 82-2". Every source I found says L 144 x H 82-2, so I used L 144. Please check this against the release minutes.
Searches run: 4 (release/agronomy; breeder/institute; research papers; seed availability). Seednet portal pages did not appear in any result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Moderately resistant to wilt, as listed by the institute's variety page -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity.html ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
Wilt resistance is also listed among several chickpea varieties, including Shubhra (IPCK 2002-29), that are reported to have stable wilt resistance (a PVS study on Zone-III B / Buxar) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338331526_Identification_of_suitable_chickpea_varieties_for_Zone-III_B_in_general_and_Buxar_in_particular_through_farmers'_participatory_varietal_selection_approach
Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found for this variety. The salinity QTL results in the chickpea review concern other lines, so I excluded them -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/268280312_Chickpea
Ecology: suitable for irrigated and timely-sown conditions (no stress tolerance claim beyond this) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/

DISEASE AND PEST
Wilt: moderately resistant (see above) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity.html
Pod borer: one DPD row for IPCK 2002-29 reads "escaping to pod borer", but the row layout is ambiguous, so I have not counted it as confirmed -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Rust: one IIPR listing mentions tolerance to rust and wilt, but the sentence is not clearly tied to Shubhra, so I have not counted it -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity.html
Resistance to Fusarium wilt or dry root rot specific to Shubhra: No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Potential yield 20-22 q/ha; duration 105-115 days; recommended for the Central Zone; irrigated and timely-sown; creamy white seed; seed weight 34.0 g/100 seeds; moderately resistant to wilt -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/
Central release table entry: yield 22 q/ha, 107 days, Central Zone, irrigated, erect plant with light green foliage, large white seed (33 g/100 seeds) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/268280312_Chickpea
AICRP chickpea report lists the same entry: L 144 x H 82-2, CZ, irrigated, 107 days, 22 q/ha -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
In 2018-19 farmer trials at Fatehpur and Jalaun (UP), Shubhra and Ujjawal gave higher yields than RVG 202; Shubhra was preferred by farmers as the best kabuli line -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372769233_Translational_Chickpea_Genomics_Consortium_to_Accelerate_Genetic_Gains_in_Chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L
Farmer-participatory (FPVS) trials in Uttar Pradesh rated Shubhra among the best-performing lines -- https://dx.doi.org/10.3390/plants10122583
Zone-III B (Buxar) PVS: Shubhra was identified as promising for grain yield among kabuli genotypes -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338331526_Identification_of_suitable_chickpea_varieties_for_Zone-III_B_in_general_and_Buxar_in_particular_through_farmers'_participatory_varietal_selection_approach
Milling quality: IPCK 2002-29 was among kabuli varieties with better milling properties; it soaks in about 1.5 hours and gives high dal recovery -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/74994/31515/189951
Yield in multi-location AICRP trials beyond the above: No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: L 144 x H 82-2 (your input says L 114; see the note above) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf ; https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/74994/31515/189951
Pedigree source: IIPR, Kanpur -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338331526_Identification_of_suitable_chickpea_varieties_for_Zone-III_B_in_general_and_Buxar_in_particular_through_farmers'_participatory_varietal_selection_approach
Breeding method: No evidence found for this variety (the pedigree entry only)
Breeding-line code: IPCK 2002-29 (IIPR institutional code) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity.html
QTL, markers, genome resources for this variety: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity.html ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
Lead breeder name for Shubhra: No evidence found. Chickpea breeders listed by IIPR (Yogesh Kumar, Srivastava, Uday Chand Jha, Biswajit Mandal, A.K. Srivastava, Abhishek Bohra) are not linked to this variety in any source, so I have not attributed Shubhra to them -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/cimprovment.html ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/cimprovment/
Station: IIPR headquarters, Kanpur (no separate station named) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/

A PVS study on Zone-III B (Buxar) lists Shubhra (IPCK 2002-29) among chickpea varieties reported to have stable wilt resistance. Rust: one IIPR listing mentions tolerance to rust and wilt, but the sentence is not clearly tied to Shubhra, so rust resistance is not counted. Fusarium wilt or dry root rot resistance specific to Shubhra: Not found in searched sources.

drought.details: No drought tolerance evidence found in the digest. The Odisha information sheet describes suitability for rainfed and irrigated shallow lowlands, which is an adaptation statement and not a drought-tolerance finding.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources.

salinity.details: Listed as tolerant to salinity in the Odisha information sheet. This rests on a single source and no mechanism or screening data were provided, so the level is provisional.

flood.details: Listed as tolerant to flood in the Odisha information sheet. The AP Seeds source lists submergence instead, and the wording differs between the two sources. Verify before citing. No mechanism data were provided.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial leaf blight (BLB): listed as tolerant by AP Seeds and the IIRR newsletter (2015), and as moderately resistant by the Odisha information sheet. A 2017-18 Bengaluru trial recorded grain discolouration of 15.93% for Amara against 40.68% for NLR 34449 and 14.78% for MTU 1010 (lowest in that trial); this is a grain quality observation, not a disease-resistance rating. The 2009 release note in the IIRR source is cited for the BLB tolerance claim.

pest_resistance.summary: Brown planthopper (BPH): listed as tolerant by AP Seeds and the IIRR newsletter (2015), and as moderately resistant by the Odisha information sheet. Gall midge (GM): moderately resistant per the Odisha information sheet only.

agronomic_details.yield: Potential yield 6.5 t/ha (Odisha information sheet). The IIRR newsletter describes high yield without a figure. Average yield is not specified in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources across environments. The IIRR newsletter describes the variety as high yielding and non-lodging.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to rainfed and irrigated shallow lowlands (Odisha information sheet). Grown across the Godavari zone of Andhra Pradesh, with more than 20,000 ha in each Godavari district in 2020-21 (AICRIP POS 2020-21). Odisha promotion is from a project sheet and is not a formal recommendation.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 115-120 days (Odisha information sheet). Described as long duration in the IIRR newsletter.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf, medium slender grain (Odisha information sheet). Non-lodging (IIRR newsletter).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Bengaluru 2017-18 trial: grain discolouration 15.93% for Amara, 40.68% for NLR 34449, 14.78% for MTU 1010 (lowest in trial). (2) Grown on more than 20,000 ha in each Godavari district in 2020-21 (AICRIP POS 2020-21). (3) Ranked among popular ANGRAU varieties at the 2021-22 Maruteru mega display. (4) Farmer preference in the Godavari zone: 38% of growers ranked it as most preferred. (5) Quality screening of 20 Andhra Pradesh varieties including Amara (Divya Prasanna Kumari et al., 2020); the digest does not report results from this study.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Amara (MTU 1064), rice. Seednet lookup under "Tamara" (BRINJAL).
Searches run: 4 of the 4 allowed. Seed availability had no dedicated search, so that heading rests on incidental hits only.

NAME NOTE: The release-minute name "Amara" (MTU 1064) matches rice sources. The Seednet name "Tamara" under BRINJAL matched no brinjal variety in any source found. The Seednet record itself was not reachable, so the crop mismatch is unresolved.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Evidence refers to Amara (MTU 1064).
Listed as tolerant to BPH, BLB and submergence -- https://apseeds.ap.gov.in/Website/Paddy.aspx
Listed as tolerant to flood and salinity -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/amara-mtu-1064-english.pdf
Flood tolerance listed at Odisha sheet is "flood" and AP Seeds lists "submergence"; the two sources differ in wording, so verify before citing.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Evidence refers to Amara (MTU 1064).
Moderately resistant to BPH, BLB and gall midge (GM) -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/amara-mtu-1064-english.pdf
Described as tolerant to BPH and BLB, with a 2009 release note -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
Grain discolouration in one 2017-18 Bengaluru trial: Amara 15.93%, against 40.68% in NLR 34449 (lowest was MTU 1010 at 14.78%) -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/8d1eb20d-bad5-45e9-9dbf-20c0995da267/content

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety has citable sources (TNAU documents, a journal manuscript, and a gazette notification for Tamil Nadu). However, no stress tolerance trait is documented for VMB-16-10 itself, since the drought, heat and salinity snippets belong to other crops or projects. The yield value is not visible, so the evidence is mainly about plant type (non-spiny, 118.6 cm height, 30.5 branches). It sits at the 'only yield/agronomic info, no stress' level. The citations might justify 60, but stress and yield evidence are too thin, so 40 is the conservative score. It is notified only for Tamil Nadu, with no Gujarat evaluation.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Non-spiny (spineless) brinjal; hybrid derivative; plant height 118.6 cm; 30.5 branches/plant; notified for Tamil Nadu (2022)

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: VMB-16-10 is a non-spiny brinjal hybrid derivative, apparently from TNAU and notified for Tamil Nadu in 2022. It is described as 118.6 cm tall with 30.5 branches per plant. No variety-specific stress tolerance, genetic marker, or commercial availability evidence was found, and the evidence quality is low.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Non-spiny brinjal hybrid derivative, 118.6 cm plant height and 30.5 branches/plant, notified for Tamil Nadu in 2022. Yield, maturity, parentage and season are not specified in the available data.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No documented drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety. The stress snippets in the search results concern other crops or separate projects. Disease and pest reaction tables exist in a yield performance paper, but their results were not retrieved. Its stress profile is therefore unconfirmed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VNR-218 (brinjal). Variety name and Seednet name are identical ("VNR-218"), so every search result below refers to both. Only four searches were allowed, so several headings have thin or no evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. -- none (searched within the four allowed queries; no source returned this)

DISEASE AND PEST
Described as resistant to bacterial wilt. -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/brinjal-hybrid-variety-vnr-218/
Commercial listings claim superior disease resistance, but these are marketing claims without trial data. -- https://www.amazon.in/Hybrid-Brinjal-Gardeing-Germination-Vegetable/dp/B0DCTHZ2WD

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Small, long-fruited hybrid. -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/brinjal-hybrid-variety-vnr-218/
Seed rate given as 150-200 g/ha; suitable for kharif and rabi sowing. -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/brinjal-hybrid-variety-vnr-218/
Maturity, yield and multi-location trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found (no parentage, pedigree or marker study was returned; parentage is "Not specified" in the record).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Source given as VNR Seeds Pvt. Ltd., Raipur, with 2012 as the year. -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/brinjal-hybrid-variety-vnr-218/
Commercial listings name VNR Seeds as manufacturer, country of origin India. -- https://www.amazon.in/Hybrid-Brinjal-Gardeing-Germination-Vegetable/dp/B0DCTHZ2WD
Lead breeder name and public-sector developing institute: No evidence found. The CSC record's "Not specified" institution is not contradicted, but it is also not confirmed. The product is presented as a private-sector F1 hybrid, so it may not have come through an ICAR or SAU programme.

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder name, role, email, phone or postal address: No evidence found. No VNR Seeds corporate or contact page was returned by the searches. No ICAR or institute contact page applies, since no public-sector developer was identified.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses or conference papers were returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY
A 10 g pack of "VNR 218 F1 Hybrid Brinjal Seeds" is listed by Amazon.in, but the listing is for a different seller and product page. -- https://www.amazon.in/Hybrid-Brinjal-Gardeing-Germination-Vegetable/dp/B0DCTHZ2WD
Another Amazon.in listing for a 10 g pack of "SEEDS Hybrid Brinjal VNR-218" is currently marked unavailable. -- https://www.amazon.in/SEEDS-Hybrid-Brinjal-VNR-218-Vegetable/dp/B0D6BMC7VS
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or Seednet availability: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
The CSC record lists Assam, West Bengal, Punjab, Jharkhand, Orissa, Portblair and the North Eastern Hill region. -- CSC release record as supplied in the task (no URL)
A secondary source lists only West Bengal and Assam. -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/brinjal-hybrid-variety-vnr-218/
These two lists disagree. Punjab, Jharkhand, Orissa, Port Blair and the NE Hill region have no supporting evidence from the searches.

Gaps to resolve: confirm the release notification on seednet.gov.in (the portal itself was not returned by search), find VNR Seeds' official contact page, and check KrishiKosh and AICRP vegetable reports for trial data.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release and cultivation in the State of Orissa, Jharkhand, West Bengal, North Eastern States, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh under rainfed/irrigated conditions. Medium maturity (115-120) days. Yield Pod 16 Q/hac
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: - Stem colour: Absent, - Flower: 5 Orange, - Streak colour: 6 Dark orange, - Peg pigmentation: Absent, - Pod beak: Slight, - Pod size: Medium, - Kernel nature: 2 seeded, - Constriction: 1 Absent,  - Reticulation: Slight with 4-5 prominent ribs ; 100 kernel wt. : 30-36 g.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Distinguishing morphological Characters: Erect growth habit, narrow elliptic leaves, stem & peg pigmentation absent, no or slight pod constriction with slight beak, Pod reticulation medium  with 4-5 promoinert ribs. - Leaf shape: 5 narrow Elliptic, - Leaf size: Medium, - Leaf Hairyness: 1 Glabrous on both sides, - Foliage colour: 3 Green, - Growth habit: 6 Erect, - Stem hairyness: 3 Sub-glaborous
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: This variety was bred under drought. It has been performing very well in AICRP Trials under Drought and has been promoted to AVT.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to PBND. For foliar diseases, in Zone-V, it is on par with GPBD-4 (Zonal chect) but superior to National check.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: This variety was found slightly superior to the checks with less damage by Leaf miner, Leaf hopper and Spodoptera. All varieties were similar for Thrips damage.

drought.details: A general agronomy blog states the variety has excellent drought tolerance and suits low-rainfall regions. The blog's authorship and the basis for the claim are not stated, so this is weak, unverified evidence. No ICAR, AICRP or peer-reviewed drought screening data specific to Vijetha was found in the digest. The ICGS-11 drought tolerance noted in the digest belongs to the parent and is not attributed to Vijetha.

A commercial kernel seller's trade listing claims resistance to various pests and diseases without naming them; this is weak commercial evidence and is not used as a basis for any level. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VIJETHA (R-2001-2) GROUNDNUT: EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC name is "Vijetha" and the Seednet name is "Vijetha (R 2001-2)". Searches used both, and the sources below mostly give "Vijetha (R 2001-2)" or "R-2001-2". No seednet.gov.in page was returned, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- A general agronomy blog says this variety has excellent drought tolerance and suits low-rainfall regions; the page's authorship and the basis for the claim are not stated. -- https://agriculture.institute/agriculture-fundamentals/groundnut-cultivation-practices-varieties/
- The same blog says it shows good resistance to foliar diseases, without naming the pathogens. -- https://agriculture.institute/agriculture-fundamentals/groundnut-cultivation-practices-varieties/
- No heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The Directorate of Oilseed Development variety table says the variety is resistant to PBND (peanut bud necrosis disease). -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx (http://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx)
- A trade listing says it is resistant to various pests and diseases, without naming them. This is a commercial kernel seller, so it is weak evidence. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/r-2001-2-vijetha-peanuts-2851679669712.html
- No peer-reviewed or ICAR screening data for leaf spot, rust, or aflatoxin was found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The variety's yield potential is listed as 1600 kg/ha. -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
- The DOD table lists 1600 and 47 without column labels. The 47 is unexplained and may be a maturity or a pod-yield value. -- http://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx
- The DOD page describes it as suitable for kharif, and also says it is recommended for rabi-summer. The two seasons conflict. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- A Tamil Nadu farmer-participatory varietal selection trial tested R 2001-2 among Spanish bunch entries. The released variety from that trial was CO 7, not Vijetha. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244117_A_new_high_yielding_spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety
- Maturity is not confirmed. A generic blog gives 100–110 days, but the sentence's subject is unclear, so I did not use it.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage is ICGS-11 x ICG-4728, and the breeding method is listed as pedigree. The compendium also lists the same parentage for Ajeya (R 2001-3), so the parentage is shared with another variety. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
- A PLOS ONE SNP study names ICGV 93260 as "Vijetha" and reports it as the closest genotype to Ajeya, with genetic distance 0.4 from GPBD 4. The PLOS page shows an ICGS 11 x ICG 4728 pedigree row, but I could not confirm that row maps to ICGV 93260. -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0259883
- ICGS-11 is an ICRISAT-bred parent with reported end-of-season drought tolerance and bud necrosis tolerance. That information belongs to the parent, not to Vijetha. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/522/
- No QTL, marker-assisted, or genome-resource study specific to Vijetha was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by UAS, Raichur. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx (http://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx)
- Notified under S.O. 211(E) dated 29.01.2010. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
- The Gazette / Central release status is listed as "Central (kharif)" in a genetic enhancement table. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
- No lead breeder or scientist name was found for this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact was found.
- No UAS Raichur institute contact, email, phone, or address was found in the retrieved pages.
- Do not use the ICRISAT Patancheru address from the search results for this variety. It belongs to ICRISAT, not to the developing institute.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text. (2021). Assessment of the genetic diversity and population structure of groundnut germplasm collections using phenotypic traits and SNP markers: Implications for drought tolerance breeding. PLOS ONE -- https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0259883
- Authors not shown in retrieved text. Status of Adoption of Improved Groundnut Technologies in Odisha State. ICRISAT Open Access Repository (year not shown) -- https://oar.icrisat.org/11904/1/Groundnut%20Variety%20Adoption%20Sep%2028.pdf
- Authors not shown in retrieved text. A new high yielding Spanish bunch groundnut variety. ResearchGate (year not shown; PDF mentions CO 7 release) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244117_A_new_high_yielding_spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety
- Authors not shown in retrieved text. Genetic Enhancement of Groundnut: Current Status and Future Prospects. ResearchGate (year not shown; variety table lists UAS Raichur, 2010) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP report specific to Vijetha was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found on Seednet, NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, or SAU seed sales. The search returned only commercial kernel and peanut-product listings. Those are not seed sources: https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/r-2001-2-vijetha-peanuts-2851679669712.html and https://www.exportersindia.com/product-detail/r-2001-2-vijetha-peanuts-9417738561.htm
- The ICAR-IIGR agronomy sheet lists Vijetha among seed options for West Bengal and the NEH region, but it does not give a supplier. -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/agro-1.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Notified list for Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Release-table area of adoption: West Bengal, Orissa, Jharkhand, Assam (Zone-IV), southern Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kalpatharu (IND 125S), Coconut

Name note: "variety_name" is Kalpatharu and "seednet_variety_name" is Kalpatharu (IND 125S). The evidence below refers to the CPCRI/AICRP variety Kalpatharu, which AICRP documents also call accession IND 125S. My searches did not query the Seednet portal directly, so I found no Seednet-specific page.

Discarded results: Amazon, Flipkart and Green View listings for "Kalpatharu coconut" plants; Kalpatharu Coconut Producer Company Ltd (Tumkur, Karnataka, a private firm); Sri Ganesh Kalpatharu Industries (Udupi); Kalpataru Products. These are different companies or products and are not used as evidence for this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Relatively tolerant to drought, and listed as adapted to water-deficit regions -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269876228_ALL_INDIA_CO-ORDINATED_RESEARCH_PROJECT_ON_PALMS
- Named among varieties relatively tolerant to moisture stress (with Chandra Kalpa, Kalpa Mitra, Kalpa Dhenu and Kera Keralam) -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/100_Years_of_Scientific_Excellence.pdf
- No evidence found for flood, submergence, salinity or heat tolerance specific to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The Coconut Board newsletter gives an average disease index for palms of this variety, but the figure was not legible in the retrieved text -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- No evidence found for specific resistance to root (wilt), eriophyid mite or other pests. Kalparaksha and Kalpasree are the varieties described as root-wilt tolerant, not Kalpatharu -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/100_Years_of_Scientific_Excellence.pdf
- Kalpa Haritha is described as having lower eriophyid mite incidence, so that trait does not apply to Kalpatharu -- https://cpcri.icar.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- CPCRI reports about 116 nuts per palm per year under rainfed conditions and copra content of 176 g -- https://cpcri.icar.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
- AICRP recommendation text reports 15,750 nuts/ha, copra output of 2.7 t/ha (15.48 kg/palm/year), and oil content of 67.2% -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269876228_ALL_INDIA_CO-ORDINATED_RESEARCH_PROJECT_ON_PALMS
- Another table gives 20,300 nuts/ha, copra 35 q/ha and oil 25 q/ha. This conflicts with the AICRP figure, and the source does not state its trial basis -- https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/name-of-variety-salient-features_24.html
- Coconut Board table lists a yield of 20,709 with 3.64 (units not stated) -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- Ball copra variety, with minimal spoilage and higher ball-copra recovery -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/100_Years_of_Scientific_Excellence.pdf
- Copra from this variety has about 47.8% lauric acid, and nuts germinate early -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- Multi-location trial data beyond the AICRP recommendation: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Selection from the Tiptur Tall accession, so tall habit -- https://ccari.res.in/dss/coconute.html ; https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/name-of-variety-salient-features_24.html
- Breeding method: selection from a germplasm accession; breeding-line code IND 125S -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269876228_ALL_INDIA_CO-ORDINATED_RESEARCH_PROJECT_ON_PALMS
- Parentage: no evidence found beyond the Tiptur Tall origin. The 2015 record lists parentage as Unknown, and the source does not contradict that.
- QTL, marker, or genome resources for this variety: No evidence found. CPCRI mentions a whole-genome sequencing initiative for coconut generally, not for this variety -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/100_Years_of_Scientific_Excellence.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-CPCRI (Kasaragod), with TNAU also named as co-developer in one list -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/coconut-breeding/55986443 (secondary source) ; https://cpcri.icar.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
- The AICRP palms recommendation for Kalpatharu is linked to the TNAU Coconut Research Station, Aliyarnagar, Coimbatore -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269876228_ALL_INDIA_CO-ORDINATED_RESEARCH_PROJECT_ON_PALMS

drought.details: No drought tolerance evidence found. The digest notes suitability for rainfed cultivation, but this is a cultivation suitability statement, not a measured tolerance result.

heat.details: No heat tolerance data found for this variety.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance evidence found in searched sources.

flood.details: No flood tolerance evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderate resistance to late leaf spot and rust is reported for BSG 0912 / BSR 2. Both sources describe moderate resistance only. No other diseases were reported in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: No confirmed pest resistance. A ResearchGate figure titled 'Reaction of Groundnut culture BSG 0912 against insects under field' exists, but the retrieved text gives no result, so field insect reaction is not found in searched sources. A Legume Research paper states that both table-type forms (VRI 10 and BSR 2 are named) are vulnerable to storage insects, but it does not clearly attribute this to BSR 2 alone; this is treated as unconfirmed.

agronomic_details.yield: Rainfed average yield 2222 kg/ha. Irrigated average yield 2360 kg/ha. The CSC record gives an average yield of 1200.00 to 1500.00 Kg/Ha, which the digest does not address and which differs from the trial figures.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability analysis was reported beyond rainfed and irrigated trial averages.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to rainfed and irrigated conditions (TNAU). The paper states suitability for all groundnut-growing districts of Tamil Nadu. A TNAU Scientific Workers Conference document lists BSR 2 (2019) among groundnut varieties with 105 days duration for Kharif and Rabi seasons. The TNAU page lists seasons from Chithiraipattam through Vaigasipattam (multiple seasons).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 115 To 120Days (CSC record). The TNAU page and the TNAU Scientific Workers Conference document give a duration of 105-110 days (105 days in the SWC document).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Spanish bunch growth habit. Table-purpose variety (Legume Research paper). Shelling outturn 70.2%, 100-kernel weight 41.0 g (rainfed trial data).
agronomic_details.field_trials: Rainfed trials: average yield 2222 kg/ha, about 5.9% above VRI 8 (2099 kg/ha), 18.3% above CO 7 and 19.1% above VRI(Gn) 6. Irrigated trials: average yield 2360 kg/ha, with gains of 15.5% over VRI 8, 14.5% over CO 7 and 22.9% over VRI(Gn) 6. Quality data: shelling outturn 70.2%, 100-kernel weight 41.0 g, oil content 45.01%. Thiruvarur evaluation (Legume Research): oil content 45% (lowest among table-purpose varieties tested) and 100-kernel weight 44 g. Sensory suitability reported for peanut butter, chutney powder and masala peanut.

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No QTL or marker-assisted studies specific to BSR 2 were found. Two F2 populations derived from BSR 2 (BSR 2 x GPBD 4 and BSR 2 x TMV 2) were studied for variability and path analysis; no QTL effects were reported.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderate resistance to late leaf spot and rust is reported for BSG 0912 / BSR 2, not drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. -- https://www.academia.edu/142999069/A_new_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety_BSR_2
- Suitability for both rainfed and irrigated cultivation is stated, but no drought or heat tolerance data were found for this variety. -- https://agris.fao.org/search/en/providers/122436/records/675acd4e0ce2cede71d18e81
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to late leaf spot and rust. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20BSR%202.html
- Pest reaction: a ResearchGate figure titled "Reaction of Groundnut culture BSG 0912 against insects under field" exists, but the retrieved text gives no result. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Morphological-Description-of-Groundnut-culture-BSG-0912_tbl2_338773637
- Storage insect susceptibility: a Legume Research paper says both table-type forms (VRI 10 and BSR 2 are named) are vulnerable to storage insects, but it does not clearly attribute this to BSR 2 alone. Treat as unconfirmed. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5318
- Seednet / other names: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Released 2019; Spanish bunch growth habit; duration 105-110 days; suited to rainfed and irrigated conditions. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20BSR%202.html
- Rainfed average yield 2222 kg/ha, about 5.9% above VRI 8 (2099 kg/ha), 18.3% above CO 7 and 19.1% above VRI(Gn) 6. -- https://agris.fao.org/search/en/providers/122436/records/675acd4e0ce2cede71d18e81
- Irrigated average yield 2360 kg/ha, with 15.5%, 14.5% and 22.9% gains over VRI 8, CO 7 and VRI(Gn) 6. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338773637_A_new_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety_BSR_2
- Shelling outturn 70.2%, 100-kernel weight 41.0 g, oil content 45.01%. -- https://agris.fao.org/search/en/providers/122436/records/675acd4e0ce2cede71d18e81
- Lowest oil content (45%) among table-purpose varieties tested in Thiruvarur, with 100-kernel weight of 44 g. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5318
- Sensory suitability for peanut butter, chutney powder and masala peanut. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5318
- Season list: Chithiraipattam through Vaigasipattam (multiple seasons). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20BSR%202.html

GENETICS AND QTL
- Cross derivative of VRI 2 × TVG 0004 (Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338773637_A_new_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety_BSR_2
- TNAU page gives parentage as VR12 × TVG 0004, which appears to be a typo for VRI 2. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20BSR%202.html
- Parentage conflict: the input record says "selection from a sample collected from Mathura district of Uttar Pradesh." Neither TNAU nor the journal paper supports this; it is probably a Brassica (brown sarson) record and does not describe this groundnut variety.
- F2 populations from BSR 2 × GPBD 4 and BSR 2 × TMV 2 were studied for variability and path analysis. -- https://horizonepublishing.com/journals/index.php/PST/article/view/5241
- QTL or marker-assisted studies specific to BSR 2: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338773637_A_new_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety_BSR_2
- Lead authors: K.N. Ganesan and Kulandaivelu Ganesamurthy, both at TNAU. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338773637_A_new_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety_BSR_2

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: BS 279 (variety_name) / BS-2 (seednet_variety_name), crop recorded as cotton, Seednet crop "BROWN SARSON"

Searches run (4): "BS 279 cotton variety"; "BS 279 brown sarson variety OUAT"; "BS-2 brown sarson variety Odisha"; "OUAT Regional Research and Technology Transfer Station brown sarson BS 279 released 2020 Odisha".

Crop conflict: the only page that names BS 279 places it in cotton, not brown sarson. Nothing I found links BS 279 or BS-2 to brown sarson, so the Seednet crop label is unsupported by the evidence. Results for "brown sarson" pages describe the crop in general and were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for BS 279 or BS-2.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data for BS 279 or BS-2 was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Brown sarson agronomy pages (e.g., The treatments comprising of 3 planting densities, 3 nitrogen levels and 2 phosphorus levels were replicated thrice using factorial randomized block design. -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020.v9.i5.12301/effect-of-planting-density-on-brown-sarson-brassica-campestris-var-brown-sarson-under-different-levels-of-nitrogen-and-phosphorus-in-mid-hills-of-himachal-pradesh) name no BS 279 or BS-2 and were discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No marker, QTL or genetic study names BS 279 or BS-2.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Partial. The OUAT research-stations page states that Cotton variety 'BS 279' has been released for Odisha by State Variety Release Committee during the year 2019-20. -- https://ouat.nic.in/research_stations. The page does not name the breeder or the station that developed the variety. The developing institution is therefore Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology (OUAT), station not confirmed. The record's "Regional Research and Technology Transfer Station" is not tied to a named station by any source found. No breeder name was found. The Mathura parentage claim was not found in any source.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. Institute-level contact found, not confirmed as the developing station: Associate Director of Research, RRTTS (CZ), OUAT, Bhubaneswar-751003, Odisha, India; Email: rrtts.bhubaneswar@ouat.ac.in; Mobile: 9437130700 -- https://ouat.ac.in/research_stations/regional-reaearch-and-technology-transfer-station-bhubaneswar-khordha/. Another OUAT station (Chiplima, Sambalpur) lists its own contact, which is not linked to this variety: https://ouat.ac.in/research_stations/regional-reaearch-and-technology-transfer-station-chipilima-sambalpur/

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, thesis, AICRP report or conference item names BS 279 or BS-2. The brown sarson papers returned (e.g., Rao, T.S. (1970). Heterosis for oil content in brown sarson (Brassica campestris var. Sarson). Euphytica -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01902929) do not mention BS 279 and were excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The OUAT station page notes stations are involved in production and distribution of quality seeds (https://ouat.ac.in/research_stations/regional-reaearch-and-technology-transfer-station-bhubaneswar-khordha/), but no source confirms BS 279 seed is sold or where.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Odisha. Source: https://ouat.nic.in/research_stations (state release for Odisha, 2019-20, as cited above). This differs from the record's release date of 2020-11-09 and was issued by the State Variety Release Committee, not a Central (CSC) notification. No CSC notification was found.

Summary of gaps: the record's crop (brown sarson in Seednet vs. cotton in the release minutes), the BS-2 name, the Mathura origin, and the release year need verification against the State Variety Release Committee minutes and the Seednet portal entry.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Evidence refers to: Shalimar Sarsaon-2 / SS-2 (variety_name). No evidence found for Seednet name "Shalimar Sarson - 1" here; sources treat SS-1 as a separate variety.
- Tolerance to biotic and abiotic stresses is claimed for SS-2 in general terms, with no named stress, trial data, or method -- https://www.greaterkashmir.com/opinion/revolutionising-oilseed-farming-in-jk/
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood, and submergence: No evidence found specific to this variety. The only drought data is a 19.2% rainfed yield gain for SS-2 in J&K, which is an AICRP yield figure, not a stress-tolerance rating -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest reaction for SS-2. The Shalimar Sarsaon-3 (KBS-3) row in the AICRP table is for a different variety and was excluded -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Seed yield about 12 to 15 quintals/ha, per a KVK-linked progressive farmer and a SKUAST-K statement in news coverage (SS2) -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuasts-high-yield-mustard-variety-ss2-profitable-farmers/
- Yield potential of about 15 quintals/ha, with suitability for rice-based systems, cited for SS-2 by SKUAST-K -- https://www.greaterkashmir.com/opinion/revolutionising-oilseed-farming-in-jk/
- SS-1, SS-2 and SS-3 are grouped together at 16 to 17 quintals/ha, so this is a series figure, not SS-2 alone -- https://kashmirreader.com/2024/04/10/revolutionizing-oilseed-farming-in-jk-skuast-kashmirs-innovations-and-impact/
- AICRP-linked rainfed trial: 19.2% yield improvement from Shalimar sarson 2 in J&K over the check -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
- Field use: front-line and cluster demonstrations in Pulwama, 2022-23 onward, about 150 ha reported under FLD/CFLD in one year -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuasts-high-yield-mustard-variety-ss2-profitable-farmers/
- Maturity days: No evidence found.
- Parentage (Gulchin x NRCB 16): No evidence found. Gulchin appears only as KOS-101 in a history piece, not as SS-2's parent -- https://www.greaterkashmir.com/opinion/revolutionising-oilseed-farming-in-jk/

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL, marker, or genetic-stock study for SS-2 was returned. A ResearchGate result on yellow-seeded brown sarson lines involved Gulchin and KOS-1 but not SS-2, so it was excluded -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318836621_Effect_of_planting_method_and_nutrient_management_practices_on_seed_yield_of_brown_sarson_Brassica_rapa_L

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology, Kashmir (SKUAST-K), Shalimar, Srinagar -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/
- Breeder or lead scientist names: No evidence found. The breeding programme is credited to SKUAST-K, with no named breeder for SS-2 -- https://kashmirreader.com/2024/04/10/revolutionizing-oilseed-farming-in-jk-skuast-kashmirs-innovations-and-impact/
- Station: Mountain Research Centre for Field Crops (MRCFC) is cited for SKUAST-K variety development, but SS-2 is not explicitly linked to it -- https://www.greaterkashmir.com/business/skuast-ks-khudwani-centre-marks-sarson-day-pushes-oilseed-self-sufficiency-drive
- Dr Javeed Mugloo, Chief Scientist and Head, KVK Malangpora, is named for SS2 demonstrations, but not as breeder -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuasts-high-yield-mustard-variety-ss2-profitable-farmers/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute page: https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/ (no email, phone, or postal address extracted from the search snippets)
- Dr Javeed Mugloo, Chief Scientist and Head, KVK Malangpora (name and role only; no email or phone found) -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuasts-high-yield-mustard-variety-ss2-profitable-farmers/
- Official email, phone and postal address of the SKUAST-K Shalimar division: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated (2021). Project Coordinator's Report (2020-21), AICRP on Rapeseed-Mustard, DRMR, Bharatpur. Report -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper naming SS-2 was found. Two ResearchGate papers were excluded because they concern SS-1 ("Shalimar brown sarson1") or other lines, not SS-2.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- SKUAST-K has seen rising demand for SS-2 from the rabi 2022-23 season -- https://www.greaterkashmir.com/opinion/revolutionising-oilseed-farming-in-jk/
- University seed chain: SKUAST-K with the J&K Department of Agriculture runs breeder-to-foundation-to-certified seed production -- https://www.greaterkashmir.com/opinion/revolutionising-oilseed-farming-in-jk/
- Free seed distribution through KVK Malangpora FLD/CFLD, with farmer-to-farmer seed multiplication -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuasts-high-yield-mustard-variety-ss2-profitable-farmers/
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, or private dealer listing for SS-2: No evidence found. A DesiKheti mustard page is generic and does not name SS-2, so it was excluded -- https://www.desikheti.com/pages/buy-mustard-seeds-in-jammu-and-kashmir-online

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Jammu and Kashmir. Confirmed by the AICRP report row for "Shalimar Sarsaon-2 ... Jammu and Kashmir" -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
- Consistent with SS2 cultivation in Pulwama district, J&K -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuasts-high-yield-mustard-variety-ss2-profitable-farmers/

Notes on names and gaps:
- The release-year value (2019-06-01) is not confirmed by any search result. The AICRP table gives the notification entry as 5.9.19 for Shalimar Sarsaon-2 (KBS-49) -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
- The Seednet name "Shalimar Sarson - 1" conflicts with the SS-2 evidence. Kashmir sources list SS-1 and SS-2 as separate varieties, so the Seednet record should be checked against the portal before use.
- The Gulchin x NRCB 16 parentage remains unverified.

drought.details: Shalimar Sarson-1 appears in Brown sarson lists in AICRP Rapeseed-Mustard Annual Group Meeting proceedings alongside a statement that 'these genotypes highly tolerant to drought' with seed yield reduction of 20% or less. The snippet does not explicitly confirm that Shalimar Sarson-1 is one of those tolerant genotypes, so the drought rating cannot be verified from the search results. Brown sarson is also listed among varieties in a 2014 Rajya Sabha document that calls for short-duration and drought-tolerant varieties, but this does not attribute drought tolerance to the variety.

heat.details: Search results report heat tolerance for other entries (for example, Vijay Mustard 2 rated highly tolerant to terminal heat stress). No result links terminal heat tolerance to Shalimar Sarson-1 directly. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GK 3150 (maize, Ganga Kaveri, A0202011)

RELEASE/NOTIFICATION: Listed as a private-sector maize entry notified 27.03.2018 under notification 1379(E), recommended for Rajasthan, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh, rabi season, normal maturity. The notification number and date match the release date in the input record. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/

BREEDER/INSTITUTION CONFLICT: The same IIMR cultivar page lists GK 3150 under JKAgrigenetics Limited, Hyderabad, rather than Ganga Kaveri. A second entry on the same page lists "GK 3150" under Ganga Kaveri Seeds Pvt Limited with a 30-03-2017 date, notification 1007 E, recommended for Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh, rabi, normal. This points to either two different entries under the same name or a data error, and needs checking against the official notification before the breeder field is relied on. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ ; https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ (same page, 2017 entry)

RECOMMENDED STATES: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh (matches input). The company's own product page instead lists Andhra Pradesh as the suitable state for GK-3150, which conflicts with the notified recommendation. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ ; https://gangakaveri-website.webflow.io/

COMPANY DESCRIPTION (unverified marketing claims): The company describes GK-3150 as over 12 feet tall with strong stalks, no lodging, and high grain and green fodder yield. These are not independent trial results. -- https://gangakaveri-website.webflow.io/

DROUGHT: No evidence found specific to GK 3150.

HEAT: No evidence found specific to GK 3150.

SALINITY: No evidence found specific to GK 3150.

FLOOD/SUBMERGENCE: No evidence found specific to GK 3150.

ABIOTIC STRESS (portfolio level only): The company says its maize breeding aims at single-cross hybrids tolerant to biotic and abiotic stresses. This is a general company statement, not a GK 3150 trial result. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/maize-seeds-10565569848.html

DISEASE RESISTANCE (portfolio level only): The company's maize listings describe some hybrids as tolerant to leaf blights and PFSR (pink/purple-type stalk rot wording as given in the source). The listing does not name GK 3150 as one of them. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/maize-seeds-10565569848.html

PEST RESISTANCE: No evidence found specific to GK 3150.

QTL/MARKERS: No evidence found.

YIELD AND TRIALS: No evidence found from AICRP or peer-reviewed trials. The IIMR cultivar table shows a numeric value of 9.145 beside the GK 3150 entry, but the page does not label its unit or meaning, so it should not be read as a yield figure. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/

BREEDER/INSTITUTION (company background): Ganga Kaveri describes itself as having started seed production with the Rockefeller Foundation and National Seeds Corporation, and as having built a germplasm bank of inbreds from national and international institutes. This is general company background, not GK 3150 breeding records. -- https://gangakaveri-website.webflow.io/ ; https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/paddy-seeds-10565600873.html

SEED AVAILABILITY (NSC, State Seed Corporations, KVKs): No evidence found for GK 3150. Only retailer listings for a different hybrid, GK 3122, were found. -- https://agroshopy.com/index.php?route=product%2Fmanufacturer%2Finfo&manufacturer_id=14

SEARCH LIMITATIONS: Only two searches were run, so seednet.gov.in, AICRP maize annual reports and peer-reviewed papers were not checked directly for GK 3150.
