drought.details: Specific information regarding the drought tolerance of CoG 6 as a sugarcane variety is not available in the provided search results. The parentage 'Fodder Bajra CO 7 x Napier FD 459' suggests a fodder grass hybrid. General information in the search results indicates that Buffel grass (Cenchrus ciliaris), which is also known as Anjan grass and Pennisetum ciliare, is highly drought tolerant and well adapted to arid and semi-arid conditions. Napier grass (Pennisetum purpureum) is also recognized as a drought-tolerant forage cultivar.

heat.details: Specific information regarding the heat tolerance of CoG 6 as a sugarcane variety is not available in the provided search results. Abiotic stresses, including heat, affect plant growth. General information on Cenchrus species (Buffel grass) indicates strategies to combat multiple abiotic stresses such as heat. Plant responses to extreme temperatures are also noted in the context of genetic engineering for stress tolerance in Buffel grass.

salinity.details: Specific information regarding the salinity tolerance of CoG 6 as a sugarcane variety is not available in the provided search results. Buffel grass (Cenchrus ciliaris, Pennisetum ciliare), identified as a potential parent type, has intermediate salinity tolerance and some genotypes exhibit salt tolerance. Salts excretory structures like salt glands and microhairs are present in grasses growing in saline habitats, including Cenchrus species.

flood.details: Specific information regarding the flood tolerance of CoG 6 as a sugarcane variety is not available in the provided search results. Buffel grass (Cenchrus ciliaris), which may relate to the parentage, does not tolerate extended periods of flooding or water-logged soils.

drought.details: Drought tolerance is listed as a special feature of TNAU Groundnut CO 6. Farmers valued its ability to withstand drought during the post-flowering phase. In a KVK Kancheepuram on-farm trial, CO 6 showed no damage during a 20-25 day dry spell without rain. The evidence is qualitative (feature listing, farmer observation, one on-farm trial); no quantitative drought-tolerance index was found in the digest, so the level is rated medium rather than high.

disease_resistance.summary: Late leaf spot (LLS): resistant, per the DOD table entry for CO-6. Rust: resistant, per the same DOD table entry. Root rot: in the KVK Kancheepuram trial, CO 6 had a lower root rot incidence (3.5%) than the comparison varieties; this is a comparative incidence observation and is not explicitly recorded as resistance. Original variety record also lists resistance to late leaf spot.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest-resistance evidence for CO 6 specifically was found in the digest. The original variety record (not verified by the digest) lists less pest incidence for jassids, thrips and leaf miner; this is not a confirmed resistance finding from searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Rainfed pod yield 1914 kg/ha; highest recorded yield 3236 kg/ha; multi-location research-station trial 2342 kg/ha; KVK Kancheepuram 2850 kg/ha. Shelling out-turn 73.5%. Oil content 49.5% (TNAU) and 50-51% (DOD table).
agronomic_details.stability: Multi-location research-station trial yield 2342 kg/ha; KVK on-farm trial yield 2850 kg/ha. Consistent above-check performance was reported in these trials, but no formal stability analysis (e.g., AMMI or GGE) was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed; rainfed season May-June. Area of adoption noted as Namakkal district, Tamil Nadu.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: TAN TESTA; MEDIUM PROMINENT BEAK, MEDIUM CONSTRICTION AND MODERATE POD RETICULATION. Bunchy pods (TNAU release data). Virginia bunch type (ResearchGate paper).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) TNAU release data: rainfed pod yield 1914 kg/ha; highest recorded yield 3236 kg/ha; duration 125-130 days; shelling out-turn 73.5%; oil 49.5%; yield 29.4% above VRI (Gn) 7 and 77.1% above local check. (2) Multi-location research-station trial: yield 2342 kg/ha. (3) KVK Kancheepuram on-farm trial: pod yield 2850 kg/ha, 32 pods/plant, 49.4% above check TMV 7, gross Rs 85,500/ha, net Rs 59,500/ha; no damage in a 20-25 day dry spell; root rot incidence 3.5%. (4) DOD table: yield potential 1914 kg/ha and oil content 50-51%.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CO 6 (Groundnut)
Variety name searched: CO 6. Seednet name: CO 6 (both identical, so all evidence below refers to the name "CO 6"). The Seednet code A0402194 did not appear in any result, so no evidence links that code to a page.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought tolerance is listed as a special feature of TNAU Groundnut CO 6 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/2010/groundnut.pdf
- Farmers valued its ability to withstand drought during the post-flowering phase -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342082023_A_New_Virginia_Bunch_Groundnut_Variety_for_Tamil_Nadu
- In a KVK Kancheepuram on-farm trial, CO 6 showed no damage during a 20–25 day dry spell without rain -- https://indianjournals.com/article/jkv-5-1-015

DISEASE AND PEST
- The DOD notified-varieties table records CO-6 as resistant to late leaf spot (LLS) and rust -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- In the KVK Kancheepuram trial, CO 6 had lower root rot incidence (3.5%) than the comparison varieties -- https://indianjournals.com/article/jkv-5-1-015
- No pest-resistance evidence for CO 6 specifically was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration 125–130 days; rainfed season May–June; rainfed pod yield 1914 kg/ha; highest recorded yield 3236 kg/ha; shelling out-turn 73.5%; oil 49.5%; bunchy pods -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/2010/groundnut.pdf
- Yield was 29.4% above VRI (Gn) 7 and 77.1% above local check in the TNAU release data -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/2010/groundnut.pdf
- Multi-location research-station trial yield of 2342 kg/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342082023_A_New_Virginia_Bunch_Groundnut_Variety_for_Tamil_Nadu
- KVK Kancheepuram: 2850 kg/ha pod yield, 32 pods/plant, 49.4% above check TMV 7; gross Rs 85,500/ha, net Rs 59,500/ha -- https://indianjournals.com/article/jkv-5-1-015
- Oil content 50–51% and a 1914 kg/ha yield potential in the DOD table -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: derivative of the cross CS 9 / ICGS 5 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/2010/groundnut.pdf
- Breeding-line code: the ResearchGate paper identifies CO 6 as ICGV 87846 (Virginia bunch) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342082023_A_New_Virginia_Bunch_Groundnut_Variety_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Breeding method, QTL/marker studies and genome resources specific to CO 6: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: TNAU, Coimbatore (DOD table) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found in any retrieved page.
- TNAU's crop-improvement release listing covers CO 6 (2010 release) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/2010/groundnut.pdf
- Release-year discrepancy: TNAU lists 2010; the DOD table gives 2012 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.
- Institute-level contact (email, phone, postal address): No evidence found. The only institute reference is the TNAU agritech portal, https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/2010/groundnut.pdf, which contains no contact details.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not confirmed). A New Virginia Bunch Groundnut Variety for Tamil Nadu. ResearchGate preprint/PDF -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342082023_A_New_Virginia_Bunch_Groundnut_Variety_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not confirmed). Evaluation of High Yielding Groundnut Varieties for North Eastern Zone of Tamil Nadu. Journal of KVK (Indian Journals) -- https://indianjournals.com/article/jkv-5-1-015
- Other results in the search were about other varieties or other groundnut research and were excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for CO 6 seed from NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, TNAU seed sales or private dealers. The only seed-related results concerned other varieties (TNAU Tindivanam breeder seed table, which does not list CO 6 seed) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/crop-improvement/

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Tamil Nadu: the DOD state-wise list of notified groundnut varieties includes CO-6 for Tamil Nadu -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Area of adoption noted as Namakkal district, Tamil Nadu -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/2010/groundnut.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: BAIF Bajra-5 (CSC minutes name "BAIF Bajra- 5"; Seednet name "BAIF BAJRA-5"; the evidence below refers to the same pearl millet fodder variety under both names. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search.)

RECOMMENDED STATES
Pearl millet varieties BAIF Bajra-5 and BAIF Bajra-6 were notified and released by the Government of India as suitable for cultivation in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. -- https://baif.org.in/baif-evolved-new-fodder-varieties
Release/notification date: BAIF's own timeline gives the notification as July 13, 2022, which differs from the 2022-06-17 release date in the request. -- https://baif.org.in/who-we-are/baif-timeline
AICRP trial listing shows BAIF Bajra-5 as a multicut summer variety, 2021-22, from BAIF Urulikanchan, for Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384978222_Souvenir_National_Group_Meet_Kharif_and_Rabi_2024_Published_by_BAU_Ranchi_and_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for BAIF Bajra-5 specifically. The only drought-tolerance wording found (BAIF Bajra Seeds product page) names no variety and was discarded as not specific to this variety. -- https://baifagro.com/products/baif-bajra-seeds

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for BAIF Bajra-5. The disease-resistance wording on the BAIF Bajra Seeds page is generic and names no variety, so it was discarded. -- https://baifagro.com/products/baif-bajra-seeds

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
BAIF forage programme document describes BAIF Bajra-5 as a summer multicut type: very tall, erect, thick-stemmed, light green foliage, broad long leaves, no pubescence, non-lodging, crude protein 9-10%, average yield 85-95 t/ha. -- https://baif.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Forage-Research-Programme-2022.pdf
AICRP-FC&U souvenir lists BAIF Bajra-5 as a multicut summer entry in the 2021-22 trial series at BAIF Urulikanchan. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384978222_Souvenir_National_Group_Meet_Kharif_and_Rabi_2024_Published_by_BAU_Ranchi_and_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization
Multi-location yield data for BAIF Bajra-5 beyond the forage programme's average yield: not found. -- https://igfri.org.in/AICRPonFFC.aspx (centre network only; no Bajra-5 data)

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No pedigree/parentage or QTL/marker study naming BAIF Bajra-5 was found (parentage is "Not specified" in the request). Search returned only unrelated bajra-napier and BAIF Bajra-1 material, which was discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: BAIF Development Research Foundation (NGO, Pune, Maharashtra), with breeder seed of BAIF Bajra-5 produced under its programme. -- https://baif.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/BAIF-Annual-Report-2023-24.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
BAIF Bajra-6 (variety_name) / BAIF BAJRA-6 (seednet_variety_name). The two names differ only in capitalisation, and all evidence below refers to the same "BAIF Bajra-6" label. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned nothing that names BAIF Bajra-6 and reports drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. A BAIF product page describes drought tolerance for "BAIF Bajra Seeds", which is a different product name, so I excluded it. -- https://baifagro.com/products/baif-bajra-seeds (excluded, different name)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The only disease-resistance claim (downy mildew and ergot) is on the "BAIF Bajra Seeds" product page, which does not name BAIF Bajra-6, so I excluded it. -- https://baifagro.com/products/baif-bajra-seeds (excluded, different name)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
BAIF Bajra-6 is described as a summer multicut forage variety that is very tall and erect in habit, from BAIF's forage research programme document (the text is truncated, so the rest of the description was not retrieved) -- https://baif.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Forage-Research-Programme-2022.pdf
BAIF Bajra-6 appears as a multicut summer entry from Urulikanchan (Pune) in the 2024 AICRP on Forage Crops and Utilization national group meet souvenir, with the trial listed under Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384978222_Souvenir_National_Group_Meet_Kharif_and_Rabi_2024_Published_by_BAU_Ranchi_and_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization
BAIF Bajra-6 is listed as a multicut summer entry in the AICRP on Forage Crops five-year (2019-2023) report -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382887644_Fodder_Crops_Technologies_A_Five_Years_2019-2023_Journey_of_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization
No yield figures specific to BAIF Bajra-6 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The only BAIF bajra entry in the multi-environment fodder paper is "Baif bajra 1", which is a different variety, so I excluded it. -- https://doi.org/10.3390/plants15071034 (excluded, different variety)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: BAIF Development Research Foundation (Urulikanchan, Pune, Maharashtra). The Ministry of Agriculture's notification of BAIF Bajra-5 and BAIF Bajra-6 for Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh is reported by BAIF -- https://baif.org.in/baif-evolved-new-fodder-varieties
Lead breeder name: No evidence found for BAIF Bajra-6 specifically. The BAIF Central Research Station page says BAIF scientists developed the multicut bajra BAIF Bajra-1 (a different variety), so it does not name the breeder of Bajra-6 -- https://baif.org.in/what-we-do/central-research-station (excluded as breeder source)
Station: BAIF Central Research Station, Uruli Kanchan, Pune (227 ha) is the technology development centre that BAIF reports for this work -- https://baif.org.in/what-we-do/central-research-station
Breeding network: BAIF's entries appear in the AICRP on Forage Crops and Utilization (ICAR) programme -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384978222_Souvenir_National_Group_Meet_Kharif_and_Rabi_2024_Published_by_BAU_Ranchi_and_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization

Institute-level only (no breeder contact found). Centre head named on the CRS page: Dr. Jayant Khadse (role: head of BAIF Central Research Station, Urulikanchan). PUBLICATIONS

BAIF (2022). Forage Research Programme 2022 (forage crop varieties/hybrids). BAIF programme document describing BAIF Bajra-6 -- https://baif.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Forage-Research-Programme-2022.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NDFB-3 (CSC variety name) / NDFB-3 (Seednet name); variety code Narendra Chara Bajra-3; crop: pearl millet (bajra) fodder

Name note: The CSC name and the Seednet name are both NDFB-3, so every finding below refers to the same name. The variety code Narendra Chara Bajra-3 also appears in the sources and was treated as the same variety.

Search scope: Four searches were run. Two of them returned mostly unrelated results, so several headings below are "No evidence found."

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The only trait recorded for NDFB-3 is "high palatable." The salinity-tolerance and single-cut descriptions in the AICRP table belong to NDFB-2 (Narendra Chara Bajra-2), a different variety, and were discarded. -- http://aicrponforagecrops.res.in/index.php/en/variety-information/38-cultivated-kharif-forages/bajra/73-bajra

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for NDFB-3. Disease and pest resistance statements in the results concern Giant Bajra and other hybrids, and were discarded. -- https://www.jntbexim.com/product.php?url=bajra (discarded, other variety)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
NDFB-3 is listed as a single-cut system in the forage variety database entry. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020
NDUAT lists NDFB-3 among its forage bajra releases and in its research highlights under Bajra (Forage) with NDFB-2. -- https://nduat.org/Doc/Crop-Varieties-Developed-by-NDUAT.pdf ; https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf
No yield figures for NDFB-3 were found. The yield values in the AICRP-linked results refer to other varieties (NDFB-11, Anand Forage Bajra-3) and were discarded. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf (discarded, other varieties)

GENETICS AND QTL
The forage variety database records the pedigree as a selection from NDFB-202, using mass selection, and propagation by seed. This conflicts with the "Not specified" parentage in the record and should be checked before use. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020
No QTL or marker studies for NDFB-3 were found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381665344_Pearl_millet_a_promising_fodder_crop_for_changing_climate_a_review (general review only; not NDFB-3 specific)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: NDUA&T (Narendra Deva University of Agriculture & Technology), Faizabad. Later named Acharya Narendra Deva University of Agriculture & Technology (NDUAT), Kumarganj, Ayodhya. -- http://aicrponforagecrops.res.in/index.php/en/variety-information/38-cultivated-kharif-forages/bajra/73-bajra ; https://www.nduat.org/
Release year in the AICRP table: 2010. This differs from the 2011-06-28 date in the CSC record. -- http://aicrponforagecrops.res.in/index.php/en/variety-information/38-cultivated-kharif-forages/bajra/73-bajra
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.
Local origin of the material: Local collection from Saidpur, Ghazipur, U.P., per the forage database. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact was found. Institute-level information only:
Institution: Acharya Narendra Deva University of Agriculture & Technology (NDUAT), Kumarganj, Ayodhya 224 229 (Directorate of Research address as printed in the research report). -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/researchreport3.pdf
Website: https://www.nduat.org/ (institute site; an NDUAT page lists a "New Bajra Variety-Narendra Chara Bajra-3 NDFB-3" document, but no email or phone was in the retrieved text). -- https://www.nduat.org/
Email and phone: No evidence found in the retrieved text. Check the NDUAT contact page directly.

PUBLICATIONS
Database of Forage Crop Varieties: 2020. Entry for NDFB-3 / Narendra Chara Bajra-3 (NDFB-3) with pedigree, breeding method and crop data. Authors and editors not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020
No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, KrishiKosh record, or AICRP annual report specifically on NDFB-3 was found. The papers returned are about other pearl millet materials (brown midrib, hybrids, general fodder) and were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The retrieved sellers (Amazon listings, Shada Agri, USA Seeds, Neera Seeds) sell generic or other hybrid bajra and do not name NDFB-3. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, NDUAT or dealer listing for NDFB-3 was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Orissa, Jharkhand and West Bengal. The AICRP table says "Uttar Pradesh"; the CSC record says "Eastern Uttar Pradesh." The narrower CSC wording is what the record uses. -- http://aicrponforagecrops.res.in/index.php/en/variety-information/38-cultivated-kharif-forages/bajra/73-bajra

EVIDENCE DIGEST: PCB 166 (bajra/pearl millet, Seednet name PCB 164, code FBL 4), Punjab Agricultural University

Search budget: 4 web_search queries were run (PCB 166 variety; PCB 164 bajra fodder variety; PCB 166 breeder; PCB 164 bajra FBL 4 research). The fourth returned unrelated results, and no query was run for seed availability because the 4-search limit was reached.

Name note: The evidence below refers to PCB 166 unless stated otherwise. The Seednet name PCB 164 belongs to an older PAU composite, released in 2003 (80-day maturity, about 15 q/acre grain, tolerant to downy mildew). It is not the same variety as PCB 166, so no PCB 164 trait data is attributed to PCB 166 here. Release-date note: the input gives 2022-10-26, but the PAU announcement is dated 08-03-2022 and lists PCB 166 among eight varieties recommended for Punjab. The 26 October date could not be verified.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found for PCB 166. The PAU kharif package listing describes it as tolerant to all major pearl millet diseases, which is a disease statement, not a stress statement. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- PAU lists PCB 166 as tolerant to all the major diseases of pearl millet. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=6340 ; https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- No pest-resistance data was found for PCB 166. No specific downy mildew or ergot rating was found for PCB 166 in these results.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Dual-purpose composite, tall (about 281 cm), long broad leaves, more tillers, late maturing (about 89 days to 50 percent flowering, per PAU). -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=6340
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Yield: about 282 q/acre green fodder (PAU release notice) and about 16.3 q/acre grain (PAU kharif package). The kharif package gives a maturity range that is garbled in the text ("42 124 days"), so maturity should be checked against the original PDF. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=6340 ; https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- PAU's 2022 annual report lists PCB 166 under the North West and South Zone entries for bajra. This confirms the zone entry but gives no trial numbers. -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage was found. The input states "Not specified", and no QTL or marker study was found in these searches.

drought.details: The variety is resistant to moisture stresses and tolerant to drought, requiring minimal water. It withstands adverse agroclimatic conditions.

heat.details: Tolerant to high temperatures.

salinity.details: Tolerant to salt stress.

flood.details: Bajra, as a crop, does not tolerate water-logging; therefore, standing rainwater should be avoided.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to downy mildew and other biotic stresses. It exhibits moderate resistance to smut, red leaf spot, and zonate leaf spot disease.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to shoot fly and less susceptible to top borer.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported fodder yields include 585.2 q/ha, 234 q green fodder, and 31197.2 kg/ha (311.972 q/ha). Grain yields reported are 12.8 q and 32.1 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Suitable for all bajra growing areas of Punjab and is noted for its ability to withstand adverse agroclimatic conditions, indicating good stability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: A quick-growing, dual-purpose composite variety suitable for grain and fodder production. It is adapted to all bajra growing areas of Punjab, and can also be cultivated in regions like Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu due to its stress tolerance. Conflicting reports describe it as both 'early maturing' and 'late maturing'.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: A dual-purpose composite variety known for good quality stover and fodder, and very good popping quality. It is tolerant to lodging and is considered a hardy fodder crop.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Yield performance has been compared against check varieties, with PCB 165 showing a fodder yield of 585.2 q/ha compared to 535.4 q/ha for a check. Another variety, PCB 166, showed superiority over PCB 165 in green fodder yield by 12.3%.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Parentage involves chain crossing of 8 elite phenotypically superior lines. No specific genetic markers (e.g., SNP, SSR) directly associated with PCB 165 were specified in the provided results.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs for PCB 165 were identified in the provided search results.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: No specific molecular mechanisms (genes or pathways) for PCB 165 were identified in the provided search results.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for TSFB 17-7 or Telangana Fodder Bajra 1. -- none

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The CGIAR leaf-spot and blight resistance statement refers to the 2020 TSFB 15-4 and TSFB 15-8 releases, not TSFB 17-7, so I did not attribute it here. -- https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/rising-fodder-shortage-prompts-release-of-two-pearl-millet-varieties-with-superior-and-higher-forage-in-south-india/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Performance of TSFB 17-7 and TSFB 18-1 against national and zonal checks (2019-2021) is charted in an ICRISAT press release, but the retrieved text gives no yield values. -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/two-pearl-millet-varieties-with-superior-forage-yields-released-in-india
TSFB 17-7 is described as a single-cut pearl millet variety for the rainy season (maturity and yield figures not stated). -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/two-pearl-millet-varieties-with-superior-forage-yields-released-in-india
Single-cut listing for TSFB 17-7, released 2021 by PJTSAU, Hyderabad, with recommended states Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka (release year conflicts with the 2022 CVRC date). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382887644_Fodder_Crops_Technologies_A_Five_Years_2019-2023_Journey_of_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization

GENETICS AND QTL
Developed from ICRISAT pearl millet breeding material in collaboration with PJTSAU (this is the only origin statement found; parentage is not specified). -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/two-pearl-millet-varieties-with-superior-forage-yields-released-in-india
No QTL, marker or genomic study for TSFB 17-7 was found. Recurrent-selection and SSR studies returned in the search concern TSFB 15-4, TSFB 15-8 or unrelated germplasm and were discarded. -- none

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU), Hyderabad, in collaboration with ICRISAT. -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/two-pearl-millet-varieties-with-superior-forage-yields-released-in-india
Release listing: "Telangana Fodder Bajra 1 (TSFB 17-7)", released 2022, CVRC, in the Fodder Bajra table, with no station name given. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/
Breeder name: No named breeder for TSFB 17-7 was found. Dr T Shashikala (PJTSAU Forage Breeder) and Dr SK Gupta (ICRISAT Pearl Millet Breeder) are named only for TSFB 15-4 and TSFB 15-8, so they are not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/rising-fodder-shortage-prompts-release-of-two-pearl-millet-varieties-with-superior-and-higher-forage-in-south-india/
Institution naming: the PJTSAU page spells it "Professor Jayashankar Telangana Agricultural University". -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute website: www.pjtsau.edu.in (https://pjtsau.edu.in/index.html), as listed on the FAO AGRIS record. -- https://www.fao.org/agris/zh/node/124619
Headquarters location: Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, Telangana (institute-level; no postal address or PIN for the forage programme was found). -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professor_Jayashankar_Telangana_State_Agricultural_University
Official email and phone: not found in any retrieved page. No breeder-level contact found.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not stated in retrieved text (2023). Fodder Crops Technologies: A Five Years (2019-2023) Journey of AICRP on Forage Crops and Utilization. AICRP on Forage Crops and Utilization report -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382887644_Fodder_Crops_Technologies_A_Five_Years_2019-2023_Journey_of_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization
No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper specifically on TSFB 17-7 was found. The Pharma Innovation Journal 2021 forage pearl millet trial and the Shashikala forage-resources paper do not name this variety, so they were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The search returned only private listings for other fodder bajra products (VitaGraze, Nitya Vikas, Iagrifarm, Sonal, Pahuja) and a PJTSAU seed-production table with no TSFB 17-7 row. None of these were attributed to this variety. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/fodder-bajra-vitagraze-seed-17507828312.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Telangana, as stated for TSFB 17-7 in the ICRISAT release. -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/two-pearl-millet-varieties-with-superior-forage-yields-released-in-india
The AICRP listing adds Andhra Pradesh, which conflicts with the three-state input. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382887644_Fodder_Crops_Technologies_A_Five_Years_2019-2023_Journey_of_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization

NAME NOTE
CSC minutes name ("variety_name"): Telangana Fodder Bajra 1 (TSFB 17-7), per the PJTSAU release table. Seednet name ("seednet_variety_name", TELANGANA FODDER BAJRA (TSFB 17-7)): the Seednet page was not retrieved; evidence for the Seednet string is the same PJTSAU and ICRISAT pages naming "TSFB 17-7". -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to leaf spot and blight, as stated in the ICRISAT Asia Governing Board April 2021 crop-breeding slide, which describes TSFB 15-8 and TSFB 15-4 as forage varieties resistant to these diseases with higher green and dry fodder yields than checks. No disease data beyond this statement was found, and the slide does not quantify the level of resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No pest data (shoot fly, stem borer, downy mildew, head miner) specific to TSFB 15-8 was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Kharif 2021, AICRP on Forage Crops, ARI Rajendranagar (Hyderabad): green fodder 769.8 q/ha, dry fodder 191.7 q/ha, 6.0% crude protein, highest among varieties tested. A related ResearchGate record reports 821.1 q/ha green and 198.4 q/ha dry. The ICAR Indian Farming (January 2023) entry lists green fodder 420 and dry fodder 86 (units as printed). The digest notes the 420/86 figures conflict with the Telangana trial yields, likely due to different seasons, locations and cutting systems.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability analysis was found; results come from individual trials in Telangana and Punjab.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended at 120 kg N/ha with three cuts for southern Telangana. Adaptation to low soil fertility is claimed in one Telangana study. The Pusa study describes TSFB 15-8 as a viable substitute for BAIF bajra-1. The ICAR entry lists it as a single-cut variety, which conflicts with the three-cut recommendation.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Single-cut type, per the forage variety database entry and the ICAR Indian Farming (January 2023) entry. The Telangana study recommends three cuts, which conflicts with the single-cut classification. Crude protein 6.0% (Telangana 2021) and 8.3% (Punjab 2018).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Kharif 2021, AICRP on Forage Crops, ARI Rajendranagar, Hyderabad: highest green (769.8 q/ha) and dry (191.7 q/ha) fodder yield among varieties tested, 6.0% crude protein; recommended 120 kg N/ha with three cuts for southern Telangana. (2) Related ResearchGate record: 821.1 q/ha green and 198.4 q/ha dry yield, with higher net returns than TSFB 15-4. (3) Punjab Agricultural University, kharif 2018 (four genotypes, 0-90 kg N/ha): TSFB-15-8 had the lowest green and dry fodder yield but the highest crude protein (8.3%). (4) Punjab rainfed kharif: 120 kg N/ha under three cuts mentioned in the AICRP forage souvenir. (5) Pusa: described as a viable substitute for BAIF bajra-1 (Moti bajra was similar). (6) ICAR Indian Farming (January 2023): green 420 and dry 86 (units as printed).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
TSFB 15-8 (Pearl millet / Bajra, fodder). Both the CSC-minutes name and the Seednet name are "TSFB 15-8"; the PJTAU table also lists it as "Telangana Fodder Bajra 15-8". All evidence below refers to TSFB 15-8 unless stated.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- ICRISAT's April 2021 Governing Board crop-breeding slide says the forage varieties TSFB 15-4 and TSFB 15-8 are resistant to leaf spot and blight, with higher green and dry fodder yields than checks -- https://www.slideshare.net/icrisatsmco/asia-governing-board-april-2021
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance data for TSFB 15-8 was found. Adaptation to low soil fertility is claimed in one Telangana study -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2023/Nov/28-nov-23/2023_IJECC_109237/Revised-ms_IJECC_109237_v1.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Leaf spot and blight resistance, as stated in the ICRISAT slide above -- https://www.slideshare.net/icrisatsmco/asia-governing-board-april-2021
- No pest data (shoot fly, stem borer, downy mildew, head miner) specific to TSFB 15-8 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Kharif 2021, AICRP on Forage Crops, ARI Rajendranagar (Hyderabad): TSFB 15-8 gave the highest green fodder yield (769.8 q/ha) and dry fodder yield (191.7 q/ha) among the varieties tested, with 6.0% crude protein -- https://journalijecc.com/index.php/IJECC/article/view/3559
- The same study recommends TSFB 15-8 at 120 kg N/ha with three cuts for southern Telangana -- https://journalijecc.com/index.php/IJECC/article/view/3559
- A related ResearchGate record reports 821.1 q/ha green and 198.4 q/ha dry yield, with higher net returns than TSFB 15-4 -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/doc/Rev_IJECC_89755_Els_A.pdf
- Punjab Agricultural University, kharif 2018 (four genotypes, 0-90 kg N/ha): TSFB-15-8 had the lowest green and dry fodder yield but the highest crude protein (8.3%) -- https://forageresearch.in/influence-of-different-nitrogen-levels-on-growth-yield-and-quality-of-forage-pearl-millet-pennisetumglaucum-l-genotypes/
- Punjab rainfed kharif: TSFB 15-8 with 120 kg N/ha under three cuts is mentioned in the AICRP forage souvenir -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384978222_Souvenir_National_Group_Meet_Kharif_and_Rabi_2024_Published_by_BAU_Ranchi_and_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization
- At Pusa, TSFB 15-8 was described as a viable substitute for BAIF bajra-1 (Moti bajra was similar) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301355655_Forage_quality_water_use_and_nitrogen_utilization_efficiencies_of_pearl_millet_Pennisetum_americanum_L_grown_under_different_soil_moisture_and_nitrogen_levels
- ICAR Indian Farming (January 2023) lists TSFB 15-8 as a single-cut pearl millet variety, released 2020, with green fodder 420 and dry fodder 86 (units as printed) -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf
- Note: the 420/86 figures conflict with the Telangana trial yields above, which likely reflect different seasons, locations and cutting systems.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- A forage variety database entry headed TSFB 15-8 gives pedigree IP 22269, IP 15352, HTGP, breeding method recurrent selection, propagation through seed, single-cut type -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020
- Caveat: the entry is in a jumbled text extraction and sits beside other varieties' entries, so the pedigree attribution is unverified. The parentage field in the brief is "Not specified".
- No QTL, marker, GWAS or genome study on TSFB 15-8 was found.
- Discarded: the "Giant bajra x FD-473-1" pedigree and the Rahuri (MPKV) development claim (1987) belong to bajra-napier hybrids, not this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Prof. Jaishankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU, Hyderabad). The 2019 AICRP souvenir lists TSFB 15-8 as a single-cut variety released by PJTSAU for Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384978222_Souvenir_National_Group_Meet_Kharif_and_Rabi_2024_Published_by_BAU_Ranchi_and_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization
- The 2021 field trial was run at AICRP on Forage Crops and Utilization, ARI Rajendranagar, Hyderabad -- https://journalijecc.com/index.php/IJECC/article/view/3559
- No lead breeder or scientist name for TSFB 15-8 was found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact was found. The only institute-level page located is the PJTAU Director of Research page, https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/ . Its text lists the Director of Research, Prof. Balram Marathi, but no email, phone or address was shown in the captured content. Please verify the contact details on that page directly before use.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured (2023). Nitrogen levels and cutting management on fodder yield and nutritional quality in fodder pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum L.). International Journal of Environment and Climate Change -- https://journalijecc.com/index.php/IJECC/article/view/3559
- Maninder Kaur; Meenakshi Goyal (year not shown; kharif 2018 trial). Influence of different nitrogen levels on growth, yield and quality of forage pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum L.) genotypes. Punjab Agricultural University, Forage and Millet Section, journal not shown -- https://forageresearch.in/influence-of-different-nitrogen-levels-on-growth-yield-and-quality-of-forage-pearl-millet-pennisetumglaucum-l-genotypes/
- Authors not captured (year not shown). Green fodder yield and quality of dual purpose pearl millet varieties as influenced by cutting and nitrogen management. Journal not shown. Page text mixes results; verify before citing -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/337210042_GREEN_FODDER_YIELD_AND_QUALITY_OF_DUAL_PURPOSE_PEARL_MILLET_MILLET_PENNISETUM_GLAUCUM_L_VARIETIES_AS_INFLUENCED_BY_CUTTING_AND_NITROGEN_MANAGEMENT
- Authors not captured (2024). Souvenir, National Group Meet (Kharif and Rabi 2024). BAU Ranchi and AICRP on Forage Crops and Utilization -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384978222_Souvenir_National_Group_Meet_Kharif_and_Rabi_2024_Published_by_BAU_Ranchi_and_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization
- Authors not captured (year not shown). Database of Forage Crop Varieties: 2020. AICRP on Forage Crops (assumed; not confirmed) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020
- Authors not captured (2023). Indian Farming, January 2023. ICAR -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf
- Authors not captured (2021). Asia Governing Board, 98th ICRISAT meeting, crop breeding, pearl millet -- https://www.slideshare.net/icrisatsmco/asia-governing-board-april-2021
- Discarded: the ResearchGate Obeng et al. (US) and Joshi, Pankhaniya and Mohammadi (Gujarat) records show Telangana study text, so they cannot be attributed to TSFB 15-8 from those pages.
- No DOI or KrishiKosh thesis for TSFB 15-8 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- NDDB Annual Report 2022-23: breeder seed from ICAR and agricultural universities was supplied to 15 dairy cooperatives, and TSFB 15-8 and TSFB 15-4 (bajra) were brought into the seed multiplication chain as newly notified fodder varieties -- https://www.nddb.coop/sites/default/files/pdfs/NDDB_AR_2023_090124_Eng.pdf
- PJTAU Seed Research & Technology Centre table: bajra 9.20 q in 2023-24 (crop-level, not variety-specific) -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sale or private dealer listing for TSFB 15-8 was found. Dealer pages found were for other bajra varieties and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, per the 2019 AICRP souvenir -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384978222_Souvenir

STRESS TOLERANCE

- Balaji (CABBAGE, Seednet name): No evidence found. The only related page is a commercial F1 listing that describes vigorous plants but gives no stress data -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/welcome-balaji-cabbage-seeds

DISEASE AND PEST
- BALAJI (jatropha): No evidence found.
- Balaji (CABBAGE): No evidence found. Listing gives no resistance information -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/welcome-balaji-cabbage-seeds

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- BALAJI (jatropha): No evidence found for a variety-level trial. Species-level agronomy only -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/bio-fuels/Biofuel_jatropa.html
- Balaji (CABBAGE): Commercial seed-company listing gives maturity of 75-80 days, head weight of 2.0-2.5 kg, semi-flat bluish-green heads, and says it is an F1 hybrid. This is marketing data, not trial data -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/welcome-balaji-cabbage-seeds

GENETICS AND QTL
- BALAJI (jatropha): No evidence found. The Jatropha breeding study returned concerns CJH backcross clones from TNAU, not BALAJI -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9449966/

- BALAJI (jatropha): No breeder or developing institute found. Balaji Plantations of Shahjahanpur is a commercial nursery business, not a breeding programme -- https://www.indiamart.com/balaji-plantations/
- Balaji (CABBAGE): No ICAR, SAU or institute breeder found. Balaji Seeds (a private company) states that it releases cultivars, but names no breeder for a cabbage variety -- https://www.balajiseeds.in/ ; Balaji Agribiotech is a private hybrid-seed company -- http://www.balajiagribiotech.com/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Arka Krishna (CSC name) / Hare Krishna (Seednet name), Dolichos bean (Lablab purpureus)

Name note: The evidence below refers to Arka Krishna, the dolichos bean variety from ICAR-IIHR. Under the Seednet name "Hare Krishna" with crop "CABBAGE", the only hit was a private F1 cabbage hybrid, so it is not evidence for this variety. The Seednet portal produced no dolichos record for this name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Only the general pole-type description is given; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance is recorded for Arka Krishna. Low-moisture tolerance is attributed to other IIHR dolichos varieties (Arka Jay, Arka Vijay) -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties
- No evidence found for Arka Krishna-specific terminal moisture stress tolerance. The 2023 Legume Research paper refers to a released variety only in general terms, without naming Arka Krishna -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4418

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to Arka Krishna. Rust resistance is recorded for Arka Prasidhi, not Arka Krishna -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Arka Krishna is described as a pole type, photo-insensitive and early variety, with pods borne in clusters that are dark green, per the IIHR variety page -- https://www.iihr.res.in/dolichos-bean-arka-krishna
- Pod yield is reported at 30.0 t/ha over a 120-day duration. The "early" description and the 120-day duration are inconsistent and should be checked against the release notification -- https://www.iihr.res.in/dolichos-bean-arka-krishna
- No Arka Krishna-specific multi-location trial results found. The Telangana and Dharmapuri trial papers concern Arka Amogh and Arka Sambhram, not Arka Krishna -- https://www.academia.edu/164908507/Performance_Evaluation_of_Dolichos_Bean_Lablab_purpureus_L_Variety_Arka_Amogh_for_Growth_Yield_and_Economic_Traits_under_Semi_Arid_Agro_Ecosystems_of_Telangana ; http://www.plantarchives.org/SPL%20ISSUE%2020-2/611__3762-3765_.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: developed by pedigree selection from F7 generation of the cross IIHR 178 x Arka Swagath -- https://www.iihr.res.in/dolichos-bean-arka-krishna
- The PPV&FRA DUS guideline uses Arka Krishna as a reference for several descriptors (e.g., fresh seed colour, seed shape, pod pubescence). The per-character attributions in the extracted table are ambiguous -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/dolichosbeanguideline.pdf
- No QTL or marker study found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru -- https://www.iihr.res.in/dolichos-bean-arka-krishna ; https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-15/
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The IIHR page does not name the breeder.
- Division: Division of Vegetable Crops, IIHR (per a Plant Breeding scientist's slide deck on dolichos seed production; not confirmed as the Arka Krishna breeder) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/dolichos-seed-production/151052854

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. B.R. Raghu, Scientist (Plant Breeding), Division of Vegetable Crops, IIHR, Bangalore; email raghubr@iihr.res.in. Source is a slide deck, not an official directory, and he is not confirmed as the variety's breeder -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/dolichos-seed-production/151052854
- Institute website: iihr.res.in -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-15/
- Postal address, phone and official institute contact page: No evidence found in search results.

PUBLICATIONS
- No Arka Krishna-specific peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper was found in the searches.
- Related but not about Arka Krishna: Balaraju, S. & Ramesh, S. (2023). Identification of Indices for Empirical Selection of Dolichos Bean [Lablab purpureus (L.) Var. Lignosus] Genotypes for Tolerance to Terminal Moisture Stress. Legume Research 46(6): 695-699 -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4418
- Related but not about Arka Krishna: Mahesh, R.O. et al. (2019). Evaluation of dolichos bean genotypes. Journal of Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry 8(4): 1729-1732 -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue4/PartAC/8-4-269-407.pdf
- Related but not about Arka Krishna: Sharma, V.K. et al. (2025). Performance Evaluation of Dolichos Bean Variety 'Arka Amogh' under Semi-Arid Telangana. Journal of Scientific Research and Reports -- https://doi.org/10.9734/JSRR/2025/V31I123852

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for Arka Krishna seed from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales or private dealers.
- Seednet search under "Hare Krishna" returned only a private Tokita F1 cabbage hybrid and unrelated items -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/tokita-hare-krishna-cabbage-seeds
- The IIHR portal has an online seed portal entry for related varieties (Arka Vijay, Arka Jay), not confirmed for Arka Krishna -- https://www.iihr.res.in/indian-beandolichos-bean-lab-lab-purpureus-l-arka-vijay-0

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Karnataka, per IIHR (suitable for Karnataka) -- https://www.iihr.res.in/dolichos-bean-arka-krishna

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The hybrid has credible institutional citations: IARI annual reports, the seednet new-varieties list and review articles. It also has yield data (47.92 t/ha in trials) and maturity of 70-75 days. However, no stress trait is documented for this hybrid specifically, because the drought, heat, salt and submergence snippets refer to other genotypes or crops. There is no evidence of Gujarat suitability. This fits the '60: at least one citation, but weak on stress traits' tier. A score of 75 would need confirmed stress-trait evidence.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: CMS-based F1 hybrid (Pusa Hybrid-82). Dark green, waxy leaves. Flat, compact heads. Matures in 70-75 days. Trial yield about 47.9 t/ha.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: KTCBH-822 (Pusa Hybrid-82) is a CMS-based white cabbage F1 hybrid from ICAR-IARI Katrain. It has dark green, waxy leaves and compact flat heads, and it matures in 70-75 days with trial yields of about 47.9 t/ha. Institutional sources document its release and yield, but no stress tolerance, disease or pest resistance, or Gujarat suitability is confirmed for this hybrid.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: A CMS-based cabbage hybrid from IARI Katrain, with flat, compact heads and dark green waxy leaves. It matures in 70-75 days and yielded 47.92 t/ha in 2015-16 trials, above the check Pusa Cabbage Hybrid 1 (41.54 t/ha).
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No stress tolerance has been documented for this hybrid. The drought, heat, salt and submergence snippets refer to other genotypes or crops. No disease or pest data were found, and no genetic marker or QTL information exists.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Karan 5 (CSC name "Karan 5"; Co 0124; Seednet name "Karan"; crop sugarcane)

Searches run: 4 (within the 3–4 limit). Name note: the evidence below refers to "Karan 5 (Co 0124)" from the ICAR-SBI and PPVFRA lists. No search returned a Seednet portal record for "Karan" under sugarcane or cabbage, so the Seednet name and the CABBAGE crop label remain unverified. Results for "Karan" also matched other Karan-named varieties (Karan 1, 2, 4, 13), which I excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for Co 0124 specifically. A 2010–11 ICAR report mentions drought and salinity tolerance for unnamed lines, and the snippet does not clearly link that to Co 0124 -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for Co 0124 specifically. A ChiniMandi article describes an unnamed 2009 North West Zone variety with moderately resistant reaction to pathotypes cf7 and cf8, but it does not name Karan 5, so I did not attribute it -- https://www.chinimandi.com/icar-sbi-readies-to-release-three-disease-resistant-high-yield-sugarcane-varieties-in-2026-director/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No Co 0124-specific yield, maturity, or trial data found. The only mention is a truncated listing of "Co 0124 (Karan 5)" in a 2010–11 ICAR crop-improvement annual report -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The QTL papers retrieved concern other populations, such as Brazilian cultivars, CP clones, and Indian bi-parental crosses that do not include Co 0124 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00122-011-1748-8

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Co 0124 is listed among CVRC-released and notified varieties of ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute (SBI), Coimbatore -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/from-the-director-s-desk?id=363
  -- The ICAR-SBI Regional Centre Karnal states it developed Co 0124 among its recent early varieties -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=5563
  -- Breeder names for Co 0124: No evidence found. Dr. P. Govindaraj is named as ICAR-SBI institute director, not as a breeder of this variety -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/ag-tech-research-news/icar-sbi-breeds-three-disease-resistant-sugarcane-varieties-for-indias-cane-belt/
  -- Parentage: No evidence found. Year of release: No evidence found. Release year is blank in the input and was not found in the search results.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. No email, phone, or postal address for SBI or the Karnal centre appeared in the results. Institute-level pages: ICAR-SBI site -- https://sugarcane.res.in/ (also listed as sugarcane.icar.gov.in). Karnal Regional Centre page -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=5563. The SBI plant-breeding page has a "Contact Address" heading, but the address text is not in the retrieved content -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/plant-breeding/

PUBLICATIONS
DARE/ICAR (2011). Annual Report 2010–11, Crop Improvement (sugarcane section names "Co 0124 (Karan 5)", snippet truncated). DARE/ICAR Annual Report -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
  -- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, or KrishiKosh record specific to Co 0124 found. Journal of Sugarcane Research papers retrieved concern other varieties (Co 12029/Karan 13, Co 15002) and were excluded -- https://doaj.org/article/29241a90f42b4452b49c4d6d66772b16

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No Karan 5 seed source found (no NSC, state corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing). ICAR-SBI runs a seed portal and a farmers' participatory seed production programme, but these are institute-level and not variety-specific -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=11140. A general note says commercial seed usually follows formal notification by one to two seasons -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/ag-tech-research-news/icar-sbi-breeds-three-disease-resistant-sugarcane-varieties-for-indias-cane-belt/

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Co 0124 is listed for the North West Zone, with a zone table naming Rajasthan and Central and Western Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.nitiforstates.gov.in/public-assets/Policy/policy_files/TNG1660A000065.pdf. The NWZ listing also includes Co 0124 -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/plant-breeding/. The NWZ state coverage (Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttaranchal, Western and Central UP) is given in -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf. Uttar Pradesh policy requires state adoption of CVRC-notified varieties in their recommended zone -- https://www.etvbharat.com/en/bharat/sugarcane-farmers-approach-centre-seeking-clarification-on-notified-varieties-for-sowing-enn26022804888

drought.details: Co 0237 (Karan-8) is listed among sugarcane varieties suited to drought conditions and is described as an early maturity clone. The digest does not grade the level of drought tolerance and reports no drought trial data or physiological mechanism.

heat.details: No heat trial evidence for Co 0237 was found in the digest. Leaf-tip drying is reported as common in summer, but this is not attributed as a heat-tolerance result for the variety.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. No salinity evidence for Co 0237 was found. The only salinity-related hit was a generic paper on the variety list in the CO 11015 study, which concerns a different variety and is excluded.

flood.details: Co 0237 is reported as tolerant of waterlogging. The digest does not describe a flood trial or mechanism, and waterlogging tolerance is used here only as the closest available evidence for flood conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: Red rot: Co 0237 is rated moderately resistant to red rot, with the prevalent races noted (one source). The second source repeats the moderately resistant rating to the red rot pathogen. No evidence was found for smut, wilt or other diseases specific to Co 0237.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence was found for top borer or insect resistance specific to Co 0237.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield under normal condition is 71.33 ton/ha (cane). In AICRP trials in the North Western Zone, Co 0237 averaged 71.33 t/ha cane and 9.34 t/ha sugar.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The digest gives zone-level trial means only, with no multi-environment stability analysis.
agronomic_details.adaptation: North Western Zone (AICRP trials and ICAR-SBI North-West recommendation). Recommended for Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh (western and central). Release year note: the record lists 2011-06-28, but the sources say the clone was identified in 2010 by the AICRP varietal identification committee. No notification number was found. The release date needs checking against CVRC notifications.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not specified in digest. The digest describes Co 0237 as an early-maturing clone but gives no day count.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Free of spines and splits (per digest). Jaggery quality is rated A1 with a light yellow colour, and fibre is about 12.98%. Morphological details beyond these are Not specified.
agronomic_details.field_trials: AICRP North Western Zone trials: Co 0237 averaged 71.33 t/ha cane, 9.34 t/ha sugar and 18.78% juice sucrose. Checks were CoJ 64 (67.59 t/ha cane) and CoPant 84211 (66.84 t/ha cane). Within the zone, the clone ranked first for juice sucrose, fourth for sugar yield and fifth for cane yield. The AICRP varietal development table reports the same cane yield (71.33) and sucrose (18.78) figures and lists the clone as early-maturing, identified in 2010 for the North West Zone. No stress-specific trial results were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Karan 8 (variety_name) / Karan (seednet_variety_name), crop: sugarcane, variety code Co 0237

Name note: Every page I found that mentions Karan 8 does so as Co 0237 (Karan-8). None of the results came from the Seednet portal, so I cannot confirm that the Seednet record "Karan" refers to this clone. The Seednet crop field reads "CABBAGE", which does not match sugarcane. That field needs checking against the portal.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Co 0237 (Karan-8) is listed among sugarcane varieties suited to drought conditions, and is described as an early maturity clone. -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- Co 0237 is reported as tolerant of waterlogging. -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- Co 0237 is described as free of spines and splits, and leaf-tip drying is common in summer. -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- No salinity, flood or heat trial evidence for Co 0237 was found in these results. The only salinity-related hit was a generic paper on the variety list in the CO 11015 study (see PUBLICATIONS).

DISEASE AND PEST
- Co 0237 is rated moderately resistant to red rot, with the prevalent races noted. -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/
- Co 0237 is rated moderately resistant to the red rot pathogen. -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- No evidence found for smut, top borer, wilt or insect resistance specific to Co 0237.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- In AICRP trials in the North Western Zone, Co 0237 averaged 71.33 t/ha cane, 9.34 t/ha sugar and 18.78% juice sucrose, against checks CoJ 64 (67.59 t/ha) and CoPant 84211 (66.84 t/ha). -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/
- Within the zone, the clone ranked first for juice sucrose, fourth for sugar yield and fifth for cane yield. -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/
- The AICRP varietal development table lists Co 0237 as an early-maturing variety with the same cane yield (71.33) and sucrose (18.78) figures, identified in 2010 for the North West Zone. -- https://www.iisr.nic.in/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm
- Jaggery quality is rated A1 with a light yellow colour, and fibre is about 12.98%. -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/
- Release year: the record lists 2011-06-28, but the sources say the clone was identified in 2010 by the AICRP varietal identification committee. No notification number was found. The release date needs checking against CVRC notifications.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Co 0237 was selected from the progeny of the cross Co 93016 GC. -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/ (also https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/)
- This is a selection source, not a full pedigree. The record's parentage field ("Not specified") should be reviewed against the official notification. No QTL or marker study on Co 0237 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Co 0237 was bred at the Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Regional Centre, Karnal (Haryana), part of ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute (Coimbatore). -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/ ; https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/component/content/article?id=171

Name note: variety_name "Pusa Cabbage-1" and seednet_variety_name "Pusa Cabbage-1 (KGMR-1)" refer to the same hybrid. Every finding below uses both names, and I did not find separate evidence for either.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Prachi (HI 1563), wheat

NAME NOTE: The evidence below refers to "Pusa Prachi" / "HI 1563" (variety_name and variety_code). The Seednet name "Pusa Pakchoi-1" (listed under CABBAGE) returned no evidence. The only results were pak choi retailers in the UK and US, which were discarded.

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION (supporting line, no heading assigned)
Pusa Prachi (HI-1563) is listed in a Bihar notified-variety list with a date of 25/03/2011 and S.O. 632(E); the input release date is 2010-12-23, and the list's date column is not labelled -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
HI 1563 is listed among wheat varieties notified in India since 1965 by the CVRC sub-committee -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of HI 1563 / Pusa Prachi. The search returned only general IARI pages and other varieties (Pusa Basmati 1121, HD 3386, Pusa Malvi), which were discarded.

commercial_availability.seed_corporations: Not found. The report mentions seed production by IARI and a State Seed Corporation, but only for other crops such as hybrid PJHM-1.
commercial_availability.private_dealers: Not found

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety is documented as officially notified (2022) and as the first indigenous Pakchoi for the North Indian Plains. However, no stress or climate traits, no yield figures and no peer-reviewed citations were found. The sources are institutional reports, so the score falls between the 'minimal info' and 'only yield info' tiers. No Gujarat-specific adaptation evidence exists, and the variety is notified only for Delhi. It is not recommended for Gujarat without local trials.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: First indigenous Pakchoi variety (IARI); for North Indian Plains; notified for NCT of Delhi; suited to drip irrigation studies

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Pusa Pakchoi-1 is an IARI-developed Pakchoi variety, the first indigenous one for the North Indian Plains, and it was notified in 2022 for NCT of Delhi. No stress tolerance, disease or pest resistance, yield, maturity or molecular data were found, and the evidence consists only of institutional reports and a gazette notification. Evidence quality is low and Gujarat suitability is untested.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: IARI-bred Pakchoi (a non-heading Chinese cabbage type) notified in 2022 for Delhi and the North Indian Plains. Yield, maturity, parentage and morphology are not specified in the sources.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No variety-specific evidence of abiotic stress tolerance or biotic resistance was found. Drought, disease and resistance snippets in the results refer to other crops. The only related work is a drip irrigation and soil matric potential study.

drought.details: The abiotic-stress variety table in PMC7501393 lists CoOr 03151 (Sabita) under the SRS Nayagarh row as tolerant to drought and waterlogging. No level scale is given, so a graded level cannot be assigned. A sugarcane chapter table (ResearchGate 381880091) rates the variety moderately tolerant to drought, but the digest states that the row attribution is unclear (it may belong to the neighbouring Co 86249 row), so this rating is not used.

flood.details: The stress-tolerance table in PMC7501393 lists the variety as tolerant to waterlogging (see drought entry). This is recorded as waterlogging tolerance only; no level scale or mechanism is given, so the level is unknown.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistance to red rot and smut is reported in a sugarcane chapter table (ResearchGate 381880091), but the digest states that the row attribution to CoOr 03151 is unconfirmed and that no clean source or AICRP entry was retrieved. Red rot and smut reaction for Sabita is therefore not confirmed. No other disease resistance was found in searched sources.

I'll start with the first three searches in parallel, since they don't depend on each other.STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerant to drought and waterlogging, as listed for CoOr 03151 (Sabita) in the SRS Nayagarh row of an abiotic-stress variety table -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7501393/
Rated moderately tolerant to drought in a sugarcane chapter table, but the table layout makes it unclear whether this descriptor belongs to CoOr 03151 or the neighbouring Co 86249 row -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381880091_Sugarcane

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to red rot and smut in the same chapter table; the same row-attribution caveat applies -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381880091_Sugarcane
Red rot and smut reaction for CoOr 03151 (Sabita) is therefore not confirmed from a clean source; no AICRP entry for this variety was retrieved.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Identified in 2009 as an early-maturing selection; AICRP table lists CoOr 03151 with cane yield 105.28 (units as given in table) and release years 2009-2011 -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm
Described in an AICRP-linked review as spreading fast in the East Coast Zone -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
Odisha table lists CoOr 03151 (SABITA) with value 110.0 and code R; column headings are not in the retrieved text, so the meaning of these figures is unverified -- https://magazines.odisha.gov.in/Orissareview/2015/Jan/engpdf/104-107.pdf
Share of area reported as 18% in Odisha (AICRP-based review) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9012054/

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: a selection from the progeny of CoC 671 x Co 1148 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
No QTL or marker study for CoOr 03151 (Sabita) was found. The stress-responsive miRNA table in PMC7501393 names miRNAs for stress tolerance but does not link them to this variety's genotype; treat as no evidence.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing station: Sugarcane Research Station, Nayagarh (OUAT, Panipoila), an AICRP centre since 1983 -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/nayagarh.htm and https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/regularcentres.htm
Station-level linkage: the Tables page for stress tolerance attributes the CoOr 03151 (Sabita) entry to SRS Nayagarh -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7501393/
Named breeder for CoOr 03151 (Sabita): No evidence found. The station page names a sugarcane breeder and officer-in-charge, but does not tie him to this variety (see CONTACT DETAILS).
The "Co" prefix is the ICAR Sugarcane Breeding Institute naming convention, but no retrieved source names SBI Coimbatore as the developer of Sabita; do not assume it.

CONTACT DETAILS
Station contacts from the SRS Nayagarh page (station-level, not variety-specific) -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/nayagarh.htm
  Dr. Pramod Kumar Nayak, Sugarcane Breeder and Officer-In-Charge, Mob: 09937140810, pknpbg@gmail.com

  Ms. Swagatika Mohanty, Assistant Plant Pathologist, Mob: 09438639301, swagat.saroj@gmail.com
Station postal location: Sugarcane Research Station, Panipoila, 12 km from Nayagarh district headquarters, Odisha -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/nayagarh.htm
University-level contact (not station): Odisha University of Agriculture & Technology, Bhubaneswar-751003, Odisha; (0674)-2397970/2397818; registrar@ouat.ac.in; www.ouat.ac.in -- https://ouat.ac.in/commodity/seed-research-nayagarh-sugarcane/

PUBLICATIONS
Dutta, D., & Ghosh, K. (2024). Sugarcane. In Modern Crop Production Technology of Kharif Crops (Vol. I, Ch. 14, pp. 160-177). JAYA Publishing House. Lists CoOr 03151 (Sabita, 2011) for the East Coast Zone -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381880091_Sugarcane
Shukla, S. K., Zubair, A., Awasthi, S. K., & Pathak, A. D. (2018). AICRP technical publication-II: Sugarcane varieties identified by AICRP (S) in India. Lucknow: ICAR-IISR. Cited in a review that gives CoOr 03151 an 18% share in Odisha -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9012054/
Authors not shown (2020 or thereabouts, not confirmed). Forty Five Years of All India Coordinated Research Project on Sugarcane. Report, AICRP on Sugarcane, ICAR-IISR -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
Authors not shown. Current breeding and genomic approaches to enhance cane and sugar productivity under abiotic stress conditions (review, PMC7501393). Journal not shown in retrieved text -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7501393/
Note: the Co 15002 paper (Durai et al., 2021, J. Sugarcane Research, DOI 10.37580/JSR.2021.1.11.83-90) concerns a different clone and is excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No seed source for CoOr 03151 (Sabita) was retrieved from NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer pages. The seed-availability search was not run; the fourth search was used for contact details instead.

RECOMMENDED STATES
East Coast Zone; Odisha is named in the AICRP-based review and the chapter table -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9012054/ and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381880091_Sugarcane
The chapter table places CoOr 03151 (Sabita, 2011) in the East Coast Zone, listing Odisha, coastal Andhra Pradesh and coastal Tamil Nadu as its states -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381880091_S

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance in Arka Prasan (blackgram) or Arka Basant (capsicum). The digest reports no quantified drought data for any source retrieved. The Arka Prasan name in the evidence refers only to ridge gourd, and the Arka Basant evidence refers to capsicum, so neither applies to the blackgram record.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance. No abiotic stress data was retrieved for any variety named in the record.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance. No abiotic stress data was retrieved for any variety named in the record.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance. No abiotic stress data was retrieved for any variety named in the record.

disease_resistance.summary: Field tolerance of common leaf diseases is claimed for Arka Basant (capsicum, not blackgram) in a secondary commercial source; no quantified data were found. A possible triple resistance to powdery mildew, downy mildew and anthracnose appears on the IIHR variety list, but the text sits beside other entries and may belong to a different capsicum variety, so it is unconfirmed for Arka Basant. No blackgram disease resistance evidence was found for Arka Prasan.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for pest resistance, virus resistance or nematode resistance specific to Arka Prasan or Arka Basant.

agronomic_details.yield: No blackgram yield data found. For Arka Basant (capsicum, not the record's crop): IIHR bunch-type description gives yield potential of 40 t/ha and 36 kg/vine; an older slideshare summary gives 15 t/ha; technicalkisan gives 15-18 t/ha; an older release summary gives yield potential of 16 t/ha. These figures conflict across sources.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Arka Prasan / ARKA BASANT

NAME AND CROP MISMATCH (read first)
Blackgram: no evidence found. The "Arka Prasan" name in the CSC minutes appears only for ridge gourd, not blackgram. -- https://kvkariyalur.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/KVK-Ariyalur-TN-Annual-Report-2024.pdf (KVK Ariyalur, ridge gourd OFT); https://www.iihr.res.in/field-day-ridge-gourd-var-arka-prasan-organized-icar-iihr-panasachowdanahalli-village
The Arka Prasan ridge gourd variety is credited to IIHR Bengaluru, with a 2013 or 2016 release year given inconsistently in the KVK report. -- https://kvkariyalur.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/KVK-Ariyalur-Action-Plan-Detailed-Report-2024-25.pdf
The Seednet name ARKA BASANT refers to capsicum, and the evidence below for it is a different crop from the blackgram in the record. The evidence below refers to Arka Basant (capsicum), not to any blackgram variety. Parentage matches the capsicum record: "Improvement over IHR 225-1-1 (Var. Soroksan) followed by mass selection." -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties
Year of release: not found for Arka Basant in any source retrieved. The "NaT" value is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Field tolerance of common leaf diseases is claimed for Arka Basant, with no quantified drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found. -- https://technicalkisan.com/seeds/capsicum/arka-basant (secondary commercial site)
A possible "triple resistance" to powdery mildew, downy mildew and anthracnose appears on the IIHR variety list, but the text sits beside other entries and may belong to a different capsicum variety, so treat it as unconfirmed for Arka Basant. -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties
No evidence found for abiotic stress tolerance (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence).

DISEASE AND PEST
Field tolerance to common leaf diseases is the only disease claim found (see above). -- https://technicalkisan.com/seeds/capsicum/arka-basant
No evidence found for pest resistance, virus resistance or nematode resistance specific to Arka Basant.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity and yield figures conflict across sources:
- Harvest about 158-160 days from pruning; average bunch 410 g; TSS 20-21 °B; yield potential 40 t/ha and 36 kg/vine (IIHR bunch-type description). -- https://iihr.res.in/crop-wise
- Yield 15 t/ha in 180 days (older slideshare summary). -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/capsicum-varietal-wealth/193187274
- Yield 15-18 t/ha, rabi season, about 150-160 days, nursery seed rate 400-500 g/ha, spacing 60-75 cm by 45-60 cm. -- https://technicalkisan.com/seeds/capsicum/arka-basant
- Fruit weight 50-80 g, fruit erect, cream turning orange-red at maturity; yield potential 16 t/ha in 150 days (older release summary). -- https://www.slideshare.net/THANKLORD/varieties-of-capsicum
- Field-trial evidence: Arka Basant x IIHR-4096 showed good fruit length and earliness in a shadenet bell pepper hybrid study at IIHR. -- https://www.academia.edu/29284617/Evaluation_of_Varities_and_Hybrids_for_Yield_Attributes_in_Bell_Pepper_Capsicum_annuum_L_Under_Insect_Proof_Net_Cum_Shadenet
No blackgram agronomy or trial evidence found. Ridge gourd Arka Prasan OFT yielded 152.2 q/ha in Ariyalur (not the record's crop). -- https://kvkariyalur.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/KVK-Ariyalur-TN-Annual-Report-2024.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Ccs (capsanthin-capsorubin synthase) gene-specific marker polymorphism for red fruit colour, with Arka Basant among red-fruited lines at IIHR Bengaluru, 2013. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/314455223_Validation_of_Candidate_Gene_Specific_Markers_for_Ripe_Fruit_Colour_in_Bell_Pepper_Capsicum_annuumvar_grossum
No blackgram QTL or marker study linked to this variety found. The blackgram GWAS found (Punjab Agricultural University, 2022) covers a different panel and does not name this variety. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9310006/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru, Hesaraghatta Lake Post. -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties
Origin: selection from Hungarian 'Soroksari' via IIHR 225-1-1, released by IIHR Bengaluru. -- https://www.slideshare.net/THANKLORD/varieties-of-capsicum
Lead breeder name: No evidence found for any named breeder or scientist for Arka Basant or Arka Prasan.
Division: Vegetable Crops, IIHR (as described in an IIHR marker study). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/314455223_Validation_of_Candidate_Gene_Specific_Markers_for_Ripe_Fruit_Colour_in_Bell_Pepper_Capsicum_annuumvar_grossum

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level; no breeder contact found)
ICAR-IIHR Technology Management Unit (ITMU) -- email itmu@iihr.res.in; postal address Hesaraghatta Lake Post, Bengaluru 560 089; website http://www.iihr.res.in -- https://iihr.res.in/sites/default/files/varieties%20and%20technologies-english).pdf
IIHR institute headquarters: Bengaluru, Karnataka (no phone number found in retrieved text). -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Horticultural_Research
IIHR varieties page: https://iihr.res.in/varieties

PUBLICATIONS
Varsha V., Mishra S., Lingaiah H.B., Venugopalan R., Rao K.V., Kattegoudar J., Reddy K.M. (2021). Combining ability studies to develop superior hybrids in capsicum (Capsicum annuum var. grossum) (title truncated in source). Journal of Horticultural Sciences 16(2): 199-205 -- https://jhs.iihr.res.in/index.php/jhs/article/download/1080/908/7389 (Arka Basant is one of seven parents; Arka Basant shows good combining ability for plant height, days to flowering, and fruit numbers)
Rao and Reddy (2016), cited within a marker study; full author list not confirmed. Ccs gene marker validation for ripe fruit colour in bell pepper. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/314455223_Validation_of_Candidate_Gene_Specific_Markers_for_Ripe_Fruit_Colour_in_Bell_Pepper_Capsicum_annuumvar_grossum
No blackgram publications, KrishiKosh theses, or AICRP reports for Arka Prasan or Arka Basant found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
ICAR-IIHR Seed Portal -- https://seed.iihr.res.in/ (the seed portal lists capsicum hybrid seed; Arka Basant listing not confirmed on the retrieved page)
IIHR caution notice: Arka seeds are sold only through the seed portal, the ICAR-IIHR ATIC, and the Sanjay Nagar sales counter. -- https://www.iihr.res.in/caution-notice-icar-iihr-arka-seeds-and-planting-material
IIHR price list lists Arka Basant at 7000 (unit not stated). -- https://iihr.res.in/sites/default/files/varieties%20and%20technologies-english).pdf
No private dealer, KVK, or State Seed Corporation listing found for Arka Basant. No blackgram seed source for Arka Prasan found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Karnataka: not confirmed by any retrieved source; the institute is in Bengaluru, and Karnataka is the state named in the record. -- https://iihr.res.in/crop-wise
Tamil Nadu: Arka Basant appears in TNAU's capsicum variety list, which is not a formal recommendation. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_vegetables_capsicum_variety.html
No CSC/CVRC notification or state recommendation found for Arka Basant. For Arka Prasan (ridge gourd), Ariyalur district (Tamil Nadu) recommendation appears in a KVK report. -- https://kvkariyalur.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/KVK-Ariyalur-TN-Annual-Report-2024.pdf
