drought.details: No evidence found in the digest for drought tolerance in Arka Kamini (China aster). For the seednet record ARKA MOHINI (capsicum), no evidence was found for any abiotic stress tolerance. Record flagged as unresolved: the CSC name (aster) and Seednet name (capsicum) refer to different crops, and the parentage matches capsicum Arka Mohini.

heat.details: No evidence found in the digest for heat tolerance in Arka Kamini. No abiotic stress tolerance evidence found for ARKA MOHINI (capsicum).

salinity.details: No evidence found in the digest for salinity tolerance in Arka Kamini. No abiotic stress tolerance evidence found for ARKA MOHINI (capsicum).

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest for flood tolerance in Arka Kamini. No abiotic stress tolerance evidence found for ARKA MOHINI (capsicum).

disease_resistance.summary: Arka Kamini: No evidence found in the digest for disease resistance in Kamini itself. A 2019-era IIHR production slide deck attributes Alternaria leaf spot resistance to a different genotype, AAC-1, not to Kamini. ARKA MOHINI (capsicum): No evidence found for disease resistance. The bacterial wilt tolerance reported in the sources belongs to Arka Gaurav, not Mohini.

pest_resistance.summary: Arka Kamini: No evidence found in the digest for pest resistance. ARKA MOHINI (capsicum): No evidence found for pest resistance. The CSC record field 'pest_reaction' is listed as 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record value: 20000.00 to 25000.00 Kg/Ha. This value is not corroborated by any yield evidence for Arka Kamini in the digest, and the digest flags the record as unresolved. For ARKA MOHINI (capsicum), IIHR gives 16 t/ha (indeterminate type, one page) and 20 t/ha (determinate type, another page), and a seed yield of about 150 kg/ha is listed by a third-party source.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for Arka Kamini. Trial results vary by location and comparator (see field_trials), and no multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Arka Kamini: Popularised under the IIHR-ICRISAT Bhoo-Samrudhi project in four Karnataka districts. Recorded trial performance in a New Alluvial Zone of West Bengal (seed production) and a Kerala tropical-plains trial. The CSC record lists adaptation as 'Not specified', while the CSC recommended states are West Bengal, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu. The digest contains no evidence supporting the CSC recommended states beyond these trial locations.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Thick fleshed fruits, dark green, blocky fruits turning red on ripening. Fruit are pendunt, average fruit weight 180 -200 g. (CSC record. The digest contains no corroborating evidence for these traits in Arka Kamini.) Aster production slide deck: plant height about 60 cm, about 138 days to flower, about 50 flowers per plant, 6 cm flower diameter, about 8 days vase life. IIHR describes flowers as semi-double, deep pink, suited to garlands and cut flowers.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Chikkaballapur, Karnataka, IIHR-ICRISAT Bhoo-Samrudhi project: popularised in four Karnataka districts; a farmer reported early flowering and better colour and uniformity. (2) New Alluvial Zone of West Bengal seed-production trial: Kamini recorded about 61.4 flowers per plant, behind Arka Poornima. (3) Kerala tropical-plains trial: Kamini recorded about 16.27 flowers per plant, on par with several other genotypes. (4) 2024-25 Nagpur trial of Arka-series varieties: Arka Aadya gave the highest flower count; Kamini's rank was not reported in the excerpt. (5) Production slide deck metrics as listed under plant_characteristics (source does not specify trial location). No trial results were found for ARKA MOHINI beyond the capsicum descriptions listed under yield.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources for Arka Kamini. For ARKA MOHINI (capsicum), no marker study was found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No QTL evidence for Arka Kamini. For ARKA MOHINI, no QTL study was found; the combining-ability study cited is a crossing study, not a QTL study.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. The digest records the parentage of ARKA MOHINI (selection from Titan, and improvement over IIHR-214-1 followed by mass selection). The CSC parentage for the record (IHR 31-2-1-2, Titan followed by mass selection) matches capsicum Arka Mohini per the digest, not China aster Kamini.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Arka Kamini / Arka Mohini

NAME AND CROP MISMATCH: The CSC name "Arka Kamini" (aster) and the Seednet name "ARKA MOHINI" (capsicum) refer to different crops. The parentage given (IHR 31-2-1-2, Titan followed by mass selection) matches capsicum Arka Mohini, not China aster Kamini. The 2023 release year matches neither: IIHR's capsicum page says Arka Mohini was released in 1984 and 1986, and no release year for Kamini was found. Treat the record as unresolved until the CSC minutes are checked.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Arka Kamini (China aster): No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. -- https://www.iihr.res.in/performance-china-aster-cv-arka-kamini-chikkaballapur-under-icrisat-iihr-bhoo-samrudhi-project
ARKA MOHINI (capsicum): No evidence found for any abiotic stress tolerance. -- https://iihr.res.in/capsicum-arka-mohini-1

DISEASE AND PEST
Arka Kamini (China aster): No evidence found for Kamini itself. A 2019-era IIHR production slide deck attributes Alternaria leaf spot resistance to a different genotype, AAC-1, not to Kamini. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/china-aster-flower-and-breeding-techniques-pdf/274821569
ARKA MOHINI (capsicum): No evidence found for disease or pest resistance. The bacterial wilt tolerance reported in the sources belongs to Arka Gaurav, not Mohini. -- https://www.slideshare.net/THANKLORD/varieties-of-capsicum

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Arka Kamini (China aster): IIHR describes the flowers as semi-double, deep pink, suited to garlands and cut flowers. -- https://iihr.res.in/china-aster-arka-kamini
Arka Kamini (China aster): A production slide deck gives plant height about 60 cm, about 138 days to flower, about 50 flowers per plant, 6 cm flower diameter and about 8 days vase life. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/china-aster-and-dahlia-production-technology/239173609
Arka Kamini (China aster): Popularised under the IIHR-ICRISAT Bhoo-Samrudhi project in four Karnataka districts, with a farmer in Chikkaballapur reporting early flowering and better colour and uniformity. -- https://www.iihr.res.in/performance-china-aster-cv-arka-kamini-chikkaballapur-under-icrisat-iihr-bhoo-samrudhi-project
Arka Kamini (China aster): In a New Alluvial Zone of West Bengal seed-production trial, Kamini recorded about 61.4 flowers per plant, behind Arka Poornima. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344378197_Variation_in_seed_production_potential_of_China_aster_genotypes_in_the_New_Alluvial_Zone_of_West_Bengal
Arka Kamini (China aster): In a Kerala tropical-plains trial, Kamini recorded about 16.27 flowers per plant, on par with several other genotypes. -- https://jtropag.kau.in/index.php/ojs2/article/view/877
Arka Kamini (China aster): In a 2024-25 Nagpur trial of Arka-series varieties, Arka Aadya gave the highest flower count; Kamini's rank was not reported in the excerpt. -- https://zenodo.org/records/18400962
ARKA MOHINI (capsicum): IIHR gives indeterminate-type plant descriptions with a 16 t/ha yield in 150 days on one page, and determinate-type with 20 t/ha in 160 days on another. -- https://iihr.res.in/capsicum-arka-mohini-1 ; https://iihr.res.in/variety/arka-mohini
ARKA MOHINI (capsicum): Fruit weight and habit descriptions conflict across IIHR and third-party pages (130-150 g, 150-180 g, 180-200 g). -- https://iihr.res.in/variety/arka-mohini ; https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/commercial-varieties-of-capsicum.html
ARKA MOHINI (capsicum): Seed yield of about 150 kg/ha is listed. -- https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/commercial-varieties-of-capsicum.html

GENETICS AND QTL
Arka Kamini (China aster): No evidence found for QTL, marker or molecular studies.
ARKA MOHINI (capsicum): Its parentage (selection from Titan, and improvement over IIHR-214-1 followed by mass selection) is recorded, but no QTL or marker study was found. The combining-ability study is a crossing study, not a QTL study. -- https://www.slideshare.net/THANKLORD/varieties-of-capsicum ; https://jhs.iihr.res.in/index.php/jhs/article/download/1080/908/7389

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Arka Kamini (China aster): Developed by ICAR-IIHR, Bengaluru. Scientists named as advising the Bhoo-Samrudhi farmer: Dr R. Senthil Kumar, Dr Rajeev Kumar, Dr A.K. Nair, Dr J. Sathisha, and Dr P.C. Tripathi. No explicit breeder-of-record statement was found. -- https://www.iihr.res.in/performance-china-aster-cv-arka-kamini-chikkaballapur-under-icrisat-iihr-bhoo-samrudhi-project
Arka Kamini (China aster): IIHR

2. "VL Shimla Mirch-2 Capsicum breeder institute"
3. "VL Shimla Mirch-2 Capsicum research"
4. "VL Shimla Mirch-2 capsicum seed availability"

Results were generic Shimla Mirch (bell pepper) seed-shop listings, general crop guides, nutrition and polyhouse articles, and an unrelated chilli landrace (Almora Lakhori Mirchi, a Capsicum annuum chilli from Uttarakhand). None named VL Shimla Mirch-2, so I discarded all of them under the relevance rule.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searches returned no page on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety. Results were general cultivation guides only (for example, https://arowest.com/vegetables/capsicum/ and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/395477527_Cultivation_of_Capsicum_Shimla_Mirch_in_Polyhouse_A_Detail_Guide_Article_ID_60308), and they do not mention this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. Seed-shop pages (for example, https://beejrseeds.com/capsicum-mix-color-hybrid-shimla-mirch-vegetable-seeds/) make generic claims about disease resistance for unnamed hybrids. These are not about this variety and were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. No maturity, yield, or multi-location trial data for VL Shimla Mirch-2 were returned. Only generic sowing and growing guides appeared, for example https://arowest.com/vegetables/capsicum/ and https://www.hobbyplus.in/Capsicum-Hari-Shimla-Mirch. These do not name this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The parentage given in the record ("introduction and selection from AVRDC line 9955-36 (EC 565199)") was not confirmed by any search result. No breeding-line code, breeding method, or genome resource was found for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. No page named a breeder, scientist, or developing station for VL Shimla Mirch-2. Searches on the institution name did not return VPKAS or ICAR pages about this crop. The only breeder-like hit (Trinidad Moruga scorpion, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinidad_Moruga_scorpion) is a different chilli and was discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, postal address, or contact-page URL for VPKAS was returned in these searches. Note that the institution's contact page was not directly retrieved. A direct check of the VPKAS site (Almora, Uttarakhand) is still needed.

Searches returned general capsicum reviews (for example, https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2024.v8.i8.b.1709 on nutrient content, and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333602494_Profitability_of_Capsicum_Cultivation_under_Protected_Condition on protected cultivation). AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No trial, yield or maturity data for either name was retrieved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution is named in the input as the Indian Institute of Spices Research (ICAR-IISR, Kozhikode). The IISR varieties page lists "Appangala 2" among cardamom varieties, which places it in IISR's variety listing. No breeder name was found. -- https://www.spices.res.in/pages/cardamom-varieties

CONTACT DETAILS -- The only institute address retrieved is for ICAR-IISR, Kozhikode, Kerala, PIN 673 012, from an IISR-branded PDF. No breeder email or phone was found. No institute email or phone was retrieved from the snippets. -- https://www.indianspices.com/sites/default/files/cultivation_practices-Cardamom.pdf

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, report, thesis or KrishiKosh record naming either variety was retrieved.

A cardamom cultivation PDF lists "Appangala 1" and "Appangala 2" in a table titled as important farmers' varieties in cardamom, not as released varieties with seed sources. -- https://www.indianspices.com/sites/default/files/cultivation_practices-Cardamom.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found confirming Karnataka and Kerala from a source. The input record gives "Karnataka & Kerala". Nothing retrieved verified it.

Flags for the record:
- The IISR and cultivation-practice pages list these names as cardamom varieties or farmers' varieties. Neither page confirms the 2017 CSC release, the NHY 35 code, or the recommended states.
- The Seednet name APPANGALA-1 and the CSC name Appangala-2 are not clearly the same entry. The evidence does not establish that the two names refer to one variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Rhizome rot (clump rot) caused by soil pathogens: resistant. Selected through clonal selection for this resistance together with high yield. Described as tolerant to rhizome rot and suited to valley planting; named as a rhizome-rot-resistant variety for valleys and rot-prone areas. Causal organisms named in one source as Pythium vexans and Rhizoctonia solani. Recommended for cultivation in areas prone to rhizome rot, in the context of chlorotic streak management. Not the katte/CMV-resistant variety; IISR Vijetha is the one recommended for mosaic areas, so no mosaic/katte resistance is attributed to IISR Avinash. Isolates of Colletotrichum gloeosporioides and Fusarium/Rhizoctonia/Pythium antagonists were tested on Avinash, but these results are not a resistance rating.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance rating found for IISR Avinash. Leaf blight and thrips reactions specific to this variety: no evidence found; the leaf blight and thrips results in the sources do not name it.

agronomic_details.yield: Conflicting figures in sources. (1) 2006 paper: average 643 kg/ha dry capsules, potential 979 kg/ha, dark green quality capsules. (2) IISR variety table and Krishi Jagran: 847 kg/ha dry capsules, potential 1483 kg/ha. The IISR table also reports essential oil 6.7%.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Yield recorded for 3 years at the original location only; multi-environment stability not reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to valley planting and rot-prone areas (rhizome rot). Yields well at 2.5 x 2 m spacing (IISR variety table). Recommended for Karnataka and Kerala.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 228.6 cm and 46 tillers per clump (Krishi Jagran). Dark green quality capsules (2006 paper). Essential oil 6.7% and extended flowering period (IISR variety table).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Selection trial: 4 plants selected from a population of over 51,000 plants for non-susceptibility to natural infection over 4-5 years and for high yield; yield recorded for 3 years at the original location. (2) Yield trials: 643 kg/ha average and 979 kg/ha potential (2006 paper); 847 kg/ha average and 1483 kg/ha potential (IISR table and Krishi Jagran). (3) Hybrid trial: in a preliminary evaluation trial (PET III) of 23 F1 hybrids, Mudigere 2 x IISR Avinash showed the highest plant height. (4) Breeding use: used as a female parent in hybridization with Appangala-1, Njallani green gold and Clone 893. Dry recovery figures (6-9%, 30.4/34.6 comparison values) appear in the digest without explicit attribution to this variety and are excluded.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: IISR (Avinash), cardamom (Elettaria cardamomum)

Name check: The variety_name ("IISR (Avinash)") and seednet_variety_name ("IISR (Avinash)") are identical. Sources use "IISR Avinash", "IISR-Avinash (RR1)" and "IISR Avinash (RR-1)". All findings below refer to this variety. The "Avinash-I" in one ISSR marker study is a different accession from Kozhikode and is excluded. The variety code H020216707 does not appear in any source found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to rhizome rot (clump rot) caused by soil pathogens; selected through clonal selection for this resistance and high yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/264348817_IISR_Avinash_-_a_rhizome_rot_resistant_and_high_yielding_variety_of_cardamom_Elettaria_cardamomum_Maton
- Described as tolerant to rhizome rot and suited to valley planting -- https://spices.res.in/itm-abi/page/spice-varieties
- Named as a rhizome-rot-resistant variety for valleys and rot-prone areas -- https://www.celkau.in/Crops/spices/cardamom/varieties.php (http://www.celkau.in/Crops/spices/cardamom/varieties.php)
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The moisture-stress trial in the Annual Report snippet does not name Avinash in the retrieved text -- https://spices.res.in/storage/app/public/publications/english/pdf/jN5n8KJzaRRuSEYMFdzuatH3A3HiOxp18YHPTmhm.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Rhizome rot resistance, with the causal organisms named as Pythium vexans and Rhizoctonia solani -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/grow-these-cardamom-varieties-for-higher-profitability-and-better-yields/
- Recommended for cultivation in areas prone to rhizome rot, in the context of chlorotic streak management -- https://www.indianspices.com/sites/default/files/cultivation_practices-Cardamom.pdf
- Not the katte/CMV-resistant variety; IISR Vijetha is the one recommended for mosaic areas -- https://pop.kau.in/spices&condiments.htm
- Leaf blight and thrips reaction specific to Avinash: No evidence found (leaf blight and thrips results in the sources do not name it) -- https://spices.res.in/mail/upload/202112272.pdf
- Isolates of Colletotrichum gloeosporioides and Fusarium/Rhizoctonia/Pythium antagonists were tested on Avinash, but the results are not a resistance rating -- https://spices.res.in/storage/app/public/publications/english/pdf/d6JJPi7unKVF2N6DLfJEQOwocCxXiKIEA2k4zhfK.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Average yield 643 kg/ha (dry capsules), potential 979 kg/ha, dark green quality capsules (2006 paper) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/264348817_IISR_Avinash_-_a_rhizome_rot_resistant_and_high_yielding_variety_of_cardamom_Elettaria_cardamomum_Maton
- Conflicting figures: 847 kg/ha dry capsules with potential 1483 kg/ha, essential oil 6.7%, extended flowering period, yields well at 2.5 x 2 m spacing (IISR variety table) -- https://spices.res.in/itm-abi/page/spice-varieties
- Same 847 / 1483 figures, plant height 228.6 cm, 46 tillers per clump -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/grow-these-cardamom-varieties-for-higher-profitability-and-better-yields/
- Selection trial details: 4 plants selected from a population of over 51,000 plants for non-susceptibility to natural infection for 4-5 years and high yield; yield recorded for 3 years at the original location -- https://spices.res.in/mail/upload/202112272.pdf (see also the 2006 paper: https://www.researchgate.net/profile/D-Prasath-2/publication/264348817_IISR_Avinash_-_a_rhizome_rot_resistant_and_high_yielding_variety_of_cardamom_Elettaria_cardamomum_Maton/links/53d9cb610cf2a19eee880790/IISR-Avinash-a-rhizome-rot-resistant-and-high-yielding-variety-of-cardamom-Elettaria-cardamomum-Maton.pdf?origin=publication_list)
- Dry recovery of 6-9% in the medium class, and 30.4 / 34.6 values in a comparison table -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/smallcardemom.pdf and https://www.resurgentagric.com/img/resurgentagric_cardamom.pdf
- Breeding use as a parent: used as a female parent in hybridization with Appangala-1, Njallani green gold and Clone 893 -- https://spices.res.in/mail/upload/202112272.pdf
- Hybrid trial: Mudigere 2 x IISR Avinash showed the highest plant height in a preliminary evaluation trial (PET III) of 23 F1 hybrids -- https://spices.res.in/storage/app/public/publications/english/pdf/jN5n8KJzaRRuSEYMFdzuatH3A3HiOxp18YHPTmhm.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Developed by clonal selection, so no parentage is recorded in the sources. The "parentage: Not specified" entry is consistent with this. The sources conflict on origin: the IISR table says it is a selection from open-pollinated progeny of Appangala 1, while Krishi Jagran says it is derived from CCS-1 -- https://spices.res.in/itm-abi/page/spice-varieties ; https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/grow-these-cardamom-varieties-for-higher-profitability-and-better-yields/
- Used as a reference entry in a PPV&FRA small cardamom descriptor table (DUS traits, e.g. panicle number and dry recovery) -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/smallcardemom.pdf
- QTL or marker-assisted studies specific to Avinash: No evidence found. The ISSR study names "Avinash-I" from Kozhikode, which is not this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/386098757_Advancements_in_Cardamom_Elettaria_cardamomum_Maton_Breeding_Genetic_Diversity_Biotech_Strategies_and_Future_Directions

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead breeders named in the 2006 paper: M N Venugopal, D Prasath, Ravindra Mulge -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/264348817_IISR_Avinash_-_a_rhizome_rot_resistant_and_high_yielding_variety_of_cardamom_Elettaria_cardamomum_Maton
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research, Cardamom Research Centre, Appangala, Madikeri, Karnataka (later a Regional Station, from November 2014) -- https://spices.res.in/storage/app/public/publications/english/pdf/d6JJPi7unKVF2N6DLfJEQOwocCxXiKIEA2k4zhfK.pdf
- Institute history (NRCS 1986, IISR 1995), Kozhikode headquarters -- https://spices.res.in/storage/app/public/publications/english/pdf/d6JJPi7unKVF2N6DLfJEQOwocCxXiKIEA2k4zhfK.pdf
- Release date: The CSC record gives 2017-09-18. The search found 1999 as the year of selection in the IISR table and "2000s" elsewhere. No CSC notification document was found -- https://spices.res.in/itm-abi/page/spice-varieties

CONTACT DETAILS
- M N Venugopal (breeder, Cardamom Research Centre); email as printed in the PDF: venugopal@iisr.or g (line-broken; probably venugopal@iisr.org, not verified) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/264348817_IISR_Avinash_-_a_rhizome_rot_resistant_and_high_yielding_variety_of_cardamom_Elettaria_cardamomum_Maton
- Address (Cardamom

However, the sources are only an institutional annual report and a gazette notification. They contain no stress or climate traits, no yield data and no peer-reviewed research. The rubric's 50 band is for some stress or climate trait with no citation, and 60 is for at least one citation but weak stress traits. It is set at 50 as a conservative, evidence-only choice, and it could be raised to about 60 if the official sources are accepted as citations.

A fifth query ("Pusa Vashda" and "IPC HC1 carrot hybrid seednet") was blocked by the tool-call limit, so it was not run. I checked every result for "Vashda", "IPC HC1" and "HC1/HCI" and found no match for this variety. Names used in searching: "Pusa Vashda hybrid" (CSC minutes name) and "Pusa Vashda hybrid (IPC HCI)" (Seednet name). Neither name appeared in any result.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page names this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The only carrot-related results were general varieties checklists and other carrot varieties, which I discarded under the relevance rule.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage was returned, and the record's parentage field is "Not specified."

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a breeder or lead scientist. Results only mentioned IARI in general terms in a national checklist of vegetable varieties (https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/pdf/tech_bulletin/national/Checklist-of-Commercial-Varieties-of-Vegetables.pdf). That page does not name this hybrid, so I have not attributed it to this variety. The institution listed in the CSC record (Indian Agricultural Research Institute) is taken from the input record only, not from search evidence.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No IARI division, station, email, phone or address was retrieved for this variety. Official IARI contacts should be checked directly at iari.res.in.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The carrot paper returned (Economic Impact of Vegetable Variety in Haryana: A Case of Pusa Rudhira of Carrot, https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Economic-Impact-of-Vegetable-Variety-in-Haryana:-A/b3228999089e1f0aee5ed120dc44bf8ed0299afc) concerns a different variety, Pusa Rudhira, so it is excluded.

The seed listings returned were for other Pusa-branded products (for example, a Pusa Yamdagini carrot listing on Amazon.in), which are different varieties and were excluded. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listing for this hybrid was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found in search results. The input record gives "NCT of Delhi" as the recommended state, which is not confirmed by any retrieved source.

Suggested next steps: check the Seednet portal entry for "Pusa Vashda hybrid (IPC HCI)" directly, search the CSC release minutes of 2015, and check IARI's vegetable science division and KrishiKosh for records of this hybrid.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features:
It is drought tolerant variety.
Propagation  :  Stem cuttings (Sets)
Seed rate  : 12,346 stem cuttings/ha
Spacing    :  90 X 90 cm
Fertilizers: 60:60:60 kg NPK/ha. Whole of P2O5 has to be applied as a basal in last ploughing, whereas N & K are to be applied in three (3) equal split doses at 30, 60 and 90 days after planting.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: It is a semi spreading variety with pandurate leaf shape, redish brown stem, red pertiole and tuber with ream cortex and white flesh colour.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: It is drought tolerant variety
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Completely resistan tot cassava mosaic disease (CMD)
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: There is no major pests and observed low incidence of re mite

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerant to sucking pests and thrips, per the JAU new-variety release sheet. The JAU variety-13-years proceedings report lower leafhopper and fruit borer incidence than hybrid checks. These are field-level observations, not a formal resistance rating.

agronomic_details.yield: Mean seed yield 3820 kg/ha under irrigation (ICAR-IIOR entry). Station-level figure 3781 kg/ha with 48.30% oil (JAU station page). JAU release sheet gives potential yield 3500-4000 kg/ha and average 2340 kg/ha. Trial yield 3820 kg/ha, 9.0% above check GCH-7 (3503 kg/ha), in irrigated Gujarat (JAU proceedings).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The only multi-location evidence is the Assam and ARS Mandor trial mentions under field_trials, which are not established as stability data.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for irrigated areas of Gujarat (JAU). A listing under a GCH-9 (2018) heading claims rainfed recommendation for Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Odisha. This contradicts the irrigated-only Gujarat recommendation and is unverified, so it is not adopted here.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 105-110 cm; 100-seed weight 29.64 g; profuse branching; primary spike 100-104 days; seed-to-seed 210 days; first picking at 110-120 days after sowing; medium duration. Oil content is reported as 49.67% in the JAU release sheet and 48.3% in the JAU proceedings and station page. The digest flags this conflict and it is not resolved.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) ICAR-IIOR entry: mean seed yield 3820 kg/ha under irrigation. (2) JAU station page: station-level 3781 kg/ha with 48.30% oil. (3) JAU release sheet: potential 3500-4000 kg/ha, average 2340 kg/ha, oil 49.67%. (4) JAU proceedings: trial yield 3820 kg/ha, 9.0% above check GCH-7 (3503 kg/ha), irrigated Gujarat, 48.3% oil. (5) Kharif 2017 field experiment at Castor-Mustard Research Station, Sardarkrushinagar: eight hybrids tested, including JHB 1018 (the variety code); the paper's main focus is GCH 8, so results for this variety were not separately reported in the digest. (6) Assam (Jorhat) 2023-24 trial of Gujarat-bred genotypes: GCH 09 ranked among the most promising. The attribution to this variety is assumed from the name 'GCH 09' and is not confirmed. (7) ARS Mandor (Jodhpur) kharif 2022 trial: JHB 1018 among hybrids, recording the highest effective branches per plant (18.8).

NAME NOTE: CSC release minutes name this variety "Gujarat Castor Hybrid-9" (GCH-9, JHB-1018). The Seednet name "GCH-2 (GUJARAT CASTOR HYBRID-2)" refers to a different hybrid released around 1985-86 (VP-1 x JI-35). No search result linked the Seednet GCH-2 entry to GCH-9, so no GCH-2 evidence is attributed to this variety below. Release year differs by source: 2016-17 (JAU), 2018 (ICAR-IIOR, Vikaspedia). The input gives 2018-08-10. Gazette notification is S.O. 6318(E), dated 26-12-2018.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Resistant to Fusarium wilt and Macrophomina root rot, per the variety entry -- https://icar-iior.org.in/node/386
Resistant to Fusarium wilt and Macrophomina root rot, per JAU's release list -- https://www.jau.in/castor-research-station-junagadh
Tolerant to sucking pests; thrips tolerance also noted in the JAU notification sheet -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/AOilseedsCrops.pdf
Tolerant to sucking pests; lower leafhopper and fruit borer incidence than hybrid checks -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-13-years.pdf
Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found. Searches returned nothing for these stresses on GCH-9.

DISEASE AND PEST
Wilt and root rot resistance, as above -- https://icar-iior.org.in/node/386 ; https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/oilseeds/high-yielding-hybrids-and-varieties-of-castor-ricinus-communis-l

Mean seed yield 3820 kg/ha under irrigation; medium duration; first picking at 110-120 days after sowing -- https://icar-iior.org.in/node/386

Maturity and other agronomic data: no evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage given in the task (SI 8 selected from the ANDCI 8 base population) was not confirmed by any retrieved page, so it is unverified.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: Anand Agricultural University, per the AAU variety listing -- https://aau.in/variety_released. Lead breeder name(s), station and developing division: no evidence found in retrieved pages.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder contact, institute email, phone or postal address was retrieved. The institutional website is https://aau.in (listing and variety pages), but its contact page was not retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No journal paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper naming this variety was retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sales or dealer page for this variety was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Gujarat, specifically irrigated and rainfed areas of Middle Gujarat -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-castor-11

RELEASE RECORD (supporting) -- The AAU release listing names "Gujarat Anand Castor 11 (GAC 11)" as a released variety -- https://aau.in/variety_released. The 2019-06-01 release date given in the task was not confirmed by any retrieved page.

NAME NOTE -- The evidence above refers to both "Gujarat Anand Castor-11" (CSC minutes name) and "Gujarat Anand Castor 11 (GAC 11)" (Seednet name), since the AAU pages use both forms.

Many headings are therefore thin, and the breeder, contact, publication and seed-availability entries should be treated as unresolved rather than confirmed absent. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: HCH 6 (castor hybrid)

Name note: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "HCH 6", so all evidence below refers to that one name. The Seednet portal was not returned by any search, so no Seednet-specific record was found. Searches also surfaced GCH-6, ICH-66 and other hybrids; these were excluded as different varieties.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for HCH 6. Results were general castor hybrid lists and an unrelated stability paper.

DISEASE AND PEST -- A Hybrid Seed Production slide deck lists HCH-6 (Hiriyur castor hybrid-6), released 2016, as resistant to Fusarium wilt and whitefly. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/hybrid-seed-production-in-castor-ricinus-communis/284111506 (low-authority secondary source; not verified against an official release notification)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- In a 2011-12 stability analysis of castor genotypes, HCH-6 showed high correlation with ANDCI-8 and a local check, and PCH-111 was reported as the most stable entry, followed by HCH-6 and ANDCI-8. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/d25f34a5-2f0d-4fc4-9fcf-3dfefbfb8de4/content
No yield, maturity, spacing or fertilizer data specific to HCH 6 was found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage or pedigree for HCH 6 was found. The GCH-6 and other hybrid pedigrees returned were excluded because they are different varieties.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The station that developed the hybrid is documented as Castor: HCH-6 Hybrid, listed under ZAHRS - Hiriyur, a station with field crops including castor. -- https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/
A compendium chapter describes a researcher who served as Junior Breeder in AICRP on Castor from 2012 to 2018 and was involved in developing and releasing the Castor hybrid HCH-6 for Karnataka. -- https://www.satishserial.com/book/9789366268637/compendium-of-crop-improvement-volume-3-plant-breeding
The breeder's name is not given in the retrieved text, so no lead breeder name is recorded.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact was found. The UAHS research-stations page is the only institutional source located: https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/ . No official email, phone or postal address for the institute or the Hiriyur station appeared in the retrieved text. Verify on the UAHS Shivamogga contact page before use.

PUBLICATIONS -- Anonymous (n.d.). Stability analysis of varieties and hybrids in castor (Ricinus communis L.). Thesis/report (KrishiKosh) -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/d25f34a5-2f0d-4fc4-9fcf-3dfefbfb8de4/content (authors and year not visible in retrieved text; the HCH-6 entry is one of several genotypes assessed)
No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report or conference paper specifically on HCH 6 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Searches returned only ornamental castor bean sellers and a market report, none of which name HCH 6. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for HCH 6 was located.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- HCH-6 was developed and released for the Karnataka state farming community -- https://www.satishserial.com/book/9789366268637/compendium-of-crop-improvement-volume-3-plant-breeding (the Seednet/CSC recommended-states field remains "Not specified in table"; Karnataka is supported by this single secondary source only)

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to Fusarium wilt and Macrophomina root rot (JOR paper, Duraimurugan and Santha Lakshmi Prasad). The Vikaspedia salient-features table likewise describes the hybrid as resistant to Fusarium wilt and Macrophomina root rot. Botrytis tolerance is NOT attributed to ICH-66: the 2019 IIOR field-day item describes botrytis tolerance for the companion experimental hybrid ICH-538, which is a different entry and is excluded here. The original variety data lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistant to leafhopper, with hopper burn grade 0 to 1 on a 0-4 scale at multilocation trials in all screening years (JOR paper). The Vikaspedia salient-features table also lists leafhopper resistance. The original variety data lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: Station and multilocation (AICRP Castor MLT) mean seed yield 1566 kg/ha, which is 14.9% above DCH-519 (1324 kg/ha) and 18.3% above DCH-177 (1363 kg/ha). Vikaspedia lists average yield 1560 kg/ha for the 2019 release. The original variety data field 'average_yield' reads '0 Kg/Ha', which conflicts with all retrieved yield evidence and is treated as a data error. A ResearchGate snippet citing 1574 kg/ha rainfed and 3375 kg/ha irrigated was discarded as unverified.
agronomic_details.stability: Tested across multilocation trials (AICRP Castor MLTs 2015-16 to 2017-18). Hopper burn resistance was recorded at multilocations in all screening years. Year-by-year or location-by-location yield stability values were not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for rainfed castor growing regions of Peninsular India in the kharif season, especially Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Odisha (original variety data and JOR abstract). Non-lodging and non-shattering type.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Medium maturity group: Days to 50% flowering:  Rain fed: 50-51 days, Irrigated: 54-63 days; Days to maturity: Rain fed: 94-97 days, Irrigated: 110-124 days
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: -	Red stem colour -	Triple bloom -	Spiny capsules -	Dwarf, condensed nodes, cup shaped leaves -	Long conical spike (mean: 66 cm, range: 60-70 cm)	-	Red stem colour -	Double bloom -	Non-spiny capsules -	Medium long spikes (48-56 cm) -	Basal divergent branching.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Station trials at ICAR-IIOR, 2013-14 and 2014-15. (2) AICRP (Castor) MLTs, 2015-16 to 2017-18, against checks DCH-519 and DCH-177. Mean seed yield 1566 kg/ha (14.9% above DCH-519 at 1324 kg/ha; 18.3% above DCH-177 at 1363 kg/ha). Mean oil content 48.6%, versus 47.6% (DCH-519) and 47.0% (DCH-177). Primary spike length 45 cm and 100-seed weight 29.0 g under rainfed conditions, versus the checks. Maturity 100-130 days to primary spike maturity; non-lodging and non-shattering. (3) IIOR rabi-castor field day (22/02/2022, Nagarkurnool): ICH-66 grown on a farmer plot at 90 x 60 cm spacing; the farmer expected 10-12 q per acre. This is a farmer expectation, not a measured trial result. Station-level yield values for individual seasons were not found in searched sources.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. Parentage is recorded as SKP-84 x ICS-164 (SKP-84: SKP-1 x VP-1; ICS-164: 48-1 x RG-1582), per the JOR paper and consistent with Vikaspedia. Conflicting parentage entries (SKP-84 x PMC-14 from ResearchGate; High Oil Mutant x Mauthner's Dwarf from Agrifarming) were excluded as unverified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Searches run: 4 of 4 allowed. Variety name and Seednet name are both "ICH-66", so every finding below refers to ICH-66 under that single name. No Seednet portal page for ICH-66 was retrieved, and no CSC release-minute text was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE

The hybrid showed resistance to Fusarium wilt and Macrophomina root rot. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
It was also found resistant to leafhopper, with hopper burn grade 0 to 1 on a 0-4 scale at multilocations in all screening years. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Drought/rainfed suitability: recommended for rainfed areas, and the release is framed around rainfed Peninsular India (kharif). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found in the retrieved pages.

DISEASE AND PEST

Fusarium wilt, Macrophomina root rot, and leafhopper resistance, as listed above. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Salient-features table describes the hybrid as resistant to Fusarium wilt, Macrophomina root rot and leafhopper. -- https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/oilseeds/high-yielding-hybrids-and-varieties-of-castor-ricinus-communis-l
Botrytis: the 2019 IIOR field-day item describes the companion experimental hybrid ICH-538 as botrytis-tolerant, not ICH-66. Not attributed to ICH-66. -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/11101

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS

Station trials at ICAR-IIOR in 2013-14 and 2014-15, then AICRP (Castor) MLTs in 2015-16 to 2017-18 against checks DCH-519 and DCH-177. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Mean seed yield 1566 kg/ha, 14.9% above DCH-519 (1324 kg/ha) and 18.3% above DCH-177 (1363 kg/ha). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Mean oil content 48.6%, versus 47.6% for DCH-519 and 47.0% for DCH-177. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Primary spike length 45 cm and 100-seed weight 29.0 g under rainfed conditions, versus the checks. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Maturity 100-130 days to primary spike maturity; non-lodging and non-shattering. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Vikaspedia table lists average yield 1560 kg/ha for the 2019 release. -- https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/oilseeds/high-yielding-hybrids-and-varieties-of-castor-ricinus-communis-l
Field-level performance: IIOR rabi-castor field day (22/02/2022, Nagarkurnool) reported ICH-66 grown on a farmer plot at 90 x 60 cm spacing, with a farmer expecting 10-12 q per acre. -- https://icar-iior.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-02/castor-rabi-fd.pdf
Discarded: a ResearchGate snippet cites 1574 kg/ha rainfed and 3375 kg/ha irrigated for the hybrid, but the same snippet's parentage and text appear to mix other entries, so it is unverified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378522773_ICH-66_a_new_high_yielding_and_biotic_stress-resistant_castor_hybrid_suitable_for_rainfed_conditions_of_Peninsular_India_ICH-66_A_NEW_CASTOR_HYBRID_SUITABLE_FOR_RAINFED_CONDITIONS_OF_PENINSULAR_INDIA

GENETICS AND QTL

Parentage SKP-84 x ICS-164, as stated in the JOR paper. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Parentage conflict: a ResearchGate snippet gives SKP-84 x PMC-14, and an Agrifarming page gives "High Oil Mutant x Mauthner's Dwarf". Both conflict with the JOR paper and with Vikaspedia, so they are not used. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378522773_ICH-66_a_new_high_yielding_and_biotic_stress-resistant_castor_hybrid_suitable_for_rainfed_conditions_of_Peninsular_India_ICH-66_A_NEW_CASTOR_HYBRID_SUITABLE_FOR_RAINFED_CONDITIONS_OF_PENINSULAR_INDIA ; https://www.agrifarming.in/varieties-of-castor-in-india-boost-the-profit-with-high-yielding-hybrids-of-castor

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

Developed at ICAR-Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research (IIOR), Hyderabad, and identified by the Combined Varietal Identification Committee of Oilseed Crops in 2018. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Authors of the JOR paper: P. Duraimurugan and M. Santha Lakshmi Prasad, both ICAR-IIOR, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad-500 030. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Institution-level leadership: R.K. Mathur named as IIOR Director in a 2025-era news item (not a breeder of ICH-66). -- https://newsmeter.in/whats-new/hyderabad-how-iior-s-biopolymer-technology-will-revolutionize-indian-farming-739783
Vikaspedia lists ICAR-IIOR, Hyderabad, Telangana-500030 as the source institute. -- https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/oilseeds/high-yielding-hybrids-and-varieties-of-castor-ricinus-communis-l
Breeder attribution: the Duraimurugan and Santha Lakshmi Prasad authorship is the only breeder-level link found for this variety; other IIOR scientists in the results (R.D. Prasad, G. Suresh) appear in extension and field-day roles, not as ICH-66 breeders.

CONTACT DETAILS

Institute-level (AICRP Information System page, IIOR): Director, Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad -- 500 030; Phone 040-24598444, 24016141; Fax 040-24017969; E-mail director.iior@icar.org.in. -- https://icar-iior.org.in/aicrp-information-system
Named scientists with breeder-level link: P. Duraimurugan and M. Santha Lakshmi Prasad, ICAR-IIOR, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad-500 030, Telangana (no individual email or phone found). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Caution: a Google Play app listing for IIOR castor gives iior.developer@gmail.com, p.madhuri@icar.gov.in and 5-6-155, Rajendranagar, Premavathi Pet, Hyderabad 500030. These are app-developer details, not verified institute contacts; use with care. -- https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=in.org.icar_iior.icariiorcastor2&hl=en_US

PUBLICATIONS

Duraimurugan P., Santha Lakshmi Prasad M. (year not shown in retrieved text). ICH-66, a new high yielding and biotic stress-resistant castor hybrid suitable for rainfed conditions of Peninsular India. Journal of Oilseeds Research 35(4) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537 (same paper also at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378522773_ICH-66_a_new_high_yielding_and_biotic_stress-resistant_castor_hybrid_suitable_for_rainfed_conditions_of_Peninsular_India_ICH-66_A_NEW_CASTOR_HYBRID_SUITABLE_FOR_RAINFED_CONDITIONS_OF_PENINSULAR_INDIA; no DOI found)
ICAR-IIOR Annual Report 2022 (Scribd copy). Lists ICH-66 as the best check against which 60 experimental hybrids were compared, and reports 18.41 q of ICH-66 (CS) seed produced. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/738239893/56-Annual-Report-IIOR-AR-2022
KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports specific to ICH-66: No evidence found in the retrieved results.

SEED AVAILABILITY

IIOR annual report 2022 records 18.41 q of ICH-66 certified seed produced. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/738239893/56-Annual-Report-IIOR-AR-2022
At the 2019 Castor Field Day, the IIOR Director assured supply of quality seed from ICAR-IIOR. -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/11101
Seednet portal listing (CASTOR (REHRI)), NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or private dealer listings for ICH-66: No evidence found in the retrieved results.

RECOMMENDED STATES

Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Odisha, rainfed areas, as stated in the JOR abstract. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537

official_quote.quote: The proposed hybrid, ICH 66 was resistant to Fusarium wilt in wilt sick plots at two locations-ICAR-IIOR and SDAU, SK Nagar

disease_resistance.research_summary: Resistant to Fusarium wilt and Macrophomina root rot (JOR paper, Duraimurugan and Santha Lakshmi Prasad). The Vikaspedia salient-features table likewise describes the hybrid as resistant to Fusarium wilt and Macrophomina root rot. Botrytis tolerance is NOT attributed to ICH-66: the 2019 IIOR field-day item describes botrytis tolerance for the companion experimental hybrid ICH-538, which is a different entry and is excluded here. The original variety data lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified'.

official_quote.quote: The proposed hybrid was tolerant to leafhopper and thrips while the reaction to leaf eating caterpillars is similar to other hybrids like DCH-177, DCH-519 and GCH-7

pest_resistance.research_summary: Resistant to leafhopper, with hopper burn grade 0 to 1 on a 0-4 scale at multilocation trials in all screening years (JOR paper). The Vikaspedia salient-features table also lists leafhopper resistance. The original variety data lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

The input record names "Zonal Agricultural Research Station, Jawaharlal Nehru Viswa Vidyalaya" for JC-26, but no search result confirmed this. CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute, email, phone, or address was found for JC-26. Institute-level contact for JNKVV was not returned by any search.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found for JC-26. Castor papers returned (e.g., on value chains, harvesting, castor breeding reviews) do not name JC-26, so they are excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found for JC-26. Results were mandi (market) price pages and private oil or seed sellers, which do not name JC-26 and are not seed sources for it. -- https://mandibhavindia.in/en/commodity/castor-seed

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found for JC-26 from search. Madhya Pradesh appears only in the input record. The JNKVV JC-4 page lists Madhya Pradesh for JC-4, which is excluded. -- (input record only); https://icar-iior.org.in/node/451

drought.details: No direct evidence found for drought tolerance specific to PCH-111 (searched; none in results). The OUAT AICRP listing places PCH-111 under rainfed upland conditions in Odisha during kharif alongside DCH-177, but this is a suitability listing and does not establish drought tolerance or its mechanisms. Released yield range of about 1500 kg/ha under rainfed conditions versus 2000 kg/ha under irrigated conditions is reported, but no drought-specific trial data is provided.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to Fusarium wilt, per the PCH-111 salient-features entry in the Vikaspedia high-yielding hybrids and varieties of castor package. No other disease resistance evidence was found in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately tolerant to sucking pests, semilooper and spodoptera, per the Vikaspedia salient-features entry. Leafhopper (Empoasca flavescens) study reports hopper-burn score of 2 (11-25% injury) at early sowing on PCH-111 among other entries, and score 4 (over 50% injury) at late sowing. The same review notes zero wax-bloom (green-bloom) expression on PCH-111, linked to antixenosis resistance; this is indicative only. A biology study of Amrasca (jassid) on six castor varieties reports a shorter nymphal and adult-stage profile for PCH-111 than some entries, with larval durations reported; this is a biology observation and not a resistance rating.

agronomic_details.yield: Released as a hybrid with a yield range of about 1500 kg/ha (rainfed) to 2000 kg/ha (irrigated). The CSC average_yield field records only the unit 'Kg/Ha' with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Identified as superior and relatively stable for seed yield in a multi-genotype AMMI and GGE biplot study of eight genotypes including PCH-111 (Nature Scientific Reports). Specific stability statistics were not captured in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to rainfed upland conditions in Odisha during kharif (OUAT AICRP listing). Recommended for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in rainfed and irrigated areas (Vikaspedia). Trials were conducted under AICRP Zonal coordination unit V (Hyderabad) and spread from RARS Palem. Row spacing of 90 cm and plant spacing of 60 cm are recommended for rainfed upland under the general AICRP castor package; these are not PCH-111-specific.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Vikaspedia: released hybrid with yield of about 1500 kg/ha rainfed and 2000 kg/ha irrigated. (2) Nature Scientific Reports AMMI/GGE study: PCH-111 among eight genotypes, identified as superior and relatively stable for seed yield. (3) AICRP Zonal coordination unit V (Hyderabad) trials, spread from RARS Palem; no yield values captured. (4) Farmer-level problem study in Mahabubnagar district (ResearchGate): reports shortages of adequate hybrid seed quantities for PCH-111; no yield values captured. (5) Leafhopper (Empoasca flavescens) review: hopper-burn score 2 (11-25% injury) at early sowing and score 4 (over 50% injury) at late sowing on PCH-111 among other entries. (6) Amrasca (jassid) biology study on six castor varieties: shorter nymphal and adult-stage profile for PCH-111 than some entries, with larval durations reported; numeric values not captured.

disease_resistance.research_summary: Resistant to Fusarium wilt, per the PCH-111 salient-features entry in the Vikaspedia high-yielding hybrids and varieties of castor package. No other disease resistance evidence was found in the digest.

pest_resistance.research_summary: Moderately tolerant to sucking pests, semilooper and spodoptera, per the Vikaspedia salient-features entry. Leafhopper (Empoasca flavescens) study reports hopper-burn score of 2 (11-25% injury) at early sowing on PCH-111 among other entries, and score 4 (over 50% injury) at late sowing. The same review notes zero wax-bloom (green-bloom) expression on PCH-111, linked to antixenosis resistance; this is indicative only. A biology study of Amrasca (jassid) on six castor varieties reports a shorter nymphal and adult-stage profile for PCH-111 than some entries, with larval durations reported; this is a biology observation and not a resistance rating.

drought.details: PCH-222 is not separately evaluated for drought in the searched sources. The drought tolerance statement in the digest (coming up well when drought prevails) refers to the sister hybrid PCH-111 and cannot be attributed to PCH-222.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt resistance is the only disease claim tied to PCH-222 by name. PCH-222 is described as a wilt-resistant castor hybrid from RARS Palem, and farmers were advised toward wilt-resistant, high-yielding hybrids including PCH-111 and PCH-222. No PCH-222-specific disease screening scores were found. Palem's broader breeding goals include wilt complex and botrytis resistance, but these are programme goals, not PCH-222 test results.

pest_resistance.summary: No PCH-222-specific pest resistance evidence found. Palem's castor breeding goals include multiple resistances to Spodoptera, semilooper and sucking pests, but this is a programme goal and not a PCH-222 test result. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- PCH-222 is described as a wilt-resistant castor hybrid from RARS Palem, alongside PCH-111. Farmers were advised toward wilt resistant, high-yielding castor hybrids like PCH-111 and PCH-222. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/273708353_Upscaling_and_outsclaing_of_Rabi_castor_in_Andhra_Pradesh-opportunities_and_limitations
- The Palem-based PCH-111 is a sister hybrid, and PCH-222 is not separately evaluated for drought in these sources. The drought tolerance of PCH-111 is reported at comes up well even when drought situations prevail during crop growth period. This is a PCH-111 finding, not PCH-222. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/349645238_Problems_Encountered_by_Castor_Farmers_in_Cultivation_Marketing_in_Mahabubanagar_District
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Wilt resistance is the only disease claim tied to PCH-222 by name (see Stress Tolerance). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/273708353_Upscaling_and_outsclaing_of_Rabi_castor_in_Andhra_Pradesh-opportunities_and_limitations
- Palem's castor breeding goals include multiple resistances to pests such as Spodoptera, semilooper and sucking pests, plus wilt complex and botrytis. This is a programme goal, not a PCH-222 test result. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/regional-agricultural-research-station-palem/
- Specific pest and disease scores for PCH-222 in the Palem trials: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Palem scientists studied rabi castor sowing dates, irrigation scheduling and hybrid responses, and recommended PCH-111 and PCH-222 as wilt-resistant, high-yielding hybrids for good-quality seed supply. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/273708353_Upscaling_and_outsclaing_of_Rabi_castor_in_Andhra_Pradesh-opportunities_and_limitations
- A 2023 frontline demonstration series by the AICRP on Castor at RARS Palem compared improved practice with PCH-type/Palem and IIOR hybrids against farmers' practice, reporting an average seed yield advantage. It names hybrids from Palem/IIOR without listing PCH-222 explicitly in the excerpt. -- https://www.envirobiotechjournals.com/EEC/vol29jansuppl/EEC-34.pdf
- Yield values (kg/ha) for PCH-222 in AICRP trials: No evidence found.
- Maturity days for PCH-222: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage of PCH-222: No evidence found.
- QTL or marker studies on PCH-222: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Palem, Nagarkurnool district, Telangana (formerly ANGRAU, now PJTSAU). The station lists PCH-222 among castor releases. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/12.pdf and https://pjtau.edu.in/regional-agricultural-research-station-palem/
- Breeder names for PCH-222: No evidence found. The 2023 FLD paper names RARS Palem scientists (N. Nalini, K. Sadaiah, V. Divya Rani, G. Neelima, G. Maduri, Ch. Durga Rani, M. Sujatha, G.D. Sathish, M. Venkata Ramana, K. Avil Kumar, M. Damodar Raju, M. Goverdhan), but does not attribute PCH-222 to them. -- https://www.envirobiotechjournals.com/EEC/vol29jansuppl/EEC-34.pdf
- Year of release: The CSC minutes give 2013-01-18. Release year for PCH-222 is not confirmed in the search results.
- Naming: "PCH-262" (Seednet) appears in none of the results. Every source uses PCH-222. "PCS-262 (Pragathi)" is a different Palem hybrid and should not be confused with it. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/regional-agricultural-research-station-palem/

disease_resistance.research_summary: Wilt resistance is the only disease claim tied to PCH-222 by name. PCH-222 is described as a wilt-resistant castor hybrid from RARS Palem, and farmers were advised toward wilt-resistant, high-yielding hybrids including PCH-111 and PCH-222. No PCH-222-specific disease screening scores were found. Palem's broader breeding goals include wilt complex and botrytis resistance, but these are programme goals, not PCH-222 test results.

drought.details: In a morpho-physiological drought screen of 53 Indian soybean genotypes, NRC 86 recorded the highest fresh, turgid and dry weights and fell in a separate cluster from the other genotypes. This is the only drought evidence in the digest and comes from a single screen, so the level is rated medium. The AICRPS 2024-25 report lists NRC 86 as a parent in drought-tolerance crosses (JS 20-29 x NRC 86), which indicates a breeding use for drought tolerance but is not a tolerance measurement. No physiological mechanism was reported.

flood.details: No evidence found for NRC 86 specifically. The Maranna et al. waterlogging study names NRC 86 only as a check line, not as a tolerant entry, so no waterlogging tolerance can be attributed to it.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Searches used: 4 (the maximum). The seednet name RC-8 was not searched on its own, so the RC-8 headings below rest on the NRC 86 results only.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought: in a morpho-physiological drought screen of 53 Indian soybean genotypes, NRC-86 recorded the highest fresh, turgid and dry weights, and it fell in a separate cluster from the other genotypes. Evidence refers to NRC 86 under the release name. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4550
- Waterlogging: no evidence found for NRC 86 specifically. The Maranna et al. waterlogging study names NRC 86 only as a check line, not as a tolerant entry. -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-021-02064-x
- Heat and salinity: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- NRC 86 was one of four check varieties in a JNKVV Jabalpur field trial of 154 genotypes scored for charcoal rot, aerial blight and yellow mosaic. The search snippet gives no NRC 86 disease score, so no resistance rating can be recorded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381632706_Survey_and_Present_Status_of_Soybean_Diseases_in_Central_India
- Pest and disease resistance rating for NRC 86 in the IISR/SOPA slides: No evidence found. The slides list NRC 86 with no disease or pest reaction. -- https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf
- Pest and disease notes on the Kisaan Helpline page refer to soybean generally (yellow mosaic, stem fly), not to a resistance rating for NRC 86. -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/variety/soybean-enaarasi-86-ahilya-6-nrc-86

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity 95-97 days and yield 2128 (units not stated), with notification S.O. 268(E) of 28.01.2015. -- https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf
- Maturity 90-95 days and yield 20-25 (units not stated; likely q/ha). Vantika Tech attributes the table to NRC 86 (Ahilya 6). -- https://www.vantikatech.com/2020/05/improved-high-yield-soybean-variety.html
- Yield 20-25 q/ha and about 95 days; seed rate and sowing notes. -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/variety/soybean-enaarasi-86-ahilya-6-nrc-86
- NRC 86 was a yield check in the IISR 2014-15 breeding trial, and a 2230 kg/plot line outyielded it. -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-021-02064-x

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage ("a mutant from RC-1188"): No evidence found in these searches.
- Use as a parent: the AICRPS progress report 2024-25 lists NRC 86 as a parent in drought-tolerance crosses (JS 20-29 x NRC 86). This is a breeding use, not a QTL or marker study. -- http://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/AicrpsAR2024-25.pdf
- QTL or marker studies on NRC 86: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-IISR / NRCS / ICAR-NSRI, Indore. The IISR achievements page lists NRC 86 among high-yielding varieties developed and released by the institute. -- https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/significant_achievement.html
- The institute name in the record ("Directorate of Soybean Research") matches the older name of the institute that the sources describe. -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html
- Lead breeder for NRC 86: No evidence found. The 2024-25 report lists breeding staff for the programme, but does not tie any of them to NRC 86. -- http://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/AicrpsAR2024-25.pdf
- Director (institute level): Dr Kunwar Harendra Singh, Director, ICAR-IISR Indore. -- https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute address (ICAR-National Soybean Research Institute): Khandwa Road, Indore 452 001 (M.P.), India. -- http://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/AicrpsAR2024-25.pdf
- Institute address (ICAR-IISR): Khandwa Road, Indore-452001 (M.P.). -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/ExtensionBulletin2023E_2.pdf
- Institute websites: https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html and https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/significant_achievement.html
- Email and phone: No evidence found in these results.
- Variety-level or breeder contact for NRC 86: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Maranna, S. et al. (2021, year inferred from article number). Breeding for higher yield, early maturity, wider adaptability and waterlogging tolerance in soybean (Glycine max L.): A case study. Scientific Reports (inferred from DOI prefix) -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-021-02064-x (NRC 86 is a check only; the paper is not about the variety)
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Morphological and Physiological Performance of Indian Soybean [Glycine max (L.) Merrill] Genotypes in Respect to Drought. Legume Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4550
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Survey and Present Status of Soybean Diseases in Central India (includes a JNKVV trial with NRC 86 as a check). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381632706_Survey_and_Present_Status_of_Soybean_Diseases_in_Central_India
- AICRP/ICAR annual reports: Annual Report 2014-15, Directorate of Soybean Research, Indore, cited in the Maranna study. Full report not found. -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-021-02064-x
- KrishiKosh theses: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The IISR states that NRC 86 is in the seed chain, with breeder seed coordinated by the institute. -- https

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: AMV-7 (CSC name) / TMV-7 (Seednet name), mesta (Hibiscus sabdariffa / H. cannabinus), variety code AHS 160

Search note: four searches were run. Most results were about unrelated products (a mangosteen cultivar, military vehicles, clinical trials, sesame and groundnut "TMV 7"). Those were discarded under the strict relevance rule.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Under the AMV 7 entry for Hibiscus sabdariffa (mesta), a farming portal says the variety tolerates moisture stress. Name matched: AMV 7 (CSC name). -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/green-manure/mesta

DISEASE AND PEST
- The same portal says AMV 7 is resistant to pests and diseases. Name matched: AMV 7 (CSC name). -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/green-manure/mesta

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The same portal gives AMV 7 maturity at about 130-135 days and average yield of 10.5-13 quintal/acre. Name matched: AMV 7 (CSC name). This is a secondary aggregator, not a trial report. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/green-manure/mesta
- No trial report or multi-location data naming AMV-7 or TMV-7 mesta was found. Searches returned only the ANGRAU 2019-20 report, which names other mesta varieties (AHS-216, AMV 8, AMV 9), not AMV-7 or AHS 160. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/ANGRAU-AR-2019-20-Final_pdf.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The parentage in the record ("a selection from Tennessee White") was not confirmed by any search result. No QTL or marker studies were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No evidence found. No breeder name, developing institute or station was linked to AMV-7 mesta. The "institution: not specified" field remains unresolved.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No breeder or institute contact (email, phone, address) was linked to AMV-7 or TMV-7 mesta. The only institute-level match was the ANGRAU annual report, which names mesta varieties but not AMV-7; no contact details were drawn from it.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found for peer-reviewed papers, theses or AICRP reports on AMV-7 mesta. The ANGRAU report is an annual report but does not mention AMV-7.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for AMV-7 or TMV-7 mesta seed sources. A TMV 7 search returned only sesame and groundnut pages, which were discarded. An IndiaMART listing titled "Mesta Hybrid Seeds" (Coimbatore) does not name AMV-7 and was discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The CSC/SeedNet text in the record says "all Mesta growing areas of the country". No search result confirmed this. The only state-level mention found was for other mesta varieties, which was discarded.
- Release/notification: a TNAU crop-advisory PDF lists AMV-7 (mesta) among suitable jute and mesta varieties under a 2011-12 central variety notification. The record's release date is 28 June 2011, so the two dates should be checked against the CSC minutes. -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/pre_kharif.pdf

Name-mapping note: the CSC name AMV-7 is supported by the sources above. The Seednet name TMV-7 returned no mesta evidence, so none of the findings above can be attributed to TMV-7.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no page naming AMV-8, TMV-8 or AHS-216 with stress-tolerance data. The only roselle drought statements found concern mesta in general, not this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Pages that mention AMV 3 as a disease-resistant mesta variety are about a different variety, so I did not attribute them to AMV-8. The Vikaspedia page recommends AMV 3 for disease resistance -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/commercial-crops/mesta?lgn=en
The pest survey (Srikakulam and Vizianagaram, Kharif 2020-2024) does not name AMV-8 or AHS-216 -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/3440

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. Trial reports found name other mesta varieties (AMV 3, AMV 4, JRHS-1, JRR 17, HS 4288, HS 7910, CRIJAF R2), not AMV-8 or TMV-8 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42535-026-01723-6 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/272804446_Growth_and_Yield_Parameters_of_Mesta_Varieties_as_Influenced_by_Spacing_and_Nutrient_Sources

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No marker, QTL or genetic-diversity study naming AMV-8 or AHS-216 was returned. An ANGRAU MSc thesis on character association in roselle hemp (Ms. P. Pulli Bai) is on KrishiKosh, but its excerpt names no AMV-8 or AHS-216 line, so it is not attributed here -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/0f323dae-2b2e-4f6e-9ecb-0db46beb147b/content

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Name evidence: "Mesta (AHS-216)", the variety code.
ANGRAU Annual Report 2019-20 lists "Mesta (AHS-216)" under the university's crop varieties, with ANGRAU as the institution. No breeder name was found -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/ANGRAU-AR-2019-20-Final_pdf.pdf
Parentage ("a selection from Manaparai local") and the 2019-06-01 release date are not confirmed by any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level only; no breeder contact was found.
Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University, Lam, Guntur-522 034, Andhra Pradesh, India -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/ANGRAU%20AR%20%202020-21.pdf
Official email and phone: No evidence found. The annual report pages returned gave no email or phone number.

PUBLICATIONS
Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (2019-20 report, year of publication not stated). ANGRAU Annual Report 2019-20 (lists Mesta AHS-216 among crop varieties). -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/ANGRAU-AR-2019-20-Final_pdf.pdf
No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, or conference paper naming AMV-8 or AHS-216 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. A search for seed sources was not run separately because the search budget was used on the earlier topics. An ANGRAU seed-availability PDF (as of 10.11.2022) appeared in results, but its excerpt names no variety, so it is not attributed -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Seed_Production_Targets/balance%20of%20seed%2010.11.22.pdf
TMV-8 (Seednet name): No evidence found. The Seednet listing (crop "CASTOR (REHRI)") was not reachable through these searches, and that crop label does not match mesta, so it should be checked directly on seednet.gov.in.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. The states listed in the record (Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Maharashtra, West Bengal, Bihar) are unverified by any search result.

NOTES
- Searches run: 4 (variety and name check; breeder and institution; ANGRAU and variety-code research; combined). Seed availability was not searched on its own.
- Name check: "AMV-8" and "TMV-8" returned only other varieties or unrelated products (wine, rose, vehicle, cattle). Only "AHS-216" matched this crop, and only in ANGRAU's report.
- Recommended next steps: check the ANGRAU Regional Agricultural Research Station (Vizianagaram or Amadalavalasa) and the ICAR-CRIJAF roselle programme for breeder names, and check KrishiKosh and the CSC release notification for "AMV-8" directly.

disease_resistance.summary: Soft rot: Karthika was highly susceptible in Gudalur trials (Nilgiris, 2015-2018). Rhizome rot: rated highly susceptible in the same study, but a second grouping in the same paper placed Karthika among moderately tolerant rhizome-rot genotypes, which conflicts with the highly susceptible rating. Kollam trial (KAU): 8.0% disease incidence for Karthika, against 5.2% for Varada and 25.0% for the local check. Resistance status overall is therefore inconsistent across sources and should be treated as unresolved.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest-resistance evidence specific to Karthika was found beyond the Kollam trial pest score of 7.3. The table's column labels are ambiguous, so the score's meaning and direction (resistance or susceptibility) cannot be confirmed.

agronomic_details.yield: Official IISR extension figures: 19.0 t/ha fresh yield (equivalent to 19,000 kg/ha). The Vikaspedia package-of-practices table gives the same 19.0 t/ha figure. Input record lists average_yield as 'Kg/Ha' with no value. A KAU pot-culture study (Karamana, 2017-19) found foliar IISR Power Mix G raised Karthika yield by about 11% over control; the absolute yield for that study is not given in the digest. Other IISR figures: 21.6% dry recovery, 3.7% crude fibre, 7.2% oleoresin, 3.2% essential oil.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Only single-site or single-trial results were found (Gudalur, Kollam, Karamana); no multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: KAU trials were conducted in Kerala (Kollam; Karamana). The Gudalur trial was conducted in the Nilgiris district of Tamil Nadu (Gudalur region). No formal agro-climatic adaptation statement was found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 220-240 days (IISR extension figures and Vikaspedia package-of-practices table). In the KAU Kollam trial, Karthika matured in 240 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: In the KAU Kollam trial, Karthika rhizomes were medium bold. Dry recovery was 21%, second to Athira. Other compositional values are listed under yield. No plant architecture or morphological data was found.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Gudalur trials, Nilgiris (2015-2018): Karthika was highly susceptible to soft rot and rated highly susceptible to rhizome rot; a conflicting grouping placed it among moderately tolerant rhizome-rot genotypes. (2) KAU Kollam trial: 8.0% disease incidence (Varada 5.2%, local check 25.0%); pest score 7.3 with ambiguous labels; matured in 240 days; medium bold rhizomes; 21% dry recovery, second to Athira; the trial recommended Karthika for both fresh and dry ginger use. (3) KAU Karamana pot-culture study (2017-19): foliar IISR Power Mix G raised yield by about 11% over control. (4) BIRAC-listed product development used Karthika as a high-gingerol source, yielding a stable product with 8% gingerol.
