search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CAULIFLOWER / Karthika: the variety name and crop name differ. Seednet lists the crop as CAULIFLOWER, but every search was run for ginger, and no evidence links Karthika to cauliflower. The release year 2013-06-04 and the "Not specified" fields are from the input record; no search result confirmed them. Four searches were run.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Karthika was highly susceptible to soft rot in Gudalur trials (Nilgiris, 2015-2018), and was rated highly susceptible to rhizome rot in the same study. -- https://ijcmas.com/7-7-2018/S.%20Karthikeyan,%20et%20al.pdf
- A second grouping in the same paper placed Karthika among moderately tolerant rhizome-rot genotypes, which conflicts with the highly susceptible rating. -- https://ijcmas.com/7-7-2018/S.%20Karthikeyan,%20et%20al.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence specific to Karthika was found. -- No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- In a KAU Kollam trial, Karthika showed 8.0% disease incidence against 5.2% for Varada and 25.0% for the local check. -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/cb08.pdf
- The Kollam trial's pest score for Karthika was 7.3, but the table's column labels are ambiguous. -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/cb08.pdf
- No pest-resistance evidence specific to Karthika was found beyond these. -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Official IISR extension figures list Karthika at 19.0 t/ha fresh yield, 220-240 days maturity, 21.6% dry recovery, 3.7% crude fibre, 7.2% oleoresin and 3.2% essential oil. -- https://www.indianspices.com/sites/default/files/cultivation_practices-ginger.pdf
- The Vikaspedia package-of-practices table gives the same figures (19.0 t/ha, 220-240 days). -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/spices/ginger?lgn=en
- In the KAU Kollam trial, Karthika matured in 240 days, was medium bold, and gave 21% dry recovery, which was second to Athira. -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/cb08.pdf
- The Kollam trial recommended Karthika for both fresh and dry ginger use. -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/cb08.pdf
- A KAU pot-culture study (Karamana, 2017-19) found foliar IISR Power Mix G raised Karthika yield by about 11% over control. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348508256_Growth_nutrient_uptake_and_yield_of_ginger_as_impacted_by_potting_media_foliar_nutrition_and_microbial_inoculants
- A BIRAC-listed product development used Karthika as a high-gingerol source, yielding a stable product with 8% gingerol. -- https://birac.nic.in/product-detail.php?product=12

GENETICS AND QTL
- Karthika was developed as a somaclonal selection from Maran through tissue culture. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348508256_Growth_nutrient_uptake_and_yield_of_ginger_as_impacted_by_potting_media_foliar_nutrition_and_microbial_inoculants
- Karthika is grouped with Athira and Aswathy as a somaclonal variety developed at a centre for plant biotechnology. The page does not name the institute. -- https://permacultureplants.com/plants/ginger/iisr-mahima/
- No QTL or marker study on Karthika was found. -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Kerala Agricultural University (KAU), Thrissur, Kerala. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348508256_Growth_nutrient_uptake_and_yield_of_ginger_as_impacted_by_potting_media_foliar_nutrition_and_microbial_inoculants
- Also cited as a KAU ginger variety in the BIRAC product listing. -- https://birac.nic.in/product-detail.php?product=12
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.
- Station or division: the KAU Centre for Plant Biotechnology is named only as the origin of the somaclonal group, not for Karthika specifically. -- https://permacultureplants.com/plants/ginger/iisr-mahima/
- Note: ICAR-IISR Kozhikode is a separate institute and is not recorded as Karthika's developer. -- https://www.indianspices.com/sites/default/files/cultivation_practices-ginger.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- KAU, Thrissur – 680 656, Kerala (institute address, from the Vikaspedia variety table header). -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/spices/ginger?lgn=en
- Named breeder, email and phone for Karthika: No evidence found.
- Unrelated institute contact found: ICAR-IISR, Kozhikode – 673 012, Kerala (not the developer). -- https://naturalingredient.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/ginger-growing.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- Karthikeyan, S. et al. (2018). Evaluation of Ginger (Zingiber officinale) Genotypes for High Yield and Resistance to Soft Rot Suitable for Gudalur Regions in Nilgiris District. Int. J. Curr. Microbiol. App. Sci. 7(7): 2979-2985 -- https://doi.org/10.20546/ijcmas.2018.707.348
- Authors (year), title and report: Growth, nutrient uptake and yield of ginger as impacted by potting media, foliar nutrition and microbial inoculants. KAU Karamana trial, 2017-19. Authors not shown in the search result -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348508256_Growth_nutrient_uptake_and_yield_of_ginger_as_impacted_by_potting_media_foliar_nutrition_and_microbial_inoculants
- KAU ginger trial report (Kollam): authors and year not shown in the search result -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/cb08.pdf
- No AICRP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis or QTL paper on Karthika was found. -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No Indian source (NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, KAU seed sales or dealer) for Karthika seed was found. Search 4 returned only foreign retail ginger seed listings. -- No evidence found
- Karthika appears in a spice-nursery variety list, but that does not confirm stock. -- https://spicenurseries.in/varieties-list.php?View=details&PL=1da2601619665a078436fQ69d3591d812aUxMDAwNw

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No official state recommendation or notification for Karthika was found. -- No evidence found
- The KAU trials were run in Kerala (Kollam; Karamana). -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/cb08.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAME CHECK
variety_name "Pusa Aditi" (HI 1654) is supported by the evidence below. seednet_variety_name "PUSA KATKI" is not the same variety. Under the seednet name, the evidence refers to an early cauliflower, not the wheat. Crop mismatch: the record says wheat, Seednet says cauliflower.
Homonym: "Pusa Aditi" is also a grape hybrid and a guava name in other sources, so these results were excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Pusa Aditi (HI 1654) is listed as tolerant to wheat blast and leaf rust in the IIWBR newsletter table -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
Heat, drought, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance specific to Pusa Aditi: No evidence found. The newsletter only states in general terms that recently released varieties showed low yield penalty from terminal heat in March 2022, without naming Pusa Aditi -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
High resistance to blast, stripe rust and leaf rust for HI 1654 (Pusa Aditi) -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
Moderate resistance to leaf blight, powdery mildew, Karnal bunt and flag smut is reported for HI 1654 in the IARI Annual Report 2023 -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf (this text sits in the HI 1654 entry in that report's extracted layout; the Pusa Aditi entry itself is clearly the blast/rust entry, so treat the moderate-resistance line as tentative)
Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Released for timely sown, restricted irrigated conditions of NWPZ; average yield 51.8 q/ha -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
Potential yield 78.2 q/ha in the IIWBR identification table -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
Maturity and duration: No evidence found for HI 1654 specifically.
Multi-location trial data: No Pusa Aditi-specific trial data found beyond the averages above.

GENETICS AND QTL
Pusa Aditi-specific QTL or marker study: No evidence found. The IARI Annual Report 2018-19 describes marker-assisted pyramiding of all three rust resistance types in wheat, but does not name HI 1654 -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/IARIANNUALREPORT2018_19_30072019.pdf
Parentage: The task record says "Not specified". The IIWBR compendium gives a pedigree string for HI 1654 (Pusa Aditi) that is garbled in extraction and needs checking against the original -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Indore, for the NWPZ release -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. The IIWBR newsletter's "Roop Ram, PA, ICAR-IIWBR Regional Station" entry belongs to a different institute and is not the breeder -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
Station role: IARI Regional Station Indore is described as dedicated to bread and durum wheat research for central India -- https://www.youtube.com/@IARI_RSIndore_Pusaindore

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder: No evidence found.
Institute: ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Indore (Madhya Pradesh). Official email, phone and postal address: No evidence found in the retrieved text. The only institute contact-type URL found is the IARI main site -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Agricultural_Research_Institute (secondary source citing www.iari.res.in). The IARI Regional Station Pusa (Bihar) address in the results is a different station and should not be used.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2023). Annual Report 2023, Indian Agricultural Research Institute. ICAR-IARI, New Delhi -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2022). Wheat and Barley Newsletter, Vol. 162. ICAR-IIWBR, Karnal -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2024). Compendium of Wheat Varieties Notified in India During 2018-2023 (RB-51). ICAR-IIWBR, Karnal -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2023). Pusa Krishi Vigyan Mela 2023 press release. IARI -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Press_release_PKVM_2023_01032023.pdf (lists HI 1654 among varieties displayed)
Peer-reviewed or thesis or KrishiKosh record specific to HI 1654: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Pusa Aditi (HI 1654): No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales or dealers.
PUSA KATKI (Seednet name): No evidence of a Pusa Katki seller in the results. The RPCAU Directorate of Seed, Dholi lists cauliflower planting material at KVKs only as Sabour Agrim -- https://rpcau.ac.in/directorate-of-seed-dholi/ . The NSC vegetable list shows cauliflower varieties PSBK-1, PSBK-25 and PSB-1 and hybrid Sheetal, not Pusa Katki -- https://indiaseeds.com/vegetables

RECOMMENDED STATES
The IARI Annual Report 2023 gives the release area as the NWPZ, timely sown, restricted irrigated conditions -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
The state-by-state list in the input (Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan except Kota and Udaipur, western UP except Jhansi, Jammu and Kathua, Una and Paonta Valley, Tarai Uttarakhand) could not be verified against a retrieved notification. Only the NWPZ zone is confirmed.
Release date: The input gives 2022-10-26. The compendium table has a date string beside the entry that reads 06.03.2023 and is ambiguous; verify against the Gazette or CVRC minutes.

SEEDNET RECORD, PUSA KATKI (CAULIFLOWER) -- SEPARATE EVIDENCE
Pusa Katki is an early cauliflower from IARI New Delhi, maturing October-November -- http://eagri.org/eagri50/HORT281/lec13.html
Reference: Pusa Katki, Haryana Journal of Horticultural Sciences 29(3-4): 223-224 and 265-266 -- https://eurekamag.com/research/001/512/001512452.php
The Seednet name and crop therefore appear to be a mismatch with the wheat variety. Check the Seednet record before using it.

drought_tolerance.technical_details: No variety-specific drought data. The G3 genetics paper mentions drought tolerance only in an Arabidopsis gene context, which is unrelated to this variety's performance.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: It is an early-season, tropical-type (Indian) cauliflower sown mid-July to August and maturing in Sept-Nov. Lecture notes classify Indian cauliflower as heat tolerant. An airitilibrary abstract (Taiwan) refers to a 'heat-tolerant seedling of Pusa Katki' used in curd initiation research. These are mostly generic classifications or snippets, not controlled trials of this variety.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: Only generic statements are available (cauliflower is moderately tolerant to salinity). No variety-specific salinity data.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: One source says 'Indian types are resistant to water logging and heat'. This is a generic type-level claim and not specific to Pusa Katki.

submergence_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence found. The submergence result retrieved concerns rice (Swarna-Sub1), not cauliflower.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: A Scribd lecture snippet places 'Resistant to downy mildew' adjacent to Pusa Katki's description, but it is ambiguous which variety it refers to and it is not verified. Not confirmed.
disease_resistance.technical_details: No resistance genes or screening data found.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: Multiple citations and extension or academic references describe the variety (ICAR advisory, state packages, a genetics paper, a review and a Taiwan abstract), so the 'at least one citation' criterion is met. However, stress trait evidence is weak and mostly generic: heat adaptation by cauliflower type, plus one snippet on a heat-tolerant seedling. There is no verified yield figure, no disease or pest resistance, no flood or salinity data, and no Gujarat-specific evidence. This does not reach the 75 tier (a verified stress trait with a citation), so it stays at 60.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Early-season tropical cauliflower; 60-80 days; medium plant with bluish-green waxy leaves; sown July-Aug; possible heat adaptation (weak evidence)
dashboard_data.seasons: Early/first-season crop: sowing mid-July to early August; curds Sept-Nov

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Pusa Katki is an early-maturing (60-80 days), tropical-type cauliflower from IARI, widely listed in Indian extension materials for July-August sowing. Stress tolerance evidence is limited to generic heat adaptation and a single heat-tolerant seedling mention; there is no verified data on disease, pest, salinity or flood tolerance. Evidence quality is low-to-moderate, and nothing is specific to Gujarat.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Early cauliflower with medium plant and bluish-green waxy leaves, sown mid-July to August at 60x60 cm, maturing in 60-80 days. Yield is not given in the input record (a package table suggests about 20 t/ha, unverified).
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Only weak, generic heat adaptation is indicated; drought, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance and disease and pest resistance are undocumented. Downy mildew resistance is an unverified snippet. Overall stress tolerance is not demonstrated.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Shobha (CSC name) / PUSA SHUBRA (Seednet name)

Name check: Searches on "Pusa Shobha" returned onion evidence only. Searches on "PUSA SHUBRA" (spelled "Pusa Shubhra" in the literature) returned cauliflower evidence only. Nothing links the two. The record's parentage (MGS-2-3, 15-1-1, D-96) matches the cauliflower Pusa Shubhra, not the onion. The Seednet crop (CAULIFLOWER) and the CSC crop (onion) therefore conflict, and the Seednet entry should be checked before the record is finalised.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pusa Shubhra (cauliflower): developed as a black rot and curd blight resistant cauliflower -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijh-50-4-017
- Pusa Shubhra (cauliflower): recurrent selection was used to transfer resistance from donor to recurrent parent to develop 'Pusa shubhra', a cauliflower variety resistant to black rot, curd blight and riceyness -- https://www.isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/493/442
- Pusa Shubhra (cauliflower): a 1991 reference reports it as field-resistant to black rot and curd blight -- https://eurekamag.com/research/001/512/001512452.php
- Pusa Shobha (onion): No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The searches returned only quality and processing data.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Pusa Shubhra (cauliflower): listed among Alternaria leaf spot sources in a breeding review -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370321881_Seventy_five_years_of_research_and_development_in_cauliflower_and_cabbage_A_journey_from_temperate_to_tropicalization_and_aristocrats_to_commoners
- Pusa Shubhra (cauliflower): black rot resistance is governed by dominant polygenes in the source lines MGS 2-3 and Pusa Kea -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.4489/MYCO.2003.31.3.173
- Pusa Shobha (onion): No evidence found for disease or pest resistance.
- Note: the byjus and vedantu quiz pages naming Pusa Shubhra as resistant to white rust or chilli mosaic virus were discarded as unreliable and inconsistent with the primary sources.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pusa Shubhra (cauliflower): Average curd weight is 700-800 g, curds are non-ricey, and it takes 125-130 days for 50% harvest. -- https://www.biologydiscussion.com/vegetable-breeding/cauliflower-origin-production-and-varieties-india/68621
- Pusa Shubhra (cauliflower): yield is given as an average of 12 t/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330564347_Scientific_Cultivation_of_Cauliflower_Brassica_oleracea_L_var_botrytis. A second source gives 220-250 quintals/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313098865_Cole_crops. These two yield figures conflict and should be checked.
- Pusa Shobha (onion): an ICAR note reports a mid-maturity group, with bulbs ready 140-160 days after transplanting -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-06/ICAR-News-July-September-2019_Low-Res.pdf
- Pusa Shobha (onion): bulb weight 70-100 g and yield potential of 33-35 t/ha in the same ICAR note -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-06/ICAR-News-July-September-2019_Low-Res.pdf
- Pusa Shobha (onion): a crop duration of February to June under north Indian plains -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/145390/54400/410705
- Pusa Shobha (onion): dehydration and storage quality trial results -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/view/145390

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pusa Shubhra (cauliflower): a selection from a triple cross of MGS-2-3, 15-1-1 and D-96, developed at IARI, New Delhi -- https://www.biologydiscussion.com/vegetable-breeding/cauliflower-origin-production-and-varieties-india/68621. A 2013 review instead says it was developed from Pua kea and MGS2-3 lines -- https://www.isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/493/442
- Pusa Shubhra (cauliflower): MGS 2-3, Pusa Kea and S-445 were resistant to black rot, shown to be governed by dominant polygenes -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.4489/MYCO.2003.31.3.173
- Pusa Shobha (onion): No evidence found for QTL, marker or genetic studies.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Pusa Shobha (onion): developed at Division of Vegetable Science, ICAR-IARI, New Delhi -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-06/ICAR-News-July-September-2019_Low-Res.pdf. No breeder name was found.
- Pusa Shubhra (cauliflower): the developers are Ram Singh, S.S. Chatterjee, V. Swarup, B.M. Trivedi and Bineeta Sen, Division of Vegetable Crops, IARI, New Delhi -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijh-50-4-017

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact was found for either name. Institute-level contacts are given below.
- IARI Director: Dr Ashok Kumar Singh; email director@iari.res.in; phone +91-11-25842367; postal address ICAR-IARI, Pusa Campus, New Delhi-110012 -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-12/ICAR-INSTITUTE-PROFILE_.pdf
- Division of Vegetable Science: Dr Krishna Kumar Gangopadhyay, Head (Acting); email head_veg@iari.res.in (as shown on the page); postal address ICAR-IARI, Pusa Campus, New Delhi-110012 -- https://www.iari.res.in/en/introduction.php?div_id=38
- IARI general contact page: info@iari.res.in; Pusa Helpline 011-25841670 / 25841039 -- https://www.iari.res.in/en/contact-us.php

PUBLICATIONS
- Singh, R., Chatterjee, S.S., Swarup, V., Trivedi, B.M., & Sen, B. (1993). Evolution of Pusa shubhra: A resistant cauliflower to black rot and curd blight diseases. Indian Journal of Horticulture 50(4): 370-372 -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijh-50-4-017
- Chatterjee, S.S., Swarup, V., Trivedi, B.M., & Sen, B. (1991). Cauliflower 'Pusa Shubhra' is field-resistant to black-rot and curd-blight. Indian Horticulture 36(2): 31, 33-34 -- cited in https://eurekamag.com/research/001/512/001512452.php (reference listed on that page, not the paper itself; no DOI found)
- Authors not shown in the retrieved snippet (2024). Pusa Shobha: Onion for Dehydration. Indian Horticulture 69(2): 36-38 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/view/145390
- Authors not shown in the retrieved snippet (2013). Vegetable Science 40(2): 121-136, a cauliflower resistance-breeding review that discusses Pusa Shubhra -- https://www.isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/493/442

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Pusa Shobha (onion): No variety-specific evidence found. The ICAR and Krishi Jagran pages list the variety but give no seed source.
- Pusa Shubhra (cauliflower): No variety-specific evidence found.
- General IARI seed channel

drought.details: No variety-specific drought tolerance evidence found. The BAU variety page describes the variety as suitable for rainfed upland ecology, which is a site-suitability statement and not a tested tolerance result. Note: the digest's searches used the name 'Sabour Agrim' only; no retrieved page used the SBECF code.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat tolerance evidence found. The only heat-related remark (that cauliflower bolts in extreme heat) is a general crop remark and was discarded as not variety-specific.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in this variety.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence of disease resistance in this variety. The Farmer FIRST demonstration paper lists integrated pest and disease management as part of a technology package, not as a varietal trait.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence of pest resistance in this variety. The same Farmer FIRST paper references pest management only as part of a technology package.

agronomic_details.yield: BAU expected yield: 180-190 q/ha. Field results reported in the digest range from 184.18 q/ha (Purnea KVK, marketable curd yield) to 223.5 q/ha (Arwal, highest marketable curd yield at 15 July transplanting). Other reported values: 185.26 q/ha (Bhagalpur demonstration, flagged as internally inconsistent) and 208 q/ha maximum (Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh). The original data field 'average_yield' is given as Kg/Ha without a value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources as a formal stability analysis. Results come from multiple locations and seasons (Arwal two-year trial, Saharanpur four kharif seasons), but no stability statistics were reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Described by BAU as an early-season cauliflower suited to rainfed upland ecology. Trial sites in the digest are Arwal, Bhagalpur and Purnea districts of Bihar and Saharanpur in Uttar Pradesh. The digest contains no explicit agro-climatic fit analysis.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: No day count found in searched sources. BAU lists a late September to October maturity group, with curds maturing mid to late October.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources beyond the description as an early-season cauliflower.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Arwal, Bihar, two-year kharif trial (2013-14): transplanting on 15 July gave the highest marketable curd yield, 223.5 q/ha, with 430.8 g marketable curds. (2) Bhagalpur district, kharif 2017-18 and 2018-19 demonstrations: reported demonstration yield 185.26 q/ha; the same abstract gives 287.50 q/ha for farmers' practice while describing the demonstration as higher, which is internally inconsistent, so these figures should be treated with caution. (3) Purnea district KVK front-line demonstrations: marketable curd yield 184.18 q/ha versus 154.06 q/ha for the local check, B:C ratio 6.28. (4) Saharanpur (Uttar Pradesh) multi-location trials over four kharif seasons: maximum yield 208 q/ha for Sabour Agrim versus 157 q/ha for the local variety, with curds reported as about 30 percent higher yielding. (5) Seed-production trials at BAC Sabour (2019-20 and 2020-21) used Sabour Agrim for curd-cutting and micronutrient seed-yield work; no yield values were reported in the digest. (6) Rabi 2022-23 trial on zinc and boron effects on seed quality of the variety; no result values were reported in the digest.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. No SNP, SSR or other marker data found for this variety.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. The QTL study on time to curd induction (PMC5807883) does not name Sabour Agrim and was excluded. A diversity study from RPCAU Pusa places Sabour Agrim in a cluster with the highest total yield and suggests it as a parent for hybridization; this is a diversity-analysis finding, not a QTL or mapping result.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SABOUR AGRIM EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: Searches used both "Sabour Agrim (SBECF-01/09)" and the Seednet form "Sabour Agrim (SBECF- 01/09)". No retrieved page used the SBECF code, so every finding below refers to the cultivar name "Sabour Agrim" (cauliflower, Bihar Agricultural University, Sabour). The release year (2013) matches the BAU page. I did not retrieve a Seednet portal page or CSC minutes.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. The searches returned only general cauliflower remarks (for example, that it bolts in extreme heat), which I discarded as not variety-specific. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/jkv-4-1-018 (general remark, not used as variety evidence)
- The BAU variety page describes it as suitable for rainfed upland ecology, which is a site-suitability statement and not a tested tolerance result. -- https://bausabour-ac-in.translate.goog/varieties-developed.aspx?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance in this variety. The Farmer FIRST demonstration paper lists integrated pest and disease management as part of a technology package, not as a varietal trait. -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020.v9.i2.11110/impression-of-off-season-vegetable-varietal-adoption-demonstration-on-the-yield-and-economics-of-early-cauliflower-brassica-oleracea-var-botrytis-cv-sabour-agrim-in-bhagalpur-district-of-bihar

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- BAU lists it as an early-season cauliflower with a late September to October maturity group, maturing mid to late October, and an expected yield of 180-190 q/ha. -- https://bausabour-ac-in.translate.goog/varieties-developed.aspx?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc
- Arwal, Bihar, two-year kharif trial (2013-14): transplanting on 15 July gave the highest marketable curd yield, 223.5 q/ha, with 430.8 g marketable curds. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/jkv-4-1-018
- Bhagalpur district, kharif 2017-18 and 2018-19 demonstrations: the reported demonstration yield was 185.26 q/ha. The same abstract gives 287.50 q/ha for farmers' practice while describing the demonstration as higher, which is internally inconsistent, so treat these figures with caution. -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020.v9.i2.11110/impression-of-off-season-vegetable-varietal-adoption-demonstration-on-the-yield-and-economics-of-early-cauliflower-brassica-oleracea-var-botrytis-cv-sabour-agrim-in-bhagalpur-district-of-bihar
- Purnea district KVK front-line demonstrations: marketable curd yield of 184.18 q/ha versus 154.06 q/ha for the local check, B:C ratio 6.28. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2019/vol7issue4/PartAN/7-4-451-560.pdf
- Saharanpur (Uttar Pradesh) multi-location trials over four kharif seasons: maximum yield of 208 q/ha for Sabour Agrim, against 157 q/ha for the local variety, with curds reported as about 30 percent higher yielding. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-6-2017/B.P.%20Shahi,%20et%20al.pdf
- Seed-production trials at BAC Sabour (2019-20 and 2020-21) used Sabour Agrim for curd-cutting and micronutrient seed-yield work. -- https://hal.science/hal-05337924v1

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL or marker evidence found for this variety. The QTL study on time to curd induction (PMC5807883) does not name Sabour Agrim, so I excluded it.
- A diversity study from RPCAU Pusa places Sabour Agrim in a cluster with the highest total yield and suggests it as a parent for hybridization. This is a diversity-analysis finding, not a genetic mapping result. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/special/11/Pramila2,%20et%20al.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Bihar Agricultural University, Sabour, Bhagalpur, Bihar 813210. The BAU variety list names Sabour Agrim (2013) under cauliflower. -- https://bausabour-ac-in.translate.goog/varieties-developed.aspx?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc
- Development unit: BAU's Department of Horticulture (Vegetable and Floriculture) at BAC Sabour, which seed collection and seed-production papers cite. -- https://hal.science/hal-05337924v1 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/282839893_Performance_of_Early_Cauliflower_Variety_Sabour_Agrim_vis_a_vis_Different_Dates_of_Transplanting_in_Arwal_District_of_Bihar
- Named lead breeder: No evidence found. No retrieved page names the scientist who developed Sabour Agrim. Several papers name trial authors and the Sabour department, but none names the breeder.
- Excluded: The SABAGRIs incubator page (https://www.sabagris.com/) names BAU officials, but it is an agribusiness incubator and not the breeding unit, so I did not attribute these contacts to the variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Directorate of Research, Bihar Agricultural University, Sabour-813210, Bhagalpur, Bihar. Phones: 0641-2451039 / 0641-2451056 / 0641-2452614. Emails: registrarbau2015@gmail.com / drbau1908@gmail.com. -- https://bausabour-ac-in.translate.goog/varieties-developed.aspx?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc
- Aggregator listing (less authoritative): phone +916412452604, email registrar.bau.sabour@gmail.com. -- https://www.edarabia.com/bihar-agricultural-university-sabour-bhagalpur-bihar-india/
- Aggregator listing (less authoritative): Opposite Railway Station, Sabour Road, Sabour, Bhagalpur-813210. -- https://www.justdial.com/Bhagalpur/Bihar-Agricultural-University-Opposite-Railway-Station-Sabour/9999PX641-X641-130510173905-J3C9_BZDET
- Breeder-level contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Singh, K. P., Kumar, R., Sohane, R. K., & Das, A. K. (2015). Performance of Early Cauliflower Variety Sabour Agrim vis a vis Different Dates of Transplanting in Arwal District of Bihar. Journal of Krishi Vigyan 4(1): 84-87. -- DOI 10.5958/2349-4433.2015.00067.7 ; https://indianjournals.com/article/jkv-4-1-018 (ResearchGate lists different authors for the same title: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/282839893_Performance_of_Early_Cauliflower_Variety_Sabour_Agrim_vis_a_vis_Different_Dates_of_Transplanting_in_Arwal_District_of_Bihar)
- Kant, K., Ghanshyam, Gupta, S. K., Patel, A. B., Kumar, S., Kumar, A., Vishwakarma, R., & Sohane, R. K. (2020). Impression of off season vegetable varietal adoption demonstration on the yield and economics of Early Cauliflower (Brassica oleracea var. botrytis) cv. Sabour Agrim in Bhagalpur District of Bihar. Journal of Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry 9(2): 1754-1757. -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020.v9.i2.11110/impression-of-off-season-vegetable-varietal-adoption-demonstration-on-the-yield-and-economics-of-early-cauliflower-brassica-oleracea-var-botrytis-cv-sabour-agrim-in-bhagalpur-district-of-bihar
- Shahi, B. P., et al. (2017). Impact Assessment of Cauliflower Variety Sabour Agrim in Saharanpur (UP), India. International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences 6(6): 111-117. -- DOI 10.20546/ijcmas.2017.606.013 ; https://www.ijcmas.com/6-6-2017/B.P.%20Shahi,%20et%20al.pdf
- Singh, A. P. (2019). Yield gap analysis of early cauliflower (Brassica oleracea var. botrytis) cv. Sabour Agrim through front line demonstrations. International Journal of Chemical Studies 7(4): 2271-2273. (Only the first author's name was captured.) -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2019/vol7issue4/PartAN/7-4-451-560.pdf

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. The digest states no evidence was found for CSH 27 specifically for flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Grain mould tolerance is listed for CSH 27 in the grain-mould tolerance and lodging-resistance description of the source table. No other disease resistance was found for CSH 27 in the searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. Shoot fly and stem borer tolerance appears in the same source, but the layout places it beside the CSV 27 entry, so it is not attributed to CSH 27 and is not counted as evidence.

agronomic_details.yield: The dual-purpose hybrid is reported at 39 q/ha grain (equivalent to 3,900 kg/ha) and 136 q/ha fodder (equivalent to 13,600 kg/ha). The figure is truncated in the source table, so the value is not fully confirmed. The input average_yield field is recorded only as units (Kg/Ha) with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data was found for CSH 27.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for rainfed kharif cultivation in zone I (per the source listing of Rajasthan, North Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu). Input adaptation_ecology: rainfed condition in Kharif season.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not confirmed. The source table row shows a value of 106 days, but the column is not labelled in the retrieved text. The same row lists medium maturity.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Lodging resistance is listed for CSH 27 in the same source row as the grain-mould tolerance description. No other morphological characteristics were found.
agronomic_details.field_trials: One result: a dual-purpose hybrid reported at 39 q/ha grain and 136 q/ha fodder (figure truncated in the source table). No multi-location or other field-trial results for CSH 27 were found. Results for CSV 27, a different variety, were discarded.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CSH-27 / CH-27 (sorghum)

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Named in the grain-mould tolerance and lodging-resistance description for the CSH 27 entry; the same table row also lists medium maturity -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280066083_Sorghum_cultivation_for_value-added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives
- Shoot fly and stem borer tolerance appears in the same source, but the layout places it beside the CSV 27 entry, so I am not attributing it to CSH 27 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280066083_Sorghum_cultivation_for_value-added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found for CSH 27 specifically.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Grain mould tolerance is listed for CSH 27 (see STRESS TOLERANCE above) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280066083_Sorghum_cultivation_for_value-added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives
- Shoot fly and stem borer: attribution to CSH 27 is ambiguous (see STRESS TOLERANCE); not counted as CSH 27 evidence.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Dual-purpose hybrid reported at 39 q/ha grain and 136 q/ha fodder (the figure is truncated in the source table) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280066083_Sorghum_cultivation_for_value-added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives
- Maturity: the table row shows a value of 106 days, but the column is not labelled in the retrieved text, so it is unconfirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280066083_Sorghum_cultivation_for_value-added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives
- Multi-location or field-trial results for CSH 27: No evidence found. Results returned for CSV 27 (a different variety, not this hybrid) were discarded, including https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/3-Sorghum-Kharif-Grain-Breeding-Report-agm23.pdf, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318440517_Production_potential_of_improved_grain_sorghum_cultivars_Sorghum_bicolor_under_staggered_plantings_in_non-traditional_areas_of_Eastern_India, https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020/vol9issue2S/PartA/S-9-2-12-481.pdf and https://www.envirobiotechjournals.com/issues/article_abstract.php?aid=14401&iid=391&jid=1

GENETICS AND QTL
- Cross listed for the CSH 27 entry as "A × CB 11" (the column carrying "279" is unlabelled); this partly contradicts the "Not specified" parentage in the input -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Directorate of Sorghum Research (DSR), Hyderabad, listed for CSH 27 (SPH 1644) with 2012 release year -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum
- Lead breeder or scientist name for CSH 27: No evidence found. The breeder named on the CSV 27 (SPV 1870) technology sheet was excluded because it is a different variety -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/SORGHUM_VARIETAL_Technology_AT_A_GLANCE.pdf
- Seednet name CH-27 under CHILLIES: No evidence found. Chilli results (for example https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sirarakhong_Hathei_chilli and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhiwapur_chilli) are unrelated varieties and were discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Directorate of Sorghum Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad 500 030, Andhra Pradesh, India -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384766_Sorghum_Vision_2030
- Institute website as printed: www.sorghum.res.in -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384766_Sorghum_Vision_2030
- Institute address as printed in the DSR brochure: Directorate of Sorghum Research (DSR), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad 500030, Andhra Pradesh -- https://www.millets.res.in/press/DSR_NationalScienceDay_Feature.pdf
- Breeder-level email or phone: No evidence found for CSH 27. A telephone and email (umakanth@sorghum.res.in, 091-40-24018651) were seen on the CSV 27 sheet and excluded because they belong to a different variety -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/SORGHUM_VARIETAL_Technology_AT_A_GLANCE.pdf
- No institute contact page URL for CSH 27 was found beyond the website above.

PUBLICATIONS
- Chapke RR, Bhagwat VR, Patil JV (eds.) (2013). Sorghum cultivation for value-added diversified products and sweet sorghum perspectives. Directorate of Sorghum Research, Hyderabad (ISBN 81-89335-46-4) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280066083_Sorghum_cultivation_for_value-added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Fifty years of research and development under All-India Coordinated Research Project on Sorghum. Report (AICRP Sorghum) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum
- Peer-reviewed papers, theses, KrishiKosh items or DOIs dedicated to CSH 27: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for CSH 27 at NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealers. Only one search was run for this topic (within the four-query limit), and it returned nothing specific to this hybrid.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Recommended for rainfed kharif cultivation in Rajasthan, North Gujarat, UP, AP and Tamil Nadu (zone I) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280066083_Sorghum_cultivation_for_value-added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives
- Same five-state listing in the DSR-linked Fifty-years report -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum
- Rajasthan medium-to-heavy soil zones list CSH 27 among recommended hybrids (secondary news source) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-sorghum-varieties-for-rajasthan/
- Tamil Nadu statewide list includes CSH 27 (secondary news source) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-sorghum-varieties-for-tamil-nadu/

NAME AND TYPE NOTES
- CSC release name: CSH-27 (sorghum hybrid, not a variety). Variety code SPH-1644 matches the Fifty-years report.
- Seednet name CH-27 under CHILLIES: the record is not supported by any sorghum evidence, and the crop assignment looks like a portal error. No chilli evidence was found for CH-27.

drought.details: CH-27 plants demonstrate an inability of cells to combat stress. While MS-12, a female parent, is known for drought tolerance, this specific trait is not confirmed for the CH-27 hybrid itself.

heat.details: General breeding objectives for chilli hybrids released by PAU, including CH-27, aim for resistance to abiotic stresses like heat. However, no specific heat tolerance level or mechanisms for CH-27 have been detailed in the provided results.

salinity.details: Alkaline soils with high salt concentration are indicated as unsuitable for chilli hybrids including CH-27, suggesting low tolerance.

flood.details: CH-27 is identified as a sudden wilt susceptible cultivar, a condition that can be exacerbated by waterlogging. No evidence of flood tolerance is provided; rather, susceptibility to sudden wilt indicates potential vulnerability to excess moisture.

disease_resistance.summary: CH-27 is a multiple disease resistant chilli hybrid, specifically resistant to leaf curl virus, fruit rot, and root knot.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance beyond diseases listed (e.g., leaf curl virus, which is sometimes categorized under biotic stress in general pest/disease contexts) is detailed for CH-27 in the search results.

agronomic_details.stability: CH-27 has spread to several North Western states, suggesting good adaptation and stability across different environments within these regions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted to Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Jharkhand. It has shown adaptability and spread in North Western states.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plants are spreading and tall, continuing to bear fruits for a long time. Fruits are medium long (6.7-7.5 cm), thin, and pungent (0.8% capsaicin).
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field trials have been conducted for CH-27, utilizing designs such as the α-lattice square design in three replications.

drought.details: The variety is described as suited to rainfed kharif cultivation in Gujarat, and the same abstract links it to rainfed conditions. The digest gives no drought tolerance mechanism, trait score or stress-trial data, so a drought tolerance level cannot be assigned. Non-lodging and non-shattering habit is reported, but it is not linked to drought tolerance in the evidence.

disease_resistance.summary: Reported resistant to leaf blast, neck blast and grain smut (evidence refers to the GV-5 / WV-297 little millet). The same disease reaction is reported in the AGRESCO-linked abstract record (dated 2026 in the digest).

pest_resistance.summary: Resistant reaction to shoot fly (evidence refers to the GV-5 / WV-297 little millet). The same shoot fly reaction is reported in the AGRESCO-linked abstract record.

agronomic_details.yield: Grain yield 1748 kg/ha, averaged over eleven state trials (2020-21 to 2023-24). This is 12.78% above the local check GV-4 and about 31.35% above the national check JK-8. The 31.35% figure over JK-8 is the same in both sources. The figure over OLM-203 conflicts between sources: the JABB paper gives 31.20%, while the AGRESCO release proposal gives 10.55%.
agronomic_details.stability: Yield is reported as an average across eleven state trials. No stability analysis or environment-specific yield data were found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for kharif sowing in the little millet growing region of Gujarat, under rainfed conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Non-lodging, non-shattering little millet type; 1000-seed weight 2.22 g; 5.9 productive tillers per plant; panicle length 34.5 cm.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Eleven state trials, 2020-21 to 2023-24: mean grain yield 1748 kg/ha, 12.78% above local check GV-4, about 31.35% above national check JK-8, and 31.20% above OLM-203 per the JABB paper (10.55% per the AGRESCO release proposal; the two sources conflict). Trial-level yields for individual locations were not found in the digest.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Released as a non-lodging, non-shattering little millet type; the breeding abstract reports this under the test name WV-297 (GV-5 release name) -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/3747
- Described as suited to rainfed kharif cultivation in Gujarat; the same abstract links it to rainfed conditions -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/3747

DISEASE AND PEST
- Reported resistant to leaf blast, neck blast and grain smut, and a resistant reaction to shoot fly (evidence refers to the GV-5 / WV-297 little millet) -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/3747
- Same disease and shoot fly reaction reported in the AGRESCO-linked abstract record -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/3747 (abstract, 2026)
- No evidence found for the Seednet name G-5 under CHILLIES. The searches for "G-5 chillies" returned only foreign chilli seed shops and a Goa chilli (Khola) page, which are unrelated and were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity 90-100 days, early maturing, 1000-seed weight 2.22 g, 5.9 productive tillers per plant, panicle length 34.5 cm (WV-297 / GV-5) -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/3747
- Grain yield 1748 kg/ha, 12.78% above local check GV-4 and about 31.35% above national check JK-8, averaged over eleven state trials, 2020-21 to 2023-24 -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/3747
- Release proposal at the 20th AGRESCO house gives the same 1748 kg/ha and 31.35% over JK-8, but reports 10.55% over OLM-203, whereas the JABB paper gives 31.20% over OLM-203. The two sources conflict on the OLM-203 figure -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//20th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_775.pdf
- Recommended for kharif sowing in the little millet growing region of Gujarat -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//20th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_775.pdf
- Release date: the record gives 2025-03-13. No notification page or gazette entry confirming this date was found. The AGRESCO proceedings are dated 2024 and the paper is dated 2026.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pure line selection from local germplasm collected at Mahal village, Ahwa taluka, Dang District; tested as genotype WV-297 -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/3747
- Parentage in the record is "Not specified"; the selection history above is the only origin information found.
- No QTL, marker or genetic study on GV-5 was found. The Magnaporthe virulence paper (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10203591/) and the finger millet blast screening (https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2023/Dec/27%20dec%2023/2023_IJPSS_110972/Revised-ms_IJPSS_110972_v1.pdf) concern other millets and were discarded. The foxtail millet diversity paper (http://www.plantarchives.org/article/237-245%20(01).pdf) was discarded for the same reason.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Authors of the GV-5 paper: P.A. Vavdiya, G.D. Vadodariya, H.E. Patil and B.N. Chaudhary, all at the Hill Millet Research Station, NAU, Waghai (Dangs) -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/3747
- The AGRESCO release proposal assigns the action item to an Associate Research Scientist, HMRS, Waghai (name not given) -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//20th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_775.pdf
- The paper's authors are the closest evidence of breeders. Named breeder of record is not confirmed by any source.
- Developing institution: Navsari Agricultural University, Hill Millet Research Station, Waghai, Dist. The Dangs. The station was established in 1954-55 with a mandate for early maturing, high yielding paddy and small millets -- https://nau.in/unithome/Hill%20Millet%20Research%20Station%20Waghai
- Station is listed as a small millet centre within NAU's 25 research centres -- https://nau.in/index

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or personal contact was found for GV-5 or HMRS.
- Institute-level contact page: https://nau.in (NAU home page; headquarters at Navsari). No official email, phone or postal address for HMRS was found in the retrieved text.
- Names as found: P.A. Vavdiya (corresponding author, HMRS Waghai, Dangs); G.D. Vadodariya; H.E. Patil; B.N. Chaudhari(Chaudhary in the author list) -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/3747
- Station location as found: Hill Millet Research Station, Waghai, Dist. The Dangs, cross-section latitude 20.77 N, longitude 73.50 E -- https://nau.in/unithome/Hill%20Millet%20Research%20Station%20Waghai (a second coordinate pair on the same page, 20.807545 N 73.022260 E, places the farm 4 km from Gandevi town, so the page is internally inconsistent)

PUBLICATIONS
- Vavdiya, P.A., Patil, H.E., Vadodariya, G.D., & Chaudhari, B.N. (2026). 'GV-5' (Mauli): Early Maturing Little Millet (Panicum sumatrense L.) Variety for Cultivation in Gujarat, India. Journal of Advances in Biology & Biotechnology 29(3): 423-434 -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/3747 ; DOI 10.9734/jabb/2026/v29i33747
- Note: the page's author list gives P.A. Vavdiya and G.D. Vadodariya first. The "How to cite" line gives the order used above.
- 20th AGRESCO proceedings, NAU Navsari (2024, virtual), Section 20.1.1.16 "Little millet: Gujarat Vari-5 (GV-5: Mavli)" release proposal. Authors not listed. Report -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//20th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_775.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report entry or peer-reviewed paper beyond the JABB article was found for GV-5.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The searches did not return any seed sale listing from NSC, the Gujarat state seed corporation, KVK, NAU seed sales or private dealers for GV-5 or G-5. A dedicated seed-availability search was not run because the search budget was used on the variety, breeder, research and name-check queries.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Gujarat (little millet growing region, kharif season) -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//20th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_775.pdf
- Gujarat (state release, rainfed conditions) -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/3747

NAME AND CROP NOTES
- Variety name GV-5 (also called Mavli / Mauli / Gujarat Vari-5) refers to little millet (Panicum sumatrense). The crop field "millet" is therefore ambiguous; the evidence supports little millet only.
- Seednet name G-5 under CHILLIES: no evidence found. The seednet crop label "CHILLIES" conflicts with the little millet evidence, so the Seednet record should be checked against the release minutes.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Gujarat Chilli 3 (variety_name) / GAJARAT CHILLI-2 (seednet_variety_name), chilli, S.D. Agricultural University, released 2012-07-24, variety code H0703010

NAME MAPPING NOTE: The four searches returned no page that names "Gujarat Chilli 3", "GAJARAT CHILLI-2", or SDAU as the source for this variety. The only Gujarat-specific match is a generic reference to "Gujarat Chilli-1 and Chilli-2". I could not open seednet.gov.in, so I could not check the Seednet record. Every finding below is therefore generic or about other varieties. Under each heading I state which name, if either, the evidence could relate to.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for either name (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence). -- https://www.ijsat.org/papers/2025/2/3679.pdf (searched; no variety-specific tolerance data)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for either name. Nearby, a Gujarat-based chilli leaf curl virus screening study names other resistance sources (KSP 1234 and US 730) but not this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269397457_Chilli_Capsicum_annuum_L_breeding_in_India_An_overview
Nearby, a Gujarat-based chilli leaf curl virus screening study identifies KSP 1234 and US 730 as stable resistance sources, not Gujarat Chilli 3 or GAJARAT CHILLI-2. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269397457_Chilli_Capsicum_annuum_L_breeding_in_India_An_overview

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found for either name. Trial data on the AAU station (Anand) concern other cultivars, including S-49 and GVC-111, and are not this variety. -- https://aau.in/college-menu/251/236
Gujarat-level context: Gujarat-released chillies are described as high-yielding with moderate pungency, but no yield figure is given for this variety. -- https://www.ijsat.org/papers/2025/2/3679.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for either name. The only related item is a 2018 AAU report on CGMS hybrid seed production in chilli, which concerns a different line. -- https://aau.in/college-menu/251/236

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found that SDAU (Sardarkrushinagar) developed Gujarat Chilli 3 or GAJARAT CHILLI-2. The only related text credits "state agricultural universities" with Gujarat Chilli-1 and Chilli-2 and does not name an institution or breeder. -- https://www.ijsat.org/papers/2025/2/3679.pdf
Gujarat chilli releases located in the search results belong to Anand Agricultural University (AAU), not SDAU. -- https://aau.in/college-menu/251/236

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder name, SDAU contact, email, phone, or address for this variety was found. The only Gujarat chilli contact located belongs to AAU's Main Vegetable Research Station (Anand), which is a different university and is not used here: Phone (02692)290251 (office), (02692)261817 (farm), Email rsmvrs@aau.in, Anand 388110. -- https://aau.in/college-menu/251/236
Recommended next step: SDAU's official site or the Seednet portal's breeder/institute fields. Neither was reachable in this session.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. None of the KrishiKosh theses or journal items returned is on Gujarat Chilli 3 or GAJARAT CHILLI-2. They cover other chilli cultivars or general topics, such as anthracnose, mosaic virus, and drip fertigation. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for either name at NSC, a State Seed Corporation, a KVK, SDAU, or a private dealer. The seller listings found were general or hybrid chilli sellers, including BigHaat, BeejKart, and Desi Kheti, and none names this variety. -- https://www.bighaat.com/collections/chilli

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. The record says "Not specified", and none of the searched pages name a state recommendation for either name.

disease_resistance.summary: Kashi Kranti is described as resistant to yellow vein mosaic virus (YVMV) and okra enation leaf curl virus (OLCV) under field conditions (IIVR okra list). The same IIVR list names YVMV, powdery mildew and Fusarium wilt as major okra diseases in general, not specific to Kashi Kranti. A 2023 IIVR annual report describes Agrobacterium-mediated transformation aimed at OYVMV resistance in Kashi Kranti (in-vitro regeneration of 16 plantlets); this is a transformation effort and does not by itself confirm resistance. No evidence was found for resistance to powdery mildew or Fusarium wilt specifically in Kashi Kranti.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest-resistance claim is recorded for Kashi Kranti. Leafhopper and whitefly screening in okra genotypes did not include Kashi Kranti as a named test entry in the excerpt reviewed. No evidence was found for resistance to any specific pest.

agronomic_details.yield: IIVR reports 125-145 q/ha (approximately 12,500-14,500 kg/ha; the raw CSC unit 'Kg/Ha' is not reconciled with this figure in the digest). In a Bihar (Kishanganj, farmer-field) comparison of four varieties, the maximum fruit yield was 136.7 q/ha (approximately 13,670 kg/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended states per IIVR: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Punjab. Field trials are reported in Bihar (Kishanganj; BAU Sabour, kharif) and Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh (BHU). No agro-climatic or soil adaptation data were found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not specified in the CSC record. First harvest is reported at 45-46 days after sowing (IIVR). In the Bihar four-variety comparison, earliest flowering was at 52.30 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Dark green fruits; 17-18 fruits per plant (8-10 cm fruit length) (IIVR). No plant height or morphological data were found for Kashi Kranti (the plant height and pod data in the digest refer to Kashi Ageti and were excluded).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Bihar, Kishanganj, farmer-field comparison of four varieties: maximum fruit yield 136.7 q/ha; earliest flowering 52.30 days. (2) Growth-regulator trial on cv. Kashi Kranti at BAU Sabour, Bihar, kharif: GA3 at 100 ppm gave the most leaves, branches and plant height. (3) Two-variety trial with Kashi Pragati at Mandsaur, Madhya Pradesh (rabi 2016-17) on nutrient sources; the digest gives no Kashi Kranti result. (4) Spacing trial at Varanasi (BHU) comparing Kashi Kranti, Kashi Pragati and Pusa Sawani: Kashi Kranti gave more seeds per pod. (5) Combining-ability study: Kashi Kranti is a good general combiner (tester) for fruit yield and yield components. (6) IIVR field data: 125-145 q/ha, first harvest at 45-46 days after sowing.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kashi Kranti (okra, VRO-22) and Kaveri Kranti (Seednet, listed under CHILLIES)

Name note: The CSC name "Kashi Kranti" is the one the evidence supports. The Seednet name "Kaveri Kranti" under CHILLIES did not appear in any result. The Seednet hits were Kaveri Seed Company chilli hybrids (KHPH series), not a notified variety called Kaveri Kranti, so I found no evidence linking the Seednet entry to okra or to Kashi Kranti.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Field resistance to YVMV and OLCV is reported under field conditions. -- https://icariivr.org.in/okra-2/
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance data were found for Kashi Kranti. -- No evidence found (searched all four queries)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Kashi Kranti is described as resistant to YVMV and OLCV under field conditions. -- https://icariivr.org.in/okra-2/ ; https://icar.org.in/en/icar-iivrs-okra-variety-kashi-chaman-fetches-bumper-yield-farmers-field (no, this is Kashi Chaman; not used)
- The same IIVR list gives YVMV resistance for Kashi Kranti and lists YVMV, powdery mildew and Fusarium wilt as major okra diseases in general, not specific to Kranti. -- https://icariivr.org.in/okra-2/
- A 2023 IIVR annual report describes Agrobacterium-mediated transformation aimed at OYVMV resistance in Kashi Kranti (in-vitro regeneration of 16 plantlets). -- https://icariivr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Annual-Report-2023-2024.pdf
- Leafhopper and whitefly screening in okra genotypes did not include Kashi Kranti as a named test entry in the excerpt, so no pest-resistance claim is recorded. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/c7f78a4c-cfec-4f34-a2c1-fb2ec5b384a1/content

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- First harvest at 45–46 days after sowing; dark green fruits; 17–18 fruits per plant (8–10 cm); yield 125–145 q/ha. -- https://icariivr.org.in/okra-2/
- Maximum fruit yield of 136.7 q/ha in a Bihar (Kishanganj, farmer-field) comparison of four varieties, with earliest flowering at 52.30 days. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/special/7/Hemant%20Kumar%20Singh,%20et%20al.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366809299_Evaluation_of_growth_and_yield_attributes_of_okra_variety
- Growth-regulator trial (GA3 100 ppm gave the most leaves, branches and plant height) on cv. Kashi Kranti at BAU Sabour, Bihar, kharif. -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/doc/Rev_IJPSS_89190_Nar_A.pdf
- Two-variety trial with Kashi Pragati at Mandsaur, MP (rabi 2016-17) on nutrient sources. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279222868_Response_of_Okra_Abelmoschus_esculentus_L_to_Growth_Regulators_and_Organic_Manures
- Spacing trial at Varanasi (BHU) comparing Kashi Kranti, Kashi Pragati and Pusa Sawani; Kashi Kranti gave more seeds per pod. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-8-2020/Pankaj%20Kumar%20Singh,%20et%20al.pdf

- Kashi Kranti is a good general combiner (tester) for fruit yield and yield components in a combining-ability study. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijfs-15-2-013

- No Kashi Kranti-specific QTL or marker study was found. -- No evidence found

disease_resistance.research_summary: Kashi Kranti is described as resistant to yellow vein mosaic virus (YVMV) and okra enation leaf curl virus (OLCV) under field conditions (IIVR okra list). The same IIVR list names YVMV, powdery mildew and Fusarium wilt as major okra diseases in general, not specific to Kashi Kranti. A 2023 IIVR annual report describes Agrobacterium-mediated transformation aimed at OYVMV resistance in Kashi Kranti (in-vitro regeneration of 16 plantlets); this is a transformation effort and does not by itself confirm resistance. No evidence was found for resistance to powdery mildew or Fusarium wilt specifically in Kashi Kranti.

drought.details: LCA-625 is described as drought tolerant (RESULT_6) and highly tolerant to drought stress with high yield potential (RESULT_10, RESULT_18). It has recorded the highest dry fruit yield per plant under drought stress conditions (RESULT_8, RESULT_17). Earlier assessments noted it as moderately tolerant (Original data) or slightly tolerant to drought under field conditions (RESULT_2). In vitro screening for proline concentration under stress environments has been conducted for LCA-625 (RESULT_1, RESULT_12, RESULT_31).

heat.details: The variety is highly tolerant to heat stress (RESULT_10, RESULT_18). It has been investigated for photosynthesis-related parameters under heat stress, with LCA-625 showing a mean value of 57.33°C in studies on heat tolerance in chili pepper genotypes (RESULT_11, RESULT_34). LCA-625 has also been identified as a promising heat-tolerant chilli genotype (RESULT_14).

salinity.details: No specific information regarding the salinity tolerance level of LCA-625 was found in the provided search results.

flood.details: No specific information regarding flood tolerance for LCA-625 was found. Mentions of waterlogging avoidance techniques or grafting to improve waterlogging tolerance refer to general practices or other crops (RESULT_36, RESULT_39).

disease_resistance.summary: LCA-625 is highly tolerant to chilli leaf curl virus (RESULT_32) and tolerant to Gemini virus (RESULT_33). It was noted as slightly tolerant to chilli leaf curl virus under field conditions in an earlier assessment (RESULT_2).

pest_resistance.summary: Not Specified

agronomic_details.yield: LCA-625 is a high-yielding chilli variety, with an reported yield advantage of 25-35% (RESULT_10, RESULT_18, RESULT_28). In an advanced yield trial of hot pepper, it recorded a dry pod yield of 6750 kg/ha (RESULT_7, RESULT_23). It has also recorded the highest dry fruit yield per plant in certain evaluations (RESULT_8, RESULT_17). In another assessment, it recorded a high yield of 12.6 (units not specified) (RESULT_48).
agronomic_details.stability: LCA-625 is noted for its high color and high pungency (RESULT_4, RESULT_13, RESULT_35, RESULT_49). While general statements about hybrids adapting better to stress are made (RESULT_15), specific data on LCA-625's yield stability across diverse environments is not detailed.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for cultivation in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh (RESULT_28). It is considered ideal for dry chilli production (RESULT_33).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: LCA-625 is a single cross derivative of G-4 x LCA-334 (Original data). Plants are described as tall with strong stems (RESULT_33). Fruits exhibit high color and high pungency (RESULT_4, RESULT_13, RESULT_35, RESULT_49). Starch content is reported at 24-26% (RESULT_6). It is an open-pollinated variety (RESULT_30, RESULT_46).
agronomic_details.field_trials: LCA-625 has been evaluated in advanced yield trials for hot pepper (RESULT_7, RESULT_23, RESULT_24) and performance studies for yield and fruit quality (RESULT_14, RESULT_37). It was part of studies on photosynthesis-related parameters (RESULT_3, RESULT_11, RESULT_21, RESULT_34). Field studies involving LCA-625 have been conducted in Anakapalli District of Andhra Pradesh (RESULT_9, RESULT_19, RESULT_25, RESULT_40, RESULT_42). It has also been identified as a good general combiner for fruit number in breeding studies (RESULT_47).

The variety is a single cross derivative of G-4 x LCA-334 (Original data).

genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: In vitro screening of LCA-625 has been conducted to study proline concentration under stress, which is generally considered to confer tolerance to water deficit, suggesting research into physiological responses to stress (RESULT_1, RESULT_12, RESULT_31). The variety is a single cross derivative of G-4 x LCA-334 (Original data).

agronomic_performance.yield: LCA-625 is a high-yielding chilli variety, with an reported yield advantage of 25-35% (RESULT_10, RESULT_18, RESULT_28). In an advanced yield trial of hot pepper, it recorded a dry pod yield of 6750 kg/ha (RESULT_7, RESULT_23). It has also recorded the highest dry fruit yield per plant in certain evaluations (RESULT_8, RESULT_17). In another assessment, it recorded a high yield of 12.6 (units not specified) (RESULT_48).
agronomic_performance.stability: LCA-625 is noted for its high color and high pungency (RESULT_4, RESULT_13, RESULT_35, RESULT_49). While general statements about hybrids adapting better to stress are made (RESULT_15), specific data on LCA-625's yield stability across diverse environments is not detailed.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Recommended for cultivation in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh (RESULT_28). It is considered ideal for dry chilli production (RESULT_33).
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: LCA-625 is a single cross derivative of G-4 x LCA-334 (Original data). Plants are described as tall with strong stems (RESULT_33). Fruits exhibit high color and high pungency (RESULT_4, RESULT_13, RESULT_35, RESULT_49). Starch content is reported at 24-26% (RESULT_6). It is an open-pollinated variety (RESULT_30, RESULT_46).
agronomic_performance.field_trials: LCA-625 has been evaluated in advanced yield trials for hot pepper (RESULT_7, RESULT_23, RESULT_24) and performance studies for yield and fruit quality (RESULT_14, RESULT_37). It was part of studies on photosynthesis-related parameters (RESULT_3, RESULT_11, RESULT_21, RESULT_34). Field studies involving LCA-625 have been conducted in Anakapalli District of Andhra Pradesh (RESULT_9, RESULT_19, RESULT_25, RESULT_40, RESULT_42). It has also been identified as a good general combiner for fruit number in breeding studies (RESULT_47).

breeder_and_contacts.breeder: Dr. Y.S.R Horticulture University, with researchers like N. Sathi Babu involved in field studies (RESULT_9, RESULT_19, RESULT_25, RESULT_40, RESULT_42).
breeder_and_contacts.contacts: Not specified.
breeder_and_contacts.publications: LCA-625 is featured in various research articles and annual reports concerning chilli improvement, including studies on in vitro screening (RESULT_1), photosynthesis (RESULT_3), yield performance (RESULT_7), and genotype evaluation (RESULT_14, RESULT_37).

commercial_availability.seed_corporations: Listed among new varieties of vegetable crops by Seednet.gov.in (RESULT_4, RESULT_13, RESULT_35, RESULT_49), indicating official recognition.
commercial_availability.kvk: Chilli (LCA 625) is listed as being supplied or utilized by KVK, Kondempudi (RESULT_22).
commercial_availability.private_dealers: No specific private dealers mentioned in the provided search results.
commercial_availability.availability_status: Foundation seeds of LCA-625 were available for sale at the Regional Horticultural Research Station, Lam farm (RESULT_33). Its cultivation is suggested for farmers to reduce costs (RESULT_30, RESULT_46), implying general availability for farming.

drought.details: LCA-620 is reported to be highly tolerant to drought. It is also listed among climate-smart cultivars tolerant to reduced moisture.

heat.details: The variety is highly tolerant to heat stress. It has been investigated for photosynthesis-related parameters indicative of heat tolerance.

salinity.details: While no direct statement on LCA-620's salinity tolerance is provided, studies on fertilizer recommendations for this variety were conducted using irrigation water reported to be moderately saline.

flood.details: Conflicting evidence exists regarding flood tolerance. LCA-620 is listed among cultivars with multiple stress tolerance including flash flood and stagnant flood in the context of climate-smart agricultural technologies. However, another source suggests strategies like planting on ridges were used to avoid waterlogging for this variety, implying a need to mitigate flood impact.

disease_resistance.summary: The variety is reported as highly tolerant to chilli leaf curl virus. One source also states it is slightly tolerant to chilli leaf curl virus.

pest_resistance.summary: LCA-620 has been identified as a resistant/tolerant source against major pests of chilli.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported with an excellent dry fruit yield of 138 q/ha. It consistently shows a yield advantage of 20-30% over variety LCA-334. An earlier trial (2010-11) reported a yield of 62.92 q/ha (6292 kg/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly detailed, but its use as a national check implies good performance under various conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for cultivation in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and has shown good performance in farmer's fields in Telangana. It is used as a national check in chilli hybrid trials.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Characterized by excellent dry fruit color, paprika type, and intermediate growth habit. It exhibits a high root length (12.60 cm) and favorable chlorophyll stability index (0.72) and total chlorophyll content (0.82 mg/g) which are parameters related to photosynthesis and abiotic stress tolerance.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field trials have been conducted in farmer's fields in Telangana State (e.g., Karimnagar, Peddapalli districts) and Anakapalli District, Andhra Pradesh. It has also been introduced through Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) demonstrations in Nellore, Andhra Pradesh. LCA-620 is used as a national check in chilli hybrid trials conducted by institutions like IARI.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (QTLs, SNPs, SSRs) identified for LCA-620 in the provided results. Genetic variability studies indicated moderate estimates of GCV (18.78%) and PCV (18.79%) for traits like root length.

stress_confirmation_note: The flood entry is labelled unknown, yet its details cite two documents that list LCA-620 as flood-tolerant, so the level and the cited evidence are inconsistent.

drought.basis: Five cited documents attribute high drought tolerance to LCA-620: drysrhu.ap.gov.in YSRHU Improved Varieties Book; ICAR IH Nov-Dec 2021; Current Horticulture 9(1) 2021; ICAR-NRRI Climate-Smart PDF; IAUA publication.
drought.label: Confirmed by 2+ sources

heat.basis: Three cited documents state high heat tolerance for the variety: Current Horticulture 9(1) 2021; cyberleninka photosynthesis-parameter article; ICAR-NRRI Climate-Smart PDF.
heat.label: Confirmed by 2+ sources

salinity.basis: No tolerance statement. The cited DRYSRHU 2013-14 report only used moderately saline irrigation water in fertilizer trials, which is not a tolerance finding.
salinity.label: Not confirmed

flood.basis: Level unknown with conflicting evidence. ICAR IH 2021 and ICAR-NRRI Climate-Smart PDF list LCA-620 among flash/stagnant flood-tolerant cultivars, but ridge planting to avoid waterlogging is mitigation, not tolerance.
flood.label: Not confirmed

submergence.basis: Level low. The ResearchGate chapter says submergence lowers productivity, which implies susceptibility rather than a tolerance statement, so it is not counted.
submergence.label: Not confirmed

disease_resistance.research_summary: The variety is reported as highly tolerant to chilli leaf curl virus. One source also states it is slightly tolerant to chilli leaf curl virus.

Search status: The search tool hit its usage limit after the first query was run and repeated, so only one query's results were usable. Queries 2 to 4 (breeder/institute, research/publications, seed availability) were not completed, and the breeder, contact, publication and seed headings below are not fully searched. Treat this record as incomplete.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page giving LCH-111 drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No LCH-111 disease or pest resistance data was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- On-farm trial (OFT) on chilli new hybrids at KVK Kalikiri, Chittoor district, Andhra Pradesh, with LCH 111 listed alongside Arka Haritha and Arka (the trial page does not report yields or results) -- https://www.kvkkalikiri-angrau.org/more/photos/item/573/asInline

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage "LCA 709 x LCA-315" comes from the input record only; no independent source confirmed it. The KVK page labels LCH 111 a "New Hybrid", which fits a cross but does not confirm the parents or breeding method -- https://www.kvkkalikiri-angrau.org/more/photos/item/573/asInline

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. The search returned no page naming a lead breeder or scientist for LCH-111. The input record names Dr. Y.S.R Horticulture University as the institution, but I found no page confirming that for this variety. A search result from an ICAR journal issue (Indian Horticulture, Nov–Dec 2021) mentions the university's chilli releases but its visible text did not name LCH-111, so I excluded it -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/119909/46119

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute or divisional contact was retrieved. The only address found belongs to a different institution: KVK Kalikiri, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, PIN 517 234, under Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University. It is not the breeding institution and is not listed as a contact for this variety. Verify contacts on the Dr. YSR Horticultural University site before use.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, report, thesis or KrishiKosh record naming LCH-111 was returned. The research search was not completed.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-availability search was not completed, so no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was checked.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Andhra Pradesh, as given in the input record only (not verified by any source). The KVK page shows Andhra Pradesh trial activity, which is not a formal recommendation.

Suggested next steps: rerun the breeder, research and seed-availability queries once the search limit resets, and check the Seednet CHILLIES listing for LCH-111 and the Dr. YSR Horticultural University release notification.
