search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: LAM-353 (CSC minutes name) / Lam-334 (Seednet name) / LCA-353 (variety code), chilli

Search note: I ran 4 web_search queries (the maximum). The search engine returned almost nothing specific to this variety, so most headings below report no evidence. Name check: the search hits use LCA-353 and Lam-353 (agronomy blog, review article) and LCA 334 (the ResearchGate paper). "Lam-334" and "LCA 334" may be a different variety from LAM-353/LCA-353. I have not treated the LCA 334 evidence as evidence for LAM-353.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for LAM-353 / LCA-353 / Lam-334 drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for LAM-353 / LCA-353 / Lam-334 disease or pest resistance. A ResearchGate paper mentions fruit rot in chilli at a Main Agricultural Research Station in kharif 2012 and 2013, but the snippet does not link that trial to any named variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/289520552_Productivity_in_chilli_cv_LCA_334_as_influenced_by_organic_and_inorganic_nutrient_management_in_vertisols

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- LCA-353 plants are medium height and bushy, with thin, bright red fruits 7-9 cm long, suitable for both green and dry chilli, maturing earlier than Warangal Local, and yielding about 50-55 q/ha under irrigation. -- https://agritechblogspot.blogspot.com/2011/08/chillies-package-of-practices.html (non-official blog; yield figure not verified against a primary trial report)
- Kiranmayi et al. (2014), as reported in a review, recorded in Lam-353 a plant height of 83.33 cm, spread of 137.33 cm and 17 primary branches with 20 ppm NAA + 0.05% boron spray. -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue6/PartAI/8-5-536-574.pdf
- A field trial at the Regional Agricultural Research Station, Lam, Guntur (kharif 2003-04 and 2004-05, vertisols) compared organic and inorganic nutrient management on cv. LCA 334 (a different name from LAM-353; see note above). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/289520552_Productivity_in_chilli_cv_LCA_334_as_influenced_by_organic_and_inorganic_nutrient_management_in_vertisols
- A separate Lam, Guntur trial on organic and biofertilizer yield improvement in chilli in vertisols reports no variety-specific result for LAM-353. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/a79e/19548c56c0d945ae718a071165ea31e9c62b.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for QTL, marker or genetic studies on LAM-353 / LCA-353 / Lam-334. Parentage (G-4 x Hot Pepper) comes only from the input record, not from search. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348432487_Advances_in_Horticulture_Chapter_9_Chilli_Production_Challenges_and_Modern_Breeding_Approaches (general chilli breeding context; LAM-353 not listed)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Crop improvement work on chilli at Lam, Guntur has run since 1928, and that chapter names several earlier cultivars but not LAM-353. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348432487_Advances_in_Horticulture_Chapter_9_Chilli_Production_Challenges_and_Modern_Breeding_Approaches
- The Lam farm at Guntur is listed among active chilli germplasm centres, with ICAR-IARI, IIHR and state universities. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/377178696_Chilli_Breeding_and_Genomics
- Institution named in the CSC record: A.P. Horticultural University, Horticultural Research Station. The search did not confirm that this station is the Lam station. No breeder name found.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for a breeder name, email, phone, postal address or institute contact page for LAM-353 / LCA-353 / Lam-334. The searches did not return any institute contact page.

PUBLICATIONS
- Kiranmayi et al. (2014). Study on Lam-353 chilli growth response to NAA and boron spray, as cited in a review. Full citation not retrieved -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue6/PartAI/8-5-536-574.pdf
- Authors not captured (2019). Review on plant growth regulator research in chilli. Journal of Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry 8(6): 2122-2132 -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue6/PartAI/8-5-536-574.pdf
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Productivity in chilli (cv. LCA 334) as influenced by organic and inorganic nutrient management in vertisols. Journal/report not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/289520552_Productivity_in_chilli_cv_LCA_334_as_influenced_by_organic_and_inorganic_nutrient_management_in_vertisols
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Organic and biofertilizer yield improvement in chillies in vertisols, Lam, Guntur. Journal/report not captured -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/a79e/19548c56c0d945ae718a071165ea31e9c62b.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR report, or DOI for LAM-353 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for LAM-353, LCA-353 or Lam-334 on Seednet, a State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer. A Guntur Lam Farm article reports a foundation seed sale, but it covers LCA-625 and LCA-643, not this variety. -- https://www.gktoday.in/guntur-lam-farm-releases-two-new-chilli-varieties/

RECOMMENDED STATES
No search evidence found. The states listed come only from the input record: Eastern Madhya Pradesh, Orissa, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Punjab, Tarai Region of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Release date from the input record: 2008-10-07.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for Nandi 64 (MSH 199) specifically. The only tolerance statements in the results concern other millet entries or general pearl millet. -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf (not Nandi 64-specific)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for Nandi 64 specifically. Blast and downy mildew material in the results refers to other entries or to ICRISAT breeding lines. -- https://aicpmip.res.in/pcr2024.pdf (not Nandi 64-specific)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Generic pearl millet hybrid guidance only: hybrids were reported to need about 40 to 150 kg N/ha for optimum grain yield, depending on soil moisture. This is not Nandi 64-specific. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384608302_PEARL_MILLET_CULTIVATION
No Nandi 64 multi-location trial, yield, or maturity data were found in the results. The AICPMIP hybrid table has a Nandi 64 row, but its maturity text is garbled and cannot be attributed reliably, so maturity is unconfirmed. -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage (from the AICPMIP hybrid table): NMS 2-11A x NMP 4-1. -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
No QTL, marker, or genomic study specific to Nandi 64 was found. -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developer: New Nandi Seeds Corporation, Ahmedabad (private sector). The corporation is listed as developing the largest number of hybrids in a pearl millet hybrid review, and Nandi 64 appears in its list. No individual breeder name was found. -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status
Notification: S.O. 211(E), 29 January 2010, as Nandi-64 (MSH-199) (NMH-69). The year of release in the record is "NaT" and should be corrected to 2010 (notification year; release year not separately confirmed). -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
Also listed as a released pearl millet variety in the ICAR/DARE Annual Report 2010-11, Crop Improvement. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. New Nandi Seeds Corporation: Ahmedabad location only; no email, phone, or address found in the results.
Institute-level contact (national pearl millet programme, not the developer): AICRP on Pearl Millet, Mandor, Jodhpur 342 304, Rajasthan, India (address as printed in the Springer article). Official website: http://www.aicpmip.res.in/ (no phone or email found in the results). -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40003-013-0089-z

PUBLICATIONS
Singh, S. (2014). Hybrid breeding in pearl millet: past and present status. Journal not identified in the record (ResearchGate PDF) -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status
DARE/ICAR (2011). Annual Report 2010-11, Crop Improvement (lists MSH 199 / Nandi 64 among released pearl millet hybrids). -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
AICPMIP. Table 3: Parentage, notification details, adaptation niches, maturity group/duration and major salient features of pearl millet hybrids (undated). -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP trial report, or journal paper specific to Nandi 64 was found in the results.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or official Seednet listings for Nandi 64.
Name check: the Seednet name "Nandi (435)" under crop "CHILLIES" returned no link to this record. The "Nandi" chilli results are commercial F1 chilli products (Nunhems and others), not a notified variety. The "CHILLIES" crop label appears to be a mismatch, and Seednet entry 435 should be verified directly on seednet.gov.in. -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/basf-nunhems-nandi-chilli-seeds

RECOMMENDED STATES
Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan: summer-season areas for Nandi 64 (MSH 199), per the AICPMIP table. -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Tamil Nadu: summer growing areas per the ICAR/DARE 2010-11 report. Tamil Nadu appears here but not in the raw record. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
Uttar Pradesh: no evidence found in any source. It is listed in the raw record but is not supported by these results.

Name and crop check: The CSC notification records and AICPMIP tables describe Nandi-65 (MH-1549) as a pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum) hybrid. The Seednet record lists "Nandi (435)" under CHILLIES, and the only "Nandi" chilli I found is a Nunhems F1 chilli hybrid, which is a different product. The Seednet crop entry ("CHILLIES") and the input crop ("millet") conflict, and I found no Seednet page for Nandi-65 or Nandi (435) as a millet. The findings below refer to Nandi-65 (MH-1549), pearl millet, unless stated otherwise. The Nunhems chilli evidence is not about this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- No reliable stress-tolerance data (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) found for Nandi-65 in any source searched. -- https://pearl-millet searches returned no Nandi-65 stress record (search 1 and 4 results)

DISEASE AND PEST:

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerance to yellow vein mosaic virus is the only stress trait the sources report for Punjab Lalima; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=7292
Yellow vein mosaic virus tolerance is also listed in the PAU 2022 annual report, which I could not separately confirm as a stress trait -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
PAU's 2022 annual report says Punjab Lalima is resistant to red leaf spot and moderately resistant to zonate leaf spot -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf
Yellow vein mosaic virus tolerance is recorded for Punjab Lalima -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=7292
No pest-resistance data was found for Punjab Lalima.
Note: the Kashi Lalima (IIVR, Varanasi) tolerances to YVMV and OLCV belong to a different variety and are not evidence for Punjab Lalima -- https://icariivr.org.in/okra-2/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Average marketable yield is reported as 50 q/acre -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=7292
PAU's 2022 report gives about 275 q/acre green fodder and 7.0 q/acre grain yield, and describes plants as medium-tall with dark red stems and petioles, lobed leaves with a purple basal spot, and thin, long, dark red, five-ridged, tender fruits -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf
The same report notes good fodder quality (high crude protein, favourable in-vitro dry matter digestibility, lower HCN) -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf
Punjab Lalima is rich in anthocyanin and iodine -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=7292
No multi-location or AICRP trial results specific to Punjab Lalima were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
A 2026 Springer study used Punjab Lalima as a parent in a heterosis and combining-ability analysis; the Punjab-8 × Punjab Lalima cross gave the best heterosis for moisture and dry matter, and Punjab Lalima's general combining ability was not reported as a finding -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42535-026-01717-4
No QTL or marker studies for Punjab Lalima were found.
Parentage: not specified in the sources.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=7292
Release was approved by the State Varietal Approval Committee, chaired by the Director of Horticulture, Punjab, and announced by PAU as one of 18 new horticultural varieties -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=7292 ; https://thesummernews.com/post?slug=18-new-horticultural-varieties-released-pau-comes-up-with-dragon-fruit-apple-and-tarwanga-varieties

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNS-10 (CSC release name) / S-10 (Seednet name), sugarcane

Searches run: 4 (the maximum). Results were weak. Only one page names this variety, and it does so only in a varietal list.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The "GNS-10 sugarcane variety" search returned a rum brand (10 Cane) and unrelated pages. No page gave drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. None of the results mentioned resistance or susceptibility for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No yield, maturity, or trial data for this variety were returned. One page (ResearchGate, "Current status of sugarcane agriculture and sugar industry in India") refers to a sugarcane study that reports variety effects on growth, yield, and quality, but it does not name GNS-10 in the excerpt returned, so I have not attributed it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353774930_Current_status_of_sugarcane_agriculture_and_sugar_industry_in_India

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage or marker data were returned. The variety code "2008 N 210" did not appear in any result. Parentage is recorded as "Not specified" in the input.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for the lead breeder or the Navsari Agricultural University (NAU) Sugarcane Research Station. The "GNS-10 sugarcane breeder institute" search returned only the Wikipedia page for the Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore (ICAR), which is a different institution. It is not attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute, or station contact details were returned for this variety. Do not use the Coimbatore SBI page as a contact for GNS-10.

PUBLICATIONS -- Partial evidence only. The page below lists "CoN 13073 (GNS 10)" among sugarcane varieties in a list. It is a passing mention in a review of Indian sugarcane agriculture, not a study of this variety, and the authors and year are not visible in the excerpt. Entry: Authors not identified (Year not identified). Current status of sugarcane agriculture and sugar industry in India [title truncated in search result]. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353774930_Current_status_of_sugarcane_agriculture_and_sugar_industry_in_India
No other publications for this variety were found. The "GNS-10 sugarcane research paper" search returned a 2025 Sugar Tech systematic review (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12355-025-01685-0) that does not name this variety in the excerpt, so it is not listed.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listings were returned. The "S-10 chillies variety seednet" search returned only Amazon chilli seed listings. These concern a different crop and are discarded. No Seednet record for S-10 under sugarcane was found. The Seednet entry is listed under the crop name "CHILLIES", which conflicts with the sugarcane crop in the record. This needs checking directly on seednet.gov.in.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The input states Gujarat, but none of the searches confirmed the recommendation. The only related mention is the varietal list in the ResearchGate page above, which gives no state recommendation.

NOTES FOR THE RECORD
- Name mismatch: CSC name GNS-10, Seednet name S-10, and the Seednet crop is "CHILLIES". The Seednet entry appears to be mis-filed under the wrong crop and should be verified before use.
- Next steps (outside this search budget): check the NAU website (navsari.ac.in) and its Sugarcane Research Station pages for the breeder, contact, and release notification. Check the CSC release minutes and the ICAR-SBI variety catalogue for the 2008 N 210 / CoN 13073 pedigree and trial data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches returned no stress-tolerance data for Shakti / JBM-81. The only mesta stress-related pages found covered other varieties or general crop management.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The only mesta disease/pest pages found (a begomovirus study and pest-descriptor material from CRIJAF) do not name Shakti or JBM-81. The SATSA table lists resistance for JRM-5, a different variety, so I did not attribute it here.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- JBM 81 (Shakti) is listed in a Mesta varieties table with release year 2013, a yield value of 25.50 (unit not shown in the excerpt), and sowing guidance of mid-April to mid-May; the table also describes its pod shape as slightly cylindrical. -- https://satsawb.org/annual-technical-issue/29/FILE-NO-20.pdf
Note: The name evidence refers to "JBM 81 (Shakti)" in the same table row. The Seednet name "Shakti" and the CSC name are linked only through this table entry.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No QTL, marker, or parentage data for Shakti or JBM-81 was found. The parentage field is "Not specified" in the record, and no source gave it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The institution for the variety is linked to ICAR-CRIJAF, Barrackpore, through the evidence search, but no page names a lead breeder or scientist for Shakti / JBM-81. Institute-level identification: ICAR-Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibres, Nilganj, Barrackpore, Kolkata, which covers mesta among its six fibre crops. -- https://crijaf.res.in/ ; https://crijaf.icar.gov.in/home.html
Note: The SATSA table does not name the developing institution for JBM 81, so the CRIJAF link rests on the institute's mandate covering mesta, not on a variety-specific credit.

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level only (no breeder contact found):
- Director named on the institute site: Dr. Gouranga Kar, Director, ICAR-CRIJAF. -- http://crijaf.res.in/
- Postal address as printed on the institute site: ICAR-Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibres, Nilganj, Barrackpore, Kolkata - 700121, India. -- http://crijaf.res.in/
- Website: https://crijaf.icar.gov.in/home.html (no email or phone was shown in the retrieved excerpts).
- No official email or phone number for this variety or division was found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The mesta papers returned (CRIJAF authors on mesta yellow vein mosaic virus, mesta inter-specific hybridization, and mesta seed-yield trials) do not name Shakti or JBM-81, so none are listed.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The "Shakti" seed listings returned were for paddy, cotton, onion, and vegetable products from unrelated companies. The Mesta hybrid seed listing from Coimbatore does not name Shakti or JBM-81. Seednet, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, and SAU listings were not retrieved. The Seednet crop field "CHILLIES" does not match mesta, and no Seednet page for this variety was found under either name.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The SATSA table describes JBM 81 (Shakti) as suited to the traditional mesta-growing belt of the country. -- https://satsawb.org/annual-technical-issue/29/FILE-NO-20.pdf
Note: The record's "recommended_states_raw" value matches this wording.

DISCARDED (name resemblance, not this variety or crop):
- Bihar notified-varieties list entry "SHAKTI (IET-3232)" (1978) -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/Licence/Document/Variety.pdf (no crop or mesta link shown; treated as a different variety)
- Seed-yield trial of 14 mesta varieties (HS 4288, HS 7910, JRR 17, CRIJAF R2) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42535-026-01723-6 (Shakti not named)
- ICAR annual report mention of one mesta (roselle) variety released -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf (no variety name given)
- Shakti Taj paddy, Shakti cotton, Bhima Shakti onion, Vachan Shakti vegetable, and Shakti Vardhak mustard listings -- unrelated crops and companies.

RECORD ISSUES FOR REVIEW:
- year_of_release is "NaT"; the SATSA table gives 2013 for JBM 81 (Shakti). Verify against the CSC notification before correcting.
- Breeder, parentage, disease resistance, trial data, and seed sources remain unverified. A Seednet check and a CRIJAF direct inquiry are needed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GM-4 (Supriya) / Seednet "Supriya (G-701)", fenugreek

Name note: The CSC name is "GM-4 (Supriya)" and the Seednet name is "Supriya (G-701)". Seednet lists it under CHILLIES. None of the retrieved sources mention "Supriya" or "G-701" as a fenugreek variety, so every finding below refers to the code "GM 4" and not to the Supriya name. The search also found that "GM 4" appears in a groundnut context, which is a significant discrepancy (see RECOMMENDED STATES and STRESS TOLERANCE).

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for fenugreek. The only "GM 4" tolerance record is for groundnut: GM 4 is a very good variety, but farmers of middle Gujarat did not grow it in summer because of its susceptibility to MYMV. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364333852_GAM_8_A_New_High_yielding_MYMV_Virus_Resistant_Variety_for_Middle_Gujarat

DISEASE AND PEST -- Groundnut only: GM 4 had up to 100% MYMV disease from summer 2016 to summer 2019. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364333852_GAM_8_A_New_High_yielding_MYMV_Virus_Resistant_Variety_for_Middle_Gujarat. No fenugreek disease or pest resistance evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A NAU fenugreek study of 40 genotypes was run at Navsari during rabi 2010-11, in a randomized block design with three replications. This shows NAU fenugreek trial activity but does not name GM-4 or Supriya in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325201060_Fenugreek_Trigonella_foenum-graecum_L_An_Underutilized_Edible_Plant_of_Modern_World. No GM-4 yield data for fenugreek found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for GM-4 or Supriya. A 2025 review of fenugreek breeding covers marker and omics approaches generally and does not mention this variety. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12678331/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: Navsari Agricultural University (NAU), Navsari, Gujarat, as the CSC record states. NAU's own portal describes its mandate and varieties, but no breeder name was found for GM-4 or Supriya. -- https://resolution.nau.in/resolution/about-us. The Plant Authority annual report lists NAU among institutions with fenugreek activity, and names Dr. C. J. Dangaria as Vice-Chancellor (administrative role, not breeder). -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/eannual-report-15-16.pdf. Lead breeder for GM-4 fenugreek: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. No NAU email, phone, or postal address for the crop improvement or breeding division was found in the retrieved results. Institute-level address from the NAU profile: headquarters in Navsari, Gujarat (https://scholar9.com/institute/navsari-agricultural-university-nau-1063). Verify official contact details on nau.in before use.

PUBLICATIONS -- No GM-4 or Supriya fenugreek publication found. Related NAU item (authors not shown in retrieved text): Authors not shown (2010-11). Forty fenugreek genotypes evaluated at Navsari Agricultural University, rabi 2010-11. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325201060_Fenugreek_Trigonella_foenum-graecum_L_An_Underutilized_Edible_Plant_of_Modern_World

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for GM-4 or Supriya seed through NSC, Gujarat state seed corporation, KVK, NAU seed sales, or dealers. The results were consumer spice-seed sellers, which are not relevant to a certified variety. A national notification batch that includes fenugreek and chilli was reported, but the retrieved text does not name Supriya or G-701. -- https://agrospectrumindia.com/news/8/34411/centre-notifies-22-new-seed-varieties-to-strengthen-crop-productivity-and-quality-across-india.html

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Gujarat is taken from the input record. No fenugreek-specific notification or recommendation for Gujarat was found. The GM 4 groundnut records describe Gujarat-based trials and release context, which points to a groundnut variety rather than fenugreek.

YEAR OF RELEASE AND PARENTAGE -- No evidence found. Release year is "NaT" in the input and was not located in any source. Parentage is "Not specified" and was not located either.

Overall: The only GM 4 material retrieved is for groundnut, from AAU Anand, not fenugreek. Before this record is used, check the CSC minutes and the Seednet entry (which lists the variety under chillies). Confirm the crop and the institute of origin.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Arka Kirti (Chrysanthemum)

Search note: The search budget ran out after the first batch of four queries. The first printout showed only about 300 characters per result, so I could not read the full pages. Findings below are limited to what those snippets showed. Several headings could not be filled and need a manual check.

Name check: The CSC release minutes name and the Seednet name are both given as "Arka Kirti" in the input, so one name was searched. The only result naming this variety is the IIHR page, so the evidence refers to "Arka Kirti" on that page. I found no Seednet listing, so I cannot confirm the Seednet entry.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page on disease or pest resistance for this variety was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The IIHR page gives only a flower description: double Korean type, white fading to pink, suited to floral decoration and bedding. It gives no yield, maturity or trial data. -- https://www.iihr.res.in/varieties/arka-kirti

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. Parentage was not specified in the input and no page supplied it. The variety code H050216774 was not found on any page I could read.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The IIHR variety page lists Arka Kirti under varieties and technologies released by ICAR, which matches the institution in the input (ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research). The page did not name a breeder or scientist. -- https://www.iihr.res.in/varieties/arka-kirti

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact was found. The IIHR variety page was returned but its contact or address section was not visible in the snippet. Institute contact details should be taken from the IIHR site (https://www.iihr.res.in) after checking that page directly.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for this variety. One result was a ResearchGate paper titled "Evaluation of chrysanthemum (Dendranthema grandiflora Tzvelev) genotypes for morphological and yield traits during different seasons". I could not confirm from the snippet that it covers Arka Kirti, so I have not listed it as a publication for this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381761427_Evaluation_of_chrysanthemum_Dendranthema_grandiflora_Tzvelev_genotypes_for_morphological_and_yield_traits_during_different_seasons

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for this variety. The one seed-related result was a commercial retailer's chrysanthemum seed catalogue (sowtrueseed.com). It is not a source for Arka Kirti and was discarded. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or IIHR seed-sales page was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Not verified by search. The input lists Himachal Pradesh and Punjab. No search result confirmed this.

Suggested next steps: check the full IIHR variety page for the release notification, breeder names and contact block. Then check Seednet (seednet.gov.in) under CHRYSANTHEMUM for the listing and code H050216774. Search KrishiKosh and IIHR annual reports for trial and breeding-line data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Search limit reached: I ran the 4 permitted searches, and the fifth call was refused. Several headings are therefore thin. Name check: the variety_name "Sabour Sadabahar" and seednet_variety_name "PUSA SADABAHAR" were searched under both names, and the results do not match the record's crop or institution cleanly (see notes).

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found (no stress-tolerance data for Sabour Sadabahar surfaced in the searches).

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A brinjal seed nutripriming and foliar phosphorus study in the Journal of Plant Nutrition (2025) came up under the trial query, but the visible snippet does not name Sabour Sadabahar as a tested variety, so it is not linked to this variety -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/01904167.2025.2451931

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Bihar Agricultural University (BAU), Sabour, is the institution named in the record. A BAU newsletter ("Happening at BAU", Issue 227) lists "Sadabahar" alongside "Sabour Krishnakali" in a passage about crops/varieties, but the snippet gives no breeder name, release year, or crop attribution -- https://bausabour.ac.in/happening/file13_07_202105_45_19PIMG1.pdf
BAU Annual Report 2022-23 was returned, but the retrieved text showed no Sadabahar entry -- https://bausabour.ac.in/album/File117_04_202309_57_08PIMG1.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. Institute-level page available: https://bausabour.ac.in (BAU Sabour; no email, phone or postal address was captured in the snippets, so none is reported).

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed or AICRP publication specifically on Sabour Sadabahar was found. Not searched for KrishiKosh theses (search budget exhausted).

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Seller listing found for "Pusa Sadabahar" (Amazon.in search page, https://www.amazon.in/pusa-seed/s?k=pusa+seed). The listing describes Pusa Sadabahar as a chilli seed pack, and Pusa Navbahar as a guar/cluster bean hybrid. This is a private marketplace listing, not an NSC, state seed corporation, or SAU source, and it does not support a cluster bean identity for Pusa Sadabahar.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found for the record's "Bihar" entry in the searched sources.

NOTES FOR THE RECORD
- Crop conflict: the record says brinjal, but seednet_crop_name says CLUSTER BEAN. The market listing associates "Pusa Sadabahar" with chilli. None of the three crop labels is confirmed by an official source. Verify on seednet.gov.in before use.
- Name conflict: "PUSA SADABAHAR" (seednet name) and "Sabour Sadabahar" (CSC name) are different identities. The evidence above does not establish that they are the same variety.
- Release year is missing ("NaT"). No release notification was found.
- Parentage ("selection from local strain of Rajasthan") is unverified; the sources searched did not confirm it.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I could only retrieve partial evidence. My first batch of four searches ran, but a follow-up call hit the server's tool-use limit, so I could not open the full pages or run further searches. Most headings below therefore say "No evidence found" because the snippets I received did not cover them, not because I confirmed their absence.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC release minute name and the Seednet name are both "Kamrupa (Assam Green Tall)", so the evidence below refers to that name under both headings.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no information on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned no information on disease or pest resistance for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The AAU directorate page lists the variety under coconut, but the snippet I received gave no yield, maturity or trial data. The full page was not accessible. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found for genes, QTL, breeding-line codes or genome resources. The parentage given in the request (local pureline selection from Dodora village, Hajo, Kamrup, Assam) was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Assam Agricultural University is named as the releasing institution on the AAU directorate page. No breeder or scientist name was found. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder contact, institute email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Chowdhury D, Nath JC, Mohan NK (2001). 'Kamrupa'—a newly released coconut variety by Assam Agricultural University. Cited within a book chapter, "Breeding of Coconut (Cocos Nucifera L.): The Tree of Life" -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-319-91944-7_17
  Caution: this 2001 reference predates the 2021 release year in the request. It may refer to an earlier Kamrupa release or to the same material, and I could not verify which. I have not treated it as proof of this variety's 2021 release.
- No other publications were found. KrishiKosh, AICRP and ICAR report searches were not completed because of the tool limit.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No official seed source was found. The only seed-related result was a commercial listing by a private firm in Nagaon for "Assam Tall" green coconut plants. I excluded it because it is a similarly named commercial product from a dealer, not evidence for this variety. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/green-coconut-plant-2850302237030.html

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found specifically naming the recommended state. The variety is listed as "ASSAM" in the request data, which I could not verify from a source.

Next steps: rerun the stress/disease, breeder/contact, KrishiKosh/AICRP and seed-availability searches once the tool limit resets. Priority sources are the AAU Directorate of Research pages, the AAU coconut research station, and the ICAR-CPCRI and Seednet pages.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Mahuva (coconut)

Scope note: Four web_search queries ran. A fifth attempt, made to check the CSC release notification, was refused by the tool's usage limit, so the search that would have confirmed the release details did not run. Only partial page text was captured, and I did not verify the release record, variety code, parentage, or any trial data. Nothing below should be read as confirmation that a coconut variety named "Mahuva" was released by CSC. The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Mahuva," so every finding below refers to that name.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searched in query 1 (variety name plus crop); no result described drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance for a Mahuva coconut variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Searched in query 1; no result described disease or pest resistance for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Partial. The Junagadh Agricultural University page for the Agriculture Research Station (Fruit Crops), Mahuva, lists coconut seed production and a coconut museum for live demonstration of different varieties. It also mentions a study on irrigation levels and organic mulch in coconut seedlings. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Heat: a 2025 heat-stress screen used DHPM 2769 as a susceptible check, and its heat susceptibility index was higher than several test lines, though the extracted values are garbled and the stress condition for each value is unclear. -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2025/vol9issue8S/PartN/S-9-8-136-503.pdf
Contingency planting: the variety is listed as suitable for contingency planting. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
Drought, flood, salinity, submergence: No evidence found for this variety specifically. A review describes proso millet in general as climate-resilient, but does not attribute drought tolerance to DHPM 2769. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338206781_Proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L-a_climate_resilient_crop_for_food_and_nutritional_security_A_Review

DISEASE AND PEST
Lodging, shoot fly and rust: The proso millet review lists lodging resistance, shoot fly tolerance and rust resistance as traits, but the snippet does not clearly tie these to DHPM 2769. Treat as unverified for this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338206781_Proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L-a_climate_resilient_crop_for_food_and_nutritional_security_A_Review
Blast, smut, shoot fly, rust specific to DHPM 2769: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity and yield: One improved proso millet release table lists DHPM-2769 (released 2018) at 70–72 days, with an average yield of 24–25 (units given as kg/ha in the column header, which is likely q/ha), suited to Agro-climatic Zone-3 and 8 of Karnataka. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
Sowing date and nitrogen trial: A field trial at a Karnataka site used DHPM-2769 as the test variety at 25 x 10 cm spacing across four sowing dates and several nitrogen levels; 60 kg N/ha gave the highest panicle number, panicle length, grain weight per panicle and thousand-grain weight. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5622
Multi-location grain mineral evaluation: DHPM-2769 was evaluated across Dharwad-area locations (Hanumanamatti, Mudhol and others) for iron and zinc content, with zinc values reported as stable across locations. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue1/PartA/7-1-21-828.pdf
Tripura demonstration: The variety appears under the spelling HDPM-2769 in a Tripura popularisation programme for proso millet with improved practices on farmers' fields (20 ha). -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip20/Small_Millets/report20/7-SM-NEH-report-agm21.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Pedigree: Recorded as a selection from IPM-2769. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-16-9257-4_8
Origin (duplicate record): Also listed as a selection from IPM-2769, developed at ARS Hanumanamatti. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338206781_Proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L-a_climate_resilient_crop_for_food_and_nutritional_security_A_Review
Use as a parent: DHPM 2769 is a parent in AICRP proso millet crosses, e.g. PMV 466 (DHPM 60-4, from DHPM 2769 x DHPM 2164) and PMV 472 (DHPM 6-3, from DHPM 2181 x DHPM 2769), and in a DHPM 2769 x GPUP 21 cross. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip22/Small_Millets/reports22/1-Breeding.pdf
Breeding method: Selection from an existing line, followed by multi-location testing; the crossing history above is for progeny. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-16-9257-4_8
QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ARS Hanumanamatti, University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS) Dharwad. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-16-9257-4_8
Institution (repeated in a 2024 food system report): ARS Hanumanamatti, UAS Dharwad. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384662135_Food_System_for_Sustainability_and_Profitability_of_Millets
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The author names on the Springer chapter (Vilas A. and others at ICAR-IIMR and IARI) are chapter authors and are not attributed to DHPM-2769.

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder or scientist contact for DHPM-2769: No evidence found.
Institute-level (not variety-specific): ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, Telangana 500 030. This is the national millets institute, not the developing station. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
UAS Dharwad / ARS Hanumanamatti email, phone or address: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2021). Physico-chemical and nutritional composition of proso millet varieties (DhPM-2769 vs local proso millet). Journal not shown -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353973333_Physico-chemical_and_nutritional_composition_of_proso_millet_varieties
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2021). Standardization and Nutrient Composition of the Proso Millet Chakli. Journal not shown -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355182556_Standardization_and_Nutrient_Composition_of_the_Proso_Millet_Chakli

Authors not shown in retrieved text (2024). Mineral content of small millet genotypes across Dharwad-area locations. International Journal of Research in Agronomy, 7(1): 24-36 -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue1/PartA/7-1-21-828.pdf
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2025). Heat-tolerance screening of 22 proso millet genotypes including DHPM 2769 as check. Biochemistry journal archive, Vol. 9, Issue 8S -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2025/vol9issue8S/PartN/S-9-8-136-503.pdf
Authors not shown in retrieved text. Effect of times of sowing and nitrogen levels on yield and yield attributes of proso millet (DHPM-2769). Agricultural Science Digest -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5622
Authors not shown in retrieved text. Seed development and maturation studies in proso millet (DHPM-2769 among five varieties). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357767277_Seed_development_and_maturation_studies_in_Proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L

KrishiKosh theses: No evidence found in this search; not searched directly.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Source seed: Seed was obtained from the UAS Dharwad seed unit for a nutritional study. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353973333_Physico-chemical_and_nutritional_composition_of_proso_millet_varieties
Breeder seed demand: DHPM 2769 appears among four proso millet varieties with breeder seed indents from 2016–17 to 2021–22. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/94d6/2200bf2dc92fd6df62002b8cdea8c632ba8f.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Non-lodging habit and fertilizer responsiveness are listed as traits of TNAU 164 (name matches "TNAU 164"; variety_name "TNAU - 164" and seednet "TNAU-164" are treated as the same entry) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370509403_New_High_Yielding_Short_Duration_Pearl_Millet_Hybrid_TNAU_Cumbu_Hybrid_CO_9
- A 2020 review table gives TNAU 164 as "non-lodging" and tolerant of a stress, but the stress is not clearly legible in the extract -- https://www.tropicalplantresearch.com/archives/2020/vol7issue1/29.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to TNAU 164 (searched)

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to TNAU 164 (searched). The only resistance trait in the review table belongs to a different variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Released as a high-yielding, non-lodging, fertilizer-responsive, early-maturing proso millet culture, developed at TNAU's Department of Millets, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, Coimbatore, and tested nationally 2006–2009 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370509403_New_High_Yielding_Short_Duration_Pearl_Millet_Hybrid_TNAU_Cumbu_Hybrid_CO_9
- Average grain yield reported as 2488 kg (unit given as "kg of grain" in the abstract; per-hectare basis not stated) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370509403_New_High_Yielding_Short_Duration_Pearl_Millet_Hybrid_TNAU_Cumbu_Hybrid_CO_9
- In All India Coordinated trials, grain yield was 4.91, 8.29, 4.58, 4.88 and 10.34 percent above qualifying and national checks TNAU 155, GPUP 22, GPUP 23, GPUP 21 and K 1 respectively -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370509403_New_High_Yielding_Short_Duration_Pearl_Millet_Hybrid_TNAU_Cumbu_Hybrid_CO_9
- Maturity 70–75 days in the 2020 review table; 72 days in the millets.res.in table -- https://www.tropicalplantresearch.com/archives/2020/vol7issue1/29.pdf ; https://www.millets.res.in/books/Part-2.pdf
- Proso millet PMV 442 trial report cites TNAU 164 as a national check, yielding 12.44% less than PMV 442 (not a TNAU 164 result) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355465828_A_new_high_yielding_proso_millet_variety_Panicum_miliaceum_L_PMV_442
- Crop identity note: the evidence describes TNAU 164 as proso millet (Panicum miliaceum), which SeedNet lists as common millet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370509403_New_High_Yielding_Short_Duration_Pearl_Millet_Hybrid_TNAU_Cumbu_Hybrid_CO_9

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: derivative of the cross TNAU 137 x CO 4 (matches the input "TNAU 137 x CO4") -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370509403_New_High_Yielding_Short_Duration_Pearl_Millet_Hybrid_TNAU_Cumbu_Hybrid_CO_9
- No evidence found for QTL or marker studies on TNAU 164 (searched)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Authors listed for the TNAU 164 release paper: Angamuthu Nirmalakumari, Subramanian Alagesan, Sangeeth Manoharan, and T.S. Raveendran -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370509403_New_High_Yielding_Short_Duration_Pearl_Millet_Hybrid_TNAU_Cumbu_Hybrid_CO_9 (the author list does not state which person was the lead breeder)
- Developing institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore; Department of Millets, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370509403_New_High_Yielding_Short_Duration_Pearl_Millet_Hybrid_TNAU_Cumbu_Hybrid_CO_9
- Station: TNAU Millet Breeding Station, Coimbatore is listed as developer of other TNAU millets; TNAU 164 is not explicitly attributed to it in the source found -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or personal contact found for Nirmalakumari, Alagesan, Manoharan or Raveendran (searched)
- Institute seed contact: Director, Seed Centre, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore - 641 003; Phone 0422-6611232; Email seedunit@tnau.ac.in -- https://tnauseed.in/
- Institute seed contact (order line): Call for orders, respective centres, 04226611232 -- https://tnauseed.in/
- Seed Centre address as printed in the stock report: Seed Centre, Coimbatore (Director (Seeds), TNAU, Coimbatore - 641 003) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- Nirmalakumari, A.; Alagesan, S.; Manoharan, S.; Raveendran, T.S. (year not found). A High Yielding Prosomillet National Variety TNAU 164. Journal not identified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370509403_New_High_Yielding_Short_Duration_Pearl_Millet_Hybrid_TNAU_Cumbu_Hybrid_CO_9

SEED AVAILABILITY

heat.details: No heat tolerance evidence in digest. Digest states dry, cool, frost-free January weather is best for full yield, which describes a seasonal preference rather than measured heat tolerance.

salinity.details: No salinity evidence in digest.

flood.details: No flood tolerance evidence in digest. Digest mentions soils with drainage suitability only.

disease_resistance.summary: Stem gall (Protomyces macrosporus): released as a stem-gall resistant cultivar. In hot-spot fields it showed a near-immune response, where no other commercial variety can give good production (research digest, ResearchGate 309135524). In multilocation trials in 2013-14 and 2014-15, stem gall disease score was 2.3% for ACr-1 versus 42% for RCr 435 and 78% for the local check CS 6 (ResearchGate 316589094). Fusarium wilt: resistance is reported only for the parent line ACr-01-256 (citing Malhotra 2003); no direct varietal wilt trial was found, so wilt resistance in ACr-1 is not confirmed.

disease_resistance.research_summary: Stem gall (Protomyces macrosporus): released as a stem-gall resistant cultivar. In hot-spot fields it showed a near-immune response, where no other commercial variety can give good production (research digest, ResearchGate 309135524). In multilocation trials in 2013-14 and 2014-15, stem gall disease score was 2.3% for ACr-1 versus 42% for RCr 435 and 78% for the local check CS 6 (ResearchGate 316589094). Fusarium wilt: resistance is reported only for the parent line ACr-01-256 (citing Malhotra 2003); no direct varietal wilt trial was found, so wilt resistance in ACr-1 is not confirmed.

agronomic_details.yield: Quantitative yield information is not specified in the provided results. However, AGCr-1 is released for leafy purpose, and its performance for green leaf yield has been evaluated in shade nets. Yield performance trials have been conducted at research stations and farmers' fields.
agronomic_details.stability: Yield performance has been assessed through station and farmers' field trials, suggesting evaluation for stability across tested environments. The variety is considered suitable for normal sown conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Ajmer Green Coriander-1 is suitable for off-season cultivation and recommended for cultivation in Rajasthan. It has also been evaluated under rainfed regions of the semi-arid northern Telangana zone.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: This is a leafy variety of coriander. Agronomic recommendations include a sowing time of 9 April, seed rate of 10-12 kg/ha with 25 cm line-to-line and 5 cm plant-to-plant distance, 5-6 irrigations depending on soil and climatic conditions, and fertilizer application of 5-10 t/ha FYM, 60 kg N2, 45 kg P2O5, and 30 kg K2O/ha.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field trials include evaluation at research stations and farmers' fields. The variety has undergone evaluation and testing of advanced coriander lines in station trials and was evaluated at a research field in Telangana. Performance for green leaf yield in shade net has also been assessed.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Gujarat Dantewada Coriander (Leafy coriander-1) / Seednet name: Gujarat Dantewada (Leafy Coriander-1) (GDLC-1)

Scope note: I ran four web searches (variety, breeder/institution, research, seed availability). The evidence below mostly refers to the code GDLC-1 in trial papers. None of the sources is an official CSC minute or Seednet page, so the 2015-04-07 release date and the SDAU attribution are unverified here. Where a source refers to "Gujarat Coriander-1" or "Gujarat Coriander 3" instead, I say so.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Powdery mildew screen: GDLC-1 was the tallest genotype (75.34 cm) in a Navsari Agricultural University trial, but the source does not report GDLC-1's disease reaction -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/ce1f/ee7c92b3272db9acb413f18fbc48772166dc.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to GDLC-1.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Powdery mildew: "Evaluation of coriander (Coriandrum sativum L.) genotypes against powdery mildew" includes GDLC-1 among the genotypes, with maturity and plant height correlated with disease intensity. No resistance rating for GDLC-1 is stated in the excerpt -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/ce1f/ee7c92b3272db9acb413f18fbc48772166dc.pdf
- Aphids: the ICAR-NRCSS Ajmer aphid screen did not include GDLC-1. It tested Gujarat Coriander-1 and Gujarat Coriander-2, among others -- https://www.redalyc.org/journal/5770/577062030005/html/
- No evidence found for GDLC-1 resistance to aphids, Alternaria, wilt or other pests.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Karnataka multi-entry trial (rabi 2018-19, College of Agriculture, Bheemarayanagudi): 16 varieties including GDLC-1 were evaluated under a randomized block design with three replications. The excerpt shows GDLC-1 performing at par with other entries on some traits, but the full table was not captured -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-7-2020/Ravi%20Pujari,%20et%20al.pdf
- Gujarat cultivar evaluation (Phurailatpam, Geetha, Meena & Maiti, 2015): 19 cultivars were tested in semi-arid Gujarat conditions. The excerpt does not confirm that GDLC-1 was among them -- https://files.core.ac.uk/download/pdf/236024501.pdf
- No evidence found for GDLC-1 recommended sowing dates, seed rate, spacing, or green-leaf versus seed yield figures.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No marker, QTL, parentage or DUS-characterisation study for GDLC-1 was found. Parentage is listed as "Not specified" in the input record and I could not verify it.

- Local press: a regional news article refers to "Dantiwada Coriander-1" being found in Gujarat and given to farmers since 2014, which suggests a possible origin before the 2015 release year. drought.details: Jawahar Dhaniya-10 has been a subject of research related to water stress and drought. It was registered with considerations of seeds harvested from plots under water stress conditions, though subsequent water deficit severed the effect (RESULT_1, RESULT_45). Experiments have been conducted using PEG-induced drought stress to study the impression of foliar-applied Plant Growth Regulators (RESULT_4, RESULT_20, RESULT_44). The variety is also mentioned in the context of research on mitigating adverse effects of soil water deficit (RESULT_19, RESULT_21). Researchers like Ankita Sharma have focused on environmental stresses such as drought in their work involving Jawahar Dhaniya-10 (RESULT_3, RESULT_7).

heat.details: Jawahar Dhaniya-10 is referenced in the context of studies on various abiotic stress factors, including heat (RESULT_11, RESULT_12, RESULT_13, RESULT_16, RESULT_25, RESULT_27). It is also listed as a subject in the context of 'Genetic Analysis of Heat Stress Tolerance in Wheat', indicating its relevance to broader heat stress research (RESULT_8, RESULT_26).

salinity.details: This variety is involved in research concerning salt stress. Seed priming has been investigated as a beneficial technique for salt stress with Jawahar Dhaniya-10 (RESULT_14). It is also mentioned in the context of studies where exogenous hormones like 6-benzyladenine (6-BA) enhance salt tolerance in other plants, implying its use in related stress physiology research (RESULT_16, RESULT_18). Salinity is identified as one of the major abiotic stress factors relevant to research involving this variety (RESULT_13, RESULT_16).

flood.details: Flooding is listed as one of the abiotic stress factors in studies where Jawahar Dhaniya-10 is a featured article or subject (RESULT_11, RESULT_12, RESULT_25, RESULT_27).

disease_resistance.summary: No direct evidence of specific disease resistance for Jawahar Dhaniya-10 is provided. However, the variety is mentioned in the context of broader research on plant immune responses upon pathogen attack (RESULT_31), early blight disease resistance (RESULT_32), and virus resistance (RESULT_40, RESULT_41). These mentions are often in reviewer lists or as related articles focusing on other crops or general disease management, rather than direct resistance claims for Jawahar Dhaniya-10 itself.

pest_resistance.summary: No direct evidence of specific pest resistance for Jawahar Dhaniya-10 is provided. The variety is listed in the context of research on managing insect pests and harnessing host plant resistance (RESULT_33, RESULT_38). It is also mentioned in a study where cytokinins increased pest resistance in cotton, although this does not directly imply inherent pest resistance in Jawahar Dhaniya-10 (RESULT_37).

agronomic_details.field_trials: Experiments on Jawahar Dhaniya-10 have been set up using a Randomized Block Design with three replications (RESULT_9, RESULT_11, RESULT_12, RESULT_19, RESULT_21, RESULT_25, RESULT_27, RESULT_41, RESULT_43). These trials focused on assessing the influence of Plant Growth Regulators on various agronomic aspects, including growth, seed yield, and economics (RESULT_10, RESULT_23, RESULT_24, RESULT_28, RESULT_36, RESULT_47). The variety's seeds, obtained from JNKW, Jabalpur, were used in studies involving PEG-induced drought stress (RESULT_4, RESULT_20, RESULT_44) and optimizing seed priming duration and copper levels (RESULT_2).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pratap Raj Dhania-1 (RKD 18), coriander

Name note: The CSC name is "Pratap Raj Dhania-1" and the Seednet name is "Pratap Raj Dhania-1 (RKD- 18)". I searched both and found no Seednet portal page. All evidence below refers to the variety under the names "Pratap Raj Dhania-1" or "RKD 18" in journal and trader sources. Its release year is recorded as 2013 in the CSC record, but one review gives 2012 (see RECOMMENDED STATES).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Semi-dwarf stature is cited as giving lodging resistance. -- https://www.ijmfmap.in/pdf_vol9_2/vol_9_2_24.pdf
- A trader describes RKD 18 as having lodging resistance. -- https://www.shreeshyamvegetablespice.co.in/coriander-seeds.htm
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were found. -- No evidence found (searched in query 1 and query 3)

DISEASE AND PEST
- The status paper claims tolerance to pests and diseases but names no specific pathogen or insect. -- https://www.ijmfmap.in/pdf_vol9_2/vol_9_2_24.pdf
- No pathogen-specific or pest-specific resistance scores were found. -- No evidence found (searched in query 1)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Days to 50% flowering are 55–58; plant height 70–80 cm; days to maturity 100–105; test weight 12–15 g; seed yield 18–20 q/ha. -- https://www.ijmfmap.in/pdf_vol9_2/vol_9_2_24.pdf
- Earliness and high essential oil are listed as key traits. -- https://www.ijmfmap.in/pdf_vol9_2/vol_9_2_24.pdf
- KVKs under Kota university ran frontline demonstrations of RKD 18 on farmers' fields to promote it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334478805_Molecular_characterization_of_coriander_Coriandrum_sativum_L_genotypes_using_random_amplified_polymorphic_DNA_RAPD_markers
- No multi-location AICRP yield trial data for RKD 18 were found. -- No evidence found (searched in query 3)

GENETICS AND QTL
- RAPD marker analysis placed RKD-18 among 23 genotypes and found a unique band in RKD-18. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334478805_Molecular_characterization_of_coriander_Coriandrum_sativum_L_genotypes_using_random_amplified_polymorphic_DNA_RAPD_markers
- RKD-18 showed a Jaccard similarity of 0.93 with RKC-39 I, the highest similarity reported in that set. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334478805_Molecular_characterization_of_coriander_Coriandrum_sativum_L_genotypes_using_random_amplified_polymorphic_DNA_RAPD_markers
- No QTL or marker-trait association studies were found. -- No evidence found (searched in query 3)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The developing institution is the Agricultural Research Station, Agriculture University, Kota (Rajasthan). -- https://www.ijmfmap.in/pdf_vol9_2/vol_9_2_24.pdf
- The status paper's authors are Preeti Verma, Rajesh Kumar, Chaman Jadon, Pradeep Kumar and S.L. Yadav. The sources do not state that these people were the breeders. -- https://ijmfmap.in/journal/IJMFMAP_9-2-Dec-2023.pdf
- No named lead breeder was confirmed. -- No evidence found (searched in query 2)

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone, postal address or institute contact page was found. -- No evidence found (searched in query 2)
- Institute name for contact purposes: Agricultural Research Station, Agriculture University, Kota (Rajasthan), as named in the status paper. -- https://www.ijmfmap.in/pdf_vol9_2/vol_9_2_24.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- Verma, P., Kumar, R., Jadon, C., Kumar, P., Yadav, S.L. (2023). Pratap Raj Dhania-1 (RKD 18): Promising coriander (Coriandrum sativum L.) variety for farmers of South Eastern Rajasthan. International Journal of Minor Fruits, Medicinal and Aromatic Plants 9(2): 205–208. -- https://www.ijmfmap.in/pdf_vol9_2/vol_9_2_24.pdf (no DOI for this article was confirmed; the DOI printed near it belongs to a different article)
- Sharma, A., Rajpurohit, D., Verma, P., Joshi, A. (2019). Molecular characterization of coriander (Coriandrum sativum L.) genotypes using random amplified polymorphic DNA (RAPD) markers. -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Molecular-characterization-of-coriander-(-sativum-L-Sharma-Rajpurohit/eb58b7f18acf8e6a1cdf0103ea8ccd86b46c0940 (no DOI confirmed; journal not identified)
- Meena, R.S., Kakani, R.K., Choudhary, S., Singh, B., Panwar, A. (2014). Genetic diversity analysis in coriander (Coriandrum sativum) varieties. Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences 84(12). -- https://doi.org/10.56093/ijas.v84i12.45252 (RKD-18 is not in the cluster lists reported)
- Singh, R.S. et al. Status of seed spices research and development in India (lists RKD-18 with a 2012 date). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/272425610_Status_of_seed_spices_research_and_development_in_India
- No AICRP/ICAR annual report or KrishiKosh thesis entries were found. -- No evidence found (searched in query 3)

SEED AVAILABILITY
- A Ajmer-based seed trader lists RKD 18 (Pratap Raj Dhania 1) as a seed-purpose coriander. -- https://www.shreeshyamvegetablespice.co.in/coriander-seeds.htm
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sale or Seednet listing was found. Query 4 returned mainly retail spice sellers that do not name this variety. -- No evidence found (searched in query 4)

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The variety is described as notified for Rajasthan under a 2015 S.O.268(E) notification, but the source text is garbled and the exact wording should be checked against the gazette. -- https://www.ijmfmap.in/pdf_vol9_2/vol_9_2_24.pdf
- The seed-spices status review gives the RKD-18 release year as 2012, which differs from the CSC record's 2013. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/272425610_Status_of_seed_spices_research_and_development_in_India
- The status paper targets farmers of South Eastern Rajasthan. -- https://www.ijmfmap.in/pdf_vol9_2/vol_9_2_24.pdf

drought.details: The variety Punjab Sugandh is known for its drought tolerance. Its development by Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) is within the context of breeding lines for water stress tolerance.

heat.details: Punjab Sugandh is explicitly stated to be heat tolerant.

salinity.details: While general coriander cultivation practices note that alkaline soils with high salt concentration are not suitable, and some general statements indicate 'slightly more tolerant to medium salt concentrations', there is no direct evidence specifically linking Punjab Sugandh to a high level of salinity tolerance.

flood.details: The variety exhibits tolerance to water logging.

disease_resistance.summary: Punjab Sugandh is resistant to major diseases under field conditions, specifically powdery mildew and rust disease.

pest_resistance.summary: The variety is moderately tolerant to pests based on All India Coordinated Trial Data. It is moderately resistant to pod borer.

agronomic_details.yield: 3.5 quintals per acre
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for cultivation in northern India, particularly suited for winter temperatures. It is a dual-purpose variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Green plants are semi-erect, producing profuse tillers. Leaves are medium in size, green, tender, and possess an excellent aroma. It is suitable for foliage cutting.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Included in All India Coordinated Trial Data for pest reactions.

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: The developing institution, Punjab Agricultural University, works on mapping genes/QTL for drought and water logging tolerance, indicating a focus on these traits in their breeding programs, but specific QTLs for Punjab Sugandh are not detailed.

These were excluded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found -- No page named ACH-171-2 BG II. The only ACH-numbered trial hit was "ACH 177-2 BG II" in a 2010-11 Raichur/Siruguppa Bt hybrid trial (https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2518). It was excluded because the number differs. The AICRP 2022-24 HDPS summary (https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__05_29-04-2025.pdf) does not name this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL

The only developer statements found concern Ajeet 177 (https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ajeet-177-bg-hybrid-cotton-seeds), which is a different designation and is not attributed here. Institution from the CSC record only: Ajeet Seeds Pvt. Ltd. (variety code A0501443, release date 2020-11-09). No source confirmed the release.

CONTACT DETAILS

PUBLICATIONS

Results on other BG II cotton work (for example, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382146455_Blending_procedure_is_crucial_for_BG-II_cotton_hybrids_to_adhere_to_the_prescribed_'Refugia_in_Bag'_standards) do not name this variety.

The GEAC approved-product list (http://www.geacindia.gov.in/resource-documents/approved-products/Final_commercially_approved.pdf) was retrieved, but the snippets returned did not show an ACH-171-2 BG II entry, so it cannot be used to confirm this variety.

- Retailer listing says the hybrid suits both irrigated and rainfed fields and is sown in Kharif on medium to heavy soils; it gives no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ajeet-ach-900-2-bg-ii-premium-cotton-hybrid-seeds
- Retailer listing claims "reduces crop loss due to pest attack and environmental stress" without any trial figures -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ajeet-ach-900-2-bg-ii-premium-cotton-hybrid-seeds
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance from a trial or official source.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Retailer listing describes Bollgard II-based resistance to bollworms, plus tolerance to sucking pests and leaf reddening -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ajeet-ach-900-2-bg-ii-premium-cotton-hybrid-seeds
- No evidence found for disease resistance (wilt, blight, leaf spot, rust) specific to this variety.
- Not attributed to this variety: the ANGRAU Aditya BG-2 article (LAM BG-II 2208, a different public-sector variety) describes bollworm and disease tolerance; excluded -- https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/andhra-pradesh/angrau-unveils-public-sector-bt-cotton-variety-aditya-bg-2-1961377

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Retailer listing advises sowing at the start of Kharif in moist, well-prepared medium to heavy soils and following recommended spacing and nutrient schedules; no numeric spacing or fertilizer rates -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ajeet-ach-900-2-bg-ii-premium-cotton-hybrid-seeds
- No evidence found for yield data, maturity days or multi-location trial results for this variety.
- Excluded: the AICRP Cotton bulletin (2025-26 No. 5) lists an "ACH 9-2 BG II" as best irrigated hybrid in 2022-23 AET (32.84% yield gain). The name is not an exact match to "ACH-900-2 BG II", so it is not attributed -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__05_29-04-2025.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: ADT 1 (sunnhemp / cotton / rice ambiguity)

Search status: 4 web_search calls completed. A fifth call was blocked by the tool-use limit, so the dedicated seed-availability search and a second contact-detail search were not run. Where a heading says "No evidence found", that means the searches I did run returned nothing for it.

Name and crop check: The CSC record says crop "sunnhemp", but the Seednet crop is "COTTON (KAPAS)" and the institution is Tamil Nadu Rice Research Institute (TRRI, Aduthurai). None of the searches confirmed that ADT 1 or ADT-1 is a sunnhemp or cotton variety. The institution points to rice. Verify the crop and variety name against the CSC minutes and the Seednet entry before using this record.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found for ADT 1 or ADT-1 (no stress-tolerance data in any result) -- none (search 1 "ADT 1 sunnhemp variety" and search 3 "ADT 1 rice variety breeder" returned no variety-specific data)

DISEASE AND PEST: TRRI's breeding unit page describes a programme to develop varieties resistant to biotic stresses such as bacterial leaf blight, and to lodging resistance. This is institute-level and does not name ADT 1 -- https://sites.google.com/a/tnau.ac.in/trriadt/home/plant-breeding-genetics-unit

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: A 2024 split-plot field trial (fivefold replication, summer) on sunnhemp varieties measured residual effects on soil nutrients and on the succeeding rice crop. The snippet does not name ADT 1, so it cannot be attributed to this variety -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5521

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found -- searches returned no QTL, marker, or genetic study for ADT 1 or ADT-1.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Institution named in the CSC record is Tamil Nadu Rice Research Institute, Aduthurai. The TRRI plant breeding and genetics unit page describes its breeding programme, but no individual breeder or scientist is named for ADT 1 in the results -- https://sites.google.com/a/tnau.ac.in/trriadt/home/plant-breeding-genetics-unit

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder contact found. No email, phone, or postal address for TRRI Aduthurai appeared in the snippets. The only institute-level source is the TRRI page above (URL only; full page not reviewed for address).

PUBLICATIONS:
- Residual management of sunnhemp (Crotalaria juncea) varieties in releasing soil nutrients and their impact on succeeding rice crop. Legume Research (journal, year not shown in snippet) -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5521 (does not mention ADT 1 in the snippet; included only as a sunnhemp variety-trial reference)
- No other publication matching ADT 1 was found. The ResearchGate "Cotton Cultivation in Tamil Nadu" chapter came up for the cotton query but did not mention ADT-1 in the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/305748899_Cotton_Cultivation_in_Tamil_Nadu

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The dedicated seed-availability search (NSC, TNAU, KVK, dealers) was not run because the tool limit was reached.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. The only source is the CSC record itself, which lists Tamil Nadu. This is not verified by any search result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Seller listing says the hybrid is suited to irrigated systems and has notable tolerance to common pests and diseases; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found. Marketing claim, not trial data (name is "ARCH 045 Zian BG II", Dharti Seeds listing) -- https://www.krushivista.com/products/j9dbc414c5/1477796000004619302

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: ATCH-605 BGII / ATCH-605 BG II (cotton, kapas)
Variety code A05011052; institution Agri Top Seeds Pvt. Ltd.; release 2020-11-09; recommended states as given: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh.
Searches run (4): "ATCH-605 BGII cotton variety"; "ATCH-605 BG II cotton breeder developed by"; "ATCH-605 BGII cotton research paper"; "ATCH-605 BGII cotton seed availability".
Name check: both "ATCH-605 BGII" (CSC name) and "ATCH-605 BG II" (Seednet name) were searched. No page used either name.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for ATCH-605 BGII or ATCH-605 BG II. Results were unrelated Bt cotton hybrids and US patent cultivars (for example DP 611 BGII/RR, https://patents.google.com/patent/US7166775).

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No page named this variety with bollworm, sucking pest, leaf curl virus or other resistance data. Pages returned were for other BG II hybrids, such as Dhanlaxmi's Cotton Hybrid 2025 BGII (https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/cotton-hybrid-2025-bgii-seeds-23827913362.html) and Yashoda's Speedboll BG II (https://yashodaseeds.com/product/hybrid-cotton-seeds/speedboll-bg-ii). Both were discarded as different products.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. No maturity, yield or trial data for this variety. The Speedboll and Dhanlaxmi pages above describe other hybrids and were discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. No parentage or marker data. The only parentage-related field is "Not specified" in the input record. The ResearchGate heterosis paper on Bt BGII upland cotton (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389601710_Assessment_of_heterosis_and_combining_ability_for_fibre_yield_its_contributing_and_quality_traits_in_Bt_BGII_upland_cotton_Gossypium_hirsutum_L) does not name this variety, so it was discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. No breeder name, developing scientist, or Agri Top Seeds station was found. The GEAC list (http://www.geacindia.gov.in/resource-documents/approved-products/Final_commercially_approved.pdf) contains "NAMCOT-605 BGII" (Namdhari Seeds) and "RCH-605 BGII" (Rasi Seeds). These are different varieties and companies, so they were not attributed to ATCH-605 BGII. An "Atcha..." reference in a YouTube result (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_bubX1c7fp4) concerns an ANGRAU Bt cotton launch and is unrelated to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address or contact page for Agri Top Seeds or any institute linked to ATCH-605 BGII was returned. I have not supplied contact details from memory because they could not be verified.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP or ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, conference paper or trial report naming ATCH-605 BGII was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for ATCH-605 BGII or ATCH-605 BG II was returned. Listings returned were for other products, including V-Sport BGII (https://agribegri.com/products/v-sport-bgii-cotton-seeds--buy-online-cotton-seeds-.php), Tukaram BG-II (https://rjbiotech.com/product/bg-ii-cotton-hybrid-tukaram/) and SANKET NBC 101 BGII (https://www.indiamart.com/kisan-kranti-krishi-kendra-and-machenry-store/hy-cotton-seeds.html). All were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. The states given in the input record (Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh) could not be confirmed from any search result. No Seednet or GEAC entry for ATCH-605 BGII was returned.

Recommended next step: check the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) directly under variety code A05011052 and the GEAC approved-products list for the ATCH-605 BGII entry. Neither was reachable through these searches.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: ATCH-704 BGII / ATCH-704 BG II (cotton, kapas), code A05011051

Search scope: four web_search queries were run. Query 1 used "ATCH-704 BGII cotton variety" (release name). Query 2 used "ATCH-704 BG II cotton breeder developed by Agri Top Seeds" (Seednet name). Query 3 used "ATCH-704 cotton research paper AICRP trial". Query 4 used "ATCH-704 BG II cotton seed availability dealers". No result named ATCH-704 in any form, so every heading below is "No evidence found". Nothing was attributed to this variety by name resemblance.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Query 1 returned only unrelated Bt cotton pages (for example, a USPTO cultivar patent for DP 579 BGII and a SP 7007 BGII page). None mention drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence for ATCH-704.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The pages returned for ATCH-704 queries described other products. Examples are a Haryana/Punjab BGII hybrid and generic Bollgard II hybrids. None mention ATCH-704 resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No ATCH-704 yield, maturity or trial data appeared. The AICRP-Cotton 2024-25 annual report (https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf) was returned but covers cotton generally and does not name ATCH-704, so I excluded it.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No marker, QTL or event-construction study for ATCH-704 was returned. The GEAC list of Bt cotton hybrids (http://www.geacindia.gov.in/resource-documents/approved-products/Final_commercially_approved.pdf) appeared in query 1 and query 2. The retrieved excerpts did not include an ATCH-704 entry, so it is not a source for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No breeder name, developing scientist or station was found for ATCH-704. The only breeder-related hit was a Wikipedia page for Rajagopalan Krishnamurthy (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajagopalan_Krishnamurthy). It does not mention ATCH-704 or Agri Top Seeds, so I excluded it. Agri Top Seeds Pvt. Ltd. was not confirmed as the developer by any retrieved page.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No Agri Top Seeds Pvt. Ltd. email, phone, address or contact page was returned. Queries 2 and 4 did not surface an official company page.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report chapter, thesis, KrishiKosh record or conference paper for ATCH-704 was returned. The AICRP and CICR material that did appear is general and does not name this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Query 4 returned dealer listings for other products, including US 7067 BG II (US Agri), Speedboll BG II (Yashoda), Recharge BG II ELS (Paras Genetech) and Fortuner 555 BG II (Shree Airson Agro Seeds). "US 704 BG II" appeared as a thumbnail label on a US Agri page. It is a different product and was excluded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for ATCH-704 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The states Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh come from the input record only. No search result confirmed them for ATCH-704. The Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) was not reachable through these searches.

Suggested next steps: check the Seednet entry for "ATCH-704 BG II" (code A05011051) and the CSC release minutes for the notified name, breeder and recommended states. Also check the GEAC approved-products list in full and the AICRP-Cotton zonal reports for "ATCH" entries.

seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: NO SEVER DISEASE OBSERVED.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: NEGLIGIBLE INCIDENCE OF COMMON CROP PESTS WAS OBSERVED.
