agronomic_details.yield: BGDS 1033 is a parent in the cross GSHV 172 x BGDS 1033, which exhibited significant standard heterosis (29.27%) for kapas yield per plant and fiber quality traits. The individual yield of BGDS 1033 as a standalone variety is not specified, but its contribution to heterotic crosses indicates potential for yield improvement.
agronomic_details.stability: Studies on heterosis, combining ability, and stability for yield and fibre quality traits in crosses involving BGDS 1033 (e.g., GSHV 172 x BGDS 1033) were conducted. The need for verification of stability for kapas yield per plant in such crosses is mentioned.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Searches returned only cotton pages for "Bikaneri Narma" and nothing on the grass. Perennial habit is the only stress-related trait noted -- https://raubikaner.org/agriculture-research-station-bikaner/

DISEASE AND PEST -- Bikaneri Dhaman (RCCB-2) is described as showing good resistance to all insect pests and diseases, with no pathogen, pest species or screening data given -- https://raubikaner.org/agriculture-research-station-bikaner/
Seednet name BIKANERI NARMA: the only pest and disease material found concerns Bikaneri Narma cotton (Bt/leaf-curl context), a different crop, so discarded -- no grass evidence.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Approx. 130 q/ha green fodder from one cutting -- https://raubikaner.org/agriculture-research-station-bikaner/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Crude protein about 9.00% -- https://raubikaner.org/agriculture-research-station-bikaner/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Perennial; established by seed or rooted slips -- https://raubikaner.org/agriculture-research-station-bikaner/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Six cuttings per year possible with irrigation -- https://raubikaner.org/agriculture-research-station-bikaner/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Centre maintains and evaluates about 350 Lasiurus sindicus lines, 150 Cenchrus setigerus lines and 90 Cenchrus ciliaris lines (germplasm, not this variety's trial data) -- https://raubikaner.org/agriculture-research-station-bikaner/
Seednet name BIKANERI NARMA: cotton trial and maturity material (for example 150-155 day medium-staple cotton) concerns a different crop -- discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No QTL, marker or genetic study was found for Bikaneri Dhaman. Parentage given in the CSC record ("selection from non-descriptive hirsutum mixture") is a cotton (Gossypium hirsutum) pedigree and conflicts with a grass variety -- https://raubikaner.org/agriculture-research-station-bikaner/ (no parentage stated there)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developed/maintained under the AICRP on Forage Crops and Utilization at Agriculture Research Station (ARS) Bikaner, Swami Keshwanand Rajasthan Agriculture University -- https://raubikaner.org/agriculture-research-station-bikaner/
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No lead breeder or scientist name was found on any page. The CSC record's "institution: Not specified" is therefore resolved only at the university/station level.
Seednet name BIKANERI NARMA: the cotton variety was linked to the Dharwad university and CICR in cotton-only pages; these are a different crop and are not attributed to this record.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The ARS Bikaner page returned no email, phone or postal address in the retrieved text. Institute-level contact is the Swami Keshwanand Rajasthan Agriculture University website (https://raubikaner.org/) -- the page was found but its contact section was not retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for Bikaneri Dhaman (RCCB-2) in peer-reviewed journals, AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses or conference papers. Results for the search were about Bikaneri Narma cotton (for example a 1977 AGRIS record, "'Bikaneri Nerma' - a promising American cotton variety", Singh C. and Yadav B.D., Haryana Agricultural Univ. -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=IN19790369373) and were discarded as a different crop.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sales or dealer listing for the grass was found. Search results about Bikaneri Narma seed concerned Bt cotton and were discarded as a different crop.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Rajasthan (state-level release, stated as 2015 on the ARS Bikaner page, not 2018 as in the CSC record) -- https://raubikaner.org/agriculture-research-station-bikaner/

NOTE ON NAMES: "Bikaneri Dhaman" (CSC variety_name) matches the forage grass page. "BIKANERI NARMA" (Seednet name) is a cotton variety and its evidence is not attributed to this record. The Seednet crop (cotton) conflicts with the CSC crop (dhaman grass), and the release year conflicts (2018 in the record, 2015 on the source). My searches returned no Seednet portal page, so all evidence below refers to the name "CCH 2623" in general sources, not to a Seednet record. Several sources classify CCH 2623 as a hybrid, while one lists it as a G. hirsutum variety. The release date (2015-06-25) and parentage ("Not specified") could not be confirmed.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. -- searched via "CCH 2623 cotton variety" and "CCH 2623 cotton research paper trial"

DISEASE AND PEST:
Cotton rust (Phakopsora gossypii) disease index on CCH 2623 was about 11.26% at 140 days after sowing in 2022 and about 7.42% in 2023, from a rust storage/infection study at ICAR-CICR; no resistance category was stated in the retrieved text. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13378466/
No other disease or pest resistance evidence found. -- as above

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
AICRP trial 2008-09 (ICAR-CICR, S. Manickam's ICAC presentation): seed cotton yield of CCH 2623 was 1911 kg/ha, versus 1537 kg/ha for the zonal check and 1758 kg/ha for the local check (CCH 4474 in same table: 1649 kg/ha). -- https://icac.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/04SManikam-7C.pdf
Maturity is given as about 166–170 days, in a description of the hybrid developed from ICAR-CICR G. barbadense breeding lines. -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf
Listed among cotton varieties/hybrids for Tamil Nadu seasons and districts; no district-level yield data retrieved. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/agri_seasonandvarieties_cotton.html
Field-trial or multi-location data beyond the AICRP 2008-09 figures: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL:
No evidence found. Parentage is only indirectly described as derived from G. barbadense breeding lines (hybrid description) -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf
Classification conflict: a table lists CCH 2623 as a G. hirsutum variety (not a hybrid). -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/51140

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
Developing institution: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur, per the source naming. -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13378466/
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.
Station: ICAR-CICR Regional Station, Coimbatore is named as the source of the AICRP data presentation. -- https://icac.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/04SManikam-7C.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS:
Breeder name, role, email, phone: No evidence found.
Institute-level: "ICAR-CICR, Regional Station, Coimbatore" and "Director, ICAR-CICR, Nagpur" are named; no email, phone or postal address appeared in retrieved text. -- https://icac.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/04SManikam-7C.pdf
Institute contact page URL: not retrieved in these searches; check the official CICR website directly.

PUBLICATIONS:
Pandian, V. (year not confirmed). Infection process, viability and survival of cotton rust (Phakopsora gossypii) under different storage conditions. ICAR-CICR Department of Plant Pathology -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13378466/
Manickam, S. (year not confirmed; AICRP data 2008-09). Subiksha, the compact long staple cotton variety with high strength suitable for high density planting. ICAC presentation -- https://icac.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/04SManikam-7C.pdf
Other peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR annual reports, theses (KrishiKosh): No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
No evidence found from NSC, State Seed Corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or private dealers. The seed-seller result returned was unrelated.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
Tamil Nadu: listed among cotton varieties/hybrids in the TNAU season and variety listing. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/agri_seasonandvarieties_cotton.html
Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka (from the variety record): No evidence found in the retrieved sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name key: "C58" = CICR-H Cotton 58 (release-minutes name, code CNH 17395). "N54" = CICR-H Cotton 54 (Nano) (Seednet name). The evidence for C58 names it under the alias "ICAR-H NC Cotton 58 (CNH 17395) Shalini." The evidence for N54 names it as "CICR-H Cotton 54 (Nano)" and does not mention 58.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- C58 and N54: No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance under either name. The search returned only unrelated pages (a heat-screening paper on other G. hirsutum lines, and an Egyptian nano-fertilizer study). -- https://www.cotton.org/journal/2012-16/3/upload/JCS16-190.pdf (unrelated, not cited as evidence)

DISEASE AND PEST
- C58 and N54: No evidence found. The AICRP 2024-25 report covers CLCuD and boll rot in general terms without naming either variety. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- N54: The CICR profile of Dr. S. Manickam classes it as a compact variety, released 2022, for irrigated and rainfed conditions in the Central and South Zones. -- https://cicr.org.in/manickam/
- C58: The AICRP 2024-25 report has a list of non-Bt varieties identified by the Variety Identification Committee in 2024 that includes the heading "CICR-H Cotton 58." The row shows the code CNH 18529, which the CICR profile of M Saravanan attributes to a different naturally coloured variety. I could not confirm which entry the heading belongs to. The report also dates identification to 2024, while the release date in the record is 2022. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf
- C58: No yield or multi-location trial data found.
- N54: No yield or multi-location trial data found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- C58 and N54: No evidence found. A 2022 poster on lintless-fuzzless genetics in the Manickam profile does not name N54, so it was excluded. -- https://cicr.org.in/manickam/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- N54: Dr. S. Manickam is listed as the developer of CICR-H Cotton 54 (Nano) in the ICAR-CICR at-a-glance document, which places the variety in G. hirsutum. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ICAR-CICR-At-Glance-with-coverpages.pdf
- N54: Dr. S. Manickam's profile gives his designation as Principal Scientist with a plant breeding specialization, and lists the variety among his released varieties. -- https://cicr.org.in/manickam/
- C58 (CNH 17395, Shalini): The profile of M Saravanan lists the development of ICAR-H NC Cotton 58 (CNH 17395) Shalini, a brown-linted naturally coloured cotton for rainfed conditions in the Central Zone, under his technology record. The page does not explicitly name him as lead breeder. -- https://cicr.org.in/m-saravanan/
- Institution (both): ICAR-

CICR-H Cotton 54 (Nano) -- evidence name: "CICR-H Cotton 54 (Nano)", which matches the Seednet name "CICR-H COTTON 54 (NANO)". Only one source names this variety, and it is a breeder profile page, so most headings below have no evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The four searches returned no stress-tolerance data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The four searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The breeder profile lists the variety as a compact type, released in 2022, for irrigated and rainfed conditions in the Central and South Zones. CICR-H Cotton 54 (Nano) · Compact variety · 2022 · Central and South Zone · Irrigated& rainfed -- https://cicr.org.in/manickam/
No maturity, yield, or multi-location trial results were found for this variety. The AICRP and CICR snippets that mention compact or trial work do not name this variety, so I discarded them. (Source: https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf)

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage or QTL/marker data for this variety was returned. The parentage field "Not specified" was not resolved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Dr. S. Manickam is listed as a Principal Scientist in Plant Breeding at CICR, and his profile lists CICR-H Cotton 54 (Nano) among the varieties he developed. -- https://cicr.org.in/manickam/
The institution is ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research, Nagpur, headquartered in Nagpur with regional units at Coimbatore and Sirsa. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research (secondary source; verify on cicr.org.in)
Co-breeders were not identified. The "(Breeder)" entry in the AICRP 2024-25 report is for another line, so I did not attribute it to this variety. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf

drought.details: CPD-1652 was identified as a drought tolerant cotton genotype (G. hirustum) with significantly higher mean seed yield.

disease_resistance.summary: No specific disease resistance for the plant variety CPD-1652 is mentioned in the provided results. While one result mentions resistance to Bacterial Leaf Blight, this was in reference to a different cotton genotype (AKH-09-5). Another source mentions 'bacteria and viruses' in the context of textile fibers, not plant resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: No information on pest resistance for CPD-1652 is available.

agronomic_details.yield: CPD-1652 was found to be superior for seed cotton yield (SCY) and lint yield compared to other varieties like NH-615 and RAH-1071. It also exhibits high GCA for SCY, indicating its ability to transmit high yield traits to its offspring.
agronomic_details.stability: No specific information on yield stability across diverse environments is provided.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The variety is recommended for cultivation in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Orissa. Its drought tolerance suggests suitability for rainfed conditions or areas prone to water scarcity.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CPD-1652 exhibits desirable traits such as high Number of Bolls per Plant (NBP) and high Boll Weight (BW), which contribute to its superior yield.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Screening of cotton genotypes, including CPD-1652, for stress tolerance was conducted. Diallel and biplot analyses for genetic insights and hybrid evaluation imply extensive field trials.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (SNP, SSR) or QTL positions are identified.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: CPD-1652 exhibits high General Combining Ability (GCA) for Seed Cotton Yield (SCY), Number of Bolls per Plant (NBP), and Boll Weight (BW). This insight was derived from integrated biplot and numerical diallel analyses, indicating its potential as a parent for hybrid development. Hybrids involving CPD-1652, such as GBHV-200 × CPD-1652, have been identified.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: No specific molecular mechanisms or genes are described.

disease_resistance.summary: No resistance rating for CSH-3129 was found. The only disease-related evidence is a 2017-18 and 2018-19 treatment trial for root rot and wilt management using biocontrol agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas, arbuscular mycorrhiza) and fungicides; this is a treatment trial, not a resistance rating. A separate seed-treatment assay on CSH-3129 and CICR-3 measured germination, seed rot and vigour; the combined treatment gave the highest vigour index in CSH-3129. Seed-rot or vigour results are not a resistance rating.

pest_resistance.summary: No resistance rating for CSH-3129 against bollworm or sucking pests was found in searched sources.

The North zone evaluation (ICAR-CICR Regional Station, Sirsa) places CSH-3129 under irrigated conditions; this is context for the trial, not a stated adaptation. The supplied recommended states (Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan) are unverified in the digest.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified. No plant-type or morphological data specific to CSH-3129 were found in any retrieved text.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) North zone evaluation of G. hirsutum advanced populations (ICAR-CICR Regional Station, Sirsa; ICAC presentation, Ahuja 2024): CSH-3129 appears as a check or entry for ginning out-turn (GOT) above 40% and high yield under irrigated conditions; the slides show a field view of CSH-3129 and list it among donor lines with high GOT. (2) ICAC presentation on the Subiksha long-staple variety (Manikam 2024): CSH 3129 is listed among genotypes consolidated for yield and fibre-quality evaluation; yield values were not extracted. (3) Disease-management treatment trial, 2017-18 and 2018-19: CSH-3129 tested for root rot and wilt management with biocontrol agents and fungicides; no resistance outcome reported. (4) Seed-treatment assays: CSH-3129 and CICR-3 tested for germination, seed rot and vigour; the combined treatment gave the highest vigour index in CSH-3129. No quantitative yield results were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CSH-3129 (cotton)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "CSH-3129", so every search used that name. I did not reach the Seednet portal itself, and no search result came from it. Crop was matched as cotton (G. hirsutum, Sirsa/CICR context) in every retained item.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of CSH-3129. Searches returned only unrelated cotton pages. Searched: "CSH-3129 cotton variety", "CSH-3129 cotton research".

DISEASE AND PEST
- CSH-3129 was tested in 2017-18 and 2018-19 for root rot and wilt management using biocontrol agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas, arbuscular mycorrhiza) and fungicides. This is a treatment trial, not a resistance rating. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s41938-023-00739-3
- Seed-treatment assays on CSH-3129 and CICR-3 measured germination, seed rot and vigour; the combined treatment gave the highest vigour index in CSH-3129. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s41938-023-00739-3
- No resistance rating for CSH-3129 against bollworm or sucking pests was found. -- searched via "CSH-3129 cotton variety"

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- CSH-3129 appears as a check or entry in a North zone evaluation of G. hirsutum advanced populations for ginning out-turn (GOT) above 40% and high yield under irrigated conditions (ICAR-CICR Regional Station, Sirsa). The slides show a field view of CSH-3129 and list it among donor lines with high GOT. -- https://icac.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/1-Ahuja-4B.pdf
- In an ICAC presentation on the Subiksha long-staple variety, CSH 3129 is listed among genotypes consolidated for yield and fibre-quality evaluation. Yield values for CSH-3129 were not extracted. -- https://icac.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/04SManikam-7C.pdf
- No maturity, plant-type or yield data specific to CSH-3129 were found in any retrieved text. The CICR crop-improvement page and the AICRP 2024-25 report did not name this variety. -- https://cicr.org.in/crop-improvement/ ; https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- CSH 3129 was used as a female parent in a male-sterility/hybrid breeding table (GMS 26 x CSH 3129). This is a breeding use, not a QTL or marker study. Authors and year were not shown. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/male-sterility-in-cotton/146290655
- No QTL, marker or DNA-fingerprinting study specifically for CSH-3129 was found. -- searched via "CSH-3129 cotton research"

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CSHG 1862 (cotton, Gossypium hirsutum)

Name note: The release-minutes name and the Seednet name are both "CSHG 1862", so one set of evidence covers both headings. I found no separate Seednet portal page, so Seednet-specific fields (variety code A0501309, release date 2013-01-18, parentage) are unverified. Searches 3 and 4 returned mostly unrelated 19th-century and US patent material, so those headings rest on little evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf (searched; the report mentions only the irrigated north zone)

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance. -- searched across the first two searches; no CSHG 1862 resistance data appeared

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- CSHG 1862, a GMS-based hirsutum hybrid released for the irrigated north zone, recorded an overall mean seed-cotton yield of 2.1 tonnes/ha. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- The same report says the hybrid is capable of spinning at 40s counts, and has been found superior (text cut off in the source; comparator not visible). -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- Maturity, plant type, fibre length and multi-location trial data: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- CSHG 1862 is a GMS (genetic male sterility) based intra-hirsutum hybrid, as listed in the CICR list of intra-hirsutum hybrids alongside Savitha, Suguna, Surya, Kirthi and Omshankar. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf ; https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/51140
- Parentage: not found (Seednet also lists "Not specified").
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), which was established at Nagpur, in 1976. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ICAR-CICR-At-Glance-with-coverpages.pdf
- Regional stations: its headquarters at Nagpur and its Regional Stations at Coimbatore and Sirsa. The Sirsa station is the north-zone station relevant to this hybrid, though the source does not explicitly tie CSHG 1862 to Sirsa. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ICAR-CICR-At-Glance-with-coverpages.pdf
- Lead developer name(s): The CICR At-a-Glance document has a table headed "Name | Lead developer | Species | Year", but the names did not appear in the retrieved text. Needs manual check of that PDF. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ICAR-CICR-At-Glance-with-coverpages.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder name, email or phone found.
- Institute-level: ICAR-CICR, Nagpur (headquarters, NH 44 Nagpur-Wardha Road) and Sirsa campus (NH9, Sirsa, Haryana). Postal codes and phone numbers not in the retrieved text. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research
- Institute website: cicr.org.in (cited in the CICR technical bulletin and the At-a-Glance PDF, though no contact page was retrieved). -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf
- Director named on Wikipedia: Dr. V. N. Waghmare (date of listing not confirmed). -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research

PUBLICATIONS
- ICAR (2012?). Crop Improvement, Annual Report 2011-12 (section on CSHG 1862 release). ICAR Annual Report -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf (author and year not confirmed in the retrieved text)
- Authors not stated in retrieved text. CICR varieties and hybrids, Technical Bulletin No. 13. Central Institute for Cotton Research, Nagpur -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf (CSHG 1862 not confirmed in the retrieved excerpt)
- No peer-reviewed papers, theses (KrishiKosh) or conference papers on CSHG 1862 found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU or private dealers. The search returned no seed-sales results for CSHG 1862.

RECOMMENDED STATES

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance of Suchitra (CCH 12-2) in the retrieved sources. Plant-type notes are the only agronomic traits found: compact and erect plant architecture, specially promoted for HDPS to increase plant population and boost overall yield per hectare -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf (name in source: "Cotton Hybrid: Suchitra (CCH 12-2)")

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found on disease or pest resistance for Suchitra (CCH 12-2). The CICR crop improvement page lists "Suchitra" among varieties used as sources in a genetic-resource context, but does not attribute any resistance to it -- https://cicr.org.in/crop-improvement/ (name in source: "Suchitra", no CCH 12-2 designation)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity: This cotton hybrid matures in 150 days. -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf
Fibre and spinning: Staple type: Long-staple cotton with fibre length of 30–34 mm and suitable for up to 60s count yarn -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf
Multi-location yield data: no evidence found beyond a tabular entry in a Odisha state training document listing Suchitra (CCH 12-2), type H, release 2018, developed by ICAR-CICR, Coimbatore; the yield columns in that entry could not be reliably matched to the variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353572829_Capacity_Building_Program_on_Cotton_Production_Technologies_State_Department_of_Agriculture_Odisha_under_Technology_Mission_on_Cotton_For_official_use_only_Lecture_Notes_of_Exposure_Visit_cum_Capacity

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: not specified in any retrieved source (matches the record's "Not specified"). No QTL or marker study for CCH 12-2 found. The CICR profile of Dr V.N. Waghmare mentions general linkage-map and fibre-gene mapping work in cotton, not this hybrid -- https://cicr.org.in/present/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), per the Odisha document naming "ICAR-CICR, Coimbatore" for Suchitra (CCH 12-2) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353572829_Capacity_Building_Program_on_Cotton_Production_Technologies_State_Department_of_Agriculture_Odisha_under_Technology_Mission_on_Cotton_For_official_use_only_Lecture_Notes_of_Exposure_Visit_cum_Capacity
CICR is established at Nagpur, Maharashtra (central India), in 1976 with regional units at Coimbatore and Sirsa -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research
Lead breeder for CCH 12-2: no evidence found. Dr V.N. Waghmare is listed as CICR director and cotton breeder in a CICR profile, but is not linked to this variety in any source -- https://cicr.org.in/present/
Seednet portal entry ("Central Cotton CCH 12-2 (Suchitra)" / "COTTON (KAPAS)"): not retrieved; no evidence found from Seednet.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute director named in indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in: Dr Y G Prasad, Director -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/organisations/ministry-and-departments/icar-central-institute-cotton-research (no email, phone, or address shown in the retrieved text)
Dr V.N. Waghmare, Director, ICAR-CICR, Nagpur (CICR profile page and Wikipedia both list him as director; they conflict with the Prasad entry, which should be verified) -- https://cicr.org.in/present/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research
Address (Nagpur campus, per Wikipedia): NH 44 (Nagpur Wardha Road), about 14 km from Nagpur Railway Station -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research
Second campus (Sirsa): NH9, Sirsa, Haryana -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research
Institute website: www.cicr.org.in -- https://asti.cgiar.org/india/directory/central-institute-cotton-research-cicr
Official email and phone: no evidence found in retrieved sources. Please check https://cicr.org.in contact page directly.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report entry, thesis, or KrishiKosh record specifically on Suchitra (CCH 12-2) was retrieved. A CICR Annual Report 2022 was located but its contents on this hybrid were not accessible in the retrieved text -- https://www.scribd.com/document/904548682/CICR-AR-2022-s1

SEED AVAILABILITY
No confirmed dealer, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU listing for Suchitra (CCH 12-2) was found. The Tamil Nadu package-of-practices book includes the variety but its seed-availability section covers TNAU varieties -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf

Suited for Central Zone states, including Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, and adopted under irrigated conditions in Tamil Nadu. -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Sunantha (CCH 14-1), cotton

Name note: The searches never returned the exact string "Central Cotton CCH 14-1". Every relevant page refers to the variety as "Sunantha (CCH 14-1)" or "CCH 14-1". The Tamil Nadu sources call it a hybrid, while the CSC minutes name it as a variety. The Seednet name "Central Cotton CCH 14-1(Sunantha)" was not found in any result, and Seednet was not reached. Pages about other crops or varieties (potato tuber notes, Suchitra CCH 12-2, Suvin, NH 1901, US variety trials) were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- The TNAU variety page lists resistance to bacterial leaf blight, grey mildew and tobacco streak virus, and immunity to root rot. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/cotton%20sunantha.html
STRESS TOLERANCE -- The Tamil Nadu recent agro-technologies book describes the hybrid as having strong resistance to bacterial leaf blight and as suited to irrigated conditions in Tamil Nadu. -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE -- The same book reports only moderate tolerance to sucking pests and to the foliar diseases common in the central cotton belt. -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- Bacterial leaf blight resistance is listed in the TNAU and Tamil Nadu agricultural briefs. Grey mildew and tobacco streak virus resistance, and root rot immunity, are listed only in the TNAU page. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/cotton%20sunantha.html ; https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Agricultural-Briefs-of-Tamil-Nadu.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- Sucking-pest tolerance is moderate, not high, per the Tamil Nadu agro-technology book. -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Duration of 150 days, winter irrigated season, and average seed cotton yield of 1680 kg/ha. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/cotton%20sunantha.html
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Uniform boll setting, synchronised maturity and ease of picking are reported. -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Fibre length 32.0 mm, fibre strength 32.7 g/tex, ginning outturn 34.2%, spinnability about 50s count (TNAU). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/cotton%20sunantha.html
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Slightly different fibre values are given in the Tamil Nadu book: staple 32.4 mm, strength 34.3 g/tex, ginning about 34.0%, spinnable to 60s. -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No multi-location trial or AICRP yield data specific to this variety was found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage is Surabhi crossed with Rai 4A-3-2 (TNAU page). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/cotton%20sunantha.html
GENETICS AND QTL -- The ICAR-CICR list gives the institute code as CICR-H Cotton 33 for Sunantha (CCH 14-1). -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ICAR-CICR-At-Glance-with-coverpages.pdf
GENETICS AND QTL -- Breeding method, marker studies, QTL and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- ICAR-CICR's release list records a lead developer for Sunantha, but the name is cut off in the retrieved text and could not be read. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ICAR-CICR-At-Glance-with-coverpages.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The developing institution is ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ICAR-CICR-At-Glance-with-coverpages.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The Tamil Nadu book links the hybrid to ICAR-CICR's Regional Centre at Coimbatore. -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Named individual breeder: No evidence found. The Krishnamurthy and Ravindranath pages describe other cotton breeders and are not attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research, Nagpur, Maharashtra, with a mandate page at https://cicr.org.in/about-us/about-cicr-mandate-duplicate-1/ . The address "NH 44 (Nagpur Wardha Road)" comes from Wikipedia, not an official source. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research
CONTACT DETAILS -- Regional Station Coimbatore is named as the AICRP cotton breeding centre, with Dr. S. Manickam as Principal Investigator (Plant Breeding) listed in the AICRP chairman/breeder table. This is not a confirmed Sunantha contact. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf
CONTACT DETAILS -- Official email, phone and postal address: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The only related hit was a general cotton book chapter with no mention of this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Breeder seed of other CICR hybrids (CICR-H Cotton 54 Nano, CCH 19-4, CICR-B Cotton 55) is said to be available at ICAR-CICR Regional Centre, Coimbatore. Sunantha is not named in that statement. -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf
SEED AVAILABILITY -- Sunantha-specific availability from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales or dealers: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The Tamil Nadu book says the hybrid is released for Central and Peninsular states including Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Tamil Nadu. This is broader than the supplied list of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf
RECOMMENDED STATES -- Tamil Nadu is confirmed as a growing state in the TNAU page. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/cotton%20sunantha.html

RELEASE YEAR -- Not confirmed. The "Released in 1985" text in the Tamil Nadu book belongs to a potato entry and was excluded. The supplied release year of 2020 is unverified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: DAMAK MC5459 BGII / DAMAK MC5459 BG II (cotton, Rallis India Ltd.)

Searches run: 4 web_search queries (variety overview, breeder/institution, research/trials, seed availability). No result named either "DAMAK MC5459 BGII" or "DAMAK MC5459 BG II". Both names are therefore unconfirmed for every heading below. The search did not reach seednet.gov.in, the CSC minutes, or any Rallis variety page.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The variety-name search returned only unrelated US cotton cultivar patents (DP 570 BGII, DP 576 BGII, and others) and a Nigerian seed-portal entry for MAHYCO C571 BGII. None names this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The searches returned only general Bt cotton material, including a 2022 Genes paper on Cry-gene segregation in Indian Bt hybrids (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9859209/). That paper does not name this variety, so it was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. A Cotton Association of India bulletin reporting AICRP BG II hybrid trials for 2022-23 and 2023-24 (https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__05_29-04-2025.pdf) lists other hybrids such as Rasi Max 003 BG II and ARH 2020 BG II, not this variety. Discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The only marker or QTL hit was a 2022 Uzbek upland cotton study (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9168987/) on different cultivars. Discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The Rallis seeds page (https://www.rallis.com/innovation/seeds) describes the company's cotton programme generally, but does not name this variety or any breeder. Discarded under the strict-relevance rule. The Rallis Dhaanya seeds page (https://www.rallis.com/business/seeds-cn) likewise does not name it.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute contact or address for this variety was returned. The only Rallis-linked results were company and product pages.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, AICRP/ICAR report, thesis or KrishiKosh record names this variety. The KrishiKosh search was not run as a separate query, so this result reflects the four searches only.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The closest result was a KisanShop listing for "Tata Pravir (MC5403) BG II" by TATA Rallis (https://www.kisanshop.in/product/tata-pravir-mc5403-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds). It is a different variety (MC5403, not MC5459) and was discarded. No NSC, state corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for MC5459 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. The states Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat appear only in the input record and were not verified by any search result.

NOTES FOR THE RECORD
- Name check: "variety_name" (DAMAK MC5459 BGII) and "seednet_variety_name" (DAMAK MC5459 BG II) gave the same null results, so the evidence applies to neither name.
- Parentage: "Not specified" in the input. No search result supplied it.
- Suggested next steps: search seednet.gov.in directly for "DAMAK MC5459 BG II" under COTTON (KAPAS) and check the CSC release minutes for the exact name. Also check KrishiKosh and the AICRP cotton annual reports for the 2022–2024 seasons.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: DH 114 (Him Pratham), Wheat, CSKHPKV Palampur, release 2016

Name check: "DH 114" is the CSC release-minute name and "DH 114 (Him Pratham)" is the Seednet name. Every relevant hit used "DH 114" or "Him Pratham" together, and I found no Seednet portal page itself. I did not run a dedicated seednet.gov.in query, so Seednet-specific evidence is missing.

STRESS TOLERANCE
A 2020 Himachal Journal of Agricultural Research study screened DH 114 (described as a released CSK HPKV variety) against other genotypes under early drought stress. It reported that DH 114 showed comparatively small shoot-length reduction, and the authors classed DH 114, DH 40 and C 306 as drought-tolerant -- https://hjar.org/index.php/hjar/article/download/158200/109195
Heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found for DH 114. The release-era review mentions heat tolerance only for unnamed genetic stocks, not DH 114 -- https://academia.edu/49040675/Development_and_release_of_new_wheat_and_barley_varieties_for_different_zones_and_states

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for DH 114 specifically. The same release review says rust resistance is common among 2016-17 releases, but it does not name DH 114 for that trait -- https://www.academia.edu/49040675/Development_and_release_of_new_wheat_and_barley_varieties_for_different_zones_and_states
The Journal of Cereal Research article on DH breeding discusses rust-resistance genetic stocks, but the snippet does not link them to DH 114 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352755629_Developing_genetic_stock_for_yellow_and_brown_rust_resistance_in_Triticum_aestivum_L_via_Imperata_cylindrica-mediated_doubled_haploidy_technique

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Yield, maturity and multi-location trial data for DH 114: No evidence found. The search returned only generic 2016-17 yield ranges across new releases (21.3 to 63.0 q/ha), which are not attributed to DH 114 -- https://www.academia.edu/49040675/Development_and_release_of_new_wheat_and_barley_varieties_for_different_zones_and_states
Sowing and altitude context: A CSK HPKV trial sowing wheat advance lines at four altitudes in rabi 2016-17 is described, but the snippet does not confirm DH 114 was among the entries -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/90083/36774/231170

GENETICS AND QTL
Breeding method: DH 114 was developed by doubled haploid technique -- https://www.academia.edu/49040675/Development_and_release_of_new_wheat_and_barley_varieties_for_different_zones_and_states
Chromosome-elimination route: DH 114 (Him Pratham) is described as the first doubled haploid wheat from the wheat × Imperata cylindrica system, built on work from 2013 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/133100/50408/364658
Gynogenesis: The approach is credited with producing India's first gynogenesis-based wheat cultivar, Him Pratham -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352755629_Developing_genetic_stock_for_yellow_and_brown_rust_resistance_in_Triticum_aestivum_L_via_Imperata_cylindrica-mediated_doubled_haploidy_technique
Parentage: Not confirmed. One HJAR table row pairs "DH 114" with "VWFW 452 × WW 24," but the snippet is ambiguous and I have not attributed it as parentage -- https://hjar.org/index.php/hjar/article/download/158200/109195
Breeding-line codes beyond DH 114 and Him Pratham: No evidence found. The Imperata-DH F1 cross (HS 542/China 84-40,022) is attributed to Patial et al. but not explicitly to DH 114 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352755629_Developing_genetic_stock_for_yellow_and_brown_rust_resistance_in_Triticum_aestivum_L_via_Imperata_cylindrica-mediated_doubled_haploidy_technique
Genome resources, markers and QTL: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: CSK HPKV, Palampur -- https://www.academia.edu/49040675/Development_and_release_of_new_wheat_and_barley_varieties_for_different_zones_and_states
Lead breeder names: No evidence found. The review article's authors include Madhu Patial (ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Tutikandi, Shimla) and Kumar Bishnoi (ICAR-IIWBR, Karnal), with CSKHPKV Palampur as a co-affiliation, but the snippet does not state they bred DH 114 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/133100/50408/364658
Institution-level credit: CSKHPKV's crop-improvement page says the university's faculty developed the DH-breeding approach used for wheat, but the snippet does not name DH 114 -- http://hillagric.ac.in/edu/coa/crop_improvement3/achievements.html
Vice-Chancellor statement: Him Pratham is described as India's first DH wheat variety, and the VC is quoted, but no breeder is named -- https://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_637705204495014146.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder contact: No evidence found.
Institute contact: No evidence found for an official email, phone or postal address for CSKHPKV's wheat programme. The Google Scholar snippet shows a hillagric.ac.in domain only as a faculty-email domain for other authors, so I have not used it as a contact for DH 114 -- https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=yu3JE0YAAAAJ
Related institutional facts without contact details: CSKHPKV Palampur's wheat-related research sites include the Rice and Wheat Research Centre at Malan and the Hill Agricultural Research and Extension Centre at Bajaura, Kullu -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/90083/36774/231170

Not found: a DH 114 entry in the IIWBR "Wheat varieties notified in India" compendium (the snippets seen did not include it) -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
Official listing: The Himachal Pradesh Department of Agriculture lists Him Pratham (D.H.-114) among approved wheat varieties under timely sowing -- https://agriculture.hp.gov.in/en/varieties/
Distribution: The 2024-25 and 2025-26 seed-sales reports name other varieties (DBW-187, PBW-550, DBW-303, and others) and do not mention DH 114 -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/himachal/wheat-seeds-now-available-at-agriculture-sales-centres/amp
Institutional seed production: CSKHPKV Palampur produces breeder and quality seed for hill crops under ICAR-AICRP on Seed, but the answer does not confirm any DH 114 lot -- https://sansad.in/getFile/lsapps/loksabhaquestions/annex/188/AU343_xmE8pP.pdf
Private dealers and NSC: No evidence found.

Himachal Pradesh, higher hills -- https://www.academia.edu/49040675/Development_and_release_of_new_wheat_and_barley_varieties_for_different_zones_and_states

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. No search result gave drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for F2228. Results mentioning F 2228 only cite it as a yield comparator in PAU Bt trials.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for F2228 specifically. The PAU Bt 2/3 announcement describes resistance traits of those Bt varieties, not F2228, and F2228 is named only as a non-Bt check. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=4977

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
F2228 was the non-Bt zonal check in the two-year, five-location North Zone AICRP cotton evaluation of PAU Bt 2 and PAU Bt 3, where it averaged 2,409 kg/ha seed cotton yield. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=4977
The same trial result, reported separately, gives the same 2,409 kg/ha check yield for F 2228. -- https://smartagripost.com/pau/
In the PAU Bt 5 AICRP evaluation (2019–2022, five North Zone locations), F 2228 was one of the comparators; PAU Bt 5 averaged 2,572 kg/ha, and the report cites a 0.25% margin over F 2228. These are PAU Bt 5 results, not F2228 results. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z ; https://bioengineer.org/new-bt-cotton-variety-pau-bt-5-delivers-higher-yields-for-north-india/
Yield context: a 2015 state approval report says F-2228 was approved by the State Varietal Approval Committee with a yield of 7.4 quintals per acre. The page's URL suggests a March 2015 date, which does not match the 2016-08-12 release date in the record. -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/punjab-agri-dept-releases-9-new-varieties-of-crops-115031701010_1.html

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage, pedigree or marker data for F2228 was returned. The PAU Bt 5 paper's pedigree (LH 2298 × PAU Bt 1) belongs to that variety, not F2228. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found for F2228 breeder names, developing scientists or station. The developing institution named in the record is Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana. That institution is confirmed by the state approval report, which lists F-2228 among PAU-developed cotton varieties. -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/punjab-agri-dept-releases-9-new-varieties-of-crops-115031701010_1.html
Breeder names from the PAU Bt 5 paper (Dharminder Pathak and Harish Kumar, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, PAU; Paramjit Singh, Vineet Kumar, Gomti Grover, PAU-RRS Bathinda; Pankaj Rathore, PAU-RRS Faridkot) belong to PAU Bt 5 and are not attributed to F2228. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z

CONTACT DETAILS
No F2228-specific contact found. Institute-level only: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana, Punjab, India; website www.pau.edu (cited in the Wikipedia entry for PAU, which gives the institute's location as Ludhiana and the URL as www.pau.edu). No official email, phone or postal address was returned in the search results. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_Agricultural_University

PUBLICATIONS
Singh, P., Kumar, V., Grover, G., Rathore, P., Pathak, D., & Kumar, H. (2026). American Cotton Bt Variety- PAU Bt 5 (PBH Bt 21). Springer journal (publication details as listed on the article page; F 2228 appears only as a comparator) -- DOI 10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z
No other peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper on F2228 was found. The search returned unrelated cotton papers that do not name F2228.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No Seednet, NSC, PSC, KVK, PAU seed sales or private dealer listing for F2228 was returned. A Tribune article notes that subsidies apply to PAU-approved seed varieties, but it does not name F2228. -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/punjab/punjab-announces-33-subsidy-on-cotton-seeds-to-revive-shrinking-acreage/

RECOMMENDED STATES
Punjab (state-level approval). The 2015 State Varietal Approval Committee report approved F-2228 for Punjab. -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/punjab-agri-dept-releases-9-new-varieties-of-crops-115031701010_1.html
F2228 was used as a zonal (North Zone) check, which indicates it was a Punjab-region reference variety in the AICRP trials, not a North Zone recommendation. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=4977

NAME CHECK
Variety name and Seednet name are both "F2228." No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so the Seednet record and variety code A0501475 could not be verified. The record's 2016 release year is not confirmed; the approval report found is from 2015.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
F2383 (cotton) evidence digest

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "F2383", so every search used both. No page used a different name for this variety. Crop: cotton. Searches run: (1) variety/release/traits, (2) breeder/institution, (3) research papers and trials, (4) seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The variety search returned only unrelated USPTO cotton patents for other varieties (19R238NRB3XF, 16R232B2XF, etc.), which were discarded. No page reports drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for F2383.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page links F2383 to resistance or susceptibility to leaf curl, bacterial blight, leaf spot, nematodes or pink bollworm. The PAU pages on leaf curl and virus-resistant breeding lines (https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/pau-unveils-virus-resistant-cotton-breeding-lines/ and https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&dataE=datae&intID=9404) and the PAU Bt 5 paper (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z) concern other varieties or lines, so I excluded them.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS --
- Plant height of F2383 is recorded as 73.60 cm, versus 56.40 cm for MRC6301, 98.10 cm for MRC6304 and 149.0 cm for LH2076, in a handheld picker field evaluation -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318307499_Field_evaluation_of_portable_handheld_type_cotton_picking_machines_for_different_cotton_varieties
- The same paper records roller-type picker labour on F2383 at 868 man-h/ha, the highest of the four varieties tested -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318307499_Field_evaluation_of_portable_handheld_type_cotton_picking_machines_for_different_cotton_varieties
- A spacing/density study lists F2383 among three varieties (with RCH773 and Suraj) at three locations, including PAU Ludhiana; it reports the most sympods (40) for F2383 at 67.5 x 30 cm spacing at PAU, and the lowest yield (595 kg/acre) for F2383 at 45 x 30 cm at PAU -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339412999_Response_of_desi_cotton_Gossypium_arboreum_L_hybrids_to_spacing_and_fertilizer_levels_under_irrigated_conditions. Caveat: the page title refers to desi cotton hybrids, but the abstract is about F2383 as a G. hirsutum-type entry; treat the crop label as unconfirmed.
- F2383 is listed among semi-compact genotypes suitable for high-density planting systems, with an average yield gain of around 30% under high-density planting across the genotypes studied (this is a group average, not F2383-specific) -- https://www.ojs.pphouse.org/index.php/IJEP/article/download/4891/2397/4839

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No pedigree, parentage or marker/QTL study for F2383 was returned. Parentage is "Not specified" in the release record and the search did not resolve it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found naming a breeder for F2383. The search returned PAU cotton breeding staff pages (Dr Dharminder Pathak, Principal Cotton Breeder, https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?DO=viewFacultyData&_act=manageDepartments&intDepTitleID=0&intFacultyID=36&intLinkID=9&strDepTitle=; Dr Pankaj Rathore, Principal Cotton Breeder, https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/pau-unveils-virus-resistant-cotton-breeding-lines/). These pages do not mention F2383 and are not attributed to it. Institution from the release record: Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana; the PAU Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics handles cotton breeding (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z).

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found for F2383 specifically. The PAU faculty page for Dr Dharminder Pathak shows the email field as "[email protected]" (obfuscated in the extract), with no phone or postal address captured; it is not attributed to F2383 and the email should not be used without checking the source directly -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?DO=viewFacultyData&_act=manageDepartments&intDepTitleID=0&intFacultyID=36&intLinkID=9&strDepTitle=. No PAU institute address or phone was captured in the results.

PUBLICATIONS --
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Field evaluation of portable handheld type cotton picking machines for different cotton varieties. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318307499_Field_evaluation_of_portable_handheld_type_cotton_picking_machines_for_different_cotton_varieties
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Response of desi cotton (Gossypium arboreum L.) hybrids to spacing and fertilizer levels under irrigated conditions. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339412999_Response_of_desi_cotton_Gossypium_arboreum_L_hybrids_to_spacing_and_fertilizer_levels_under_irrigated_conditions
- Authors not captured (2019). Response of Cotton to Varied Levels of Agronomic practices / high-density planting paper. Cotton Association of India (page header dated 16 April 2019). International Journal of Environment and Plant Science, not confirmed -- https://www.ojs.pphouse.org/index.php/IJEP/article/download/4891/2397/4839
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report or DOI for F2383 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The searches returned Pakistani Punjab Seed Corporation pages and a 2025 Tribune item on a 33% seed subsidy for PAU-approved cotton varieties (https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/punjab/punjab-announces-33-subsidy-on-cotton-seeds-to-revive-shrinking-acreage/). None names F2383, so they were excluded. No NSC, Punjab state seed corporation, KVK, PAU seed sale or dealer listing for F2383 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Punjab, per the release record (variety_name and seednet_variety_name both "F2383"). No search result independently confirmed the recommendation or the release notification date (2016-08-12 in the record). No CSC release minute or Seednet portal page was retrieved.

seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Growth habit of plants of FBt 16-4 indeterminate. The plants are tall and its stem has no pigmentation with sparse hairiness. The leaves of FBt 16-4 are palmate in shape with medium hairiness and presence of nectarines and gossypol glands. The bracts of FBt 16-4 are normal. It has cream flower and open, medium size ovate shaped bolls with pitted surface. Seed fuzz of FBt 16-4 is medium and white in colour.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to FDK 124. Searches returned only general statements about desi cotton. The compendium and Tribune pages describe reduced flower drop compared with other desi varieties, but they do not link this to drought or any other stress, so it is not treated as drought evidence.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to FDK 124. The reduced flower drop reported in the compendium and Tribune pages is not linked to heat in the sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Cotton leaf curl virus (CLCV): a 2011 press report says PAU expected FDK-124 to be highly resistant to CLCV. This is a pre-release expectation, not a field-validated result, and no peer-reviewed or trial confirmation was found. No other disease resistance was found; CSC disease reaction is 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: Whitefly and jassid: pages describe FDK 124 as tolerant to jassid and whitefly (compendium, Tribune) and list resistance to whitefly and jassid (Apnikheti). Evidence is descriptive; no trial data were found. CSC pest reaction is 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 20 to 21.00 q/ha (under normal condition). Compendium: 23.2 q/ha. Apnikheti: about 9.3 quintals/acre (approximately 23 q/ha by conversion). AICRP 2024-25 (indicative, ambiguous table layout): mean seed cotton yield about 2873 kg/ha and mean lint yield about 1086 kg/ha. The compendium describes FDK 124 as a high-yielding desi variety.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability analysis was found; AICRP 2024-25 multi-location data are indicative only.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC adaptation_ecology: irrigated conditions. Trial locations in the AICRP 2024-25 report: Sriganga Nagar, Faridkot, Bathinda and Sirsa. Sowing guidance (first April to 15 May for desi cotton in Punjab) is a general desi-cotton statement, not FDK 124 specific, and is kept as context only.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Morphological characteristics: Not specified in CSC record. CSC agronomic feature: spacing of 67.5 x 45.0 cm and 100% dose of N, i.e. 75 kg N/ha, recommended. Apnikheti and croplibrary pages report fibre length 21 mm and ginning outturn 36.4%. AICRP 2024-25 gives GOT about 37.8% (indicative).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: FDK 124 (cotton, desi/Gossypium arboreum)

Name note: The CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "FDK 124" in the input, and I found no separate Seednet portal record. All evidence below refers to the name "FDK 124" (also written FDK-124 or FDK124). Several pages discuss other PAU cotton varieties (LD 327, LD 694, FDK 331, PAU Bt 1), and I excluded those.

Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder/institution, research, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pages describe FDK 124 as tolerant to jassid and whitefly, and as producing less flower drop than other desi varieties. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf ; https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/bathinda/demand-for-native-cotton-varieties-on-the-rise-231086
- A 2011 press report says PAU expected FDK-124 to be highly resistant to cotton leaf curl virus (CLCV); this is a pre-release expectation, not a field-validated result. -- https://agrisalsa.wordpress.com/2011/08/27/pbw-621for-wheat-and-fdk-124-desi-cotton-new-varieties-from-pau-ludhiana/
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to FDK 124. Searches returned only general statements about desi cotton.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistance to whitefly and jassid is listed for FDK 124. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/fibre-crops/cotton
- CLCV resistance is claimed in the 2011 press release (see above). No peer-reviewed or trial confirmation was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity about 160 days; average yield about 9.3 quintals/acre; fibre length 21 mm; ginning outturn 36.4%. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/fibre-crops/cotton ; https://croplibrary.com/cotton-farming-profit-per-acre/
- Compendium gives yield 23.2 q/ha and states that FDK 124 is a high-yielding desi variety with early maturity in the desi-cotton list. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf
- The 2024-25 AICRP-Cotton annual report lists FDK 124 (ZC) as a zonal check in trials at Sriganga Nagar, Faridkot, Bathinda and Sirsa. The table gives a mean seed cotton yield of about 2873 kg/ha and mean lint yield of about 1086 kg/ha, with GOT about 37.8%. The table layout is ambiguous, so treat these values as indicative. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf
- Sowing: first April to 15 May for desi cotton in Punjab. -- http://ekapas.com/punjab/ (this is a general desi-cotton statement, not FDK 124 specific; keep only as context)

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: selection from LD 830. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf
- No QTL, marker or mapping study naming FDK 124 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Released by Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf ; https://agrisalsa.wordpress.com/2011/08/27/pbw-621for-wheat-and-fdk-124-desi-cotton-new-varieties-from-pau-ludhiana/
- The press item quotes PAU Director of Research S S Gosal on the variety's development. -- https://agrisalsa.wordpress.com/2011/08/27/pbw-621for-wheat-and-fdk-124-desi-cotton-new-varieties-from-pau-ludhiana/
- No page names the individual breeder who developed FDK 124. The PAU Plant Breeding department page lists Dr Dharminder Pathak as Principal Cotton Breeder, and the AICRP report names Dr Paramjit Singh as Principal Cotton Breeder at RRS Bathinda. Neither page links them to FDK 124 as developers, so they are not attributed here. -- https://pau.cyberframe.in/pau-new/public/college/coa/departments/Plant ; https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or direct contact for FDK 124 was found.
- Institute-level: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana. No PAU contact page with phone or email was retrieved in these searches. Please check the PAU website directly.
- Email addresses that appear in a symposium volume (ashokkumar@pau.edu, vineet2906@pau.edu) belong to other papers' authors and are not attributed to this variety, so I have not listed them as contacts. -- https://www.crdaindia.com/downloads/files/n5ed776da939b5.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- Gosal SS (ed.) (year not shown). A Saga of Progress: Compendium of 50 Years of Achievements. Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf
- AICRP on Cotton (2025). Annual Report 2024-25 (FDK 124 as zonal check, multi-location trial data). Central Institute for Cotton Research -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Comparative studies on seed protein characteristics in eight lines of two Gossypium species. Journal of Cotton Research -- https://jcottonres.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s42397-019-0024-3 . Caution: this uses an "FDK-124" line of G. arboreum, and the page does not confirm it is the PAU variety.
- Excluded: an ResearchGate entry on Bt cotton under Khanewal conditions (Pakistan) mentions "FDK124", but the page does not establish it is the PAU variety, so I have not listed it.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- A 2011 press item stated that sufficient seed was available for multiplication. -- https://agrisalsa.wordpress.com/2011/08/27/pbw-621for-wheat-and-fdk-124-desi-cotton-new-varieties-from-pau-ludhiana/
- A Tribune article (roughly ten years old) reports strong farmer demand for FDK-124 seed in the Bathinda cotton belt, with desi seed sold out early in the season. -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/bathinda/demand-for-native-cotton-varieties-on-the-rise-231086
- Ekapas lists FDK 124 as a recommended desi variety for Punjab. -- http://ekapas.com/punjab/
- No Seednet listing, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales page for FDK 124 was found. Bharat Beej result did not mention FDK 124 and was discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Punjab: confirmed by the PAU compendium and press items. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf ; https://agrisalsa.wordpress.com/2011/08/27/pbw-621for-wheat-and-fdk-124-desi-cotton-new-varieties-from-pau-ludhiana/
- Haryana and Rajasthan: No evidence found in the searched pages. These states appear only in the input record and are unverified here.
- Release year: the input gives 2010-12-23 (CSC minutes), but the PAU compendium and 2011 press report give 2011. This discrepancy should be checked against the CSC notification.

drought.details: No evidence found of drought tolerance ratings for F 2228. A kharif 2017 sowing-date trial at Faridkot and Bathinda reported that seed cotton yield fell with each delay in sowing across all tested cultivars. This is a general trend for the trial and not a tolerance rating for F 2228, and it does not describe drought mechanisms.

disease_resistance.summary: No evidence found that F 2228 itself is rated resistant or susceptible to cotton leaf curl disease (CLCuD) or other diseases. The researchgate source reports yield only. A search at ncbi PMC9442625 returned only unrelated Texas cotton work and was not used as evidence for F 2228. F 2228 was one of the American genotypes used as a parent, crossed with three wild or synthetic donors, to transfer CLCuD resistance. This is parentage evidence, not a resistance rating. The krishikosh.egranth.ac.in source was not directly retrieved and is not cited. The source actually retrieved for this statement is the crdaindia PDF.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found that F 2228 is rated resistant or susceptible to bollworms or other pests. The ncbi PMC9442625 search returned only unrelated Texas cotton work.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yield of 7.4 quintal per acre at approval in 2015. Two-year AICRP North Zone trial at five locations: F 2228 was the non-Bt zonal check at 2,409 kg/ha seed cotton yield. Kharif 2017 Faridkot/Bathinda trial: 2,295 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the multi-location AICRP North Zone trial results summarised under field trials. The digest reports no stability analysis for F 2228.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Punjab. Listed among PAU-developed American cotton varieties released in 2015. Tested at Faridkot and Bathinda in south-western Punjab under kharif 2017 sowing-date conditions. No further agro-climatic adaptation data found.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Kharif 2017 Faridkot/Bathinda trial reported a plant height in the 153-155 cm range group. Other morphological characteristics: Not specified in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Two-year AICRP North Zone trial at five locations: F 2228 served as non-Bt zonal check at 2,409 kg/ha seed cotton yield; PAU Bt 2 and PAU Bt 3 were 20.6% and 17.9% higher. (2) Kharif 2017 Faridkot/Bathinda trial: F 2228 yielded 2,295 kg/ha, below the Bt hybrids NCS 855 BGII (2,997 kg/ha) and RCH 650 BGII (2,884 kg/ha); plant height 153-155 cm range group. (3) AICRP 2019-2022 North Zone trial: the newer PAU Bt 5 exceeded F 2228 by a marginal 0.25%. F 2228 is only the comparator in this result, which concerns PAU Bt 5.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE (name: F 2228; variety and Seednet names are identical)
- No evidence found of drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance ratings for F 2228. A kharif 2017 sowing-date trial at Faridkot and Bathinda reported that seed cotton yield fell with each delay in sowing across all tested cultivars, which is a general trend and not a tolerance rating -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330037095_Performance_of_Bt_and_non_Bt_cotton_cultivars_under_different_sowing_environment_of_south_western_Punjab

DISEASE AND PEST (name: F 2228)
- No evidence found that F 2228 itself is rated resistant or susceptible to cotton leaf curl disease, bollworms or other pests. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330037095_Performance_of_Bt_and_non_Bt_cotton_cultivars_under_different_sowing_environment_of_south_western_Punjab (the page reports yield only); https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9442625/ returned only unrelated Texas cotton work
- F 2228 was one of the American genotypes used as a parent, crossed with three wild or synthetic donors, to transfer cotton leaf curl disease resistance. This is parentage evidence, not a resistance rating -- https://www.krishikosh.egranth.ac.in (not directly retrieved); source actually found: https://www.crdaindia.com/downloads/files/n5ed776da939b5.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (name: F 2228)
- Approved by the Punjab State Varietal Approval Committee in 2015 alongside F-2383, with a reported yield of 7.4 quintal per acre -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/punjab-agri-dept-releases-9-new-varieties-of-crops-115031701010_1.html
- Listed among PAU-developed American cotton varieties released in 2015 -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/features/a-year-of-highs-and-lows-for-farm-varsity-175053
- Two-year AICRP North Zone trial at five locations: F 2228 served as the non-Bt zonal check at 2,409 kg/ha seed cotton yield; PAU Bt 2 and PAU Bt 3 were 20.6% and 17.9% higher -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=4977
- Kharif 2017 Faridkot/Bathinda trial: F 2228 yielded 2,295 kg/ha, below the Bt hybrids NCS 855 BGII (2,997 kg/ha) and RCH 650 BGII (2,884 kg/ha); its plant height was 153-155 cm range group -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330037095_Performance_of_Bt_and_non_Bt_cotton_cultivars_under_different_sowing_environment_of_south_western_Punjab
- AICRP 2019-2022 North Zone trial: the newer PAU Bt 5 exceeded F 2228 by a marginal 0.25% -- https://bioengineer.org/new-bt-cotton-variety-pau-bt-5-delivers-higher-yields-for-north-india/ (F 2228 is only the comparator here) and https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z

GENETICS AND QTL (name: F 2228)
- No evidence found of QTL, marker or pedigree studies on F 2228. Its only genetic role found is as a parent in CLCuD introgression work

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
GBCH-1801 BG II (variety name and Seednet name are identical)

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Search 1 ("GBCH-1801 BG II cotton variety") returned no page naming this variety. It returned pages on other BG-II products, including Aditya BG-2 (LAM BG II-2208, ANGRAU), which is a different variety and is excluded.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches 1 and 3 returned only other BG-II hybrids and Bollgard II research papers that do not name GBCH-1801 BG II. These are excluded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. Search 3 ("GBCH-1801 BG II cotton research paper trial") returned trial and efficacy papers on Bollgard II in Burkina Faso, the USA and India, none about this variety. Excluded.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Searches 1 and 3 returned QTL and gene-expression studies on upland cotton and Bt cotton generally, none about this variety. Excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. Search 2 ("GBCH-1801 BG II cotton breeder developed by") returned biographies of Indian cotton breeders (Ravindranath, Krishnamurthy) and a BT-cotton history note. None names a developer of GBCH-1801 BG II. The input record lists the institution as Green Gold Seeds Pvt. Ltd., but no search result confirms this, so it is unverified. Breeder names from the search results are not attributed here because they do not refer to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No institute, company or breeder contact page for this variety was returned. Green Gold Seeds Pvt. Ltd. contact details were not found in search results.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Search 3 returned journal articles and reports on Bt cotton, BG-II hybrids and refugia in India. None names GBCH-1801 BG II. No KrishiKosh, AICRP or ICAR report was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Search 4 ("GBCH-1801 BG II cotton seed availability") returned retailer listings for other BG-II products (Alpgiri, Speedboll, Mr. White, Sanket NBC 101, Sawaj and others). None lists GBCH-1801 BG II. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU source was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Not verified. The only source is the input record ("Maharashtra, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh"). No search result confirms it.

Notes: The 2022-06-17 release date and the parentage ("Not specified") come only from the input record and are not confirmed by any search result. All four searches were run, and none returned evidence about this variety. A search on the Seednet portal or the CSC release minutes is the next step, since those are the primary sources for a variety record.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The same CICR paper reports that GN Cot-25 gives 25 to 30 q/ha seed cotton yield, cited to Venugopal et al. (2013), and describes it as a cheaper alternative to Bt hybrids. This is a secondary citation, not a trial result. -- https://baumwollboerse.de/wp-content/uploads/vortraege/Patil-Desi-herbaceum-India.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- An encyclopedia entry gives GN Cot-25 (2010) a duration of 140 to 210 days, 37 to 39% ginning outturn, 23 mm mean hair length and 30 to 40 count spinning. This is low-reliability and has no primary source. -- https://grokipedia.com/page/Gossypium_herbaceum

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found for parentage, breeding-line code, breeding method, QTL or genome resources. The only Navsari combining-ability paper found concerns G. hirsutum and GN.Cot-22, so it was discarded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/326738680_Combining_Ability_Analysis_for_Seed_Cotton_Yield_and_Its_Component_Traits_in_Cotton_Gossypium_hirsutum_L

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution: Navsari Agricultural University (NAU), per the CICR breeding paper and the encyclopedia entry. -- https://baumwollboerse.de/wp-content/uploads/vortraege/Patil-Desi-herbaceum-India.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. The NAU Main Cotton Research Station (Surat) is the likely station, but no page links a named breeder to GN.Cot. 25. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/533b4-aboutus_cottonhighlight.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level only (no breeder contact found):
Institution: Main Cotton Research Station, Navsari Agricultural University, Athwa Farm, Surat 395007, Gujarat -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/533b4-aboutus_cottonhighlight.pdf
Email: cottonist@nau.in (listed under NAU in the cotton highlights document) -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/533b4-aboutus_cottonhighlight.pdf
Postal address for applications: Research Scientist (Cotton), Main Cotton Research Station, NAU, Ghod Dod Road, Athwa Farm, Surat-395007 -- https://gujaratasmita.net/navsari-agricultural-university-nau-cotton-research-station-surat-recruitment-2025/
Phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Patil, S. (year not confirmed in extracted text). Breeding and genetic improvement of G. herbaceum desi cotton in India. ICAR-CICR, Division of Crop Improvement (conference presentation; author surname taken from the file name) -- https://baumwollboerse.de/wp-content/uploads/vortraege/Patil-Desi-herbaceum-India.pdf
Sandipan, P. B., Patel, R. K., Faldu, G. O. and Patel, D. M. (2019). Status of Different Diseases of Cotton under South Gujarat Region of India. Journal not identified (ResearchGate record, NAU Main Cotton Research Station, Surat) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/337082723_Status_of_Different_Diseases_of_Cotton_under_South_Gujarat_Region_of_India
Caionline (2015). History of Cotton in Gujarat. Report/publication; states GN.Cot.25 was released for the entire state in 2010 -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/34_24-11-2015.pdf
No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or QTL study specific to GN.Cot. 25 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The NAU seed-sale page returned only Gujarati notices with no cotton listing. Breeder seed production is mentioned for the Main Cotton Research Station, but no GN.Cot. 25 quantities or dealers were found. -- https://www.nau.in/pages/seed-available-for-sale-1555953550
Seednet (seednet.gov.in) was not reached by any search.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Gujarat. A history document says the variety was released for cultivation across the entire state. -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/34_24-11-2015.pdf
The "recommended_states_raw" field (Not specified) should be updated to Gujarat from this source.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease rating for G.Cot-38 was found, including for bacterial blight and wilt. The JAU Cotton Research Station page names jassid and bacterial blight resistance as breeding goals of the station, but it does not state that G.Cot-38 carries either trait. No resistance is confirmed for any disease.

pest_resistance.summary: Jassid (Amrasca biguttula biguttula): in a rainfed screen of cotton genotypes, GJHV-497 recorded 6.0 jassids per 3 leaves per plant. The paper states that none of the 13 entries was rated resistant, but the snippet does not give GJHV-497's category, so no jassid resistance rating is assigned to G.Cot-38. No other pest reaction was found.

The sheet's layout makes it unclear whether these lines belong to G.Cot-38 or to a preceding entry, so they are reported here only as unattributed agronomy and are not assigned to G.Cot-38. Fibre quality and other multi-location trial data were not found.
