drought.details: MR-786 is identified as a good general combiner for days to 50% flowering and days to 50% boll bursting within discussions on biotic and abiotic stress management. Its direct drought tolerance level is not specified.

heat.details: MR-786 is identified as a good general combiner for days to 50% flowering and days to 50% boll bursting. It is mentioned in the context of identifying temperature stress/heat tolerant donors as parents in breeding programs, implying its potential utility in developing heat-tolerant lines, but its direct heat tolerance level is not specified.

salinity.details: MR-786 is identified as a good general combiner for days to 50% flowering and days to 50% boll bursting in discussions that include salt tolerance evaluations of other lines (e.g., FL 478). Its direct salinity tolerance level is not specified.

flood.details: MR-786 is identified as a good general combiner for days to 50% flowering and days to 50% boll bursting in the context of studies on field performance of genotypes under natural flash flood conditions. Its direct flood tolerance level is not specified.

disease_resistance.summary: MR-786 is stated to possess robust disease-resistant traits. It is also recognized as a good general combiner for traits related to multiple disease resistance and for identifying resistant sources.

pest_resistance.summary: MR-786 is commercially marketed as 'अमेरिकन नॉन बीटी नरमा' (American Non-Bt cotton), indicating it does not carry Bt-mediated insect resistance. While general discussions about insect resistance in cotton (including a novel cry2AX1 gene) are present in the search results, no inherent pest resistance mechanisms are explicitly attributed to MR-786.

agronomic_details.yield: MR-786 is described as a good general combiner for cotton yield per plant, indicating its genetic potential for contributing to high yields. It is also mentioned in the context of genetic improvement for kapas yield. Quantitative yield for MR-786 specifically is not provided, however, a hybrid cross involving MR-786 (MCU 13 x MR 786) recorded a yield of 2138 (units not specified).
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly specified in the provided search results.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for cultivation in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh. Its performance in crosses has been evaluated in various trials.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not available in image. A hybrid cross involving MR-786 (MCU 13 x MR 786) has a maturity duration of 140-150 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: MR-786 is identified as a good general combiner for early flowering (days to 50% flowering) and boll development (days to 50% boll bursting). For the hybrid MCU 13 x MR 786, desirable characteristics include a high Ginning outturn (36.2%), high boll number (39.0), and long staple length (UHML – 29.5 mm).
agronomic_details.field_trials: MR-786 has been utilized in breeding programs, with its performance as a parent in crosses (e.g., MCU 13 x MR 786) discussed in proceedings from Tamil Nadu Agricultural University. It was also part of discussions regarding the field performance of genotypes under natural flash flood conditions.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not specified for MR-786 specifically.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs linked to MR-786 were identified.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Molecular breeding is generally mentioned in the context of achieving submergence tolerance in cotton. Discussions also include a novel cry2AX1 gene for insect resistance in cotton, but this is not applicable to MR-786 as it is a non-Bt variety. No specific molecular mechanisms are detailed for MR-786 itself.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NBC 1821 BG II (cotton)

Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder/institution, research papers and trials, seed availability). Both names were searched: "variety_name" NBC 1821 BG II and "seednet_variety_name" NBC 1821 BG II. The retailer pages use the marketing name "Rana-900" (also written "Rana 900"), and I treated that as the same product only where the page also gives NBC-1821. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so no finding below is from seednet.gov.in.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Water stress: an eAgroStore listing claims "very high-level water stress tolerance" for NBC 1821 Rana-900 BG II. This is an unverified retailer claim, not a trial result. -- https://eagrostore.com/item/nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii/
- Heat, salinity, flood, submergence, drought (trial-based): No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Sucking pests: listings describe "high degree sucking pests tolerance" and resistance to sucking pests. -- https://eagrostore.com/item/nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii/ ; https://agribegri.com/products/buy-nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii-cotton-seeds.php ; https://www.krushivista.com/products/ba1f4aac33/1477796000004641896
- Bollworm resistance: The BG II trait is listed as "BGII technology" on the agribegri page. The page gives no bollworm trial data. -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii-cotton-seeds.php
- Disease resistance (wilt, leaf curl, blight, etc.): No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity: 150 days (eAgroStore); about 160–170 days harvest (agribegri). These two sources conflict. -- https://eagrostore.com/item/nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii/ ; https://agribegri.com/products/buy-nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii-cotton-seeds.php
- Plant type and boll traits: vigorous, erect habit; boll weight 6–8 g; oval white bolls; ginning 35–38%; compressed bolls, chain boll-bearing, synchronous boll bursting. -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii-cotton-seeds.php ; https://eagrostore.com/item/nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii/
- Sowing window: June to July; well-drained black and loam soil; sowing depth 3–5 cm. -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii-cotton-seeds.php
- Yield: only a qualitative "high yield potential" claim. No yield numbers (q/ha) found. -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii-cotton-seeds.php
- Multi-location or AICRP trial results for this variety: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Trait technology: BG II is the only genetic information in the sources. No parentage, marker or QTL data was found. The "Parentage: Not specified" entry is therefore unchanged. -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii-cotton-seeds.php
- QTL and marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developer or company: listings name Nath Bio-Genes / Nath Seeds as brand and manufacturer, with country of origin India. -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii-cotton-seeds.php
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.
- Developing station or research institution: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. No institute-level email, phone, postal address or contact page was found for Nath Bio-Genes (1) Ltd. in these results. The only contact-like data is a generic "contact us" for bulk orders on the agribegri page. -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii-cotton-seeds.php

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. The searches returned no peer-reviewed paper, thesis, conference paper or AICRP report that names NBC 1821 or Rana-900.
- Discarded for name resemblance or other varieties: AICRP BG II hybrid trial summaries (they name Rasi Max 003, ARH 2020 and RCH 773, not NBC 1821) -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__05_29-04-2025.pdf ; a 2018 industry note that mentions a Nath Seeds Bt event sourced from China, which does not identify this hybrid -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/20_14-08-2018.pdf ; and the Aditya BG-2 (LAM BG II-2208) release from ANGRAU, a different variety -- https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/andhra-pradesh/angrau-unveils-public-sector-bt-cotton-variety-aditya-bg-2-1961377

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Online retailer listing (Rana-900 NBC-1821 BG II, Nath, F1 hybrid, about Rs 899): listed as available on a marketplace but recorded in the search as "No reviews". -- https://www.desikheti.com/collections/cotton-seeds-buy-online

- KrushiVista (Tierra-branded pack, 475 g): recorded as out of stock, about Rs 901. -- https://www.krushivista.com/products/ba1f4aac33/1477796000004641896
- agribegri: recorded as out of stock. -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii-cotton-seeds.php
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or ICAR seed-sales listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The record lists Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. None of the retrieved pages names these states for NBC 1821. The only regional statement is "suitable for Central and South India" on the agribegri listing. -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii-cotton-seeds.php
- Confirmation of the four states from an official notification: No evidence found.

Overall: the evidence is limited to retailer listings, which are commercial claims rather than official records. Release date, breeder, institute contact, trial yields and publications need to be checked against the CSC/CVRC minutes, the Seednet portal entry, and KrishiKosh before this record is treated as complete.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NBHB-1851 (Seednet name NBHB-11), cotton (Kapas)

Searches run: 4 (variety name, Seednet name, breeder/contact, research). No search result named NBHB-1851 or NBHB-11 as a cotton variety, so almost every heading below is "No evidence found."

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for NBHB-1851 or NBHB-11. The heat-tolerance study returned (50 cotton genotypes at seedling stage) does not name this variety, so I excluded it. -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39881237/ (excluded)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for NBHB-1851 or NBHB-11. The only pest-related hit was a Nath Bio-Genes BG II hybrid product page (V-Sport), which is a different product, so it was excluded. -- https://agribegri.com/products/v-sport-bgii-cotton-seeds--buy-online-cotton-seeds-.php (excluded)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found for NBHB-1851 or NBHB-11. No field-trial or agronomy result named either name. A Nath Bio-Genes Kashinath 2 cotton product was listed, but it is a different variety and was excluded. -- https://agroinfomart.com/Nath-Bio-genes-India-Ltd (background only, excluded for relevance)

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for NBHB-1851 or NBHB-11. No parentage (164 x 5006) or marker data appeared in any result. The parentage is only in the input record, not verified by search.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Company-level evidence only; no breeder is named for NBHB-1851 or NBHB-11.
- Nath Bio-Genes (I) Ltd. is described as the flagship company of the Nath Group, supplying BT, hybrid and varietal seeds, with a history dating to 1979. -- https://www.nathbiogenes.com/about/
- The company's about page says its first scientists included Dr. C T Patel, who began the cotton breeding program. This is a company-level statement; it does not link Dr. Patel to NBHB-1851 or NBHB-11. -- https://www.nathbiogenes.com/about/
- Shri Satish Kagliwal is listed as Managing Director, and Nandkishor Kagliwal as promoter. These are corporate roles only, not breeding roles. -- https://www.nathbiogenes.com/about/

PUBLICATIONS

The result for "L-1851" (USPTO cotton cultivar L-1851) is a different Greek G. barbadense variety and was excluded. -- https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/8399748 (excluded)

SEED AVAILABILITY

RECOMMENDED STATES

No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/armita-ncs2778-bt2-hybrid-cotton-seeds
A retailer page claims resilient performance in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh field conditions, but it gives no trial data, so I have not treated this as stress-tolerance evidence. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/armita-ncs2778-bt2-hybrid-cotton-seeds

DISEASE AND PEST
The retailer lists the hybrid as carrying Bollgard II (Cry1Ac + Cry2Ab) technology for pest protection. This is a trait description on a sales page, not an efficacy study. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/armita-ncs2778-bt2-hybrid-cotton-seeds
No disease-resistance evidence found. -- (none)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The 2025 CAI newsletter names "Armitha (NCS 2778)" as the hybrid used by a farmer in Nalgonda district, Telangana, in the 2023 season, under high-density planting at 90 cm x 18 cm spacing. GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for parentage, marker or QTL studies for this variety. The Bollgard II trait description above is the only genetic detail, and it comes from the retailer page. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/armita-ncs2778-bt2-hybrid-cotton-seeds

No lead breeder or scientist name found. -- (none)

No listings from NSC, a state seed corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or other private dealers found.

pest_resistance.summary: Leafhopper: in a 2011-12 and 2012-13 Warangal trial, non-Bt Orugallu Krishna had the lowest leafhopper count (1.53 per top three leaves); Neeraja was the only entry statistically on par. Chewing and other pests: Helicoverpa armigera, Spodoptera litura and Erias vitella larvae were present on non-Bt Orugallu Krishna but below the economic threshold; pink bollworm incidence was nil. These are comparative field observations in one trial series, not formal resistance ratings.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Orugallu Krishna (WGHH-2), cotton (Gossypium hirsutum)

Name note: The CSC name "Orugallu Krishna" and the Seednet name "Orugallu Krishna (WGHH-2)" refer to the same entry. Every source below uses the WGHH-2 code or the bare name for this variety, so the evidence applies to both headings.

Search coverage: 4 web_search queries (release/traits, breeder/institution, research, seed). The Seednet portal, KrishiKosh, and AICRP annual reports were not queried directly. Release year (2010) and parentage (WGHP-1 x WGHP-2) come from the input record; I found no search source confirming either.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/central-telangana-zone/
- Early maturity and big boll size are described, but not as stress tolerance. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/7.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- In a 2011-12 and 2012-13 Warangal trial, the non-Bt Orugallu Krishna had the lowest leafhopper count (1.53 per top three leaves). Neeraja was the only entry statistically on par. -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/EVALUATION-OF-DUAL-TOXIN-TRANSGENIC-Bt-COTTON-PESTS-Kumar/ff339baebed6b00c9191cde23c1d1518263457ca
- Helicoverpa armigera, Spodoptera litura, and Erias vitella larvae were present on non-Bt Orugallu Krishna but below the economic threshold. Pink bollworm incidence was nil. -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/EVALUATION-OF-DUAL-TOXIN-TRANSGENIC-Bt-COTTON-PESTS-Kumar/ff339baebed6b00c9191cde23c1d1518263457ca
- Disease resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield is given as 30-40 q/ha, with staple length of 26-28 mm, under wide adaptability. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/7.pdf
- Listed among intra-specific cotton varieties/hybrids in the RARS Warangal cotton package of practices. -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/package%20of%20practices/Cotton.pdf
- Used as the non-Bt comparison entry in the dual-toxin Bt hybrid trial at RARS Warangal, kharif 2011-12 and 2012-13. -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/EVALUATION-OF-DUAL-TOXIN-TRANSGENIC-Bt-COTTON-PESTS-Kumar/ff339baebed6b00c9191cde23c1d1518263457ca
- Multi-location or AICRP yield data: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found (no QTL, marker, or parentage-confirmation study located).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing station: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Warangal, now under Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTAU/PJTSAU). The input record says ANGRAU; the search sources name PJTAU. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/7.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. Kaderbad Ravindranath is a cotton breeder linked to ANGRAU, but no source links him to Orugallu Krishna, so he is not attributed here. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaderbad_Ravindranath
- The station's mandate includes developing high-yielding G. hirsutum hybrids and varieties for rainfed and irrigated systems. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/7.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Station in-charge: Dr. Ravula Uma Reddy, Associate Director of Research, RARS Warangal. Email: adrwgl@pjtau.edu.in. Mobile: 8332970385. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/central-telangana-zone/
- Postal address: Office of the Associate Director of Research, RARS Warangal, Mulugu Road, Hanamkonda (Warangal). -- https://pjtau.edu.in/central-telangana-zone/
- Lead cotton breeder: No evidence found; institute-level contacts above.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured in search snippet (2011-13). "Evaluation of dual toxin transgenic Bt cotton hybrids against insect pests of cotton." Semantic Scholar record (Kumar et al. listed by URL slug; verify before citing). -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/EVALUATION-OF-DUAL-TOXIN-TRANSGENIC-Bt-COTTON-PESTS-Kumar/ff339baebed6b00c9191cde23c1d1518263457ca
- Authors not captured in snippet (c. 2017-18). "Incidence and management of sucking pest complex in dual toxin transgenic Bt cotton hybrids." ResearchGate record; the abstract confirms the RARS Warangal trial. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324571370_Incidence_and_management_of_sucking_pest_complex_in_dual_toxin_transgenic_Bt_cotton_hybrids
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report, or release-notification record was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The Ekapas Telangana list includes Orugallu Krishna (WGHH-2) among recommended cotton options. This is not a seller listing. -- http://ekapas.com/telangana/
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sales, or private dealer listing for Orugallu Krishna was found. The dealer pages returned were for other hybrids.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The input record says "Not specified," and no source gave a notified state list. The only geographic evidence ties the variety to the Warangal station in Telangana. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/7.pdf
- Official CSC/gazette notification, including states of recommendation: No evidence found.

The TNAU Cotton Research Station, Srivilliputhur "Varieties Released" page (https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-srivilliputhur/varieties-released/) is an unverified lead, since it lists released cotton varieties, but the retrieved text did not show PA 833 or PA-183.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: Searches used "PA-740" and "PA 740". All relevant pages use "PA 740" (the CSC/variety name and the Seednet name "PA-740" refer to the same variety). The Seednet portal itself returned no results in these searches. The crop is desi cotton, Gossypium arboreum, not G. hirsutum.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The release paper reports the variety as tolerant to bacterial blight and Alternaria leaf spot, and tolerant to sucking pests. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The paper only describes consistent yield across the South Zone under rainfed conditions. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bacterial blight and Alternaria leaf spot tolerance and sucking-pest tolerance, as listed above. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- No evidence found for specific pest or disease ratings beyond these.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Mean seed cotton yield was 13.63 q/ha, against 13.67 q/ha for the zonal check and 13.50 q/ha for the local check. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- On-farm trials showed about 17.81% higher seed cotton yield than check PA 402. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- Fibre traits: mean length 27.86 mm, strength 25.06 g/tex, micronaire 5.06. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- The release paper describes the fibre as long staple with high strength and acceptable micronaire. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- Maturity, plant density and fertiliser recommendations: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Breeding method: pedigree method. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- Parentage "PA 183 x PA 375" comes from the task input only. No search result confirmed it.
- QTL, marker or genomic studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety was developed at the Cotton Research Station, Maheboob Baugh Farm, Vasantrao Naik Marathwada Krishi Vidyapeeth (VNMKV), Parbhani. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- The research station page lists PA 740 among its desi cotton releases (PA 528, PA 740, PA 810, PA 812, PA 837). -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/research_ResearchStations.php
- The university's Nanded station page records PA 740 as released by the Central Variety Release Committee in 2019. -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/Research/CottonResearchStationNanded
- Named lead breeder: No evidence found. The release-paper authors are VN Chinchane, KS Baig, SB Borgaonkar and AH Rathod. Their roles as breeders are not stated in the search results. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or direct contact was found in the search results.
- Institute-level: Cotton Research Station Mahboob Baugh Farm, Parbhani - 431 401 (MS), as listed. No email or phone shown. -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/research_ResearchStations.php
- University postal address, Parbhani - 431 402, from a VNMKV document (MoU text). No email or phone shown. -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/Research/CottonResearchStationNanded
- The Nanded station page shows an "Officer Incharge" label, but the name is cut off in the search result, so it is not recorded here. -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/research_ResearchStations.php

PUBLICATIONS
- Chinchane, V. N.; Baig, K. S.; Borgaonkar, S. B.; Rathod, A. H. (2020). PA 740: High yielding, superior fibre quality Desi cotton (Gossypium arboreum) variety for South zone of India. The Pharma Innovation Journal (chemijournal.com), Vol. 8, Issue 6, pp. 1951-1954 -- https://www.doi.org/10.22271/chemi.2020.v8.i6ab.11051
- Journal name is taken from the chemijournal.com site. The search result does not show the journal title explicitly.
- No AICRP/ICAR annual reports, KrishiKosh theses, or QTL papers on PA 740 were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealers for PA 740. The seed-related results returned unrelated products (US cotton seed, a Punjab subsidy notice that does not name PA 740, and craft threads). Seednet was not returned by any search.
- The VNMKV accreditation report mentions a state seed corporation (Mahabeej) producing seed of a different cotton variety (NHH-44), not PA 740. -- https://vnmkv.ac.in/static/documents/accreditation/UNIVERSITY_VNMKV_SSR.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Released for rainfed South Zone (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu) by the Central Variety Release Committee in 2019. Telangana is included in this source but was not in the task input. -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/Research/CottonResearchStationNanded
- Also released for Marathwada region of Maharashtra by Joint AGRESCO and notified in 2019. -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/Research/CottonResearchStationNanded
- The release paper gives the same South Zone rainfed recommendation. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PBH 115 (cotton, Gossypium hirsutum)

Name checked: "PBH 115" (CSC minutes name) and "PBH 115" (Seednet name). The two names are identical, so one search set covered both.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The search returned a Pakistani cotton line, NIBGE-115, and it is not this variety.
DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The search returned NIBGE-115 (CLCuD tolerance) and Prabhat Supercot PCH-115 (a Bt hybrid), and neither is this variety.
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The search returned no trial or agronomy page naming PBH 115.
GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The search returned no marker or QTL study naming PBH 115.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. No page names a breeder or developing station for PBH 115.
CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No Punjab Agricultural University contact page or PBH 115 contact turned up.
PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis names PBH 115.
SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The only "PCH 115" listings are for Prabhat Seeds Supercot PCH-115 BG-II, a private hybrid, and they are discarded as a different product. Other listings for it (IndiaMART, Kisan Center) are discarded for the same reason.
RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. No page links PBH 115 to Punjab, Haryana or Rajasthan.

Discarded results (name resemblance only): NIBGE-115 (Pakistan, not PBH 115); Prabhat Supercot PCH-115 BG-II hybrid (private, not PBH 115); DMC 115 pearl cotton thread (not a crop).

Unverified lead, not attributed to PBH 115: a PAU Bt cotton release named "PAU Bt 5 (PBH Bt 21)" was found. Its DOI is 10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z and it is at https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z. It reports release in 2023 for Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan, and its pedigree is LH 2298 × PAU Bt 1. The "PBH Bt 21" designation is different from "PBH 115", and the 2023 release year differs from the 2022-06-17 date in the record, so I have not linked it to this variety. The record's name and release date should be checked against the CSC minutes and the Seednet entry before any link is made.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PCH 5677 Bt2 / PCH 5677 Bt II (cotton)

Names searched: "PCH 5677 Bt2" (variety_name, CSC minutes) and "PCH 5677 Bt II" (seednet_variety_name). Neither name was matched on any page returned. Crop: cotton (kapas). Variety code A05011055 and release date 2020-11-09 come from the input record only and were not verified by any search.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The variety-plus-trait search returned no page naming PCH 5677 Bt2 or PCH 5677 Bt II.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The search returned general Bt cotton pages (Bollgard I and II, Monsanto technology) and a Brazilian field-efficacy paper on other Bt events. None names this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The trial search returned only the Brazilian Bt event study (DAS-21023-5 x DAS-24236-5 x SYN-IR102-7), which is a different product and was discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Nothing returned on marker, QTL or event composition for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. The breeder search returned Bollgard technology pages (Monsanto), which are not this variety and were discarded. No lead breeder, developing station or institute page for PCH 5677 Bt2 was found. The input lists the institution as Prabhat Agri Biotech Ltd., which is unverified.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute or company contact, email, phone or address for this variety was returned.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The research search returned no paper, AICRP or ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper naming this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for this variety. The one seed listing returned is for "Prabhat Seeds Supercot PCH-115 BT2" at https://kisancenter.com/product/prabhat-seeds-supercot-pch-115-bt2-cotton-seeds/217988. It is a different product name and was discarded under the strict relevance rule. The seed-availability search also returned an ANGRAU Lam BG II-2208 (Aditya BG-II) release article, which is a different variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The states Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh appear only in the input record and were not confirmed by any search result.

NOTE: The four permitted searches were used in the first pass, and the first-pass results were the basis of this digest. A second verification pass was attempted and was refused by the tool's usage limit, so no further checks were run. Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in), CSC release minutes, and the Prabhat Agri Biotech site are the most likely sources to verify these details directly.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Phule Satpuda (JLA-1207), cotton (Gossypium arboreum, desi)

Name check: The search results used "Phule Satpuda (JLA-1207)" for both the CSC-minutes name (variety_name) and the Seednet name (seednet_variety_name). The only difference is spacing, so I treat them as one variety. No Seednet portal page was retrieved directly, so the Seednet evidence below comes from the notification lists and the ICAR report. The searches did not return CSC minutes themselves.

Discrepancies to resolve:
- Release year: the record says 2023-05-02. A notification dated 25 September 2023 is reported in news coverage (The notification was released by Pankaj Yadav, Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare on 25th September 2023. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-106-new-varieties-of-31-major-crops-for-farmers/). A review lists JLA-1207 with the year 2022 (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378713890_Significance_of_desi_Cotton_Gossypium_arboreum_-A_Brief_Review).
- Institution: the record names the Oilseeds Research Station. The review attributes the desi cotton varieties, including JLA-1207, to Agriculture Research Station; Jalgaon, Maharashtra, Agriculture Research Station, Jalgaon; affiliated to MPKV, Rahuri is the prime research center (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378713890_Significance_of_desi_Cotton_Gossypium_arboreum_-A_Brief_Review).
- Parentage (JLA-794 x JLA-104): not confirmed by any retrieved source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Suitable for rainfed conditions; resistant to jassids and bacterial leaf blight, and moderately resistant to grey mildew -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. Desi cotton in general is described as resilient to drought and pests, but this is not variety-specific (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378713890_Significance_of_desi_Cotton_Gossypium_arboreum_-A_Brief_Review).

DISEASE AND PEST
- Jassid resistance, bacterial leaf blight (BLB) resistance and moderate grey mildew resistance are as listed above -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf
- Pest resistance beyond jassids: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Seed cotton yield of 14.14 q/ha and maturity of 165-170 days, as reported in the ICAR annual report for 2023-24 -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf
- Multi-location trial data and the original release trial details: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage JLA-794 x JLA-104: No evidence found in retrieved sources.
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: the Agriculture Research Station, Jalgaon, affiliated to MPKV Rahuri, is credited with desi cotton varieties including JLA-1207 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378713890_Significance_of_desi_Cotton_Gossypium_arboreum_-A_Brief_Review
- Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder names, roles, emails, phones: No evidence found.
- Institute-level contact (Jalgaon station or MPKV Rahuri): No evidence found. No address, email, phone or contact-page URL was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Patil, S. S., Gavit, A. F., Magar, N. M., & Pawar, V. Y. (2009). Phule JLA 794 diploid cotton variety for Khandesh tract of Maharashtra. J. Cotton Res. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378713890_Significance_of_desi_Cotton_Gossypium_arboreum_-A_Brief_Review (cited through a review; DOI not retrieved; concerns the parent JLA-794, not JLA-1207)
- No variety-specific peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR trial reports, theses (KrishiKosh) or conference papers were found for JLA-1207.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for Phule Satpuda (JLA-1207) from NSC, a State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU sales or private dealers. The seed-dealer listings retrieved (IndiaMART Sonpeth, NaPanta) name other products and do not mention this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, South Rajasthan and Gujarat, listed as an open-pollinated cotton variety for sale -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/indian-government-released-2-new-varieties-of-cotton-for-farmers/ and https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-106-new-varieties-of-31-major-crops-for-farmers/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RVA 1001 / RAH-100 (cotton, Kapas): EVIDENCE DIGEST

Search log: 4 web_search queries run. Query 1 covered "RVA 1001 asalio cotton variety". Query 2 covered "RAH-100 cotton variety developed by". Query 3 covered "RVA 1001 cotton research paper trial". Query 4 covered "RVSKVV KNK College of Horticulture Mandsaur cotton variety RVA 1001 seed". None returned a page that names RVA 1001 or RAH-100 together with cotton. Nothing below is attributed to this variety.

Name check: the evidence refers to neither name. "RVA 1001" and "RAH-100" both returned zero matching pages, and no Seednet page was returned. The "asalio" crop name also matched nothing, and the Seednet crop is COTTON (KAPAS).

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Query 1 and query 3 returned only unrelated cotton trials and products: desi cotton varieties such as Aravinda, Srinandi, Yaganti and Veena, plus Kanchana (LPS 141) and LK-861 from a Rajendranagar package-of-practices PDF (https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/package%20of%20practices/Cotton.pdf). None of these is RVA 1001 or RAH-100.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned US and Australian variety records (for example, cotton variety 781000G exhibits resistance to bollworm, cotton leafworm, pink bollworm, and tobacco bud worm, https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/7714201). These are other varieties and are discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Query 3 returned trial reports for other cultivars, such as the University of Georgia study on the cotton cultivar Deltapine 2038 B3XF (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378429025005507). It does not mention RVA 1001 or RAH-100 and is discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No QTL, marker or pedigree source for RVA 1001 or RAH-100 was returned. The parentage string in the record, "( RAMPBS 155 X MCU5) X RAS- 299 - 1 X LARA 5166)", was not found in any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for this variety. The only Indian cotton breeder returned was Kaderbad Ravindranath, who at ANGRAU developed ten new cotton varieties such as Narasimha and Aravinda (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaderbad_Ravindranath). He is not linked to this variety, so he is not attributed to it. The institution in the record, RVSKVV's KNK College of Horticulture, Mandsaur, is a horticulture college. A RVSKVV page lists 12 departments including plant breeding and genetics and plant pathology (https://www.rvskvv.net/index.php/institutions). No cotton programme or RVA 1001 release by that college was found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level only; no breeder contact found. Institute contact for College of Horticulture, Mandsaur (listed as the institution in the record; not confirmed as this variety's developer): contact info dean[dot]mandsaur[at]rvskvv[dot]net, address Mandsaur-485001, Mandsaur, Madhya Pradesh (https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/allstinstitutions/college-horticulture-mandsaur-0). Institution website: http://www.rvskvv.net (https://www.rvskvv.net/index.php/institutions). The email address above is written in obfuscated form in the source; verify it on the official site before use.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper naming RVA 1001 or RAH-100 was returned. Query 3 returned only unrelated cotton items, such as USPTO patents for other cotton varieties.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Query 4 returned a RVSKVV seed production page that describes Raj Vijay seed and planting materials produced as per state and national requirement (https://www.rvskvv.net/index.php/research/seed-production-programme). It does not name this variety, so it is not counted as a finding. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or dealer listing for RVA 1001 or RAH-100 was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The record lists Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat, but no search result confirms this for the variety. The MP-state context above (the Mandsaur institution) is institutional, not variety-specific.

Overall: the record for RVA 1001 / RAH-100 could not be verified from these sources. The listed institution is a horticulture college, and the record's parentage and crop name should be checked against the CSC release minutes and the Seednet portal directly.

drought.details: No evidence found in the digest for drought tolerance specific to RLC 2. The record's stress_reaction field states the variety is eminently adapted to extremes of climatic conditions including drought, high rainfall and floods, but the digest does not corroborate this claim. A 2024 germplasm stability study lists RLC-2 among top performers for photosynthetic pigment stability across environments; the digest explicitly classifies this as a stability result, not a stress-tolerance result, so it is not used to assign a drought level.

heat.details: No evidence found in the digest for heat tolerance specific to RLC 2. The record's general stress_reaction statement is not corroborated by the digest. The 2024 pigment stability study is not stress-tolerance evidence and is not used here.

salinity.details: No evidence found in the digest for salinity tolerance specific to RLC 2.

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest for flood tolerance specific to RLC 2. The record's stress_reaction statement mentioning floods is not corroborated by the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The digest found no evidence of disease resistance for RLC 2. The white-rust resistance returned by the PAU page is attributed to RLC 3, not RLC 2, and has been excluded. The record's disease_reaction field is 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The digest found no evidence of pest resistance for RLC 2. The record's pest_reaction field is 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: Record value: 3000.00 to 3500.00 Kg/Ha. Digest values from two sources: 2039-2342 kg/ha (AICRP release/identification table and review table). The record value is not corroborated by the digest and conflicts with both digest sources.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for yield stability across environments. The 2024 germplasm study lists RLC-2 among top performers with high stability for photosynthetic pigment content and composition across environments; this is a pigment stability result, not a yield stability result.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended states per digest sources: Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Jammu and Rajasthan (parts of Rajasthan per the AICRP report). The record lists Punjab only, which is narrower than both sources. Suitability for July-August sowing and non-lodging habit are stated in the record's agronomic_features field; the digest does not corroborate these. Stress-related adaptation (drought, flood) is not corroborated by the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RLC 2 (variety_name) / RCH-2 (seednet_variety_name), mustard (Brassica juncea), IC 511615

Name note: all evidence below refers to RLC 2 (also written ELM 123 in the sources). No search returned a page naming RCH-2. The seednet crop field in the record says COTTON (KAPAS), which conflicts with the mustard crop field. Four searches were run; none targeted RCH-2 or the Seednet portal directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to RLC 2. One 2024 germplasm stability study lists RLC-2 among top performers for photosynthetic pigment stability across environments, which is a stability result rather than a stress-tolerance result. The combined analysis found NPJ-182, NC-533728, CN-105233, RLC-2, CN-101846, JA-96, PBR-357, JM-3, and DTM-34 as top performers with high stability. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11120-024-01116-3

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for RLC 2 disease or pest resistance. The white-rust resistance returned by the PAU page is attributed to RLC 3, not RLC 2. -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewMatter&intDepTitleID=20&intLinkID=9

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Release/identification table: RLC 2 (IC 511 6), identified 2016, 142-150 days to maturity, yield 2039-2342 kg/ha, oil 36.3-38.9%, low erucic acid, Punjab. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
Second AICRP row gives 132-155 days maturity, 35.2-40.2% oil, and a 2011 entry with parentage "QM 4 x Pusa". This conflicts with the record's 2016 release year and its parentage RC91A x RC 86R. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
Review table: RLC-2 (ELM 123), 2011/2012 entry, 2039-2342 kg/ha, 36.3-38.9% oil, superior oil quality, suited to Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Jammu and Rajasthan. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13051604/

GENETICS AND QTL
RLC 2 is listed with 1.8 erucic acid and genotype e1e1 e2e2, consistent with low erucic acid. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.738805/xml
RLC 2 was among varieties with least admixture in an SSR diversity analysis of Indian mustard. -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0272914
No QTL or mapping study specific to RLC 2 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No breeder name found for RLC 2. The PAU page credits PAU with zero-erucic RLC 1 and canola-quality RLC 3, but does not name RLC 2. -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewMatter&intDepTitleID=20&intLinkID=9
The AICRP report lists RLC 2 in the national varietal identification table without naming a developing centre. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
The PAU link above is the only developing-institution page retrieved. Ownership of RLC 2 by PAU is therefore not confirmed by the retrieved evidence; the record's institution field is unverified.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, email, phone or postal address for RLC 2 appeared in the results. The PAU College of Agriculture page retrieved contains no contact details. -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewMatter&intDepTitleID=20&intLinkID=9

PUBLICATIONS
Ansari, A.A., Akhatar, J., Sharma, S. et al. (2024). Integrating multiple statistical indices to measure the stability of photosynthetic pigment content and composition in Brassica juncea (L.) Czern germplasm under varying environmental conditions. Photosynthesis Research 162, 63-74 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11120-024-01116-3 (DOI not shown in retrieved text; the DOI is 10.1007/s11120-024-01116-3 per the URL)
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2021). Development and Validation of Kompetitive Allele-Specific PCR Assays for Erucic Acid Content in Indian Mustard [Brassica juncea (L.) Czern and Coss.]. Frontiers in Plant Science -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.738805/xml (DOI 10.3389/fpls.2021.738805)
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2022). Molecular characterization and genetic diversity analysis in Indian mustard (Brassica juncea L. Czern & Coss.) varieties using SSR markers. PLOS ONE -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0272914 (DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0272914)
Authors not shown in retrieved text. AICRP Rapeseed-Mustard Project Coordinator's Report (2020-21). ICAR-DRMR -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for RLC 2 or RCH-2 from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales or dealers. The NSC listing returned was for RH-725/RH-761, which are different varieties and were discarded. The Punjab seed-trader listings name no variety and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Punjab, Haryana, New Delhi, Jammu and parts of Rajasthan. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Jammu and Rajasthan. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13051604/
The record lists Punjab only, so it is narrower than both sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RCH-971 BG II (cotton)

Name check: the CSC release-minute name and the Seednet name are both "RCH-971 BG II", so every item below refers to the same name. I did not retrieve a seednet.gov.in page. All evidence comes from commercial seed-retailer pages and one 2025 journal article, so none of it is an official ICAR, CICR, or SAU source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Retailer pages describe tolerance to sucking pests and to viral disease, and say the variety suits both irrigated and rain-fed conditions. -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds ; https://www.kisanshop.in/product/rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds ; https://managramasethu.in/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bgii-cotton-hybrid-seed
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned no claims on these stresses for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
Tolerance to TSV (tobacco streak virus) and the sucking pest complex is claimed on a retailer listing. -- https://kisanestore.com/products/cotton-rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii
A retailer page also lists "natural resistance to sucking insects" and a general claim of disease, virus and pest resistance. These are marketing claims, not trial data. -- https://agribegri.com/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bgii-hybrid-cotton-seeds.php
Bollgard II (Cry1Ac + Cry2Ab) bollworm protection is stated on retailer pages. -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds ; https://www.kisanshop.in/product/rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds
Pest-resistance evaluation in official trials: No evidence found. The IPM and Cry-toxin papers that came up do not name this variety, so I excluded them.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity of 150–160 days, early flowering, and boll weight of 6–7 g are listed. -- https://agribegri.com/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bgii-hybrid-cotton-seeds.php ; https://managramasethu.in/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bgii-cotton-hybrid-seed
Sowing and agronomy: May–July sowing, dibbling at 2–3 cm depth, 4 ft row spacing, a seed rate of about 950 g per acre, and 5–7 irrigations. These are retailer specifications. -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds ; https://www.kisanshop.in/product/rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds
Field demonstrations: a 2025 article reports 60 high-density planting (HDPS) demonstrations of RCH-971 BG-II, at 90 x 15 cm spacing against a 120 x 30 cm control, in Nandyal district, Andhra Pradesh, 2023-24 to 2024-25. The work was under an ICAR-CICR special project. The article does not report yield figures in the retrieved text. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue7S/PartD/S-8-7-12-416.pdf
Yield data for this variety: No evidence found. One retailer page says yield is "based on agricultural practices," with no figure.
Multi-location AICRP yield results for this variety: No evidence found. The AICRP summary that came up covers BG II hybrids in general and names RCH 659, not RCH-971, so I excluded it. -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__05_29-04-2025.pdf (excluded)

GENETICS AND QTL
Trait construction: the hybrid is described as carrying BollGard II (two Cry genes). No parentage is given. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds
Parentage: No evidence found. The registration record says "Not specified".
QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RCH 846 BG II -- Evidence Digest

Name note: "variety_name" and "seednet_variety_name" are identical ("RCH 846 BG II"). Retailer and listing pages also use "RCH 846 BGII", "RCH-846-BGII" and "RCH 846 BG". I treated these as the same variety. No Seednet or CSC record was found, so the evidence under each heading is commercial listings, not official records.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listing claims good tolerance to pests and diseases, with no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/rasi-rch-846-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds
- Retailer says the hybrid is described as resistant to pests and diseases, reducing spray needs. This is marketing text, not trial data -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/cotton-seeds-online-rasi-846-variety
- No abiotic stress (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) evidence found for this variety -- searched under query 1, no hits.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bollgard II (Cry1Ac and Cry2Ab) technology is stated for resistance against certain pests, with bollworm protection implied -- https://www.badikheti.com/cotton-seeds/pdp/rasi-rch-846-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds-kapas-ke-beej/90hxopn3
- Retailer lists leaf spot and leaf blight as the disease the companion fungicide controls. This is a fungicide recommendation, not variety resistance -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/cotton-seeds-online-rasi-846-variety
- No independent pest or disease screening data found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Early-maturing hybrid, big bolls, easy picking -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/rasi-rch-846-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds
- Retailer gives crop duration of 140-145 days, yield of 14-15 quintal (unit and basis not stated), sowing May-June, dibbling, 2-3 cm depth, row spacing 4.5 ft and plant spacing 2 ft, 7-8 irrigations, medium to heavy soil -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/cotton-seeds-online-rasi-846-variety
- Badikheti FAQ gives sowing season April-May and seed rate about 950 g per acre. This conflicts with the May-June sowing window above -- https://www.badikheti.com/cotton-seeds/pdp/rasi-rch-846-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds-kapas-ke-beej/90hxopn3
- No field-trial or multi-location data for RCH 846 BG II found. The AICRP North Zone BG II hybrid trial report names RCH 659 BG II, not this variety -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__05_29-04-2025.pdf (excluded)

GENETICS AND QTL
- Bt trait is Bollgard II (Cry1Ac and Cry2Ab), per listing -- https://www.badikheti.com/cotton-seeds/pdp/rasi-rch-846-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds-kapas-ke-beej/90hxopn3
- Parentage: not specified in the input; no parentage found in any search.
- No QTL or marker studies found for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Listing identifies the developer as Rasi Seeds Pvt. Ltd. -- https://www.badikheti.com/cotton-seeds/pdp/rasi-rch-846-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds-kapas-ke-beej/90hxopn3
- Rasi Seeds Pvt. Ltd. is listed as manufacturer of RCH-846-BGII from Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. This is a company listing, not a breeder record -- https://www.indiamart.com/rasi-seeds-pvt-ltd-lucknow/cotton-products.html
- Named individual breeder: none found for this variety. R. Krishnamurthy is described as Rasi's cotton research director in general, with no link to RCH 846 BG II -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajagopalan_Krishnamurthy (not attributed to this variety)
- Kisanshop page lists brand as "Mahyco Seeds" for the same product. This conflicts with Rasi and is unresolved -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/rasi-rch-846-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found.
- Institute-level: Rasi Seeds (P) Ltd. is described as having been started in 1973 at Attur, Salem District, Tamil Nadu -- https://www.indiamart.com/rasi-seeds-salem/ (no email, phone or postal address for this variety)
- Rasi Seeds Private Limited, Salem, Tamil Nadu: listed contact is "Madakannu (Marketing Manager)". This is a sales contact, not a breeding contact, and the page does not name RCH 846 BG II -- https://www.indiamart.com/rasiseedssalem/hybrid-cotton.html (institute-level only, excluded from variety attribution)
- Rasi Seeds Pvt. Ltd., Jalgaon, Maharashtra: listed contact is "Amit Kumar (Manager)". The page does not name RCH 846 BG II -- https://www.indiamart.com/rasi-seeds-p-ltd-jalgaon/ (excluded)
- No official email, phone, or ICAR/SAU contact page found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. Searches for papers, theses, AICRP reports and KrishiKosh returned only RCH 2, RCH 659, MRC 7201, Bunny and other Bt cotton studies, none naming RCH 846 BG II. Excluded examples include https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277098324_Studies_on_performance_of_Bt_cotton_genotypes_under_rainfed_situation_through_farmers_participatory_approach and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341265522_BT_COTTON_PRODUCTIVITY_AND_PROFITABILITY_AS_INFLUENCED_BY_NUTRIENT_LEVELS_AND_NITROGEN_SPLIT_APPLICATION_UNDER_IRRIGATION

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Kisanshop: 475 g pack priced at about ₹900, listed as out of stock -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/rasi-rch-846-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds
- Badikheti: 2,375 g (5 x 475 g) listed at ₹4,500, shipping ₹90, cash on delivery offered -- https://www.badikheti.com/cotton-seeds/pdp/rasi-rch-846-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds-kapas-ke-beej/90hxopn3
- Krushidukan: 475 g x 2 combo with UPL Saaf fungicide, now marked out of stock -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/cotton-seeds-online-rasi-846-variety
- Amazon.in: 475 g pack, currently unavailable, manufacturer listed as a generic "Shree Shyam Kisan Seva Kendra" -- https://www.amazon.in/Cotton-Plant-Seeds-Farming-Gardening/dp/B0F48D7VD2
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or official seed-sales listing found. Seednet was not reached.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/rasi-rch-846-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds
- Same states on Badikheti listing -- https://www.badikheti.com/cotton-seeds/pdp/rasi-rch-846-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds-kapas-ke-beej/90hxopn3
- Krushidukan lists no recommended states.
- Official CSC release minutes and Seednet state notifications: not found. The 2020-11-09 release date and variety code A0501453 are unverified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RCH 929 BG II (cotton)

Name check: the CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "RCH 929 BG II", so they are identical and no separate Seednet-name search was needed. Variety code A0501455, institution Rasi Seeds (P) Ltd., released 2020-11-09. Four searches were run: variety/release, breeder/institution, research/trials, and seed availability.

Result: none of the four searches returned a page that names RCH 929 BG II. The pages returned were about other Rasi cotton hybrids (RCH 926, 947, 971, 999, 659, 2, 515, 668, 779) and other companies' Bt hybrids. I excluded all of them under the strict relevance rule. The only near-match, RCH 926 BG II, is a different variety, so its CLCuV tolerance and plant-habit notes are not attributed here.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searches returned only drought, CLCuV, and sucking-pest claims for other RCH hybrids.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The only Bollgard II pest-resistance material returned concerns RCH 947, RCH 971, RCH 999 and RCH 659, which are different varieties.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The AICRP 2022-23 Bt trial report that appeared in results covers BG II hybrids in general and names RCH 659 BG II (ZC), not RCH 929 BG II. Maturity, yield and spacing data for this variety were not found.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. No parentage, pedigree, or marker study for RCH 929 BG II was returned. Parentage remains "Not specified."

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. No breeder or scientist is named against RCH 929 BG II. Institution-level text on the Rasi Seeds product list concerns RCH 1 and RCH 2 (1992), not this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. One Rasi Seeds listing gives a Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu location and an owner name, but it appears on a page for RCH 2 BG II, not this variety, so it is excluded. Source: https://www.indiamart.com/rasi-seeds-pvt-ltd/cotton-products.html

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. Returned papers and reports concern BG I/BG II hybrids and cotton in general, and none names RCH 929 BG II. The KrishiKosh and AICRP searches did not surface any item for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. Rasi Seeds' own product pages sell RCH 926, 947, 971, 999, 659 and 779, but no seller listing for RCH 929 BG II was returned. Rasi Seeds corporate page: http://www.rasi.in/rasiseeds/products.html

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found for this variety. The GEAC approved-products list returned contains RCH-2 BG II and RCH-515 BG II (Rasi), but the excerpts seen do not include RCH 929 BG II. The raw states given in the record (Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu) could not be checked against any source. Source for the list: http://www.geacindia.gov.in/resource-documents/approved-products/Final_commercially_approved.pdf

Suggested next steps for this record: check the CSC release minutes for 2020-11-09 directly, look up A0501455 on the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in), and search KrishiKosh and the Rasi Seeds company office for breeder and contact details.

Only the Rasi Seeds product page mentions a stress-related trait for this variety. It says the hybrid has better tolerance to jassid, which is a sucking-pest tolerance, not an abiotic stress. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found. -- https://www.rasiseeds.com/cotton/rch-951/

DISEASE AND PEST
The same Rasi page describes RCH 951 as a CLCuV tolerant hybrid, meaning tolerance to cotton leaf curl virus. This is a manufacturer claim with no trial data attached. -- https://www.rasiseeds.com/cotton/rch-951/
The same page also lists big bolls with clean bursting (manufacturer claim). -- https://www.rasiseeds.com/cotton/rch-951/
No independent evaluation of this variety's pest or disease resistance was found. The other pages returned (RCH 971, RCH 659, RCH 947, RCH 999) describe different varieties and were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No yield, maturity, plant-type or spacing data was found for RCH 951 BG II. A YouTube video titled "Rasi 951 Cotton Seeds| RCH 951 Review" exists, but the indexed text is Hindi and contains no verifiable technical figures. It was not used as evidence. -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuSGBpNJN7Y&pp=ygUHI3JjaDc5MQ%3D%3D
Result: No evidence found for yield, maturity or multi-location trial performance of RCH 951 BG II.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The variety is a Bollgard II (Cry1Ac and Cry2Ab, MON 15985) hybrid according to the variety name, but no page the searches returned names RCH 951 with that construct. The GEAC list returned covers other Rasi hybrids (RCH-2 BG II, RCH-515 BG II) and was discarded for this variety. -- http://www.geacindia.gov.in/resource-documents/approved-products/Final_commercially_approved.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No breeder or scientist name for RCH 951 BG II was found. The only institution named for this variety is the developer and seller, Rasi Seeds (P) Ltd, per the CSC record and the Rasi product page. -- https://www.rasiseeds.com/cotton/rch-951/
Rasi Seeds' own corporate page describes its early cotton research hybrids (RCH 1 and RCH 2 in 1992), which is company history, not a link to this variety. -- http://www.rasi.in/rasiseeds/products.html

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact was found. Company-level contact information was found only on a listing for a different variety (RCH 2 BG II), and it is recorded here as company-level, not as a verified contact for RCH 951 BG II: Rasi Seeds Pvt. Ltd., Satay Murthy Road, Ram Nagar, Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu (address on the listing; phone and email not shown). -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rch-2-bg-ii-cotton-21125879333.html
No official email, phone or institute contact page for Rasi Seeds was found in the search results. The Rasi products page was returned but its contact details were not in the indexed text. -- http://www.rasi.in/rasiseeds/products.html

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. The search returned no paper, AICRP or ICAR report, thesis or KrishiKosh record naming RCH 951 BG II. Results that appeared (for example the Springer IPM paper on BG-II pink bollworm, and the PKV journal paper on rainfed cotton productivity) do not name this variety and were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No seller listing for RCH 951 BG II was found. Retailers returned listings for other Rasi hybrids (RCH 971 BG II/Swift, RCH 947 BG II/Prime, RCH 659 BG II, RCH 797 BG II, RCH 578 BG II/Neo), which were discarded. -- https://www.kisanestore.com/cotton-seeds?sort=p.price&order=DESC
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale record was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
The Rasi Seeds page for RCH 951 lists Recommended States: Rajasthan. -- https://www.rasiseeds.com/cotton/rch-951/
This conflicts with the CSC record, which gives Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan. The CSC-recorded states are not supported by any page found in this search. Note the conflict in the reference record; the CSC minutes should be checked directly.

drought.details: No evidence found that RG-18 (or "RGT - 1") has any tested drought tolerance. Searches returned no RG-18 record. Nandyal Sanaga 1 (NBeG 3), released 2013 by ARS Nandyal for irrigated Andhra Pradesh, is listed as tolerant to drought, but it matches only the release year, not the name, so it is not a confirmed match. Gaur et al. (2019) reviews drought and heat breeding at ANGRAU Nandyal among other institutes but does not mention RG-18. Barmukh et al. (2022) and Bharadwaj et al. (2021) relate to QTL-hotspot drought adaptation and are not about RG-18.

heat.details: No RG-18 heat tolerance evidence found. Gaur et al. (2019) reviews breeding for heat adaptation in chickpea with ANGRAU Nandyal among contributing institutes, but does not mention RG-18.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. No salinity evidence for RG-18 in the digest.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. No waterlogging or flood evidence for RG-18 in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: No evidence found for RG-18 disease resistance. Nandyal Sanaga 1 is listed as tolerant to wilt, but it is an unconfirmed match and not this variety. Nandyal Gram 452 (ANGRAU, RARS Nandyal, 2020) is listed as tolerant to wilt-unrelated pod borer only in the pest context and is a different variety; no disease claim is attributed to it in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for RG-18 pest resistance. Nandyal Gram 452 (ANGRAU, RARS Nandyal, 2020) is listed as tolerant to pod borer Helicoverpa, but it is a different variety. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found that RG-18 (or "RGT - 1") has any tested stress tolerance. Searches 1 and 3 returned no RG-18 record. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Nandyal Sanaga 1 (NBeG 3), released 2013 by ARS Nandyal for irrigated Andhra Pradesh, is listed as tolerant to drought and wilt. This matches the release year only, not the name, so it is not a confirmed match to this record. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Gaur et al. (2019) reviews breeding for drought and heat adaptation in chickpea, with ANGRAU Nandyal among the contributing institutes. It does not mention RG-18. -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/pbr.12641

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for RG-18 disease or pest resistance. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Nandyal Gram 452 (ANGRAU, RARS Nandyal, 2020) is listed as tolerant to pod borer Helicoverpa. It is a different variety. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Nandyal Sanaga 1 (unconfirmed match, see STRESS TOLERANCE) is listed as tolerant to wilt. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No RG-18 yield, maturity, or trial data found. Searches 1 and 3 returned no record of the name. Search 3 found no RG-18 trial data. -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Nandyal Sanaga 1 (unconfirmed match): about 110 days, yield 23-24 q/ha, irrigated. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- A 2017-18 Rabi trial at RARS Nandyal (ANGRAU) evaluated chickpea cultivars for mechanical-harvest suitability. Its cultivar list was not captured, so RG-18 cannot be confirmed as included. -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2018/vol7issue5/PartAJ/7-5-220-230.pdf
- Ratnam, Sowmya and Kishore Babu (2023) studied foliar nutrition on chickpea at RARS Lam, which is not variety-specific. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/TJRA/article/view/148699

GENETICS AND QTL
- No RG-18 genetic, pedigree, or QTL evidence found. The parentage SC-75 x RG-2-1 was not found in any result. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/
- Barmukh et al. (2022) characterises QTL-hotspot introgression lines for drought adaptation. It is not about RG-18. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9730794/
- Bajaj et al. (2015) reports seed-weight and yield-component QTLs in a desi x kabuli mapping population. It is not about RG-18. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4365403/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Identity note: the variety name "RGT - 1" is corrupted in the input, and no search result matched it. The Seednet name "RG-18" is listed under cotton (kapas), which conflicts with the chickpea crop in the release record. No evidence was found linking RG-18 to chickpea. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No breeder name for RG-18 was found. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/
- Institution context: ANGRAU Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Nandyal, is the chickpea research station in the search results and is the only ANGRAU chickpea centre named in the results. -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34961053
- Veera Jayalakshmi is a Principal Scientist at ANGRAU RARS Nandyal and a chickpea breeder. Her link to RG-18 is not established. -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/women-scientists-create-top-3-climate-smart-chickpea-varieties-in-india-for-2022

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. Name: Veera Jayalakshmi, role: Principal Scientist, ANGRAU RARS Nandyal (not confirmed as RG-18 breeder). Email as found: veera.jayalakshmi@gmail.com. Phone: not found. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/
- Institute address as found: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), Nandyal 518501, India. -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34961053
- Official ANGRAU institute email or phone: not found in results. ANGRAU site is angrau.ac.in. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/ANGRAU-AR-2019-20-Final_pdf.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- No RG-18 publication found. Searches 1 and 3 returned no paper, report, thesis, or KrishiKosh item naming RG-18 or the release.
- Gaur et al. (2019). Integrated breeding approaches for improving drought and heat adaptation in chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.). Plant Breeding (author list partly captured) -- https://doi.org/10.1111/pbr.12641
- Barmukh, R. et al. (2022). Characterization of 'QTL-hotspot' introgression lines reveals physiological mechanisms and candidate genes associated with drought adaptation in chickpea. Journal of Experimental Botany -- https://doi.org/10.1093/jxb/erac348
- Bajaj, D. et al. (2015). A combinatorial approach of comprehensive QTL-based comparative genome mapping and transcript profiling identified a seed weight-regulating candidate gene in chickpea. Scientific Reports -- https://doi.org/10.1038/srep09264
- Bharadwaj, C. et al. (2021). Introgression of "QTL-hotspot" region enhances drought tolerance and grain yield in three elite chickpea cultivars. The Plant Genome -- https://doi.org/10.1002/tpg2.20076
- Ratnam, M., Sowmya, D. and Kishore Babu, G. (2023). Enhancing the productivity of chickpea through foliar nutrition under rainfed conditions. Journal of Research ANGRAU 51(4), 27-33 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/TJRA/article/view/148699
- Authors not captured (2018). Estimate of growth and yield parameters of chickpea cultivars amenable to mechanical harvesting. Journal of Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry 7(5), 2089-2091 -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2018/vol7issue5/PartAJ/7-5-220-230.pdf

- Seed production centres and farmers' access constraints for chickpea in Kurnool and Prakasam were reported, with no RG-18 detail. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/5066/1/rr-adoption-cp-ap.pdf
- Dealer directories for Anantapur (NaPanta) are generic and not chickpea-specific. -- https://www.napanta.com/seed-dealer/andhra-pradesh/anantpur/

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Andhra Pradesh, as given in the release record. No RG-18 notification or state recommendation was found in the search results. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Nandyal Sanaga 1 (unconfirmed match) is listed for Andhra Pradesh. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I could not complete this record. The tool-call limit was reached partway through, so the evidence below comes from one batch of four searches whose output I only partly captured.

Search status: My first batch ran the four queries (variety, breeder, research, seed availability). I then re-ran the same batch to print fuller snippets, which used up the search quota. Only the first 300 characters of each result were printed, so most pages were not fully read. Some of the relevant text may sit in the parts I did not see.

EVIDENCE DIGEST (RS 2818, Cotton / COTTON (KAPAS))

Name check: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "RS 2818". Seednet was not searched separately, so all evidence below refers to the name "RS 2818" and I cannot confirm a Seednet entry.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found in the captured text. The searches did not return any drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for RS 2818.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found in the captured text.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A review on high-density planting in Indian cotton lists RS 2818 in a table of released varieties, with a year of 2020 and central release status. It is in a section on high-density planting systems. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74172 (also indexed at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/347285247_High_Density_Planting_System_of_Cotton_in_India_Status_and_Breeding_Strategies). The snippet does not give yield or maturity figures for RS 2818.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. The input lists parentage as "Not specified", and no search result gave parentage, breeding-line codes or genome data.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- A Rajasthan Agricultural University (RAU) directorate page says RS 2818 is an American cotton variety developed by the AICRP on Cotton at the Agricultural Research Station, Sriganganagar, for the high-density planting system, and that it was released and notified. -- https://raubikaner.org/directorate-of-research/ . This matches the institution in the input, which names the Agricultural Research Station of S.K. Rajasthan Agriculture University. No individual breeder name was found for RS 2818. The M. V. Venugopalan (CICR, Nagpur) reference on the intechopen page is about a different topic and is not attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder contact was captured. The RAU directorate page (https://raubikaner.org/directorate-of-research/) is the only institutional source found, but I did not capture its contact details. I have not invented any email, phone or address.

PUBLICATIONS -- The intechopen chapter (https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74172) mentions RS 2818 in a variety table. Its authors and title line were not captured, so I cannot give a formatted citation. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or trial report specific to RS 2818 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed search returned only the same review chapter, with no seed source, dealer, NSC, SAU or KVK listing.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The input lists Rajasthan, Punjab and Haryana. I did not find these states confirmed in the captured text. The RAU page supports only the development and release of the variety.

Discrepancies to resolve:
- Release year: the input says 2021, but the intechopen table says 2020.
- Notification: the RAU page says it was released and notified, but the notification number and date were not captured.

Recommended next steps (with search access restored): check the CSC/AICRP-Cotton release notification for the official name, year and states; look up the Seednet entry for RS 2818 under COTTON (KAPAS); search the Sriganganagar ARS and RAU pages for the breeder's name and contact; and search KrishiKosh and AICRP-Cotton annual reports for trial data.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for RAHH 455 or Raichur Shakthi-455. The only related text is the Raichur centre's note that RAHH 455 was released for South Zone rainfed situations -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for either name. -- searched: https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html (no such data on page)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found for RAHH 455 or Raichur Shakthi-455 (maturity, yield, trials). The AICRP page lists duration and seed-cotton yield only for other entries (LHDP 1, LAHB Cotton-1, LHDP Cotton-5), which do not concern this variety -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The page says the centre derived its varieties and hybrids, including RAHH 455, by the pedigree method, but it gives no parentage -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
RAHH 455 is listed among three intra-hirsutum hybrids developed at the AICRP on Cotton centre, UAS Raichur (Karnataka). The page does not name a breeder for RAHH 455 specifically -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html
Name match: evidence refers to "RAHH 455" (code RAHH-455). No source used the name "Raichur Shakthi-455". The record's parentage ("Not specified") is unchanged.
Release date: the page gives release in 2015 and notification in 2016 (S.O. 3540(E)). The record's 2016-08-12 matches the notification year, not the 2015 release.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level contact on the AICRP on Cotton centre page (no breeder-specific contact found for RAHH 455): Dr. Jayaprakash Mohan Nidagundi, AICRP on Cotton, Main Agricultural Research Station, UAS Raichur, Karnataka, India, Pincode 584104; Mobile +91 9480653790; E-mail jaysun050@uasraichur.edu.in and jaysun050@rediffmail.com -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html
Dr. Shivanand Hanchinal is listed on the same page as Scientist (Agricultural Entomology). He is not linked to RAHH 455 and is not a breeder for it; his contact details are not recorded here.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record for RAHH 455 or Raichur Shakthi-455 appeared in the search. The research search returned only unrelated pages (a Raichur cotton note on Scribd, a US patent for a different cultivar DP 455 BG/RR, and a Chinese cotton paper).

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed search returned only market price pages for cotton seed in Karnataka, which do not name this variety. No Seednet, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was found. A dedicated Seednet query was not run because the four-search limit was reached.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Partly supported. The AICRP page says RAHH 455 was released for South Zone rainfed situations, without naming states. The state list (Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh) on that page belongs to SUJAY (SCS 793), a different variety, so it must not be attributed to RAHH 455 -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html
