search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: SAMIR BGII (cotton)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "SAMIR BGII". Seednet (seednet.gov.in) did not appear in any search result, so no Seednet-portal evidence was found. The only pages that name this variety use "Ankur Samir BG II" (retailer spelling). They describe a commercial hybrid from Ankur Seeds, not a CSC-notified variety. Parentage is not specified, and no notification or release-minute record turned up.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to SAMIR BGII. The one page that names it describes irrigated cultivation only, not stress tolerance. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg

DISEASE AND PEST
Retailer listing says the hybrid carries Bollgard II (Cry1Ac and Cry2Ab) protection against specified bollworms. No disease-resistance data was given. This is a seller claim, not a trial result. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Retailer listing gives a crop duration of about 160–170 days and says the seed is suited to irrigated cultivation with medium maturity. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg
Retailer listing reports an average yield of about 20.91 q/ha "under evaluated conditions" but names no trial, season or location. Treat as unverified. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg
No AICRP, ICAR or SAU trial entry for SAMIR BGII was found. The AICRP/CICR Bt cotton reports that appeared cover other entries. -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__05_29-04-2025.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Retailer listing gives the transgenic event as MON 15985 (Bollgard II). This is a transgene description, not QTL or marker work. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg
No QTL or marker study for SAMIR BGII was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: the retailer listing attributes the product to Ankur Seeds Pvt. Ltd. (brand "Ankur Seeds"). -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg
No breeder or lead scientist was named for SAMIR BGII. The Kaderbad Ravindranath and Rajagopalan Krishnamurthy Wikipedia pages came up, but they describe other varieties and hybrids, so they are excluded. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaderbad_Ravindranath ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajagopalan_Krishnamurthy

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder, email, phone or institute contact page for SAMIR BGII was found.
Company-level location only: an IndiaMART listing describes Ankur Seeds Pvt. Ltd. as a manufacturer based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. No email, phone or street address was given. -- https://www.indiamart.com/ankur-seeds-pvt-ltd-ahmedabad/

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Searches of journal and thesis-type results returned papers on other BG II lines (e.g., MRC-7201 BGII, heterosis studies on unnamed BG II hybrids) and none named SAMIR BGII. These are excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Retailer listing: "Ankur Samir BG II Hybrid Cotton Seeds", 475 g pack, sold online by kisanshop.in. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg
No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or official seed-portal listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Conflict: the retailer listing recommends Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg
The CSC record lists Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat. No search result supports that list for this variety. The two sets do not overlap, so the official CSC recommendation should be checked against the CSC release minutes before use.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches on drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance returned nothing that names SCS 1061.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
SCS 1061 appears as one of several genotypes in a comparison table in an ICAR-CICR cotton variety paper, but the column labels are not recoverable, so no yield or fibre figure can be attributed to it. -- https://icac.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/04SManikam-7C.pdf
Heterosis trial: SCS-1061 was one of the lines or testers crossed in a line × tester design. Among 40 hybrids, the crosses CPD-462 × SCS-1061, FLT-36 × SCS-1061 and CPD-462 × NNDC-30 were judged the best, and the authors recommended multi-location testing before any release as commercial hybrids. Seed cotton yield of the hybrids ranged from 656.67 to 1890.00 kg/ha. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-5577
Odisha cotton technology capacity-building notes contain a table row listing SCS 1061, with "H", 2019, UAS Raichur and a value of 14.79. The paper does not give SCS-1061's cluster membership in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393206376_Parental_Diversity_and_Earliness-Seed-Lint_Index_of_Twelve_Cotton_Gossypium_hirsutum_L_Genotypes
QTL/marker studies and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

Institution: the only location hint is "UAS Raichur" in the Odisha table row. The heterosis study mentions an ARS Dharwad farm for its field work. Neither source states who developed SCS 1061, so the "University of Agricultural Sciences" entry in the input record cannot be matched to a station with confidence. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353572829_Capacity_Building_Program_on_Cotton_Production_Technologies_State_Department_of_Agriculture_Odisha_under_Technology_Mission_on_Cotton_For_official_use_only_Lecture_Notes_of_Exposure_Visit_cum_Capacity

The Rallis Seeds page (https://www.rallis.com/innovation/seeds) describes the company's cotton and hybrid programmes but does not mention MC5444, so it is company context only. PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper names this variety. Retrieved items about BGII cotton in general (Springer and ResearchGate pink bollworm study, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s41938-021-00393-7; ResearchGate refugia-in-bag study, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382146455_Blending_procedure_is_crucial_for_BG-II_cotton_hybrids_to_adhere_to_the_prescribed_'Refugia_in_Bag'_standards) do not name this variety and are discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The only page naming this variety (SP 7670 BGII, the Seednet spelling) lists no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. It says only that the variety suits rainfed and irrigated conditions in the central and south zones (name matches the Seednet variant "SP 7670 BGII") -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Cotton/SP_7670_BGII

DISEASE AND PEST
Claimed good tolerance to foliar diseases and moderate tolerance to sucking pests (evidence refers to the Seednet variant "SP 7670 BGII"; the page does not name the release-minute name "SP 7670 BG II") -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Cotton/SP_7670_BGII
No independent or official pest/disease screening data found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity listed as 160-170 days; tall, open, erect plant type; medium to big bolls of 5.4-5.6 g; suited to closer spacing; more yield in the first two pickings (evidence refers to "SP 7670 BGII") -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Cotton/SP_7670_BGII
These are manufacturer-style product claims. No replicated, multi-location or AICRP trial data for this variety were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The name implies a Bollgard II (BG II) trait, but no page found confirms the transgenic event or any marker/QTL study for this variety. Search returned general BG II papers and other hybrids (for example, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s41938-023-00742-8 on Cry protein expression in BG-II cotton), which are not attributed to this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. No page names a breeder, developing scientist or station for SP 7670 BG II / SP 7670 BGII. The only page found (https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Cotton/SP_7670_BGII) is a third-party product listing and does not mention Bayer Bio Sciences Pvt. Ltd. The Bayer name appears only on an unrelated product (Surpass Firstclass BGII) at https://www.bighaat.com/products/surpass-firstclass-bgii, which was discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone or postal address was found. The Crystal Crop Protection page has only a generic "contact us" label with no details, and it is not an institute source.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Searches returned papers on BG II cotton in general or on other varieties and hybrids (for example, Deshmukh, Baig and Sharma on Bt BGII upland cotton hybrids at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389601710_Assessment_of_heterosis_and_combining_ability_for_fibre_yield_its_contributing_and_quality_traits_in_Bt_BGII_upland_cotton_Gossypium_hirsutum_L). None of these names SP 7670 BG II or SP 7670 BGII, so none is listed.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or official dealers. The only listing is the manufacturer-style page at https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Cotton/SP_7670_BGII, which has no price, stockist or availability information. Seednet (seednet.gov.in) and the CSC release minutes were not reached by any search.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Discrepancy. The supplied record lists Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. The Crystal Crop Protection page (evidence refers to the Seednet variant "SP 7670 BGII") gives a longer list: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Cotton/SP_7670_BGII
The official CSC or Seednet list was not found, so the discrepancy cannot be resolved from the evidence.

SEARCH NOTES
- Four searches were run. None returned Seednet, ICAR, SAU or KrishiKosh pages naming this variety.
- The release date (2020-11-09) and parentage ("Not specified") in the record could not be verified from any search result.
- Only one page (https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Cotton/SP_7670_BGII) names this variety, so every finding above depends on that single non-official source.

SRCH 207 BG II -- COTTON (KAPAS) DIGEST

Name check: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "SRCH 207 BG II", so one set of searches covered both. The company pages spell it "Srch-207 BG II Hybrid Cotton Seeds". All evidence below refers to that spelling. No Seednet (seednet.gov.in) record was returned by any search, so the release notification and variety code A05011056 are unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
No evidence found. The four searches returned no page giving drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for SRCH 207 BG II. Nearby results concerned other hybrids (Nath KSCH 207, Nuziveedu Mallika NCS 207), which were discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST:
No evidence found for SRCH 207 BG II specifically. The only pest-related text came from pages about other products. The Nath KSCH 207 Himalaya BG II page claims sucking-pest tolerance, and the Nuziveedu Mallika NCS 207 BG II page claims resistance to American bollworm and spotted bollworm. Both were discarded as different varieties. Sri Rama's own product page for SRCH 207 BG II gives no pest-resistance information.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- The company listing gives plant height of 150-160 cm and 45-50 days to 50% flowering for Srch-207 BG II -- https://www.sriramaseeds.co.in/srch-207-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds.htm
- Boll shape and size are described as oval and medium -- https://www.sriramaseeds.co.in/srch-207-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds.htm
- Fibre quality is listed as ginning 35-36%, staple length 25-27 mm, strength 21-24 g/tex and micronaire 4.0-4.9 -- https://www.sriramaseeds.co.in/srch-207-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds.htm (same figures on https://www.exportersindia.com/product-detail/srch-207-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds-9722545397.htm)
- Yield, maturity group (days to maturity) and recommended sowing or spacing: No evidence found for this variety. Sources only give fibre and plant data.
- Multi-location or AICRP trial results naming SRCH 207 BG II: No evidence found. The AICRP report summaries found (https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__05_29-04-2025.pdf) concern compact BG II hybrids generally and do not name this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL:
- Bt event: No evidence found that names SRCH 207 BG II. The GEAC approved-products list (http://www.geacindia.gov.in/resource-documents/approved-products/Final_commercially_approved.pdf) includes entries named "KSCH-207 Bt (BGII)" by Kohinoor Seed and "NCS 207 BGII" by Nuziveedu. Neither is SRCH 207, so both were discarded.
- Cry-gene segregation paper (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9859209/): discarded, because it studies other commercial Bt hybrids and does not name this variety.
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- Developing institution (company as listed): Sri Rama Agri Genetics (India) Private Limited, Siddipet, Telangana -- https://www.exportersindia.com/sri-rama-agri-genetics-india-private-limited/ . The company is listed as the source of Srch-207 BG II. This is a seed company, not a research institution. The name in the CSC record ("Sri Rama Agrigenetics (1) Pvt. Ltd.") differs from the company's own name; the company's site uses "(India) Private Limited".
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. No search returned a breeder name for this variety.
- Parentage: No evidence found. The record says "Not specified", and no search filled that gap.

CONTACT DETAILS:
- Company phone numbers as listed: +91-8897855001 and +91-9652688388 -- https://www.sriramaseeds.co.in/srch-207-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds.htm
- Location as listed: Siddipet, Telangana -- https://www.exportersindia.com/product-detail/srch-207-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds-9722545397.htm (the listing gives this as the address, with no street address)
- Official email, postal street address, breeder contact or institute contact page: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS:
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP or ICAR report, thesis or conference paper names SRCH 207 BG II. Papers on BG II cotton that surfaced (for example, Mahesh and Muralimohan, Genes 2022, DOI 10.3390/genes14010065, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9859209/) concern other hybrids and were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- Sold by Sri Rama Agri Genetics as a manufacturer, supplier and trader, with a minimum order of 1 ton and shipment described as "anywhere in India" -- https://www.sriramaseeds.co.in/srch-207-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds.htm
- Listed on a B2B marketplace with a 1 ton minimum order, Siddipet seller -- https://www.exportersindia.com/product-detail/srch-207-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds-9722545397.htm
- Also listed in the company's product range -- https://www.exportersindia.com/sri-rama-agri-genetics-india-private-limited/
- National Seeds Corporation, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or retail availability: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
No evidence found. The CSC release minutes were not located, so the Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat recommendation could not be checked. The company's own listing does not name recommended states. Results for Telangana in the listings reflect the company's location, not a recommendation.

RECORD NOTES FOR THE REFERENCE FILE:
- Release year 2020-11-09 and variety code A05011056 are not confirmed by any source found.
- Searches were limited to four queries, and no search reached Seednet, ICAR, KrishiKosh or a CSC document. Check the Seednet portal and CSC minutes directly before finalising.

The original variety record states that SVPR 6 is tolerant of drought and high temperature prevailing in the summer season, but this claim is not corroborated by any source in the digest and is not used to assign a level. disease_resistance.summary: Reported tolerance to bacterial leaf blight and Alternaria leaf spot, per the Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding (EJPB) paper. The digest does not give quantitative scores or the trial conditions behind these reports. The original record lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to jassid and whitefly (EJPB paper). The TNAU variety table independently confirms moderate jassid resistance. No pest resistance evidence beyond these was found; the original record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: Average seed cotton yield of 2285 kg/ha across trials, 11.5% above the zonal check Suraj (2049 kg/ha) and 30.9% above the local check SVPR 4 (1589 kg/ha). Potential yield of 3392 kg/ha at Raichur in 2013-14. The TNAU table lists 2232 kg/ha (category I). All figures come from research trials, not farmer-field data.
agronomic_details.stability: Trial data summarized across multiple environments in the EJPB paper, but the digest does not report a formal stability analysis (e.g., GxE statistics). Stability across environments cannot be confirmed from the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to February-March sowing in summer-irrigated tracts of Tamil Nadu (TNAU). The digest states it is notified for the southern zone, specifically winter-irrigated and summer-irrigated tracts of Tamil Nadu. The four-state list in the original record (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu) is NOT confirmed by any source found and is therefore not used here.

drought.details: The SVPR 4 release description reports tolerance to drought, and a related publication describes it as highly tolerant to drought in the summer irrigated season. This agrees with the CSC record of tolerance to drought and high summer temperature. No physiological mechanism, stress index or field measurement for SVPR 4 appears in the search results.

heat.details: The CSC record states tolerance to the high temperature of the summer season. It is recommended for February-March sowing in summer irrigated tracts. The search results give no independent quantitative heat-tolerance data, so the rating rests on the CSC record and the season of adaptation.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance data for SVPR 4 appear in the search results.

flood.details: No flood tolerance data for SVPR 4 appear in the search results.

disease_resistance.summary: No specific disease resistance is recorded for SVPR 4 (CSC: Not Specified). The search results mention disease-resistance donor screening in TNAU cotton proceedings, but nothing specific to this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: SVPR 4 is moderately resistant to leaf hopper (jassid), according to the release description. It can spin 40s counts, which is a fibre quality trait and not a pest trait.

agronomic_details.yield: No quantitative yield for SVPR 4 is given in the snippets. It is described as a high yielding, superior medium staple cotton. SVPR 6 (TSH 04/115) was reported superior to SVPR 4 and Suraj in seed cotton yield. In the TNAU cotton proceedings, SVPR 4 x SCS 1001 gave 2138 kg/ha in 2024 and 2546 kg/ha in 2022 and was compared against SVPR 5, SVPR 6 and SVPR 3 as checks.
agronomic_details.stability: No multi-environment stability analysis is available in the search results.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Summer irrigated tracts of Tamil Nadu, sown in February-March. The TNAU crop production guide lists it for districts including Madurai, Virudhunagar, Tirunelveli, Trichy and Salem. Medium staple, spins 40s counts.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: STEM IS SLIGHTLY PUBESCENT, PIGMENTED WITH PURPLE COLOUR WHEN EXPOSED TO SUNLIGHT, AS IN MCU5. BRACT IS PIGMENTED WITH PURPLE COLOUR WHEN EXPOSED TO SUNLIGHT
agronomic_details.field_trials: SVPR 4 was included in frontline demonstrations (FLD) with SVPR 5, SVPR 6 and CO 17. Abstracts also report comparisons with MCU 5, in which MCU 5 registered a higher span length (2.5%) than SVPR 4. SVPR 4 is used as a check in TNAU cotton trials.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The search for "UASR-COT-1 cotton variety" returned only unrelated cotton pages (US cultivars UA-48 and UA103, a Chinese genome paper, and generic seed-market pages), none naming UASR-COT-1 or BGDS-1063.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The same search returned no UASR-COT-1 pages. The hits were US cultivars and an insect-resistance patent for a different transgenic event.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. The research search returned Arkansas, Texas and other non-Indian trial reports, plus an unrelated UAV spraying study. None names UASR-COT-1.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No pedigree or marker study naming UASR-COT-1 appeared. Parentage is recorded as "Not specified", and no source fills that gap.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found for a breeder of UASR-COT-1. The pages below concern the developing institution and its cotton programme, not this variety.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: US 704 BG II (cotton)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "US 704 BG II", so one name was searched. The only retrieved page that names this variety is a seller listing (SEED AVAILABILITY). It does not confirm the Seednet/CSC record.

No evidence found. Searches for this variety returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. Results covered US 7067 BG II and other hybrids, which were discarded. -- https://www.bighaat.com/collections/best-quality-us-agri-cotton-seeds

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for US 704 BG II. Pest-related pages retrieved were about US 7067 BG II, which carries Cry1Ac + Cry2Ab for bollworm protection, and were discarded. Generic Bollgard II reviews in the results do not name this variety. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/us-agriseeds-7067-cotton-hybrid-seeds

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. No trial, yield or maturity data for US 704 BG II were retrieved. The AICRP BG II hybrid trial report names other hybrids (Rasi Max 003 BG II, ARH 2020 BG II) and was discarded. -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__05_29-04-2025.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage, pedigree or marker data for this variety were retrieved. The stated parentage ("Not specified") was not verified. -- https://www.cottongen.org (no variety-specific page retrieved)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

(the institution in the brief) does not appear on any retrieved page. The "US Agri" and "US Agriseeds" brands on seller pages were not linked to this institution. -- https://www.bighaat.com/collections/best-quality-us-agri-cotton-seeds

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address or contact page for the developer or institute was retrieved. -- (no URL)

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No journal article, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper naming US 704 BG II was retrieved. The GEAC approved Bt cotton list was returned, but the retrieved text shows "704" only as a list serial number, not as this variety. -- http://www.geacindia.gov.in/resource-documents/approved-products/Final_commercially_approved.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CNA 1003 (Roja), G. arboreum cotton, ICAR-CICR

Name note: The release minutes name is "Cotton" and the Seednet name is "cotton." I did not search the Seednet portal directly. My queries used "CICR NA 1003" and "CNA 1003," and the only variety-name match was "CNA 1003 (Roja)" in an institutional review. The evidence below refers to that CNA 1003 name, not to the generic "Cotton" entry. Four searches were run, and the results are generic or institute-level unless stated otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for CNA 1003 specifically. The AICRP on cotton programme says it screens cotton genotypes for resistance to major pests and diseases, and for salinity and drought tolerance, but this is not tied to the variety -- https://circot.icar.gov.in/all-india-coordinated-research-project-cotton-quality-research

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for CNA 1003 specifically. The 2024-25 AICRP annual report describes disease surveillance across 364 villages in 42 districts, not this variety -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. The 2024-25 AICRP report shows 10 non-Bt varieties notified that year, but CNA 1003 is not among the results shown -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for CNA 1003. Institute-level only: the CICR director's profile reports a genetic linkage map built from a wild species and fibre-quality gene mapping, not linked to this variety -- https://cicr.org.in/present/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- CNA 1003 (Roja) is listed among G. arboreum varieties from CICR -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/51140
- CNA1003 is among varieties that CICR's Crop Improvement Division maintains and multiplies, with single-plant selection over 2023-24 -- https://cicr.org.in/crop-improvement/
- Lead breeder or scientist name: not found in results.
- Developing institution: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research, Nagpur, established 1976 -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research (secondary source)
- Varietal release route: the Varietal Identification Committee and state release committees handle release, as described in -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/51140

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found.
- Institute-level: Director Dr. V. N. Waghmare (ICAR-CICR, Nagpur) -- https://cicr.org.in/present/
- Nagpur campus address: NH 44 (Nagpur Wardha Road), about 14 km from Nagpur Railway Station -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research
- Sirsa campus: NH9, Sirsa, Haryana -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research
- Official institute site domain: cicr.org.in (email and phone not found in results)

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found for a paper, thesis, or report specific to CNA 1003. I did not search KrishiKosh directly.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for NSC, state corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer sales of CNA 1003.
- CICR tracks breeder seed production of its varieties for 2015-2025, but the table values were not visible in the result -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ICAR-CICR-At-Glance-with-coverpages.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found confirming Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka or Tamil Nadu for CNA 1003. These states come from the input record only. Release year (2015-06-25) and parentage ("Not specified") are also unverified by search.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: UPC 621 (variety_name "UPC 621"; seednet_variety_name "UPC-621")

Name note: The CSC name is "UPC 621" and the Seednet name is "UPC-621". Seednet lists the crop as "COWPEA (FODDER)", not field pea. The evidence below concerns a Pantnagar cowpea line, so it is about a cowpea and not a field pea. Where a finding is for UPC 628 (a sister forage cowpea) rather than UPC 621, I say so.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No UPC 621-specific stress data found. The ICAR release notice that describes field resistance to yellow mosaic virus, leaf spot, anthracnose, root rot, aphid, flea beetle and root-knot nematode concerns UPC 628, not UPC 621 -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- The same ICAR notice says that UPC 628 was released in 2010 and is named in the notice as a forage cowpea from G.B. Pant University -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- A heat-stress study of fodder cowpea genotypes (Vellayani, Kerala) includes a genotype labelled "UPC 621" in the text, but the extracted snippet is fragmentary and gives no results for it -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/397217111_Genotypic_Variation_in_Fodder_Cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_L_Walp_for_Adaptability_to_Heat_Stress_An_Evaluation_of_Growth_Physio-Biochemical_Traits_and_Fodder_Quality

DISEASE AND PEST
- No UPC 621-specific disease or pest data found. The resistance profile quoted above (yellow mosaic virus, leaf spot, anthracnose, root rot, aphid, flea beetle, root-knot nematode) belongs to UPC 628 -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No UPC 621 yield or trial data found. The ICAR notice gives yield figures for UPC 628 only (350-425 q/ha green fodder and 50-55 q/ha dry matter at 85-90 days), so these must not be transferred to UPC 621 -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- A GBPUAT released-varieties list includes UPC 621 among cowpea and other crop entries, but the extracted layout is mixed with soybean and other crops, so its crop category is unclear -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/Released_crop_varieties.pdf
- A Pantnagar cowpea review lists varieties under trial at GBPUAT but does not name UPC 621 -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue5S/PartH/SP-8-5-12-110.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No genetics, parentage or QTL/marker study for UPC 621 found. Parentage is still unknown.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUAT), Pantnagar, is the developing institution for the UPC-series forage cowpea releases -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- No lead breeder name for UPC 621 was found in any result. The Pantnagar AICRIP centre page places the cowpea-relevant breeding base in the Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, GBPUAT -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf
- Bir Bahadur Singh (1944-2024) worked on cowpea at Pantnagar. The record cannot confirm that he developed UPC 621 -- https://cowpea.org/
- The GBPUAT newsletter names pulse breeders (R.K. Panwar, S.K. Verma, Anju Arora) in the context of urd, not cowpea or UPC 621 -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/26.07.2021_Issue-13_COA_Pantnagar_Newsletter.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder name, email, phone or postal address for UPC 621 was found.
- Institute-level only: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar, Uttarakhand. No email, phone or address was present in the extracted results. Institute site: https://www.gbpuat.ac.in
- ICAR Krishi Bhavan (source of the release notice) gave no contact details in the extracted text -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593

PUBLICATIONS
- Singh, Y.V.; Nautiyal, M.K.; Singh, B.B.; Pandey, Bhawana; Sharma, C.L. (2010). Performance of short duration cowpea varieties for enhanced pulses production in different seasons under Tarai conditions of Uttarakhand. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Name and crop check: The CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "UPC 628", so the evidence below applies to both. The Seednet crop is "COWPEA (FODDER)", i.e. forage cowpea (*Vigna unguiculata*), not field pea. The crop field in the input is wrong, and I searched on cowpea. The searches ran 4 times. Searches 2 and 4 returned no usable breeder, contact or seed-source evidence for UPC 628, so those headings say so.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Field resistance to cowpea yellow mosaic virus, leaf spot, anthracnose, collar/root rot, aphid, flea beetle and root-knot nematode is reported, and pods are tolerant to seed shattering -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence result specific to UPC 628 was found. UPC 628 appears only as one of 30 genotypes in a heat-stress study with no variety-specific result retrieved -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/397217111_Genotypic_Variation_in_Fodder_Cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_L_Walp_for_Adaptability_to_Heat_Stress_An_Evaluation_of_Growth_Physio-Biochemical_Traits_and_Fodder_Quality

DISEASE AND PEST
- Field resistance to the diseases and pests listed under STRESS TOLERANCE -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- No separate disease or pest trial data for UPC 628 was retrieved.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Notified yield potential is 350-425 q/ha green fodder and 50-55 q/ha dry matter at 85-90 days, with 6-8 q/ha seed yield -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- Fodder digestibility is reported at 65-70% and crude protein at 16-18%; pods are 15-17 cm -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- A review table lists UPC 628 under pedigree breeding with 340-360 q/ha -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/116-Enhancing%20Fodder%20Cowpea%20through%20Breeding%20and%20Omic%20Innovations%20A%20Review.pdf
- In a 2008 Raipur kharif trial, UPC-628 was one of six cowpea varieties tested under three phosphorus levels; the highest green fodder yield was UPC-626, not UPC-628 -- https://rjstonline.com/HTML_Papers/Research%20Journal%20of%20Science%20and%20Technology__PID__2009-1-3-2.html
- A 2017 IJCMAS trial with UPC 628 as entry V4 reports growth and seed-yield values in a table, and the text does not name UPC 628's own performance -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-10-2017/Anjum%20Ahmad,%20et%20al.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker or genomic study specific to UPC 628 was found. The review above records its breeding method as pedigree breeding -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/116-Enhancing%20Fodder%20Cowpea%20through%20Breeding%20and%20Omic%20Innovations%20A%20Review.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar, and released and notified by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Variety in Agricultural Crops at its meeting on 27-28 June 2010 in Chennai -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- Breeder name(s) and station not found in the retrieved evidence. The Pantnagar release list shows UPC 628 under field crops -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/Released_crop_varieties.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder name, email, phone or postal address for UPC 628 was found in the retrieved evidence.
- Institute-level page only: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar. The released-varieties list is at https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/Released_crop_varieties.pdf. No contact page URL was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Ahmad, A.; Tomar, G.S.; Taunk, S.K.; Verma, N. (2017). Evaluation of New Cultivars of Fodder Cowpea in Terms of Growth Attributes and Seed Yield as Influenced by Various Doses and Varieties. Int. J. Curr. Microbiol. App. Sci. 6(10): 937-944 -- https://doi.org/10.20546/ijcmas.2017.610.112
- Thakur, M.K. et al. (year not shown in retrieved text). Enhancing Fodder Cowpea through Breeding and Omic Innovations: A Review. Journal not confirmed in retrieved text -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/116-Enhancing%20Fodder%20Cowpea%20through%20Breeding%20and%20Omic%20Innovations%20A%20Review.pdf
- Authors not retrieved (year not shown). Effect of phosphorus levels on fodder and seed yields of cowpea varieties including UPC-628, IGKV Raipur, kharif 2008. Research Journal of Science and Technology -- https://rjstonline.com/HTML_Papers/Research%20Journal%20of%20Science%20and%20Technology__PID__2009-1-3-2.html
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report or DOI-indexed paper specific to UPC 628 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or private dealers. The one search for this returned only unrelated products.
- Dairy cooperatives are reported to lift breeder seed of UPC 628 from ICAR and agricultural institutes, but the retrieved text gives no supply details -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381409043_Role_of_dairy_cooperatives_in_fodder_seed_production_system

RECOMMENDED STATES
- ICAR notice: Uttarakhand, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Assam, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- Your input also lists Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir. Neither appears in the ICAR notice, so those two need verification against the CSC minutes.
- A separate DPD cowpea document lists UPC-628 for Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand -- http://dpd.gov.in/Cowpea.PDF

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bundel Lobia-4 / BUNDEL LOBIA-2 (IL-1177)

Name and crop caveat: The variety_name is garbled in the input ("Bundel Lobilya - 4"). I read it as Bundel Lobia-4. The Seednet name is BUNDEL LOBIA-2, and the Seednet crop is cowpea (lobia), while the input crop says "fieldpea". The evidence below relates to cowpea/lobia lines and does not confirm that IL-1177 is the same entry as either name.

Search budget: All 4 permitted web_search calls were used. A fifth call was blocked by the tool limit. I reviewed only the truncated snippets from the first batch and did not open full pages, so some findings may be incomplete.

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION: No evidence found for a CSC notification, release gazette, or Seednet record for IL-1177 or Lobia-4 with the 2015-06-25 date. The release year and region come only from the input.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No direct evidence found for Bundel Lobia-4 or BUNDEL LOBIA-2. A general cowpea overview says the crop is drought hardy with wide, droopy leaves that help hold soil moisture -- http://dpd.gov.in/Cowpea.PDF (this is general cowpea, not this variety).

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found for this variety. The TNAU research highlights describe a different fodder cowpea, CO 9, with moderate resistance to blast, RTD and brown spot -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/49th-Research-Highlights-2015-2017.pdf (CO 9 is not Bundel Lobia-4 or Lobia-2).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: A ResearchGate study reports that three cowpea fodder varieties, BL-1, BL-2 and BL-4, were developed by IGFRI and evaluated against a check. The snippet reports a high green fodder yield, but the figures were truncated -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325626254_Nutritive_value_of_cowpea_fodder_cultivars_and_their_effect_on_nutrients_intake_digestibility_and_nitrogen_balance_in_sheep (BL-4 may correspond to Bundel Lobia-4; this is not confirmed).

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The TNAU page notes that CO 9 derives from a CO 5 / Bundel Lobia 2 cross, which suggests Bundel Lobia 2 has been used as a parent -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/49th-Research-Highlights-2015-2017.pdf. No QTL or marker studies were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The institution is IGFRI, as stated in the input. The ResearchGate study credits IGFRI with developing BL-1, BL-2 and BL-4 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325626254_Nutritive_value_of_cowpea_fodder_cultivars_and_their_effect_on_nutrients_intake_digestibility_and_nitrogen_balance_in_sheep. No breeder name was found. The parentage "Selection from I.L. 978 (ACC. No. 978)" comes only from the input.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, scientist, email, phone, postal address or IGFRI contact page appeared in the search results. Verify the IGFRI contact page directly before use.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Authors not identified (year not identified). Nutritive value of cowpea fodder cultivars and their effect on nutrients intake, digestibility and nitrogen balance in sheep. ResearchGate entry, journal not identified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325626254_Nutritive_value_of_cowpea_fodder_cultivars_and_their_effect_on_nutrients_intake_digestibility_and_nitrogen_balance_in_sheep
- Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (2015-2017). 49th Research Council Meeting, Research Highlights. TNAU report -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/49th-Research-Highlights-2015-2017.pdf (cites Bundel Lobia 2 as a parent of CO 9; not a direct study of this variety).
- No KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR reports or journal papers found for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No official source found (no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or Seednet listing). A commercial listing for "Bundel Lobia" dried white cowpea seed appears at https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/white-cowpea-seed-2851737418091.html. This is a trader listing for a dried grain product, not evidence of certified seed of this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found beyond the input value "North Eastern region". Nothing in the search results confirms this.

I could not complete the research. The search tool hit its usage limit after the first batch of four queries, so the searches for breeder contacts, publications, and seed sources were not run. The digest below reflects only what those four queries returned.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searched "GC 7 (Banas Tejas) fieldpea variety"; no result described stress tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Same search as above; the only related snippet was from an ICAR report on a different rabi field pea line (moderate resistance to Alternaria blight and white rust), which does not identify GC 7 -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for GC 7 / GC 1501. The ICAR 2023-24 report snippet (maturity 130 days, seed yield 16.48 q/ha) is for an unidentified rabi field pea entry and cannot be attributed to this variety -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Not verified. The Pulses Research Station, S.D. Agricultural University is named in the input record. A search for the breeder returned a 17th Combined AGRESCO proceedings PDF from SDAU, but the snippet did not show a GC 7 or GC 1501 entry; the full document was not checked -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone, or address was retrieved. Official SDAU contact pages were not reached.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The search for research papers returned only unrelated cowpea work (an Ethiopian AMMI/GGE study), which does not concern this variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Gujarat Cowpea-6 (variety code GC 6; Seednet name GUJARAT COWPEA-2; crop listed as fieldpea in the record, but Seednet lists it under cowpea)

Searches run: 4 (variety and recommendation; breeder and institution; research papers; seed availability). No page names "Gujarat Cowpea-6" or "Gujarat Cowpea-2" as a variety. The only match is the code "GC-6" in a cowpea study, which I list as provisional. The field pea crop label has no supporting evidence at all; every crop-matched page is cowpea.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The drought and water-deficit screening paper names GC-6 among eight cowpea genotypes, but its drought results are not attributed to GC-6 specifically (provisional name/code match only) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/27797110_Screening_cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_L_Walp_varieties_by_inducing_water_deficit_and_RAPD_analyses

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Pages on cowpea golden mosaic disease in Gujarat and on other cowpea varieties name no GC 6 resistance data (-- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18516489/ is about a virus isolate, not this variety).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The Junagadh rainfed weed-management trial (2007) and the Bharuch nutrient trial (2022) name no GC 6 entry (-- https://zenodo.org/records/805353 ; -- https://journalijpss.com/index.php/IJPSS/article/download/4476/8842/6583). The Bharuch trial used GC-5, not GC-6.

GENETICS AND QTL -- Provisional only. A RAPD marker study reports a genetic similarity of 0.857 between Pusa Komal and GC-6 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/27797110_Screening_cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_L_Walp_varieties_by_inducing_water_deficit_and_RAPD_analyses . No QTL or marker study specific to GC-6 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a breeder of Gujarat Cowpea-6. The search returned breeder information for other cowpea and chickpea varieties (e.g., IIVR cowpea list, SDAU vegetable cowpea), which I have excluded. Parentage in the record says it was selected from local germplasm and tested as Chharodi-1; no page confirms this.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No variety-specific contact found. Institute-level only: S.D. Agricultural University Pulses Research Station, Sardarkrushinagar; contact on a seed-hub listing for a different variety (GAU 4): Dr. M. P. Patel, rspulses@sdau.edu.in, 9428137237 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/iiprseedportal/seed_availabilty.php . This is not linked to GC-6 by the page.

PUBLICATIONS -- Only the provisional RAPD paper. Authors (year) and journal are not shown in the retrieved record; I cannot complete the format. Title: "Screening cowpea [Vigna unguiculata (L.) Walp.] varieties by inducing water deficit and RAPD analyses" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/27797110_Screening_cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_L_Walp_varieties_by_inducing_water_deficit_and_RAPD_analyses . No KrishiKosh, AICRP, or ICAR report entry for GC 6 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No variety-specific evidence. The Gurabini (Gujarat State Seeds Corporation) cowpea summer table lists Gujarat-4 and Gujarat-5 but no Gujarat-6 entry in the retrieved text -- http://www.gurabini.com/cropDetails.aspx?id=26 . The corporation's seed-dealer network is described generally -- https://www.chinimandi.com/quality-and-certified-seeds-from-seed-corporation-driving-gujarats-agricultural-growth/ . Institution-level only: Gujarat State Seeds Corporation, Beej Bhavan, Sector 10-A, Gandhinagar 382010 -- https://nddb.coop/farmer/animal-nutrition/state-wise-list-of-seeds-producer-supplier . The ICAR-IIPR seed hub lists GAU 4 and GU-2 in Gujarat, not GC-6 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/iiprseedportal/seed_availabilty.php

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The DPD arid-legume table lists GC 4 and GC 5 for Gujarat, with no GC 6 row in the retrieved text -- https://dpd.gov.in/Varieties/ARID%20LEGUMES%20VARIETIES.pdf . The record's "Gujarat" entry is unverified.

Recommended next step: check the SDAU and Navsari/Junagadh cowpea release notifications, KrishiKosh, and the Seednet record directly, since none of the four searches returned an official release notification for this variety.

(3) 2026 Shivamogga trial (Kharif 2025) on growth retardant (cycocel) and NPK levels using cultivar KBC 9; an agronomy trial, not a release trial. (4) Hisar (CCSHAU) kharif 2017 evaluation: KBC 9 placed in the medium fodder and medium-to-low grain yield group.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: KBC-9 (cowpea)

Name note: The CSC release minutes name this variety "KBC-9" and the crop "fieldpea". The Seednet portal lists the crop as "COWPEA (LOBIA/ASPARAGUS BEAN/YARD LONG BEAN)". The evidence below concerns cowpea (Vigna unguiculata). None of the retrieved sources links KBC-9 to field pea (Pisum sativum). The field pea list I found (dpd.gov.in) does not show KBC-9. Searches were run under both names and the crop label mismatch should be checked against the CSC minutes. Parentage was not found in any source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No KBC-9-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data found in the retrieved text. No evidence found. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/varieties-hybrids-recommended-for-release-during-2019-20/ (other KBC/KC cowpea entries only)

DISEASE AND PEST
- A 2026 agronomy paper describes KBC 9 as erect, with purple flowers, grey pubescence, light-yellow seeds, an 80-85 day maturity, and resistance to pod borer. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2026/vol9issue9/PartH/9-9-56-884.pdf
- No KBC-9-specific data on yellow mosaic virus, rust, leaf spot, or bacterial leaf blight was found. The UAS 2019-20 release notice for KC-8 (KBC-11), a sister line, reports YMV, rust and leaf spot resistance. This does not apply to KBC-9. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/varieties-hybrids-recommended-for-release-during-2019-20/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- In AICRP/ICAR arid legume trials (2019-20), KBC 9 served as the check. Its mean yield across the listed centres was about 953 kg/ha (Ananthapuram, Bangalore, Pattambi, Coimbatore, Vamban, Madurai, Warangal, Pandharpur). The table's "yield advantage" column for KBC-12 versus checks is ambiguous; treat it cautiously. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12119430/
- KBC-9 was used as the best check in farm trials of KBC-12 in Zones 5 and 6 of Karnataka. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12119430/
- A 2026 Shivamogga trial used KBC 9 for growth-retardant (cycocel) and NPK studies. It is an agronomy trial, not a release trial. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2026/vol9issue9/PartH/9-9-56-884.pdf
- A Hisar (CCSHAU) kharif 2017 evaluation placed KBC 9 in the medium fodder, medium-to-low grain yield group. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343696597_Meteroglyph_Analysis_of_Cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_LWalp_Elite_Genotypes

GENETICS AND QTL
- No KBC-9-specific marker, QTL, or genetic-diversity study was found. KBC-9 appears as a standard in an UAS GKVK mini-core-set selection study, but that paper's SSR or trait-marker content was not retrieved. No evidence found. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/9-1.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The Mysore Journal of Agricultural Sciences text states that KBC-9 was developed at University of Agricultural Sciences, Bangalore (GKVK). The authors are from the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, AICRN on Potential Crops, and Plant Pathology at GKVK. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/9-1.pdf
- The breeder's name was not found. No evidence found. -- (no breeder-level source retrieved)
- The institution is the University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru (GKVK campus, Bengaluru). -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandhi_Krishi_Vigyana_Kendra

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder: No evidence found.
- Institute: University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru, GKVK campus, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560065, India. Website: www.uasbangalore.edu.in. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandhi_Krishi_Vigyana_Kendra (address and website). No official email or phone was found in the retrieved text.
- Seed (Crops) unit, GKVK: Scientific staff listed are Dr. K. Madhusudan (Special Officer, Seeds) and Dr. T.M. Ramanappa (Principal Scientist, Genetics and Plant Breeding). Their emails and phones were not in the retrieved text. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/seed-crops-gkvk-bengaluru/
- Quality Seed Production, GKVK: Dr. Krishna T V (Senior Scientist, Plant Breeding). Email and phone not in the retrieved text. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/quality-seed-production-gkvk-bengaluru/

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (n.d.). Mini core set selection of cowpea accessions for rabi, including KBC-9 as standard C7. Mysore Journal of Agricultural Sciences -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/9-1.pdf
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2026). Growth and yield of cowpea under fertilizer levels and cycocel, Kharif 2025, Shivamogga; cultivar KBC 9. International Journal of Research in Agronomy 9(9): 593-595 -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2026/vol9issue9/PartH/9-9-56-884.pdf
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2025). Marker-assisted introgression of bacterial leaf blight and cowpea mosaic virus resistance into cultivar C-152 (KBC-12 release; KBC-9 check). Molecular Breeding -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11032-025-01570-4 (DOI 10.1007/s11032-025-01570-4)
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2020). Meteroglyph analysis of cowpea (Vigna unguiculata L. Walp) elite genotypes, CCSHAU Hisar kharif 2017. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343696597_Meteroglyph_Analysis_of_Cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_LWalp_Elite_Genotypes
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP annual report specific to KBC-9 was found. No evidence found. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in (not retrieved)

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No KBC-9 seed source (NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, UAS sales, or dealer) was found. No evidence found.
- The GKVK Seed (Crops) unit's mandate covers breeder-seed production and supply, plus quality seed through university seed farms and farmer fields. This is an institutional mandate, not a KBC-9 availability listing. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/seed-crops-gkvk-bengaluru/
- UAS Bengaluru district-level recommendation PDFs list cowpea varieties including KBC-1, KBC-2, KM-9, KC-8 (KBC-11) and others, but KBC-9 was not seen in the retrieved excerpts. -- https://rawe2020.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/GKMS-E-12.05.2026-Kodagu-District.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The CSC/Seednet recommended states (Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, part of Odisha) were supplied in the input record only. No retrieved source confirmed them. -- (input record; not independently verified)
- Karnataka zones 5 and 6 were named as the target zones for the related release KBC-12, with KBC-9 as the check. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11032-025-01570-4

drought.details: The provided search results contain general information on drought-resistant plants, including mention of cowpea, and note that some yard long bean varieties experienced 100% mortality under combined drought and heat stress. However, no specific information regarding drought tolerance for the fieldpea variety MFC-08-14 was found.

heat.details: The search results indicate that some yard long bean varieties (MATTATHRIVENI, PARAMBUVATTAN) were found moderately tolerant to heat stress, while others showed 100% mortality under combined drought and heat stress. Cowpea does not tolerate frost. No specific information regarding heat tolerance for the fieldpea variety MFC-08-14 was found.

salinity.details: The search results mention that tolerant yard long bean varieties showed decreased electrolyte leakage under salt stress and that cowpea (lobia) can be highly salt tolerant and grown in saline soil. Dhaicha is noted as suitable for saline soil. No specific information regarding salinity tolerance for the fieldpea variety MFC-08-14 was found.

flood.details: A general statement indicates that a drought resistant plant (referring to yard long bean) cannot tolerate water logging. Dhaicha is noted as suitable for waterlogged soil. No specific information regarding flood tolerance for the fieldpea variety MFC-08-14 was found.

disease_resistance.summary: The provided search results mention studies on Fusarium wilt disease management and mosaic resistance in yard long bean. Cowpea mosaic virus is noted to be transmitted by aphids. General statements refer to developing disease resistance in crops and managing disease epidemics in pulses. No specific disease resistance information for the fieldpea variety MFC-08-14 was found.

pest_resistance.summary: The provided search results generally mention insect pest outbreaks in pulses and note that a wild species, Khasianum, is resistant to shoot and fruit borer. Cowpea mosaic virus is transmitted by aphids. No specific pest resistance information for the fieldpea variety MFC-08-14 was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MFC-09-1

Name and crop note: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both MFC-09-1, so the names match. The input crop is "fieldpea", but the seednet crop is cowpea, and every relevant source describes MFC-09-1 as a forage cowpea (Vigna unguiculata). No source describes it as field pea. All findings below refer to forage cowpea. Searches used: release/traits, breeder/institute, research papers, and seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance specific to MFC-09-1. The only stress-related text was general cowpea background, which I did not attribute to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for MFC-09-1. A DUS characterization paper on elite forage cowpea genotypes reports yellow mosaic virus in KBC-2, which is a parent, not MFC-09-1, so I discarded it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318593466_CHARACTERIZATION_OF_ELITE_FORAGE_COWPEA_GENOTYPES_FOR_VARIOUS_DUS_TRAITS

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Five-location South Zone trial: the trial compared MFC-09-1 with RR-3, BL-1, UPC-5286 and UPC-9202 ZC at five locations in the South Zone, in a randomized complete block design with three replications. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc
- Trial sites: Vellayani, Mandya, Hyderabad and Dharwad were named as test centres for MFC-09-1. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc
- Green forage yield: MFC-09-1 gave 246.9 q/ha in the South Zone, 14.2% above the zone comparison, and ranked first nationally with 1.4% superiority in GFY. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc
- Dry matter yield: 42.5 q/ha in the South Zone (19.4% above comparison), and 4.9% superiority nationally. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc
- A review table lists MFC-09-1 with a pedigree-breeding origin and a yield of 321.7 q/ha, with no trial conditions given; treat this figure as unverified. -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/116-Enhancing%20Fodder%20Cowpea%20through%20Breeding%20and%20Omic%20Innovations%20A%20Review.pdf
- Maturity/habit: a draft DUS test guideline for cowpea uses MFC-09-1 as reference material and places it in plant-habit and flowering classes. The table layout is ambiguous, so no days-to-maturity figure is stated here. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/DraftCowpeaDUSguideline11019.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for QTL, marker, or genomic studies on MFC-09-1. The only genetic information is the pedigree, KBC-2 x CoFC-8, from the trial paper. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Origin: the trial paper states that MFC-09-1 was developed at the Mandya centre by crossing KBC-2 with CoFC-8. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc
- Parent sources: a DUS paper lists CoFC-8 as coming from TNAU, Coimbatore, and KBC-2 as coming from UAS Bangalore. These are parent-line sources, not confirmed developers of MFC-09-1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318593466_CHARACTERIZATION_OF_ELITE_FORAGE_COWPEA_GENOTYPES_FOR_VARIOUS_DUS_TRAITS
- Breeder name: no evidence found. The input "University of Agricultural Sciences." is incomplete, and no source names the university for MFC-09-1.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute, email, phone, postal address, or contact page for MFC-09-1 appeared in the searches. The UAS Bangalore release page that appeared lists other varieties (for example MFC-09-3), so I did not use it. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/varieties-hybrids-recommended-for-release-during-2019-20/

PUBLICATIONS
- Thakur et al. (year not found). Enhancing Fodder Cowpea through Breeding and Omic Innovations: A Review. Plant Archives -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/116-Enhancing%20Fodder%20Cowpea%20through%20Breeding%20and%20Omic%20Innovations%20A%20Review.pdf
- Authors not shown in the indexed text (2015 conference paper, listed on a ResearchGate profile for Narasimhan Manasa; authorship not confirmed from the PDF). MFC-09-1: A new forage Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata (L.) Walp) variety for south zone of India. Conference paper, Nov 2015 -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc ; https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Narasimhan-Manasa
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report, or peer-reviewed journal paper on MFC-09-1 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Searches returned only unrelated seed retailers and Niger cowpea seed data. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing for MFC-09-1 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Source evidence: the trial paper recommends MFC-09-1 for farmers' fields in southern India, based on the South Zone results. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc
- The state list in the input record (Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry) is not confirmed by any search result. The release date of 2016-08-12 in the input record is also not confirmed; the earliest evidence found is the 2015 conference paper.
- Release notification: no CSC notification or seednet page was found for MFC-09-1 in these searches.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 12.00 to 15.00 Kg/Ha. Station document: 11 to 13 q/ha. DPD central list: 12 to 15 q/ha. Unit discrepancy: q/ha values are 100 times the CSC Kg/Ha values as written; the CSC unit should be checked against the notification.

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Station document: yield 11 to 13 q/ha; released for Western Maharashtra. (2) DPD central list: yield 12 to 15 q/ha; state release, Maharashtra; days to maturity not recorded. (3) AICRP South Zone, 9 trials at national level: mean yield advantage over checks of 11.09%, 16.31%, 38.66% and 32.32% in the cited comparisons; the trial years, locations and check varieties are not stated in the digest. No KrishiKosh or AICRP annual report record specific to Phule Sonali was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I'll run the searches first, then write the digest. The Seednet crop name is cowpea, while the brief says fieldpea, so I'll check both.PHULE SONALI: EVIDENCE DIGEST

CROP AND NAME CHECK
- Crop mismatch: the brief says fieldpea, but Seednet lists this variety under COWPEA (LOBIA/ASPARAGUS BEAN/YARD LONG BEAN). The evidence supports cowpea. The breeding station's cowpea release list includes Phule Sonali. Treat "fieldpea" in the brief as an error. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf ; https://dpd.gov.in/7%20to%2012%20Arid%20Legumes%20Varieties.pdf
- Name: the DPD list uses "PhuleSonali", which matches the Seednet name. The breeding-station document uses "Phule Sonali" with a space, which matches the CSC name. Both names refer to the same cowpea line.
- Release year conflicts: the station document gives 2020-2021, the DPD list gives 2023, and the Seednet record gives 2022-10-26. Record all three and do not pick one.
- Originating centre conflict: the DPD list names PDKV Akola as the originating centre. The station document names MPKV's Pandharpur station. The brief names MPKV POCRTC. I am recording the station document and the brief as primary, with the DPD entry noted as a conflict.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance data for Phule Sonali was found. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to YMV, Cercospora leaf spot, collar rot and leaf spot. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf
- Station document notes the group was moderately resistant to pests and diseases and gave higher market prices. This is a group-level claim, not specific to Phule Sonali. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield 11 to 13 q/ha, white shiny seed coat, released for Western Maharashtra. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf
- DPD central list gives 12 to 15 q/ha, state release, Maharashtra. Days to maturity not recorded for this line. -- https://dpd.gov.in/7%20to%2012%20Arid%20Legumes%20Varieties.pdf
- AICRP South Zone (9 trials, national level) mean yield advantage over checks: 11.09%, 16.31%, 38.66% and 32.32% in the cited comparisons. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf
- Growth habit: erect, non-viney, determinate-type, early, dwarf, bushy. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. Parentage is RC 101 x Phule Vithai. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf
- MPKV biotechnology centre describes QTL and marker work in general, not for this variety. No specific marker or QTL study was found. -- https://mpkv.ac.in/Uploads/Education/Molecular%20Biology%20and%20Biotechnology_20230731055300.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder name: no evidence found for Phule Sonali.
- Institution: Pulses and Oilseed Crop Research and Training Centre, Pandharpur, Solapur, MPKV. The station was founded in 1981 and works on cowpea, horsegram, mothbean and clusterbean. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf ; https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf
- The station is listed under MPKV research schemes as "Pulses & Oilseed Research Project & Training Centre, Pandharpur". -- https://mpkv.ac.in/Research/ResearchSchemNonPlan
- Caution: ICAR-IIPR lists Dr. A. K. Parihar as a field pea breeder. This is not evidence for Phule Sonali and should not be attributed to it. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/cimprovment/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder/scientist email, phone or personal contact: no evidence found.
- Institute address: MPKV, New Admin Building, Rahuri (now Ahilyanagar) appears on the MPKV site. The Pandharpur station is about 3 km from Pandharpur city. A postal code, phone or email for the station was not found. -- https://mpkv.ac.in/Research/ResearchSchemNonPlan ; https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf
- Mahabeej (Akola) head office: Mahabeej Bhavan, Krishi Nagar, Akola 444104. This is a seed corporation address, not a breeding contact. -- https://www.mahabeej.co.in/uploads/files/Seed-License.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report entry, thesis or KrishiKosh record specific to Phule Sonali was found.
- Station document, author not stated in the excerpt (the filename suggests "Thambe" but this is not confirmed): "Research at Glance on Cow pea at Agriculture Research Station (MPKV), Pandharpur". Year not stated. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf
- DPD Central varieties of Cowpea/Lobia (Government of India, Bhopal). Year not stated. -- https://dpd.gov.in/7%20to%2012%20Arid%20Legumes%20Varieties.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No seed listing for Phule Sonali was found at Mahabeej, MPKV or a dealer.
- Mahabeej (Maharashtra State Seeds Corporation) is a state seed corporation based in Akola. It supplies seed to private dealers and cooperatives. -- https://msscl.blogspot.com/
- Mahabeej Seed Testing Lab, Parbhani: Masoom Colony, Bank Colony, Parbhani 431401; phone 8669642736; toll-free 1800-233-8877; qclabparbhani@mahabeej.com. Testing lab only, not a sales point for this variety. -- https://www.mahabeej.co.in/mahabeej-seed-testing-lab-parbhani
- Seednet portal listing and availability: not checked, because the search results did not return the Seednet page.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Maharashtra. -- https://dpd.gov.in/7%20to%2012%20Arid%20Legumes%20Varieties.pdf
- Released for Western Maharashtra. A group statement also mentions South India, but this is not specific to Phule Sonali. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf

OPEN ITEMS
- Confirm the breeder name, release year and originating centre with the MPKV Pandharpur station or the CSC notification.
- Confirm the Seednet variety code A030317998 against the CSC notification.
- Search KrishiKosh and AICRP arid legumes annual reports for the Phule Sonali trial data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Chickpea-1 (CSC name) / Shalimar Cowpea-1 (Seednet name, code SKUA-C-23311)

Searches run: 4 of 4 allowed. Queries covered the variety and breeder/institution, the Seednet name, and seed availability. No search returned a page naming either "Shalimar Chickpea-1" or "Shalimar Cowpea-1" together with its crop, so every heading below is "No evidence found."

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searches returned chickpea and cowpea general pages, and a PMC paper on pod borer resistance that refers only to "Shalimar chickpea-02" (a different variety, so discarded).

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. A DPD Government of India arid legumes table lists a SKUAST-Kashmir cowpea released in 2023 with resistance to cowpea mosaic and yellow mosaic viruses, but it is named "Shalimar Cowpea-2 (SKUA-WCP-149)," not Cowpea-1 or SKUA-C-23311, so it was discarded. -- https://dpd.gov.in/7%20to%2012%20Arid%20Legumes%20Varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The AICRP chickpea 2021-22 report contains product profiles for other chickpea varieties only. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf (no Shalimar Chickpea-1 entry)

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The only Shalimar chickpea genetics paper returned concerns Shalimar chickpea-02 (pod borer QTLs), a different variety, so it was discarded. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. No page names a breeder or developing scientist for Shalimar Chickpea-1 or Shalimar Cowpea-1. The institution is SKUAST-Kashmir per the record, but no search result confirms this variety's development.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. The IIPR Pulses Seed Hub lists a SKUAST-Kashmir contact (Dryland Agriculture Research Station, Srinagar, P O Box-61, GPO Srinagar; M. Ashraf Bhatt; mashrafbhat@skuastkashmir.ac.in) for "Shalimar Cowpea 3," a different variety, so it was not attributed here. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/iiprseedportal/seed_availabilty.php

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, thesis, report or conference item names this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The same IIPR Seed Hub page lists SKUAST-Kashmir cowpea seed only for "Shalimar Cowpea 3" (0.00 q available), which is a different variety. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/iiprseedportal/seed_availabilty.php

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. The only J&K recommendation found is for Shalimar Cowpea-2 in the DPD table, which is a different variety.

Name discrepancy: the CSC record calls this a chickpea and the Seednet record calls it a cowpea. No source links the two names or the code SKUA-C-23311 to either crop, so the record cannot be confirmed from these searches. Checking the CSC minutes or the Seednet entry directly would be the next step.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I'll run the first three searches now, since they don't depend on each other.EVIDENCE DIGEST: TC-901

Name note: The CSC release record calls this "fieldpea" (variety_name TC-901). The Seednet portal lists it under COWPEA (LOBIA/ASPARAGUS BEAN/YARD LONG BEAN) with the same name, TC-901. Every usable source I found describes TC-901 as a cowpea. No source links TC-901 to field pea, so the field-pea crop label is unconfirmed. The findings below refer to the cowpea TC-901 unless marked otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as a cowpea mutant suited to summer cultivation, the first such variety in the country -- https://www.barc.gov.in/ebooks/9788196745349/paper02.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence trial data for TC-901 were found in the retrieved results -- none found (searched)

DISEASE AND PEST
- No disease or pest resistance data for TC-901 were found in the retrieved results -- none found (searched)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pictured in BARC's pulse-variety display alongside other Trombay pulse varieties, with a field-visit note at the Gamma field, BARC -- https://www.barc.gov.in/ebooks/9788196745349/paper02.pdf
- Maturity, yield and multi-location trial figures for TC-901 were not found -- none found (searched)
- Field pea trial and maturity figures in the search results (for example VL Matar and other field pea varieties) belong to other varieties and do not apply to TC-901 -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/12/Field%20Pea

GENETICS AND QTL
- Listed by BARC as a direct mutant, while other Trombay pulse varieties are mutant derivatives; the source names BARC's radiation-induced mutagenesis and recombination breeding for food legumes including cowpea, but does not state the mutagen used for TC-901 -- https://www.barc.gov.in/ebooks/9788196745349/paper02.pdf
- No parentage, QTL or marker data were found; the parentage field "Not specified" stands -- none found (searched)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by the Nuclear Agriculture and Biotechnology Division (NA&BTD), Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, Trombay, Mumbai; the BARC pulse table lists TC-901 as a 2018 cowpea release -- https://www.barc.gov.in/ebooks/9788196745349/paper02.pdf
- Individual lead breeder name for TC-901: not found in the retrieved results -- none found (searched)
- Division head listed on the BARC organisation chart: Dr. A. D. Ballal, Head of Division -- https://barc.gov.in/div/66_209.html

CONTACT DETAILS

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Bushy, determinate, photo-nonsensitive vegetable cowpea, reported as tolerant to cowpea golden mosaic virus (name: BIDHAN SADABAHAR BCCP-3) -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/vegetable-crops-achievements-planning-en
- Listed as tolerant to cowpea aphid-borne mosaic virus, with early maturity and determinate habit (name: Bidhan Sadabahar BCCP 3) -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety. The searches returned only other varieties (e.g., Bidhan Coix-1 forage, Bidhan Barbati entries), which were discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Cowpea golden mosaic virus tolerance (name: Bidhan Sadabahar / BCCP-3) -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/vegetable-crops-achievements-planning-en
- Cowpea aphid-borne mosaic virus tolerance (name: Bidhan Sadabahar BCCP 3). Note: this conflicts with the golden mosaic virus statement above; both are BCKV sources -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- No evidence found for insect-pest resistance specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Average pod yield about 11.32 t/ha; first pod picking about 45 days after sowing; plants determinate with green foliage (name: BIDHAN SADABAHAR BCCP-3) -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/vegetable-crops-achievements-planning-en
- Seed yield 10-12 t/ha; early maturity of 45 days (name: Bidhan Sadabahar BCCP 3) -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- AICRP on Vegetable Crops, Kalyani centre salient-findings table lists BCCP-3 at 120-170 q/ha in the cowpea row (name: BCCP-3) -- https://bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-vegetable-crops-en
- Spring-summer 2023 evaluation of 24 vegetable cowpea genotypes at Kalyani: Bidhan Sadabahar had 100-seed weight of 12.55 g and marketable pod yield per plant of 154.68 (g) in the table; it was grouped in a cluster with Kashi Kanchan and others (name: Bidhan Sadabahar) -- https://horizonepublishing.com/index.php/PST/article/download/9633/11934/72485
- Recommended for intensive cropping systems: no such statement found for this variety; the search only returned a statement for a different variety, which was discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Developed through advanced-generation selection from a cross between Bidhan Barbati-1 and Kashi Kanchan. This resolves the "Not specified" parentage in the record (name: BIDHAN SADABAHAR BCCP-3) -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/vegetable-crops-achievements-planning-en
- No QTL or marker study for this variety found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya (BCKV), Mohanpur, Nadia, West Bengal, under the AICRP on Vegetable Crops (name: BIDHAN SADABAHAR BCCP-3; SVRC notification S.O. 3220(E), 05.09.2019) -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- A BCKV faculty CV credits a scientist with developing and notifying Bidhan Sadabahar among nine vegetable varieties. The individual's name was not visible in the retrieved text, so no named breeder can be given -- https://www.aappbckv.org/govebodymemberdetails.php?id=13
- Release was by the State Variety Release Committee, West Bengal, in 2018/2019 (name: Bidhan Sadabahar), listed in BCKV's list of varieties released 2016-17 to 2020-21 -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/images/pdf/Varieties-developed_nw.pdf
- Release date: the record gives 2019-06-01. BCKV sources give 2019 as the year, and the crop-variety page gives the notification date as 05.09.2019. The record's exact month/day is not confirmed.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute address: Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya, Mohanpur, Nadia, West Bengal-741252; landmark Barajaguli on NH-34 -- https://wbjeeb.in/assets/ALPG/SU/BCKV.pdf
- Institute website: www.bckv.edu.in -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/
- No breeder name, personal email or phone number for this variety was found in the retrieved text. The BCKV contact information on the faculty CV page is not visible in the snippet -- https://www.aappbckv.org/govebodymemberdetails.php?id=13

PUBLICATIONS
- Sarkar, M.; Mandal, A. R.; Sengupta, S.; Sinha, G.; Baul, D.; Chakraborty, I.; Mandal, A. K.; Chattopadhyay, A. (year not shown in retrieved text). Multivariate study of 24 vegetable cowpea genotypes including Bidhan Sadabahar, Kalyani, spring-summer 2023. Plant Science Today (ISSN 2348-1900) -- https://horizonepublishing.com/index.php/PST/article/download/9633/11934/72485
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report, or DOI-indexed paper specific to this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The search returned only generic cowpea seed studies from other countries, which were discarded. No NSC, West Bengal seed corporation, KVK, BCKV seed sales or dealer listing was found, and no Seednet listing page was retrieved directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- West Bengal, 2019, sourced to seednet.gov.in via a DPD state-wise recommended pulses compilation. This compilation lists the variety under the fieldpea heading and again under the Lathyrus table -- https://dpd.gov.in/1.%20Final%20State-wise%20within%2010%20Yrs.%20Pulses%20(Compile).pdf
- Crop check: the record's crop is "fieldpea", but every BCKV source and the Seednet crop name (COWPEA (VEGETABLE)) identify BCCP-3 as a vegetable cowpea (Vigna unguiculata). The DPD fieldpea and Lathyrus entries look like misfiling. The record's crop field should be corrected to vegetable cowpea after verification on seednet.gov.in -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en

Name note: CSC release-minute name "Bidhan Sadabahar" and Seednet name "BIDHAN SADABAHAR BCCP-3" refer to the same variety in all sources found. The 2003 "SADABAHAR" entry in a Bihar notified-variety list is a different variety and was discarded.
