search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Jagrati (HI 1653), wheat

Name note: variety_name "Pusa Jagrati" and variety code "HI 1653" are the names used in the wheat sources. The seednet_variety_name "PUSA BARSATI" and seednet_crop_name "COWPEA (VEGETABLE)" do not match this wheat variety. Under SEED AVAILABILITY I explain what the Pusa Barsati evidence refers to. No Seednet page for HI 1653 was retrieved. Searches run: 4 (the maximum).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Released for timely-sown, restricted-irrigated conditions of the NWPZ; immune to blast; highly resistant to stripe and leaf rust; average yield 51.1 q/ha -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- Resistant to wheat blast and leaf rust; high sedimentation value 69.3 (potential yield per the source column) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- Abiotic-stress tolerance (heat, drought, salinity, flood) is not specifically documented for HI 1653 in any retrieved source. No evidence found for flood, submergence, drought, heat or salinity specifics.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Immune to blast; highly resistant to stripe and leaf rusts -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- Resistant to wheat blast and leaf rust; good resistance to wheat blast and Karnal bunt, with grain and end-product quality noted -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- Insect pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration 145-150 days, suited to bread, biscuit and chapati uses, sedimentation value 57.7 ml; developed for NW plains -- https://krishijagran.com/news/icar-iari-develops-6-new-high-yielding-disease-resistant-wheat-varieties/
- Average yield 62.5 q/ha, plant height 101 cm, timely-sown sowing time, potential yield 69.3 q/ha; chapati quality 7.3, biscuit spread factor 8.4 -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- Note: the ZTM page's 62.5 q/ha average conflicts with the 51.1 q/ha average in the IARI 2023 annual report and the 2022 newsletter. Treat as unresolved.
- Multi-location trial data for HI 1653 (AICRP-type tables): No evidence found in the retrieved text.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage as shown in the IIWBR compendium appears to read "Pusa NADI/COPIO//NA" (the extracted text is garbled) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Your input states parentage as "A SELECTION FROM PHILIPPINE VAREITY, ADAPTED TO LONG DAY CONDITIONS". This does not match the compendium text; verify against the official notification.
- QTL or marker studies specific to HI 1653: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Indore; notified in March 2023 per the principal scientist and head KC Sharma -- https://krishijagran.com/news/icar-iari-develops-6-new-high-yielding-disease-resistant-wheat-varieties/
- Listed as an ICAR-IARI RS Indore release in the 2022 newsletter -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- Lead breeder name for HI 1653 specifically: No evidence found. Station-level staff only (see CONTACT DETAILS).
- Release year: user input says 2022-10-26; Krishi Jagran says notified March 2023. Unresolved; check the CSC minutes.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. K.C. Sharma, Head (Acting), IARI Regional Station Indore (Madhya Pradesh) -- phone 0731-2927921; email head_indore[at]iari[dot]res[dot]in; alternate email kc_64sharma[at]yahoo[dot]com -- https://iari.res.in/index.php?Itemid=735&id=301&option=com_content&view=article
- Postal address of Indore station: No evidence found in retrieved text.
- ZTM & BPD Unit (IARI headquarters, which holds the variety information page): ICAR-IARI, Pusa Campus, New Delhi-110012 -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- Generic Pusa Krishi contact: connect@pusakrishi.in; phone +91-8750281830 -- https://pusakrishi.in/contact-us/ (general portal, not verified as the breeder's line)

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated (2023). Annual Report 2023, ICAR-IARI. Annual Report, pp. covering HI 1653 (Pusa Jagrati) entry -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- Authors not stated (2022). Wheat-Barley Newsletter V.162, IIWBR (variety table row for Pusa Jagrati). Newsletter -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- Authors not stated (2024). Compendium of Wheat Varieties Notified in India During 2018-2023, RB-51, IIWBR. Report -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Peer-reviewed papers, theses (KrishiKosh) and DOIs specific to HI 1653: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Wheat seed sources (NSC, state corporation, KVK, SAU, dealers) for HI 1653: No evidence found.
- Seednet "PUSA BARSATI" entry: the retrieved sources describe Pusa Barsati as a cowpea variety selected from a Philippines collection, not a wheat variety -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/agricultural-and-biological-sciences/pusa . The Seednet record appears to be mis-mapped and should not be used as seed evidence for wheat.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Recommended for NWPZ, with the Indore station's recommendation summarised as northwest plain zones of the country -- https://krishijagran.com/news/icar-iari-develops-6-new-high-yielding-disease-resistant-wheat-varieties/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Basant (HD 2985), wheat

Name note: "variety_name" is Pusa Basant (HD 2985). The Seednet name "PUSA BARSATI" (listed under COWPEA (VEGETABLE)) did not appear in any search result, and no search targeted seednet.gov.in directly. Every finding below refers to the wheat variety Pusa Basant / HD 2985, not to any Seednet entry. Release-year evidence conflicts with the input (2010-10-10); see the notes under RECOMMENDED STATES.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Ambiguous: the IARI technology booklet says HD 2985 "tolerant to high temperature at seedling as well as at maturity stages," but the text block is not clearly tied to this variety rather than a neighbouring entry -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
- Lodging (not a named stress tolerance): in a maize-system conservation agriculture trial sown 16 Nov 2014 with a storm on 8 Mar 2015, HD 2985 showed the highest lodging of the varieties tested, against HD 2967 with the lowest -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311970190_SLOW_RELEASE_NITROGEN_IN_CONSERVATION_AGRICULTURE_FOR_ENHANCING_CROP_HEALTH_YIELD_AND_SOIL_PROPERTIES_IN_INTENSIFIED_MAIZE_SYSTEMS (same data also at https://isa-india.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Extended-Summaries-book-Vol.-3.pdf)
- No drought, heat-field, salinity, flood or submergence evaluation for HD 2985 was found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to brown rust per the late-sown block; the ICAR/IARI page layout does not clearly tie the yellow/brown rust resistance line to HD 2985 -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- Ambiguous: a "moderate resistance to leaf blast and brown spot" line appears in the IARI booklet, probably for a different entry -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
- No pest data found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Late-sown irrigated (recommended per the ICAR 2011-12 report): listed under the North-eastern plains zone -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- Maturity of 105-110 days and average yield of 3.5-4.0 t/ha for the late-sown condition, from the IARI page (layout ambiguous) -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- Conflicting yield/maturity figures in the IARI booklet: 2.0 t/ha average yield, 140-145 days, and 115-120 days; these lines are not clearly tied to HD 2985 -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
- Production condition given as timely-sown rainfed in the IARI booklet, versus late-sown irrigated in the ICAR report; treat as unresolved.
- Grain yield in the maize-system trial ranged 3.04-5.72 t/ha across varieties (individual HD 2985 value not extracted) -- https://isa-india.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Extended-Summaries-book-Vol.-3.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker or genetic-stock study for HD 2985 was found. The only genetic record is the IP/registration entry (REG/2011/255) -- http://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/Wings/files/basic-html/page33.html
- Parentage "a selection from Philippine variety, adapted to long-day conditions" from the input could not be verified by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Registration table lists "Dr. G. P. Singh" as the developer of Hd 2985 (Pusa Wheat Basant), registered 6 Jan 2011 under ICAR IP ownership; the institution cell is garbled in the extract -- http://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/Wings/files/basic-html/page33.html
- Wheat research and release coordination sits with ICAR-IIWBR, Karnal (formerly Directorate of Wheat Research) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/about/
- The AICRP compendium lists HD 2985 (Pusa Basant) among varieties notified, without a separate breeder name in the extract -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. G. P. Singh (breeder named in the registration table; no role, email, phone or address found) -- http://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/Wings/files/basic-html/page33.html
- ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research, Karnal-132001, Haryana (address as printed on the AICRP compendium header) -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf
- Institute website for the AICRP wheat and barley project: https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in
- Institute "About" page: https://iiwbr.org.in/about/
- No email or phone number for the institute or breeder was found in any result.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis or KrishiKosh record specific to HD 2985 was found. The results below are general, and the nearest items are:
- Authors not extracted (year not extracted). Slow release nitrogen in conservation agriculture for enhancing crop health, yield and soil properties in intensified maize systems. Field trial including HD 2985 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311970190_SLOW_RELEASE_NITROGEN_IN_CONSERVATION_AGRICULTURE_FOR_ENHANCING_CROP_HEALTH_YIELD_AND_SOIL_PROPERTIES_IN_INTENSIFIED_MAIZE_SYSTEMS
- Authors not extracted (year not extracted). Fourth International Agronomy Congress extended summaries, Vol. 3. Contains the same HD 2985 trial data -- https://isa-india.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Extended-Summaries-book-Vol.-3.pdf
- Indian Council of Agricultural Research (2011-12). Crop Improvement chapter, Annual Report. Notes HD 2985 in the North-eastern plains zone -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (2024). Compendium of wheat varieties notified in India during 2018-2023 (Bulletin RB-51). Does not cover HD 2985 specifically -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No seed source for Pusa Basant / HD 2985 was found.
- The PUSA seed portal (pusabeej.iari.res.in) is cited for six IARI wheat varieties, but HD 2985 is not confirmed among them -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/use-these-6-new-varieties-of-pusa-know-how-to-order-seeds-4084
- No National Seeds Corporation, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Eastern UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, Orissa, Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam and plains of NE states -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/ (also https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf)
- North-eastern plains zone, late-sown irrigated -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- Bihar state notified-variety list: Pusa Basant (HD 2985), notification date 07/02/2011, S.O. 632(E) -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Release year conflict: the IARI booklet gives 2006 (CVRC); the Bihar list gives notification 2011; the ICAR registration table gives 2011. The input value of 2010-10-10 was not found in any result.
- The input field "recommended_states_raw: Not specified" is contradicted by the sources above.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Ujjawal (IPCK 2004-29), Chickpea

Search limit note: the tool hit its use limit partway through. My first batch of three searches returned output I could not read, and a retry failed on the limit. Only one search returned readable results (query: "Ujjawal chickpea IPCK 2004-29"). The findings below come from that single search, so most headings have no evidence. Name matching: the IIPR listing refers to "IPCK 2004-29 (Ujjawal)", so it matches both the variety_name and seednet_variety_name. The CSC release-minutes name "Ujjawal" and the Seednet name "Ujjawal (IPCK 2004-29)" were not checked separately on Seednet.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Moderately resistant to fusarium wilt is listed for IPCK 2004-29 (Ujjawal) on the IIPR varieties page -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity.html

DISEASE AND PEST -- Moderate resistance to Fusarium wilt (IPCK 2004-29 / Ujjawal) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity.html. No other disease, pest or nematode evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The IIPR page lists a figure of "20-22" next to the variety's entry, with the zone code "CZ". The column heading is not visible in the retrieved text, so I cannot say whether this is yield, maturity or another trait. No yield, maturity or multi-location trial data found -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity.html

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. The parentage string supplied in the brief was not confirmed by any retrieved page. The "IPCK" prefix in the code is consistent with the IIPR Kanpur chickpea naming pattern, but I have not verified it.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SEARCH NOTE: The evidence shows that PRG 176 "Ujwala" is a pigeonpea (redgram) variety, not chickpea. The Seednet "Ujjwala" listing under cowpea (vegetable) found no matching evidence. Four searches were run (variety/release, breeder/institution, research, and a seed-related query). No search was run specifically for seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The four searches returned no stress-tolerance data for Ujwala or PRG 176. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data for Ujwala or PRG 176 appeared in the results. The only chickpea disease hits concerned other varieties or general pathology. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A cluster front-line demonstration in Mahbubnagar district, Telangana, used PRG 176 (Ujwala) as a redgram variety, with 50 demonstrations under cluster management. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286613635_Pigeonpea_Cajanus_cajan_research_in_India_-_An_overview
- The same source gives PRG 176 a yield potential of 20 q/ha on light soils, with a demonstration-field average of 15.4 q/ha. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286613635_Pigeonpea_Cajanus_cajan_research_in_India_-_An_overview

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage, marker, or QTL data for Ujwala or PRG 176 was found. The "Parentage: Not specified" field was not contradicted by any source. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The release table lists "Ujwala (PRG 176)", released in 2015 through the SVRC, with the station given as the Associate Director of Research, RARS, Palem, Nagarkurnool district. This is a redgram entry, and its release year (2015) differs from the year in the CSC record (2016). -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/
- The Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU) is the developing institution. The university was separated from ANGRAU in 2014 and is headquartered at Rajendranagar, Hyderabad. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professor_Jayashankar_Telangana_State_Agricultural_University
- No lead breeder or scientist name is linked to Ujwala or PRG 176. The "Prof. Jaysankar" entry in the input record is an institution-level attribution only. Named individuals on the university page are not linked to this variety. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. Institute page: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, Telangana, website www.pjtsau.edu.in. Email and phone not found in the results. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professor_Jayashankar_Telangana_State_Agricultural_University
- Institute research page: https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/ (no direct contact details were captured from it).

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated (year not stated). Pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan) research in India: An overview. Book chapter/report, ResearchGate listing -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286613635_Pigeonpea_Cajanus_cajan_research_in_India_-_An_overview
- No chickpea-specific publication, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis for Ujwala was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No seed-sale listing for Ujwala or PRG 176 appeared. The Seednet cowpea results listed other cowpea names (for example Gold-302, 309 and Surabhi) and did not mention Ujjwala. -- https://seednet.gov.in/material/Seed_Producers_Marketers.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Telangana: the release is recorded under the SVRC and the demonstrations were in Mahbubnagar, Telangana. Official notification scope was not confirmed beyond this. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: ICAR-Central Plantation Crops Research Institute, Kasaragod, Kerala
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: In laterite soils application of 100 g N, 40 g P2O5 and 140 g K2O is recommended as a general dose of fertilizer every year. In addition, application of 12 kg each of green leaf and compost per palm is also recommended.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
1.	Variety is free from major diseases and effective control measures ar available against common seasonal diseases like fruit rot and bud rot. 
2.	 Fruit rot can be managed by following phytosanitary measures, proper drainage in the gardens especially those which are in low lying and water logged conditions and spraying 1 % Bordeaux mixture to the bunck at least three times at an interval of 40 to 45 days.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests:
1.	No major pest attacks observed under field conditions. Minor pests like spindle bug and mites observed occasionally which can be controlled effectively. If infestation of spindle bug is noticed on of the following management strategies may be followed, placement of Thiamethoxam 25 WG of (2 g) in perforated poly-sachets in the inner most two leaf axils of areca palms during April-May or spraying with Thiamethoxam 25 WG (0.25 g per litre water) in and around the spindle and inner shorl of leaves, 
2.	if infestation continues, second spray can be given after 45 days interval. For managing mites, cut and remove the dried leaves due to mite attack, conserve predatory mites which will check the population of phytophagous mites and application of neem oil emulsion (5 ml/litre water) two-times at 15 days intervals.
seednet_fields.Average Yield (Kg/Ha): This variety gives an average yield of 3.96 kg dry dernel/palm/year or 3.26 kg dry tender processed nuts/palm/year. Kg/Ha

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CO (BN) 5 (variety_name) / CO (BN) 5 (TNCN 074) (seednet_variety_name), Napier grass (Bajra Napier hybrid)

Search status: Four web_search calls were made (three topic queries plus one seed-availability query). A fifth call, made to re-read the full text of those results, was blocked by the tool's usage limit, so I could only inspect the short snippets from the first batch. The searches returned almost nothing that names this variety, so most headings below are "No evidence found". The record cannot be treated as verified from search results.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The searches returned a commercial LinkedIn article titled "Cultivating Hybrid Cumbu Napier Grass CO(BN)5 for Camel and Cattle Feed", which names CO (BN) 5 and mentions its water requirements. Its snippet gave no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. -- https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/cultivating-hybrid-cumbu-napier-grass-cobn5-camel-rivashaa-agrotech (commercial source, not an official record; not used for stress claims)

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The same LinkedIn article is a commercial cultivation guide and is not a trial report. The ResearchGate paper on CO (CN) 4 (2023 kharif/rabi trials) was discarded because it concerns a different variety.

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage only, from the supplied record and not confirmed by search: fodder bajra IP 20594 x Napier grass FD 437. Breeding method, breeding-line code (TNCN 074 is the Seednet code only) and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Developing institution per the supplied record: Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore. No breeder name was found in any search result. No evidence found for a named lead breeder.

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder contact found. Institute-level address from the supplied record only (not verified by search): Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore-641 003. No official email, phone or institute contact-page URL was found.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The ResearchGate result (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374536154_A_High_Yielding_Cumbu_Napier_Hybrid_Grass_CO_CN_4) is about CO (CN) 4 and was excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No official source found (no Seednet, TNAU, KVK or NSC listing). One Amazon.in listing titled "N.G.M. AGROCARE CO 5 (Bajra Napier/pennisetum perpureum)" offers slips under the name "CO 5". It does not name CO (BN) 5 and comes from a private seller, so it was excluded as a similarly named product. -- https://www.amazon.in (listing for N.G.M. Agrocare CO 5)

RECOMMENDED STATES: Per the supplied record only, not confirmed by search: A AND N ISLANDS (Andaman and Nicobar Islands). Release year 2014 is also from the supplied record. No notification or CSC minute was found in search results.

Next steps: verify the release notification and recommended states on the ICAR/CSC or Seednet portal, find the breeder names and TNAU contact page at tnau.ac.in, and search KrishiKosh and TNAU fodder research publications using the names CO (BN) 5 and TNCN 074.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Timely sown, irrigated conditions
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: BH 885 is tolerant to lodging; resistant to shattering; responsive to recommended doses of fertilizers and irrigations. Suitable for timely sown (10th -25th November) with a seed rate of 37.5 kg/acre.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Plant height : 90 cm, Distinguishing morphological character : The variety has medium height, erect spikes, high biomass and more grains per spike, Growth habit : Erect, Anthocyanin pigmentation, Coleoptile : Absent, Leaf sheath : Green, Auricle (at flag leaf stage) : Absent, Foliage colour (boot stage) : Dark green, Leaf width (boot stage) : Medium, Average day to heading : 84 days,  Average days to maturity : 129 days, Waxiness (at ear emeragence), Flag leaf : Non waxy, Leaf sheath : Waxy, Ear : Waxy, Peduncle : Waxy, Ear colour at maturity : Yellow, Ear shape : Parallel, Ear density : Intermediate, Six rowed / two rowed : Two rowed, Awns length : Intermediate, Awn colour (at flowering and maturity) : Green & yellow, Glume pubescence : Absent, Grain, Hulled/hull-less : Hulled, Colour : Whitish yellow, Texture : Fine, Crease width : Intermediate, Shape : Oval, 1000-grain weight (g) : 50.0
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: BH885 Performed better under salinity alkalinity stress conditions. The variety also showed minimum reduction in grain yield under terminal heat stress conditions.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistance to yellow rust, brown rusts, leaf blight, stripe diseases and powdery mildew.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Average score against aphid attack under natural conditions. Tolerant to aphids and susceptible to CCN.

seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: BH 946 gave compatible yield performance to check NDB 1173 in salinity alkali trials. The variety also showed minimum reduction in grain yield under terminal heat stress conditions.

drought.details: No evidence found in searched sources. The searches returned no pages that name BH 946 for drought tolerance.

heat.details: No evidence found in searched sources for heat tolerance. The CSC release brief states that BH 946 showed minimum reduction in grain yield under terminal heat stress conditions; this statement is not corroborated by any retrieved page.

salinity.details: A field screen of barley genotypes using stress-susceptibility indices on several traits rated BH 946 as salt tolerant, although its ranking was not the top one. A saline-irrigation study under nitrogen levels reported its early growth-indices response (crop growth rate, leaf-area duration) relative to 2-row varieties, with no separate tolerance rating given. A malt-quality trial under saline irrigation recorded BH 946 with lower hectolitre weight than DWRB 101 and BH 885. The CSC release brief states that BH 946 gave compatible yield performance to the check NDB 1173 in salinity-alkali trials.

flood.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Rust, smut, leaf blotch and other disease reactions: No evidence found in searched sources. The CSC release brief (not corroborated by the searches) states excellent degree of resistance to yellow rust and leaf rusts, leaf blight, covered smut and powdery mildew.

pest_resistance.summary: Cereal cyst nematode (Heterodera avenae), Ludhiana populations: rated moderately resistant in a CCS HAU nematology study; the authors suggested it as a parent for CCN-resistance breeding. Aphid: the CSC release brief states at par reaction to checks against aphid attack; not corroborated by the searches.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC release brief: 52.0 q/ha. ICAR-IIWBR pocket guide yield table (irrigated, timely sown): 51.96 q/ha. Dual-purpose trial at Hisar: grain yield 5.25 t/ha and straw yield 7.62 t/ha. Non-official Hindi news article: 20-22 quintals per acre (not an official source).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the trial results listed under field_trials. The nitrogen-level trial and the nitrogen-by-variety trial are the only multi-entry comparisons retrieved.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Timely sown irrigated conditions in Punjab, Haryana, Western Uttar Pradesh (excluding Jhansi division), Delhi, Rajasthan (excluding Kota and Udaipur divisions), Uttarakhand, and Jammu & Kathua districts of J&K (CSC release brief). The digest's ICAR-IIWBR source classes BH 946 as a feed type; the Hisar trial was dual-purpose (fodder plus grain).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Digest identifies BH 946 as a 6-row variety (malt-quality trial under saline irrigation). Tolerant to lodging and resistant to shattering (CSC release brief). Other morphological characteristics: Unknown. Plant height: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Dual-purpose (fodder plus grain) trial at Hisar: BH 946 gave the highest effective tillers (416/m2), test weight (45.51 g), grain yield (5.25 t/ha) and straw yield (7.62 t/ha) among the four varieties tested. (2) Nitrogen-by-variety trial: BH 946 judged most suitable for grains per spike and yield among BH 946, BH 393, BH 885 and Karan 16. (3) Nitrogen-level trial under irrigated timely sowing: BH 946 gave the highest average grain yield among the varieties tested. (4) Malt-quality trial under saline irrigation: BH 946 is 6-row with higher protein than the 2-row entries and lower hectolitre weight than DWRB 101 and BH 885. (5) Field screen of barley genotypes for salinity tolerance: BH 946 rated salt tolerant, ranking not the top one. (6) Saline-irrigation nitrogen study: early growth indices (crop growth rate, leaf-area duration) reported relative to 2-row varieties; no tolerance rating given. (7) ICAR-IIWBR yield table: 51.96 q/ha under irrigated timely sown conditions. (8) Plant growth regulator trial (Rabi 2018-19, Hisar): BH 946 included among barley varieties; numeric result not stated in the digest. (9) Storage containers and seed quality study (CCS HAU, Hisar): BH 946 result not stated in the digest. (10) Nutrient management study comparing BH 946 with DWRB 160: numeric results not stated in the digest. Seed rate: 35-37.5 kg/acre for timely sown crop (CSC release brief); 100 kg/ha cited in an IIWBR-linked paper.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: BH 946 (Barley, Hordeum vulgare)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "BH 946" and the variety code is the same. No Seednet portal page or CSC release-minutes page came back in any search, so every finding below comes from third-party or institutional pages, not from the official notification.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- BH 946 was rated salt tolerant in a field screen of barley genotypes, using stress-susceptibility indices on several traits, although the ranking was not the top one -- https://www.agriculturejournal.org/volume12number2/assessment-of-barley-genotypes-for-salinity-tolerance-based-on-various-indices-under-field-condition/
- A saline-irrigation study of BH 946 under nitrogen levels reported its early growth-indices response (crop growth rate, leaf-area duration) relative to 2-row varieties; no separate tolerance rating was given -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/view/140
- Drought, heat, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned no pages that name BH 946 for these stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST
- BH 946 was rated moderately resistant to cereal cyst nematode (Heterodera avenae) Ludhiana populations in a CCS HAU nematology study, and the authors suggested it as a parent for CCN-resistance breeding -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331673876_Identification_of_Resistance_Sources_to_Cereal_Cyst_Nematode_Heterodera_avenae_Wollenweber_in_Barley_Hordeum_vulgare_L
- Rust, smut, leaf blotch and other disease reactions: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- In a dual-purpose (fodder plus grain) trial at Hisar, BH 946 gave the highest effective tillers (416/m2), test weight (45.51 g), grain yield (5.25 t/ha) and straw yield (7.62 t/ha) among the four varieties tested -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/view/5730 (see also https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286941050_Evaluation_of_dual_purpose_barley_for_fodder_and_grain_under_different_cutting_schedules)
- Nitrogen-by-variety trial: BH 946 was judged most suitable for grains per spike and yield among BH 946, BH 393, BH 885 and Karan 16 -- https://scialert.net/fulltext/index.php?doi=ijar.2022.1.4
- Nitrogen-level trial under irrigated timely sowing: BH 946 gave the highest average grain yield among the varieties tested -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344596811_RESPONSE_OF_BARLEY_GENOTYPES_TO_DIFFERENT_NITROGEN_LEVELS_UNDER_IRRIGATED_TIMELY_SOWN_CONDITIONS
- Malt-quality trial under saline irrigation: BH 946 is a 6-row variety with higher protein than the 2-row entries, and lower hectolitre weight than DWRB 101 and BH 885 -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6037
- ICAR-IIWBR pocket guide lists BH 946 (irrigated, timely sown) at 51.96 q/ha in a yield table, and classes it as a feed type -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
- Maturity, plant height, and sowing date/seed rate for release: No evidence found. seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Suitable for timely sown conditions, having good culm strength, seed rate - 100kg/ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics:
DWRB123 is two-row malt barley having erect flag leaf, pale-green spikes with rudimentary lateral florets.  The peduncle is waxy.  Grains are yellow, bold with narrow crease width.
1.	Growth habit : Erect
2.	Anthocyanin pigmentstion of 
a.	Coleoptile : absent
b.	Leah sheath : absent
c.	Auricle (atflag leaf stage) : absent
3.	Foliage colour : green
4.	Leaf width : medium
5.	Average days to heading : 88 days
6.	Averagd days to maturity : 130 days
7.	Waxiness
a.	Leaf sheath : waxy
b.	Ear : non waxy
c.	Peduncle : highly waxy
8.	Average plant height : 93cm
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to yellow and brown rust and also showed better resistance to leaf blight over checks.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 90 kg N: 40 kg P2O5: 20 kg K2O (1/2 N and full dose of P and K as basal dose and remaining ½ N at the time of first irrigation as top dressing.)

disease_resistance.summary: Spot blotch (Bipolaris sorokiniana): the main documented tolerance trait. Trial testing at 18 locations over three years reported that the variety outperformed standard checks for yield and spot blotch resistance; it was superior to all checks at 10 locations. A researcher profile describes the variety as high yielding and resistant to spot blotch and other fungal diseases. A RADBET 2025 invited lecture reports excellent performance for higher yield and resistance to spot blotch, and states that linked gene(s) were tagged without naming them. Original variety data (no digest source) lists very high resistance to yellow rust, leaf rust, leaf blight and aphid; the digest found no direct evidence for rust or other pest resistance, so these listed reactions remain unverified against the searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found in searched sources for rust, insect or other pest resistance specific to this variety. Original variety data (no digest source) lists high resistance to aphid; this is not confirmed by the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: Original variety data: 42.0 q/ha. The trial paper reports an average of about 38.76 q/ha, 7.46 to 8.54 percent above check varieties in the All India trial. The two figures differ and have not been reconciled.
agronomic_details.stability: Superior to all checks at 10 of 18 tested locations over three years (trial report). Stability beyond this count is not reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Released for timely sown irrigated conditions as a feed barley in the North Eastern Plain Zone (NEPZ). Original variety data lists adaptation as the plains of North Eastern States. Original data also states it is very suitable for timely sown conditions. Seed rate is 80-100 kg/ha (original data).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi dwarf and semi erect plant type, resistant to lodging. No problem of shattering or breaking of ear heads (original variety data). Morphological characteristics: Unknown.
agronomic_details.field_trials: All India trial (source page titled 'Vivek Maize hybrid 51', text stated to cover this barley variety): average yield about 38.76 q/ha, 7.46 to 8.54 percent above check varieties; protein 9.0 to 10.1 percent; average maturity about 119 days (unit truncated in source). Multi-location trial (18 locations, three years): superior to standard checks for yield and spot blotch resistance; superior to all checks at 10 locations. BHU 2014-15 annual report: six fixed lines were in AICRP trials under various sowing conditions and 42 lines were sent for NBDSN testing; these lines are not explicitly tied to this variety and are not counted as variety results.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Molecular profiling used 120 SSR/STS markers covering the barley genome (trial paper, see caveat in evidence_sources). Reference varieties used for DNA fingerprinting were K-508 (also written K-506 in another copy), RD 2552 and Jyoti. No marker IDs or positions found for the tagged resistance gene(s).
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. Linked resistance gene(s) were tagged, but no QTL name, position or effect was found.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Mahamana 113 (HUB 113), Barley

Name note: The evidence uses both "Mahamana 113 (HUB-113)" and "HUB 113 (Mahamana 113)". No search returned the CSC release minutes or a Seednet portal page, so I could not confirm which name each source uses. Four searches were run; the Seednet portal and the ICAR/CVRC notification were not reached directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistance to spot blotch (Bipolaris sorokiniana) is the main documented tolerance trait. Testing at 18 locations over three years showed it outperformed standard checks for yield and spot blotch resistance. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277815184_Variety_HUB-113_Mahamana-113
- The Ravindra Prasad profile describes the variety as high yielding and resistant to spot blotch and other fungal diseases. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Ravindra-Prasad-4
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. The search returned general barley and rice pages instead.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Spot blotch (Bipolaris sorokiniana) resistance, as above. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388399759_RADBET_2025_INVITED_LECTURES_36 (the lecture says the linked gene(s) were tagged, but names no gene)
- No evidence found for rust, insect, or other pest resistance specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Released for timely sown irrigated conditions as a feed barley in the NEPZ. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277815184_Variety_HUB-113_Mahamana-113
- Average yield was about 38.76 q/ha, 7.46 to 8.54 percent above check varieties in the All India trial. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554
- Protein ranged from 9.0 to 10.1 percent, with average maturity of about 119 (days, unit truncated in source). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554
- The trial report says 18 locations were tested and the variety was superior to all checks at 10 locations. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277815184_Variety_HUB-113_Mahamana-113
- BHU 2014-15 annual report: six fixed lines were in AICRP trials under various sowing conditions, and 42 lines were sent for NBDSN testing. These lines are not explicitly tied to this variety. -- https://www.bhu.ac.in/Images/files/Eng_Annual_Report2014-15.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: Karan 280 / C 138. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277815184_Variety_HUB-113_Mahamana-113
- Breeding method: pedigree. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554
- Molecular profiling used 120 SSR/STS markers covering the barley genome. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554
- Reference varieties for DNA fingerprinting were K-508 (also written K-506 in another copy), RD 2552 and Jyoti. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277815184_Variety_HUB-113_Mahamana-113
- Breeding-line code: HUB 113. No other line codes found.
- Linked resistance gene(s) were tagged, but no gene name, QTL or marker ID was found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388399759_RADBET_2025_INVITED_LECTURES_36

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, Institute of Agricultural Sciences, Banaras Hindu University, Varanasi, in 2013. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277815184_Variety_HUB-113_Mahamana-113
- Lead breeder: Ravindra Prasad (Assistant Professor, BHU). -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Ravindra-Prasad-4
- Team named in the BHU 2014-15 annual report: Prof. Ravi P. Singh (Director) with the developing team. -- https://www.bhu.ac.in/Images/files/Eng_Annual_Report2014-15.pdf
- Co-authors of the trial paper: Lal Chand Prasad, Ravindra Prasad, Ram Dhari, R. Chand, R.K. Singh and S.S. Vaish. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554

CONTACT DETAILS
- Ravindra Prasad: no email or phone found.
- Institute: Institute of Agricultural Sciences, Banaras Hindu University, Varanasi-221005, U.P., India (postal address from the BHU site). -- https://www.bhu.ac.in/Site/UnitHomeTemplate/2_17_228_Faculty-of-Agriculture-Genetics-and-Plant-Breeding
- Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, Varanasi 221 005 (address from the trial paper). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554
- No official email, phone or contact page URL for the department was found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Ravindra Prasad (n.d.). Variety HUB-113 (Mahamana-113). Indian Society of Genetics and Plant Breeding (publisher per record metadata; journal not confirmed) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277815184_Variety_HUB-113_Mahamana-113
- Lal Chand Prasad, Ravindra Prasad, Ram Dhari, R. Chand, R.K. Singh, S.S. Vaish (year not confirmed). Trial report on HUB-113 (page titled "Vivek Maize hybrid 51"; text covers this barley variety). Journal not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554
- Excellent performance of HUB-113 barley variety for higher yield and resistance to spot blotch and genetic components (RADBET 2025 invited lecture; authors not shown in the excerpt; year 2025). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388399759_RADBET_2025_INVITED_LECTURES_36
- Banaras Hindu University (2015). Annual Report 2014-2015. BHU -- https://www.bhu.ac.in/Images/files/Eng_Annual_Report2014-15.pdf
- AICRP on Wheat and Barley (2019). Breeder and Nucleus Seed Production Programme of Barley (Rabi 2017-18). AICRP-W&B -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Barley-BSP-BNS-2019.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis, DOI or peer-reviewed journal article for this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seed produced under the Mega Seed and National Seed projects at BHU was sold by the respective principal investigators. -- https://www.bhu.ac.in/Images/files/Eng_Annual_Report2014-15.pdf
- The AICRP breeder seed production table lists HUB 113 (Mahamana 113), released 2014, with a breeder seed figure of 60.00 in 2018-19 (table column meaning unclear). -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Barley-BSP-BNS-2019.pdf
- No Seednet, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing for this variety was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- North Eastern Plain Zone (NEPZ) of India. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277815184_Variety_HUB-113_Mahamana-113
- Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Assam and the plains of North Eastern States. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554
- Release year: 2013 per the research summaries; BHU 2014-15 annual report and AICRP table use 2014. The year needs checking against the CVRC notification.

OPEN ITEMS
- Seednet portal entry and CVRC/Gazette notification number were not retrieved. A Seednet search and the Gazette notification (S.O. 1543 is cited in one source but not confirmed) should be checked before finalising.
- Breeder contact email/phone and a department page were not found. The BHU Faculty of Agriculture page and the department's web contact should be checked directly.

seednet_fields.Parentage: Base populations: Base population comprising BB-2, IL2001-409, IL2001-439, IL2001-114 and IL2001-514. Breeding method: Phentypic recurrent selection
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: JHB-18-2 was identified and recommended for release in the states of Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, UT of Jammu and Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Resistant to H. armigera; and resistant to moderately susceptible to aphid
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Late in initiation of flowering, late maturity, broad leaf, fast regrowth and bold seed size.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: JHB-18-2 requires an average of 145 days from seedling stage to initiation of flowering, 155 days seedling to 50% flowering and 185 days from seedling to seed maturity.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Resistant to root rot diseases, moderately resistant to, resistant to stem rot

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: Crop Improvement Division ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat & Barley Research Karnal.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: North Eastern Plains Zone (NEPZ) comprising wheat growing areas of Eastern UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Plains of NE states.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: (1)	DBW 252 (37.7 q/ha) yielded higher than sown recent check variety HD 3171 (37.5 q/ha) in agronomical experiments at different irrigation levels. (2)	It showed significant yield superiority over popular check varieties HD 2888 (16.0%) and K 8027 (17.8%) at all the irrigation levels. (3)	It also showed higher yield advantage (13.0%) at increased irrigation level (2-irrigations) (9.0%) and HD 3171 (7.9%). (4)	Additionally, DBW 252 also has hihest grain number per spike (30.8) and comparable performance for spike number/m2 (307) and 1000-grains weight (42g).
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: DBW 252 has Drought Sensivity Index (DSI) of 0.74 based on evaluations in multilocational DTSN and is categorized as a Drought Tollerant variety.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
(a)	DBW 252 is highly resistance (Av 2.5%) to wheat blast disease which is a potential threat for wheat crop in NEPZ. None of the checks were resistance (Av<10.0).
(b)	DBW 252 showed high resistance to leaf (ACI-3.4) and stripe (ACI-18.1) rusts. It also showed high degree of adult plant resistance to leaf rust. 
(c)	Better resistance to Karnal bunt (Av.5.1%), leaf blight (Av.45) and powdery mildew (Av.3) was observed in DBW 252.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: There is no major problem of insect pests in NEPZ. However, DBW 252 showed better resistance to shoot fly and brown wheat mite under controlled conditions as compared to check varieties.
seednet_fields.Average Yield (Kg/Ha): 14.50 q/acre to 15.2q/acre with mean  yield of 14.8q/acre and yield potential of 22.2q/acre. Kg/Ha
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 90:60:40 (N:P:K) 1/2 or 1/3 at sowing and remaining at first node stage.

drought.details: Drought susceptibility index of 0.74, described in the sources as highly tolerant. One source states the variety needs only one irrigation. Another describes a high-yielding, restricted-irrigation profile. The index is repeated in a product listing, which is a secondary and non-independent restatement. No mechanism-level evidence (root traits, physiological markers) was found in the searched sources. The digest notes the Seednet name was not confirmed on seednet.gov.in.

heat.details: No evidence found for DBW 252 specifically. Heat-tolerance claims returned by the search referred to other varieties (DBW 327, DBW 187/222) and were discarded.

salinity.details: No evidence found in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Wheat blast: highly resistant, average blast incidence of 2.5 percent in Bangladesh trials, reported as a potential threat in the NEPZ. Blast high resistance is also listed on the IIWBR variety page. Leaf rust: a reaction of 3.4 ACI is reported (Amazon listing), and the IIWBR and Krishi Jagran sources are not otherwise quantified in the digest. Karnal bunt: resistance is noted in the Amazon listing, but the wording is truncated in the source, so no value can be confirmed. Rust, mildew and smut reactions beyond blast and leaf rust: Not found in searched sources. Note: the CSC record also reports stripe rust ACI 18.1, leaf blight average 45, powdery mildew average 3 and Karnal bunt average 5.1 percent, and describes high adult-plant resistance to leaf rust. These values are not linked to a source URL in the digest and could not be verified against the searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Insect pests: Not found in searched sources. The digest reports no evidence for DBW 252 pest reactions. The CSC record states that DBW 252 showed better resistance to shoot fly and brown wheat mite under controlled conditions compared with check varieties, but this statement has no source URL in the digest and is not verified by the searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 36.7 q/ha and potential yield 55.6 q/ha (Global Agriculture). Seed yield 37.0 q/ha with potential 55.6 q/ha under timely-sown restricted-irrigation conditions (IIWBR). The CSC record gives 14.50 to 15.2 q/acre (mean 14.8 q/acre) and potential 22.2 q/acre; these units and values differ from the digest figures and have no source URL in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment or AICRP stability data for DBW 252 were found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Timely-sown, restricted-irrigation conditions in the North Eastern Plains Zone (NEPZ), covering Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, Assam and plains of North Eastern states. The qualifier 'excluding hills' for West Bengal was not found in any source. Global Agriculture (2022) does not mention Odisha or Assam.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Days to heading 81 (range 65 to 95). Days to maturity 127 (range 100 to 147; IIWBR gives 125 to 130). Plant height 98 cm (range 82 to 112). Grain number per spike 30.8, spikes per m2 307 and 1000-grain weight 42 g, as reported in the CSC agronomic features; no source URL is given for these in the digest. Sedimentation value 61.2 ml, indicating good flour quality (Global Agriculture).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Global Agriculture: average yield 36.7 q/ha and potential 55.6 q/ha; sedimentation value 61.2 ml. (2) Krishi Jagran: days to heading 81 (65 to 95), days to maturity 127 (100 to 147), plant height 98 cm (82 to 112). (3) IIWBR variety page: seed yield 37.0 q/ha, potential 55.6 q/ha, maturity 127 days (125 to 130), plant height 98 cm, under timely-sown restricted-irrigation conditions. The digest reports no multi-location AICRP/ICAR trial data for DBW 252. Yield comparisons with checks (HD 3171, HD 2888, K 8027) appear only in the CSC record and have no source URL in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY RECORD: Karan Shriya (DBW 252), Wheat
Name note: The CSC name "Karan Shriya" and the Seednet name "Karan Shriya (DBW 252)" both appear in the evidence below. Sources also spell it "Karan Shreya." No seednet.gov.in page was returned, so no Seednet-specific evidence is reported. All four searches used the DBW 252 code and the name variants. Parentage is not confirmed by a second source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought: drought susceptibility index of 0.74, described as highly tolerant, and needs only one irrigation -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/high-yielding-wheat-varieties-developed-by-iiwbr/
- Drought index 0.74 repeated in a product listing -- https://www.amazon.in/Green-World-Agriculture-Kgs-pack/dp/B0BBWDJZJ2
- Drought index 0.74 and a high-yielding, restricted-irrigation profile -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-wheat-variety-wheat-variety-dbw252-karan-shriya/
- Heat tolerance: No evidence found for DBW 252 specifically. The search returned only heat-tolerance claims for other varieties (DBW 327, DBW 187/222), which were discarded.
- Salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Highly resistant to wheat blast (average blast incidence 2.5% in Bangladesh trials) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-wheat-variety-dbw-252-karan-shreya/
- Wheat blast high resistance, listed in the IIWBR variety page -- https://iiwbr.icar.gov.in/varieties-of-wheat/
- Leaf rust reaction of 3.4 ACI and Karnal bunt resistance noted (the Karnal bunt wording is truncated in the source) -- https://www.amazon.in/Green-World-Agriculture-Kgs-pack/dp/B0BBWDJZJ2
- Rust, mildew and smut reactions for DBW 252 beyond the blast and leaf rust entries: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Average yield 36.7 q/ha; potential yield 55.6 q/ha -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-wheat-variety-wheat-variety-dbw252-karan-shriya/
- Days to heading 81 (65-95); days to maturity 127 (range 100-147); plant height 98 cm (82-112) -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/high-yielding-wheat-varieties-developed-by-iiwbr/
- Seed yield 37.0 q/ha, potential 55.6 q/ha, maturity 127 days (125-130), plant height 98 cm, timely-sown restricted-irrigation conditions -- https://iiwbr.icar.gov.in/varieties-of-wheat/
- Sedimentation value 61.2 ml, indicating good flour quality -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-wheat-variety-dbw-252-karan-shreya/
- Multi-location trial data (AICRP/ICAR reports): No evidence found for DBW 252 in the search results.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage (partially truncated in source): PFAU/MILAN/5/C... with the Aegilops-derived line listed in the notification row -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Full parentage as supplied in the request (PFAU/MILAN/5/CHEN/AEGILOPS SQUARROSA (TAUS)//BCN/3/VEE#7/BOW/4/PASTOR.): consistent with the truncated compendium entry; not independently verified.
- Breeding method, QTL, marker studies, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ICAR-IIWBR, Karnal (Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-wheat-variety-dbw-252-karan-shreya/
- The same institute attribution appears on the Krishi Jagran IIWBR list -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/high-yielding-wheat-varieties-developed-by-iiwbr/
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found in any result.
- Station: Karnal is the developing station per the sources above.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute page for the variety listing (institute-level only): https://iiwbr.icar.gov.in/varieties-of-wheat/
- Official email, phone, postal address of the institute or division: No evidence found in the returned text. Visit the institute contact page on iiwbr.icar.gov.in to obtain them.
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, conference paper or AICRP report specific to DBW 252 was found. A ResearchGate entry on DBW 187 was discarded because it concerns a different variety.
- Notification compendium (retrieved, listed as a report): Author not stated in retrieved text (IIWBR) (2024 upload). Compendium of Wheat Varieties Notified in India During 2018-2023. IIWBR Report RB-51 -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- KrishiKosh theses: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Directorate of Seed, Dholi (Rajendra Agricultural University, Bihar): the rabi 2025-26 seed sale availability table lists DBW-252 -- https://rpcau.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Availability-of-different-category-of-seed-for-sale-during-Rabi-2025-26-at-Directorate-of-Seed-Dholi.pdf
- Private retail listing (Green World, 10 kg pack): https://www.amazon.in/Green-World-Agriculture-Kgs-pack/dp/B0BBWDJZJ2
- Seed company product list (lists DBW 252 Karan Shriya under a hybrid-category heading, so the category is unreliable): https://www.indiaseeds.com/products.html
- National Seeds Corporation, State Seed Corporation, KVK listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- IIWBR listing: NEPZ, covering Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Assam and the plains of North Eastern states; timely-sown, restricted-irrigation conditions -- https://iiwbr.icar.gov.in/varieties-of-wheat/
- Global-agriculture (2022): Eastern UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and NE plains states (Odisha and Assam not mentioned) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-wheat-variety-wheat-variety-dbw252-karan-shriya/
- Notification: 99(E), dated 06.01.2020 -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-wheat-variety-dbw-252-karan-shreya/
- The "excluding hills" qualifier for West Bengal in the request was not found in any result.

Mechanisms are not described in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: The CSC record states resistance to stripe, brown and stem rust, and resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses in general. The searched sources contain only a general statement of disease resistance. No rust, blast, smut or other disease ratings were found for this variety. Blast resistance found in the digest belongs to NIAW 4028 (Phule Anurag), a different variety, and was excluded. The stripe, brown and stem rust claims are therefore unverified by the searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: The CSC record states resistance to major pests. No pest resistance evidence was found in the searched sources.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for restricted irrigation conditions. The CSC record lists the North Western Plains Zone. Seed morphology (from the characterization paper, seed not plant): white-seeded, oblong, very soft and narrow, among 19 varieties tested at ARS Niphad. These values conflict.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety significantly outyielded check varieties in the Peninsular and North Western Plains zones, but no yield figures were retrieved. It was identified by the Varietal Identification Committee at the 58th AGM of AICRP on Wheat & Barley for restricted irrigation conditions. No multi-location trial tables were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Phule Satwik (NIAW 3170), Wheat

Searches run: 4 (general variety/notification; breeder/institute; research papers; seed availability). Name note: the CSC/notification evidence uses "Phule Satwik" and the compendium lists it as "Phule Satwik / NIAW 3170". No Seednet portal page for "Phule Satwik (NIAW 3170)" appeared in any result, so no Seednet-specific evidence is recorded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as a bread wheat with high yield potential under restricted irrigation conditions, with disease resistance and superior grain quality noted, but no specific stress or disease tests are named -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380116234_Phule_Satwik_NIAW_3170_A_soft_bread_wheat_variety_for_North_Western_Plains_and_Peninsular_Zone_of_India
- Listed under a "drought resistant" bread wheat heading in a related paper; no drought trial data shown in retrieved text -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Bc-Game
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- General statement of disease resistance only; no rust, blast, smut or pest resistance ratings were found for this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380116234_Phule_Satwik_NIAW_3170_A_soft_bread_wheat_variety_for_North_Western_Plains_and_Peninsular_Zone_of_India
- Blast resistance is attributed to NIAW 4028 (Phule Anurag), a different variety; discarded -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387674976_NIAW_4028_Phule_Anurag_A_new_blast_resistant_bread_wheat_variety_for_restricted_irrigation_conditions_of_Peninsular_India

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Significantly outyielded check varieties in the Peninsular and North Western Plains zones; no yield figures (q/ha) retrieved -- https://www.agriculturejournal.org/volume12number1/phule-satwik-niaw-3170-a-soft-bread-wheat-variety-for-north-western-plains-and-peninsular-zone-of-india/
- Identified by the Varietal Identification Committee at the 58th AGM of AICRP on Wheat & Barley for restricted irrigation conditions -- https://www.agriculturejournal.org/volume12number1/phule-satwik-niaw-3170-a-soft-bread-wheat-variety-for-north-western-plains-and-peninsular-zone-of-india/
- Maturity days, plant height and seed rate: No evidence found
- Seed morphology: white-seeded, oblong, very soft, narrow, classed among 19 varieties tested at ARS Niphad -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376892745_Characterization_of_Wheat_Triticum_Spp_Varieties_on_the_Basis_of_Seed_Morphology
- Grain quality: biscuit spread factor reported as above 10 in one source and 9.34 (PZ) in the IIWBR compendium, which conflicts -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: Skoll X Rolf 07, selected from the Elite Spring Wheat Yield Trial -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Nilesh_Magar (the trial year 2012-13 and source at IIWBR Karnal are from the supplied record, not confirmed by search)
- Compendium pedigree entry: SKOLL/ROLF07 -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Breeding method (pedigree/bulk, generations): No evidence found
- Breeding-line code NIAW 3170 is confirmed in the compendium and the characterization paper -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Genes, QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed at Agricultural Research Station, Niphad, Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth (MPKV), Nashik, Maharashtra -- https://www.agriculturejournal.org/volume12number1/phule-satwik-niaw-3170-a-soft-bread-wheat-variety-for-north-western-plains-and-peninsular-zone-of-india/
- Notification-year and station are also given in the compendium, which lists Niphad as the source -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Named scientists on the release paper (per the publication record): Nilesh Madhavrao Magar, Suresh Dodake, Dnyandeo Gadekar, Bhanudas Game, Rajendra Lokhande, Bhalchandra Mhaske, Yogesh Patil -- https://www.magazines.cornous.com/downloadpdf/257 and https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Nilesh_Magar
- Lead breeder designation for this variety: Not explicitly stated in retrieved text; Nilesh Magar is the first-listed author, so treat as probable only
- Co-authors Umesh Kamble, C N Mishra and Amit Sharma appear on a 2023 seed-production paper that mentions the variety in a list; not confirmed as breeders -- https://www.magazines.cornous.com/downloadpdf/176

CONTACT DETAILS
- No official email, phone, postal address or institute contact page URL for ARS Niphad or MPKV was found in the retrieved results: No evidence found
- Named individuals' contact details: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- Magar, N.; Dodake, S.; Gadekar, D.; Game, B.; Lokhande, R.; Mhaske, B.; Patil, Y. (2024). Phule Satwik (NIAW 3170): A soft bread wheat variety for North Western Plains and Peninsular Zone of India. Current Agriculture Research Journal 12(1): 348-355. -- https://www.agriculturejournal.org/volume12number1/phule-satwik-niaw-3170-a-soft-bread-wheat-variety-for-north-western-plains-and-peninsular-zone-of-india/ ; DOI 10.12944/CARJ.12.1.28
- Authors not confirmed (year approx. 2023). Characterization of Wheat (Triticum spp.) Varieties on the Basis of Seed Morphology. Journal (not confirmed) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376892745_Characterization_of_Wheat_Triticum_Spp_Varieties_on_the_Basis_of_Seed_Morphology
- Authors not confirmed (2023/2024). Parameters of Wheat to be Considered for Biscuit and Bakery Purposes. Journal (not confirmed) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387657777_Parameters_of_Wheat_to_be_Considered_for_Biscuit_and_Bakery_Purposes
- IIWBR (2023). Compendium of Wheat Varieties Notified in India During 2018-2023. Research Bulletin No. 51, ICAR-IIWBR Karnal -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports, multi-location trial tables: No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No state seed corporation, NSC, KVK, SAU seed-sales or dealer listing for Phule Satwik was found: No evidence found
- Indiamart and similar dealer results returned other wheat varieties and were discarded

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Notified as: Peninsular Zone (Maharashtra, Karnataka) and North Western Plains Zone (Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Jammu & Kashmir), under restricted irrigation, notified 07.10.2020 -- https://www.agriculturejournal.org/volume12number1/phule-satwik-niaw-3170-a-soft-bread-wheat-variety-for-north-western-plains-and-peninsular-zone-of-india/ and https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Mismatch: the supplied state list includes Himachal Pradesh (Poanta Valley, Una), Tarai Uttarakhand, Kashmir (Jammu/Kathua), and excludes Maharashtra and Karnataka. The published notification text does not show these HP and Tarai entries, and the supplied list should be checked against the official gazette or CSC minutes before use.
- A global-agriculture.com blog lists Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Goa and Tamil Nadu for this variety; this is a secondary commercial page and was not used as the basis for the state list -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-wheat-variety-hi-8826-pusa-poshtik-for-peninsular-india/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Reported as moderately resistant to bacterial wilt, and tolerant to phomopsis blight and to fruit borer and leaf-eating caterpillars -- https://assamtribune.com/brinjal-developed-by-aau-named-after-sudhakantha
Tabulated as R/MR to bacterial wilt, with the variety described as a long-fruited type edible by cooking and roasting -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0006292
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to ABU.

DISEASE AND PEST
Bacterial wilt (R/MR) and phomopsis blight and fruit/shoot borer tolerance, as listed above -- https://assamtribune.com/brinjal-developed-by-aau-named-after-sudhakantha ; https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0006292
No evidence found for little leaf or leaf curl resistance in ABU specifically. (The leaf curl resistance mention in the bioinfopublication paper refers to a different line, 09/TLCVRES-1.)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Yield 270-275 q/ha, long fruit, R/MR to bacterial wilt, edible by cooking and roasting -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0006292
Fruit long, smooth and light green; suited to processing into value-added products -- https://assamtribune.com/brinjal-developed-by-aau-named-after-sudhakantha
Earliness and quality are emphasised as key traits -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0006292
Tested across several agroclimatic zones of North East India -- https://assamtribune.com/brinjal-developed-by-aau-named-after-sudhakantha
No maturity-day figure for ABU was found. The 130-day duration in the same table belongs to JC-1, not ABU.
No release/notification year found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: cross of Brinjal Local Long x Long -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0006292
Variety code GB 09-12; IC number IC 599663 (NBPGR accession) -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0006292
Breeding method: pedigree-type selection from the cross; the exact method is not stated -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0006292
No evidence found for QTL, markers or genome resources for ABU.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed at Assam Agricultural University, Jorhat, and the Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics lists "Abu" among its recommended varieties -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/12

Dr Gobin Chandra Bora is described as principal scientist of the AICRP on Vegetable Crops at AAU Jorhat, and the variety is named after the late Dr Abu Shadeque -- https://assamtribune.com/brinjal-developed-by-aau-named-after-sudhakantha ; https://www.aau.ac.in/faculty/profile/Dr-Gobin-Chandra-Bora/335

Dr Gobin Chandra Bora, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics / AICRP Vegetable, AAU -- profile page at https://www.aau.ac.in/faculty/profile/Dr-Gobin-Chandra-Bora/335 (no email or phone found on the page returned)

Authors not stated (2000s-2010s). Abu and Bhupendra: two promising brinjal (Solanum melongena L.) varieties suitable for cultivation under changing climatic conditions of NE India. XV Eucarpia Meeting on Genetics and Breeding of Capsicum and Eggplant, Torino, Italy -- https://www.aau.ac.in/faculty/profile/Dr-Gobin-Chandra-Bora/335 (listed on the profile page; year and DOI not given)
No KrishiKosh, AICRP annual report or peer-reviewed journal paper specifically on ABU was found in this search set.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, AAU seed-sales or dealer listing for ABU appeared. AAU's Seed Museum and AICRP Seed page is about conservation, not sales -- https://www.sentinelassam.com/topheadlines/assam-agricultural-university-unveils-seed-museum-and-sprinkler-system-to-boost-sustainable-farming

Assam is the only state named in the input. The sources say the variety is tested across North East India and was developed by AAU Jorhat; they do not give a formal state notification or recommendation -- https://assamtribune.com/brinjal-developed-by-aau-named-after-sudhakantha

seednet_candidate_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: PLANT BREEDER, HP KRISHI VISHVAVIDYALAYA, OIL SEEDS RESEARCH STATION, KANGRA (HP).
seednet_candidate_fields.Parentage: It is a composite population developed from a cross between Pusa Kalyani and Yukina.
seednet_candidate_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Suitable for general calculation in HP from 700 m to 1300 m above m.s.l.
seednet_candidate_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: Very broad basal leaves with dark green colour, hairy on lower side and shining glabrous on upper side; branchings from base of the plant.
seednet_candidate_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: plant height : 145 cm; the variety is medium tall (145 cm) with broad and dark green leaves, thick stem, profused branching, long siliquae with medium bold seed size. on an average it yields 1060 kg/ha. at Research Station, Kangra. At other research stations an average yield of 1234 kg/ha., was recorded an average yield of 1085 was recorded in coordinated yield ranged from 550-800 kg/ha. Nitrogen 60 kg, P2O5, 90 and a seed rate of 10 kg/ha. was recorded optimum in agronomical trials.
seednet_candidate_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to white rust but susceptible to Alternaria blight.
seednet_candidate_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Its reaction to pest is similar to the standard BSH1 i.e attacked by aphids.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat-tolerance evidence was found in the digest. The only heat-tolerance statements found concern cauliflower types generally. disease_resistance.summary: No variety-specific disease resistance was found in the digest. The IIVR cultivation table lists black rot, damping-off, Alternaria leaf spot, downy mildew, and other problems as crop-level issues, not as traits of this variety. The CSC record states moderate resistance to downy mildew, but the digest does not confirm this for Kashi Agahani.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The IIVR cultivation table lists cutworms, diamondback moth, aphids and cabbage butterfly as crop-level pests, not as traits of this variety. The CSC record lists pest reaction as unknown.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: average yield 215 q/ha. The digest also reports 250-280 q/ha on the IIVR cauliflower page, labelled mid-late type, but this is not clearly attributed to Kashi Agahani and is treated as unconfirmed. The IIVR Kashi Agahani page gives no yield figure. The 180-190 q/ha figure on the ResearchGate page is unattributed and excluded.

agronomic_details.adaptation: The CSC record recommends the variety for Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Delhi, and gives suitability for mid-sown conditions (second week of August to last week of September) with harvest from mid November to late December under north Indian plains. The digest found conflicting state lists: Punjab, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh (IIVR Kashi Agahani page); Bihar, Jharkhand, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh (IIVR cauliflower page); and Delhi appears in none of the digest sources. The ResearchGate source lists Punjab, U.P. and Jharkhand.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Conflict: CSC record states Mid maturity group. The ResearchGate source states Mid-late maturity group.

Days to 50% harvesting: 75-80 days, xvi. Maturity (Days seed to seed): 210-220 days, xvii. Reaction to environmental stress: Tolerant to high temperature and humid condition during vegetative growth. xviii. CHaracteristics different from those of he parents: Intermediate stalk, petiole and leaf lamina and vigorous growing habit.
agronomic_details.field_trials: One multi-cultivar plant-spacing trial included Kashi Agahani as one of 15 cultivars. The 30.77 t/ha yield reported in that study applies to the spacing treatment across cultivars and is not attributed to this variety. No other variety-specific field trial, AICRP report or multi-location trial was found. The DUS morphological characterization study at IIVR includes Kashi Agahani, but per-variety scores were not reported because the character-state lists were hard to read.
