search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kashi Agahani (cauliflower)

Name note: The CSC/release name "Kashi Agahani" appears in every source found. The Seednet name "Kashi Agahani (IVRMC-12)" and code "ivrmc-12" did not appear in any result, so no evidence links IVRMC-12 to this variety. My searches did not query Seednet directly. The variety code and the "Hazipur, Bihar" gene-pool origin are unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Kashi Agahani. The only heat-tolerance statements found concern cauliflower types generally, not this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364092494_A_Text_Book_of_Cool_Season_Vegetable_Crops

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for variety-specific disease or pest resistance. The IIVR cultivation table lists black rot, damping-off, Alternaria leaf spot, downy mildew, cutworms, diamondback moth, aphids and cabbage butterfly as crop-level problems, not as traits of this variety. -- https://icariivr.org.in/cauliflower-2/
- A reference to riceyness resistance appears next to the Kashi Agahani heading, but it belongs to Pusa Early Synthetic and is excluded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364092494_A_Text_Book_of_Cool_Season_Vegetable_Crops

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity: Kashi Agahani: Mid-late maturity group, recommended for Punjab, U.P., and Jharkhand. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390795138_Advances_in_Production_Technology_of_Cauliflower
- Yield (IIVR cauliflower page): 250–280 q/ha, mid-late type. -- https://icariivr.org.in/cauliflower-2/
- Yield (IIVR Kashi Agahani page): no figure given. -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/kashi-agahani
- Seed rate: the 375–400 g/ha figure applies to the mid-late and late groups generally, not to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390795138_Advances_in_Production_Technology_of_Cauliflower
- Spacing: 60 x 45 cm is recommended for mid and late groups generally. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370321881_Seventy_five_years_of_research_and_development_in_cauliflower_and_cabbage_A_journey_from_temperate_to_tropicalization_and_aristocrats_to_commoners
- Multi-cultivar trial: Kashi Agahani was one of 15 cultivars evaluated under plant-spacing trials. The 30.77 t/ha yield in that study is for the spacing treatment across cultivars and is not attributed to this variety. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/eb091f0b-5640-4956-b447-dc7763144bd5/content
- Unattributed: a yield of 180–190 q/ha and rainfed-upland suitability appear on the same page as the Agahani entry, but the text does not clearly link them to this variety, so they are excluded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390795138_Advances_in_Production_Technology_of_Cauliflower

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Breeding method: It has been developed by selection. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364092494_A_Text_Book_of_Cool_Season_Vegetable_Crops
- Parentage: No evidence found for parentage or a gene-pool origin. The Hazipur, Bihar collection claim was not confirmed.
- Pant Gobhi-4 was selected from a local "Agahani" material at Pantnagar. It is a different variety and is excluded. -- https://www.biologydiscussion.com/vegetable-breeding/cauliflower-origin-production-and-varieties-india/68621
- QTL, marker and genome resources: No evidence found.
- DUS morphology: Kashi Agahani is included in a DUS morphological characterization study at IIVR. Several character-state lists in that paper are hard to read, so I have not reported per-variety scores. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261100614_MORPHOLOGICAL_CHARACTERIZATION_OF_CAULIFLOWER_VARIETIESCULTIVARS_USING_DUS_CHARACTERS

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder name: No evidence found for a named lead breeder or scientist.
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR), Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh. -- https://icariivr.org.in/cauliflower-2/
- Station: IIVR Varanasi (Varanasi-221305, Uttar Pradesh). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261100614_MORPHOLOGICAL_CHARACTERIZATION_OF_CAULIFLOWER_VARIETIESCULTIVARS_USING_DUS_CHARACTERS

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. No official email or phone number for this variety was found.
- Institute page: ICAR-IIVR, Varanasi. -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/kashi-agahani
- Institute address fragment ("ICAR – Indian Institute of Vegetable Research Post Bag No.", the rest truncated). -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-66969-0_7
- Cauliflower variety page of IIVR: https://icariivr.org.in/cauliflower-2/

PUBLICATIONS
- Varun B.H. and others (2023). Advances in Production Technology of Cauliflower. Journal not identified (ResearchGate listing) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390795138_Advances_in_Production_Technology_of_Cauliflower
- Authors not shown (2022). Seventy five years of research and development in cauliflower and cabbage: A journey from temperate to tropicalization and aristocrats to commoners. International Journal of Innovative Horticulture 11(2):182-195 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370321881_Seventy_five_years_of_research_and_development_in_cauliflower_and_cabbage_A_journey_from_temperate_to_tropicalization_and_aristocrats_to_commoners
- Behera, T.K. (2023). A study on assessing area, production and impact of vegetable varieties from ICAR-Indian Institute of Vegetable Research, Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, India. Journal title truncated in source ("Vegetable ...") -- https://www.isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/395/326
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Performance of different cauliflower cultivars, including Kashi Agahani, in plant-spacing trials. KrishiKosh thesis/report; the title is truncated -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/eb091f0b-5640-4956-b447-dc7763144bd5/content
- Authors not shown (year not shown). A Text Book of Cool Season Vegetable Crops. Book/textbook -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364092494_A_Text_Book_of_Cool_Season_Vegetable_Crops
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Morphological characterization of cauliflower varieties/cultivars using DUS characters. IIVR Varanasi -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261100614_MORPHOLOGICAL_CHARACTERIZATION_OF_CAULIFLOWER_VARIETIESCULTIVARS_USING_DUS_CHARACTERS
- No evidence found for a peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, or multi-location trial specific to this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or IIVR seed-sales listing for Kashi Agahani was returned.
- Excluded: a listing for "Super Agahani" seeds from RP Seeds, Patna. This is a different product name from a different seller and is not this variety. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/super-agahani-cauliflower-seeds-2852105734533.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Conflicting state lists were found:
  - Punjab, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh. -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/kashi-agahani
  - Bihar, Jharkhand, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh. -- https://icariivr.org.in/cauliflower-2/
  - The user-supplied list (Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Delhi) is not supported by any source found. Delhi appears in none of them.
- Notification: 2008 via AICRP-VC, Gazette S.O. 2978(E) dated 26.12.2008. -- https://icariivr.org.in/cauliflower-2/
- The IIVR listing says the variety was notified through the Central Variety Release Committee. -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/kashi-agahani

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B:
AICRP on Chickpea,
Regional Agricultural Research Station,
Nandyal – 518502 (AP).
seednet_fields.Parentage:
ICCV 2 X PDG 84-16

The cross was made at ICRISAT and the material was made available to RARS, Nandyal.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Recommended nitrogen is 20 kg/ha and P2O5 is 50 kg/ha. NBeG 47 being a semi erect plant type with pod bearing nodes towards upper portions of the branches responded well to high plant population. A plant population of 4.44 lakhs per ha with a spacing of 30 cm x 7.5 cm or 22.5 cm x 10 cm recorded significantly higher seed yield than the normal spacing of 30 cm x 10 cm. Thus, recommended seed rate is 115 125 kg/ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics:
i)	Plant type : Semi erect 
ii)	Plant colour : Green with anthocyanin pigmentation
iii)	Flower : pink
iv)	Pod and leaflet size : Medium
v)	Vegetative growth : Medium but grows very fast in early stage.
vi)	Seed character : medium bold, brown coloured seed with angular shape.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Recorded significantly less dry root rot and wilt incidence at RARS, Nandyal and comparable in its performance with resistant checks. In AICRP trials, it recorded resistant reaction to wilt at three locations and moderately resistant reaction at three locations out of 8 locations.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: NBeG 47 exhibited moderately tolerant reaction against pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera) which is a major problem and key pest in all chickpea growing areas
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 20 kg N and 50 kg P per ha. (50 kg urea and 300 kg SSP or 125 kg DAP at the final preparation of field).

seednet_fields.Parentage: It is a selection from ICCV 37 X ICC 12451. The cross was made at ICRISAT and advance breeding line was supplied to RARS, Nandyal.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Suitable for cultivation in all chickpea growing districts in Andhra Pradesh during rabi season under rainfed conditions.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: 1.	In AICRP trials (2015-16) under normal planting sates (with 20 kg N and 50 kg P2O5 kg/ha) tested at six locations, N BeG 452 recorded 8.74 per cent (1344 kg/ha) higher yield than GCP 101 (1236 kg/ha) and 15.6 per cent higher yield than JG 315 (1163 kg/ha). 2.	At RARS, Nadyal (2019-20), N BeG 452 recorded 19.6 per cent (2205 kg/ha higher) yield at 20 kg N/ha compared to no nitrogen application (1844 kg/ha) and at 40 kg N/ha 24.7 per cent increased yield (2299 kg/ha) was recorded which is on par with 20 kg N/ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Semi spreading plant type, medium in height, green with anthocyanin pigmentation. It has small leaflets, pink flowers, and attractive. Pods with bold seeds.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: On par with check/popular varieties in its reaction to major diseases.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: NBeG 452 is on par with tolerant check in its reaction to pod borer Helicoverpa.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Basal application of 20:50 kg N: P2O5 per ha. Basal application of ZnSo4 @ 20 kg/ha.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to anthracnose (reported on the IIVR variety page, the Global Agriculture seed-industry note and the ResearchGate good agricultural practices document for chilli in North East India). No evidence found of resistance to Pepper leaf curl virus; the digest reports no resistance for that disease.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerant to thrips and mites (IIVR variety page, Global Agriculture note, ResearchGate good agricultural practices document, and icariivr.org.in chilli page, which lists the attribute as 'Tolerant to thrips and mites'). The supplied record also notes less attack of thrips. A pest-management trial at IIVR reported a 48.16% reduction in thrips population under integrated modules; this is a management result and the digest does not establish it as intrinsic varietal resistance. The 73.59% reduction in the same trial is not attributed to a specific pest in the source snippet, so it is not assigned here. No evidence found that the variety is resistant to Pepper leaf curl virus or its whitefly vector; the trial reports only reduced infestation.

agronomic_details.yield: Average red-ripe fruit yield of 150 q/ha reported by the IIVR variety page, the Global Agriculture note and the ResearchGate good agricultural practices document. The icariivr.org.in chilli page gives 100 q/ha, a conflict. The supplied variety record gives 95-99 q/ha. The conflict is unresolved.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources (no multi-location trial data).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for autumn-winter cultivation in West Bengal and Assam (IIVR page). The Global Agriculture note states sowing in kharif and rabi seasons, which differs from the autumn-winter recommendation. Nursery sowing mid July to mid August (supplied record). Planting distance 60 x 45 cm; fertilizer 100:60:60 NPK kg/ha; seed rate 400-500 g/ha (Global Agriculture note; supplied record gives 500 g/ha).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Red ripe maturity after 95-100 days of seeding and 65-70 days after transplanting. Medium maturity.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Bushy plant with dark green foliage; 50% flowering 35-40 days after transplanting; fruits 9-11 cm long and 1.1-1.2 cm thick; fruit dark green, turning dark red at ripening; fruit pendant and pungent.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) IIVR pest-management trial on Scirtothrips dorsalis and Polyphagotarsonemus latus in chilli, in which Kashi Gaurav (with Kashi Anmol) was grown in IIVR experimental plots: a 48.16% reduction in thrips population under integrated modules and a cost-benefit ratio of 1:6.66 were reported; a 73.59% reduction in an unnamed pest measure was also reported; leaf curl infestation was reported as 11.18% lower under the control module, with the attribution not fully clear in the snippet. (2) IIVR technical bulletin seed-production table lists Kashi Gaurav quantities (3.84 kg, Rs. 0.70 lakh in one row). No multi-location trial data found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAMES CHECKED: The CSC/release name is "Kashi Gaurav". The Seednet name is "Kashi Gaurav (VR 338)". The evidence below refers to Kashi Gaurav (VR-338). Four web_search queries were run. No seednet.gov.in or CSC minutes page appeared in the results, so the release record rests on IIVR and secondary pages.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Tolerant to anthracnose, thrips and mites; average red-ripe fruit yield 150 q/ha -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/varieties/kashi-gaurav
- Same tolerance profile (anthracnose, thrips, mites) and 150 q/ha yield; the page reports the variety as released by ICAR-IIVR, Varanasi, 2011 -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/chilli-hybrid-variety-vr-338-kashi-gaurav/
- Tolerant to anthracnose, thrips and mites, with 150 q/ha average red-ripe yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373629483_Good_Agricultural_Practices_for_Important_Spices_of_North_East_India_-_Chilli
- Listed as "Tolerant to thrips and mites" (special attribute), with yield given as 100 q/ha; this conflicts with the 150 q/ha figure above -- https://icariivr.org.in/chilli/
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found for this variety in the results.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Tolerant to anthracnose, thrips and mites (see above) -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/varieties/kashi-gaurav
- Pest-management trial at IIVR: Kashi Gaurav showed a reduction of 73.59% in one pest measure and 48.16% in thrips population under integrated modules; leaf curl infestation was 11.18% lower under the control module, with cost-benefit ratio 1:6.66 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336685035_Bio-intensive_Management_of_Scirtothrips_dorsalis_and_Polyphagotarsonemus_latus_on_Chilli_Crop (the snippet does not label which pest the 73.59% figure refers to; the leaf curl figure refers to Pepper leaf curl virus vectored by whitefly)
- Pepper leaf curl resistance: No evidence found that Kashi Gaurav is resistant; the trial above reports only reduced infestation.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Bushy plant, dark green foliage, 50% flowering 35-40 days after transplanting, fruits 95-100 days from sowing, 9-11 cm long, pungent -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/varieties/kashi-gaurav
- Fruit dark green, turning dark red at ripening; 9-11 cm long and 1.1-1.2 cm thick, pendant and pungent -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/varieties/kashi-gaurav
- Seed rate 400-500 g/ha; sowing in kharif and rabi seasons -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/chilli-hybrid-variety-vr-338-kashi-gaurav/
- Field trial: Kashi Gaurav (with Kashi Anmol) was grown in IIVR experimental plots for the pest-module trial above -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336685035_Bio-intensive_Management_of_Scirtothrips_dorsalis_and_Polyphagotarsonemus_latus_on_Chilli_Crop
- Area, production and impact study of IIVR vegetable varieties lists Kashi Gaurav with release year 2012 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378422483_A_study_on_assessing_area_production_and_impact_of_vegetable_varieties_from_ICAR-Indian_Institute_of_Vegetable_Research_Varanasi_Uttar_Pradesh_India
- Multi-location trial data: No evidence found in the results.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: The supplied record says "Selection from Local collection." No source in the results confirms or contradicts this. The IIVR page does not state parentage -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/varieties/kashi-gaurav
- Conflict: One source calls VR-338 (Kashi Gaurav) a "chilli hybrid variety" -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/chilli-hybrid-variety-vr-338-kashi-gaurav/. IIVR's technical bulletin calls it an "Institute release variety," and the IIVR page describes it as a "very good general combiner." Neither confirms a hybrid parentage. Treat the breeding-method question as unresolved.
- Breeding-line code: VR-338 is the code given on the Seednet-style name. No other breeding-line code was found -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/chilli-hybrid-variety-vr-338-kashi-gaurav/
- QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR), Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/386020316_Breeding_of_Solanaceous_Vegetables_Tomato_Brinjal_and_Chilli_Technical_Bulletin_No_110 and https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/chilli-hybrid-variety-vr-338-kashi-gaurav/
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found in the results.
- Variety-page source for IIVR's chilli programme: https://icariivr.org.in/chilli/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Names, roles, official email, phone, postal address: No evidence found. The retrieved text on the IIVR variety and chilli pages contains no contact details.
- Institute pages that carry the variety record (URLs only; no contact details were retrieved from them): https://iivr.icar.gov.in/varieties/kashi-gaurav and https://icariivr.org.in/chilli/

PUBLICATIONS
- Breeding of Solanaceous Vegetables: Tomato, Brinjal and Chilli (2024). Technical Bulletin No. 110, ICAR-Indian Institute of Vegetable Research, Varanasi -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/386020316_Breeding_of_Solanaceous_Vegetables_Tomato_Brinjal_and_Chilli_Technical_Bulletin_No_110
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Bio-intensive Management of Scirtothrips dorsalis and Polyphagotarsonemus latus on Chilli Crop. Journal/report not shown -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336685035_Bio-intensive_Management_of_Scirtothrips_dorsalis_and_Polyphagotarsonemus_latus_on_Chilli_Crop
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Exploring changes in texture, colour, pungency and storability in diverse chilli genotypes for discriminating behaviour beyond harvest. Journal not shown (ScienceDirect) -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304423824008227 (Kashi Gaurav is one of the genotypes; it is not clear the paper is about this variety's breeding)
- Authors not shown (year not shown). A study on assessing area, production and impact of vegetable varieties from ICAR-IIVR, Varanasi. Journal/report not shown -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378422483_A_study_on_assessing_area_production_and_impact_of_vegetable_varieties_from_ICAR-Indian_Institute_of_Vegetable_Research_Varanasi_Uttar_Pradesh_India
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR annual reports and DOIs: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- IIVR technical bulletin reports seed production of chilli varieties including Kashi Gaurav, with quantities and values in a table (3.84 kg; Rs. 0.70 lakh in one row, and 3.60 kg, 0.20 and 0.04 in other rows). Year and sale channel are unclear from the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/386020316_Breeding_of_Solanaceous_Vegetables_Tomato_Brinjal_and_Chilli_Technical_Bulletin_No_110
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- West Bengal and Assam, for autumn-winter cultivation; notified vide gazette S.O. 456(E), 16.03.2012 -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/varieties/kashi-gaurav
- Same states and notification year 2012 (AICRP-VC) -- https://icariivr.org.in/chilli/
- Same states listed in the seed-industry note -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/chilli-hybrid-variety-vr-338-kashi-gaurav/

OPEN ISSUES
- Yield conflicts: 150 q/ha (IIVR page and technical bulletin source) versus 100 q/ha (icariivr.org.in).
- Hybrid versus inbred/selection status conflicts across sources, and parentage remains unverified.
- No breeder names, contacts, seed-channel listings or CSC minutes were retrieved.

csc_fields.special_traits: Plant height: 50-60 cm. Distinguishing morphological characteristics: The plants are dushy, tolerant to thrips and mites, dark green foliage, very good general combiner, 50% flowering in 35-40 days after transplanting, fruits and dark green and dark red when ripe, 9-11 cm long and 1.1-1.2 cm thick, pedant and pungent. Agronomic features: Nursery sowing: mid July to mid August, Planting distance - 60 x 45 cm, Fertilizer - 100:60:60 NPK kg/ha, Seed rate - 500 g per hectare. pest_resistance.research_summary: Tolerant to thrips and mites (IIVR variety page, Global Agriculture note, ResearchGate good agricultural practices document, and icariivr.org.in chilli page, which lists the attribute as 'Tolerant to thrips and mites'). The supplied record also notes less attack of thrips. A pest-management trial at IIVR reported a 48.16% reduction in thrips population under integrated modules; this is a management result and the digest does not establish it as intrinsic varietal resistance. The 73.59% reduction in the same trial is not attributed to a specific pest in the source snippet, so it is not assigned here. No evidence found that the variety is resistant to Pepper leaf curl virus or its whitefly vector; the trial reports only reduced infestation.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kashi Sinduri (IVPBC-535), Chilli

Search coverage: three web searches ran (variety/release, breeder/institution, research papers). A fourth search, for contacts and seed availability, was blocked by a tool-use limit, so those two headings rely on incidental hits only. Name tags: "KS" = "Kashi Sinduri" (CSC name); "IVPBC" = "IVPBC-535" (Seednet name). Pages that name both are tagged "KS+IVPBC".

STRESS TOLERANCE
KS: Described as resistant to anthracnose -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/kashi-sinduri
KS: A later IIVR chilli page describes it as only moderately resistant to anthracnose, a conflict with the page above -- https://icariivr.org.in/chilli/
IVPBC: Listed as susceptible to pepper leaf curl virus (PepLCV) in a transcriptome study, where it served as the susceptible comparator to resistant BS-35 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4987506/
KS: Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
KS+IVPBC: Anthracnose resistance is recorded (see above). Leaf curl virus susceptibility is recorded for the IVPBC-535 genotype in the PepLCV transcriptome study -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4987506/
KS: ChiLCVD (chilli leaf curl) resistance breeding: a recombinant inbred line (RIL) population of Kashi Sinduri x BS-35 (F11, 109 families) was screened under field conditions for ChiLCVD resistance -- https://icariivr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Annual-Report-2023-2024.pdf
KS: Insect or mite pest resistance: No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
KS: Spreading plant; 50% flowering at 30-35 days after transplanting; fruit ripens 95-100 days after sowing; fruit 10-12 cm long and 1.1-1.3 cm thick, pendant, non-pungent, oleoresin about 15%; red ripe yield about 140 q/ha -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/kashi-sinduri
KS: Package of practice: nursery sown July-August in northern plains; transplant at 30 days, 45 cm x 60 cm spacing; seed rate 450 g/ha; FYM 20-30 t/ha; NPK 120:80:80 kg/ha with nitrogen in three splits -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/kashi-sinduri
IVPBC: Seed rate 400-500 g/ha; sowing in kharif, rabi and zaid seasons; yield 150 q/ha -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/chilli-hybrid-variety-ivpbc-535-kashi-sinduri/
KS: IIVR chilli page gives a different profile: paprika type, determinate growth, ASTA colour value above 140, green-fruit yield 200-225 q/ha. These conflict with the 140 q/ha red-ripe figure above -- https://icariivr.org.in/chilli/
KS: Multi-location or AICRP trial results specific to this variety: No evidence found (the 2023-24 IIVR report mentions AICRP chilli/capsicum rainy-season trials only in general terms) -- https://icariivr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Annual-Report-2023-2024.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
IVPBC: Breeding-line code IVPBC-535 (the Seednet code) is used in the Plant Authority DUS test guidelines, which list Kashi Sindhuri (IVPBC-535) as a reference variety -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/chillbellpeppepaprika.pdf
KS: Parentage as supplied ("introduction from AVRDC, Taiwan & selection"): not confirmed by any searched page
KS: Used as a parent in a RIL population (Kashi Sinduri x BS-35) for ChiLCVD resistance mapping/breeding -- https://icariivr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Annual-Report-2023-2024.pdf
IVPBC: Transcriptome (microarray) gene-expression profile after PepLCV inoculation, 319 differentially expressed genes between resistant BS-35 and IVPBC-535 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4987506/
KS+IVPBC: Genome sequence or marker/QTL mapping for this variety: No evidence found
KS+IVPBC: Breeding method: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
KS+IVPBC: Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR), Varanasi; source year given as 2009 -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/chilli-hybrid-variety-ivpbc-535-kashi-sinduri/

seednet_fields.Parentage: The variety has been developed through pedigree method from the hybridization between RGC-1038 x RGC-1017
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana and Maharashtra
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Lodging & shattering resistant, responsive to inputs, suitable for timely sown conditions
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics:
1.	Habit: Branched, erect and indeterminate plant type Pink
2.	Flower colour: Pink
3.	Seed colour: Light grey with black brown eye
4.	Leaf type: Trip innate type
5.	Leaf serration: Serrated margin
6.	Plant pubescence: Pubescent
7.	Seed shape: Flat and Round
8.	Pod shape: Straight and Hairy
9.	Plant Height: Medium tall
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Proposed variety has higher degree of resistance with major diseases like bacterial blight, root rot and alternaria leaf blight
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Minimum incidence of white fly, leaf hopper and aphid was observed as compared to check variety
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 20 kg N and 40 kg P2O5/ha as basal application at the time of sowing through drill. Application of zinc sulphate @ 15-20 kg/ha also improves the yield.

seednet_fields.Parentage: Local pureline selection, collected from village: Dodora, Mandal: Hajo, Dist-Kamrup, Assam
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Rain fed area of Assam, Especially in the Bais (homestead) system of cultivation in the north east region wherein most of the farmers tend to grow a few coconut palms in their holdings.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Having good responsiveness to major nutrients i.e., NPK as well as micro nutrient more particularly to boron
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Tolerant to high rainfall (from June to August) and semi-waterlogged condition, hight humidity, low temperature (during winter) and acidic soil (pH: 4.5  5.5)
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Tolerant to stem bleeding caused by Thielaviopsis paradoxa, Bud rot (Phytophthora palmigvora) and Grey leaf spot (Pestalotia palmarum).
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Tolerant to Red palm weevil.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to Kamrupa in the searched sources. The supplied variety data reports tolerance to high rainfall (June to August) and semi-waterlogged conditions, which is not drought evidence.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat (high temperature) tolerance specific to Kamrupa. The AICRP on Palms page reports tolerance to low temperature for the Kamrup entry at the Kahikuchi centre; this is cold tolerance, not heat tolerance, and is not scored here.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to Kamrupa in the searched sources.

flood.details: The AICRP on Palms crop improvement page reports tolerance to semi-waterlogged conditions for the Kamrup entry (Kahikuchi centre). The digest does not grade this tolerance, so 'medium' reflects a reported but ungraded tolerance. Vikaspedia advises against coconut in flood-prone or waterlogged low-lying areas in general, without naming this variety. The supplied variety data also lists tolerance to high rainfall and semi-waterlogged conditions, and acidic soil (pH 4.5 to 5.5).

disease_resistance.summary: The AICRP on Palms page reports tolerance to stem bleeding (Thielaviopsis paradoxa), crown choking, and grey leaf spot (Pestalotia palmarum) for the Kamrup entry at the Kahikuchi centre. The supplied variety data also lists bud rot (Phytophthora palmivora) tolerance, but the digest does not confirm this. Assam Tribune reports monkey and squirrel damage with heavy losses in Kamrupa plantations in Kamrup district; this is documented damage, not documented resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: The AICRP on Palms page reports tolerance to red palm weevil for the Kamrup entry at the Kahikuchi centre. Monkey and squirrel attacks are reported as causing heavy losses (see disease_resistance); this is damage, not documented resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: The AICRP on Palms page reports more than 100 nuts/palm/year, a copra yield of 2.86 t/ha, 253 ml tender nut water, and 64.5% oil content. The supplied variety data gives 100.6 nuts/palm/year and 17,605 nuts/ha/year; the digest does not confirm the per-hectare figure.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for performance across environments. The AICRP on Palms page notes wide soil adaptability and farmer acceptance.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rain-fed area of Assam, especially the bais (homestead) system of cultivation in the north-east region (supplied data). Vikaspedia lists Assam Tall and Kamrupa as best suited to Assam. The Kahikuchi centre falls in the Lower Brahmaputra Valley zone. The supplied data reports responsiveness to NPK and boron, and tolerance to acidic soil (pH 4.5 to 5.5).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Unknown
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICRP on Palms: yield and quality figures reported for the Kamrup entry (see yield); this is the only field-level result attributed to Kamrupa in the digest. (2) Indian Horticulture (Hebbar et al.): describes Kamrupa as high-yielding and suited to Assam; gives no trial data. (3) Vikaspedia: general mother-palm selection criteria (age above 20 years, more than 100 nuts/palm/year) and seednut guidance; not Kamrupa-specific trial results. (4) Maheswarappa et al.: rain-fed hybrid trials at Kahikuchi (hybrid MYD x WCT) with Assam Green Tall as local control; the paper does not confirm the control was Kamrupa material, so this is NOT attributed to Kamrupa and is indirect only. (5) Journal of Plantation Crops (2021): 12-year black pepper intercrop trial in 38-year-old Assam Green Tall palms at Kahikuchi; the palms are NOT confirmed as Kamrupa, so this is NOT attributed to Kamrupa.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kamrupa (Assam Green Tall), Coconut

Name notes: The CSC release listing (AAU Directorate of Research page) gives the name as "Kamrupa (Assam Green Tall)", with a release date of April 7, 2021. That matches the Seednet name, so the evidence below refers to that entry. Some sources spell it "Kamrup" (AICRP on Palms, Kahikuchi centre). I treated those as this variety because they name the same Kahikuchi centre and the same Assam recommendation. The AICRP/CPCRI listings date the release to 2001, which conflicts with the 2021 date you gave. Both dates are recorded here.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- AICRP on Palms crop improvement page reports tolerance to low temperature and semi-waterlogged conditions for the Kamrup entry (Kahikuchi centre) -- http://www.aicrppalms.res.in/cropimprovement.html
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, or submergence tolerance specific to Kamrupa. Vikaspedia's Assam coconut page advises against coconut in flood-prone or waterlogged low-lying areas in general, without naming this variety -- https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/technologies-for-ne-india/plantation-crops/coconut

DISEASE AND PEST -- AICRP on Palms page reports tolerance to stem bleeding, red palm weevil, crown choking, and grey leaf spot for the Kamrup entry -- http://www.aicrppalms.res.in/cropimprovement.html
DISEASE AND PEST -- Assam Tribune (Feb 2025-era report, "256 days ago") says monkeys and squirrels are causing heavy losses in Kamrupa plantations in Kamrup district, with some farmers reporting near-total losses. This is damage, not documented resistance -- https://assamtribune.com/assam/monkey-squirrel-menace-hits-kamrupa-coconut-varieties-farmers-report-decline-1608840

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- AICRP on Palms page gives a yield of more than 100 nuts/palm/year and a copra yield of 2.86 t/ha, with 253 ml tender nut water and 64.5% oil content. It also notes wide soil adaptability and farmer acceptance -- http://www.aicrppalms.res.in/cropimprovement.html
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Indian Horticulture (Hebbar et al.) describes Kamrupa as a high-yielding coconut variety suited to Assam and lists it among tall varieties for the Northeast. It gives no trial data for Kamrupa itself -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/148529/53887/472679
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Vikaspedia lists Assam Tall and Kamrupa as best suited to Assam, and gives mother-palm selection criteria (age above 20 years, more than 100 nuts/palm/year) and seednut guidance. These are general recommendations, not Kamrupa-specific trial results -- https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/technologies-for-ne-india/plantation-crops/coconut
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Maheswarappa et al. (Indian Journal of Horticulture) evaluated hybrids under rainfed conditions at Kahikuchi against Assam Green Tall as the local control. Assam Green Tall is this variety's code, but the paper does not confirm that the control plants were Kamrupa material. Treat as indirect -- https://journal.iahs.org.in/index.php/ijh/article/download/112/55
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Journal of Plantation Crops (2021) reports a 12-year black pepper intercrop trial in 38-year-old Assam Green Tall palms at Kahikuchi. The palms are not confirmed as Kamrupa -- https://doi.org/10.25081/JPC.2021.V49.I3.7451

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage: the AICRP on Palms entry gives "selection from Assam Tall" (Kahikuchi centre). This conflicts with the parentage you supplied (local pureline from Dodora village, Hajo, Kamrup). Record both and verify -- http://www.aicrppalms.res.in/cropimprovement.html and https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/tb104.pdf
GENETICS AND QTL -- Breeding method: the AICRP entry describes a selection-based origin. The Springer coconut breeding chapter on India describes mass selection and hybridization generally and does not name Kamrupa's breeding line code -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-319-22518-0_7
GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for breeding-line codes, QTL, marker studies, or genome resources specific to Kamrupa.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Dr. Jogesh Chandra Nath, Chief Scientist (Principal Scientist and PI, AICRP on Palms, earlier), Horticultural Research Station, AAU Kahikuchi. His achievements list credits him with developing the 'Kamrupa' variety, which was released and notified -- https://www.aau.ac.in/faculty/profile/Dr-Jogesh-Chandra-Nath/281
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Dr. Kusum Kumar Deka, Principal Scientist, AAU HRS Kahikuchi. Listed as an associated scientist in the development of Kamrupa for NER (2001) -- https://www.aau.ac.in/faculty/profile/Dr-Kusum--Kumar-Deka/305
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Chowdhury D, Nath JC and Mohan NK are cited as the authors of the 2001 release paper for Kamrupa by Assam Agricultural University -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-319-91944-7_17
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: Horticultural Research Station (AICRP on Palms), Kahikuchi, under Assam Agricultural University, Jorhat. The station falls in the Lower Brahmaputra Valley zone -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/122 and https://aicrponpc.org/centres.html

seednet_fields.Parentage: From the germplasm accession IND 004 at Central Plantation Crops Research Institute, Kasaragod, Kerala, inter se mating was done between the selected palms in the population. Subsequent selection from the seedling population was done at various AICRP on Palms Centres.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release and cultivation in the rainfed condition in Maharashtra and irrigated condition of costal ANdhra Pradesh, Tamilnadu and Chhattisgarh States. Longevity 100 years.
seednet_fields.Maturity (in days): This selection is a regular bearer, comes to bearing by 73 months after planting and yields 110 to 117 nuts/palm/year.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Tolerance to water logging and cyclonic winds.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: Length of leaflet (cm): 138.55, - Breadth of leaflet (cm): 6.28, - Number of leaf scars in 1 m length: 32.67, - Length of inflorescence (cm): 113.34, - Length of Spikelet bearing portion (cm): 64.50, - Length of stalk (cm): 46.50, - Length of spike lets in : 51.49
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: a) Plant height: 1231.20 cm, b) Distinguishing morphological characters: - Girth of trunk (cm): 138 (cm), - Habit: Tall, - Crown shape: Circular, - Leaves on crown: 36.54, - Length of petiole (cm): 108.5, Length of leaflet bearing portion (cm): 350.12, - Number of leaflets (left): 98.66, Number of leaflets (right): 94.92
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: This selection is widely adapted to different agro climatic zones. Even in the Jagadalpur Centre in Chhatisgarh State located in the non-traditional coconut belt, the selection could yield 82.5 nuts per palm per year (11438 nuts/ha) with 16.3 kg of copra/palm. This tall palm exhibited quick recovery and gives stable yield after 1996 Novembr Cycolone at Ambajipeta Centre.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Moderately susceptible to Stem bleeding disease.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Infestation level of Rhinoceros beetle is low.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The digest provides no resistance evidence for Kera Bastar against any disease. pest_resistance.summary: Rugose spiralling whitefly (Aleurodicus rugioperculatus): Kera Bastar recorded the lowest incidence (51.11%) and intensity (69.20%) among the tall varieties tested, compared with 87.53% incidence and 92.79% intensity for Gautami Ganga. This indicates relatively low whitefly infestation. Rhinoceros beetle: in the Jagdalpur (Bastar) trial, Kera Bastar showed the minimum rhinoceros beetle infestation. The source reports the whitefly percentage in the same sentence, so the rhinoceros beetle result is stated as reported and was not separately quantified.

The CCARI crop page (110 nuts/tree, copra 180 g/nut, oil 68.7%) and the DBSKKV Maharashtra table (116-120 nuts/palm, copra 169 g/nut, oil 67.0%, copra 3.18 t/ha) were excluded from attribution because the digest does not explicitly tie these figures to Kera Bastar.

The SOD heat-stability paper lists Kera Bastar only as one genotype among many and reports no tolerance result for it -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276306595_Superoxide_dismutase_isozymes_and_their_heat_stability_in_coconut_Cocos_nucifera_L_leaves_Pages_298-304

DISEASE AND PEST
- Whitefly (rugose spiralling whitefly): Kera Bastar recorded the lowest incidence (51.11%) and intensity (69.20%) among the tall varieties tested, against 87.53% and 92.79% for Gautami Ganga -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/399856519_STUDIES_ON_COCONUT_VARIETAL_PREFERENCE_OF_EXOTIC_WHITE_FLY-RUGOSE_SPIRALLING_WHITEFLY_RSW_ALEURODICUS_RUGIOPERCULATUS_MARTIN_ON_COCONUT
- Rhinoceros beetle: In the Jagdalpur (Bastar) trial, Kera Bastar showed the minimum rhinoceros beetle infestation, reported with a whitefly percentage in the same sentence -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue12S/PartO/S-10-12-119-930.pdf
- Bud rot and leaf blight: Lasiodiplodia work is at Aliyarnagar and does not name Kera Bastar, so it was discarded -- https://coconutboard.in/images/icj-2022-01.pdf
- Red palm weevil and general disease resistance: No evidence found for Kera Bastar specifically.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield (AICRP on Palms release note): 167 nuts/palm/year, 29,227 nuts/ha/year, copra 35.9 kg/palm/year (6.28 t/ha), oil 67.2% -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/tb104.pdf
- Yield (Coconut Board / ICJ): an average of 98 nuts/palm/year, copra 3.18 t/ha, with the table showing 19,470 nuts/ha -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- Yield (CCARI crop page): 110 nuts/tree, copra 180 g/nut, oil 68.7% -- https://ccari.res.in/dss/coconute.html ; the same figures appear at https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/name-of-variety-salient-features_24.html
- Maharashtra table (DBSKKV): first bearing at 6-7 years, 116-120 nuts/palm, copra 169 g/nut, oil 67.0%, copra 3.18 t/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341149848_Coconut_and_Arecanut_Production_Protocol_under_A

drought.details: Multiple sources describe the hybrid as drought tolerant. CPCRI describes it as a high-yielding, moisture-deficit stress tolerant hybrid with high nitrogen use efficiency. CPCRI's crop-improvement page lists it among varieties relatively tolerant to drought. CCARI describes it as relatively drought tolerant compared with other released hybrids, with tender nut water of 346 ml per nut. The CPCRI Technology Book reports it as relatively drought tolerant with high nutrient use efficiency. The Journal of Plantation Crops paper reports better water conservation in IND 376 and superior drought tolerance in trials. The qualifier 'relatively' is used in several sources, so the level reflects comparative rather than absolute tolerance.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Drought tolerance is the most consistent trait reported: CPCRI describes the hybrid as a high-yielding, moisture-deficit stress tolerant hybrid with high nitrogen use efficiency -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
CPCRI's crop-improvement page lists Kalpa Samrudhi among varieties relatively tolerant to drought -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/cpcri_crop_improvement
CCARI describes the hybrid as relatively drought tolerant compared with other released hybrids, with tender nut water of 346 ml per nut -- https://ccari.res.in/dss/coconute.html
The CPCRI Technology Book says the hybrid was found relatively drought tolerant with high nutrient use efficiency -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/Technology_Book.pdf
The Journal of Plantation Crops paper reports that IND 376 showed better water conservation and that the hybrid was superior in drought tolerance trials -- https://updatepublishing.com/journal/index.php/JPC/article/download/5653/4974
Salinity, flood, submergence and heat tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
Root (wilt) disease: the ICAR Ready-for-Commercialization volume recommends the hybrid for root (wilt) disease-prone tracts of Kerala, Maharashtra and coastal Andhra Pradesh; this states suitability for those tracts, not explicit resistance -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-02/Horticulturevolume-IIreadytocomm.pdf
Specific disease or pest resistance (root wilt, bud rot, leaf rot, mites, rhinoceros beetle): No evidence found for this variety. The root-wilt tolerance found in the sources belongs to Kalpa Sankara, not Kalpa Samrudhi -- https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/name-of-variety-salient-features_24.html

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Evaluation trial: a 28-year trial, with palms planted at ICAR-CPCRI Kasaragod in 1981, identified IND 376 as the superior hybrid -- https://updatepublishing.com/journal/index.php/JPC/article/download/5653/4974
Yield under rainfed Kerala: 117 nuts per palm per year, copra about 4.5 t/ha, oil about 3.04 t/ha; flowering starts after about 45 months -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/275155900_Development_of_a_Dwarf_x_Tall_coconut_hybrid_'Kalpa_Samrudhi' and https://updatepublishing.com/journal/index.php/JPC/article/download/5653/4974
Yield (CPCRI and other compilations): 117 nuts per palm per year, copra 4.38 t/ha, oil 3.04 t/ha, suited to tender nut use -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/Technology_Book.pdf and https://agriculture.institute/production-tech-fruit-crops/botanical-characteristics-varieties-coconut/
CPCRI Coconut Varieties page: 152–213 nuts/palm/year is cited for a different variety block; the Kalpa Samrudhi block lists 108–213 nuts/palm/year, flowering 3–4 years after planting, tender nut water 346 ml, copra about 220 g, oil 67.5% -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
Farm-level yield in CCARI table: 20,475 nuts/ha, copra 45 q/ha, oil 30 q/ha under rainfed conditions -- https://ccari.res.in/dss/coconute.html
Hybrid yield per hectare reported in the journal paper: potential of 25,025 fruits per ha -- https://updatepublishing.com/journal/index.php/JPC/article/download/5653/4974

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage conflict: the brief lists parentage as "Unknown", but the sources give it. The hybrid is MYD × WCT (Malayan Yellow Dwarf × West Coast Tall) -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
Breeding-line codes: the journal abstract names IND 058S as female parent and IND 069S as male parent -- https://updatepublishing.com/journal/index.php/JPC/article/download/5653/4974 and https://www.academia.edu/126269680/Development_of_a_Dwarf_x_Tall_coconut_hybrid_Kalpa_Samrudhi_
The same paper and the CPCRI Technology Book give the hybrid as IND 376 (IND058S × IND069S) -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/Technology_Book.pdf
Breeding method: a dwarf × tall hybrid selected from a multi-year (28-year) evaluation of hybrid combinations; no marker-assisted selection evidence was found -- https://www.academia.edu/126269680/Development_of_a_Dwarf_x_Tall_coconut_hybrid_Kalpa_Samrudhi_
Genome resources: CPCRI reports whole-genome sequencing of coconut as a new initiative; no Kalpa Samrudhi-specific genome data found -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/100_Years_of_Scientific_Excellence.pdf
QTL or marker studies for this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (CPCRI), Kasaragod, Kerala -- https://updatepublishing.com/journal/index.php/JPC/article/download/5653/4974
Named developers (per the journal paper and its ResearchGate record): Augustine Jerard Bosco B., Niral Vittal, Samsudeen Kukkamgai, with George V. Thomas listed as author -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/275155900_Development_of_a_Dwarf_x_Tall_coconut_hybrid_'Kalpa_Samrudhi' and https://www.academia.edu/126269680/Development_of_a_Dwarf_x_Tall_coconut_hybrid_Kalpa_Samrudhi_
Annual report reference, Augustine Jerard, Niral, Samsudeen, Nair and George V. Thomas: "Development of 'Kalpa Samrudhi'- a Dwarf x Tall coconut hybrid at ICAR-CPCRI" -- https://cpcri.gov.in/old_server_images/images/publications/2015.pdf
Release year conflict: the brief says 2015. CPCRI sources state the hybrid was released in 2009 with Kalpa Sankara -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/100_Years_of_Scientific_Excellence.pdf and https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/Technology_Book.pdf
CSC release minutes name: not found in searches.

csc_fields.special_traits: Plant height: 733.82 cm 28 years after planting. Distinguishing morphological characteristics: The palms are semi tall without prominent bole. The colour of the petiole is green. The variety bears green coloured, oval fruits and the dehusked fruits are found in shape. The seedlings are vigourous, producing more number of leaves within 12 months, having more leaf area and dry weight. Characteristics different from those of the parents: The female parent palms are dwarf, takes 66 months for flowering, bears bright yellow fruits and has yellow petiole colour. The male parent palms are tall, bearing green fruits and takes about 98 months for flowering. The palms of IND 376 bear bright green fruits; have bright green petioles; semi tall habit, takes 45 months for initiation of flowering; and profuse bearing. Description of variety: Age of measurement (years) 28, Category Semi Tall, Crown shape Circular, Presence of bole Absent, Plant height (cm) 733.82, Girth of trunk (cm) 69.36, Total number of leaves 33, Length of petiole (cm) 122.27, Length of leaflet bearing portion (cm) 376.45, Number of leaflets 109, Length of leaflet (cm) 122.73, Breadth of leaflet (cm) 6.01, No. of leaf scars in 1 m length 25, Length of 10 internodes (cm) 39.18, Age at 50% flowering (months) 60, Length of inflorescence (cm) 88.64, Length of spikelet bearing portion (cm) 40.36, Length of stalk (m) 48.27, Length of spikelet (cm) 41.09, No. of spikelet's in the inflorescence 37.18, Number of female flowers 26, Number of inflorescences on the crown 14, Colour and shape of fruit Green, Oval, Length of fruit (cm) 19.38, Breadth of fruit (cm) 15.44, Weight of fruit (g) 1032.33, Thickness of husk (cm) Apical 6.00, Distal 2.75, Equatorial 2.35, Shape of nut Round. Weight of nut (g) 681.33, Percent of husk to whole fruit weight 34.0, Thickness of kernel (cm) 1.77, Weight of kernel (g) 359.67, Weight of copra (g) 219.46. Agronomic features: The palms are regular bearers and commence flowering in 45 months after planting under rain fed conditions. The average time taken for flowering of 50% of the palms in the hybrid population is 60 months. Higher nitrogen use efficiency was observed in the seedling of the proposed hybrid. Quality attributes: The average quantity of tender nut water is 346 ml. Based on the organoleptic test; the tender nut water is classified as -good- in taste with a TSS of 6- Brix. The tender nut water has Na content of 35.1 ppm and K content of 2370 ppm. The oil extracted from the copra of this hybrid is having 45.4% lauric acid. Recommended for Table/processing/export/any other. Reaction to environmental stress: Tolerant to drought. Reaction to major diseases: No major disease out break observed under field conditions. Reaction to major pests: No Major pest attacks observed under field conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: Root (wilt) disease: tolerance is claimed; resistance is not claimed (CPCRI). Evidence from field records: a 1991 planting of 31 CGD x WCT palms recorded about 65% disease incidence while the 10-year cumulative average was about 84 nuts/palm/year, which the authors read as disease tolerance. At 14 years after planting about 68% of hybrid palms were diseased; disease-free hybrids averaged about 96.3 nuts/palm/year and diseased hybrids about 72. Varietal resistance screening (38+ varieties against CSPWD) recorded CGD x WCT incidence of 64.5% in 2002. The CPCRI/IJH 2022 description calls it a root (wilt) disease tolerant dual-purpose D x T hybrid. The FAO/CPCRI presentation calls it a tolerant hybrid. A field report attributed disease tolerance to the CPCRI Kayamkulam station head. The disease incidence figures above show the palms became diseased in the field, so tolerance is partial and not immunity. Other diseases: Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest-resistance evidence found for this variety in the searched sources. The original variety record states that adequate plant protection is required against major pests, particularly red palm weevil, when large-scale plantings are adopted. This is a management requirement, not a resistance finding.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY: Kalpa Sankara (variety_name and seednet_variety_name "Kalpa Sankara (CGD x WCT hybrid)"). Crop: Coconut.
Note: No search result showed a Seednet portal page or a CSC release-minutes name, so I could not confirm whether the two names differ. All evidence below refers to "Kalpa Sankara (CGD x WCT)" unless stated otherwise. I ran 4 searches. I did not search seednet.gov.in directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
-- Root (wilt) disease tolerance and moisture-deficit stress tolerance are listed for the CGD x WCT hybrid on the CPCRI varieties page -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
-- The CPCRI page describes the variety as high yielding and tolerant to root (wilt) disease and moisture deficit stress -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
-- A 1991 planting of 31 CGD x WCT palms recorded about 65% disease incidence, yet a 10-year cumulative average of about 84 nuts per palm/year, which the authors read as disease tolerance -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281137664_Performance_of_CGD_x_WCT_hybrid_in_the_root_prevalent_tract
-- At 14 years after planting, about 68% of hybrid palms were diseased; disease-free hybrids averaged about 96.3 nuts/palm/year and diseased ones about 72 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331140257_Varietal_Resistance_in_Coconut
-- The hybrid was described as moisture-stress tolerant among the combinations studied, and as tolerant to root (wilt) disease -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
-- A CPCRI/IJH 2022 description calls it a root (wilt) disease tolerant dual-purpose D x T hybrid -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/129746/48480/472817
-- An FAO/CPCRI presentation calls it a tolerant hybrid with higher nut yield -- https://www.fao.org/fileadmin/templates/rap/files/meetings/2013/131030-research.pdf
-- Field report: short stature, precocity, disease tolerance and satisfactory yield, per CPCRI Kayamkulam station head -- https://www.ft.lk/Agriculture/root-wilt-resistant-coconut-varieties-help-recover-yields-in-india/31-13085

DISEASE AND PEST
-- Root (wilt) disease: tolerance only; resistance is not claimed -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
-- Varietal resistance screening (38+ varieties against CSPWD) reviewed; CGD x WCT incidence 64.5% in 2002 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331140257_Varietal_Resistance_in_Coconut
-- No pest-resistance evidence found for this variety in the search results.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
-- Semi-tall stature and precocious bearing; mean 85 nuts/palm/year; copra 2.5 t/ha; oil 1.69 t/ha -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/qr_seedlings
-- Flowering 3-4 years after planting; tender nut water 375 ml; copra about 170 g; oil 67.5%; yield 80-126 nuts/palm/year under good management -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
-- TMOC guideline table: Kalpasankara average 84.0 nuts, copra 170.0 g, oil 67.5% -- https://coconutboard.in/images/TMOC/Pdf/TMOCUpdates/guidelines-hybridization-tmoc.pdf
-- Trial of 31 CGD x WCT palms planted in 1991: flowering in 30-40 months; 10-year average 84 nuts/palm/year -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281137664_Performance_of_CGD_x_WCT_hybrid_in_the_root_prevalent_tract
-- Coconut Development Board table lists Kalpa Sankara at about 14868 nuts/ha, with a copra and oil value that could not be cleanly attributed from the snippet -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
-- Commercial table lists yield 14700 nuts/ha, copra 25 q/ha, oil 17 q/ha (secondary source; not verified) -- https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/name-of-variety-salient-features_24.html

GENETICS AND QTL
-- Parentage: Chowghat Green Dwarf x West Coast Tall; both parents root (wilt) disease-free -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
-- Parent-order conflict: the CPCRI seedlings page says Kalpasree (female) x WCT (male), with parental palms chosen from root (wilt) hotspots. The FAO/CPCRI slide lists WCT x CGD. -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/qr_seedlings ; https://www.fao.org/fileadmin/templates/rap/files/meetings/2013/131030-research.pdf
-- CGD is described as a promising donor of root (wilt) resistance, leading to Kalpasree and Kalpa Sankara -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281137664_Performance_of_CGD_x_WCT_hybrid_in_the_root_prevalent_tract
-- Breeding method: introduction, selection and hybridization; D x T and T x D hybrids by simple emasculation -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/READYRECKONERENGLISH2.pdf
-- Genetic purity testing with EST-SSR markers CnKGDEST126 and CnKGDEST117 (co-dominant, polymorphic between parents) -- https://updatepublishing.com/journal/index.php/JPC/article/download/3101/5015
-- SSR-based identification of Kalpa Sankara hybrids, reported as Rajesh et al. (2012) -- https://updatepublishing.com/journal/index.php/JPC/article/download/3101/5015
-- Breeding-line codes: No evidence found. QTL studies: No evidence found. Genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
-- Developing institution: ICAR-CPCRI, Regional Station, Kayamkulam (per input and CPCRI pages) -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/qr_seedlings
-- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.
-- Dr P M Mathew is named as Head of the CPCRI station (Kayamkulam). This is a station-head role, not confirmed as the breeder of this variety. -- https://www.ft.lk/Agriculture/root-wilt-resistant-coconut-

Agronomic features: High yield (14,700 nuts/ha/year) and early bearing (36-40 months after planting). Tolerance to root (wilt) disease. Quality attributes: The quantity of tender nut water is 373 ml and sweet in taste. The nutritive value of tender nut water; Total sugars-4.80 g/ml, Potassium content-2150 ppm, Sodium content- 22.40 ppm, TSS - 4.8 Brix. Data on Fatty acid profile reveals that Kalpasree is rich is Long chain Unsaturated Fatty Acids (LUSFA's) and is healthier. Kalpasree oil is having 25% to 40% more essential fatty acids during all seasons compared to oil from WCT and COD, respectively. Besides, Kalpasree oil is rich in essential fatty acids especially Linoleic acid. Reaction to environmental stress: Tolerance to moisture stress gives better yield under rainfed conditions in farmer's plots in the root (wilt) disease prevalent tract. Reaction to major diseases: Chowghat Green Dwarf as female parent and West Coast tall as male parent. Parental palms were selected from hotspots of root (wilt) disease and the parental palms were disease free and high yielding. No major disease out break observed under field conditions. Reaction to major pests: Requires adequate plant protection measures against major pests particularly red palm weevil when large scale plantings are adopted. No Major pest attacks observed under field conditions.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kalpasree (CSC release name) / Kalpasree (Chowghat Green Dwarf) (Seednet name), Coconut

Search note: 3 web searches completed. A 4th (seed availability) could not run because the tool-call limit was reached, so SEED AVAILABILITY is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE: Only the root (wilt) disease resistance claim below was found. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence was found. -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST: Described as a root (wilt) disease resistant variety. The page does not give screening data, resistance mechanism or pest information. -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Described as having high yield potential for homestead cultivation. No yield figures, maturity data or multi-location trial results were found. -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage per the supplied record: selection from Chowghat Green Dwarf grown in farmers' plots. The search did not independently confirm this. No QTL, marker, breeding-line code or genome-resource evidence was found. -- No evidence found (independent source)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Developed by the Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (CPCRI), Regional Station, Kayamkulam. Individual breeder or scientist names were not found. -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder contact, official email, phone or postal address was found. Institute-level contact not retrieved. -- No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS: No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, thesis or KrishiKosh record naming this variety was found. -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY: Not searched (tool limit). A commercial Amazon listing for "Kerala Kalpasree Hybrid Variety Dwarf Coconut Plant" was returned. It was discarded: it is a retailer product page, not an official source, and its "hybrid" description conflicts with the supplied selection-based parentage. -- https://www.amazon.in/Kalpasree-Coconut-Variety-Outdoor-Resistant/dp/B0F6JQKPCF

RECOMMENDED STATES: The supplied record states "root (wilt) diseased tracts of the country." The search found no independent confirmation of this wording or of specific states. -- No evidence found (independent source)

Name check: The only relevant source found uses the name "Kalpasree" (CSC-style name). No page was found that explicitly links "Kalpasree (Chowghat Green Dwarf)" as a Seednet entry. The ICJ article mentions Chowghat Green Dwarf only as a separate popular cultivar, so it was not used to link the two names.

csc_fields.special_traits: Plant height: 50 to 70 cm. Growth habit: Semi-erect plant with 6-9 primary branches and 10 to 16 secondary branches. Leaves: Raised with an arcus of 45- longest basal leaf, deeply incised with 3 lobes, upper leaves more than twice pinnate. Plants have medium foliage. Stem: Greenish stem. Inflorescence: Contains 18-25 umbels and 5 to 8 umbellets per umbel with 30-50 schizocarps per umble. Grains are oblong in shape with medium size with high volatile oil content (0.40-0.45%). Less susceptible to diseases. No significant damage from any disease or pest observed during evolution of the variety.
csc_fields.breeding_method: A selection made from the land race collected from Koilakuntla village of Kurnool district by practicing mass selection. Tested under the name LCC-170 in different yield evaluation trials conducted at Horticultural Research Station. Lam and in All India Coordinated Comparative Yield Trials.
csc_fields.yield_performance: Average yield 10 Qtls./Ha under irrigated conditions; 8.5 to 10 Qtls/ha under rainfed cultivation; 12 to 15 Qtls./ha under irrigated cultivation.
csc_fields.additional_notes: Recommended for notification for entire country.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: S.K.N. college of Agriculture, (Rajasthan Agricultural University) Campur - Jobner 303329.
seednet_fields.Parentage: The Variety has been developed through recurrent selection based on individual plant progeny (half sib) performance in UD-728 which was a local collection from Garoth, Mandsaur (MP).
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release and cultivation in the States of Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Haryana under irrigated conditions. Medium maturity.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: i. Sowing time: Last week of October to first week of November is the best sowing time for the variety., ii. Seed rate and spacing: A seed rate of 10-12 kg/ha is enough. Sowing should be done behind the plough in rows keeping 30 cm apart., iii. Irrigation: Three to six irrigations depending upon oil type and weather conditions., iv. Fertilizers and manures: 5-10 tones of FYM, 60 KgN/ha, 30 kg P2O5 and 20 Kg K2O in the form of fertilizers are required to obtain best results, Nitrogen should be applied in 3 equal splits; 1/3 of total Nitrogen, total P2O5 and 20 Kg K2O at the time of sowing one third Nitrogen at 45 DAS and remaining one third at flowering stage should be applied.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: a) Plant height: 78.05 cm, b) Distinguishing morphological characters: 1. Bushy and erect plant type., 2. Early growth vigour is high.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: It was found free from stemgall and powdery mildew while it was found to be moderately resistant to wilt and root knot nematode.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Coriander is attached by aphids, infection intensity is at par with other cultivars.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: North Zone (Haryana, Punjab and Rajasthan) during Kharif season under irrigated conditions and HDPS (High Density Planting System).
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: In Punjab, agronomy trials were conducted at three locations: Faridkot, Bhatinda and Abohar, in Haryana at one location of Hisar (HAU) and in Rajasthan at one location of Sriganganagar (Tables 2A& 2B). At Sriganganagar location of Rajasthan the proposed variety CSH-3075 was statistically significant in Seed cotton yield than the qualifying variety F-2381 recommended along with proposed variety for agronomic trial in AICCIP meeting of 2015-16

6.	Leaf: Nectaries : Absent

seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Developed for Irrigated conditions
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: •	At Sriganganagar location of Rajasthan reaction to cotton leaf curl disease of CSH-3075 during 2014 15 was reported as Resistant whereas local check exhibited susceptible reaction to leaf curl disease. Qualifying verities RS-2718 and F-2381 were moderately resistant at this location. At Hisar and Faridkot locations; CSH-3075, local checks at 67.5x10 cm and all the qualifying varieties RS-2718, F-2381 and F-2383 were susceptible and highly susceptible respectively to these locations to cotton leaf curl disease. At Bhatinda location the purposed variety was susceptible to leaf curl disease reaction in comparison to highly susceptible reaction of local check in 67.5x10 cm spacing. moderately susceptible reaction of qualifying varieties RS-2718 and F-2383 and moderately resistant of F-2381. (Table 3A)

C152 x GL. C152 is a released variety and highly adapted variety of Cowpea in Karnataka state with semi-spreading habit and medium brown type seeds.
GL-Bold seeded (Test wt: 18g) local land race in North Karnataka(Belgaum, Dharwad districts) and Goa.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology:
South zone
Southern Locations: Karnataka, AP, Tamil nadu, Kerala(B'lore, Vamban, Tirupati, Madurai, Coimbatore, Killikulam, Palem, Anantapuram, Dharwad, Pattambi, etc.)
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Highest yield of DC15 recorded with 45 cm spacing and Full Package (11.72 q ha') compared to checks DCS47-1(10.54 q ha), Kanakamony (LC) (8.58 q ha') & Goalocal (9.23 q ha¹) at Pattambi; Suitable for sowing during II Fortnight of June; Seed rate @ 25kg ha

seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress:
Moderately resistant to Cowpea Mosaic;
Moderately tolerant to Aphids and Pod borer which is on par with checks RC101 & GC3.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: On par with check RC101 and GC3 for Cowpea yellow mosaic virus and dry root rot.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Tolerant to pod borer damage (%) and aphids.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Full POP 25:50:25 NPK kg ha (Rainfed assured rainfall situations); 12.5:25:12.5 NPK kg ha (Other scanty rainfall situations.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: There was loss of 3.74% in seed cotton yield when LD 949 was sown at wider spacing. seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: HI 8759 showed tolerance to heat stress which is evident from the good performance of the variety under both timely and late sown conditions.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: HI 8759 showed good levels of field resistance to stem and leaf rusts, the ACI values remaining 6.1 for stem rust and 4.2 for leaf rust. disease_resistance.summary: Stem rust and leaf rust: field resistance reported in the release-trial summary. Stem rust ACI reported as 6.0 and leaf rust ACI as 4.1 in a Hindi extension article; the reference variety record gives 6.1 and 4.2 respectively, a minor discrepancy. The reference record also reports high adult-plant resistance to stem rust pathotypes 40A and 117-6 and leaf rust pathotypes 77-5 and 104-2; no digest source corroborates these pathotype results. Yellow rust and leaf rust: described as having good tolerance (Krishi Jagran). Loose smut and foot rot: better resistance than the checks, per a commercial seed listing reproducing release-notice text. Flag smut and Karnal bunt: comparable resistance to the checks, per the same listing; the release-trial title also describes the variety as Karnal bunt resistant. The commercial listing is a secondary source.

pest_resistance.summary: Insect pests: no evidence found in the searched digest. The reference variety record states that no major insect pests were reported affecting HI 8759 and that reactions are on par with durum wheat check varieties; this is not corroborated by a digest source.

agronomic_details.yield: Release-trial summary: yield potential above 75.5 q/ha, average 56.9 q/ha across trials, and 3.8 to 12.0 percent higher yield than durum checks HI 8498, MPO 1215, HI 8737 and HD 4728. Farm yields of 5.5 to 6 t/ha under recommended practices in medium and deep black soils (Krishi Jagran). Frontline demonstrations reported a bumper yield of 107 q/ha. The reference record gives an average yield of 59.9 q/ha and superiority over MPO 1215 (21.5 percent), HI 8498 (12.3 percent) and HI 8737 (7.1 percent) under timely sown conditions, and over MPO 1215 (15.6 percent) under late sown conditions. The 21.5 percent figure is not found in the digest, and the digest range of 3.8 to 12.0 percent differs from it.
agronomic_details.stability: Digest reports an average of 56.9 q/ha across trials. Stability across environments is not otherwise quantified in the digest. The reference record reports good adaptation under timely and late sown conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Timely-sown irrigated, high-fertility conditions in the Central zone, including medium and deep black soils. The reference record describes the adaptation area as the Central zone comprising Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Kota and Udaipur divisions of Rajasthan, and Jhansi division of Uttar Pradesh. The digest describes sowing in early to mid-November under timely-sown irrigated conditions.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 70 To 80Days (reference record). The Krishi Jagran source states about 110 to 115 days, described as early maturing. The two values conflict and are reported as found.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Morphology: Unknown. Grain quality: 1000-grain weight 53 to 56 g, test weight 83.1 kg/hl, and high protein of about 12 percent. Seed rate of 45 kg per acre is seller text. Durum wheat (Triticum durum).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Release trials: three years of coordinated trials across 34 locations; yield potential above 75.5 q/ha, average 56.9 q/ha, and 3.8 to 12.0 percent above durum checks HI 8498, MPO 1215, HI 8737 and HD 4728. (2) Frontline demonstrations: bumper yield of 107 q/ha. (3) Farm-level yields: 5.5 to 6 t/ha in medium and deep black soils. (4) Fertility trial: HI 8759 used as the durum entry in an NPK plus sulphur trial at Indore. (5) Grain quality data from an ICAR publication as listed above.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Tejas (HI 8759), Wheat

Name note: "variety_name" is Pusa Tejas and "seednet_variety_name" is PUSA TEJAS (HI 8759). No Seednet portal page surfaced in these four searches, so every finding below refers to the name Pusa Tejas / HI 8759 as it appears in the source. The crop is durum wheat (Triticum durum), not bread wheat. Sources disagree on the developing institute: primary ICAR records credit IARI Regional Station, Indore, while one popular article credits IIWBR. Parentage (HI 8663 / HI 8498) was not confirmed by any source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Stem and leaf rust: field resistance to stem and leaf rust was reported in the release-trial summary. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342231273_High_yielding_durum_wheat_variety_HI_8759_Pusa_Tejas_-a_new_rust_and_karnal_bunt_resistant_variety
Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found. The variety is described as suited to timely-sown irrigated, high-fertility conditions. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342231273_High_yielding_durum_wheat_variety_HI_8759_Pusa_Tejas_-a_new_rust_and_karnal_bunt_resistant_variety

DISEASE AND PEST
Rust, Karnal bunt and smut: Field resistance to rusts was reported, with better resistance to loose smut and foot rot than the checks and comparable resistance to flag smut and Karnal bunt. This comes from a commercial seed listing that reproduces release-notice text. -- https://www.amazon.in/GREEN-WORLD-Pusa-Tejas-Agriculture/dp/B08LZK3PX3 and https://www.grainx.in/products-detail/pusa-tejas-hi-8759-wheat-seed
Yellow and leaf rust: Described as having good tolerance to yellow rust and leaf rust. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/pusa-tejas-hi-8759-grow-more-earn-more-and-nourish-better-with-india-s-super-wheat
Stem rust (ACI): A Hindi extension article gives the stem rust ACI score as 6.0 and the leaf rust ACI score as 4.1. -- https://kisansamadhan.com/farmers-plant-new-developed-variety-of-wheat-pusa-tejas-hi-8759-for-higher-yield/
Insect pests: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Yield: Yield potential above 75.5 q/ha, with an average of 56.9 q/ha across trials, and 3.8 to 12.0 percent higher yield than durum checks HI 8498, MPO 1215, HI 8737 and HD 4728. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342231273_High_yielding_durum_wheat_variety_HI_8759_Pusa_Tejas_-a_new_rust_and_karnal_bunt_resistant_variety
Trial base: Three years of coordinated trials across 34 locations are cited for the release. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342231273_High_yielding_durum_wheat_variety_HI_8759_Pusa_Tejas_-a_new_rust_and_karnal_bunt_resistant_variety
Maturity: About 110 to 115 days, described as early maturing. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/pusa-tejas-hi-8759-grow-more-earn-more-and-nourish-better-with-india-s-super-wheat
Farm yields: 5.5 to 6 t/ha under recommended practices in medium and deep black soils (Krishi Jagran). Frontline demonstrations reported a bumper yield of 107 q/ha. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/pusa-tejas-hi-8759-grow-more-earn-more-and-nourish-better-with-india-s-super-wheat and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362251802_Pusa_Tejas_HI_8759_A_milestone_variety_boosting_Indian_durum_wheat_production
Sowing: Early to mid-November, timely-sown irrigated conditions. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/pusa-tejas-hi-8759-grow-more-earn-more-and-nourish-better-with-india-s-super-wheat
Seed rate: 45 kg per acre (seller text). -- https://www.grainx.in/products-detail/pusa-tejas-hi-8759-wheat-seed
Grain quality: 1000-grain weight 53 to 56 g, test weight 83.1 kg/hl, and high protein about 12 percent. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/121194
Fertility trial: HI 8759 was used as the durum entry in an NPK plus sulphur trial at Indore. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348432282_IARI_Indore_Madhya_Bharat_Wheat_News_Vol_62

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage HI 8663 / HI 8498: No evidence found in these searches.
Breeding-line code: HI 8759 is the line code, with Pusa Tejas as the release name. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/90060
Breeding material use: HI 8759 is listed as a donor in an IARI Regional Station Indore durum breeding table. -- https://icar-iirr.org/CRP/index.php/crparticles/wheat?view=article&id=33%3Aiari-regional-station-indore&catid=9&showall=1
Breeding method, QTL/markers, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institute: ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Indore (Madhya Pradesh). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/90060
Conflicting attribution: One article credits ICAR-IIWBR with AICRPW&B collaboration. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/pusa-tejas-hi-8759-grow-more-earn-more-and-nourish-better-with-india-s-super-wheat
Lead scientists: T L Prakasha (Scientist), Rahul M Phuke (Principal Scientist), K C Sharma (Principal Scientist), A K Singh (Principal Scientist), G P Singh (Chairperson), K V Prabhu (Chief Technical Officer). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/90060
Also listed as author: Jang Bahadur Singh, IARI Regional Station Indore. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362251802_Pusa_Tejas_HI_8759_A_milestone_variety_boosting_Indian_durum_wheat_production
Release: 2017, central zone. -- https://ebook.icar.gov.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/121194
Breeder seed: Breeder seed was distributed from IARI Regional Station, Indore. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362251802_Pusa_Tejas_HI_8759_A_milestone_variety_boosting_Indian_durum_wheat_production

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute address: ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute, Regional Station, Indore, Madhya Pradesh 452 001. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/90060
Breeder email or phone: No evidence found. No institute email, phone or contact page was retrieved.
The only phone and email found belong to Shri Chandra Enterprises, Jodhpur, a commercial packer (mobile 9166125220, shrichandraenterprises16@gmail.com). This is not an institute contact and is not used here as one. -- https

The reference record also reports high adult-plant resistance to stem rust pathotypes 40A and 117-6 and leaf rust pathotypes 77-5 and 104-2; no digest source corroborates these pathotype results. Yellow rust and leaf rust: described as having good tolerance (Krishi Jagran). Loose smut and foot rot: better resistance than the checks, per a commercial seed listing reproducing release-notice text. Flag smut and Karnal bunt: comparable resistance to the checks, per the same listing; the release-trial title also describes the variety as Karnal bunt resistant. The commercial listing is a secondary source.
