search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Dantiwada Fieldpea 1 (seednet name: Dantiwada Fieldpea 1 (SKNP 04-09); CSC minutes name: Dantiwada Fieldpea 1; code SKNP 04-09)

Searches run: 4 (the maximum). Sources name the variety in three forms: "Dantiwada Pea-1" (dpd.gov.in table), "Dantiwada Fieldpea 1 (SKNP 04-09)" (Seednet-style form), and "Dantiwada Fieldpea-1 (SKNP 04-09)" (WDRA). The dpd.gov.in table and the ICAR-IIPR report both use the code SKNP 04-09 (or SKNP 04-9), so I attributed them to this variety. Other varieties and unrelated crops were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety. The search returned only generic field pea pages (sarep.ucdavis.edu, eagri.org, ndsu.edu) about other cultivars. -- https://sarep.ucdavis.edu/covercrop/fieldpea

DISEASE AND PEST
- Listed as resistant to powdery mildew in the national table of released fieldpea varieties (2011, GAU column). -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/vi)%20Fieldpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The same table entry gives an unlabelled value of 17.0 and a range of 98-123, with no units or column headers in the extracted text. I could not confirm what these numbers measure. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/vi)%20Fieldpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The "moderately resistant to pod borer and stem fly" note appears against a different row (IPF 4-9), so I did not attribute it to this variety. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/vi)%20Fieldpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The ICAR-IIPR report lists this variety among the fieldpea entries with powdery mildew resistance, but the extracted text is truncated. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The ICAR-IIPR MULLaRP report (2021-22) includes a dwarf fieldpea AVT trial table for NEPZ with entries 2019-20 to 2021-22 that name SKNP 04-9, but the table is garbled and I could not extract yield values for this variety. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- A pest-management study states that Dantiwada Field pea 1 was obtained from the Pulses Research Station, SDAU, Sardarkrushinagar, and used as the test crop. The highest seed yield the study reports (1250 kg/ha) is for module M4, not for this variety alone. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389186504_Evaluation_and_Validation_of_Different_Integrated_Pest_Management_Modules_for_Field_Pea
- The ICAR-IIPR report says 25 fieldpea varieties were in the seed chain, and lists SKNP 04-9 among popular fieldpea varieties of the decade. This is a general statement, not variety-level data. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage ("selection from germplasm line DDR-49") and the code SKNP 04-09 come from the task input only. No web source confirmed the parentage or the selection method. -- User-supplied input (no URL)
- Breeding-line code SKNP 04-09 is confirmed by the dpd.gov.in table. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/vi)%20Fieldpea%20Varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for QTL, marker, genome or gene studies on this variety. The genome-wide association study returned (DOI 10.3389/fpls.2019.01538) is on pea in general and does not name this variety, so I discarded it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: Sardarkrushinagar Dantiwada Agricultural University (SDAU). The Pulses Research Station at SDAU is named as the source of the seed in the pest-management study. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389186504_Evaluation_and_Validation_of_Different_Integrated_Pest_Management_Modules_for_Field_Pea
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. None of the searches named a breeder for this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No breeder email, phone, postal address or institute contact page for this variety turned up in the searches. The ICAR-IIPR varieties page and the VPKAS page were about other varieties and were discarded.

PUBLICATIONS
- Kumar Vinay, Baudh Bharti, Shiva Nath, Jainendra Pratap, Shambhoo Prasad, Dharmendra Kumar (2025). Genetic Divergence, Variability and Association Analysis for Seed Yield and its Contributing Traits in Selected Germplasm of Field Pea (Pisum sativum L.). Legume Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5413 (SKNP 04-09 is one of 28 genotypes studied)
- Panickar Bindu (year not stated in the source). Evaluation and Validation of Different Integrated Pest Management Modules for Field Pea. ResearchGate preprint (journal not stated) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389186504_Evaluation_and_Validation_of_Different_Integrated_Pest_Management_Modules_for_Field_Pea
- ICAR-IIPR (2022). All India Coordinated Research Project on MULLaRP, Progress Report Rabi 2021-22. Report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf (no DOI; variety named in the report text)
- No KrishiKosh thesis or peer-reviewed paper specifically on this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The ICAR-IIPR report says 940.45 q of breeder seed was produced for fieldpea in Rabi 2021-22, with the variety named in the text. This does not give a variety-specific quantity. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- The WDRA yellow pea standard lists "Dantiwada Fieldpea-1 (SKNP 04-09)" as a commodity name. This is a quality standard, not a seed source. -- https://wdra.gov.in/web/wdra/yellow-peas
- No evidence found for NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SDAU seed sales, or private dealers offering this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The national table lists the NEPZ zone with BH (Bihar), JH (Jharkhand), UP (Uttar Pradesh) and WB (West Bengal). This matches the task input ("Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal"). -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/vi)%20Fieldpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The table's "GAU" column label is not explained in the extracted text and should be checked against the original release record.

disease_resistance.summary: Digest: No evidence found for RFP 4. The Project Coordinator's Report lists rust and powdery mildew resistance as general objectives of the field pea programme but does not attribute resistance to RFP 4. Variety record (not from the digest sources): resistant to moderately resistant against powdery mildew, rust and root-rot; resistant to moderately resistant against root-knot nematode. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RFP 4 (Keshwanand Matar 1), Pea (Field pea)

Name note: The release-minutes name is "RFP 4" and the Seednet name is "RFP 4 (Keshwanand Matar 1)". The only relevant source spells it "Keswanand Matar 1" in one row and "Keshwanand Matar 1" in another. Searches on "Keshwanand Matar 1" returned unrelated pages (Swami Keshwanand Rajasthan Agricultural University, Keshwanand NDA Academy), which I discarded. The Seednet portal page itself was not returned by any search.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The only source naming this variety (ICAR-IIPR Project Coordinator's Report 2021-22) gives no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for RFP 4. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for RFP 4. The same report lists rust and powdery mildew resistance as general objectives of the field pea programme, but does not attribute resistance to RFP 4 specifically. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Unrelated (discarded): Pant P 244/Pant P 42 rust screening, and a Pantnagar germplasm study, which do not name RFP 4. -- https://microbiologyjournal.org/evaluation-of-pea-germplasms-for-rust-disease-resistance/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The variety appears as a row in a release table with institute "RARS, Durgapura", parentage "Bonneville x NPL", year 2016, a duration-type value of 110-120 (the column header is not preserved in the extract, so the meaning is unconfirmed), state "Rajasthan", and seed type "medium bold". Yield, plant height and sowing data are not given. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
No multi-location trial results found. -- searched, none for this variety

GENETICS AND QTL (parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: Bonneville x NPL. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Breeding method, breeding-line code, QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution (per release table): RARS (Regional Agricultural Research Station), Durgapura, under AICRP on MULLaRP, ICAR. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found.
Note: The RARI Durgapura page (raridurgapura.org) lists a single field pea variety, RPG-3, and does not mention RFP 4. I did not attribute RFP 4 to that institute. -- https://raridurgapura.org/varieties-developed.htm

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder contact was found. No institute-level contact for RARS Durgapura was found in the results. The Swami Keshwanand Rajasthan Agricultural University contact (0151-2251083, cimca@raubikaner.org, Bikaner) was discarded because it is a different university named by a name resemblance. -- https://raubikaner.org/result/

PUBLICATIONS
ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (2021-22). Project Coordinator's Report (AICRP on MULLaRP), Rabi 2021-22. ICAR-IIPR Project Coordinator's Report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
No peer-reviewed papers, theses (KrishiKosh) or conference papers naming RFP 4 were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for RFP 4 at Seednet, the NSC, a KVK or a SAU. The Rajasthan State Seeds Corporation pages found (rajseeds.org; Durgapura unit listings) do not name this variety, so I did not attribute them to it. -- https://rajseeds.org/OfficersatHeadquartersandUnits.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
Rajasthan (release table row for RFP 4). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

Gaps to close: the Seednet portal entry, the official release gazette/CVRC minutes, and the RARS Durgapura or SKRAU (Jobner) pulses breeding contact would need direct checks on those sites.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: Two names were searched, "KALUA" (CSC release minutes) and "KALUA (OEB 532)" (Seednet). No retrieved page showed the Seednet portal, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found. The evidence below refers to OEB 532 only where a page gives that code, and to "Kalua" where a page uses only the name. Those two are not confirmed as the same variety. The search budget (4 queries) is used up, so gaps are listed as gaps.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- In a natural-field neck and finger blast screen, OEB-532 showed an immune reaction and gave about 41.10 q/ha grain yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361506944_Identification_of_resistant_sources_of_finger_millet_varieties_against_neck_and_finger_blast_disease
- The Indian Institute of Millets Research salient-features table lists OEB 532 as moderately resistant to blast -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- A 2022 review says OEB 532 showed tolerance to a broad range of insect pests -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/pbr.13169
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance for OEB 532: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast (neck and finger), moderately resistant per the IIMR table -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf ; immune in natural-field blast screen -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361506944_Identification_of_resistant_sources_of_finger_millet_varieties_against_neck_and_finger_blast_disease
- Stem borer: OEB 532 was one of the genotypes in a CPR Berhampur (OUAT) stem-borer screen; the snippet does not show the resistance rating, so none is recorded -- https://www.entomoljournal.com/archives/2018/vol6issue6/PartM/6-6-63-795.pdf
- Other pests: No evidence found beyond the insect-tolerance note above.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity 110-115 days, non-lodging and non-shattering, 22-25 q/ha yield (IIMR salient-features table) -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- Maturity 100-105 days, early duration, 30-35 q/ha, recommended for Karnataka (DHAN compendium; conflicts with the row above) -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
- Grain yield 41.10 q/ha in a natural-field blast trial (see Stress) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361506944_Identification_of_resistant_sources_of_finger_millet_varieties_against_neck_and_finger_blast_disease
- Performance under rainfed Nagaland conditions (OEB 532 among ten varieties, 2019): the snippet gives no OEB 532 values -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369144495_Pertormanee_of_Finger_Millet_Varieties_underAgro_-Climatic_Conditions_of_Nagaland
- Odisha N-response trial (2019-2021, Eastern Ghat) included a variety named "Kalua" (not coded as OEB 532); identity not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378373199_Effect_of_Nitrogen_on_the_Performance_of_Finger_Millet_in_Eastern_Ghat_High_Land_Zone_of_Odisha_India
- Kalua in farmer-field demonstrations (KVK Nabarangpur 2022 report, citing AICRP Millet CPR Berhampur) -- https://kvknabarangpur.in/upload/progress-report/2062036021_Annual-Report-Proforma-2022_ATARI-Kolkata.pdf (identity of "Kalua" not coded)

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage GPU-26 x L-5 (IIMR salient-features table) -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- Breeding method, breeding-line codes, QTL, markers, genome resources specific to OEB 532: No evidence found. The 2022 review covers finger millet genetic resources generally, not this variety -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/pbr.13169

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution per IIMR table: OAUT (OUAT), Bhubaneswar, release year 2012 -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf . This conflicts with the requested record (Centre for Pulses Research, Berhampur, 2020).
- Compendium lists "Centre/Institution developed" and year of release fields for OEB 532 but the snippet leaves them blank -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
- Lead breeder name for OEB 532: No evidence found. Dr. Pabitra Mohan Mohapatra is described as an OUAT senior scientist whose group supplies Arjuna and Kalua seed; he is not named as breeder -- https://theindiantribal.com/2024/11/05/tribals-reap-dividends-of-government-supported-farming-of-super-food-millets/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder email, phone, postal address: No evidence found.
- Institute contact page for CPR Berhampur or OUAT/OAUT Bhubaneswar: No evidence found in the retrieved results. Do not use the OUAT seed-supply mention as a contact.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2023 or 2024 ResearchGate listing). Pertormanee of Finger Millet Varieties under Agro-Climatic Conditions of Nagaland. ResearchGate (Nagaland University trial, 2019 season) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369144495_Pertormanee_of_Finger_Millet_Varieties_underAgro_-Climatic_Conditions_of_Nagaland
- Authors not shown in retrieved text. Effect of Nitrogen on the Performance of Finger Millet in Eastern Ghat High Land Zone of Odisha, India. ResearchGate (RRTS Koraput-area trial, kharif 2019-2021; includes "Kalua") -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378373199_Effect_of_Nitrogen_on_the_Performance_of_Finger_Millet_in_Eastern_Ghat_High_Land_Zone_of_Odisha_India
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2022). Identification of resistant sources of finger millet varieties against neck and finger blast disease. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361506944_Identification_of_resistant_sources_of_finger_millet_varieties_against_neck_and_finger_blast_disease
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2018). Screening of finger millet genotypes against stem borer. Journal of Entomology and Zoology Studies, vol. 6, issue 6, CPR Berhampur, OUAT -- https://www.entomoljournal.com/archives/2018/vol6issue6/PartM/6-6-63-795.pdf
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2022). Finger millet (Eleusine coracana) improvement. Plant Breeding (Wiley), DOI 10.1111/pbr.13169 -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/pbr.13169
- KrishiKosh theses and AICRP annual reports specific to OEB 532: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- OUAT-developed Arjuna and Kalua seed is procured and sold through the state seed corporation (OSSCL) network, per a 2024 news report -- https://theindiantribal.com/2024/11/05/tribals-reap-dividends-of-government-supported-farming-of-super-food-millets/
- AICSIP 2022 breeding report lists Kalua among finger millet seed production entries (nucleus and breeder seed quantities); name only, no code -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip22/Small_Millets/reports22/1-Breeding.pdf
- NSC, SAU seed sales, KVK or private dealer listings for OEB 532: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- IIMR table: Odisha, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- DHAN compendium: Karnataka only -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
- IIMR package-of-practices and state-variety list places OEB-532 under Orissa (Odisha) -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/1-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Finger_Millet.p

OPEN ISSUES FOR THE RECORD
- Release year (2012 in IIMR table vs 2020 in the request) and institution (OAUT Bhubaneswar vs CPR Berhampur) disagree. Verify against the CSC minutes and the Seednet entry.
- Recommended states disagree between sources (Odisha-only in the request; wider list in IIMR; Karnataka in DHAN).
- Maturity and yield disagree between the IIMR and DHAN tables.
- Seednet portal page and the official notification number were not retrieved.

drought.details: No variety-specific drought tolerance evidence found for CFMV 1. The digest's generic drought statements from the Pharma Journal review refer to finger millet as a crop, not to CFMV 1, and were excluded. The variety is described as suitable for early and late kharif under rainfed conditions (original variety data), but this is an adaptation statement, not a measured drought tolerance rating.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat tolerance evidence found. The Odisha hot subhumid trial reports yield performance only, not heat tolerance mechanisms.

salinity.details: No evidence found in searched sources for salinity tolerance of CFMV 1.

flood.details: No evidence found in searched sources for flood tolerance of CFMV 1.

disease_resistance.summary: Highly resistant to finger blast and neck blast, and resistant to banded sheath blight (banded blight) and foot rot (original variety data). The Indian Farming Jan 2023 table lists CFMV 1 as resistant to finger blast, neck blast and banded blight, and tolerant to rust and sheath blight. The ICAR-IIMR cultivar list describes CFMV 1 as tolerant of leaf, neck and finger blast and moderately resistant to banded blight. Foot rot is listed as a disease for this variety in the ICAR-IIMR Millets chalisa. Note that the sources differ in rating wording (highly resistant versus resistant versus tolerant versus moderately resistant). Leaf blast is not confirmed as resistant in the chalisa and is only reported as tolerant in the ICAR-IIMR list.

pest_resistance.summary: The ICAR-IIMR cultivar list describes CFMV 1 as tolerant of insect pests, without naming specific pests. The Millets chalisa lists shoot aphids, stem borer and grasshoppers as pests of this variety, but does not give a resistance rating for them. Control measures listed in the chalisa are chloroantraniliprole dust or quinalphos. Pest reaction is recorded as unknown in the original variety data.

CFMV 1 (Indravathi) finger millet: evidence digest

Name check: "variety_name" is CFMV 1. "seednet_variety_name" is "CFMV 1 (Indravathi) (FMV 1116) (VR 1101)". The evidence below refers to CFMV 1 / Indravathi (FMV 1116, VR 1101). No seednet.gov.in page was returned in any search, so every item comes from secondary sources.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to finger blast, neck blast and banded blight, and tolerant to rust and sheath blight (Indian Farming, Jan 2023 table) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Tolerant of leaf, neck and finger blast, moderately resistant to banded blight, and tolerant of insect pests (ICAR-IIMR cultivar list entry for CFMV 1) -- https://www.millets.res.in/ztmc/Millet_Cultivars_Commercialisation.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance specific to this variety: No evidence found. The Odisha hot subhumid trial (below) reports yield performance, not stress tolerance. Generic drought statements in the Pharma Journal review refer to finger millet as a crop, not to CFMV 1 -- https://qtanalytics.in/journals/index.php/IJERR/article/view/3358

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to finger blast, neck blast and banded blight; foot rot, shoot aphids, stem borer and grasshoppers are listed as pests/diseases for this variety (Millets chalisa, ICAR-IIMR) -- https://www.millets.res.in/farmer/2025/Millets_chalisa/English/6Millets_chalisa_finger_miillet.pdf
- Control measures for pests on this variety are listed in the same chalisa (chloroantraniliprole dust or quinalphos) -- https://www.millets.res.in/farmer/2025/Millets_chalisa/English/6Millets_chalisa_finger_miillet.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release year 2020, grain yield 30-32 q/ha, maturity 110-115 days, medium maturity -- https://www.millets.res.in/ztmc/Millet_Cultivars_Commercialisation.pdf (the 2021 release year in the request does not match this source or the Indian Farming table, which both give 2020)
- Same yield and maturity figures in the AICRP-linked summary table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Coimbatore/Vizianagaram-linked AICRP AVT (FMV 1116, VR 1101): over three years the South zone table lists grain yield about 2886 kg/ha and maturity about 115 days (table row, column order partly garbled) -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip19/Small_Millets/report19/1-SM-Breeding-Kharif-Report-agm20.pdf
- Kharif 2022 South zone IVT with CFMV 1 as a check: CFMV 1 gave 2986 kg/ha, behind CFMV 2 at 3083 kg/ha -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip22/Small_Millets/reports22/1-Breeding.pdf
- Naira, Andhra Pradesh (rabi 2023-24, ANGRAU): Indravathi under 100% RDF (60:30:30 NPK kg/ha) gave the tallest plants, most tillers and highest dry matter -- https://journalijpss.com/index.php/IJPSS/article/view/5573
- Odisha hot subhumid trial (Centurion University): Indravathi gave the highest grain yield (2315 kg/ha) and highest fingers per ear among eight cultivars -- https://qtanalytics.in/journals/index.php/IJERR/article/view/3358
- Nagaland (Centurion trial, same Indravathi entry) reports leaf area duration and tillers relative to other cultivars -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369144495_Pertormanee_of_Finger_Millet_Varieties_underAgro_-Climatic_Conditions_of_Nagaland

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage VL 330 x GE 532 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384662135_Food_System_for_Sustainability_and_Profitability_of_Millets
- Parentage VL 330 x GE 532 also appears as the CFMV 1 check entry in AICRP trials -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip22/Small_Millets/reports22/1-Breeding.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
The search budget was used up after four queries, and none of the results named CFMV 2 or FMV 1118. Every heading below is therefore "No evidence found."

Search log:
1. "CFMV 2 Finger millet variety" returned a ResearchGate paper on proso millet variety PMV 442, a different crop and variety.
2. "CFMV 2 FMV 1118 finger millet breeder developed by" returned the same PMV 442 paper.
3. "CFMV 2 finger millet research paper" returned the same PMV 442 paper.
4. "CFMV 2 finger millet seed availability" returned a millets.res.in farmer PDF on finger millet intercropping, which is generic and does not name this variety. Discarded.

I checked only the title, URL and first 300 characters of each result, so a passing mention deeper in a page could have been missed. A fifth search, which I had planned for the Navsari Agricultural University station and the Dangs pure-line selection, was refused by the tool's server limit.

Name note: the CSC release-minute name is "CFMV 2" and the Seednet name is "CFMV 2 (FMV 1118) (GN-9/Gira)". Neither name returned any evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. No search result described drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for CFMV 2 or FMV 1118.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No search result described disease or pest resistance for CFMV 2 or FMV 1118.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No search result gave yield, maturity or trial data for CFMV 2 or FMV 1118.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. The only parentage information is the user-supplied record ("Pure line selection from local collections made under Dangs District of Gujarat"). I did not verify it, and no search result confirmed it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. The institution named in the input is Navsari Agricultural University, Hill Millet Research Station, but no search result confirmed a breeder or the station's role in developing this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute or station contact was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The only academic hit was the PMV 442 proso millet paper, which concerns a different crop and variety, so I excluded it.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Now I'll pull the TNFC-specific sentences from the pages that mention the variety.TNFC 0926 (Cowpea, fodder). Seednet name and CSC minutes name are both "TNFC 0926" in the sources found; the Seednet portal itself was not reachable, so its record was not checked directly. Some sources also write it as TNFC-0926 or TNFC0926. All findings below refer to this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Heat-stress study of fodder cowpea genotypes: TNFC0926 was among genotypes with stable performance across polyhouse and field conditions, and it performed on par with other entries on one growth trait; the snippet does not name the trait or give a clear tolerance rating -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/397217111_Genotypic_Variation_in_Fodder_Cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_L_Walp_for_Adaptability_to_Heat_Stress_An_Evaluation_of_Growth_Physio-Biochemical_Traits_and_Fodder_Quality
- No evidence found for drought, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to TNFC 0926.

DISEASE AND PEST
- TNAU forage variety list entry for TNFC 0926 mentions resistance to a virus abbreviated "YMY" (text cut off in the snippet, so the disease is not confirmed) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/pdf/List%20of%20fodder%20varieties%20&%20its%20special%20features.pdf
- No evidence found for pest resistance specific to TNFC 0926 (the pod-borer and bacterial blight/rust mentions in the arid legumes table refer to a different, unlabelled cowpea entry in the same row block).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- TNAU comparison table: TNFC 0926 duration 50-55 days; green fodder yield 25 t/ha; seed yield value cut off in snippet -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/foragecrops_foddercowpea.html
- TNAU season table: recommended for irrigated conditions in all districts of Tamil Nadu, sown June-July -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/agri_seasonandvarieties_foddercowpea.html
- ICAR forage database 2020: multi-cut type, described as high fodder and seed yielding, suitable as dual-purpose -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020
- Review of fodder cowpea breeding: TNFC-0926 by pedigree method, green fodder 252.9 q/ha, dry matter 49.4 q/ha -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/116-Enhancing%20Fodder%20Cowpea%20through%20Breeding%20and%20Omic%20Innovations%20A%20Review.pdf
- TNAU Research Council highlights 2015-2017: TNFC 0926 was identified for release for a northern zone (text truncated) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/49th-Research-Highlights-2015-2017.pdf
- Genetic variability study: TNFC 0926 was among four genotypes judged good prospects for green fodder production -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385083054_Evaluation_of_Genetic_Variability_in_Fodder_Cowpea_for_Enhancing_Yield_and_its_Contributing_Traits
- Same genotype set also reported in an AGRIS record -- https://agris.fao.org/search/en/providers/122436/records/675ac70c0ce2cede71d1386c

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: CO 5 × KBC 2 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/foragecrops_foddercowpea.html and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020
- Breeding line code: TNFC 0926 (the "TNFC" prefix indicates a TNAU forage cowpea culture; the ICAR database gives the name as TNFC-0926).
- Breeding method: pedigree method -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/116-Enhancing%20Fodder%20Cowpea%20through%20Breeding%20and%20Omic%20Innovations%20A%20Review.pdf
- Combining ability study: TNFC0926 clustered with CO(FC) 8 and CO 9 on genetic distance; FD 1052 × TNFC0926 showed heterosis for a trait abbreviated CPR -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384584797_Comprehensive_Analysis_of_Combining_Ability_and_Genetic_Parameters_for_Green_Fodder_Yield_and_Quality_Traits_in_Indian_Cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_L
- No evidence found for QTL, marker or genome-resource studies on TNFC 0926.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by the Department of Forage Crops, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020
- Listed among fodder crop varieties released by the same CPBG forage programme -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/cpbg/forage-crops-technologies-developed/
- No evidence found for the lead breeder's name.

CONTACT DETAILS

- Institute page: https://tnau.ac.in/site/cpbg/forage-crops-technologies-developed/ (no email or phone shown in the snippet)
- No evidence found for an official email or phone number.

PUBLICATIONS

- Authors not shown (year not shown). Evaluation of genetic variability in fodder cowpea for enhancing yield and its contributing traits. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385083054_Evaluation_of_Genetic_Variability_in_Fodder_Cowpea_for_Enhancing_Yield_and_its_Contributing_Traits

- Authors not shown (year not shown). Genotypic variation in fodder cowpea (Vigna unguiculata (L.) Walp.) for adaptability to heat stress. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/397217111_Genotypic_Variation_in_Fodder_Cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_L_Walp_for_Adaptability_to_Heat_Stress_An_Evaluation_of_Growth_Physio-Biochemical_Traits_and_Fodder_Quality

- ICAR (2020). Database of Forage Crop Varieties 2020. ICAR report -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report or DOI was found for this variety.

- TNAU lists TNFC 0926 among varieties for irrigated sowing in all districts of Tamil Nadu -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/agri_seasonandvarieties_foddercowpea.html
- No evidence found for seed stock, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealers. Seednet was not successfully queried.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Tamil Nadu (irrigated, all districts, June-July sowing) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/foragecrops_foddercowpea.html
- Conflict: the TNAU comparison table says TNFC 0926 was released for the North Eastern Zone of India, and the variety list gives a release year of 2016 (input says 2017). The TNAU research highlights also mention a northern-zone release. The input's "Tamil Nadu" is supported for cultivation, but the zonal release status needs checking against CSC minutes -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/pdf/List%20of%20fodder%20varieties%20&%20its%20special%20features.pdf

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Irrigated winter/Rabi season cultivation in plains of Uttarakhand including Tarai and Bhabar regions for fodder production.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Tolerant to seed shattering, good response to nitrogenous fertilizer on green forage, dry matter and crud protein yields. Suitable for irrigated winter/Rabi cultivation under timely sown conditions.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Obtuse, slightly bent leaves, equilateral panicle, whitish yellow seed, glabrous lemma and no awns.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Adapted to low moisture conditions and moderately tolerant to other edaphic stresses.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to leaf blight, crown rust (P. caronata f. sp. avenae) and loose smut (Ustilago avenae) under field conditions.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Resistant to aphids.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 80:60:40 (N:P:K) : Half of the N at sowing  and rests ½ N at 30-35 days after sowing (DAS). Additional N @ 25 kg/ha after first cut in multi cut (MC) forager oat.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Forage Oat 4 (variety_name; seednet_variety_name "Pant Forage Oat 4 (UPO 10-2)"; crop Oat)

Search note: Four web_search queries were run. Most results were about forage oats in other countries or other products. Only one page names this variety (the ResearchGate "Health benefits of oat" table, which lists "Pant Forage Oat-4"), and it is the source for most findings below. The search did not return the Seednet page, so no evidence here is under the "UPO 10-2" name. The release year is 2020 in that table, not 2021 as in the record.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The searches returned no variety-specific stress data.

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to leaf blight, crown rust, loose smut and aphids, per the table row for Pant Forage Oat-4 (the row text is truncated, so the insect list may be incomplete) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365785271_Health_benefits_of_oat_Avena_sativa_and_nutritional_improvement_through_plant_breeding_interventions

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Quality values listed for this variety in the same table: crude protein 9-11% and in-vitro dry matter digestibility (IVDMD) 58-60% -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365785271_Health_benefits_of_oat_Avena_sativa_and_nutritional_improvement_through_plant_breeding_interventions
No evidence found for multi-location yield trial results, AICRP yield data, or agronomic recommendations specific to this variety. The Nature article on oat cutting and nutrient management (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-28099-y) does not name this variety in the retrieved text.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage (Gopher x Kent)-97-1-1 and breeding method pedigree -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365785271_Health_benefits_of_oat_Avena_sativa_and_nutritional_improvement_through_plant_breeding_interventions
Breeding-line code UPO 10-2 appears only in the supplied record; no search result confirms it.
No evidence found for QTL, marker, or genome-resource studies on this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUAT), Pantnagar -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365785271_Health_benefits_of_oat_Avena_sativa_and_nutritional_improvement_through_plant_breeding_interventions
The GBPUAT press release says the university has developed four forage oat varieties and runs an AICRP on Forage Crops at Pantnagar since 1995, but does not name this variety or its breeders -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/news/28-05-26news1.pdf
No breeder or scientist name found for this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder contact, institute email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for this variety was retrieved. The institution name is GBPUAT, Pantnagar, but no contact details were found for it in the results.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Health benefits of oat (Avena sativa) and nutritional improvement through plant breeding interventions. Journal not shown -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365785271_Health_benefits_of_oat_Avena_sativa_and_nutritional_improvement_through_plant_breeding_interventions
No other peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper naming this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for this variety was returned. Searches returned only unrelated forage-oat seed sellers in the US and elsewhere.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No independent confirmation found. The only source for "lower hills and plain areas of Uttarakhand" is the supplied record. The search results do not state recommended states for this variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: UPO-06-1 / Pant Forage Oat-3 (Oat, Avena sativa)

Name note: The release-minutes name UPO-06-1 appears as "UPO-06-01" in the Frontiers table and as "UPO-06-1" in the seed-demand tables. The Seednet name "Pant Forage Oat-3 (UPO-06-1)" appears in a 2023 Acta Scientific agronomy paper. All findings below refer to this same variety under one or both names. Searches run: 4 (variety, breeder/institute, research, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE:
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to UPO-06-1. The only trait descriptions are general. The oat drought/salt bibliometric review discusses oats in general, not this variety -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11279746/
A sodic-soil nutritional study of oat genotypes lists UPO-212, not UPO-06-1; discarded as a different variety -- https://www.envirobiotechjournals.com/EEC/Vol32JulySupplIssue2026/EEC-18_20260803_101322.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST:
Frontiers (2025) lists UPO-06-01 (2016, GBPUAT) with the feature "resistance to major diseases and pests" and a single-cut type. No pathogen names or screening data are given -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2025.1525422/full

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Nano-urea scheduling trial, Instructional Dairy Farm, Nagla, GBPUAT, Rabi 2021-22. Pant Forage Oat-3 (UPO-06-1) was sown manually on 15 November 2021 at 30 cm row spacing. The trial assessed productivity, profitability and residual fertility of multicut fodder oat -- https://actascientific.com/ASAG/pdf/ASAG-07-1219.pdf
- South Asian J. Agric. Sci. (2023) reports UPO-06-1 and UPO-212 as giving the highest green and dry yields, with a twice-harvest option under 50% basal nitrogen -- https://www.agrijournal.org/article/88/3-2-2-658.pdf
- Germplasm evaluation (38 accessions, PLoS ONE / PMC) classes UPO-06-1 among eight accessions superior for high fresh weight (fodder). Fresh weight per plant for the group ranged from 166 to 197.33 g -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9907803/
- Forage oat variety trial (forageresearch.in, 323-327) uses UPO 06-1 as the "best qualifying" comparator for the newer variety OS 403. It is a comparator in that trial, not a finding about UPO-06-1's own yield -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/323-327.pdf
- Forage oat seed trial (forageresearch.in, 185-191) reports UPO 212 and Kent, not UPO-06-1; no UPO-06-1 data found -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/185-191.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources):
- Parentage: (UPO 201/UPO 211//UPO 201)-56-1-15, pedigree method, GBPUAT -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2025.1525422/xml
- Parent UPO 201 is (Kent/Orbit)-13-2 and parent UPO 211 is (Portal/Kent//Rapida)-6-9-2. These come from the parentage data supplied in the request, not from a search result.
- Germplasm variability study (PLoS ONE / PMC) includes UPO-06-1 in a genotypic-diversity analysis. No marker or QTL results specific to it were found -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0280450
- QTL, marker, or genome-resource results for UPO-06-1: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- Developing institution: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUAT), Pantnagar, per the variety tables -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2025.1525422/xml
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. The breeder search returned seed-demand tables and unrelated oat programmes (Minnesota, Illinois, South Australia), which were discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS:
- Institute name only: GBPUAT, Pantnagar. No email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for the institute or the oat breeding division was found in the results. No evidence found for breeder contacts.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2025). Oat varietal listing with UPO-06-01 (2016, GBPUAT, pedigree method). Frontiers in Plant Science -- https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2025.1525422
- Saklani, S.; Pal, M. S. (2023). Effect of nano urea scheduling on productivity, profitability and residual fertility of multi cut oat (Avena sativa L.). Acta Scientific Agriculture, 7(1) -- https://actascientific.com/ASAG/pdf/ASAG-07-1219.pdf
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2023). Oat varieties UPO-06-1 and UPO-212 under nitrogen management. South Asian Journal of Agricultural Sciences, 3(2): 17-20 -- https://www.agrijournal.org/article/88/3-2-2-658.pdf
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown; PMC-indexed, likely 2023). Agro-morphological and genetic variability analysis in oat germplasms with special emphasis on food and feed. PLoS ONE -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0280450
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2025). Analysis of trends and future projections in fodder oats for quality seed production in India. Frontiers in Plant Science (ResearchGate/PMC copies: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12009856/) -- https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2025.1525422
- Theses (KrishiKosh): No evidence found. AICRP/ICAR annual reports: No evidence found for UPO-06-1 specifically.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- A fodder-oat seed analysis lists UPO-06-1 from GBPUAT with an allocation of 13.3 q and production of 0.0 q, giving a deficit of 100%. The period is not stated in the retrieved text -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12009856/
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales and private dealer listings: No evidence found. Results from US and other commercial oat sellers were discarded as unrelated.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- The Frontiers table gives the area of adoption as the northwest plains and lower hills of Uttarakhand, not Uttar Pradesh. This conflicts with the "UTTAR PRADESH" entry in the request and should be checked against the CSC/Seednet notification -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2025.1525422/xml

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Mega Sweet (seednet name: Mega Sweet (SPH 1890) (ADV 6681)); crop: Sorghum

Name note: The evidence for the commercial name "Mega Sweet" and code "ADV 6681" comes from retail and seller pages. The code "SPH 1890" appears only in the AICRP sorghum report, so that line refers to SPH 1890. Most Mega Sweet search hits were Australian forage products from Pioneer and Notman, which I discarded as a different product.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. A retail listing describes it as able to "thrive in diverse growing conditions", but that is marketing copy, not test data -- https://www.amazon.in/Sweet-Hybrid-Sorghum-Variety-ADV-6681/dp/B0DVLS6KDV

DISEASE AND PEST
AICRP sorghum report (2018) says SPH 1890 was among the most promising entries for foliar disease resistance at the Deesa centre (refers to SPH 1890) -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip18/reports18/rb/AICRP-Sorghum-Coordinating-Team.pdf
No evidence found for specific pest resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
AICRP sorghum report (2018) lists SPH 1890 as a sweet genotype that maintained higher fresh and dry biomass at flowering at Deesa (refers to SPH 1890). It is also grouped among forage hybrids in the same report, so the category is unclear -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip18/reports18/rb/AICRP-Sorghum-Coordinating-Team.pdf
No evidence found for maturity days, grain or fodder yield in kg/ha, or multi-location yields for this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: the parentage statement (both parents from the UPL/Advanta breeding project at Pune) is supplied in the input record only. No independent source confirmed it.
Breeding method: a retail listing describes it as a hybrid (refers to ADV 6681) -- https://www.amazon.in/Sweet-Hybrid-Sorghum-Variety-ADV-6681/dp/B0DVLS6KDV
Breeding-line codes: no A/B line or restorer identities found for this hybrid. The ResearchGate pedigree database says the SPH prefix means Sorghum Project Hybrid, which is a naming convention only and not evidence about this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: a market-research press release lists Advanta Seeds as part of UPL Limited (refers to ADV 6681 / Mega Sweet by association with the Advanta brand) -- https://www.openpr.com/news/3490058/sweet-sorghum-seed-market-size-2031-report-by-key-players-dupont-advanta-seeds-upl-limited-chromatin-inc
The AICRP report names "UPL Limited, Hyderabad" as a testing participant (refers to SPH hybrids generally, not specifically to SPH 1890) -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip18/reports18/rb/AICRP-Sorghum-Coordinating-Team.pdf
Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found.
Developing station: the input record states Pune, Maharashtra. No independent source confirmed this.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for a breeder, UPL or Advanta email, phone, postal address or contact page for this variety. Institute-level contact: none retrieved. The only institution references are the UPL Limited and Hyderabad mentions above.

PUBLICATIONS
Not stated in retrieved text (2018). Report of the AICRP on Sorghum Coordinating Team 2018. AICRP on Sorghum annual report -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip18/reports18/rb/AICRP-Sorghum-Coordinating-Team.pdf
No peer-reviewed papers, theses or KrishiKosh records for this variety were found in the search. The sweet sorghum papers retrieved (for example, the Queensland biomethane paper) mention "Mega Sweet" only as a feedstock, which is a different product, so they were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Online retail listing for "Mega Sweet ADV 6681" hybrid sweet sorghum seed (1 kg pack) -- https://www.amazon.in/Sweet-Hybrid-Sorghum-Variety-ADV-6681/dp/B0DVLS6KDV
Online listing for "Advanta Mega Sweet ADV 6681 Jowar Seeds" -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-advanta-hybrid-sorghum-mega-sweet-6681-fodder-seeds-online.php
Trader listing for Advanta Mega Sweet forage seed (500 g) offered by Shriram Krishi Udyog, Pune, at a listed price -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/advanta-mega-sweet-forage-2849423881455.html
Retailer listing for Mega Sweet forage seed -- https://www.farmersstop.com/products/mega-sweet-forage-advanta
Listing on KisanShop brand page -- https://www.kisanshop.in/brand/advanta-golden-seeds
No evidence found for NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed sales.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found for official state recommendations or notification. The "All India" entry comes from the input record only.

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION (not a required heading; recorded for completeness)
No evidence found in CSC minutes, the Seednet portal or the Gazette. The Seednet name could not be checked because the portal was not accessible through search.

disease_resistance.summary: Thrips and foliar diseases: the DOGR variety description states the variety is field tolerant to thrips and foliar diseases (the description refers to Bhima Purple by name, not NRCRG-1). Purple blotch: described as moderately susceptible in a Telangana rabi 2018-19 trial (phytojournal source); 10.4% purple blotch incidence reported in the Kolar (Karnataka) thrips and purple blotch screen, with no genotype immune. Virus status: meristem-derived mericlones of Bhima Purple reported 76% virus-free after testing (meristem culture study, short-day garlic cultivars Bhima Omkar and Bhima Purple). Pest and disease resistance rating in release minutes: Not found in searched sources (no CSC minutes retrieved).

pest_resistance.summary: Thrips: conflicting evidence. The DOGR variety description reports field tolerance to thrips, whereas the Kolar (Karnataka) screen placed Bhima Purple in the susceptible thrips group. Both statements are reported as found; no resolution is available from the digest. No other pests: Not found in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: DOGR average yield 6-7 t/ha. Telangana rabi 2018-19 (AINRP on Onion and Garlic, SKLTSHU Hyderabad): 84.64 q/ha. Zonal station trial: 8.65 t/ha (on par with Yamuna Safed-3). Micronutrient trial (zinc, boron, iron sprays): 125.60 q/ha at best treatment (single-season plot study). Organic cultivation trial: 97.2 q/ha reported in one table row, but the row layout is garbled, so the value is unverified.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources as a formal multi-environment stability analysis. Results are from single-season or single-site trials in Telangana, Karnataka-linked screening, Zonal station and plot studies.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended states as listed under adaptation and recommendation data. The input lists adaptation as Zone-III and Zone VI; the digest does not confirm these zones. The Telangana trial describes the variety as well adapted to Telangana conditions. Short-day garlic type per the general garlic review cited.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Purple skin; cloves 16-20 per bulb; clove diameter 1.0-1.2 cm; TSS 33.6 Brix; allicin 2.9 mg/g fresh weight and 9.6 mg/g dry weight; soft-neck tropical type (DOGR). Photoperiod: short-day (SD) type per a general garlic improvement review; variety-specific confirmation not found. A saponin-related biochemical composition statement in the digest was not attributed to this variety by name and was excluded.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Telangana rabi 2018-19, AINRP on Onion and Garlic, SKLTSHU Hyderabad: 84.64 q/ha, with a supporting bulb-weight and cloves-per-bulb table; described as moderately susceptible to purple blotch and well adapted to Telangana. (2) Kolar (Karnataka) thrips and purple blotch screen: placed in the susceptible thrips group; purple blotch incidence 10.4% in the table text; no genotype immune. (3) Organic cultivation trial (rabi, three years, B:C ratio 3.87-3.99): 97.2 q/ha in one garbled row, unverified. (4) Micronutrient trial (zinc, boron, iron sprays): 125.60 q/ha at best treatment, single season. (5) Pre-release or early comparison with Bhima Omkar and Yamuna Safed types at a Zonal station: 8.65 t/ha, on par with Yamuna Safed-3. (6) GA3 with inductive photoperiod trial (bolting and floral induction) using Bhima Purple, Gadag Local and CITH-5: result not stated in digest. (7) Meristem culture and virus testing: 76% virus-free mericlones. (8) In vitro conservation under slow-growth conditions with osmotic agents, with Bhima Omkar. Farmer-level guidance of 24-28 quintals/acre is general guidance, not a trial result.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Field tolerant to thrips and foliar diseases, per the DOGR variety description (Bhima Purple, not NRCRG-1 by name) -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/research/varieties-developed?layout=edit
Telangana rabi 2018-19 trial: described as moderately susceptible to purple blotch and well adapted to Telangana conditions -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020/vol9issue5/PartV/9-5-243-829.pdf
Kolar (Karnataka) thrips and purple blotch screen: Bhima Purple placed in the susceptible thrips group, and purple blotch incidence was reported at 10.4% in the table text, with no genotype immune -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331199294_Reaction_of_garlic_genotypes_to_thrips_and_purple_blotch_in_South_India
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Bhima Purple. Searches returned only generic garlic cultivation pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
Thrips and foliar disease reaction (field tolerant), as above -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/research/varieties-developed?layout=edit
Purple blotch (moderately susceptible in Telangana; 10.4% incidence in Kolar screen), as above -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020/vol9issue5/PartV/9-5-243-829.pdf and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331199294_Reaction_of_garlic_genotypes_to_thrips_and_purple_blotch_in_South_India
Virus status: meristem-derived mericlones of Bhima Purple, with 76% reported virus-free after testing -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324874613_Production_of_virus_free_planting_material_through_meristem_culture_in_short_day_garlic_cultivars_Bhima_Omkar_and_Bhima_Purple
Pest and disease resistance rating in the release minutes: No evidence found (no CSC minutes retrieved).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity 120-135 days; average yield 6-7 t/ha -- https://dogr.icar.gov.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=126&Itemid=178&lang=en
Telangana rabi 2018-19 (AINRP on Onion and Garlic, SKLTSHU Hyderabad): Bhima Purple yielded 84.64 q/ha, with a supporting bulb-weight and cloves-per-bulb table -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020/vol9issue5/PartV/9-5-243-829.pdf
Farmer-level yield guidance of 24-28 quintals/acre -- https://farmer.in/articles/garlic-farming-guide/
Organic cultivation trial (rabi season, three years, B:C ratio 3.87-3.99): one table row reports 97.2 q/ha for Bhima Purple, but the row layout is garbled, so treat as unverified -- https://agriarticles.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/E-06-02-262-987-992.pdf
Micronutrient trial (zinc, boron, iron sprays) on Bhima Purple: reported total yield 125.60 q/ha at the best treatment; the source is a single-season plot study -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2022/vol11issue1/PartD/10-12-337-761.pdf
Pre-release or early field comparison (Bhima Purple, Bhima Omkar, Yamuna Safed types): Bhima Purple recorded 8.65 t/ha in the Zonal station trial where it was on par with Yamuna Safed-3 -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2018/vol7issue3S/PartH/SP-7-3-86-757.pdf
GA3 with inductive photoperiod trial (bolting/floral induction) using Bhima Purple, Gadag Local and CITH-5 -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-07/QRT-DOGR-01.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: No evidence found. Parentage is listed as Unknown in the input and no source gave pedigree.
Breeding-line code NRCRG-1: No evidence found on any retrieved page. The code appears only in the input.
Breeding method: No evidence found for Bhima Purple. The mass-selection method on DOGR's site is attributed to a different onion variety, so it is excluded.
Photoperiod type: short-day (SD) garlic -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/319902256_Present_status_and_future_prospects_of_garlic_Allium_sativum_L_improvement_in_India_with_special_reference_to_long_day_type
Morphology and quality: purple skin, cloves 16-20, clove diameter 1.0-1.2 cm, TSS 33.6 Brix, allicin 2.9 mg/g fresh weight and 9.6 mg/g dry weight, described as soft-neck tropical type -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/research/varieties-developed?layout=edit
Biochemical composition (purple-tinge variety, higher saponin than white types): -- https://www.ifrj.upm.edu.my/30%20(06)%202023/16%20-%20IFRJ22563.R1.pdf (URL as retrieved: http://www.ifrj.upm.edu.my/30%20(06)%202023/16%20-%20IFRJ22563.R1.pdf)
QTL/marker studies, genome sequence or SSR profiling: No evidence found for Bhima Purple. The Heliyon SSR study covers Allium accessions generally and does not name this variety, so it is excluded.
In vitro conservation: Bhima Purple and Bhima Omkar were tested under slow-growth conditions with osmotic agents -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12320307/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (ICAR-DOGR), Rajgurunagar, Pune, Maharashtra -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/research/varieties-developed?layout=edit
Garlic varieties listed as developed by ICAR-DOGR, including Bhima Purple -- https://dogr.icar.gov.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=126&Itemid=178&lang=en
Two garlic varieties (Bhima Omkar and Bhima Purple) credited to DOGR genetic improvement during the review period -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-07/QRT-DOGR-01.pdf
National-level identification: Bhima Purple identified for release at the AINRPOG group meeting at Ooty (TNAU Coimbatore) in 2011 -- https://www.dogr.res.in/images/Vision/Vision2050.pdf
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. No source named the breeder or scientist for Bhima Purple.
Release year 2018 (input): not confirmed. The only dated national-level event found is the 2011 identification noted above.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research, Chandoli, Tal. Khed, Dist. Pune (Maharashtra) 410 505; Rajgurunagar, Pune 410 505 (MS), India -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/research/varieties-developed?layout=edit
Phone: 02135-222026, 02135-222697, 02135-224056 -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/research/varieties-developed?layout=edit
Email (as displayed on the site, with obfuscation decoded): director.dogr@icar.gov.in -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/research/varieties-developed?layout=edit
Email as printed in the extension folder: director.dogr@icar.gov.in; website http://www.dogr.res.in -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356833474_Agri_Business_Incubation_ICAR-DOGR_Pune_extension_folder
Institute contact page: https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/research/varieties-developed?layout=edit (the same site lists the Garlic Agropedia page at https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/component/content/article/garlicagropedia?layout=edit)
Individual breeder or scientist contact: No evidence found. Institute-level contacts above are the only ones available.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Gujarat Garlic-7 (variety_name) / Gujarat Garlic-7 (GG-7: Anand Kesari) (seednet_variety_name), Garlic

Name note: Every relevant hit used "Gujarat Garlic 7 (Anand Kesari)", the AAU page title. The seednet_variety_name ("Gujarat Garlic-7 (GG-7: Anand Kesari)") did not appear in any result, so the evidence below refers to the AAU name. Two discrepancies: the brief gives a 2021 release year, but the AAU page gives 2019 (50th SSSC). The brief's parentage was not verified by any search result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The AAU page describes storage and pest traits only, not abiotic stress. -- http://www.aau.in/gujarat-garlic-7-anand-kesari

DISEASE AND PEST
The AAU profile reports low incidence of thrips compared with check varieties. No disease resistance data found. -- http://www.aau.in/gujarat-garlic-7-anand-kesari

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The AAU profile reports bulb yield of 79 q/ha and says the variety gave 16.00, 11.65, 15.13 and 14.00% higher bulb yield than checks GG 4, GJG 5, GAG 6 and G 282 in Gujarat. It also reports pyruvic acid 80.05 µmol/g, carotenoids 7.75 mg/100 g, TSS 21.82 °Brix, reducing sugar 2.23%, antioxidant activity 0.118%, and storage loss 15.60%. -- http://www.aau.in/gujarat-garlic-7-anand-kesari
Patel, Kotecha and Goswami (AAU, B.A. College of Agriculture, Anand) ran a rabi 2022-23 trial on Anand Kesari with three planting dates (first week Oct, third week Oct, first week Nov) and three spacings (15x10, 15x15, 20x10 cm). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/377435211_Effect_of_planting_time_and_spacing_on_growth_of_garlic_Allium_sativum_L_cv_Anand_Kesari
Maturity days and multi-location yield data for this variety: No evidence found. -- (no URL)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Breeding line code DG 08-11 and the parentage narrative (Dahod collection 2008-09, bulb-to-row, PET 2011-12, SSVT 2012-13, LSVT 2013-14 to 2017-18) come only from the input brief. No search result confirmed them. -- input brief, not a search URL
Parentage, QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found. -- (no URL)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
The AAU variety profile lists Gujarat Garlic 7 (Anand Kesari) as a garlic release of Anand Agricultural University with release year 2019. Breeder names: No evidence found. -- http://www.aau.in/gujarat-garlic-7-anand-kesari
AAU's released-variety list places this garlic entry in the 50th State Seed Sub-Committee (2019) list. -- https://aau.in/variety_released
A third-party listing names Gujarat Garlic 7 (Anand Kesari) among AAU varieties (Other-Institute-29 page). -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-29/
Institution (Main Vegetable Research Station): the MVRS-specific link was not found in results; the AAU page is the only official source. -- http://www.aau.in/gujarat-garlic-7-anand-kesari

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder contact: No evidence found.
Institute contact: No official email, phone or contact-page URL for the AAU Main Vegetable Research Station was found. The only address retrieved is the affiliation in the Patel et al. paper: Department of Horticulture, B.A. College of Agriculture, Anand Agricultural University, Anand, Gujarat, India. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/377435211_Effect_of_planting_time_and_spacing_on_growth_of_garlic_Allium_sativum_L_cv_Anand_Kesari

PUBLICATIONS
Patel K., Kotecha A.V., Goswami P. (year not shown in retrieved text). Effect of planting time and spacing on growth of garlic (Allium sativum L.) cv. Anand Kesari. Journal not identified in retrieved text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/377435211_Effect_of_planting_time_and_spacing_on_growth_of_garlic_Allium_sativum_L_cv_Anand_Kesari
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR report, or peer-reviewed multi-location paper specific to GG-7 was found. Other garlic papers in the results (for example, the Junagadh thermal-indices study on GG-4 and GJG-5) concern other varieties and were excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for GG-7 seed from NSC, the State Seed Corporation, KVKs, AAU seed sales or named dealers. The seed-supplier listings returned were generic garlic seed sellers that do not name this variety, so they were excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
The AAU profile gives the area of release as whole Gujarat. -- http://www.aau.in/gujarat-garlic-7-anand-kesari

Plant height (cm) 30-60 (it may vary as per the altitude), Leaf attitude Semi erect, Leaf shape Partly curved, Leaf cross-section V-shaped, Pseudo stem colour Green with purple trips, Pseudo stem length (cm) 5-9.0, Neck thickness (cm) 1.5 - 2.0, Leaf colour Green, Leaf waxy ness Present, Av. Leaf length (cm) 45-55 (Fourth leaf), Av. Leaf width (cm) 2-3 (Fourth leaf), Av. No. of leaves/plant 8-9, Bulbils position Top, Ability to produce scape Yes, Ability to flower No, Bulb shape Oblate. Bulb type Compact, Bulb colour Creamy - White with purple trip, Bulb size Big, Polar dia(mm) 36-45 (It may vary as per the altitude), Equitorial dia(mm) 38-60 (It may vary as per the altitude), Av. Bulb weight/plant (g) 40-70 (It may vary as per the altitude), Clove skin colour Creamy - White, Clove type Big, Clove skin thickness Thin, Av. Clove length (cm) 2.1-4.0, Av. Clove width (cm) 1-1.9, Clove flesh colour Creamy - White, Av. No. of cloves/bulb 11-15. csc_fields.meeting_title: Minutes of the 28th meeting of Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties for Horticultural Crops
csc_fields.additional_notes: General regulatory guidelines and conditions for consideration of proposals for release and notification of Horticultural crop & variety by the committee:, 1. Sponsoring Institute/organization should ensure that the proposals are submitted in proper format and must have the required documents viz., acknowledgement certificate regarding submission of seed sample with NBPGR, detailed morphological characters of varieties, AICRP data on disease and pests reaction, source of material and pedigree, package of practices of the cultivar, DNA fingerprinting profile, A-4 size coloured photographs on glossy sheet etc., 2. The committee will not consider any proposal for release or notification in case the copy of proposal is not submitted to respective Director/Project Coordinator., 3. The proposals will be submitted through email (cvrc.hort-agri@gov.in). Five signed original hard copies will be submitted to Deputy Commissioner (Quality Control), DAC&FW, Shastri Bhawan, New Delhi for records., 4. Each sponsoring institution/breeder will make of the proposal., 5. ICAR Institutes, SAUs and other organizations should devise a naming system of the name of Institute followed by crop name and then serial number of variety. Proposals with names of family members, gods and goddesses will not be accepted., 6. Any proposal with more than five years old data will not be considered by the committee., Meeting closure note: The meeting ended with a vote of thanks to the Chair.

seednet_fields.Parentage: Cross derivative from COGG 923 x VC 6040A
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Tamil Nadu.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics:
Branches : 2-3
Secondaries (No.) : -
Leaves : Dark green leaves, terminal leaflet shape is ovate.
Pods : Dark brown colored pods at maturity and presence of pod pubescence.
Seed Colour : Dull green coloured and drum shaped seed
100-seed weight(g) : 3.5 to 4.0
Protein content (%) : 20.21
Hypocotyl/ stem colour is green. Pubescence present in stem, leaf and pod. Petiole colour is green with purple splashes. Leaf vein colour is purple. Dull green and drum shaped seed
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV) and stem necrosis: The greengram culture COGG 973 recorded resistance reaction to YMV (1.0 grade) and stem necrosis (0%) while the check variety SML 1082 recorded susceptible reaction (9.0 grade) for YMV and stem necrosis (20%) under field condition. 
Root rot: The culture COGG 973 recorded moderate resistance reaction to root rot incidence (13.9%) while the check variety SML 1082 recorded susceptible reaction (62.5%) under field condition.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: The greengram culture COGG 973 recorded less stem fly pest incidence than the check variety namely Co(Gg) 7.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: VBN4 (variety name in CSC minutes and Seednet name "VBN4 (VGG 10-008)"), Green gram (Vigna radiata)

Name note: The sources mostly use "VBN 4" or "VBN4". The Seednet-style code "VGG 10-008" appears only in the Central/State varieties table from dpd.gov.in. Findings below refer to VBN4 unless stated otherwise. Four searches were run. Seednet.gov.in was not reached directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderately resistant to MYMV, leaf crinkle virus and powdery mildew are listed as salient features; the same page gives 65-70 days duration and rainfed/irrigated yields of 916/1251 kg/ha, which conflicts with the 936 kg/ha rainfed figure elsewhere -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Pulses/VBN%20-%204.html
- Drought: no inherent drought-tolerance trait was found for VBN4. A seed-priming study used VBN4 and CO8 under simulated drought (-6 bar) and reported better germination and seedling vigour after nodule-associated probiotic priming. This shows a treatment effect, not a varietal trait -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385845881_Enhancing_plant_resilience_and_drought_stress_in_green_gram_through_seed_priming_with_nodule-associated_plant_probiotics
- Heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to MYMV, ULCV (leaf crinkle) and powdery mildew -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Moderately resistant to MYMV (listed as "Moderately resistance to MYMV") -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/
- Recommended as a resistant variety in a green gram seed-production presentation (listed with VBN6 and VBN7; the same slide notes the virus is seed-borne) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/seed-production-in-green-gram-ppt/249424494
- Caution: a disease review lists "VBN 4" among urdbean (black gram) resistant genotypes. That refers to black gram, so it is discarded -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380395530_Major_Diseases_of_Green_Gram_Black_Gram_and_Their_Integrated_Management_Strategies
- Seed quality under storage: VBN4 seed coated with 4 ml NAPP kept quality for 12 months under ambient storage -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5360

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration 65-70 days, yield 1251 kg/ha irrigated and 936 kg/ha rainfed -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/
- Duration 85-90 days (conflicts with 65-70 days above) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Pulses/VBN%20-%204.html
- Yield 10-11 q/ha and duration 65-70 days in the central list -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Season advice: Adipattam (June-July) in all districts except Kanyakumari and Nilgiris, and summer (Feb-Mar) in several delta and north-east districts -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/04_Greengram.pdf
- Season advice (2019 entry): sowing in September and December is listed for all districts -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/swc/PULSES.pdf
- No multi-location trial data specific to VBN4 was found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: PDM 139 x BB 2664 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/
- Breeding method: Not stated. Pedigree is recorded only as a cross; no line codes beyond VGG 10-008 were found.
- Genome resources: No VBN4-specific marker, QTL or genome study was found. The "PDM 139" hits are a different variety (Samrat) and are discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: National Pulses Research Centre (NPRC), Vamban, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. No breeder name was returned for VBN4.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute page: https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/ (a varieties page, not a contact page)
- Name, role, email, phone, postal address: No evidence found in the retrieved pages.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not confirmed). Seed priming of green gram with nodule-associated plant probiotics (VBN4 and CO8, drought-simulated germination). Plant Science Today -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385845881_Enhancing_plant_resilience_and_drought_stress_in_green_gram_through_seed_priming_with_nodule-associated_plant_probiotics
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not confirmed). Nodule Associated Plant Probiotics on Seed Quality of Greengram (Vigna radiata L.) under Ambient Storage Condition. Legume Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5360
- No AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, or trial paper specifically on VBN4 was found. The KrishiKosh wilt thesis and the PDM 139 papers were discarded because they do not name VBN4.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Certified seed was obtained from NPRC Vamban for the two research studies above. This shows the source, not a sales listing -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385845881_Enhancing_plant_resilience_and_drought_stress_in_green_gram_through_seed_priming_with_nodule-associated_plant_probiotics
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealer listings: No evidence found. Check seednet.gov.in under "VBN4 (VGG 10-008)" and the TNAU/NPRC Vamban seed sales desk.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Tamil Nadu (listed as the state of recommendation) -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Advisory listings of TN districts are given under AGRONOMY AND TRIALS above -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/04_Greengram.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Divya (CSMG-2003-19), Groundnut

Search log: I ran the four planned queries, but my code ran a second batch of four, so 8 web_search calls were made, over the limit of 4. The tool limit was then hit, so I could not run further checks. The results below rely only on the snippets I could read.

Name check: the release-minutes name is "Divya" and the Seednet name is "Divya (CSMG-2003-19)". The DOD evidence below uses the code CSMG-2003-19, which matches both. I could not open the Seednet portal.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page giving drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Divya.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page I could read named Divya with disease or pest resistance data.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The DOD table row has numeric columns (3000 and 49) whose meaning is not labelled in the snippet, so I have not interpreted them as yield or maturity. -- http://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx

GENETICS AND QTL (parentage, breeding-line codes, method, genome resources) -- No evidence found for this variety. The brief parentage given in the task (AMBER x ICG-1697) is not confirmed by any page I retrieved. The CSMG-2003-19 code is the only breeding-line identifier I could match, and it appears on the DOD page. -- http://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Partly confirmed. The DOD listing attributes Divya to "CAUAST, Mainpuri". The task gives the institution as C.S. Azad University of Agriculture & Technology, Kanpur. The DOD entry uses a different location, and I could not resolve it. No breeder name was found. -- http://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone, address or institute contact page for Divya was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The research-oriented searches returned general groundnut review and production-practice papers (ResearchGate pages on genetic enhancement and on improved production practices). I did not see Divya named in the parts I could read, so I have not listed them as Divya publications. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-related search returned the DOD groundnut notification page but no dealer, NSC, SAU or KVK listing for Divya. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Uttar Pradesh. The DOD listing places Divya (CSMG-2003-19), released in 2011, under Uttar Pradesh. -- http://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx
Rajasthan is not confirmed by any page I could read, so I have not recorded it.

Open issues for follow-up:
1. Confirm the institution and station (Kanpur or Mainpuri) against the CSC release minutes.
2. Check the Seednet portal entry for parentage, breeder name and notification details.
3. Look up the parentage and breeder in the AICRP on Groundnut annual reports and KrishiKosh.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The sources use "Jagtial Palli 1 (JGC 2141)" (ResearchGate, IJRA 2025), "JagtialaPalli – 1 (JCG 2141)" (PJTSAU), and "Jagtial Palli 1 / JCG 2141" (ResearchGate table). I treated these as matching both the CSC name "Jagtiala Palli-1" and the Seednet name "Jagtiala Palli-1 (JCG-2141)" because the code and the RARS Jagtial station match. No page used the exact "JCG-2141" spelling. Searches returned no Seednet portal page.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerant to early-season drought; resistant to leaf spots and rust; tolerant to thrips and jassids -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396544544_Improved_production_practices_for_sustainable_groundnut_cultivation_An_Indian_perspective
Same trait list (early drought, leaf spot and rust resistance) repeated in a 2025 IJRA review -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue10/PartF/8-10-40-464.pdf
No evidence found for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
