search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. The name checked was "Kadiri Chitravathi" (the Seednet name; K1719 itself did not appear in any result). A Chittoor drought-prone-area study includes Kadiri Chitravathi as one of ten treatments, but the retrieved text does not report its results separately. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357652040_Performance_of_drought_tolerant_groundnut_variety_in_chittoor_district_of_andhra_pradesh
Godavari zone rabi 2022-23 trial: Kadiri Chitravathi was among ten entries, but the retrieved text reports Kadiri Lepakshi as best, with Kadiri Chitravathi named only as a next-best option where Kadiri Lepakshi is unavailable. No stress-specific data. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388846242_Assessment_of_Yield_and_Economic_Performance_of_Groundnut_Cultivars_in_the_Godavari_Zone_Andhra_Pradesh_India

DISEASE AND PEST
Kadiri Chitravathi is described as tolerant to leaf spot, collar rot, stem rot, virus, root rot, and sucking pests such as aphids and thrips. This is an extension-level claim from a KVK success story, not a screening report. -- https://www.kvkreddipalli-angrau.org/93-success-stories/166-enhancing-farmers-income-through-adoption-of-groundnut-variety-kadiri-chitravathi
The same KVK page says it showed better pest and disease tolerance than Kadiri-6, which suffered leaf miner, Helicoverpa, aphid, leaf spot and leaf curl damage. -- https://www.kvkreddipalli-angrau.org/93-success-stories/166-enhancing-farmers-income-through-adoption-of-groundnut-variety-kadiri-chitravathi
No evidence found for PBND, PSND, TSV, or rust resistance specific to this variety. The Tobacco streak virus study tested Kadiri 7 Bold, which is the parent named in the parentage field, not this variety, so it is not attributed here. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3784909/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Summer-season trial at ARS Kadiri (four varieties by four sowing dates, 2025 publication): Kadiri Chitravathi gave the highest mean pod yield, 2470 kg/ha, on par with Kadiri Amaravathi (2271 kg/ha) and superior to Dheeraj (2071 kg/ha) and Kadiri-6 (1782 kg/ha). -- https://www.agriculturejournal.in/archives/2025/vol7/issue2/7045
Farmer-field demonstration reported by KVK Reddipalli: 33.75 q/ha for Kadiri Chitravathi against 20.5 q/ha for Kadiri-6, with about 49% oil content and suitability for fresh/green pods. Single-farm evidence only. -- https://www.kvkreddipalli-angrau.org/93-success-stories/166-enhancing-farmers-income-through-adoption-of-groundnut-variety-kadiri-chitravathi
KVK table: Kadiri Chitravathi yield 3375 kg/ha, gross returns Rs 1,85,625/ha, cost Rs 63,750/ha, net income Rs 1,21,875/ha, versus Kadiri-6 on the same demonstration. -- https://www.kvkreddipalli-angrau.org/93-success-stories/166-enhancing-farmers-income-through-adoption-of-groundnut-variety-kadiri-chitravathi
Godavari zone rabi 2022-23 (Agricultural College Farm, Rajamahendravaram), ten varieties, randomized block: Kadiri Chitravathi was a treatment entry; results for it are not separately summarized in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/Impact-of-Agroclimatic-Conditions-on-the-Productivity-of-Groundnut-(Arachis-hypogaea-L)-Cultivars-in-the-rabi-Season-under-Godavari-Region-G-Chalapathi-Rao-49.pdf

official_quote.quote: Moderately resistant to collar rot, PSND & PBND

disease_resistance.research_summary: Moderately resistant to collar rot, PSND (peanut stripe necrosis disease) and PBND (peanut bud necrosis disease) per the original CSC/Seednet record (no URL in digest). A KVK success story (extension-level claim, not a screening report) describes the variety as tolerant to leaf spot, collar rot, stem rot, virus and root rot, and says it showed better disease tolerance than Kadiri-6, which suffered leaf miner, Helicoverpa, aphid, leaf spot and leaf curl damage. No evidence found for PBND, PSND, TSV (tobacco streak virus) or rust resistance specific to this variety in the digest. A TSV study tested Kadiri 7 Bold (the named parent), not this variety, and is not attributed here.

pest_resistance.research_summary: Moderately resistant to thrips per the original CSC/Seednet record (no URL in digest). The KVK success story describes the variety as tolerant to sucking pests such as aphids and thrips (extension-level claim) and better tolerant than Kadiri-6 to leaf miner, Helicoverpa and aphid damage. No screening data were found in the digest.

drought.details: No evidence found for RARS-T-1 specifically in the searched sources. The submitted record states tolerance to early-season drought, high proline and high relative water content, and quick regenerative capacity, and describes the variety as suitable for drought-prone groundnut areas. These claims are not confirmed by any source in the evidence digest. The RARS Tirupati pages returned describe other varieties.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. The heat-tolerance QTL paper uses an RIL population from RARS Tirupati, but its parents are not named in the retrieved text, so it is not attributed to RARS-T-1.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: No evidence found for RARS-T-1 in the digest. The ICAR-DGR compendium entry is truncated and gives no resistance data. The DOD table has a resistance line (resistant to leaf spots, tolerant to BND) immediately above the RARS-T-1 entry, but it is headed Uttar Pradesh and is not attributed to RARS-T-1. The submitted record claims tolerance to leaf spots and rust diseases; this is not confirmed by the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for RARS-T-1 in the digest. The submitted record claims tolerance to sucking pests such as thrips and jassids; this is not confirmed by the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: DOD table: pod yield 2500 kg/ha (kharif) and 4000 kg/ha (rabi), with 44% oil. The submitted record gives average yield as Unknown.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: DOD table: suited to kharif and rabi-summer seasons, with bold-seeded pods. Submitted record: suitable for drought-prone groundnut growing areas (not confirmed by the digest).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RARS-T-1 (seednet name: RARS-T-1) / Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea)

Note: The evidence below refers to RARS-T-1 under both the CSC name and the Seednet name, which are identical here. Four searches were run. The release year conflicts across sources (the submitted record says 2010; the DOD and ICAR compendium pages say 2011). The parentage in the submitted record (VEMANA x GIRNAL) is not supported by any source found. One source gives TAG-24 x TG-19.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for RARS-T-1 specifically. The RARS Tirupati pages returned describe other varieties (Dharani, Narayani, Dheeraj, TCGS 1416), not RARS-T-1. -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/varieties/groundnut1.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for RARS-T-1. The ICAR-DGR compendium entry for RARS-T-1 is truncated and gives no resistance data. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
- The DOD characteristics table lists a "resistant to leaf spots and tolerant to BND" trait line immediately before the RARS-T-1 entry, but that line is headed "Uttar Pradesh" and may belong to a different variety, so it is not attributed here. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The DOD table gives RARS-T-1 as released in 2011 by ANGRAU, Tirupati, with pod yield of 2500 kg/ha (kharif) and 4000 kg/ha (rabi), 44% oil, suited to kharif and rabi-summer, with bold-seeded pods. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- A ICRISAT/ICAR review table lists a "RARS-T-1" entry with the pedigree TAG-24 x TG-19, ANGRAU Tirupati, and a seed weight note of 67 g. The meaning of that figure is not stated. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
- A mutation-breeding review lists RARS-T-1 (TG 47) among large-seeded groundnut types. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369817954_Advances_in_Mutation_Breeding_of_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L
- No field-trial or multi-location results for RARS-T-1 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage conflict: the submitted parentage is VEMANA x GIRNAL. The review table gives TAG-24 x TG-19. A separate mutation-breeding review describes a cross of TG 19 with TAG-24 that produced "RARS-T-1 (TG 47)" among three large-seeded varieties, with 115-120 days to maturity. VEMANA x GIRNAL is not supported. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369817954_Advances_in_Mutation_Breeding_of_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
- Breeding-line code: TG 47 is given as an alias for RARS-T-1 in the mutation-breeding review. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369817954_Advances_in_Mutation_Breeding_of_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L
- Breeding method: the sources describe a recombination/hybridization route (TG 19 x TAG-24). Mutation breeding is not stated for RARS-T-1. Parentage source and method are unconfirmed.
- No QTL, marker or genome-resource study naming RARS-T-1 was found. The heat-tolerance QTL paper uses an RIL population from RARS Tirupati, but its parents are not named in the retrieved text, so it is not attributed. -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37287715/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No named breeder or lead scientist for RARS-T-1 was found in any source.
- Institution: ANGRAU, Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Tirupati, which was established in 1979 with a groundnut mandate. -- https://www.angraurabitpt.org/who-are-we
- The DOD table credits ANGRAU, Tirupati as the releasing institution. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact for RARS-T-1 was found. Institute-level contacts only:
- Institute: Regional Agricultural Research Station, S.V. Agricultural College campus, Chandragiri Road, Tirupati - 517502, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, India (the address is listed for an ANGRAU incubator at RARS). -- https://www.angraurabitpt.org/who-are-we
- RARS Tirupati groundnut seed-availability contact: Dr. P. Rajasekhar, +91 9989625209, adr.rarstpt@angrau.ac.in. This appears in a seed-stock list that does not include RARS-T-1; it is an institute-level contact only. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Seed_Production_Targets/balance%20of%20seed%2010.11.22.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper focused on RARS-T-1 was found.
- Items that name RARS-T-1 in a table or list only (authors not shown in the retrieved text):
- Authors not shown (2020/2021?). Genetic Enhancement of Groundnut: Current Status and Future Prospects. ResearchGate review -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Advances in Mutation Breeding of Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369817954_Advances_in_Mutation_Breeding_of_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Notified varieties compendium entry 103 (RARS-T-1). ICAR-DGR, Groundnut: A Crop Profile and Compendium of Notified Varieties of India -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for RARS-T-1 seed. ANGRAU seed-availability lists returned other varieties (Kadiri 6, Kadiri 7, Kadiri 9, Dheeraj, TCGS 1694, K-Lepakshi), not RARS-T-1. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Seed_Availability_in_ANGRAU_as_on_10_01_2022.pdf
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or private dealer listing for RARS-T-1 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Andhra Pradesh: RARS-T-1 appears in the state-wise list of groundnut varieties notified under the Seeds Act (2008-2019) for Andhra Pradesh. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Uttar Pradesh: a recommended-states line appears in the DOD table immediately above RARS-T-1, but its attribution is uncertain (see Disease and Pest). Treat as unverified.
- The submitted record says "Unknown". The Andhra Pradesh listing is the only state supported by the sources found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CO 2 (Lucerne / alfalfa, *Medicago sativa*; variety code TND 1308)

Name check: the CSC name and the Seednet name are both "CO 2". The search results refer to "CO 2" and "Lucerne CO 2" in TNAU and Department of Forage Crops sources. I did not retrieve any Seednet portal page, so no finding below is sourced from Seednet. Four searches were run.

Release discrepancy: the request gives 2015 as the release year. TNAU's 2013 release list and the Crop Production Guide give 2013 as the release year. The Crop Production Guide gives 2015 as the notification year.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Reported tolerance to anthracnose and stem/crown rot, with higher green fodder yield than the check variety Sargodha Lucerne in National Uniform Fodder Yield Trials -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694829_A_high_yielding_Lucerne_variety_CO_2
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence specific to CO 2 was found. The only heat-related text (not suitable for hot and humid areas) appears in a fragment of the CO 2 paper and is listed under AGRONOMY. -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to CO 2.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Anthracnose and stem/crown rot tolerance -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694829_A_high_yielding_Lucerne_variety_CO_2
- No pest-resistance evidence specific to CO 2 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Reported green fodder yield of about 130 t/ha/year, with 14 harvests per year, in a TNAU release summary -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/variety_release_2013.pdf
- Mean green fodder yield of 130.6 t/ha/year in research station and on-farm trials, about 25.9% above CO 1 -- https://www.pashudhanpraharee.com/lucerne-the-queen-of-forage-crops/
- Crop Production Guide (Kudiraimasal) table: green fodder yield 120.6 t/ha (14 harvests) and seed yield 240 kg/ha. The guide lists the variety with its districts -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/10_Lucerne_Kudiraimasal.pdf
- Seed production is done once a year in the summer months. This is recorded for TNLC 12, the line from which CO 2 was released -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694829_A_high_yielding_Lucerne_variety_CO_2
- Crude protein 23.5% versus 20.5% in CO 1 -- https://www.pashudhanpraharee.com/lucerne-the-queen-of-forage-crops/
- Seed yield about 18.2% above CO 1 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694829_A_high_yielding_Lucerne_variety_CO_2
- The CO 2 paper notes it is not suitable for hot and humid areas, and mentions Krishnagiri and Dharmapuri districts -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694829_A_high_yielding_Lucerne_variety_CO_2
- TNAU's 2015 Research Highlights used CO 2 as the check against which TNLC 14 was evaluated, so it is not a CO 2 trial result -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/3.-81st-SWC-Research-Highlights-2015.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: poly-cross derivative involving CO 1 as one of the parents -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694829_A_high_yielding_Lucerne_variety_CO_2
- Breeding-line code: TNLC 12 was developed in the Department of Forage Crops (Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, TNAU) and released as CO 2 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694829_A_high_yielding_Lucerne_variety_CO_2
- Conflicting parentage: the TNAU 2013 release summary describes the variety as a selection from the Thondamuthur local of Coimbatore -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/variety_release_2013.pdf
- Variety code TND 1308 is not linked to CO 2 in any source. The 2015 TNAU Research Highlights describe TND 1308 as a separate mutant (450 Gy) from a mutation breeding programme begun in 2010, evaluated on-farm -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/3.-81st-SWC-Research-Highlights-2015.pdf. The link between TND 1308 and CO 2 is unverified.
- Breeding method: polycross. Genome resources, QTL and marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Authors of the CO 2 release paper: C. Babu, K. Iyanar, K. Velayudham and A. Kalamani -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694829_A_high_yielding_Lucerne_variety_CO_2
- Affiliation: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore-641 003 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694829_A_high_yielding_Lucerne_variety_CO_2
- Developing unit: Department of Forage Crops, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, TNAU, Coimbatore -- https://www.pashudhanpraharee.com/lucerne-the-queen-of-forage-crops/
- Lead breeder designation: not stated in the retrieved sources.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Department of Forage Crops, TNAU, Coimbatore – 641 003 (address as listed) -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/pdf/forage%20varieties.pdf
- Email for the Forage department, as listed in a TNAU Seed Centre availability PDF: forage@tnau.ac.in -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/seed_certification/pdf

agronomic_details.yield: No trial-verified yield. The digest states that the yield figures in the field trial cannot be reliably attributed to Bilasa Kulthi because the retrieved text is garbled. agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location or multi-season results were found beyond the single trial described below.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Supplied record only, not verified: rainfed cultivation in Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Jharkhand and Gujarat; rainfed, low fertility, mid-kharif season. The only verified evidence is the trial conducted in Chhattisgarh at Bilaspur.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 102 To 107Days (supplied variety record; not confirmed by searched sources. Maturity evidence beyond the trial was not found.)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources. The supplied record field reads '0', which carries no usable information. Plant height and branching tables in the trial name Bilasa Kulthi, but the retrieved text is garbled and cannot be reliably attributed.
agronomic_details.field_trials: One trial was found: a post-kharif 2018 field trial at the Instructional Farm, BTC College of Agriculture and Research Station, Bilaspur (IGKV, Raipur). Bilasa Kulthi was compared with Indira Kulthi-1 and Chhattisgarh Kulthi-2 under three sowing dates (14, 20 and 26 September) in a split-plot design with protective irrigation. Plant height, branching and yield-attribute tables name Bilasa Kulthi, but the text is garbled, so no reliable yield or attribute values could be attributed to it. No other trial results were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bilasa Kulthi (variety_name, CSC minutes) / Bilasa Kulthi (BSP 15-1) (seednet_variety_name, Seednet portal)
Crop: Horse gram (Macrotyloma uniflorum), variety code A0306033

Search coverage: Four web_search queries were run: general variety/release, breeder/institution, research papers, and seed availability. The BSP 15-1 name was included in the research query, and no Seednet page was returned. The Seednet portal itself was not reached, so release-notification details could not be checked against it.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned only general horse gram drought-tolerance statements that do not name this variety. Those were discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The only disease-resistance claims returned concern a Karnataka line (BJPL-1) and were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Field trial, post-kharif 2018, Instructional Farm, BTC College of Agriculture and Research Station, Bilaspur, IGKV Raipur: Bilasa Kulthi was compared with Indira Kulthi-1 and Chhattisgarh Kulthi-2 under three sowing dates (14, 20 and 26 September) in a split-plot design with protective irrigation. Plant height, branching and yield-attribute tables name Bilasa Kulthi, but the retrieved text is garbled, so the yield figures cannot be reliably attributed to it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364274181_Effect_of_sowing_dates_and_varieties_on_growth_yield_attributes_and_yields_of_Horsegram_Macrotyloma_uniflorum_Lam_Verdc_under_protective_irrigation
Maturity, yield potential and multi-location results for this variety: No evidence found beyond the trial above.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage and breeding method: No evidence found in search results. The "pure line selection from landrace of Bilaspur district" parentage comes only from the supplied record and was not verified.
Genes, QTL, marker and genome-resource studies: No evidence found for this variety. A 2025 NIRS study of 139 accessions (NBPGR gene bank) does not name Bilasa Kulthi, so it was discarded. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12081650/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution (from the trial record above): IGKV, BTC College of Agriculture and Research Station, Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364274181_Effect_of_sowing_dates_and_varieties_on_growth_yield_attributes_and_yields_of_Horsegram_Macrotyloma_uniflorum_Lam_Verdc_under_protective_irrigation
Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. The breeder query returned no page naming a breeder for this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder contact, institute-level contact, email, phone or address for BTC College of Agriculture and Research Station, Bilaspur, was retrieved. No IGKV contact page was returned by the searches.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). "Effect of sowing dates and varieties on growth, yield attributes and yields of Horsegram [Macrotyloma uniflorum (Lam.) Verdc.] under protective irrigation." Journal/Report not shown in retrieved text (trial conducted post-kharif 2018) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364274181_Effect_of_sowing_dates_and_varieties_on_growth_yield_attributes_and_yields_of_Horsegram_Macrotyloma_uniflorum_Lam_Verdc_under_protective_irrigation
KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR annual reports and other conference papers naming this variety: No evidence found.
Discarded as not about this variety: the Chhattisgarh horse gram review by Ramteke et al. (does not name Bilasa Kulthi in the retrieved text), the Birsa Kulthi biomass study (Jharkhand), and the Karnataka BJPL-1 paper.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed-seller results were generic horse gram listings (Pioneer Agro Industry, Deodar Seeds, Amazon and others) with no mention of Bilasa Kulthi, BSP 15-1, NSC, the Chhattisgarh State Seed Corporation, a KVK, or the SAU seed unit. These were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Chhattisgarh: taken from the supplied variety record only. The search results did not independently confirm the notification or recommendation. The trial above was conducted in Chhattisgarh at IGKV's Bilaspur station. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364274181_Effect_of_sowing_dates_and_varieties_on_growth_yield_attributes_and_yields_of_Horsegram_Macrotyloma_uniflorum_Lam_Verdc_under_protective_irrigation

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CRIDAHARSHA (CRHG-19), Horse gram (Macrotyloma uniflorum)

Name note: "variety_name" (CSC) is CRIDAHARSHA. "seednet_variety_name" is CRIDAHARSHA (CRHG 19). The sources use "Cridaharsha (Crhg-19)", "CRIDA Harsha", and "CRHG-19", so each finding below refers to that same entry. Searches returned many CRIDA 18R, CRHG-22, AK-42/Pratap Kulthi-1 and Nature mutant-study results. These concern other varieties and were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Title describes CRIDAHARSHA (Crhg-19) as a high-yielding, drought-tolerant, brown-seeded horse gram variety for South India (Reddy et al., 2018) -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vegapareddy-Maruthi
- Heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found for this variety. Searches returned only generic horse gram tolerance statements.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. Generic horse gram breeding goals (leaf spot, anthracnose) appeared in a crop overview but were not tied to CRHG-19 -- https://www.croptrust.org/knowledge-hub/crops/crop/horse-gram/ (discarded as not variety-specific)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- CRHG-19 is used as a reference check in a 150-landrace trait-variability study, with trait-table values listed against it (plant height, number of primary branches, days to maturity, etc.). These are check values, not a yield trial of the variety -- https://ispgr.nbpgr.ernet.in/Archive/IJPGR_Vol_38_1_2025.pdf
- CRHG-19 is also a reference check in a diversity study of Indian horse gram landraces -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10675608/
- Yield (kg/ha), maturity days, and multi-location trial results for CRIDAHARSHA: No evidence found. The 2018 paper's abstract was not retrievable in full; the only snippet is a review listing its title.
- Agronomy findings for CRIDA 18R and CRHG-22 were excluded.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage "derivative of AK-42 via gamma-ray mutation" (from the supplied record): No evidence found in any search result. This is unverified.
- Breeding-line code CRHG-19 and variety code "CRHG - 19" are confirmed only as names in titles and checks, not as pedigree -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vegapareddy-Maruthi
- QTL, marker, or genome resource studies naming CRHG-19: No evidence found.
- The AK-42-derived variety found in search is Pratap Kulthi-1 (Gujarat), a different variety; discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Dr. M. Maheswari is credited with contributing to development of CRHG-22 and CRHG-19 (CRIDA Harsha), released in South Indian states. She was Director (Acting), Principal Scientist and Head of Division of Crop Sciences at ICAR-CRIDA, superannuated 31 Dec 2020 -- https://www.satishserial.com/book/9789390425563/physiological-interventions-for-developing-climate-resilient-cereals-fodder-crops
- Authors of the 2018 CRIDAHARSHA paper: P. Raghuram Reddy, K. Salini, Vegapareddy Maruthi, Kotha Sammi Reddy. Their roles in breeding are not stated in the sources -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vegapareddy-Maruthi
- Developing institution: ICAR-Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (CRIDA), Hyderabad. The institute is under ICAR and was formed in 1985 as a project directorate -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Research_Institute_for_Dryland_Agriculture ; station-level detail: No evidence found beyond Hyderabad.
- Lead breeder of record (CSC/Seednet): Not confirmed by any source.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute page (ICAR-CRIDA): https://www.icar-crida.res.in/Research_Institute.html . No official email, phone, or postal address for CRIDA or its crop-sciences division appeared in the results.
- Breeder-level contacts for P. Raghuram Reddy, K. Salini, V. Maruthi, or K. Sammi Reddy: No evidence found.
- Dr. M. Maheswari: no contact details found

seednet_fields.Parentage: 014A x AN 268. 014A was developed from the selection from IR69616A, which was procured from Barwale Foundation, Hyderabad, 2006. An 268 was developed from a local land race katari Bhog which was collected in 2005.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Gangetic Alluvial zones of West Bengal Irrigated, Transplanted
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: PAN 802 is resistant to lodging and shattering.  This hybrid is fertilizer responsive i.e. with increase in fertilizer dose there is an increment of seed yield.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: The culm attitude of PAN 802 is semi-erect, the stem length of the main axis (excluding Panicle) is short.  The panicle length is very long (>30cm).  It has well exerted panicle and its grain length is long and decorticated grain shape is long slender (LS).
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: PAN 802 (IET 23498) showed resistance to Grain Discolouration (GD) and Sheath Rot (ShR) and moderately resistant to Sheath blight, BLB and Blast when tested at Burdwan district.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: PAN 802 (IET 23498) showed tolerance to Stem Borer (SB) and Leaf Folder (LF) in both Kharif and Boro Season when tested under natural field condition in Burdwan, West Bengal.
seednet_fields.Average Yield (Kg/Ha): Kharif:- 6.5 to 7 t/ha Boro:- 7.5 to 8 t/ha Kg/Ha

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RH 0119 (variety_name "RH 0119"; seednet_variety_name "RH0119"; crop "Mustard / rapeseed")

Name note: the DOD page and the AICRP/research pages use "RH 0119" or "RH-119". No retrieved page used "RH0119" or the Seednet crop label, so the Seednet portal itself was not reached. The DOD listing places this variety under Indian mustard (Brassica juncea), not under yellow sarson as the Seednet record states. This crop mismatch is unresolved.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- DOD lists RH 0119 (Indian mustard section) with a "thermo-tolerant" trait, released in Haryana, with a year column reading 2012 and a second column reading 2009/2010; the column headers are not shown, so the 2010 release year in the record is not confirmed -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Rapeseed.aspx
- No drought, salinity, flood, submergence or heat-trial data specific to RH 0119 were found beyond the "thermo-tolerant" label -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Rapeseed.aspx

DISEASE AND PEST:
- The 2020 AICRP report lists RH 0119 as a base population parent in a white rust resistance crossing programme; this shows use in breeding, not that the variety itself is resistant -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
- No disease or pest resistance rating for RH 0119 was found -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- A plant-density study included "RH-119" as one of five mustard varieties (FRBD, replicated thrice); the retrieved text does not isolate RH-119's own yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/271515452_Performance_of_Rapeseed_and_Mustard_Varieties_Grown_Under_Different_Plant_Density
- DOD gives a yield range of 1047-2156 kg/ha and oil content of 38.5-39.8% for RH 0119 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Rapeseed.aspx
- Maturity: No evidence found -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Rapeseed.aspx
- Multi-location trial results for RH 0119 itself: No evidence found; the 2025 AICRP proceedings contain an entry "RH 2452" with pedigree RH 0119 x IC-491013 (CCS HAU Hisar), which is a different variety and is not attributed to RH 0119 -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2025/AICRP-Proceeding-2025.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources):
- Parentage PUSA BOLD x RAJAT (PCR 7) given in the record: No evidence found in retrieved pages -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Rapeseed.aspx
- Breeding use: RH 0119 is cited as a parent of RH 2452 (pedigree method) in the 2025 AICRP entry -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2025/AICRP-Proceeding-2025.pdf
- Breeding use: RH 0119 is listed among base populations for white rust crossing (fresh crosses) -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
- Breeding-line codes, QTL, markers, genome resources for RH 0119: No evidence found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279554671_Hundred_years_of_rapeseed-mustard_breeding_in_India_Accomplishments_and_future_strategies

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- Developing institution: Haryana (state listing only); the DOD table does not name a releasing centre for RH 0119 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Rapeseed.aspx
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279554671_Hundred_years_of_rapeseed-mustard_breeding_in_India_Accomplishments_and_future_strategies
- The developmental history paper lists RH 0119 among hybridisation-derived varieties (breeder seed demand, 2005-06 to 2009-10) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279554671_Hundred_years_of_rapeseed-mustard_breeding_in_India_Accomplishments_and_future_strategies

CONTACT DETAILS:
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.
- Institute contact: No email, phone or postal address was present in the retrieved text. The DRMR seed-plant page appeared in results but its content was not checked for contacts -- https://drmr.res.in/seed_plant.php
- Institute contact page for the release centre (Haryana/CCS HAU): not retrieved in this search -- No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (Year not shown). Hundred years of rapeseed-mustard breeding in India: Accomplishments and future strategies. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279554671_Hundred_years_of_rapeseed-mustard_breeding_in_India_Accomplishments_and_future_strategies
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (Year not shown). Performance of Rapeseed and Mustard Varieties Grown Under Different Plant Density (includes "RH-119"). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/271515452_Performance_of_Rapeseed_and_Mustard_Varieties_Grown_Under_Different_Plant_Density
- AICRP on Rapeseed & Mustard (2020). Annual report, breeding section (includes RH 0119 crosses). DRMR, Bharatpur -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
- AICRP on Rapeseed & Mustard (2025). Proceedings (RH 2452 entry, pedigree RH 0119 x IC-491013). DRMR, Bharatpur -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2025/AICRP-Proceeding-2025.pdf
- Theses (KrishiKosh) and peer-reviewed papers specific to RH 0119: No evidence found in the search.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listings for RH 0119: No evidence found.
- National breeder-seed indent data for rapeseed-mustard (not specific to RH 0119) -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- Haryana (DOD listing) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Rapeseed.aspx
- The record's "Unknown" is therefore partly resolved to Haryana; no other state recommendation was found.

drought.details: No evidence found for CS-58 in the searched sources.

heat.details: No evidence found for CS-58. The heat-tolerance result in the digest (CS-52, Proagro, NDR 8801) concerns other genotypes and was excluded.

salinity.details: Recommended for saline soils with an ECe of up to 11.0 dS/m. Under salinity of ECe 9-11 dS/m, irrigation water at 11-12 dS/m and pH 9-9.4, CS 58 gave 25% higher seed yield and 29% higher oil yield per hectare than the check CS54 and the high-yielding varieties Kranti and RH 0749. Reported 2.0-2.2 t/ha seed yield under saline and alkaline conditions. Comparative table lists salinity tolerance at ECe 6-11 dS/m and sodicity tolerance at pH 8.5-9.4, with yield of 2.6-2.8 t/ha in non-stress and 2.0-2.2 t/ha under salt stress. Source record describes the variety as highly salt tolerant, with yield of 20 qtl/ha under salinity (ECe < 9 dS/m, pH up to 9.0) and 24 qtl/ha in normal soils.

flood.details: No evidence found for CS-58 in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Alternaria blight: the source variety record states that CS 1100-1-2-2-3 showed resistance to Alternaria blight under natural conditions compared with checks Rohini, YSB-9, RTM-314 and CS 54, with pod AB severity at par with checks. This is not corroborated by the digest's searched sources, and the code CS 1100-1-2-2-3 was not found in any search result, so the attribution to CS-58 is unconfirmed. Newsletter: a disease profile covering mildew, downy mildew, stag head and sclerotinia stem rot is reported against checks Rohini, YSB-9, RTM-314 and CS 54. The snippet is fragmentary, and whether each disease was resistant or merely scored is unclear. No other named-pathogen resistance evidence found for CS-58.

pest_resistance.summary: Mustard aphid: the CSSRI newsletter reports a very low mustard aphid infestation index compared with checks Rohini, YSB-9, RTM-314 and CS 54. The source variety record states that data from 34 trials showed a lesser average aphid infestation index than checks CS 54, Kranti, Rohini and Varuna; this record is not corroborated by the digest's sources and is tied to the unconfirmed code CS 1100-1-2-2-3. No other pest evidence found for CS-58.

agronomic_details.yield: Seed yield of 2001 kg/ha, which is 24-25% above the two checks. Comparative table: 2.6-2.8 t/ha in non-stress and 2.0-2.2 t/ha under salt stress. Source record: 20 qtl/ha under salinity (ECe < 9 dS/m, pH up to 9.0) and 24 qtl/ha in normal soils. Under ECe 9-11 dS/m, seed yield was 25% and oil yield 29% above the check CS54 and the varieties Kranti and RH 0749.
agronomic_details.stability: Outperformed checks over four years for seed and oil yield under moderate to high salinity and alkalinity. Performed better in the All India Salinity Alkalinity Tolerant Variety Trials across salinity and alkalinity sites in Haryana, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to salt-affected soils and timely sown conditions, with sowing recommended up to 25 October. Source record recommends a seed rate of 5 kg/ha and describes the variety as highly responsive to fertilizers. The newsletter also lists Delhi and Rajasthan (North Western Plain Zone) under salt stress and timely sown conditions.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 131 To 138Days (source record). The digest reports 130-135 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height about 180 cm; 6 primary branches; 9 secondary branches; main shoot 85 cm; 1000-seed weight 5.5 g; oil content 39-40%.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Replicated yield trials ran for three years at five locations per year under saline and alkaline soils in Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, under AICRP on Rapeseed-Mustard, against national checks including CS54, RH749 and Kranti. The variety performed better in the All India Salinity Alkalinity Tolerant Variety Trials at salinity and alkalinity sites across Haryana, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh. It outperformed the checks over four years for seed and oil yield under moderate to high salinity and alkalinity. Seed yield of 2001 kg/ha was 24-25% above two checks. Under ECe 9-11 dS/m, seed yield was 25% and oil yield 29% above checks CS54, Kranti and RH 0749. Reported 2.0-2.2 t/ha seed yield under saline and alkaline conditions.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Salinity: CS-58 is recommended for saline soils with an ECe of up to 11.0 dS/m. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338254719_CS58_new_high_yielding_salt_and_alkaline_tolerant_cultivar_of_Indian_mustard
Salinity and alkalinity: under salinity of ECe 9-11 dS/m, irrigation water at 11-12 dS/m and pH 9-9.4, CS 58 gave 25% higher seed yield and 29% higher oil yield per hectare than the check CS54 and the high-yielding varieties Kranti and RH 0749. -- https://krishi.icar.gov.in/Technology/technologyShowCaseReport.jsp?id=201519288807188
Salt-stress seed yield: a 2.0-2.2 t/ha seed yield under saline and alkaline conditions was reported. -- https://cssri.res.in/poxumyse/2018/04/salinity_news_letter_jan-june_2017.pdf
Comparative table (CS 58 column): salinity tolerance ECe 6-11 dS/m, sodicity tolerance pH 8.5-9.4, yield 2.6-2.8 t/ha in non-stress and 2.0-2.2 t/ha under salt stress. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74043
Heat tolerance: No evidence found for CS-58. The heat-tolerance result (CS-52, Proagro, NDR 8801) concerns other genotypes and was excluded. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40502-013-0015-1
Flood, submergence, drought: No evidence found for CS-58.

DISEASE AND PEST
Disease and aphid reaction: the CSSRI newsletter reports a disease profile (mildew, downy mildew, stag head, sclerotinia stem rot) and a very low mustard aphid infestation index, compared with checks Rohini, YSB-9, RTM-314 and CS 54. The snippet is fragmentary, so whether each disease was resistant or merely scored is unclear. -- https://cssri.res.in/poxumyse/2018/04/salinity_news_letter_jan-june_2017.pdf
Named-pathogen resistance data beyond this: No evidence found for CS-58.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Plant type: CS 58 reaches about 180 cm height, with 6 primary branches, 9 secondary branches, 85 cm main shoot and 5.5 g 1000-seed weight. -- https://krishi.icar.gov.in/Technology/technologyShowCaseReport.jsp?id=201519288807188
Maturity, oil and sowing: maturity is 130-135 days, oil content 39-40%, and the recommended sowing is up to 25 October. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74043
Seed yield: 2001 kg/ha, which is 24-25% above the two checks. -- https://krishi.icar.gov.in/Technology/technologyShowCaseReport.jsp?id=201519288807188
Multi-location testing: replicated yield trials ran for three years at five locations per year under saline and alkaline soils in Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, under AICRP on Rapeseed-Mustard, against national checks including CS54, RH749 and Kranti. -- https://www.scielo.br/j/cbab/a/y4NfCC6DYFTg9sP784JyWhC/?lang=en
Performance in AISATVT: the variety performed better in the All India Salinity Alkalinity Tolerant Variety Trials at salinity and alkalinity sites across Haryana, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh. -- https://www.scielo.br/j/cbab/a/y4NfCC6DYFTg9sP784JyWhC/?lang=en
Four-year superiority: it outperformed the checks over four years for seed and oil yield under moderate to high salinity and alkalinity. -- https://cssri.res.in/poxumyse/2018/04/salinity_news_letter_jan-june_2017.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: CS 58 was developed by crossing the genotypes CS52 and CS609-B10. -- https://www.scielo.br/j/cbab/a/y4NfCC6DYFTg9sP784JyWhC/?lang=en ; the same parentage appears at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338254719_CS58_new_high_yielding_salt_and_alkaline_tolerant_cultivar_of_Indian_mustard
Breeding method: the CSSRI cultivars in the chapter, including CS 58, were developed by conventional methods, with the bulk method listed as one approach. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74043 (the bulk-method section heading is shown in the same source, but the chapter does not state the method for CS 58 specifically; treat as unconfirmed for this variety)
Breeding-line code: "CS 1100-1-2-2-3" was not found in any search result. No evidence found for this code.
Genome resources, QTL, markers for CS-58: No evidence found. The CS52 transcriptome and lncRNA studies concern the parent CS-52, not CS-58, and were excluded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Summary-of-read-statistics-from-RNA-sequencing-of-B-juncea-var-CS52_fig9_276361686

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developers: P. C. Sharma, Jogendra Singh and D. K. Sharma are named as developers. S. K. Sharma (CCSHAU, Hisar), Y. P. Singh (CSSRI Regional Research Station, Lucknow) and R. B. Singh (AICRP on Sorghum and Wheat, Agra) are named as co-operators. -- https://cssri.res.in/poxumyse/2018/04/salinity_news_letter_jan-june_2017.pdf
Discrepancy: one ResearchGate page lists a "Dinesh Kumar Sharma" at IARI, while the newsletter lists D. K. Sharma as a CSSRI developer. Not resolved. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338254719_CS58_new_high_yielding_salt_and_alkaline_tolerant_cultivar_of_Indian_mustard
Institution: ICAR-Central Soil Salinity Research Institute, Karnal, developed the variety. -- https://krishi.icar.gov.in/Technology/technologyShowCaseReport.jsp?id=201519288807188
Jogendra Singh's profile: Crop Improvement division, CSSRI Karnal, listed as an Indian mustard breeder. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Jogendra-Singh-6

CONTACT DETAILS
Jogendra Singh (lead developer), ICAR-CSSRI, Karnal, Haryana. Email: jogendra.singh@icar.gov.in (listed as the correspondence address on the book chapter, not verified as current). -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74043
Institute postal address (Karnal): ICAR-Central Soil Salinity Research Institute, Karnal-132001, Haryana, India. -- https://www.scielo.br/j/cbab/a/y4NfCC6DYFTg9sP784JyWhC/?lang=en
Regional Research Station (Lucknow) address: ICAR-CSSRI Regional Research Station, Lucknow-226002, Uttar Pradesh, India. -- https://www.scielo.br/j/cbab/a/y4NfCC6DYFTg9sP784JyWhC/?lang=en
Phone, institute website contact page: No evidence found in search results.

PUBLICATIONS
Singh J, Sharma PC, Singh V, Sharma DK, Sharma SK, Singh YP et al. (2019). CS 58: new high yielding, salt and alkaline tolerant cultivar of Indian mustard. Crop Breeding and Applied Biotechnology 19(4): 461-465. -- https://www.scielo.br/j/cbab/a/y4NfCC6DYFTg9sP784JyWhC/?lang=en (author list partial in the SciELO page; reference list in the chapter gives the order above)
Sharma P. C., Singh J. et al. (2017). CS 58: a new salt tolerant high yielding variety of Indian mustard released. Salinity newsletter, Jan-June 2017, CSSRI Karnal. -- https://cssri.res.in/poxumyse/2018/04/salinity_news_letter_jan-june_2017.pdf
Singh J, Sharma PC, Singh V. Breeding Mustard (Brassica juncea) for Salt Tolerance: Problems and Prospects (book chapter, year not shown). -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74043
Dhetarwal S. K. Economic Impact of Salt-tolerant Mustard Varieties (year not shown; the page is a ResearchGate listing). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380288764_Economic_Impact_of_Salt-tolerant_Mustard_Varieties
KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports, peer-reviewed trials (beyond the publications above): No evidence found in the search results.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Seednet portal listing for "CS-58." (seednet name): No evidence found. The search returned only US garden mustard greens sellers (Rare Seeds, Walmart, Everwilde and others), which are unrelated and were excluded.
NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Central notification for salinity-affected mustard areas of Zone II, comprising Haryana, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh, under gazette notification S.O. 1007(E) of 30 March 2017. -- https://krishi.icar.gov.in/Technology/technologyShowCaseReport.jsp?id=201519288807188
Different state list in the newsletter: recommended for Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Delhi and Rajasthan (North Western Plain Zone) under salt stress and timely sown conditions. -- https://cssri.res.in/poxumyse/2018/04/salinity_news_letter_jan-june_2017.pdf (differs from the gazette; both are reported)
Official oilseed list: CS-58 appears in the state-wise notified list for Haryana and Punjab (2008-2019).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CORAL-437 / CORAL-437 (PAC-437) EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: Every page found uses "Coral 437", "Coral-437" or "Coral 437 (PAC 437)" (the last in the justagriculture.in table). The SEEDNET portal page itself was not retrieved, so no finding below is confirmed from seednet.gov.in. Parentage was given only in the input and was not found in any search result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Coral 437 is listed with the trait "WRE resistant" on the DOD page. The page does not define the term, so the stress it refers to is unconfirmed. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence was found for this variety. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Rapeseed.aspx

DISEASE AND PEST
Only the "WRE resistant" entry above was found. No disease or pest evaluation for Coral 437 was found. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Rapeseed.aspx

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
A rabi 2011-12 field trial at the Agronomy Research Farm, N.D. University of Agriculture and Technology, Kumarganj, Faizabad, compared sowing dates and varieties, including Coral-437 against Kranti, Maya and PBR-357. Coral-437 gave higher plant height, siliqua traits, seed and stover yield, and the highest seed yield and oil content came from 25 October sowing. The authors called that sowing the most remunerative for eastern UP. The exact yield values were not legible in the extracted text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320131066_Effect_of_sowing_dates_and_varieties_for_higher_productivity_of_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L
Official variety table: yield potential 1831-2581 kg/ha and oil content 39.2-41.2%. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Rapeseed.aspx

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage PAC 437A x PAC 437R: from input only; not verified by search. -- No evidence found in search results.
Type: hybrid. Cytoplasmic male sterility (CMS) source is listed as Moricandia (PAC 437) in one table, but the Rajya Sabha answer says Ogu CMS. These conflict and are unresolved. -- https://www.justagriculture.in/files/newsletter/2022/february/047.pdf ; https://rsdebate.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/735470/1/PQ_258_16122022_U1122_p122_p123.pdf
Breeding method, breeding-line codes beyond the PAC codes, QTL/marker studies and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Advanta India Limited, Bangalore, per a Government of India parliamentary answer. -- https://rsdebate.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/735470/1/PQ_258_16122022_U1122_p122_p123.pdf
Table listing: Coral 437, B. juncea, 2012, developer Advanta India Ltd. -- https://www.justagriculture.in/files/newsletter/2022/february/047.pdf
Lead breeder name: No evidence found.
Breeding station: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level only: Advanta India Limited, Bangalore (no address, phone or email in the retrieved text). Institute mustard page (no contact details shown): https://dev.advantaseeds.com/in/crops/mustard/ -- this page names Coral PAC 432 and generic hybrids, not Coral 437, so it is cited only as the company's crop page.
Breeder email, phone and postal address: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not stated (year not stated). Effect of sowing dates and varieties for higher productivity of Indian mustard (Brassica juncea L.). Field trial, N.D. University of Agriculture and Technology, Kumarganj, Faizabad, rabi 2011-12 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320131066_Effect_of_sowing_dates_and_varieties_for_higher_productivity_of_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L
KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR annual reports, peer-reviewed papers and QTL studies naming Coral 437: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY (NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales, private dealers)
No evidence found. The searches returned only unrelated retail mustard seed sellers (for example, cover-crop and garden seed).

RECOMMENDED STATES
Delhi and Rajasthan: Coral 437 is listed among notified varieties (2008-2019 seed-act notifications). -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx
Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, J&K and Rajasthan: states listed for Coral 437 on the DOD variety table. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Rapeseed.aspx
Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Chhattisgarh and a Kota region of Rajasthan: stated in the Rajya Sabha answer, but that passage is garbled and may refer to Coral 432 instead. It conflicts with the DOD states and is unresolved. -- https://rsdebate.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/735470/1/PQ_258_16122022_U1122_p122_p123.pdf

RELEASE YEAR DISCREPANCY
Release year is 2012 in the DOD table and in the justagriculture.in table, but 2011 in the Rajya Sabha answer.

EXCLUDED (not about this variety)
Coral PAC 432 pages (Advanta mustard page, the hundred-years breeding review, the DRMR variety page) were excluded because they name a different variety.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: The results showed that the entry BCCC-2 recorded highest yield 29.81q/ha which was not statistically significant with the checks. BCCC-2 showed responsiveness to higher doses of fertilizer and best effect was at 100:21.8:41.7 N:P:K, kg/ha where the highest fibre yield of 31.15q/ha was observed under highest fertilizer dose F3. Although considering all the variety and fertilizer dose interaction was NS.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Large Chocolate brown seed with
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: The proposed variety is adaoted to rainfed situation and comparatively tolerant to biotic stresses like stem rot disease and insect pests like semilooper, BHC and Apion.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: The results revealed that the said variety showed moderately resistance (2.34-4.84%) against stem rot. The result revealted that the proposed variety BCCC-2 showed resistance against stem rot (0.96%).
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: The results revealted that the proposed variety BCCC-2 showed less infestation of apion (4.79-6.15%), semilooper (6.79-41.32%) and BHC (1.47%) as compared to the check variety. The results revealed that the proposed variety BCCC-2 showed less infestation of stem weevil, semilooper, BHC as compared to selected other entires and check variety.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 80:40:40 N, P2O5 and K2O per ha applied as ½ N+full P2O5 and K2O as basal, 1/4N at 35-40DAS and ¼ N at 65-70 DAS

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- The 2008-09 ICAR crop improvement report says Monalisa (RRPS-27-C-3) was notified for midland jute areas with tolerance to foot and stem rot, yellow mite, stem weevil and semilooper, and it attributes drought and waterlogging tolerance to other notified varieties. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/Crop-Improvement-29.pdf
- The AICRP jute variety table gives Monalisa's key traits as pod non-shattering, resistance to premature flowering, better pest and disease resistance, and higher fibre yield with better fineness. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- The same AICRP table has a drought and waterlogging line (drought resistance at early growth, waterlogging tolerance, about 120 days to maturity) that sits between two variety rows, so I cannot confirm it belongs to Monalisa. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- The Directorate of Jute Development table gives the same non-shattering, premature-flowering and pest/disease resistance profile for RRPS-27-C-3 (Monalisa). -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/WhiteJute.aspx

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistance to foot and stem rot, yellow mite, stem weevil and semilooper is reported for Monalisa in the ICAR 2008-09 report. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/Crop-Improvement-29.pdf
- Resistance to major pests and diseases and to premature flowering is listed for Monalisa. -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/WhiteJute.aspx
- No Monalisa-specific seed-treatment or disease-management page was found. The generic jute agronomy slides recommend carbendazim or Trichoderma seed treatment, but they do not name Monalisa. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/advances-in-agronomy-of-jute-corchorus-sp/205801621

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A 2023 pre-kharif coastal South Bengal trial of six white jute varieties reported Monalisa with the shortest plant height (289.1 cm) and the lowest gross return and B:C ratio (1.34), which the authors describe as the least desirable of the six. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390811461_Varietal_Performance_of_Jute_Corchorus_capsularis_L_Based_on_Crop_Growth_and_Yield_in_the_Coastal_Region_of_South_Bengal
- The same trial is also reported in the Renu Publishers PDF, which gives the same Monalisa results. -- https://renupublishers.com/images/article/IJBSv11n2c.pdf
- Recommended sowing is mid-March to mid-April, according to the AICRP table. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- The Directorate of Jute Development gives mid-March sowing as the suitable time. -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/WhiteJute.aspx
- Yield values for Monalisa are not stated in the retrieved text. The AICRP table lists a fibre yield class of 34 for Monalisa but does not give the unit or the basis. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (JRC-321 x NPL/KUC/094C) is not confirmed by any retrieved page. It comes from the input record only.
- The breeding-line code RRPS-27-C-3 is confirmed on several pages. -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/WhiteJute.aspx
- The Bt-jute and tricotyledon papers use JRC-321, which is a different cultivar and was discarded. -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0926669020307901
- No breeding method, QTL, marker or genome-resource evidence was found for Monalisa.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The breeder's name was not found for Monalisa.
- The institution is ICAR-CRIJAF, Barrackpore. The Walsh Medical Media abstract lists Monalisa (RRPS 27-C-3) among the varieties sent to PPV&FR for registration and says CRIJAF developed 14 tossa and 11 white jute varieties. The abstract does not say Monalisa is one of those 11. -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/promising-technologies-of-crijaf-14411.html
- The Walsh abstract also lists Monalisa among the extant varieties selected for PPV&FR registration. -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/promising-technologies-of-crijaf-14411.html
- The AINP jute variety table lists Monalisa with notification details (2009, West Bengal S.O. 2187(E), 27.08.2009). -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: ICAR-Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibres, Nilganj, Barrackpore, Kolkata - 700121, India. The institute page gives this address. The record's postal code of 700 120 does not match the page's 700121. -- http://crijaf.res.in/
- Institute website: http://crijaf.res.in/
- Director: Dr. Gouranga Kar (institute-level contact; not a breeder contact). -- http://crijaf.res.in/
- No official email, phone or breeder contact was found in the retrieved pages.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2023 trial season; year of publication not shown). Varietal Performance of Jute (Corchorus capsularis L.) Based on Crop Growth and Yield in the Coastal Region of South Bengal. Research paper, Renu Publishers PDF (IJBSv11n2c) -- https://renupublishers.com/images/article/IJBSv11n2c.pdf
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (publication date not shown). Varietal Performance of Jute (Corchorus capsularis L.) Based on Crop Growth and Yield in the Coastal Region of South Bengal. ResearchGate PDF (publication 390811461) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390811461_Varietal_Performance_of_Jute_Corchorus_capsularis_L_Based_on_Crop_Growth_and_Yield_in_the_Coastal_Region_of_South_Bengal
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Promising technologies of CRIJAF. Walsh Medical Media proceedings abstract -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/promising-technologies-of-crijaf-14411.html
- ICAR (2008-09). Varieties released by Central and State Variety Release Committees during 2008-09, Crop Improvement report. ICAR -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/Crop-Improvement-29.pdf
- The Walsh and ICAR items are institutional reports, not peer-reviewed papers. No KrishiKosh thesis or ICAR AICRP annual report focused on Monalisa was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: SUDHANGSU (JBO-1), Jute

Name check: the CSC/release-minutes name is "SUDHANGSU" and the Seednet name is "SUDHANGSU(JBO-1)". Sources spell it Sudhangsu, Sudhangshu, or Sudhangsu (JBO 1). Every finding below refers to the variety JBO-1 (Sudhangsu) in jute. Seednet.gov.in was not searched directly, so no Seednet-portal evidence was retrieved.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- JBO 1 (Sudhangshu) is named among varieties tolerant to yellow mite, which the AICRP jute achievements page lists -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
- The same achievements entry for JBO 1 describes tolerance to mealybug, spiral borer, yellow vein mosaic virus (YVM) and stem rot, though the row boundary on the page is unclear -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
- A CRIJAF-derived agronomy slide deck lists JBO 1 under yellow-mite tolerance, but its waterlogging list does not name JBO 1 -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/advances-in-agronomy-of-jute-corchorus-sp/205801621
- A general water-use blog lists JBO 1 (Sudhangsu) among drought-tolerant jute varieties; this is a secondary, non-trial claim -- https://blog.sathguru.com/agribusiness/flowing-forward-enhancing-water-use-efficiency-for-a-sustainable-and-resilient-future/
- Waterlogging/submergence, salinity, flood and heat: No evidence found for JBO-1 specifically. The search returned general jute stress reviews that do not name JBO-1 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8398869/

DISEASE AND PEST
- Yellow mite tolerance (as above) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
- Resistance to major pests and diseases is recorded in the release-table entry for JBO 1 -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- Anthracnose, root rot and stem rot: JBO 1 is not named in the anthracnose or root/stem-rot lists found; those lists name other varieties -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release-table entry: sowing from mid-March to end-April, non-shattering pods, low lignin content, resistance to premature flowering, better fibre quality, and fibre yield of 30-35 q/ha -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- The same achievements entry records fibre strength of 22.78 g/tex and fineness of 3.39 tex (row boundary unclear) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
- In a varietal trial, JBO 1 gave the highest stick and biological yield (78.3 and 108.2 q/ha), ahead of CO 58, JRO 524, NJ 7005 and JROM 1. The trial site is unclear: the title refers to coastal South Bengal, while the abstract text mentions a BJRI Rangpur trial -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390811461_Varietal_Performance_of_Jute_Corchorus_capsularis_L_Based_on_Crop_Growth_and_Yield_in_the_Coastal_Region_of_South_Bengal
- Multi-location trial data, fibre-yield figures from AICRP testing, and seed-production trials for JBO-1: No evidence found for JBO-1 in the retrieved pages. The Budbud seed-stability study names other varieties (S-19, JRO-8432, JRO-524, JRC-517, JBO-2003H, JRC-698, JRO-204) but not JBO-1 -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0926669018308070

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage (JRO-632 x Sudan Green) x Sudan Green: No evidence found. This comes from the user-supplied record and was not confirmed by any retrieved source.
- Breeding-line code: JBO-1 is the variety code given in the record; no breeding-line history was found.
- Combining ability: in a diallel of 90 hybrids and 10 parents, JBO 1 was among the two best general combiners (with JROBA 3) -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11896985/
- Hybrid JROBA 3 x JBO 1 showed an 18% biomass advantage over the national check JRO 204 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11896985/
- Breeding method, QTL, markers and genome resources for JBO-1: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. No retrieved page names a breeder for JBO-1.
- Institution: the release-table entry sits in the AICRP jute (AINP-JAF) release list, and the network's coordinating centre is CRIJAF, Barrackpore -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/ ; https://aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271 (the AAU page states CRIJAF is the coordinating centre)
- Developer per the user record: ICAR-CRIJAF, Barrackpore, Kolkata 700120 (user-supplied; consistent with the AICRP list).

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute postal address: "Barrackpore, Kolkata 700120, INDIA" (ICAR-CRIJAF footer) -- http://www.crijaf.org.in/SideLinks/Research/Varieties.html
- Institute location: Nilganj, Barrackpore, about 6 km from Barrackpore railway station -- https://arch-india.org/institution/central-research-institute-jute-and-allied-fibres
- Institute website: crijaf.icar.gov.in (given on a Wikipedia page; not verified on the official site) -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Research_Institute_for_Jute_and_Allied_Fibers
- Director named on that Wikipedia page: Dr. Gouranga Kar. This is a secondary source and is institute-level only.
- Email and phone: No evidence found for the institute or for a JBO-1 breeder.
- Excluded: Chandan.Kar@icar.gov.in appears on an NFSM "Commercial crop-jute" project record (2014–2017). It is not linked to JBO-1 and was not attributed to this variety -- https://www.indiasc

disease_resistance.research_summary: Stem rot: the user-supplied CSC record reports JBO-1 (1.92%) as resistant with lower stem rot incidence (51.89%) compared with JRO 524. The AICRP achievements page lists JBO 1 as tolerant to stem rot, but the row boundary on the page is unclear. The same entry also lists YVM (yellow vein mosaic virus) tolerance with the same unclear boundary. Root rot: the CSC record gives JBO-1 at 1.92% against JRO 524, with no full comparison stated in the digest. Anthracnose: JBO 1 is not named in the anthracnose lists found. Root rot and stem-rot lists found in the digest name other varieties.

pest_resistance.research_summary: Yellow mite: the CSC record reports JBO (5.9%) as resistant with lower incidence (28.33) compared with JRO-524. The AICRP achievements page and a CRIJAF-derived slide deck both list JBO 1 as yellow-mite tolerant. Semilooper: the CSC record reports JBO-1 (15.19%) with lower incidence (11.80%) compared with JRO-524. Stem weevil: the CSC record reports JBO-1 (10.96%) with lower incidence (8.89%) compared with JRO-524. Mealybug and spiral borer: the AICRP achievements entry lists JBO 1 as tolerant, but the row boundary on the page is unclear. The release-table entry records resistance to major pests and diseases in general terms.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Dahod Kodo 1 (CKMV 3) / seednet name "Dahod Kodo 1 (CKMY 3)" / Kodo millet

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for Dahod Kodo 1 (CKMV 3) or CKMY 3. The only trait text on the Dahod-station kodo pages refers to other varieties (CKMV 2/GAK 3 and CKMV 1), so I have not attributed it. Searched: "Dahod Kodo 1 Kodo millet variety", "Dahod Kodo 1 CKMY 3 Kodo millet research".

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for Dahod Kodo 1 (CKMV 3). The "moderately resistant to head smut" and "resistant to shootfly" statements in the sources belong to other varieties (Dahod Kodo/CKMV 2 and the CKMV 1 line), so they are excluded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383947677_Kodo_Millet_Sowing_Sustainability_for_a_Flourishing_Future ; https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found for Dahod Kodo 1 (CKMV 3). No maturity, yield, or multi-location trial data for this variety was returned. -- https://www.aau.in/college-menu/411/236

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage and breeding method ("pure line selection from locally collected germplasm") were supplied in the task brief. Searches did not confirm this from an independent source. No breeding-line code beyond CKMV 3 and no QTL or marker study specific to this variety was found. The Vikaspedia "CKMV 2" entry (pure line from RK 286) is a different variety and is not used here. -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
Genome-level kodo resources (not specific to this variety): "Genome-wide Population Structure Analyses of Three Minor Millets" -- https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/499087.full.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: ICAR-AICRP on Small Millets / Agricultural Research Station (Hill Millet Research Station), Anand Agricultural University, Muvaliya Farm, Dahod. The AAU station page lists "Dahod Kodo 1 (CKMV 3)" among the station's notified varieties (Released Year 2022, "Notification proposal sended 89th CVRC meeting"). -- https://www.aau.in/college-menu/411/236
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The station page names authors of kodo-millet papers, but none of those papers is tied to CKMV 3, so no breeder is attributed. -- https://www.aau.in/hill-millet-research-station-muvaliya-farm-dahod-2
Release year note: the brief says 2023, but the AAU listing says 2022 (proposal to the 89th CVRC meeting). Treat the year as unconfirmed.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level address only (no breeder contact found): Agricultural Research Station, Anand Agricultural University, Muvaliya Farm, Dahod -389 160, Gujarat. -- https://www.aau.in/college-menu/411/236 ; https://www.aau.in/hill-millet-research-station-muvaliya-farm-dahod-2
Official email: No evidence found. Phone: No evidence found. Institute contact page URL: not located in the search results.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found that names Dahod Kodo 1 (CKMV 3). Items below were excluded on relevance grounds:
- Dalsaniya et al. (2023). Character association and path analysis in kodo millet (Paspalum scrobiculatum L.) with relation to yield and its attributing traits. Not tied to CKMV 3 in the source. -- https://www.aau.in/college-menu/411/236
- Pali et al. (2019). High yielding kodo millet variety 'GAK-3' for cultivation in hilly region of Gujarat. Journal of Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry 8(6): 533-537. This is GAK-3, a different variety. -- https://www.aau.in/college-menu/411/236
- Minutes of the 87th CSC meeting (notification of varieties, including the Dahod Kodo (CKMV 2) entry). Different variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356664896_Minutes_of_the_87_th_meeting_of_Central_Sub-Committee_on_Crop_Standards_Notification_and_Release_of_Varieties_for_Agricultural_Crops_held_through_Video_Conferencing_on_22

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for Dahod Kodo 1 (CKMV 3) or CKMY 3. The Seednet search returned only the Seednet graph page, which is not variety-specific. Justdial lists general seed distributors in Dahod; none is linked to this variety, so none is recorded. -- https://seednet.gov.in/GraphReport/SeedGraph.aspx ; https://www.justdial.com/Dahod/Seed-Distributors/nct-10427150

RECOMMENDED STATES
Brief says: Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu.
Independent source: the IIMR/ICAR-style Kodo chalisa lists "Dahod Kodo 1 (CKMV 3)" under Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh and Andhra Pradesh. The table is garbled in text extraction, and Jharkhand was not seen for this variety. -- https://www.millets.res.in/farmer/2025/Millets_chalisa/English/10Millets_chalisa_Kodo_millet.pdf
The CSC minutes list the state set for Dahod Kodo (CKMV 2), not for CKMV 3, so it is not used. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356664896_Minutes_of_the_87_th_meeting_of_Central_Sub-Committee_on_Crop_Standards_Notification_and_Release_of_Varieties_for_Agricultural_Crops_held_through_Video_Conferencing_on_22

Name mapping: "Dahod Kodo 1 (CKMV 3)" appears in the AAU and chalisa sources. "Dahod Kodo 1 (CKMY 3)" (the Seednet form) did not appear in any result. The variety code CKMY 3 is therefore unconfirmed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kota Masoor 3 (RKL 605-03), Lentil (Lens culinaris)

Name used: "variety_name" is Kota Masoor 3 and "seednet_variety_name" is Kota Masoor 3 (RKL 605-03). The findings below refer to both names, and the sources state the RKL 605-03 code alongside Kota Masoor 3 unless noted. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- DPD Central/State release table lists Kota Masoor 3 (RKL 605-03), released 2020 by Agriculture University Kota, as tolerant to drought and high temperature under rainfed and normal-sown conditions -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- Chapter on abiotic stress-tolerant crop varieties in India lists Kota Masoor 3 (RKL 605-03) among its lentil entries, released 2020 by AU Kota -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/1150022

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. The DPD lentil PDF and the Seednet-style pages returned rust and pod-borer resistance text, but those entries did not clearly attach to Kota Masoor 3, so I have not recorded them. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- DPD table gives the entry's yield as 12-14 q/ha and days to maturity as 86-119 (column alignment in the PDF extract is uncertain) -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- Pharma Journal weed-control study (2023) used Kota Masoor-3 as the test crop. Authors not captured in the search result. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=22194&issue=8&vol=12&year=2023
- MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 project report lists Kota Masoor 3 among new lentil releases -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Not found: multi-location yield data specific to Kota Masoor 3.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (L 4682 x SL 73-3) from the input record: not confirmed by any search result.
- No evidence found for QTL, marker, or genome-resource studies on this variety.
- Discarded: a RKL 58F-3715 (Kota Masoor 4) case study names a different variety, so it is not attributed here -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358894898_Lentil_variety_RKL_58F-3715_Kota_Masoor_4_A_case_study_depicting_emergence_of_desirable_transgressive_segregants_and_recombinants_over_generations

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Agriculture University, Kota, Rajasthan, with the ARS Kota programme. ARS Kota's list of releases includes Koata Masoor 3 (RKL 605-03), year 2019 (CVRC) -- conflicts with 2020 in DPD -- https://www.aukota.org/notifications/21_SSR-Agriculture-University-Kota.pdf
- Kota Masoor 3 appears in an AU Kota state-release notification together with Kota Masoor 1, 2 and 4 -- https://www.aukota.org/notifications/21_SSR-Agriculture-University-Kota.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found for this variety. The breeder named on the Kota Masoor 4 case study is not attributed here -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358894898_Lentil_variety_RKL_58F-3715_Kota_Masoor_4_A_case_study_depicting_emergence_of_desirable_transgressive_segregants_and_recombinants_over_generations
- Institute overview: AU Kota member page -- http://www.iauaindia.org/UniversityDetails.aspx?id=3

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. No email, phone, or postal address for AU Kota or ARS Kota appeared in the search results. Institute page for follow-up: http://www.iauaindia.org/UniversityDetails.aspx?id=3 -- https://www.aukota.org (site root; contact page not retrieved)

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured (2023). Economical weed control in lentil (Lens culinaris Medik. L.). The Pharma Innovation Journal, vol. 12, issue 8 -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=22194&issue=8&vol=12&year=2023
- Discarded: Variability, correlation and path analysis in lentil (2019-20 thesis/study at ARS Ummedganj) and the IJCMAS 2020 paper. Their check varieties are KM-1, KM-2, JL-3, IPL-316 and L-4076, not Kota Masoor 3, so they do not name this variety -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/148eccda-24ef-44ce-8ff1-43d851bb6a48/content

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seednet (NSC/SFC portal): No evidence found.
- Private dealer listings for "Kota 3 Lentil Seed" appeared (Neemuch, MP, at ₹150/kg). These are not confirmed as RKL 605-03 and are treated as unverified -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/kota-3-lentil-seed-2851855695655.html
- KVK, SAU seed-sales, or NSC listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- DPD lists the recommended zone as NWPZ (Rajasthan, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh), rainfed with normal sowing -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- The input record lists MP, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, UP and Rajasthan (a central-zone list). This conflicts with the DPD entry and should be checked against the CSC/gazette notification before finalising. No evidence found in the searches for the CSC release minutes.

disease_resistance.summary: Rust: resistance reported (digest). Rust scores on the 1-9 scale in the variety record: IVT 2017-18 = 2.40; AVT 1 2018-19 = 4.00; AVT 2 2019-20 = 2.25. Stemphylium blight: resistance reported (digest); score 1.00 in IVT 2 2019-20 (variety record). Wilt: moderate resistance reported (digest); wilt percentages in the variety record are IVT 2017-18 = 21.17 (recorded in the source as 21:17), AVT 1 2018-19 = 22.60, AVT 2 2019-20 = 25.35. Ascochyta blight: score 5.00 in IVT 2017-18 (variety record); no resistance statement found in the digest. Digest also describes wilt and rust resistance as durable for commercial cultivation in major lentil-growing areas. Check entries in the variety record for DPL 62, JL 3 and IPL 316 are comparators and are not attributed to this variety here.

pest_resistance.summary: No variety-specific insect pest resistance evidence found in the digest. The digest states that aphid entries in the MULLaRP report refer to other germplasm. The variety record contains pod borer (% pod damage: IVT 2017-18 = 6.33; AVT 1 2018-19 = 2.13; AVT 2 2019-20 = 2.51; mean = 3.66) and aphid (number per 10 cm top shoot: IVT 2017-18 = 0.86; AVT 1 2018-19 = 13.94; AVT 2 2019-20 = 2.39; mean = 5.73) figures, but the digest could not confirm these against its cited sources, so they are not presented as verified resistance. Verification is recommended before use.

agronomic_details.yield: Early maturity of 105 days with mean grain yield of 1876 kg/ha (MULLaRP report). Weighted national mean of 1865 kg/ha, 22.80% superiority over national check DPL 62 (researchgate figure). Mean of 1870 kg/ha under rainfed central Indian conditions (academia.edu). The variety record gives average yield as 23.80 (%) Kg/Ha; the unit is ambiguous and not confirmed by the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Greater yield stability across the zone in coordinated varietal trials, 2017-18 to 2019-20 (slide summary). Weighted mean yield, superiority and frequency table values were not captured.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Bundelkhand region, South-East Parts of Rajasthan; suitable for rainfed conditions and normal recommended seed rate (50 kg/ha) per variety record. The AICRP release table lists it as suitable for normal sowing (10 November).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Breeding line described as medium seed, orange cotyledon, green ground colour, spotted seed coat. The digest also records the IVT entry as large seed; this conflicts with the medium seed description and is not resolved. Other plant characteristics: Unknown.
agronomic_details.field_trials: IVT 2017-18: entered Initial Varietal Trial (large seed) under AICRP on MULLaRP after preliminary and station trials. Rust 2.40, wilt 21.17 (recorded as 21:17). AVT 1 2018-19: rust 4.00, wilt 22.60, pod borer 2.13 percent, aphids 13.94 per 10 cm shoot. AVT 2 2019-20: rust 2.25, wilt 25.35, pod borer 2.51 percent, aphids 2.39 per 10 cm shoot. Coordinated trials 2017-18 to 2019-20 showed greater yield stability across the zone (slide summary). AICRP release table: maturity 110-115 days for RKL 58 F 3715 AU, Kota. Weighted mean yield table values not captured. Additional check comparisons (DPL 62, JL 3, IPL 316, L4076) appear in the variety record but are not attributed to this variety here.
