Wilt: moderate resistance reported (digest); wilt percentages in the variety record are IVT 2017-18 = 21.17 (recorded in the source as 21:17), AVT 1 2018-19 = 22.60, AVT 2 2019-20 = 25.35. Ascochyta blight: score 5.00 in IVT 2017-18 (variety record); no resistance statement found in the digest. Digest also describes wilt and rust resistance as durable for commercial cultivation in major lentil-growing areas. Check entries in the variety record for DPL 62, JL 3 and IPL 316 are comparators and are not attributed to this variety here.

pest_resistance.summary: No variety-specific insect pest resistance evidence found in the digest. The digest states that aphid entries in the MULLaRP report refer to other germplasm. The variety record contains pod borer (% pod damage: IVT 2017-18 = 6.33; AVT 1 2018-19 = 2.13; AVT 2 2019-20 = 2.51; mean = 3.66) and aphid (number per 10 cm top shoot: IVT 2017-18 = 0.86; AVT 1 2018-19 = 13.94; AVT 2 2019-20 = 2.39; mean = 5.73) figures, but the digest could not confirm these against its cited sources, so they are not presented as verified resistance. Verification is recommended before use.

Weighted mean yield table values not captured. Additional check comparisons (DPL 62, JL 3, IPL 316, L4076) appear in the variety record but are not attributed to this variety here.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page that describes drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for RVL 13-7.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page reported disease or pest reaction for RVL 13-7.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The MDPI study lists RVL 13-7 as one of its genotypes, but the retrieved text did not give yield, maturity or trial data for it. -- https://mdpi.com/2071-1050/14/10/5982/htm

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found for parentage. The user-supplied parentage (JL 1 x Black Masra) was not confirmed by any retrieved page. The MDPI study uses RVL 13-7 as a named accession, which supports only that it exists in germplasm studies.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. The retrieved pages did not name a breeder, developing scientist or station for RVL 13-7. The user-supplied institution (RVSKVV, RAK College of Agriculture) was not confirmed.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No institute email, phone, address or contact page was retrieved for RVL 13-7.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown; volume 14, issue 10, article 5982 suggests Sustainability, 2022). Phenotypic Diversity Analysis of Lens culinaris Medik. Accessions for Selection of Superior Genotypes. Sustainability -- https://mdpi.com/2071-1050/14/10/5982/htm
  This paper lists RVL 13-7 as one genotype among several accessions. It is not a study of this variety alone.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-availability search returned a Semantic Scholar PDF (https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/75e3/3468df7418bb09700623121460aab19acbdd.pdf) that mentions other lentil releases, including "Raj Vijay Lentil (Krati)". That is a different variety, so it is discarded under the strict-relevance rule. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for RVL 13-7 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Unverified. The user-supplied value is Madhya Pradesh. The only related hit was a DPD (Directorate of Pulses Development, Bhopal) PDF of central and state lentil releases -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf. The snippet did not show an RVL 13-7 entry, so the state recommendation is not confirmed from the search.

Suggested next steps (manual): Open the DPD PDF and search it for "13-7". Check the MDPI full text for the author list and the RVL 13-7 accession details. Check the RVSKVV (Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya) and RAK College of Agriculture (Sehore) websites, and the ICAR/CSC release notification for the 2019 release. Then query KrishiKosh for theses on RVL 13-7.

drought.details: The digest found no independent evidence for drought tolerance. The original variety data (CSC record, used as ground truth) states the variety is tolerant to moisture stress, but this is not corroborated by any source in the digest and no tolerance level or mechanism is documented. The AICRP release table lists the variety under rainfed conditions, which describes its recommended growing system and does not by itself establish drought tolerance.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance in searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Rust: the original variety data (CSC record) states resistant. The DOD notified-variety table says resistant to rust, while a second DOD listing says moderately resistant to powdery mildew and rust; these sources conflict. Alternaria blight and powdery mildew: the original variety data (CSC record) states moderately resistant. The AICRP page reports resistance to Alternaria blight and powdery mildew, but the span is not clearly tied to this entry, so this is unverified. Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini): the original variety data (CSC record) states moderately susceptible. The digest found LMS-149-4 in a Fusarium wilt genotype list with no visible rating and no link to Mau Azad Alsi-2; this is a weak, unverified lead and does not confirm any wilt rating.

pest_resistance.summary: Linseed bud fly: the original variety data (CSC record) states moderately susceptible. The AICRP page reports resistance to bud fly, but the span is not clearly tied to this entry, so this is unverified. No other pest reactions were found.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield under normal condition is 8.15 q/ha (original variety data, CSC record). A DOD table lists yield potential as 40.17 with an unclear unit (kg/ha or q/ha), and the digest treats this value as unreliable, so it is not used here.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for timely sown rainfed conditions in Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Odisha (original variety data, CSC record). The AICRP release table also lists the variety as rainfed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The AICRP release table lists the variety as rainfed (name: Mau Azad Alsi-2) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
Maturity: early to medium duration (name: Mau Azad Alsi-2) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Linseed.aspx

DISEASE AND PEST -- Conflicting reports on rust: the DOD notified-variety table says "resistant to rust" -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx. A second DOD listing says "moderately resistant to PM & rust" -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Linseed.aspx. The AICRP page reports resistance to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew and bud fly, but the span is not clearly tied to this entry -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/. Wilt: LMS-149-4 appears in a Fusarium wilt genotype list with no visible rating for it, and no page links it to Mau Azad Alsi-2 -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-7-2017/Virendra%20Kumar2,%20et%20al.pdf (weak lead, unverified).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Yield potential is listed as 40.17 in a table with unit ambiguity (kg/ha or q/ha) and oil content as "815 (R)", which looks garbled (name: Mau Azad Alsi-2) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx. Breeder-seed output at the Mauranipur AICRP centre: 7.0 q breeder seed in Rabi 2019-20 -- https://buat.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Part-II.pdf (this is a BUAT annual report, not a trial result). No multi-location trial data for this variety were found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage KL-178 x HIRA: No evidence found. The LMS-149-4 code appears only in the wilt genotype list above (https://www.ijcmas.com/6-7-2017/Virendra%20Kumar2,%20et%20al.pdf). Breeding method, QTL and genome resources: No evidence found. Other genetic-diversity and GCA papers in the search (AFLP, microsatellite, line x tester) concern other genotypes such as Azad Alsi-1 and were discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing centre is C.S. Azad University of Agriculture & Technology (CSAUA&T), Kanpur, with the ICAR-AICRP Linseed unit at Mauranipur (name: Mau Azad Alsi-2) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Linseed.aspx. The university's own page lists Mau Azad Alsi-2 among its developed linseed varieties -- https://csauk.ac.in/some-university-developed-varieties/. Named lead breeder: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. No institute email, phone or postal address for CSAUA&T Kanpur or the Mauranipur AICRP unit was returned. The only institute-level page surfaced is https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/ (no contact information on it). The BUAT report describes the Mauranipur Crop Research Farm as being in the centre of Mauranipur town, but gives no postal address -- https://buat.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Part-II.pdf.

PUBLICATIONS -- Virendra Kumar et al. (2017). Evaluations on Resistance Genotypes against Wilt of Linseed Caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini. Int. J. Curr. Microbiol. App. Sci 6(7): 2004-2016 -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-7-2017/Virendra%20Kumar2,%20et%20al.pdf (weak link: LMS-149-4 appears in the genotype list; Mau Azad Alsi-2 is not named). No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report chapter, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI specific to Mau Azad Alsi-2 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Breeder seed of Mau Azad Alsi-2 (700 kg) was harvested against a DAC indent of 650 kg -- https://buat.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Part-II.pdf. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sale or dealer listing was found. The Seednet portal (name: Mau Azad Alsi-2 (LMS - 149-4)) was not returned by any search. Results for "Alsi seed" from Amazon, eBay and retail sites were discarded as generic flax/linseed products.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Per the DOD notified-variety table (name: Mau Azad Alsi-2, release 2011): Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Odisha -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx. Per the AICRP release table (listed as 2012, rainfed): Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Jharkhand, Orissa, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/. The release year (2011 vs 2012) and the state list (Jharkhand and Andhra Pradesh only in AICRP) disagree between sources. The CSC minutes were not accessed.

disease_resistance.research_summary: Rust: the original variety data (CSC record) states resistant. The DOD notified-variety table says resistant to rust, while a second DOD listing says moderately resistant to powdery mildew and rust; these sources conflict. Alternaria blight and powdery mildew: the original variety data (CSC record) states moderately resistant. The AICRP page reports resistance to Alternaria blight and powdery mildew, but the span is not clearly tied to this entry, so this is unverified. Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini): the original variety data (CSC record) states moderately susceptible. The digest found LMS-149-4 in a Fusarium wilt genotype list with no visible rating and no link to Mau Azad Alsi-2; this is a weak, unverified lead and does not confirm any wilt rating.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance. The only management context is that Surya was developed for irrigated conditions (CSAU variety list).

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Rust: highly resistant (DOD). Surya is also named among rust-resistant linseed varieties, and the source states that growing resistant varieties is the only practical rust control. Wilt: moderately resistant (DOD; CSAU variety list notes wilt resistance). Alternaria blight and powdery mildew: Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Bud fly: moderately resistant (CSAU variety list). A bud fly screening study includes LCK-1404 among tested entries, but its results for this genotype are not visible in the snippet, so it is not counted as evidence. No other pest evidence found.

agronomic_details.yield: DOD lists a yield potential of 35.49 (units as printed, Kg/ha), which is inconsistent with the other figures and is not interpreted here. CSAU reports a yield potential of 2270 kg/ha under best field conditions for zone I (irrigated), with oil yield of about 500 kg/ha. The task input record gives an average yield of 1431 kg/ha, which is not confirmed by the digest sources.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: Developed for zone I (irrigated conditions) per CSAU, covering Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana and Jammu. DOD lists recommended states as Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Haryana.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not found in searched sources (the task input record lists 155-172 days from sowing to harvesting, average 166 days, but no searched source confirmed this)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Bushy habit and brown seed; high omega-3 fatty acid content (62.34%) (CSAU variety list). DOD notes oil content of "1431 (I)" as printed, which is unclear and not interpreted.
agronomic_details.field_trials: CSAU reports a yield potential of 2270 kg/ha under best field conditions with oil yield of about 500 kg/ha (zone I, irrigated). DOD lists yield potential 35.49 (units as printed). No multi-location trial data specific to Surya was found. The bud fly screening trial includes LCK-1404, but its results are not visible in the snippet.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SURYA (LCK-1404) LINSEED: EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC minutes name ("Surya") and the Seednet name ("Surya (LCK-1404)") were not separately confirmed. The DOD page lists the variety as "Surya (LCK-1404)," so the findings below refer to that name and code. Seednet itself was not reachable through search, so no Seednet-specific evidence is recorded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- DOD lists Surya (LCK-1404) as highly resistant to rust and moderately resistant to wilt. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- CSAU's variety list describes Surya as moderately resistant to bud fly, with a note on wilt resistance. -- https://csauk.ac.in/some-university-developed-varieties/
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The only management context is that Surya was developed for irrigated conditions. -- https://csauk.ac.in/some-university-developed-varieties/

DISEASE AND PEST
- Surya is named among rust-resistant linseed varieties, and the page says growing resistant varieties is the only practical control for rust. -- https://www.plantsdiseases.com/p/diseases-of-linseed.html
- Surya is listed as highly resistant to rust and moderately resistant to wilt. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Surya is listed as moderately resistant to bud fly. -- https://csauk.ac.in/some-university-developed-varieties/
- A bud fly screening trial includes the genotype LCK-1404 among tested entries, but its results for LCK-1404 are not visible in the snippet. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376046405_Effect_of_Sowing_Dates_and_Preliminary_Screening_of_Linseed_Genotypes_for_Bud_Fly_Infestation

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- DOD lists a yield potential of 35.49 (units as printed, "Kg/ha"), oil content of "1431 (I)" as printed, and release in 2019 from Kanpur. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- CSAU reports a yield potential of 2270 kg/ha under best field conditions, with oil yield of about 500 kg/ha, for zone I (irrigated). -- https://csauk.ac.in/some-university-developed-varieties/
- CSAU reports high omega-3 fatty acid content (62.34%) and a bushy habit with brown seed. -- https://csauk.ac.in/some-university-developed-varieties/
- No evidence found for maturity duration or multi-location trial data specific to Surya. -- searched in queries 1 and 3

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage SHUBHRA x H-25 was supplied in the task record only. No search result confirmed it. -- no URL (task input)
- Breeding-line code LCK-1404 is the variety code used in the DOD, CSAU and ICAR records. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- No evidence found for breeding method, QTL, markers or genome resources specific to Surya. -- searched in query 3

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Released by the AICRP on Linseed centre at Kanpur, under C.S. Azad University of Agriculture and Technology (CSAUA&T). -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Surya is described as developed for zone I (Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana and Jammu) by CSAU. -- https://csauk.ac.in/some-university-developed-varieties/
- An ICAR-IIOR table lists Nalini Tewari as the Linseed Breeder at CSAUA&T Kanpur, and Karam Hussain as Centre Incharge. The page does not link either person to Surya, so this is institution-level context only. -- https://iior.icar.gov.in/linseed
- No evidence found naming a breeder specifically for Surya. -- searched in query 2

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institution: C.S. Azad University of Agriculture and Technology (CSAUA&T), Agricultural College Lane, Nawabganj, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh 208002. -- https://csauk.ac.in/seeds/
- Linseed Project Coordinating Unit (ICAR), CSAUA&T Campus, Kanpur-208 002, Uttar Pradesh. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137694
- Nalini Tewari, Linseed Breeder, CSAUA&T, Kanpur (role per ICAR-IIOR table; phone and email not captured, the mobile number is truncated in the snippet). -- https://iior.icar.gov.in/linseed
- Karam Hussain, Centre Incharge, CSAUA&T, Kanpur (phone not captured). -- https://iior.icar.gov.in/linseed
- Departmental contact, Genetics and Plant Breeding (not confirmed as linseed contact): Prof. Vijay Kumar Yadav, Professor and Head, phone 0512-2534130, email vkyadav [at] csauk [dot] ac [dot] in. -- https://www.indiacustomercare.com/c-s-azad-university-agriculture-technology-csauat-no (third-party directory, unverified)
- Some university listing gives 0512-2533963 and 0512-2533953; the entry is a bank listing on a third-party directory, so not verified as a university line. -- https://www.indiacustomercare.com/c-s-azad-university-agriculture-technology-csauat-no

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not visible (2018). Cabinet/ICAR document recording LCK 1404 (Linseed) as identified for release. ICAR Cabinet minutes, September 2018. -- http://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-06/September_Cab_2018.pdf
- Authors not visible (year not visible). Effect of Sowing Dates and Preliminary Screening of Linseed Genotypes for Bud Fly Infestation (includes LCK-1404 among screened genotypes). ResearchGate preprint. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376046405_Effect_of_Sowing_Dates_and_Preliminary_Screening_of_Linseed_Genotypes_for_Bud_Fly_Infestation
- Authors not visible (undated). Oilseed Crops, Unit 8 (study material listing Surya (LCK-1404) among improved linseed varieties). eGyanKosh. -- https://egyankosh.ac.in/bitstream/123456789/88363/1/Unit-8.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report or KrishiKosh thesis specific to Surya was found. Query 3 returned unrelated linseed and medical papers, which were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- CSAU lists "Linseed Variety Surya & Aparna" as available from its seed programme, Kanpur. -- https://csauk.ac.in/seeds/
- No evidence found for State Seed Corporation, KVK or private dealer listings for Surya. The Surya Seeds company and Surya Food Products results are different businesses and were discarded. -- searched in query 4

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Haryana. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Zone I for irrigated conditions (Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana and Jammu). -- https://csauk.ac.in/some-university-developed-varieties/

drought.details: No evidence found in the four searches for drought tolerance of DKC 9081. The CSC record gives a stress reaction of tolerance to stresses indicated by stable performance across Zone III, but it does not name a specific stress. A 2014 Motilal Oswal report describes the variety as bred for rabi conditions in Bihar and suited to fertile soils with assured irrigation. This describes the production environment, not a measured drought tolerance mechanism.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance in the searched sources. The CSC record's general stress tolerance statement (stable performance across Zone III) does not name heat.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in the searched sources. Cyclone performance is recorded separately and is not a flood measure: the 2014 Motilal Oswal report says DKC 9081 did well after launch, while naming other Monsanto hybrids that failed to withstand a cyclone in Andhra Pradesh. The report does not state that DKC 9081 failed.

disease_resistance.summary: CSC release record (input data, no source URL in digest): tolerant to MLB (maydis leaf blight), PFSR and rust. No rated disease reaction of DKC 9081 was found in an official or trial source in the digest. Seller listings describe the hybrid as disease resistant without naming diseases; this is a generic marketing claim and is not used as evidence. The AICRP benchmarking disease-resistance row belongs to CoH(M) 9 and is excluded. Field evidence: at RPCAU Pusa (rabi 2024-25), DKC 9081 was the test variety in a nano-fertilizer study, and the best treatment kept turcicum leaf blight severity to 18.20%. This is a treatment outcome in one trial, not a resistance rating of the variety.

pest_resistance.summary: CSC release record (input data, no source URL in digest): tolerant to stalk borer. No independent trial or official source in the digest confirms this rating.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: average yield under normal conditions 9098 kg/ha. IIMR cultivar list and AICRP benchmarking document: 9.1 t/ha for DKC 9081 (MON 29). Bihar farmer anecdote (second season): about 39 quintals per acre; this is an unverified anecdote, not a trial result.
agronomic_details.stability: CSC record: tolerant to stresses as indicated by stable performance across Zone III. Responsive to fertilizer at medium and high application levels (CSC record). No multi-environment trial data found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rabi season (CSC record). Bred for rabi conditions in Bihar and suited to fertile soils with assured irrigation (2014 Motilal Oswal report). IIMR list records rabi, normal. AICRP benchmarking places it in the medium-maturity group (115-130 days in rabi). Field trials reported in Assam (AAU Jorhat), Delhi (IARI), Bihar (RPCAU Pusa) and Gujarat (NDDB Anand); no ranking of these environments is available in the digest.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Morphological characteristics: Unknown (CSC record). Lodging: tolerant to lodging according to the CSC record; seller pages claim strong stalks that resist lodging, which is an unverified marketing claim. Other plant characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AAU Jorhat, Assam, rabi 2021-22, sowing date study: 15 October sowing gave the highest grain yield, 5106.25 kg/ha, the most cobs per plant (1.57) and the heaviest cobs (201.8 g). (2) IARI New Delhi, 2021-22, zero-till weed control: several pre- and post-emergence herbicide sequences were tested; pyroxasulfone followed by tembotrione, or by topramezone, gave the best weed control. (3) RPCAU Pusa, Bihar, rabi 2024-25, nano-fertilizer and turcicum leaf blight: DKC 9081 was the test variety; the best treatment kept leaf blight severity to 18.20%. (4) Palpa, Nepal, 16 on-farm sites: the hybrid was compared with an open-pollinated variety across four nitrogen rates; the digest reports the design but no yield results. (5) NDDB Anand, Gujarat, fodder silage study across 15 cultivars: DKC-9081 had the highest crude fibre (20.21%) and the lowest dry matter (34.20%); study run under central Gujarat conditions. (6) Duration: IARI zero-till weed study gives 150-155 days; seller pages give 160-170 days; the sources disagree. (7) AICRP benchmarking and IIMR list: yield of 9.1 t/ha (see yield field).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
DKC 9081 EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC release name is "DKC 9081". The Seednet name is "DKC 9081 (MON 29)". The IIMR cultivar list and the AICRP benchmarking document use the Seednet form, so their evidence refers to this variety. Seller pages use "Dekalb 9081" or "DKC9081", and I kept them only where they name this hybrid. Four searches were run: variety, breeder/institute, research, and seed availability with contact.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found. The four searches returned nothing on these traits for this variety.
- Irrigated fertile fields: A 2014 Motilal Oswal initiation report describes DKC 9081 as bred for rabi conditions in Bihar and suited to fertile soils with assured irrigation. -- https://bsmedia.business-standard.com/_media/bs/data/market-reports/equity-brokertips/2014-04/13984202370.01286100.pdf
- Cyclone performance: The same report says DKC 9081 did well after launch, but it names other Monsanto hybrids that failed to withstand a cyclone in Andhra Pradesh. It does not say DKC 9081 failed. -- https://bsmedia.business-standard.com/_media/bs/data/market-reports/equity-brokertips/2014-04/13984202370.01286100.pdf
- Lodging: Seller pages claim strong stalks that resist lodging. These are unverified marketing claims. -- https://agribegri.com/products/bayer-dekalb-dkc-9081-makka-seeds.php

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for a rated reaction of DKC 9081 to specific diseases or pests in an official or trial source.
- Seller listings describe the hybrid as disease resistant without naming diseases. This is a generic marketing claim. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/dkc-9081-maize-seeds-2850787690112.html
- The AICRP benchmarking document has a disease-resistance row, but it belongs to a different hybrid (CoH(M) 9), so I did not attribute it to DKC 9081. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield potential: The IIMR cultivar list and the AICRP benchmarking document both give a yield of 9.1 t/ha for DKC 9081 (MON 29). -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/cultivars-2/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Maturity: The benchmarking document lists it in the medium-maturity group, which it describes as 115–130 days in rabi. The IIMR list says rabi, normal. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Duration: An IARI zero-till weed study gives 150–155 days. Seller pages give 160–170 days. The sources disagree. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329121975_Herbicide_options_for_effective_weed_management_in_zero-till_maize ; https://agribiz.farm/product/dekalb-dkc-9081/
- Sowing date, Assam: At AAU Jorhat (rabi 2021–22), the 15 October sowing gave the highest grain yield of 5106.25 kg/ha. It also gave the most cobs per plant (1.57) and the heaviest cobs (201.8 g). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390271671_Growth_Performance_of_Maize_Zea_Mays_L_under_Different_Micro-Climatic_Regimes
- Weed control, IARI New Delhi (2021–22): Several pre- and post-emergence herbicide sequences were tested on DKC 9081 in zero-till maize. Pyroxasulfone followed by tembotrione, or by topramezone, gave the best weed control. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329121975_Herbicide_options_for_effective_weed_management_in_zero-till_maize
- Nano-fertilizer and leaf blight, RPCAU Pusa (rabi 2024–25): DKC 9081 was the test variety. The best treatment kept turcicum leaf blight severity to 18.20%. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353034094_Effect_of_IFFCO_Nanofertilizer_on_Growth_Grain_Yield_and_Managing_Turcicum_Leaf_Blight_Disease_in_Maize
- Nitrogen response, Nepal: At 16 on-farm sites in Palpa, the hybrid was compared with an open-pollinated variety across four nitrogen rates. -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0378429015001379
- Fodder quality, Gujarat (NDDB Anand): Among 15 cultivars, DKC-9081 had the highest crude fibre (20.21%) and the lowest dry matter (34.20%) in the silage data. The study was run under central Gujarat conditions. -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/159-166.pdf
- Farmer report, Bihar: One farmer reported about 39 quintals per acre from DKC 9081 in its second season. This is an anecdote, not a trial. -- https://bsmedia.business-standard.com/_media/bs/data/market-reports/equity-brokertips/2014-04/13984202370.01286100.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage "FEMALE 1 x FEMALE 2/MALE 1": Supplied in the input record only. No search source confirmed it.
- Variety code MON 29: Confirmed by the IIMR list and the AICRP benchmarking document. This is a commercial code, not a documented breeding-line code. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/cultivars-2/
- Breeding method, inbred lines, QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found.
- Excluded: Results for MON810, DKC6575, DKC6666, and the MON 95379, MON 87419 and MON 87429 events are other GM products, so I did not use them.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing company: Monsanto India Limited, Bangalore, which is a private developer. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/cultivars-2/
- Testing route: DKC 9081 was tested through the AICRP maize system and listed in the IIMR cultivar notification table. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.
- Station: The company's seven breeding stations are mentioned, but no station is linked to DKC 9081. -- https://bsmedia.business-standard.com/_media/bs/data/market-reports/equity-brokertips/2014-04/13984202370.01286100.pdf
- Excluded: Atul Mehra is an equity analyst (Motilal Oswal), not a breeder or contact for the variety.

CONTACT DETAILS

- Official email: No evidence found.

drought.details: Not found in searched sources. The digest found no drought evidence specific to KMH-25K45. The 2017 Kaveri annual report drought-resistance quote refers to a different hybrid, KMH 25K55, and has been excluded. The CSC record lists drought tolerance as a stress reaction, but the digest has no independent evidence for it.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. No heat tolerance evidence specific to this variety.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. No salinity tolerance evidence specific to this variety.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. No flood tolerance evidence specific to this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: A benchmarking table lists KMH-25K45 (2700) (Bumper) as resistant to MLB, PR, TLB and CR. The source does not expand these abbreviations, and the table is garbled, so row alignment is uncertain. Treat this as low-confidence evidence. The CSC record separately lists resistance to common rust and tolerance to TLB and PFSR; the digest does not independently confirm these.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest-resistance evidence found for this variety in searched sources. The CSC record lists moderate tolerance to Chilo partellus, but the digest does not confirm this.

agronomic_details.yield: The CSC record gives 5-7 qt per acre (kg/ha). In the garbled benchmarking table, yield values of 7.8 t/ha and 5.8 t/ha appear in different rows, and they cannot be reliably assigned to this hybrid. A farmer-survey paper (Tamil Nadu, Coimbatore and Tiruppur) lists 7.0-7.6 t/ha, reported by farmers.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location yield data beyond the entries listed; ICAR AICRP maize data show none for this variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: KMH-25K45 (Maize)

Name note: The CSC release-minute name is "KMH-25K45" and the Seednet name is "KMH-25K45 (2700) BUMPER)". The AICRP list has two entries. Entry #97 is "KMH-25K45 (2700) (BUMPER)" with a 30-07-2014 date, matching the 2014 release year. Entry #87 is "KMH-25K45 (BUMPER)" with a 28-01-2015 date. Findings below say which name they refer to. No search result gave parentage, so the parentage in the record is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. The searches returned only a 2017 Kaveri annual report quote about drought resistance, which refers to a different hybrid, KMH 25K55, so I have not attributed it here. -- https://www.bseindia.com/bseplus/annualreport/532899/5328990317.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
KMH-25K45 (2700) (Bumper) is listed as resistant to MLB, PR, TLB, CR in a benchmarking table; the abbreviations are not expanded in the source, and the table is garbled, so the row alignment is uncertain. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
No pest-resistance evidence found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Benchmarking table, KMH-25K45 (2700) (Bumper), Kaveri Seed Company Ltd.: kernel is orange-yellow and dent; reported yield values in the garbled table are 7.8 t/ha and 5.8 t/ha in different rows, which cannot be reliably assigned. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Maturity is ambiguous across rows: one row reads Late maturity (>95 days in Kharif in plains), while another row reads "Medium maturity (86-95 days in Kharif in plains; 115-130 days in rabi)". The row for this hybrid cannot be confirmed from the text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Farmer-survey paper (Tamil Nadu, Coimbatore and Tiruppur): KMH 25K45 is listed at 95–100 days and 7.0–7.6 t/ha, with the survey describing farmer-reported performance. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387550184_Exploring_the_market_viability_of_hybrid_maize_seeds_in_Coimbatore_and_Tiruppur_districts_of_Tamil_Nadu
- Company claim: the Kaveri 2017 annual report says KMH 25K45 (Bumper) was identified as a national check in the coordinated trials. -- https://www.bseindia.com/bseplus/annualreport/532899/5328990317.pdf
- ICAR AICRP maize data: no multi-location yield data for this variety beyond the entries above. -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/cultivars/

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage "KML-5254 x KML-2286" is from the user-supplied record; no search result confirmed it. -- user-supplied record, not verified
- No QTL, marker, gene or genome-resource evidence found for this variety. The ZmMAPKKK45 disease-resistance paper, the kernel-moisture GWAS paper and the US Corn Belt drought paper were discarded because they do not name this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developer: Kaveri Seed Company Ltd., Andhra Pradesh, listed as a private developer in the AICRP cultivar table. -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/cultivars/
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found in any search result.
- Company breeding stations: the 2025 Kaveri annual report lists maize breeding stations including Hyderabad, Bangalore, Udaipur, Kannauj and Purnea. The source does not link these stations to this variety. -- https://stockdiscovery.s3.amazonaws.com/india/company/4779/3396/AR-25.pdf
- Company profile: KMH-25K45 (Bumper) is listed among Kaveri's maize products. -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/media/corporate-profile/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.
- Kaveri Seed Company official email, phone and postal address: No evidence found. The Kaveri corporate profile page (https://www.kaveriseeds.in/media/corporate-profile/) was returned, but it contained no contact details in the retrieved text.
- Institute-level contact (AICRP maize, which lists this variety): Indian Institute of Maize Research, Pusa Campus, New Delhi 110012. No email or phone found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

PUBLICATIONS
- Kaul, Jyoti; Kumar, Bhupinder; Karjagi, Chikkappa; Yadav, O P (2015). Benchmarking Indian maize varieties. Conference paper, Special meeting on benchmarking agricultural and horticultural crops in India, IIWBR Karnal. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- ICAR Crop Improvement Annual Report 2014-15 lists KMH 25K45 (BUMPER) among released maize hybrids. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2014-15.pdf
- Plant Variety Journal, March 2016, lists KMH-25K45 with registration number REG/2012/294 (Maize). -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvjmarch2016updated.pdf
- No peer-reviewed journal paper or thesis specific to this variety was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY: Ladhowal Quality Maize Hybrid 1 (CSC name) / Ladhowal Quality Maize Hybrid 1 (LQMH 1) (IMHQPM 1530) (Hybrid) (Seednet name). Evidence below refers to LQMH1 / IMHQPM1530 unless a line says otherwise. No retrieved page was a seednet.gov.in record, so no Seednet-specific fields were verified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to LQMH1. The searches returned generic QPM or other-hybrid material only (for example, a Zambian white maize hybrid and an unrelated Pioneer patent), which I discarded. Agrifarming describes the hybrid as responsive to high inputs, which is a management trait, not a stress trait -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-varieties-of-maize-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits

DISEASE AND PEST
One IIMR cultivar-page snippet lists LQMH1 under a disease heading that mentions sheath blight, but the text is fragmented and does not clearly state a resistance rating, so I am not recording a resistance claim. Treat as unverified -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Early single-cross QPM hybrid, kharif season, showing 22.4% grain yield superiority over the best check in Northern Hill Zone across three years of AICRP testing -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150
Yield 7.5-8.0 t/ha; maturity early (about 100 days in NHZ, 80-85 days elsewhere) -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-varieties-of-maize-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
Grain yield 84.8 q/ha and maturity 101 days, listed under the name "IQMH 201 (LQMH 1)" (name discrepancy; the page may be mislabelled) -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/biofortified-maize-varieties-a-nutritious-sustainable-and-profitable-choice-for-farmers/
Two years of AICRP-QPM testing were completed for IMHQPM 1530, after which it was promoted to the final year of testing in the Northern Hill Zone (Zone I); seed was multiplied by hand pollination for those trials -- https://icar-iirr.org/CRP/index.php/ma
Ladhowal Research Farm study, but on hybrid PMH 1, not LQMH1 -- discarded: https://publications.rmsi.in/index.php/rma/article/view/586

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: IML-343-1 x HKI 163 -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150 ; https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-varieties-of-maize-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
Breeding line codes: IML 343-1 and HKI 163 (as above). Designated code IMHQPM 1530 (also LQMH1 in the same sources).
Type: quality protein maize (QPM) -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-varieties-of-maize-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
Endosperm quality: tryptophan 0.75-0.80% and lysine 3.0-3.5% in endosperm protein -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150 (krishijagran reports lysine 3.03% and tryptophan 0.73% in protein for the same hybrid) -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/biofortified-maize-varieties-a-nutritious-sustainable-and-profitable-choice-for-farmers/
Breeding method: a QPM programme at IIMR introgressed opaque-2 into normal inbreds; the page does not name LQMH1 specifically, so this is programme context only -- https://icar-iirr.org/CRP/index.php/ma
Molecular/MAS work on QPM hybrids names IMHQPM 1530 as identified for release; it does not describe this hybrid's markers -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353162208_Molecular_breeding_for_increasing_nutrition_quality_in_maize_recent_progress
Genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR), Ludhiana -- https://niftem.ac.in/newsite/pmfme/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/maizeprocessingwriteup.pdf ; https://icar.org.in/en/icar-iimrs-hybrids-reaching-unreached-strategically-diversifying-seeds-production-site-india-0
Station: Ladhowal Research Farm, Ludhiana (IIMR) -- https://publications.rmsi.in/index.php/rma/article/view/586 (location only; not confirmed as the release station)
Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found in the retrieved pages.
Institute co-location: IIMR PAU Campus, Ludhiana, listed as an affiliation in a 2024 chapatti-quality paper on white maize hybrids (not LQMH1) -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10947182/ (cited for affiliation only)

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research, Ludhiana (Punjab) -- https://niftem.ac.in/newsite/pmfme/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/maizeprocessingwriteup.pdf
Institute website (cultivars page): https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150
Institute news page: https://icar.org.in/en/icar-iimrs-hybrids-reaching-unreached-strategically-diversifying-seeds-production-site-india-0
Official email, phone and postal address: No evidence found in the retrieved pages.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Molecular breeding for increasing nutrition quality in maize: recent progress. Book chapter (ResearchGate) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353162208_Molecular_breeding_for_increasing_nutrition_quality_in_maize_recent_progress
Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Biofortified maize varieties (agripedia article, non-peer-reviewed). Krishi Jagran -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/biofortified-maize-varieties-a-nutritious-sustainable-and-profitable-choice-for-farmers/
No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI specific to LQMH1 was found. The IIMR CRP page (https://icar-iirr.org/CRP/index.php/ma) reports AICRP trial status but is not a formal report.

SEED AVAILABILITY
ICAR-IIMR began branding and selling its own hybrid seed; first consignments of LQMH 1 were dispatched to Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir and West Bengal -- https://icar.org.in/en/icar-iimrs-hybrids-reaching-unreached-strategically-diversifying-seeds-production-site-india-0
A blog reports hybrid seed production for DMRH 1308, DMRH 1301 and LQMH 1 totalling 32,465 quintals over five years (secondary source, not verified) -- https://cornindia.com/blog/hybrid-seed-production-of-maize-how-it-works-in-india/
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings: No evidence found (no fourth search was run).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PINNACLE (MON 25), Maize

Searches run: 4 web_search queries (release/notification, breeder/institute, research papers, seed availability). Both names were searched: "PINNACLE" (CSC minutes name) and "PINNACLE (MON 25)" (Seednet name). No result named this variety together with maize in India.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The release and trait queries returned barley, oilseed rape, blueberry and forage-maize pages, all about other varieties.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The only pest-related hits concerned MON 810 insect-resistant maize in the EU and a five-event stack, which are different GM events, not this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. UK and US "Pinnacle" maize and forage pages (LG Seeds, Hubbards, Matford Arable) are a different variety from a different breeder, so they were discarded. Examples: https://lgseeds.co.uk/product/pinnacle/ and https://www.matford-arable.co.uk/products/maize-seeds/pinnacle/

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
No evidence found. The parentage "FEMALE 1/ MALE" and the code "M ON 25" did not match any page. A Danforth Center "Pinnacle Gazette" page is a newsletter name only and was discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. No breeder or developer of MON 25 was named. The only company identified is the one in the record: Monsanto India Limited (Bangalore), and no page confirmed it as breeder.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. The institute address in the record (Monsanto India Limited, No. 44/2A, Vasant S Business Park, Bellary Road, Hebbal, Bangalore 560092) comes from the input record only, not from a search result. No official email or phone was found.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. One possibly relevant document surfaced: "Maize Hybrid and Composite Varieties Released in India (1961-2010)", https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010. The snippet did not mention PINNACLE or MON 25, so it is not attributed to this variety. It should be checked directly for an entry under either name.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for the Indian variety. The only Indian listings were IndiaMART offers for "Byer DeKalb Pinnacle" single-cross hybrid seed sold by Godamayee Agro Agencies in Aurangabad, Maharashtra (https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/hybrid-maize-seeds-byer-dekalb-pinnacle-single-cross-3-5-kg-bag-26753065162.html). This is a similarly named commercial product from a different brand and company, so it was excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. The record lists Bihar, Orissa, West Bengal and Jharkhand, but no search result confirmed this.

Suggested next steps: check the CSC/AICRP-Maize notification lists for "PINNACLE" or "M ON 25" and the Seednet entry directly, since these web searches did not reach them.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Sankar Makka-5 (variety_name) / Pant Sankar Makka - 5 (PSM-5) (seednet_variety_name), Maize

Name note: No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so no evidence on the Seednet listing was found. Evidence below refers to "Pant Sankar Makka-5" or "PSM-5" as named in GBPUAT and AICRP pages. The 2021 release year and the parentage "CAL 147 x CML 451" are not confirmed by any retrieved source.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
No evidence found for PSM-5. Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety. A GBPUAT drought-tolerance paper turned up, but it does not name PSM-5, so I excluded it. -- No URL (searched in query 1)

DISEASE AND PEST:
No evidence found for PSM-5. Searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for this variety. -- No URL (searched in queries 1 and 3)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
No evidence found for PSM-5. The only performance data retrieved concerns Pant Sankar Makka-1, -2 and -4. Those were developed after testing in multilocation trials for cultivation in Uttarakhand. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/3%20AICRP%20-%20MAIZE.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources):
Breeding-line code: the AICRP Pantnagar centre page lists PSM-5 as a hybrid with code DH291, and says two hybrids (PSM-5 and PSM-6, DH296) were under pipeline of release. -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/pantnagar-uttarakhand/
DH-291 is also described in an AICRP document as one of three medium-maturity hybrids (DH-291, DH-296, DH-300) that an industry buyer graded as top quality, with high starch of about 73%. The document does not explicitly tie DH-291 to the PSM-5 name, so treat that link as unconfirmed. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/3%20AICRP%20-%20MAIZE.pdf
Parentage (CAL 147 x CML 451): No evidence found. Breeding method and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
Developing institution: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture & Technology (GBPUAT), Pantnagar. The GBPUAT list of varieties released from Genetics & Plant Breeding (June 2023) includes "Sankar Makka-5" under maize. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/08.06.2023_Varieties_Released.pdf
Lead breeder: Dr. N. K. Singh, listed as Sr. Maize Breeder at the AICRP Maize Pantnagar centre, which is based at the Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, GBPUAT, Pantnagar. -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/pantnagar-uttarakhand/ ; https://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: YM-9905 (PKVM-SHATAK), Maize

Name note: The CSC-style name YM-9905 and the variant PKVM-SHATAK both appear in the IIMR and AICMIP listings as one entry, so the evidence below refers to that entry. No Seednet page was returned, so the Seednet name is unverified. I ran four searches: variety, breeder, research, and seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The variety-name and PKVM-Shatak searches returned no stress-tolerance data for this variety. -- none returned
- Not attributed here: the AICMIP "Hybrids released from 2000" table lists tolerance traits for other hybrids (e.g., Shalimar KG Maize-1, Vivek Hybrid-5), which are different varieties and were discarded. -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- The PDKV College of Agriculture Nagpur botany/genetics page lists the variety's disease and pest reaction as tolerant to shoot borer and a hairy-caterpillar pest (the text is truncated, so the second pest is only partly legible). -- http://www.pdkvacn.ac.in/botany.htm
- No disease-resistance (e.g., turcicum leaf blight, rust, downy mildew) data for this variety were found. -- none

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration 85–100 days; sowing seasons listed as kharif, rabi and summer; yield 50–55 q/ha; seed white, bold round; starch 60.5%, protein 12.60%, oil 5.45%. -- http://www.pdkvacn.ac.in/botany.htm
- The page also states that the variety out-yielded the Manjari composite and Panchaganga. -- http://www.pdkvacn.ac.in/botany.htm
- Conflict to resolve: the same PDKV page gives 85–100 days duration, while the AICMIP table classes the variety as "Late" maturity. The yield in the IIMR/benchmarking table is 4.8 t/ha, which is below the 50–55 q/ha (5.0–5.5 t/ha) on the PDKV page. -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf ; https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
- Multi-location trial data: No evidence found beyond the KrishiKosh and benchmarking items under PUBLICATIONS. -- none

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage, pedigree, breeding-line codes, breeding method and marker/QTL data: No evidence found for this variety. -- none
- Only indirect evidence: in a KrishiKosh top-cross evaluation of white maize inbreds (NM-series), PKVM-Shatak served as the common tester and check, so it was used as a male parent in test crosses, not described as a parent of its own. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/25c1f3ff-bbd9-49e9-b4ae-d4a7ff07bc31/content

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Released by Dr PDKV (Dr Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth), Nagpur, Public variety, notified 25-03-2011, notification 632(E). -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
- The PDKV page places the breeding work in the College of Agriculture, Nagpur, Botany/Genetics section. It lists M.K. Moon (Associate Professor, Genetics and Plant Breeding) and Dr (Mrs.) Shanti Patil under that section. The page does not explicitly name either as the lead breeder of this variety, so this is unconfirmed. -- http://www.pdkvacn.ac.in/botany.htm
- Lead breeder name for this variety: not confirmed in the evidence.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No email, phone or postal address for the breeder or the division was found in the evidence.
- Institute-level web page (the only contact source found): College of Agriculture, Nagpur, PDKV, http://www.pdkvacn.ac.in/botany.htm. Verify the address and phone on that site before use.
- Breeder-level contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Kaul, J.; Kumar, B.; Karjagi, C.; Yadav, O.P. (year not stated). Benchmarking Indian maize varieties. Conference paper, Indian Institute of Maize Research (AICRP-Maize presentation). Lists YM-9905 (PKVM-Shatak) with Dr PDKV, Nagpur, Kharif, 4.8 t/ha, white semi-flint. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Authors not stated (year not stated). Evaluation of newly developed inbred lines (top-cross evaluation using PKVM-Shatak as the tester/check). KrishiKosh document. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/25c1f3ff-bbd9-49e9-b4ae-d4a7ff07bc31/content
- ICAR-ATARI Pune (2018-19). Details of Annual Progress Report of KVKs during 2018-19, KVK Sakoli. Mentions PKVM-shatak only as an improved maize variety farmers lacked knowledge about. -- https://kvksakoli.pdkv.ac.in/kvksakoli/Reports/APR-2018-19.pdf
- No peer-reviewed papers, DOIs or theses specific to this variety were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No Seednet, NSC, State Seed Corporation, SAU seed-sales or KVK seed-stock records for this variety were found. The Seednet portal was not returned by any search.
- The KVK Sakoli report notes that farmers lacked knowledge of this improved variety, which is relevant to adoption but is not seed-availability data. -- https://kvksakoli.pdkv.ac.in/kvksakoli/Reports/APR-2018-19.pdf
- A private online store listing ("Maize Seeds", Kisan Beej) does not name this variety and was discarded. -- https://store.kheti.farm/index.php?product_id=22610&route=product%2Fproduct

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Maharashtra (kharif), per the IIMR cultivar list and the benchmarking table. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- The IIMR list also gives "Kharif & Rabi" as the season, and the PDKV page lists kharif, rabi and summer sowing. The official notification text for the state recommendation was not found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Ladhowal Baby Corn Hybrid 3 (LBCH 3 / DMRHB 1305), Maize

Search log: 4 web_search queries were run (variety/release, breeder/institute, research, seed availability). Name used: the CSC/release name "Ladhowal Baby Corn Hybrid 3" and the Seednet/IIMR name "LBCH3 (DMRHB1305)" both appear on the IIMR cultivar page. The Seednet portal page itself was not retrieved, so the Seednet name is taken from the IIMR listing and the seednet crop label "Maize (fodder)" is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The IIMR cultivar entry gives no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for LBCH3. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150

DISEASE AND PEST -- The IIMR cultivar entry lists LBCH3 as moderately resistant to turcicum leaf blight, maydis leaf blight and banded leaf and sheath blight under artificial epiphytotic conditions at hot-spot locations. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150
DISEASE AND PEST -- The same entry reports resistance to maydis leaf blight and moderate resistance to Chilo partellus (stem borer). -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The IIMR entry gives de-husked baby corn yield of 1.3 t/ha, early maturity, kharif season, baby corn length of 9.6-11.6 cm, and fodder yield of 17.0-21.0 t/ha in the recommended zone. Trial-level data (sowing, density, multi-location) for this hybrid were not found. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Not found: no peer-reviewed or AICRP trial report naming LBCH3 was retrieved. The Ladhowal farm and Punjab papers returned by search concern other hybrids or general maize work. -- https://publications.rmsi.in/index.php/rma/article/view/586 (discarded as not about LBCH3)

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage: V 373 x HKI 1105 (IIMR cultivar entry). -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150
GENETICS AND QTL -- Hybrid type: single-cross type baby corn hybrid, with the DMRHB 1305 code (IIMR entry; the "DMRHB" prefix is an IIMR code, not explained further). -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150
GENETICS AND QTL -- Breeding method, breeding-line codes beyond V 373 and HKI 1105, QTL/marker studies and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR). Gazette notification S.O. 3482(E) S.N.37, dated 7 October 2020, and year of release 2020 are given in the IIMR entry. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found in any retrieved page.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. Institute-level only: "ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research, Ludhiana-141004, India" appears as an affiliation on a page about another study, not on a contact page; the institute's official email, phone and contact-page URL were not in the retrieved content. -- https://publications.rmsi.in/index.php/rma/article/view/586 (affiliation text only)
CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute website for contact details: https://iimr.icar.gov.in/ (homepage not retrieved; URL is the institute's cultivar page domain).

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, thesis, AICRP report or KrishiKosh record naming LBCH3 or DMRHB 1305 was retrieved. Excluded as name-resemblance or other-variety: the Tribune article on Punjab Baby Corn 3 (PAU, JH 32484) -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/punjab/three-pau-maize-hybrids-set-for-national-release/ ; the Frontiers and PubMed baby corn papers, which concern other hybrids.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or official seed portals. The only seed-related results were unrelated retail listings for generic "baby corn hybrid" seed (e.g., plantorbit.com and trustbasket.com), which are not about LBCH3 and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Meghalaya, Sikkim, Assam, Tripura, Nagaland, Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh (hill and northeastern zone, kharif season). -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150

Caveat: the IIMR excerpt is truncated and the last lines (length, fodder yield, leaf blight/Chilo reaction) follow the LBCH3 heading without a new heading, so they are attributed to LBCH3 with moderate confidence. Verify against the full IIMR page or the Seednet record before citing.

disease_resistance.summary: Plant Disease Research abstract (vol. 26, no. 2): Hishell reported resistant to banded leaf and sheath blight at Dhaulakuan, and resistant to ESR (Exserohilum turcicum, Turcicum leaf blight) at that site. The same abstract reports Hishell and KHB 52 as resistant to ESR, BSDM, MLB and TLB, and moderately susceptible to BSLB. The abstract's year and authors are not shown in the retrieved text. The two statements on banded leaf and sheath blight (resistant versus moderately susceptible to 'BSLB') are not reconciled in the source text and should be checked against the full paper. The CSC record also lists tolerance to Turcicum leaf blight, banded leaf and sheath blight, brown stripe downy mildew, Erwinia stalk rot and common rust, and field tolerance to stalk rot under field and controlled conditions. The digest found no independent evidence for Erwinia stalk rot or common rust. A benchmarking presentation lists Hishell without a separate disease rating in the retrieved text.

pest_resistance.summary: Field tolerance to stalk borer (Chilo partellus) is stated in the CSC record only. The digest found no independent evidence for this claim.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: average yield 6028 kg/ha. The digest contains a yield of 10.12 t/ha, but it is for a glyphosate-tolerant transgenic test entry and is excluded as a different product. No conventional-release yield was found in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: CSC record: medium maturity and high stable yield. The digest contains no multi-environment stability data.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Kharif season (CSC record and IIMR list). Benchmarking presentation: medium maturity, 86-95 days in kharif in plains. Recommended for Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Non-transgenic Hishell under atrazine pre-emergence followed by one hand weeding at 20 DAS recorded 83.63% weed control efficiency in kharif 2009. This is a weed-management result for the conventional entry, not a yield or variety-performance trial. (2) The transgenic glyphosate-tolerant Hishell test entry (10.12 t/ha, 37.15% above the unweeded non-transgenic check) is excluded because the digest identifies it as a separate transgenic test entry rather than the conventional release. (3) CSC record: average yield 6028 kg/ha, with 'high stable yield'. Trial site, season and replication details are not stated in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Hishell (MCH-42), Maize

Name check: The CSC minutes name and the Seednet name are both "Hishell (MCH-42)" in the sources found, so every finding below refers to that name. The IIMR cultivar list gives the variety code as MCH-42. The search returned no source giving the variety code "MCH 42" in the parentage or breeding-line context.

Search coverage: Four searches were run. Search 2 (breeder/developer) returned no page naming a Hishell breeder or institute contact. No separate institute-page search was possible within the search limit.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found on drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance for Hishell. The only stress-related results were a Bayer product page and a weed-control study, neither of which addresses abiotic stress. -- https://www.cropscience.bayer.in/en/improve-yield/seeds-en/xellano-en/xellano-hishell

DISEASE AND PEST
- In a Plant Disease Research abstract (vol. 26, no. 2), Hishell was reported resistant to banded leaf and sheath blight at Dhaulakuan and was among the hybrids resistant to ESR (Exserohilum turcicum) at that site. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/pdr-26-2-abs054
- The same abstract reports Hishell and KHB 52 as resistant to ESR, BSDM, MLB and TLB, and moderately susceptible to BSLB. The year and authors are not shown in the retrieved text.

- Benchmarking presentation: medium maturity, 86-95 days in kharif in plains. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Transgenic Hishell (glyphosate-tolerant test hybrid) under post-emergence glyphosate at 3600 g a.e./ha gave 10.12 t/ha grain yield, 37.15% above the unweeded non-transgenic Hishell check. This is a herbicide-tolerant transgenic test entry, not the conventional release. -- https://www.scirp.org/html/3-2600883_35340.htm
- Non-transgenic Hishell under atrazine pre-emergence followed by one hand weeding at 20 DAS recorded 83.63% weed control efficiency in kharif 2009. -- https://www.scirp.org/html/3-2600883_35340.htm
- Bayer product page: desi-type grains with good test weight, shelling above 80%, and good keeping quality. This is marketing text for Xellano Hishell. -- https://www.cropscience.bayer.in/en/improve-yield/seeds-en/xellano-en/xellano-hishell

- The Monsanto/DeKalb corporate pages retrieved describe other products and corporate history, not Hishell; they are not used here.

CONTACT DETAILS

The benchmarking deck gives a Bangalore address for Monsanto India Limited, but it is attached to IG 8011 (MCH 37), a different hybrid, so it is not used as Hishell contact information.

PUBLICATIONS

disease_resistance.research_summary: Plant Disease Research abstract (vol. 26, no. 2): Hishell reported resistant to banded leaf and sheath blight at Dhaulakuan, and resistant to ESR (Exserohilum turcicum, Turcicum leaf blight) at that site. The same abstract reports Hishell and KHB 52 as resistant to ESR, BSDM, MLB and TLB, and moderately susceptible to BSLB. The abstract's year and authors are not shown in the retrieved text. The two statements on banded leaf and sheath blight (resistant versus moderately susceptible to 'BSLB') are not reconciled in the source text and should be checked against the full paper. The CSC record also lists tolerance to Turcicum leaf blight, banded leaf and sheath blight, brown stripe downy mildew, Erwinia stalk rot and common rust, and field tolerance to stalk rot under field and controlled conditions. The digest found no independent evidence for Erwinia stalk rot or common rust. A benchmarking presentation lists Hishell without a separate disease rating in the retrieved text.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: KDMH-017 (maize)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "KDMH-017", so all evidence below refers to that name. One source writes it "KDMH017" without the hyphen, and that is treated as the same variety. The searches did not reach seednet.gov.in directly, so the Seednet record itself is unverified. Maize was the crop in every query, and non-maize and unrelated pages (DHM-117 maize, Korean KM7 hybrid, USPTO inbred patents, Ghana seed study, Nigerian portal) were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to KDMH-017. The one benchmarking source places it in the medium-maturity Kharif class, not the early-maturing drought-tolerant class it describes for rain-fed land. That is a classification inference, not a tolerance test. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

DISEASE AND PEST
- A student project report on Krishidhan products says KDMH-017 is resistant to common diseases, with no pathogen named and no scoring method given. The report is secondary and should be treated as low-reliability. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/kapil-kadiyan-report/12566236
- No evidence found for specific pest resistance (e.g., stem borer, fall armyworm) or for named disease reactions such as turcicum leaf blight or maydis leaf blight.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is given as 90-95 days in one brochure-style source, and as medium maturity (86-95 days in Kharif) in the benchmarking table. -- https://www.slideshare.net/ishu_surya01/kapil-kadiyan-report ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Yield is listed as 8.0 t/ha in the benchmarking table, and as 90-95 q/ha (9.0-9.5 t/ha) in the brochure-style report. The two figures come from different sources and conditions and have not been reconciled. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties ; https://www.slideshare.net/ishu_surya01/kapil-kadiyan-report
- Plant height is listed as 220-225 cm, and grain is described as yellow semi-flint (brochure) or orange-yellow semi-flint (benchmarking table). These descriptions differ on grain colour. -- https://www.slideshare.net/ishu_surya01/kapil-kadiyan-report ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- No field-trial or multi-location data were found. -- (no URL)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage P45CB-164-1-1-2-BBBBBBBB (KDMI 65) x AF04B-5766-314-10BBB (KDMI 57) is from the user's input only. No search result confirmed it. -- user-supplied record, not verified
- No evidence found for breeding method, QTL, marker, or genome-resource studies on KDMH-017. The generic maize QTL and GWAS hits were not about this variety and were discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The IIMR cultivar list shows KDMH-017 as a private-sector release, with the developer recorded as "Karnatakaishidhan". This is probably a misspelling of Krishidhan, the company named in the input, but the source does not say so. No individual breeder is named. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
- The benchmarking paper lists Jyoti Kaul (IARI), Bhupender Kumar (IIMR) and O.P. Yadav (CAZRI) as authors. They are not stated as KDMH-017 breeders, so they are not attributed as such. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- The input's institution is Krishidhan Seeds Pvt. Ltd., Jalna. No search result confirmed the company's registration or its address. -- user-supplied record, not verified

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. No official email or phone number for Krishidhan Seeds Pvt. Ltd. was found in any result.
- Institution-level contact from the benchmarking paper: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research, Pusa Campus, New Delhi 110012. No email or phone was in the excerpt. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Company address from the input (not verified by search): D3-D6, Additional MiDC Area, Aurangabad Road, Jalna (MS) 431 203.

PUBLICATIONS
- Kaul, J., Kumar, B., & Yadav, O. P. (year not stated). Benchmarking Indian maize varieties. Conference paper, special meeting on benchmarking agricultural and horticultural crops in India, Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research, Karnal -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Authors not stated (year not stated). Maize research in India: challenges and opportunities. ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research presentation, which lists KDMH017 among hybrids -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694676_Maize_research_in_Indiachallenges_and_opportunities
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report entry, or peer-reviewed paper specific to KDMH-017 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Justdial lists a seller in Indore offering "Krishidhan KDMH 017 Indra Maize Seed". The page snippet does not show a dealer address, phone, or price, and "Indra" may be a trade name. -- https://www.justdial.com/jdmart/Indore/Krishidhan-KDMH-017-Indra-Maize-Seed/pid-222567537/0731P731STDK002909
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or Seednet availability record was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Odisha, listed for Kharif sowing. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Release date: the IIMR list gives 19-09-2013 and a code "2817 (E)". The source does not label what these fields mean, so the year_of_release field "Unknown" could reasonably be filled with 2013, pending confirmation from the CSC minutes or Gazette notification. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/

Items to verify next: the CSC minutes or Gazette notification for the release year and the notification number; the Seednet record directly; the Krishidhan company registration and contact details; and any SAU or AICRP multi-location trial data.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Hi-Brix 39 (ADVSW-1), Maize

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The search returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance records for this variety were returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A performance-evaluation paper on a corn sheller reports Hi-brix-39 yielding up to about 13.7 t/ha in a kharif maize crop, in a comparison against traditional practice (snippet only, full text not checked) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363194997_PERFORMANCE_EVALUATION_AND_ECONOMIC_ANALYSIS_OF_CORN_SHELLER_ON_CORN_VARIETIES

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No parentage, QTL or marker evidence was returned. The variety-name evidence from the search does not include the parentage string supplied in the record (Hi-brix39F x Hi-brix39M; M2549 / EC 596839; No. 303 / EC 596838), so that parentage remains unverified. Searches on the CSC minutes and the Seednet entry were not run separately.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The ICAR-IIMR cultivar list records Hi-Brix 39 (ADVSW-1) as developed by UPL/Advanta Seeds, a private developer, and another ICAR-IIMR listing gives the developer as Advanta Limited, Hyderabad, private sector -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ ; https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/cultivars-2/ . No lead breeder or scientist name was found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, official email, phone, postal address or institute contact page for this variety was returned. The only institutional reference is the company name, Advanta Limited / UPL Limited, Hyderabad, with no address found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record naming this variety was found. The only item returned is the corn-sheller study listed under AGRONOMY AND TRIALS, whose authors and journal were not extracted from the snippet. A compiled list of maize cultivars released in India (1969-2017) on Scribd names Hi-brix-39 but gives no further detail -- https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was found. The ICAR-IIMR list gives the status as private, and the seed-source details were not returned -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Madhya Pradesh (MP), per the ICAR-IIMR cultivar list -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/cultivars-2/

RELEASE YEAR CONFLICT -- The ICAR-IIMR list gives two different dates for this variety: 30-03-2017 (listed as 1007 E in one row) and 05.09.2019 (listed as 3220(E) in another row). The record's 2017 year is consistent with the first, but the discrepancy is unresolved.

NAME CHECK -- "Hi-Brix 39" (CSC name) and "Hi-Brix 39 (ADVSW-1)" (Seednet name) appear as the same variety in the ICAR-IIMR list. The evidence refers to both names; no separate Seednet page was retrieved.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Super Sweet Corn 2 (ASKH1), Maize

Search note: I ran four web searches (variety/release, breeder/institute, research, seed availability). None returned a seednet.gov.in page, so the Seednet name "Pusa Super Sweet Corn 2 (ASKH1)" has no direct portal evidence here. The CSC minutes name "Pusa Super Sweet Corn 2" appears in the sources, and ASKH-1 is named as its pre-release code in one journal abstract. I did not run a separate Seednet query because the four-search limit was reached.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Seed vigour under sub-optimum temperature (15°C and 20°C) was assessed for Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2 and its parental lines SWT16 and SWT17. The hybrid was superior to its parents for seedling emergence and germination index. This is a seed-vigour study, not a field stress-tolerance trial, and it does not test drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/view/4331
No other evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Average yield 95.0 q/ha, sown in Kharif, maturity 77 days, special feature: extra-sweet hybrid with 16.4% Brix. -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/maize/ (name on page: "Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2"; the page does not give the ASKH1 code, and the yield figure is not tied to a named trial or location)
Seed-vigour and germination evaluation under 15°C, 20°C and 25°C, with parental lines SWT16, SWT17, VSL16 and VSL4 -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/view/4331 (variety name on page: "Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2")
No multi-location trial data found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Genotype: a shrunken2 (sh2sh2) sweet corn hybrid. ASKH-1 is described as released as Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2 (PSSC-2). -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0889157520313302 (name on page: "ASKH-1" and "Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2 (PSSC-2)")
Parental lines named in the seed-vigour study: SWT16 and SWT17. The page does not provide the parentage codes given in the brief (PMI-SWT016, PMI-SWT017, Pusa-RIL-91-Sel-sh2sh2, CM140 x DMR-sh2sh2), so those codes are unverified. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/view/4331
Note: the sciencedirect paper's O2 and CrtRB1 alleles belong to its biofortified single-cross hybrids, which are MAS-derived versions of ASKH-1. They are not attributed to Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2 itself. -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0889157520313302
Breeding method, genome resources and QTL/marker data for this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi. Release year 2020. -- https://iari.res.in/sci_db/sci_details.php?scid=TzFVREhvQzFEWlRCMXZac2o1VVpYQT09 (the page lists "Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2 (2020)" among a scientist's releases, but the page does not name that scientist in the content retrieved, so I have not attributed a breeder name)
Lead breeder names: No evidence found. The sci_db profile is consistent with a maize genetics and breeding scientist, but no name was confirmed in the text returned.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level address from the seed-vigour paper: Division of Genetics, ICAR-IARI, Pusa, New Delhi - 110 012. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/view/4331
Breeder email, phone and contact page: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not retrieved (2023). Genetic variability for early seed vigor traits for enhanced performance under sub-optimum temperatures in sweet corn (Zea mays Convar. saccharata L.). Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding -- https://doi.org/10.31742/ISGPB.83.3.10
Authors not retrieved (year not shown in retrieved text). Composition analysis of lysine, tryptophan and provitamin-A during different stages of kernel development in biofortified sweet corn. ScienceDirect (Journal of Cereal Science, unverified) -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0889157520313302 (this paper uses ASKH-1 as the source of its MAS-derived biofortified hybrids; it is not a study of Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2 alone)
Other items returned by the search were about other crops, other sweet corn hybrids (e.g. Pusa Super Sweet Corn-1, CMVL Sweet Corn-1) or general sh2 genetics, so I have excluded them.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The search returned only commercial US and other non-Indian seed catalogues, which are unrelated to this variety. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh. -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/maize/ (the page's recommended-area list matches the input list exactly)
