search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Hi-Brix 53 (ADVSW-2)

Name note: The CSC-style name "Hi-Brix 53" and the Seednet name "Hi-Brix 53 (ADVSW-2)" both appear in the IIMR cultivar table, which lists two entries (a 2017 entry spelled "Hy-brix 53 (ADVSW-2)" and a 2019 entry spelled "Hi-Brix 53 (ADVSW-2)"). The evidence below refers to these names.

Crop note: Every page that names this variety describes it as a sweet corn (fresh-cob and processing) hybrid, not fodder maize. The Seednet crop label "Maize (fodder)" conflicts with that, and the IIMR table files it under Sweet Corn.

Institution note: The IIMR table gives the developer as "UPL/Advanta Seeds" for the 2019 entry and "Advanta Limited, Hyderabad" for the 2017 entry. The record's "UPL Limited Hyderabad" does not match either exactly.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety. The only stress-related text on a page naming it is the disease note under DISEASE AND PEST.

DISEASE AND PEST:
- A compiled list of Indian maize cultivars (1969-2017) gives this hybrid's resistance profile as Fusarium stalk rot resistance and downy mildew resistance, with moderate resistance to another disease whose name is cut off in the source text -- https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf
- The same compiled list gives the same profile in a second copy of the table -- https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf
- Discarded: an African retailer's "Hybrix 53" page claiming leaf blight and maize streak virus resistance. It is a different product name in a different country. https://afrimash.com/shop/afrimash-crop-section/crop/hybrix-53-sweet-corn-high-quality-yield/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- A dealer listing for Advanta Hi-Brix 53 sweet corn describes a vigorous, medium-tall hybrid with cobs of about 400-450 g, a tight green husk, medium-bold yellow kernels suited to fresh and processing use, double cob bearing, cob length of 18-20 cm, and TSS of 13-15% -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/hi-brix-53-sweet-corn-seeds
- The IIMR cultivar table lists this hybrid as Kharif sweet corn, with a value of 13.7 in one column (unit not stated on the page) and a notification of 30-03-2017 (1007 E) for the 2017 entry -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
- The compiled 1969-2017 list gives a maturity field of 90-100 for the 2017 entry; the column is ambiguous and may not be days to maturity -- https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf
- Discarded: a Nigerian retailer's "Hybrix 53" page with 70-75 day maturity, and a Thai "Hi-brix 53" sweet corn hybrid study. Neither is confirmed as this variety. https://afrimash.com/shop/afrimash-crop-section/crop/hybrix-53-sweet-corn-high-quality-yield/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Chiang-Mais-16-Clusters-and-their-associated-clients-corn-fields-obtained-from-Relaxed_fig3_317293352

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources):
- Parentage: Hi-Brix 53F x Hi-Brix 53M, per the compiled 1969-2017 list (the same entry as Hy-brix 53 SCH, ADVSW-2) -- https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf
- Breeding method (single cross, inbred lines as parents): inferred from the F x M parentage, not stated explicitly -- https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf
- Breeding-line codes beyond "53F" and "53M": No evidence found.
- QTL, marker and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- The IIMR cultivar table lists the developer as UPL/Advanta Seeds (private) for the 2019 entry, and Advanta Limited, Hyderabad for the 2017 entry -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
- The compiled list names the releasing firm as Advanta Limited, Hyderabad, and classes it as private -- https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf
- A corporate social-media page describes Hi-Brix 53 as part of the Advanta Seeds portfolio -- https://www.facebook.com/advantavegetables/videos/farmer-testimonial-hybrid-sweet-corn-hi-brix-53hi-brix-53-is-a-hybrid-sweet-corn/2302217379938772/
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found.
- Developing station: No evidence found.
- Discarded: UPL's Brucia herbicide launch pages, which concern a different product. https://www.global-agriculture.com/crop-protection/upl-launches-new-herbicide-brucia-for-maize-crop-in-india/

CONTACT DETAILS:
- No evidence found. No breeder, UPL or Advanta email, phone, address or contact-page URL appeared in any result.
- The only institutional source for this variety is the IIMR cultivar table, which gives no contact details -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
- Discarded: the Scribd compilation and the dealer listing, which carry no contact details for the developer.

PUBLICATIONS:
No evidence found. The results contained no paper, report or thesis that names this variety. The Thai "Hi-brix 53" study (ResearchGate, figure page) concerns a different hybrid from Thailand and is excluded. Vivek Maize Hybrid 53 (FH 3556), a Uttarakhand hybrid, is also excluded. Its Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding entry (2015) is listed here for transparency only and is not evidence for this variety: Agrawal P. K. et al. (2015). Vivek Maize hybrid 53 (FH 3556). Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding 75(1):150 -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-75-1-025

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- A DesiKheti online listing sells Advanta Hi-Brix 53 sweet corn seed (F1 hybrid) for home delivery across India. The page does not mention ADVSW-2, so the match rests on the name -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/hi-brix-53-sweet-corn-seeds
- NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU and other dealer listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- 2019 entry (notification 05.09.2019, 3220(E)): Madhya Pradesh only, which matches the record -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/

disease_resistance.research_summary: Resistance to Fusarium stalk rot and downy mildew, and moderate resistance to one further disease whose name is cut off in the source text (compiled Indian maize cultivars list, 1969-2017; the same profile appears in a second copy of the table). The CSC record also names Turcicum Leaf Blight (TLB), Maydis Leaf Blight (MLB), charcoal rot and Curvularia leaf spot (moderate resistance) and 'Rajasthan Downey mildew (2014)'. The digest does not corroborate these named diseases, so they are not treated as confirmed. The African 'Hybrix 53' page claiming leaf blight and maize streak virus resistance was discarded as a different product.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JAUM0936 (variety_name) / JAUM 0936 (seednet_variety_name), Green gram (mung), SKUAST-Jammu

Search budget note: four web_search calls were used (one batch of four queries). A fifth call was refused by the tool limit, so no further searching was possible. Only the first 300 characters of each result were reviewed, so the full text of the pages was not checked for this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page naming JAUM0936 or JAU 0936 with stress data. Results were generic green gram pages (echocommunity.org) and a PubMed review on green gram chemistry.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page naming this variety with disease or pest resistance data was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No maturity, yield, or multi-location trial data for this variety was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found in search results. The parentage and pedigree details (MH-96-1 x SML-668, pedigree method) came from the variety record supplied with the request, not from any search result. They are unverified by an external source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No page named a breeder or scientist for this variety. The SKUAST-Jammu page returned (https://skuastjammu.ac.in/newsite/pdf/21-rcm.pdf, "Minutes of 21st Research Council Meeting held on 31st July, 2021") is a lead only. Its opening text refers to the release of 12 crop varieties by SKUAST-Jammu in 2020. I did not confirm that it names JAUM0936, so I have not attributed it to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder contact was found. Institute-level contact details were not found in search results. The SKUAST-Jammu site appears in the lead above, but no contact page was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The search returned no paper, thesis, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh record for this variety. The PubMed item (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3539530/, "Chemistry and technology of green gram") concerns green gram in general and does not name this variety, so it is excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The only seed result was a Pakistani retail page (greengardens.pk), which is unrelated and excluded. No Seednet, NSC, SKUAST, KVK, or dealer listing for this variety was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found from search. The supplied record states "Jammu province of UT of Jammu & Kashmir." That is unverified by an external source.

Next steps for a complete record: check the SKUAST-Jammu RCM minutes PDF for the JAUM0936 entry; search the Seednet portal directly for "JAU 0936" under GREEN GRAM (MOONG BEAN/ MOONG); and search KrishiKosh and the SKUAST-Jammu pulses division site for the breeder name and contact.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Sodicity Mungbean 12 (PSM-12), green gram (mung)

Name handling: variety_name is "Mungbean" and seednet_variety_name is "Unknown". I searched using the variety code "Pusa Sodicity Mungbean 12 (PSM-12)" and the crop name. None of the results named PSM-12, so no finding below can be attributed to either name.

Searches run (4): (1) variety/release/traits; (2) breeder/developing institute; (3) research papers; (4) seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Search 1 returned mungbean varieties from other programmes and countries (Pusa Vishal, Pusa Ratna, SML 832, Kalyan, a Nepal trial), none of which is PSM-12. A GRDC grow-notes page rates mungbean as sensitive to sodicity and waterlogging in general, but it does not mention this variety, so I have excluded it. -- https://grdc.com.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0034/238975/grdc-grownotes-mungbeans-northern.pdf.pdf (general crop, not this variety; excluded)

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. Search 1 returned MYMV-resistance claims for Pusa Vishal, Pusa Ratna, Pusa 0672 and Pusa 9531 only. These are different varieties and were excluded. -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/pulses/mungbean/ (other varieties; excluded)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. Search 1 returned yield and maturity data for other mungbean varieties only, such as Pusa Vishal, Pusa Ratna, Pusa 0672 and Pusa 9531. A 2025 PeerJ study of mungbean varieties under rhizobium inoculation was also returned, but it does not name PSM-12. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12178244/ (no PSM-12 named; excluded)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. No parentage, breeding-line code or breeding method was returned for PSM-12. Search 3 returned general mungbean GWAS and phosphorus-efficiency studies from ICAR-IARI, but none names PSM-12. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10558178/ (general mungbean; excluded)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No breeder name found for PSM-12. The institution named in the record is ICAR-IARI, which the search confirms as a mungbean breeding institute in general terms. Its own accomplishments page says IARI-bred mungbean varieties have contributed to rainfed production, but it does not mention PSM-12. -- https://iari.res.in/index.php?id=550&option=com_content&view=article (institute-level, not variety-specific)

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder contact found. Institute-level address only, as the brief allows: ZTM & BPD Unit, ICAR-IARI, Pusa Campus, New Delhi-110012 (from the IARI Zonal Technology Management & Business Development page; this page does not name PSM-12). -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/pulses/mungbean/ No official email or phone number was found in the results.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. Search 3 returned mungbean papers, but none names PSM-12. Examples excluded: a 2018 heterosis note that uses Pusa Vishal as a parent, and a 2024 processing study on Pusa Baisakhi. Neither is about this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. Search 4 returned seed-sales pages from RPCAU Directorate of Seed, Dholi (https://rpcau.ac.in/directorate-of-seed-dholi/) and a 2023 IARI Pusa Seed Sales Counter news item (https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/farmers-now-can-buy-seeds-directly-from-pusa-seed-sales-counter-inaugurated-in-new-delhi/). Neither lists PSM-12, so both are excluded. The IARI item is an institute-wide sales counter, not evidence for this variety. An Amazon listing for "Pusa Seed" returned a black gram seed, which is a different crop.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found for Uttar Pradesh or any other state. The raw value "Uttar Pradesh" in the record is unconfirmed. The IARI annual report 2018-19 lists Pusa 0871 for kharif Uttar Pradesh trials, but that is a different variety and was excluded. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/IARIANNUALREPORT2018_19_30072019.pdf (other variety; excluded)

Release year, parentage and seednet_variety_name remain Unknown. Suggested next checks: the CSC/CVRC release notification, the Seednet portal entry, and the KrishiKosh and IARI Division of Genetics or Plant Physiology publication lists searched by exact code.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Search limit reached: the search tool's usage cap was hit during my second batch, so I completed only one batch of four searches. The snippets I could read were short, so most headings below lack verified detail.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: the evidence I found refers to "Giriraj (DRMRIJ 31)", which is the Seednet name. I found no page that uses the CSC name "Giriraj (ORMRU 31)", so the two names are not confirmed as the same entry.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found (search returned only release-notification and licensing pages; no stress data was readable)

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found (not readable in retrieved snippets)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found (not readable in retrieved snippets)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage HB 9908 x HB 9916 was supplied in the task input and was not verified by any search result. No other evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Finding: a release/notification document for Giriraj (DRMRIJ 31) exists, per its title -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321746854_Notification_and_Release_of_Crop_Varieties_Mustard_Variety_Giriraj_DRMRIJ_31
Finding: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (ICAR-IIRMR) is named as the licensor of DRMRIJ-31 (Giriraj) under a memorandum of agreement with Narottam Seeds LLP, per the page title -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/icar-iirmr-signs-moa-narottam-seeds-llp-licensing-mustard-variety-drmrij-31-giriraj
No individual breeder name was found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. Institute-level contact not extracted from snippets; the ICAR-IIRMR page at the URL above is the best starting point for the institute contact page.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. Only the ResearchGate notification record was returned; its author list and journal/report details were not readable, so I cannot give a citation in the required format.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Finding: ICAR-IIRMR has licensed DRMRIJ-31 (Giriraj) to Narottam Seeds LLP for commercial seed production, per the page title -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/icar-iirmr-signs-moa-narottam-seeds-llp-licensing-mustard-variety-drmrij-31-giriraj
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found in readable text. The states in the task input (Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab) remain unverified, and the Jammu and Kashmir entry is still inferred from table layout.

Next steps for a complete record: open the ResearchGate notification page and the ICAR-IIRMR licensing page for full text, check the CSC minutes for the ORMRU 31 code, and search seednet.gov.in and the IIRMR publications/contact pages directly for the breeder, trial, and contact details.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Niger Selection 28 (JNS 28), Niger (Guizotia abyssinica)

Name note: the CSC/variety_name is "Jawahar Niger Selection 28 (JNS 28)". The DOD page writes it as "Jawahar Niger Sel-28 (JNS-29)", and the MP seed corporation page lists "Jawahar Niger Selection 28, JNS-30, JNC-9". Those variant labels (JNS-29, JNS-30) may be typos or may refer to different entries, so each finding below states which name it uses. Unless noted, the evidence refers to "JNS-28" or "Jawahar Niger Sel-28".

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Secondary web summary says JNS 28 and JNS 30 were developed by the agriculture department as resistant to amarbel (dodder, Cuscuta) -- https://www.iasgyan.in/daily-current-affairs/niger (name: JNS 28)
- Niger is described as a hardy, rainfed crop; the JNS-28 abstract describes it as a high oil and seed yielding genotype, but the snippet does not give drought or other stress data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311431684_JNS-28_A_high_oil_and_seed_yielding_promising_genotype_of_Niger_Guizotia_Abyssinica_LF_Cass (name: JNS-28)
- Indian Farming article reports wide adaptability of JNS-28, allowing it to be grown on plains as well as undulated uplands -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/123675 (name: JNS-28)
- No evidence found for salinity, flood, submergence or heat tolerance specific to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Amarbel (dodder) resistance is claimed in the secondary summary above; no primary source or screening data was found -- https://www.iasgyan.in/daily-current-affairs/niger (name: JNS 28)
- No evidence found for disease (Alternaria, rust, wilt) or insect resistance specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Indian Farming reports a seed yield of 9.25 q/ha for niger after JNS-28 cultivation in the Madhya Pradesh plains, about double the state average, with income of about Rs 15,385/ha more than soybean -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/123675 (name: JNS-28)
- A germplasm evaluation at five Indian locations used JNS-28 as a standard check; early accessions reached 50% flowering in 30-40 days and maturity in 58-75 days, but the snippet gives no maturity value for JNS-28 itself -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijpgr-34-3-015 (name: JNS-28 as check)
- Oil content listed for the variety is 34-36% -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx (name: Jawahar Niger Sel-28 (JNS-29))

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY: Phule Karala (variety_name) / Phule Karala(IGPN 2004-1) (seednet_variety_name). Niger (Guizotia abyssinica). Four searches were run. Seednet.gov.in and ICAR pages did not appear in the results, and no search targeted them directly. Where a finding concerns a name, the name is stated.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought: a ResearchGate study of Niger cultivars under drought stress reports that IGPN 2004(1) showed more cellular-level drought tolerance than the sensitive comparison cultivar, with less membrane oxidative damage -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313771436_Growth_and_Physiological_Alterations_in_Niger_Cultivars_under_Drought_Stress_1 (name: IGPN 2004(1))
- Waterlogging, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found for this variety. Waterlogging tolerance appeared only in generic Niger pages, not tied to this variety -- https://agrosiaa.com/agronomy/detail/niger (discarded for this variety)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Tolerant to Alternaria leaf spot, powdery mildew, and root rot (name: IGPN 2004-1, Phule Karala-1) -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/agricultural-and-biological-sciences/open-pollination
- Resistance to powdery mildew and Alternaria, per a release-table row for IGPN-2004-1 (Phule Karala) from ZARS Igatpuri -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381519951_Clean_Energy_Technology_Advances_and_Applications
- Pest resistance: No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Days to maturity 95–105 (ScienceDirect table) and 95–100 days (ResearchGate table); oil content 39–41%; average yield 650–700 kg/ha; shiny black seed -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/agricultural-and-biological-sciences/open-pollination ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381519951_Clean_Energy_Technology_Advances_and_Applications
- Recommended for kharif sowing in Maharashtra and Karnataka (high-rainfall areas of Maharashtra) -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/agricultural-and-biological-sciences/open-pollination
- Stability analysis: Phule Karala appears as genotype G39 (ZARS Igatpuri) in an AMMI yield-stability and GEI study of Niger -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381478847_Yield_Stability_and_GEI_by_AMMI_Model_in_Niger_Guizotia_abyssinica_L (yield values not retrieved)
- Front-line demonstration: Phule Karala replaced a local Niger variety in a Maharashtra FLD cluster (kharif 2009), with yield figures given -- https://www.acspublisher.com/journals/index.php/ijee/article/download/5155/4655/5227

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Breeding-line code IGPN 2004-1 and common name Phule Karala-1 confirmed across sources -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/agricultural-and-biological-sciences/open-pollination
- Parentage: the supplied parentage "local selection from Peth tahsil, Nashik" was not found in any retrieved page. Unverified.
- Breeding method, QTL/marker, genome resources: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth (MPKV), Rahuri, per a Niger production slide deck listing "Phule Karala (MPKV, Rahuri)" -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/niger-production-technology-with-all-package-of-practices/272099569
- Station: ZARS Igatpuri (Zonal Agricultural Research Station, Igatpuri), per the ResearchGate release-table row -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381519951_Clean_Energy_Technology_Advances_and_Applications
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. A JABB article lists a "Niger Breeder, AICRP on Niger, ZARS Igatpuri, MPKV" but names no person and concerns a safflower paper, so it is not attributed here -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/1556

CONTACT DETAILS
- No named breeder contact, email, phone, or postal address found. No MPKV or ZARS Igatpuri contact page was retrieved. Please check the MPKV website directly for institute contact details.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Growth and physiological alterations in Niger cultivars under drought stress. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313771436_Growth_and_Physiological_Alterations_in_Niger_Cultivars_under_Drought_Stress_1
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Yield stability and GEI by AMMI model in Niger (Guizotia abyssinica L.). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381478847_Yield_Stability_and_GEI_by_AMMI_Model_in_Niger_Guizotia_abyssinica_L
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Front-line demonstration report on Niger varietal replacement, Maharashtra. International Journal of Environment and Ecology (ACS Publisher) -- https://www.acspublisher.com/journals/index.php/ijee/article/download/5155/4655/5227
- Authors not retrieved. Clean Energy Technology: Advances and Applications, Section 1.2.5 Niger (release table). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381519951_Clean_Energy_Technology_Advances_and_Applications
- AICRP/ICAR annual reports, KrishiKosh theses, QTL/marker papers: No evidence found in these searches

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Official sources: No evidence found for NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer stock of this variety. Seednet was not retrieved.
- Listed in the DAC notified-varieties table for Niger (IGPN-2004-1 among recommended varieties) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx
- Retail listings (Amazon, chutney shops) sell generic niger seed, not this variety. Discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Maharashtra: Phule Karala-1 / IGPN 2004-1 is listed as a preferred variety -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/oilseeds/niger-oilseeds-1/niger-cultivation-practices ; https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/cultivation-of-niger-a-great-feed-for-milch-cattle/

csc_fields.special_traits: Plant height: 45-50 cm. Distinguishing morphological characters: Dark red coloured bulbs, stripes on bulb, oval shape, very less number of bolters and doubles in Rabi, thin neck, number of leaves ranged from 8-12, TSS 10-10.5%. Number of leaves: 8-12/plant. Polar Diameter (P): 42-45 cm. Equatorial Diameter (E): 45-50 cm. P.E.: 0.85-0.95. Neck thickness: 0.6-0.8cm. % Total soluble solids: 10-10.5. Days to harvest after transplanting: 100-105 days in Kharif, 115-120 day in Rabi. Characters different from those of the parents: Bulbs oval in shape and single centred. Maturity (range in number of days): 115-120 day after transplanting in Rabi and 100-105 days in Kharif. Maturity Group: Early in Kharif and medium in Rabi. Agronomical features: Erect Plant habit, less pseudostem length, minimum neck thickness of the bulb, uniform neck fall during Rabi, early in maturity. Quality attributes purpose for which recommended: Table/processing/export. Table quality attributes/Nutritional quality: Attractive red colour, suitable for immediate consumption. Single centered, suitable for salad, pungent. Reaction to major diseases: Field tolerance to foliar diseases. Reaction to major pests: Field tolerance to thrips. Average yield under normal condition: 250-300 qtls/ha.
csc_fields.parent_material: Dark red colour and duration resembles with Baswant 780, A.Kalyan and N-53.
csc_fields.maturity_group: Early in Kharif and medium in Rabi

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I could not complete the required research. Every web_search call failed: the first four returned "Invalid tool input" because the query was not passed, and the retries, including a single-call retry, returned "You have called the web_search tool too many times this turn." So I have no web evidence for any heading, and I have not written "No evidence found" under any heading, because that would claim a search I did not get to run.

What I can state from the record you supplied (not from web sources):

- Variety name: Sahbhagi Dhan. Seednet name: SAHBHAGI. Crop: Rice (Seednet: PADDY (DHAN)). Variety code: (IET No.19576) IR 74371-70-1-1-CRR-1).
- Sponsoring authority, year of release: not specified or unknown in the record.
- Recommended states as entered: "JHARKANDODISHA", which appears to be Jharkhand and Odisha run together. Please verify against Seednet.
- Parentage as entered: IR 55419-04 (IR 12979-24-1 (Brown)/UPL Ri 5), described as an elite drought-tolerant breeding line developed at IRRI, with Way Rarem as a drought-sensitive Indonesian upland parent. Note that this text is the input record, not a verified source, and it is the only basis for the GENETICS heading.

To finish the digest, the four searches still need to run (variety/release, breeder and contact, research papers, seed availability), ideally in a new session where the search tool is available. Suggested first checks are seednet.gov.in for the notification record and the IRRI or ICAR/state rice-program pages for the breeding history.

csc_fields.additional_notes: Deferred in the 54th Sub-committee meeting, for want of clarification on the authorship and parentage details and the Sponsoring Authority was advised to re-submit the revised proposal along with the required information for consideration. The Sponsoring Authority re-submitted the proposal without providing the required details. The Committee noted that the sponsoring authority has not made any efforts to clarify lacuna. Committee directed to the sponsoring authority to look into the decision of the 54th Sub-committee and to clarify the position. Committee further would also like to know what intervention was made in the proposal. Decisions taken: 1. Breeders/sponsoring authority should prepare themselves to provide the information with regards to DNA Marker/Finger Printing, prime number, etc. of the variety proposed for notification from 1st January, 2011 onwards. 2. While submitting the proposal, they should provide lucid photograph of the field, individual plant, cob, rachis, grain, etc. so as to consider physical appearance the cultivar.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: AHB 1269Fe (MH 2185; also listed as AHB 1269) — Pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum)

Name note: The CSC name is "AHB 1269Fe" and the Seednet name is "AHB 1269Fe (MH 2185) (AHB 1269)". The retrieved pages use "AHB 1269Fe (MH 2185)", "MH 2185" and "AHB 1269", so every finding below refers to one of those names. I did not reach seednet.gov.in directly; the four searches returned no Seednet page.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The four searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this hybrid. The only trait claims are about grain iron and grain and stover yield. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/11772/

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. None of the retrieved pages reports downy mildew, blast, ergot, smut or insect resistance scores for this hybrid. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/11772/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The Varietal Identification Committee identified MH 2185 as the biofortified hybrid AHB 1269Fe at its annual meet (22–24 March 2018, 53rd Annual Pearl Millet Workshop, ARS Jodhpur), citing high grain iron together with high grain and stover yield. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/11772/
- The hybrid was tested in AICRP-PM trials in the 2015, 2016 and 2017 seasons at 36 locations (12, 13 and 11 locations respectively), against 6 controls (86M86, 86M01, MPMH 17 and others). The retrieved text is truncated, so I could not confirm the grain or stover yield figures. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/11772/
- A 2019 entry for AHB 1269Fe appears in an ICAR Indian Farming (January 2023) table of fodder crops. The columns are not labelled clearly enough to read as grain yield, stover yield or maturity, so I have not used them. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf
- Maturity: no reliable value found. The Indian Farming table text describes the biofortified hybrids as medium maturing, but it does not name AHB 1269Fe for that claim. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf
- Grain Fe/Zn: a 2023 ICAR-IIMR article says the second set of biofortified hybrids (RHB 233, RHB 234, AHB 1269, HHB 311), released in 2019–20, contained 83–91 mg/kg Fe and 39–46 mg/kg Zn with similar grain yield. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375670979_Enhancing_productivity_and_nutrition_with_biofortified_pearl_millet_cultivars
- Nutrition profiling: a PMC study compared AHB 1269 with other biofortified and non-biofortified pearl millet cultivars. Its text gives a 2018–2020 release window for the set, but I did not retrieve its authors or journal. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9998779/
- Processing: a study on salt-popping of pearl millet used AHB 1269 among five varieties at 220, 240 and 260 °C. Authors and journal were not in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/248510140_Content_and_HCl-extractability_of_minerals_as_affected_by_acid_treatment_of_pearl_millet

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: MH 2185 is a cross between male-sterile female line ICMA1 98222 and restorer male AUBI 1105. ICMA1 98222 carries the A1 cytoplasmic male-sterility source developed at ICRISAT, Patancheru. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/11772/
- Breeding-line codes found: MH 2185 (hybrid), ICMA1 98222 (female), AUBI 1105 (male restorer). The user-supplied pedigree (ICMB 98222 backcrossed to 842 A-source; AUBI 1105 as MRC HS-130-2-2-1-B-B-3-B-B-B-1-3-1) was not confirmed by any retrieved page. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/11772/
- Breeding method: the retrieved text describes the hybrid cross and the male-sterile source only. It does not describe the backcross programme in detail. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/11772/
- Genome resources, QTL and marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The OAR record lists the release-note authors as M. Govindaraj, S. B. Pawar, R. C. Sawant, S. Satpute, D. P. Waskar, H. Shivade, A. Kanatti, T. Satyavathi and D. V. Patil. The page does not say which of them bred the hybrid, so treat them as authors of the identification note, not confirmed breeders. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/11772/
- Developing institutions: the hybrid was jointly developed and sponsored to AICRP-PM by the National Agricultural Research Project, Aurangabad, and Vasantrao Naik Marathwada Krishi Vidyapeeth (VNMKV), Parbhani, with ICRISAT, Patancheru. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/11772/
- The 2023 ICAR-IIMR article ("Enhancing productivity and nutrition with biofortified pearl millet cultivars", by P. Sanjana Reddy, Parashuram Patroti and V. M. Malathi) says the hybrid was released in collaboration with Sardarkrushinagar Dantiwada Agricultural University (SKNAU), Rajasthan, and was released at national level in 2019–20. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375670979_Enhancing_productivity_and_nutrition_with_biofortified_pearl_millet_cultivars
- Note: the article's "SKNAU" expansion is taken as written in the retrieved text. I did not verify it against an official SKNAU page.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute (ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research): ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, Telangana 500 030. This is the address as printed in the retrieved article, not a verified institute contact page. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf
- No breeder email, phone or institute contact page was found. The OAR and CGSpace records give no contact details. VNMKV Parbhani and ICRISAT contact details were not retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Govindaraj, M., Pawar, S. B., Sawant, R. C., Satpute, S., Waskar, D. P., Shivade, H., Kanatti, A., Satyavathi, T., & Patil, D. V. (2020). Variety AHB 1269Fe (MH 2185). Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding, 80(2), p. 230. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/11772/
- CGIAR Research Program on Agriculture for Nutrition and Health (2018). Iron Pearl Millet variety: AHB 1269 (MH 2185). Agriculture for Nutrition and Health Annual Report 2018. -- https://cgspace.cgiar.org/items/63cf90d1-cf57-4bae-aacf-ea429f1d791e (handle: https://hdl.handle.net/10568/122862)
- Reddy, P. S., Patroti, P., & Malathi, V. M. (2023). Enhancing productivity and nutrition with biofortified pearl millet cultivars. Indian Farming (ICAR, January 2023 issue) and ResearchGate version. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375670979_Enhancing_productivity_and_nutrition_with_biofortified_pearl_millet_cultivars (year and author list taken from the retrieved text; the ResearchGate page does not show a journal)
- Authors not retrieved (2023/2024?). Heterosis of newly developed restorers in pearl millet, Bajra Research Scheme, College of Agriculture, Dhule (Summer and Kharif 2023). AHB 1269 is used as a check. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396947047_Study_on_Heterosis_of_Newly_Developed_Restorers_in_Pearl_Millet_Pennisetum_glaucum_L_R_Br
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Comparative nutritional profiling of non-biofortified and biofortified pearl millet varieties and hybrids, including AHB 1269. PMC9998779. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9998779/
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Salt-popping study of mineral extractability in five pearl millet varieties, including AHB 1269. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/248510140_Content_and_HCl-extractability_of_minerals_as_affected_by_acid_treatment_of_pearl_millet
- Not used: the Crop Science 2024 review (DOI 10.1002/csc2.21207) and the ICRISAT preprint on biofortified breeding. Neither names AHB 1269 in the retrieved text.
- KrishiKosh thesis search: No evidence found. No thesis was retrieved in these searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. None of the four searches returned a seed producer, dealer, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing for AHB 1269Fe. The seed-related result (Crop Science 2024 review on millet breeder-seed procurement) is about millets in general and does not name this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf
- Release year: 2019 in the ICAR table. The HarvestPlus card gives 2018 for the same name, a discrepancy I could not resolve. -- https://bcr.harvestplus.org/cropsByCountri_cards/4/Pearl%20Millet
- The HarvestPlus card also lists "ICMH 1502" beside this name, which I could not reconcile with the MH 2185 code. -- https://bcr.harvestplus.org/cropsByCountri_cards/4/Pearl%20Millet

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jam Shakti (GHB 1129) (Hybrid), Pearl millet

Search status: The search tool's limit was reached after four queries, so the research is incomplete. The first query returned a page about a different variety, Moti Shakti (GHB 1225). Of the four searches, only the weed-management article and the Jamnagar station page name this variety or its station. Several topics could not be searched separately because the limit was reached first. Variety name used: "Jam Shakti" (CSC/release minutes name) and "Jam Shakti (GHB 1129) (Hybrid)" (Seednet name). The evidence below refers to the code GHB 1129 where stated.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for Jam Shakti or GHB 1129.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No search result described disease or pest resistance for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A plant-science journal article on weed management approaches in pearl millet during the summer season on loamy sand soil in middle Gujarat names the variety GHB 1129 as a bio-fortified hybrid, and describes it as rich in micronutrients. This is a weed-control trial, not a yield or variety-evaluation study; no yield data were visible in the retrieved text -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/333-Effect%20of%20weed%20management%20approaches%20on%20pearl%20millet%20in%20summer%20season%20under%20loamy%20sand%20soil%20of%20middle%20Gujarat,%20India.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No search evidence. The following comes from the supplied variety record, not from any search result, and is unverified: female line ICMA1 99222 (described as an ICRISAT line with high iron and zinc), male/restorer line J-2565 (pedigree (J-2340 x J-2480)-8-5-6-2-2-1-B-B, designated 2012, Pearl Millet Research Station, JAU, Jamnagar). No QTL or marker study was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The Main Pearl Millet Research Station, Jamnagar (Junagadh Agricultural University) page describes the station's history and mentions it was rated the best-performing AICRP on Pearl Millet centre for 2024-25 at the 60th Annual Group Meeting (28-30 May 2025, virtual). It does not name Jam Shakti or GHB 1129, and no breeder name was found -- https://www.jau.in/main-pearl-millet-research-station-jamnagar

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. The only institutional source is the station page above; no email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for the station was visible in the retrieved text. Institute-level contact should be taken from the JAU website directly.

PUBLICATIONS -- Only one item found, which names GHB 1129 and pearl millet:
Authors not visible in retrieved text (year not visible). Effect of weed management approaches on pearl millet in summer season under loamy sand soil of middle Gujarat, India. Plant Archives -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/333-Effect%20of%20weed%20management%20approaches%20on%20pearl%20millet%20in%20summer%20season%20under%20loamy%20sand%20soil%20of%20middle%20Gujarat,%20India.pdf
No peer-reviewed variety paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for Jam Shakti or GHB 1129. The only seed listing returned was for a different product, "Savrana Shakti" hybrid bajra, from a private Ahmedabad dealer (New Nandi Seeds Corporation -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/hybrid-bajra-seed-1618618012.html). It was excluded as a different product name. Seednet, NSC, state corporation and SAU seed-sale sources were not searched.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Gujarat, from the supplied variety record only. No search result confirmed the notification or recommendation.

Not verified by search: release year 2020, CSC notification details, maturity, yield, and breeder names.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MP7366 (variety_name, CSC minutes) / MP7366 (MSH 346) (seednet_variety_name), Pearl millet

Search budget note: the four allowed searches ran, but a fifth call to re-check results was blocked by the tool limit. The findings below come only from the first-pass results, which were truncated to about 400 characters each, so some details may be incomplete. The Seednet and CSC pages were never returned, so no name-level evidence from those sources was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches on "MP7366 Pearl millet variety" returned general pearl millet material, and no page described drought, heat, salinity, or waterlogging tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
The Rallis product page for MP7366 says the hybrid is tolerant to blast, rust and downy mildew (company marketing claim, not independently verified) -- https://www.rallis.com/india-business/seeds-cn/MP7366

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The same Rallis page describes it as an early-maturing hybrid with higher yield and fodder, highly compact spikes, and bold greyish grain; it also describes a medium-maturity hybrid with the highest yield compared with hybrids available on the market (the page does not clearly tie that second line to MP7366) -- https://www.rallis.com/india-business/seeds-cn/MP7366
No multi-location trial data, yield numbers, or AICRP results were found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
No search evidence found for parentage, breeding method, or QTL. The parentage MP14PO28A x MP15PO35R (female MP14PO28A, male MP15PO35R, both developed at Rallis R&D) comes from the supplied variety record only and is not verified by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Rallis India Limited is the developing company per the supplied record. The Rallis product page for MP7366 is the only search result that names this variety and confirms the company's marketing of it -- https://www.rallis.com/india-business/seeds-cn/MP7366
No breeder name or lead scientist was found.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, email, phone, postal address, or institute contact page for this variety was returned. The Rallis product page is the only page for MP7366 and was not checked for a contact section because only a snippet was returned.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. The paper search for "MP7366 pearl millet research paper" returned only a general review of pearl millet processing (https://doi.org/10.9734/jsrr/2024/v30i41914), which does not name MP7366 and was discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
A Flipkart listing names "Naaz Hybrid Dhaanya MP-7366 Bajra Seeds (1.5 kg)" as a pearl millet seed product -- https://www.flipkart.com/naaz-hybrid-dhaanya-mp-7366-bajra-seeds-pearl-millet-seeds-1-5kg-seed/p/itmb053b0aaec901 . This is a retail listing and the name differs from the Rallis code; it is not confirmed to be the same product. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or Seednet availability record was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Blast: In a disease-indexing screen, NBH 5061 fell in the moderately resistant group, with percent disease index values in the 33 to 56 range reported for that group. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361217779_Screening_of_pearl_millet_promising_hybrids_and_varieties_against_blast_Pyricularia_grisea_by_disease_indexing
- Drought: A drought-trait study of 12 released hybrids and varieties included NBH 5061 among the entries, but the snippet gives no tolerance rating for this variety. -- https://jeb.co.in./journal_issues/202303_mar23/paper_07.pdf
- Drought: No specific drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence rating was found for NBH 5061. -- No evidence found in the retrieved snippets for these stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast: Moderate resistance (see above). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361217779_Screening_of_pearl_millet_promising_hybrids_and_varieties_against_blast_Pyricularia_grisea_by_disease_indexing
- Downy mildew, rust, ergot, and insects: No evidence found for NBH 5061 specifically. The AICPMIP release table lists disease-resistance notes for other hybrids in the same table, not for NBH 5061.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS

- Multi-location stability (peninsular India, B-zone): NBH5061 was identified as one of the ideal genotypes for cultivation across B-zone, alongside 86M86 and KSB. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361712260_GGE_biplot_analysis_for_identification_of_ideal_cultivars_and_testing_locations_of_pearl_millet_Pennisetum_glaucum_LR_Br_for_peninsular_India

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PB 1852 (seednet name: PB 1852 (MH 2224)), Pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum)

Scope note: Four web_search queries were run, covering both names: "PB 1852 Pearl millet variety", "PB 1852 Pearl millet breeder developed by", "PB 1852 Pearl millet research", and "PB 1852 MH 2224 pearl millet seed". A fifth batch of three more queries was then sent in error, over the 4-search limit, and returned a limit error. Nothing from that batch was used. None of the four searches returned a page that names PB 1852 or MH 2224 together with pearl millet. Every heading below is therefore "No evidence found", and the search results that came back are listed so the gap is visible.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searches returned general pages only, such as the Wikipedia pearl millet article (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_millet), which does not mention this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No page in the results names this variety with disease or pest data.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. No multi-location or agronomic trial record for this variety was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. The parentage "PS 95 x PP 110" and the line codes "A, B & R line" come only from the request metadata and were not verified by any retrieved page. The ICRISAT breeding-lines ResearchGate PDF (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274076166_Pearl_Millet_Breeding_Lines_Developed_at_ICRISAT_A_Reservoir_of_Variability_and_Useful_Source_of_Non-Target_Traits) and a ResearchGate "Pearl Millet" chapter (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277692868_Pearl_Millet) were returned, but neither mentions PB 1852, MH 2224, PS 95 or PP 110.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The institution "Bayer Bio Science Pvt. Ltd." appears only in the request metadata. No breeder name was found for this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute, email, phone or address was retrieved for this variety.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, report or thesis naming this variety was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The seed-related search returned no NSC, state corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. The states listed in the request (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Delhi) are unverified. The one potentially relevant result, the AICPMIP released-varieties table (http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf), was returned for the seed query. Its retrieved text did not include PB 1852, MH 2224 or Bayer, so it could not confirm release, notification or state recommendation for this variety. A check of the full PDF, or of the CSC release minutes and the Seednet portal entry directly, would be needed to settle these headings.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RHB-177 (seednet name: RHB-177 (MH-1486)), Pearl millet

Search log: 4 web_search queries were run (variety and release, breeder and institute, research papers, seed availability). Search results were checked by title and opening text only. A later check of the full page text hit the tool's usage limit, so pages could not be re-read in full.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The searches returned no page naming RHB-177 or MH-1486 with drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No page naming this variety reports disease or pest resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. No maturity, yield or multi-location trial data for RHB-177 were returned.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. The parentage ICMA-843-22A x RIB-494 and the code MH-1486 were not confirmed by any returned page. A pearl millet genotype-diversity paper from Rajasthan (academia.edu, "Genetic diversity of total phenolic, flavonoid and antioxidant activity in pearl millet genotypes grown in semi-arid region of Rajasthan") appeared in results, but its snippet did not mention RHB-177, so it was not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.academia.edu/39134492/Genetic_diversity_of_total_phenolic_flavonoid_and_antioxidant_activity_in_pearl_millet_genotypes_grown_in_semi-arid_region_of_Rajasthan

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The institution given in the variety record is Swami Keshwanand Rajasthan Agricultural University, Bikaner. No page returned by the searches named a breeder or development station for RHB-177.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address or contact page for the breeding division was returned. The SKRAU contact page was not reached.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record naming RHB-177 was returned. Results that appeared but were discarded: a pearl millet hybrid breeding review (researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status), which covers hybrids generally, and a Zn fertilization study (biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2022.12.08.519627), which does not name this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for RHB-177 was returned. The ICAR crop-improvement report (icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-12-13.pdf) lists the pearl millet hybrid "RHB 173". That is a different variety and was discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found in the search results. The variety record gives Rajasthan, Haryana and Gujarat. That is the input record, not an independently verified source.

Next steps for a complete record: check the CSC/ICAR release notification for RHB-177 and the SKRAU pearl millet breeding page directly, and search KrishiKosh for RHB-177 theses.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast (Pyricularia grisea): a disease-indexing study places 86M86 among Indian pearl millet hybrids grouped as resistant, based on blast severity PDI. Downy mildew: the CSC variety data states 86M86 (MH 1684) is more downy mildew tolerant than checks; this is not verified by the digest's searched sources. pest_resistance.summary: CSC variety data states MH 1684 has low insect-pest incidence compared with checks. No digest-sourced evidence for specific insect pests: No evidence found.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC variety data: average yield 32 quintal/ha under normal conditions; mean grain yield over different nitrogen doses was 3136 kg/ha. Yield (kg/ha) in Indian trials from the digest: No evidence found in the retrieved extracts.
agronomic_details.stability: The GGE biplot study identifies 86M86 as an ideal genotype across the B-zone of peninsular India. Stability statistics are not reported in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Peninsular India B-zone (GGE biplot study). CSC data lists late maturity in normal Kharif season. Recommended states per CSC data are listed in variety_profile.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CSC variety data: non-lodging stem and very good brace root system, giving tolerance to stalk and root lodging under normal conditions. Morphological characteristics: Unknown. A biofortification comparison places 86M86 in the medium-maturity zone, which conflicts with the late-maturity classification in the release table.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-location GGE biplot study, peninsular India (B-zone): 86M86 identified as an ideal genotype with good fodder yield. (2) Pakistan field trial, Punjab, 2019-2020 (hybrid 86M86 vs. synthetic Sargodha-2011 under NPK levels): 86M86 gave higher dry biomass and a better forage quality profile than the synthetic at the stated NPK doses. This is a Pakistan trial, not an Indian one. (3) Pakistan climate-model study (Faisalabad and Layyah): field observations on 86M86 were used to calibrate CERES-Millet. (4) Biofortification comparison: 86M86 cited as a commercial check with grain iron of about 55-56 mg/kg and zinc of about 39-41 mg/kg, and as the highest-yielding commercial high-iron hybrid in that comparison. (5) Mandor kharif 2018 drought seedling study: 86M86 was a check only, with no rating. (6) Blast screening study: listed among resistant hybrids (see disease_resistance). (7) Line x tester study: 86M86 used as a check for grain yield and rancidity traits; results for 86M86 not reported in the digest.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: 86M86 (seednet name: 86M86 (MH 1684)), Pearl millet

Name note: the release-table name is "86M86" and the code is "MH 1684". Findings below say which name appears in the source. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Blast (Pyricularia grisea) disease-indexing study places 86M86 among hybrids grouped as resistant, based on blast severity PDI; the study is in Indian pearl millet hybrids [name: 86M86] -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361217779_Screening_of_pearl_millet_promising_hybrids_and_varieties_against_blast_Pyricularia_grisea_by_disease_indexing
- Drought: 86M86 served only as a check in a PEG-induced seedling water-stress study at Mandor (kharif 2018); the study reports no tolerance rating specific to 86M86 [name: 86M86] -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-5718
- Heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast: see the screening study above (listed among resistant hybrids) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361217779_Screening_of_pearl_millet_promising_hybrids_and_varieties_against_blast_Pyricularia_grisea_by_disease_indexing
- Rust, downy mildew, ergot, and insect resistance for 86M86 specifically: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Multi-location GGE biplot study (peninsular India, B-zone): 86M86 identified as an ideal genotype for cultivation across the B-zone, with good fodder yield [name: 86M86] -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361712260_GGE_biplot_analysis_for_identification_of_ideal_cultivars_and_testing_locations_of_pearl_millet_Pennisetum_glaucum_LR_Br_for_peninsular_India
- Same GGE study table lists 86M86 with 2012 release and Pioneer Overseas Corp. as the source -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361712260_GGE_biplot_analysis_for_identification_of_ideal_cultivars_and_testing_locations_of_pearl_millet_Pennisetum_glaucum_LR_Br_for_peninsular_India
- Pakistan field trial (Punjab, 2019-2020; hybrid 86M86 vs. synthetic Sargodha-2011 under NPK levels): 86M86 gave a higher dry biomass and forage quality profile than the synthetic at the stated NPK doses; this is a Pakistan trial, not an Indian one [name: 86M86] -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42729-023-01509-8 ; https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023JSSPN..23.6542S/abstract
- Pakistan climate-model study (Faisalabad and Layyah): field observations on hybrid 86M86 used to calibrate CERES-Millet; the study is Pakistan-based -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11356-018-3925-7
- Biofortification comparison: 86M86 cited as a commercial check with high grain iron (about 55-56 mg/kg) and zinc (about 39-41 mg/kg), and as the highest-yielding commercial high-iron hybrid in that comparison; newer biofortified hybrids flowered about a week earlier, placing 86M86 in the medium-maturity zone -- https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0472/9/5/106 ; https://oar.icrisat.org/9394/
- Maturity: the national release list describes 86M86 (MH 1684) as late maturing -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Yield (kg/ha) in Indian trials: No evidence found in the retrieved extracts.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage M128F x M138R (female x male); breeding-line codes as hybrid MH 1684 [name: 86M86 (MH 1684)] -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Hybrid breeding review lists 86M86 (MH 1684) with parentage M128F x M138R, notification S.O. 1708, dated 26.07.2012 -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status
- Line x tester mating design study (32 hybrids from eight lines and four testers; 86M86 and HHB 67 as checks) for grain yield and rancidity traits -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/pbr.13091
- QTL, marker, or genome-sequence studies for 86M86: No evidence found.
- Breeding method: hybrid (cytoplasmic male sterile x restorer type) breeding is implied by the parental pairing; the sources do not name the method explicitly -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing firm: Pioneer Overseas Corporation (Hyderabad), per the national release table [name: 86M86 (MH 1684)] -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Named lead breeder or scientist for 86M86: No evidence found.
- Institute or station of breeding (other than Pioneer Overseas Corp., Hyderabad): No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
MP-7792 (MH-1609) Pearl millet: EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC/AICPMIP release records use "MP-7792" (also written MP 7792), with MH-1609 given as its code. The Seednet name "MP-7792 (MH-1609)" was not retrieved directly; the evidence below refers to the same entry under both names. Four searches were run; the Seednet portal itself did not appear in the results.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Not found in the retrieved text for MP-7792 (MH-1609) beyond a possible note of downy mildew resistance (see DISEASE AND PEST). No drought, heat, salinity, or flood data located. -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- The AICPMIP release table has a "resistant to downy mildew" phrase in a cell block that also contains this entry's row, but the table layout is garbled, so it is unclear whether it applies to MP-7792 or to the adjacent entry. Treat as unverified. -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The millets.res.in release list describes the MP-7792 row as medium height with yellow anther colour, cylindrical grey earheads, and grey-coloured globular seed. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Maturity is given as "Late maturing" in the same garbled row block; the attribution is uncertain, so treat as unverified. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Yield data: No evidence found for MP-7792 (MH-1609) in trial results. The search returned general pearl millet variety performance studies that do not name this entry. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8202413/

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage/pedigree as listed in the release table: "M001A x S.O. 1708" (the task record says Unknown; this record should be checked against the original CSC minutes). -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf ; http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Breeding-line codes appearing in the same row: M001A and M004R (E). Their roles as female/male parents are not stated in the retrieved text. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Breeding method: this entry is listed as a hybrid under private-sector hybrid releases, which suggests a hybrid breeding route, but the method is not stated explicitly. -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status
- Genome resources / QTL / marker studies: No evidence found for MP-7792 (MH-1609). A review mentions MP-7792 in an abstract list of breeding materials, without molecular detail. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380432206_Recent_advances_in_the_production_technology_and_breeding_Of_pearl_millet

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Metahelix Life Sciences Limited (Metahelix Life Science Ltd.), Bangalore. This is a private company, so the variety is a private-sector hybrid rather than a public-sector (SAU/ICAR) release. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf ; https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level contact: only the location "Bangalore" is given for Metahelix Life Science Ltd. No official email, phone, postal address, or contact page URL was retrieved. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in the retrieved text (2024 year inferred from the ResearchGate ID; not confirmed). Recent advances in the production technology and breeding of pearl millet. Review article listing MP-7792 among breeding materials -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380432206_Recent_advances_in_the_production_technology_and_breeding_Of_pearl_millet
- Authors not shown in the retrieved text (year not shown). Hybrid breeding in pearl millet: past and present status. Review that lists MP-7792 (MH-1609) among private-sector hybrids and attributes it to Metahelix Life Science Ltd., Bangalore -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status
- Not located: AICRP/ICAR annual reports, KrishiKosh theses, and peer-reviewed trial papers naming MP-7792 (MH-1609). The release list at http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf is the primary official record found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for MP-7792 (MH-1609) from NSC, State Seed Corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales, or private dealers. The search returned unrelated US or generic hybrid pearl millet seed sellers, which were discarded. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8202413/ (search returned, not relevant)

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh (listed as "UP and MP" in the release table). This matches the raw list provided. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf ; http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

RELEASE RECORD
- Notification/release date: 26.07.2012 (as shown in the release table for MP-7792 / MH-1609). Consistent with year of release 2012. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf ; http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

Searches run (4 of 4 allowed):
1. Variety/release query: returned general pearl millet reviews (e.g., a ResearchGate review on climate-resilient pearl millet). No page mentions NBH 4903, MH 2035 or Balwan.
2. Breeder/institute query: returned a ResearchGate heterosis-breeding review that lists Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan only as an author affiliation. It does not mention this variety, so I have discarded it.
3. Research/publication query: returned the Millet Conclave 2023 compendium, which has no mention of this variety. Discarded.
4. Seed availability query: returned the same general pearl millet review. Nothing about seed sources for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found.
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found.
GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. The parentage "NB 105A X NB 98R" is present only in the input record and was not verified by any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute divisional, email, phone or address was tied to this variety. I did not attribute the institute-level affiliation from the heterosis review to this variety.
PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found in search results. The input record lists Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Tamil Nadu, but this is unverified; these states come from the input only.

Suggested next steps for a verified record: check the Seednet portal entry directly under both name forms, and the CSC/AICRP-Pearl Millet 2018 release notification and its annual report. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RHB 233 (MH 2173), Pearl millet

Search status: four web_search queries were run. The tool quota was then exhausted, so pages could not be opened in full. Findings below come only from the search snippets, and the coverage is thin. Both names (RHB 233 and RHB 233 (MH 2173)) were searched. The CGIAR record matches the Seednet name exactly.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No downy mildew, blast, smut or pest resistance data was returned for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A ResearchGate paper on biofortified pearl millet cultivars compares yields of several entries, and its snippet lists RHB 233 alongside RHB 234 in a group described as having similar grain yield. The snippet is ambiguous: it also describes these entries as hybrids, which conflicts with a variety release. Treat this as unverified until the full text is checked. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375670979_Enhancing_productivity_and_nutrition_with_biofortified_pearl_millet_cultivars

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found beyond the input record. The parentage given in the input (ICMA 99444 A4 x RIB 15176, with RIB 15176 from ICRISAT and purified at RARI Durgapura up to F7) was not confirmed by any search result. A CGIAR record describes the entry as a biofortified iron pearl millet, which suggests breeding for grain iron content (Project P333). -- https://cgspace.cgiar.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/307e884d-c345-41fb-99cb-eb0f47ea7b96/content

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No breeder names were found in the results. The release institution named in the input is Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute (RARI), Durgapura, Jaipur. Its involvement is not confirmed by any search result. The CGIAR record is a 2021 innovation report for a biofortified iron pearl millet variety and does not name a breeder in the snippet. -- https://cgspace.cgiar.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/307e884d-c345-41fb-99cb-eb0f47ea7b96/content

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No email, phone, postal address or institute contact page for RARI Durgapura or for this variety was returned. The ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research (Rajendranagar, Hyderabad) address appears on the ResearchGate paper, but it is the paper's affiliation and not a contact for this variety, so it is not attributed here.

PUBLICATIONS --
- Enhancing productivity and nutrition with biofortified pearl millet cultivars. Authors not captured in the snippet (2023 or later, per the ResearchGate record). Journal not captured. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375670979_Enhancing_productivity_and_nutrition_with_biofortified_pearl_millet_cultivars
- Reporting 2021 Innovation #394: Iron Pearl Millet variety RHB 233 (MH 2173). CGIAR innovation report, 2021. -- https://cgspace.cgiar.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/307e884d-c345-41fb-99cb-eb0f47ea7b96/content

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was returned. Seednet was not reached through search.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found in the search results. The states listed in the input (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu) are unverified against a CSC minutes or Seednet source.

Next steps for a complete record: open the Seednet entry for "RHB 233 (MH 2173)" and the CSC notification minutes for the release name "RHB 233", check the full ResearchGate and CGIAR texts for the breeder names and yield data, and contact RARI Durgapura directly for contact details and seed sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RHB 234 (MH 2174), Pearl millet

Name note: the release-minutes name "RHB 234" and the Seednet name "RHB 234 (MH 2174)" are used interchangeably in the sources below. Most evidence refers to RHB 234 with MH 2174 as the variety code. The AICRP success-stories page, the AICPMIP variety table, and the HarvestPlus page all pair RHB 234 with MH 2174. The HarvestPlus page also lists "ICMH 1504" as an alias, which I could not confirm elsewhere. Searches under the Seednet name returned no separate Seednet page.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to RHB 234. The search returned only general pearl millet pages and a Hisar study of HHB 234, which is a different hybrid. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375670979_Enhancing_productivity_and_nutrition_with_biofortified_pearl_millet_cultivars

DISEASE AND PEST
RHB 234 is described as resistant to major diseases and insect pests, but the page does not name specific diseases. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375670979_Enhancing_productivity_and_nutrition_with_biofortified_pearl_millet_cultivars
RHB 234 is listed among hybrids with the same general resistance wording in the ICAR Indian Farming (January 2023) issue. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf
The RARI 2024-25 annual progress report attributes downy mildew and blast resistance to RHB 223, not RHB 234, so it is not used here. -- https://www.sknau.ac.in/uploads/Annual%20Progress%20Report%20RARI%202024--25.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
A rainfed sowing-date study reports that RHB 234 gave the highest yield and profitability among the varieties tested, with 15 July sowing performing best. Authors, year and institution are not shown in the snippet. -- http://www.plantarchives.org/article/1691-1696%20(383).pdf
A study of biofortified cultivars reports that RHB 234, with similar grain yield to the other second-set hybrids, was released in 2019–20. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375670979_Enhancing_productivity_and_nutrition_with_biofortified_pearl_millet_cultivars
The ICAR-IIRR CRP page lists RHB 234 as "Identified" (not released) with RARI and SKNAU as CRP centres, and gives Fe 84 ppm and Zn 41 ppm. -- https://icar-iirr.org/CRP/index.php/pearl-millets
A nutritional-quality comparison reports RHB 234 with high fat and moisture values among biofortified entries. -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/article/view/1174/7-9-118

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Breeding-line code: RHB 234 = MH 2174 (AICRP success stories, AICPMIP table). -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/pearl/success-stories/ ; http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
Parentage (ICMA 02333 A4 x RIB 15177), breeding method and F7 purification at RARI Durgapura: No evidence found in the search results. The parentage supplied in the brief could not be verified from any page searched.
Biofortification: the variety is an iron-and-zinc biofortified hybrid, with Fe 84 ppm and Zn 41 ppm. -- https://icar-iirr.org/CRP/index.php/pearl-millets
QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found for RHB 234. The RIB 15178, RIB 15185 and RIB 15186 lines in the RARI report are different lines and are not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.sknau.ac.in/uploads/Annual%20Progress%20Report%20RARI%202024--25.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Release is credited to the AICRP on Pearl Millet, SKNAU Jaipur, in collaboration with agricultural universities of Rajasthan. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375670979_Enhancing_productivity_and_nutrition_with_biofortified_pearl_millet_cultivars
The developing centre is the Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute (RARI), Durgapura, as the AICRP PM centre. -- https://icar-iirr.org/CRP/index.php/pearl-millets ; https://www.sknau.ac.in/uploads/Annual%20Progress%20Report%20RARI%202024--25.pdf
Lead breeder for RHB 234: No evidence found. Dr S. K. Jain is named as In-charge of the AICRP on Pearl Millet at RARI, an institutional role only, so he is not attributed as the breeder. -- https://eng.ruralvoice.in/agritech/icrisat-and-partners-announce-release-of-the-world-first-three-way-pearl-millet-hybrid.html
Pedigree: the parentage source is the brief supplied with the task, not a search result.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder email, phone or direct address was found for RHB 234. Institute-level contact only:
AICRP on Pearl Millet coordinating unit, Mandor, Jodhpur 342 304, Rajasthan, India (address as printed in the AICRP seed production publication; no email or phone given). -- https://oar.icrisat.org/9237/1/Pearl%20Millet%20Seed_2.pdf
Dr S. K. Jain, In-charge, AICRP on Pearl Millet, RARI (role only; no email or phone found). -- https://eng.ruralvoice.in/agritech/icrisat-and-partners-announce-release-of-the-world-first-three-way-pearl-millet-hybrid.html
RARI Durgapura postal address, email and phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown (n.d./2023?). Sowing dates and varieties on growth, productivity and profitability of pearl millet (Plant Archives, article 1691-1696). -- http://www.plantarchives.org/article/1691-1696%20(383).pdf
Satyavathi et al. / Authors not shown (2023). Enhancing productivity and nutrition with biofortified pearl millet cultivars. Indian Farming / ResearchGate, ICAR-IIMR authors per affiliation line -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375670979_Enhancing_productivity_and_nutrition_with_biofortified_pearl_millet_cultivars
Authors not shown (year not shown). A comparative study on comprehensive nutritional profiling of indigenous non-bio-fortified and bio-fortified varieties and bio-fortified hybrids of pearl millets. PMC -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9998779/
Authors not shown (year not shown). Extension Journal nutritional-quality study of biofortified pearl millet varieties. Extension Journal -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/article/view/1174/7-9-118
Peer-reviewed or KrishiKosh thesis/AICRP annual-report entries specific to RHB 234: No evidence found beyond the items above. The RARI 2024-25 annual progress report is the only AICRP report located -- https://www.sknau.ac.in/uploads/Annual%20Progress%20Report%20RARI%202024--25.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
Rajasthan State Seeds Corporation availability list includes RHB-234 (figure 1000.00, unit not stated in snippet, likely quintal). -- http://rajseeds.org/AvailabilityOfSeeds.html
A retail listing for HYBRID BAJRA / RHB-234 from NSC-KURNOOL (1.5 kg pack). -- https://www.mystore.in/en/product/hybrid-5303-bajra-seed
Seednet portal listing: No evidence found; the seednet.gov.in page was not returned by any search.
KVK, SAU seed sales, other dealers: No evidence found for RHB 234.
Not attributed: Laxmi 234, Govinda Research Hybrid Bajra, and other dealer listings are different products and are excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Rajasthan, Haryana, Gujarat, Punjab, Delhi, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375670979_Enhancing_productivity_and_nutrition_with_biofortified_pearl_millet_cultivars
The AICPMIP table gives Rajasthan, Gujarat and Haryana in its notification row for RHB 234. The row is partly garbled and should be checked against the CSC minutes. -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

MATURITY AND YIELD (for the record)
Maturity is medium. Grain yield of about 3168 kg/ha appears in the data row for RHB 234, but the column header is not confirmed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375670979_Enhancing_productivity_and_nutrition_with_biofortified_pearl_millet_cultivars

Release dates to verify: the sources give 2019 (AICRP PM table) and 2018 for the AICPMIP notification row (S.O. 1379(E), 27.03.2018). The 2018 notification and the 2019 release year conflict and need checking against CSC minutes.
