search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Moderately resistant (MR) to wilt diseases, per a central variety table that lists Chhattisgarh Arhar-1 (RPS 2007-10) at IGKV, Raipur. Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Listed with less incidence of Sterility Mosaic Disease (SMD) and Phytophthora Stem Blight (PSB), in the same central variety table. The table row is partly garbled, so treat this as a summary. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
Pod borer, Helicoverpa and other pest resistance: No evidence found for this variety. The pest-resistance lists in the search results name other varieties only. -- http://dpd.gov.in/Pigeonpea.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Growth habit: indeterminate, semi-spreading, early maturing, suited to the pigeonpea-wheat system (the descriptor sits beside the Chhattisgarh Arhar-1 entry, but the table layout is garbled, so the attribution is probable rather than certain). -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
Maturity: 165-175 days in the same table row. Yield is printed as "Kh 18-20", with the unit unclear. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
Multi-location or field-trial results for this variety: No evidence found. The Chhattisgarh germplasm study and the spacing study found in search are not about this variety and were discarded. -- https://doi.org/10.9734/ijpss/2021/v33i1630537 (discarded: landraces, not this variety)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage "Amar x ICPL 887119 (Asha)": No evidence found. "ICPL-87119" appears in a table row for another variety, so it was not attributed. -- http://dpd.gov.in/Pigeonpea.pdf
Breeding line code (RPS 2007-10): recorded as the variety code in the central variety table. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
Breeding method, QTL/marker studies, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur, Chhattisgarh, per the central variety table. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
Lead breeder or scientist name(s) and station: No evidence found. -- search 2 returned only general pigeonpea breeding reviews.

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder email, phone, postal address, institute division or contact page: No evidence found. The one contact found (lupadhyay@gmail.com, phone 01991 28780) belongs to a Jammu KVK technical bulletin and was discarded.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found for a paper, AICRP/ICAR report, thesis or conference paper that names Chhattisgarh Arhar-1. The Chhattisgarh germplasm paper by Pandey (2021) is about native landraces, not this variety, and was discarded. -- https://doi.org/10.9734/ijpss/2021/v33i1630537

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Seed listings returned were for other varieties (Pusa 16, Bahar, generic arhar) or unrelated products and were discarded. -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/msc-arhar-bahar-pigeon-pea-seeds
A 2023-24 central pulses report lists "CG Arhar-1" in a list of locations, but the context does not say what it refers to, so it was not used as seed-availability evidence. -- http://dpd.gov.in/Annual%20Report%20%202023-24%2014.01.2025.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Krishna (LRG 105), Pigeon pea

Name note: Both names refer to the same line. Sources use "Krishna (LRG 105)" or "LRG-105 released under the name Krishna." Findings below cite whichever name the page uses. Four searches were run.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Wilt and sterility mosaic disease (SMD) resistance is reported for Krishna (LRG 105) in the central-government variety list. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- On-farm trials in Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, recorded no wilt incidence for LRG-105 in 2019 and 2020, while susceptible LRG-41 showed wilt. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue11S/PartK/S-10-10-219-287.pdf
- The SMD evaluation rated LRG-105 as moderately resistant, with 26.33% disease incidence. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/258351610_Evaluation_of_pigeonpea_genotypes_against_Sterility_Mosaic_Disease_SMD_caused_by_the_mite_vector_Aceria_cajani
- The ICAR Kharif advisory lists LRG 105 among sterility-mosaic-tolerant varieties. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/ICAR-En-Kharif-Agro-Advisories-for-Farmers-2025.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The rainfed trial below reports yield only.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Wilt resistance and SMD resistance are the reported traits (see Stress Tolerance). -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Pod borer and pod fly resistance: No evidence found for LRG-105/Krishna.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is listed as 165–180 days. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Potential yield is listed as 13–15 q/ha (the dpd row gives this range for Krishna). -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Rainfed demonstrations in Parvathipuram-Manyam (kharif 2021 and 2022) gave LRG 105 (Krishna) 6.5 q/ha pooled, against 4.8 q/ha for the local variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/392281238_Performance_of_Redgram_Variety_LRG-105_in_under_Rainfed_Conditions_of_Parvathipuram-Manyam_District
- Net returns were reported as Rs 25,810 under LRG-105 against Rs 15,254 under the local variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/392281238_Performance_of_Redgram_Variety_LRG-105_in_under_Rainfed_Conditions_of_Parvathipuram-Manyam_District
- Farmer-field trials in Chittoor (2019 and 2020) recorded 409 kg/ha and 371 kg/ha for LRG-105, against 198 kg/ha and 158 kg/ha for LRG-41. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue11S/PartK/S-10-10-219-287.pdf
- Multi-location stability study (33 advanced medium-duration lines plus six checks, rainfed, three seasons): LRG-105 is listed in the stability table, but the columns are not clear in the retrieved text. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/12626/1/Indian%20Journal%20of%20Agricultural%20Research_56_2_129-134_2022.pdf
- Seeding and fertilizer guidance: The ICAR advisory gives general pigeon pea seeding rates and nutrient doses, not LRG-105-specific ones. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/ICAR-En-Kharif-Agro-Advisories-for-Farmers-2025.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: ICPL 7414 x ICPL 87119 (the ANGRAU table). -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Redgram.pdf
- Breeding method: Pedigree method. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Redgram.pdf
- Release year and route: 2020, released through SVRC. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Redgram.pdf
- Discrepancy: The parent is written as "ICP 7414" in the brief and "ICPL 7414" in the ANGRAU table. The ANGRAU spelling is used here, but the brief's spelling should be checked.
- Discrepancy: Other sources give release in 2019 (the Pharma Innovation Journal paper and the SMD paper). The ANGRAU table and the dpd list give 2020.
- Breeding-line code: LRG 105 is the code. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Redgram.pdf
- QTL, markers, genome resources for LRG-105/Krishna: No evidence found. Parent ICPL 87119 pages discussing genome sequencing or pre-breeding were excluded because they do not name Krishna or LRG 105.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Lam, Andhra Pradesh, under ANGRAU. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The ICRISAT paper lists RARS, Lam among the institutes supplying entries, including LRG-105. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/12626/1/Indian%20Journal%20of%20Agricultural%20Research_56_2_129-134_2022.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level only: Acharya N G Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), Guntur, is named as the releasing university. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/258351610_Evaluation_of_pigeonpea_genotypes_against_Sterility_Mosaic_Disease_SMD_caused_by_the_mite_vector_Aceria_cajani
- Institute site found in results: angrau.ac.in. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Redgram.pdf
- Email, phone, postal address of RARS Lam or the breeder: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2021). Assessment of wilt and sterility mosaic disease resistant pigeonpea variety LRG-105 in Chittoor district of Andhra Pradesh (title partly truncated in retrieved text). The Pharma Innovation Journal 2021; SP-10(11): 732-735. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue11S/PartK/S-10-10-219-287.pdf
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). Performance of Redgram Variety LRG-105 under Rainfed Conditions of Parvathipuram-Manyam District. Journal/report not identified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/392281238_Performance_of_Redgram_Variety_LRG-105_in_under_Rainfed_Conditions_of_Parvathipuram-Manyam_District
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). Evaluation of pigeonpea genotypes against Sterility Mosaic Disease (SMD) caused by the mite vector, Aceria cajani. Journal/report not identified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/258351610_Evaluation_of_pigeonpea_genotypes_against_Sterility_Mosaic_Disease_SMD_caused_by_the_mite_vector_Aceria_cajani
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2022). Stability study of 33 advanced medium-duration pigeonpea lines plus checks, including LRG-105. drought.details: The release article describes IPA 203 as suited to rainfed conditions in the north-east plain zone, but no drought tolerance mechanisms or drought trial data for IPA 203 were found in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Fusarium wilt: IIPR's technology listing gives resistance to Fusarium wilt as a special character of IPA 203. The release article states that wilt can cause up to 100% loss if it occurs at the pre-podding stage, and that no long-duration cultivar then in use was wilt resistant, making IPA 203's resistance a distinguishing trait. Multiple disease resistance: the IIPR breeding page describes IPA 203 as a high-yielding, multiple-disease-resistant long-duration line, but the specific diseases are not named in the digest. Sterility mosaic: the release article notes it causes heavy losses in humid high-rainfall areas of the north-east plain zone, but IPA 203's reaction to sterility mosaic was not confirmed in the text retrieved.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No pest resistance data for IPA 203 were found.

agronomic_details.yield: IIPR lists potential yield of 25-28 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for the north-east plain zone (rainfed conditions). The release article states suitability for central and eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal. A review cites IPA 203 as a long-duration variety for the north-east plain, with empirical evidence of early vigor (genetic inheritance not reported). Seasonal fit: Kharif season.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-compact plant type (plant-type classification). Light brown, medium-size seed of 12-14 g per 100 seeds (IIPR technology listing).
agronomic_details.field_trials: IIPR technology listing: potential yield 25-28 q/ha and duration 249-255 days. Release article: contains a package-of-practices table for IPA 203 (details not retrieved in the digest). Patna (Bihar) reference: calls IPA 203 a leading long-duration variety, citing AICRP on Kharif Pulses 2023-24 data. A Bengaluru long-term sowing-window study (2004-2020) is not attributed to IPA 203 because it does not state that it tested this variety. No other trial results were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The release-minutes name is recorded as "Pigeonpea," which is generic, and the Seednet name is Unknown. All evidence below refers to the pigeonpea variety IPA 203 (Prakash), the only pigeonpea release matching the given institution and recommended states. Parentage, year of release in the CSC minutes, and Seednet entry were not confirmed.

Search limit: The tool-call budget ran out after four searches, so the seed-availability search was not run. Findings under SEED AVAILABILITY are therefore "No evidence found" for that search attempt. The stress and disease findings come from the search results, not a dedicated query.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- IIPR's technology listing gives the special characters as resistance to Fusarium wilt, with light brown, medium-size seed of 12-14 g per 100 seeds -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/
STRESS TOLERANCE -- The IPA 203 release article describes it as suited to rainfed conditions in the north-east plain zone, where wilt can cause up to 100% loss if it occurs at the pre-podding stage -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369745589_IPA_203_A_Promising_Variety_of_long-duration_pigeonpea
STRESS TOLERANCE -- The same article says no long-duration cultivar then in use was wilt resistant, which makes IPA 203's resistance a distinguishing trait; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for IPA 203 were found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369745589_IPA_203_A_Promising_Variety_of_long-duration_pigeonpea

DISEASE AND PEST -- The IIPR breeding page describes IPA 203 as a high-yielding, multiple-disease-resistant long-duration line -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/309136303_Breeding_Improved_Cultivars_of_Pigeonpea_in_India
DISEASE AND PEST -- The release article notes sterility mosaic causes heavy losses in humid high-rainfall areas of the north-east plain zone; IPA 203's reaction to sterility mosaic was not confirmed in the text retrieved -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369745589_IPA_203_A_Promising_Variety_of_long-duration_pigeonpea

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- IIPR lists potential yield of 25-28 q/ha, duration of 249-255 days, and recommended area as the north-east plain zone -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The release article contains a package-of-practices table for IPA 203 and states suitability for central and eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369745589_IPA_203_A_Promising_Variety_of_long-duration_pigeonpea
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A Patna (Bihar) reference calls IPA 203 a leading long-duration variety, citing AICRP on Kharif Pulses 2023-24 data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390795044_Pigeonpea
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A Bengaluru long-term sowing-window study (2004-2020) uses pigeonpea but does not state that it tested IPA 203, so it is not attributed to this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384953869_Weather_based_Yield_Prediction_of_Pigeonpea_Crop_with_the_Resource_Use_Efficiency_under_Varied_Sowing_Windows

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- The release article states IPA 203 was derived from a cross, but the parent names are cut off in the retrieved text, so parentage is unconfirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369745589_IPA_203_A_Promising_Variety_of_long-duration_pigeonpea
GENETICS AND QTL -- Plant-type classification places IPA 203 as semi-compact, alongside compact Bahar and spreading MA 6 -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PA-203-A-high-yielding-multiple-disease-resistant-line-of-long-duration-pigeonpea_fig2_309136303
GENETICS AND QTL -- A cleistogamy study introgressed the trait from ICPL 87154 into crosses with IPA 203 and Bahar; selected lines RCEA 14-1 and RCEA 14-5 were reported to match IPA 203 yield -- https://www.jscimedcentral.com/public/assets/articles/plantbiology-8-1116.pdf
GENETICS AND QTL -- A review cites IPA 203 as a long-duration variety for the north-east plain, with empirical evidence of its early vigor, though genetic inheritance of that vigor is not reported -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5982186/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Dr. Indra Prakash Singh, Principal Scientist and Acting Project Coordinator (Pigeonpea), is credited with developing and releasing IPA 203 (NEPZ) and IPA 206 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/team/dr-indra-prakash-singh/
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution is ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh; the Crop Improvement Division handles pigeonpea -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/cimprovment/
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- A release-article author is listed as Choudhary at ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region; the first name and role in IPA 203 development are not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369745589_IPA_203_A_Promising_Variety_of_long-duration_pigeonpea

disease_resistance.research_summary: Fusarium wilt: IIPR's technology listing gives resistance to Fusarium wilt as a special character of IPA 203. The release article states that wilt can cause up to 100% loss if it occurs at the pre-podding stage, and that no long-duration cultivar then in use was wilt resistant, making IPA 203's resistance a distinguishing trait. Multiple disease resistance: the IIPR breeding page describes IPA 203 as a high-yielding, multiple-disease-resistant long-duration line, but the specific diseases are not named in the digest. Sterility mosaic: the release article notes it causes heavy losses in humid high-rainfall areas of the north-east plain zone, but IPA 203's reaction to sterility mosaic was not confirmed in the text retrieved.

csc_fields.special_traits: Medium duration. Medium maturity, field resistant to late blade. High dry matter. Plant height: 70-80 cm. Haulms: Medium tall, semi-erect, plant canopy, semi-compact, vigorous. Stem: Many, medium thick, predominantly green with red-brown secondary pigment randomly distributed, wings feebly developed and wavy. Leaf: Intermediate, dark grey green, smooth, glossy, rachis, green. Large and many. Leaflets: Width medium, ovate-Lanceolate, margin entire, coalescence absent, midrib green. Folioles: Many, small. Foliage colour: Green. Tubers: Size medium, long oblong, white cream, smooth, eyes shallow, normal eyebrows, flesh white, texture mealy. Sprout: Red purple with green at the apex, shape spherical, pubescence of base slight and tip closed. Dormancy: Medium. Stolen: Medium. Flowers: Light red, moderate flowering, flower stalk green, calyx green, bud red, pedicel articulation above the middle, corolla primarily light red with tip on both sides white, corolla shape stellate, anthers orange, pollen fertile, anther cone normally developed, style longer than stamen column and stigma bio-lobed. Specific gravity: 1.093. Dry matter: 22.4 per cent. Cooking quality: Good. Texture: Floury. Stem-end discolouration: None. Medium maturing with Good keeping, responsive to fertilizers. Field resistant to late blight (Phystophthora infestans).
csc_fields.additional_notes: Recommended for notification for entire country.

csc_fields.special_traits: Plant height: 80-85 cm. Haulms: Tall, erect, medium-compact, vigorous. Stem: Many, thick, not coloured at base, well developed straight wings. Leaves: open, rachis green. Leaflets: Oval, rough surface with entire margin, Large and many. Folioles: Dark green. Tubers: Oval, Pale yellow, medium sized, fleet eyes, light yellow flesh. Dormancy: Medium (10 weeks). Stolons: Medium. Flowers: White, medium in size, moderate flowering in hills, sometime scanty flowering also observed in plains. Sprouts: Cylindrical, slightly red purple and hairy. Maturity (range in number of days): 75-85 days. Maturity Group: Early under short day conditions. Agronomical features: Can be grown as early (0 to 75 days harvest) variety. Recommended as main season crop variety under normal fertilization. Quality of produce: Good keeping quality (Storage behaviour at ambient temperature). Specific gravity (at 75 days harvest): 1.06. Dry matter (at 75 days harvest): 15%. Cooking quality: Good, cooks well in 30 minutes, tastes good. Texture: Waxy. Stem-end discolouration: Absent. Reaction to major diseases: Moderate resistance to late blight and resistant to early blight. Reaction to major pests: No major pest problem for potato crop during main season. This variety is a Nutrient efficient variety. Performs well under low fertility conditions.
csc_fields.yield_performance: 25-28 tonnes per hectare under early (75 days) harvest.
csc_fields.additional_notes: Seed rate - 3.0-3.5 tonnes/ha.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PMV 442 (GPUP 25), Proso millet (Panicum miliaceum)

Name note: The release-minute name is "PMV 442" and the Seednet name is "PMV 442 (GPUP 25)". Almost all evidence uses "PMV 442 (GPUP 25)" or "PMV 442", and I have treated both as this variety. Pages that mention only other proso millet varieties (GPUP 28, GPUP 21, TNAU lines) were excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderately resistant to brown spot and shoot fly is listed for PMV 442 (GPUP 25) in a small-millet variety table, which I found only through the "All states" entry. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. The general statements that proso millet withstands drought are not variety-specific and were excluded.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to brown spot and shoot fly (same table as above). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- The UAS Bengaluru small-millets page describes this variety's plant traits but gives no separate disease or pest resistance. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/small-millets-zars-gkvk-bengaluru/
- No evidence found for other disease or pest resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity 70–75 days, erect dwarf plant (85–90 cm), non-lodging, narrow leaves, semi-compact medium panicle. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.002
- Station trials: 29.78% seed-yield gain over local check GPUP 21 and 16.39% over national check TNAU 145. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.002
- All India Coordinated Trials: 12.99% over GPUP 21, 23.73% over TNAU 151, 12.44% over TNAU 164 at national level. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.002 ; also https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372966459_GPUP_28_A_New_High_Yielding_Proso_Millet_Variety_Panicum_miliaceum_L_for_Southern_and_Eastern_Dry_Zones_of_Karnataka
- Grain composition: calcium 26.0 mg/100 g, iron 6 mg/100 g, protein 7.41%, crude fibre 9.72 g/100 g. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.002
- Yield range 14–16 (unit as printed in the table, presumably q/ha) and maturity 70–75 days in the small-millets table. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Sowing: July–August is the suggested window; the Assam package lists this variety as suitable there, which is not in the CSC recommendation. -- https://www.arias.in/download/AMM/Proso%20millet%20POP%20(English).pdf
- Starch study using grain of this cultivar. -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2772753X23002411

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: derivative of GPMS 109 × GPMS 908, developed by recombining desirable characteristics of both parents. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.002 ; https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/small-millets-zars-gkvk-bengaluru/
- Breeding line code: GPUP 25. Germplasm/IC number: IC 629228. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/small-millets-zars-gkvk-bengaluru/
- Breeding method: the brief parentage line says pedigree selection, and a related page mentions a homozygosity check selecting GPUP 25. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355465828_A_new_high_yielding_proso_millet_variety_Panicum_miliaceum_L_PMV_442
- No evidence found for QTL, marker-trait associations, genes, or genome resources specific to this variety. The search results mention general proso millet SSR and genome papers, which do not name this variety, so I excluded them.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed at the AICRP on Small Millets Project Coordinating Unit, University of Agricultural Sciences, GKVK, Bengaluru, and released in 2019 at central level. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.002
- Notified in the 83rd meeting of the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties, held 4 October 2019. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372966459_GPUP_28_A_New_High_Yielding_Proso_Millet_Variety_Panicum_miliaceum_L_for_Southern_and_Eastern_Dry_Zones_of_Karnataka
- Lead author and corresponding breeder: C. Nandini (first-listed author of the 2021 release paper). The source does not name a separate lead breeder. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.002
- Other named contributors are listed under PUBLICATIONS below.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: University of Agricultural Sciences, Bangalore (UAS GKVK), Small Millets, ZARS, GKVK, Bengaluru. Page: https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/small-millets-zars-gkvk-bengaluru/
- No evidence found for an official email, phone number, or postal address for the Small Millets unit or for C. Nandini. The institute page above is the only contact URL found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Nandini, C.; Bhat, S.; Prabhakar; Jayaramegowda; Krishnappa, M.; Srinatha Reddy, S.; Ganiger, P. C.; Palanna, K. B.; Sukanya, T. S.; Boraiah, B.; Kiran, T.; Lavanya Bai, T.; Vinay, N. (2021). A new high yielding proso millet variety (Panicum miliaceum L.): PMV 442. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding 12(1): 9–16 -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.002
- Nandini, C.; Bhat, S.; Prabhakar, J.; Krishnappa, M.; Reddy, S. S.; Ganiger, P. C.; Palanna, B.; Sukanya, T. S.; Boraiah, B.; Kiran, T.; Vinay, N. (2021) cited in: Proso Millet chapter, Springer, https://doi.org/10.1007/978-981-95-1256-0_6
- Starch study on PMV 442 (GPUP 25) grain (author list not confirmed in the snippet). -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2772753X23002411
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report, or conference paper was found for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for listings at NSC, State Seed Corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales, or private dealers for this variety.
- The IIMR table notes that seed of high-yielding varieties is a limitation in general, and that IIMR has set up seed hubs. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Puducherry, as in the CSC raw list and the UAS page. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/small-millets-zars-gkvk-bengaluru/
- A millets booklet lists GPUP 25 (PMV-442) for Tamil Nadu, Uttarakhand, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. -- https://www.millets.res.in/farmer/2025/Millets_chalisa/English/9Millets_chalisa_proso_millet.pdf
- The small-millets table lists it as "All states." -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- The Assam package also recommends it. Assam is outside the CSC list and is flagged here as unverified against the release notification.

drought.details: No drought evidence found in the searched results. The only stress-related item is pod shattering resistance up to 10-12 days after harvest maturity, which is not a drought measure. The digest states this is not separately confirmed as PKV Tara-specific. The CSC record describes the variety as resistant to lodging and shattering, and stress reaction as similar to the check variety, without specifying drought.

heat.details: No heat evidence found in the searched results. The result text was truncated.

salinity.details: No salinity evidence found in the searched results.

flood.details: No flood evidence found in the searched results.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: resistant (CSC variety record supplied in the request). Story Module: Moderately resistant to SMD (sterility mosaic disease) (CSC variety record supplied in the request). Grain mold: described as 'tolerance also promising' in the PDKV circular, under the PKV Tara entry (attribution noted as sitting under the entry but not independently verified). Zonate leaf spot and leaf blight: performance noted in the same circular bullets (no resistance level stated). The digest does not confirm that the circular bullets are specific to PKV Tara.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to girdle beetle, stem fly and charcoal rot, per the PDKV circular (attribution to PKV Tara not independently verified). Pod borer: reaction similar to the check variety (CSC variety record supplied in the request).

agronomic_details.yield: Not found in searched sources. The circular reports higher fodder yield of 129.98 q/ha, but the digest does not confirm this applies to PKV Tara, and grain yield is not reported. The CSC average yield is recorded as Unknown.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for kharif planting in Vidarbha (CSC record supplied in the request). The circular's package for medium-deep black soils under rainfed Vidarbha is not confirmed as specific to this variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Unknown
agronomic_details.field_trials: Circular bullets report: maturity 110 days (conflicts with the CSC range of 154 to 189 days, so not used for the profile); white, lustrous, bold grains; oil 20.5% and protein 44%, described as higher than other varieties; fodder yield 129.98 q/ha. I could not complete the research. The search tool hit its usage limit during my second batch of calls, so I stopped there. The four searches that returned results are listed below. None of them gave verified evidence about 91H97228 or HRI 157.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: 91H97228 (variety_name) / 91 H97228 (HRI 157) (IET 19511) (seednet_variety_name), Rice

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Search 1 (release and trait query) returned a Bihar notified-varieties list PDF (https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf). I saw only a fragment, and it did not show this variety. I did not confirm whether the full document names 91H97228 or HRI 157.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No result I could verify named this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. Search 3 returned a QTL study on the restorer line R998 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5589899/). That is a different rice line, so I discarded it.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. Parentage 6CO21/6MO21 comes only from the input record, not from a search source. The R998 QTL paper above is not about this variety and was discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. Search 2 returned a Bayer hybrid rice transformation document (https://zenodo.org/records/10399640). It describes Bayer's hybrid rice program generally and does not name this variety, so I discarded it. No breeder name was found.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. The only address is the institution address in the input record: Bayer Biosciences Pvt. Ltd., 8-1-39, Tolichowki, Hyderabad - 500 008. This was not verified by any search result, and I found no email, phone, or breeder contact.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. Search 3 returned no paper about this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. Search 4 returned only an unrelated USGS page on wildlife and rice seed (https://www.usgs.gov/publications/rapid-assessment-rice-seed-availability-wildlife-harvested-fields). No seed-channel source was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Not verified by search. The input record lists Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Karnataka, and Puducherry. The Bihar notified-list PDF may bear on release status, but I could not confirm it.

Searches run: 4. Several result items returned by the tool were malformed, so I could not read full page text for all of them. The fifth call was blocked by the tool limit, so the breeder, contact, trial, and publication searches are incomplete.

Suggested next steps: check the full Bihar notified-varieties PDF for 91H97228 or HRI 157; search seednet.gov.in for the variety page; search KrishiKosh and ICAR/AICRP rice reports for "HRI 157"; and check whether Bayer's Indian rice program has a published contact page.

seednet_fields.Parentage: The proposed variety has been developed from a cross CN 1216 X CN 1131-4-4-1-4. Both the parents are pre-breeding materials developed under Shuttle Breeding programme of International Rice Research Institute (IRRI).

Under field screening without artificial inoculation the proposed variety showed Resistant to highly Resistant reaction in respect of False smut and Neck blast diseases, Resistant against Brown spot and Highly Resistant reaction in respect of False smut and Neck blast diseases, Resistant against Brown spot and Highly reaction against BLB

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Arize Tej (HRI-169) (IET 21411), Rice

Name check: the CSC minutes name and the Seednet name are both unconfirmed. The searches returned only "Arize Tej" / "Arize Tej (HRI 169) (IET 21411)" in state and industry lists. I did not reach the Seednet portal, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found. "Arize Tej Gold" is a separate product and was excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The only stress-related traits listed are biotic (see DISEASE AND PEST) -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php

DISEASE AND PEST
- Listed tolerance to leaf blast, BS, sheath rot (Sh.R), rice tungro virus (RTV), gall midge (GM), leaf folder (LF) and stem borer (SB) -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- Note: the abbreviation "BS" is not expanded on the page, so its meaning is uncertain.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration listed as 125 days (2012 entry) and 120 days (2015 entry); ecosystem irrigated; semi-dwarf, about 115-120 cm, long slender grain -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php ; https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Yield listed as 6.5-7.0 t/ha (2015 entry) and 7.0 t/ha (2012 entry) -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm ; https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Multi-location trial data: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage listed as C002/M012 (hybrid); this is a code pair, with no male-sterile or restorer line names given -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- Breeding method: hybrid (three-line/CMS system not stated). Breeding-line code HRI-169 and IET 21411 are listed in the sources above.
- QTL, marker and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developer listed as Bayer Crop Science (Hyderabad) in several sources -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391 ; https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Developer listed as Bayer Bio Science Pvt. Ltd, Hyderabad - 81 in a 2021 list -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/
- Named lead breeder or scientist: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Company-level only: "Bayer Bio Science Pvt. Ltd, Hyderabad – 81" (postal address reduced to city and postal code in the source). No email, phone, or institute contact page found for this variety -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/
- Official Indian Bayer contact page for this variety: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Book chapter (authors not captured in the search result). "Current Scenario of Breeding Approaches in Rice" -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391 (lists Arize Tej (HRI 169) as a 2015 hybrid developed by Bayer Crop Science, Hyderabad).
- Review table listing the hybrid among notified hybrids (authors not captured): "Hybrid Seed Production Technology in India" -- https://krishisanskriti.org/vol_image/25May2019010550301%20%20%20%20Arpita%20Shrivastava%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20137-145.pdf (title and author are uncertain; the author name is taken from the URL only).
- Peer-reviewed research papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, theses (KrishiKosh): No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Hariyali (Raigarh, Chhattisgarh) lists Arize Tej among its Bayer Arize products on IndiaMART -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/bayer-arize-rice-seeds-9341058533.html
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or Seednet listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- 2012 notification (S.O. 2125(E), 10.09.2012): Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm ; https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- 2015 notification (S.O. 269(E), 28.01.2015) adds Jharkhand, listing Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Jharkhand -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm ; https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Release year is therefore conflicting: 2012 (initial notification) vs 2015 (Jharkhand notification). The input field "Year of release: Unknown" can be filled as 2012 for the initial release, with 2015 for the later notification.

Note: The fifth search attempt hit the tool-call limit, so the four completed searches are the full evidence base for this digest.

drought.details: No drought data found for BPT 2295 in the searched sources.

heat.details: No heat data found for BPT 2295 in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No salinity data found for BPT 2295 in the searched sources. The CSC brief lists a salinity score of 3 and 81.52% spikelet fertility at PH 8.5 and EC 15 (germplasm screening, kharif 2013, ARS Machilipatnam), but this is not corroborated by the evidence digest, so no level is assigned.

flood.details: No flood data found for BPT 2295 in the searched sources. The CSC brief claims tolerance to flash flooding for about 7-10 days (kharif 2013 and 2014, Meelam cyclone and Nallamada drain overflow at ARS Bapatla), but this is not corroborated by the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: tolerance claimed for BPT 2295 (2018) in ARS Bapatla front-line demonstrations, with higher yield claimed; no quantitative disease scoring reported in the digest. The digest states this blast and BPH tolerance claim is the only disease or pest resistance evidence for BPT 2295. The CSC brief also lists tolerance to bacterial leaf blight and resistance to RTV, but the digest contains no evidence for these, so they are not reported as findings.

pest_resistance.summary: BPH: tolerance claimed in ARS Bapatla front-line demonstrations (2018), with higher yield claimed; no quantitative scoring in the digest. Angoumois grain moth (Sitotroga cerealella): BPT 2295 was one of 11 rice varieties sourced from ARS Bapatla and tested for field incidence and susceptibility in stored rice, but the digest reports no result specific to BPT 2295, so no resistance is claimed for this pest.

agronomic_details.yield: FLD (2018, four trials, Guntur, Andhra Pradesh): average 7.06 t/ha for BPT 2295 vs 6.56 t/ha for check BPT 5204; the digest also cites 7.62 t/ha as the advantage figure, and the state average is 5.16 t/ha. The CSC brief gives 3.5-7.0 t/ha, which the digest does not confirm.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The digest reports one set of FLDs in Guntur and nitrogen trials at ARS Bapatla only.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The digest states BPT 2295 was released for single-cropped areas of Andhra Pradesh. No further agro-climatic details were found in the digest.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not found in searched sources. The CSC brief lists 120 To 125Days, but this is not corroborated by the digest, and the digest discarded maturity figures from BPT 5204.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources in the digest. CSC brief (not corroborated by the digest): Semi-dwarf, compact tillering narrow erect green foliage extra long duration (165 days) with good grain quality and brown glumed medium slender grains, with stands submergence upto 7-10 days, long dense panicle with more number of grains and no shattering of grains under normal conditions. Non-lodging, semi-dwarf, medium green foliage, compact plant stature, moderate tillering habit, fertilizer responsive, medium slender with dirty glume colour. Note: the brief's 165-day duration conflicts with its own 120 To 125Days maturity value.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Four front-line demonstrations (FLDs) of BPT 2295 in Guntur, Andhra Pradesh, 2018: average yield 7.06 t/ha vs 6.56 t/ha for check BPT 5204; advantage figure 7.62 t/ha as stated in the digest; state average 5.16 t/ha; blast and BPH tolerance claimed with higher yield claimed. (2) Nitrogen-dose trial on BPT 2295-Bapatla Mahsuri, kharif 2013 and 2014-15, ARS Bapatla; no yield figures given in the digest. (3) Yield and growth response to seven nitrogen doses, kharif 2013 and 2014-15, ARS Bapatla, cited under the BPT 2295 name; the digest gives no numeric results. The researchgate URL for this trial carries the slug 'BPT_2231-Akshaya', which does not match BPT 2295, so the attribution rests on the digest and should be checked against the source. The digest also reports that a 2015 paper with Krishna Veni as co-author covers the same nitrogen trial.

submergence.details: No submergence data found for BPT 2295 in the searched sources. The Notable Achievements sheet names the variety but its text is cut off before any stress data.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: tolerance claimed for BPT 2295 (2018) in ARS Bapatla front-line demonstrations, with higher yield claimed; no quantitative disease scoring reported in the digest. The digest states this blast and BPH tolerance claim is the only disease or pest resistance evidence for BPT 2295. The CSC brief also lists tolerance to bacterial leaf blight and resistance to RTV, but the digest contains no evidence for these, so they are not reported as findings.

pest_resistance.summary: BPH: tolerance claimed in ARS Bapatla front-line demonstrations (2018), with higher yield claimed; no quantitative scoring in the digest. Angoumois grain moth (Sitotroga cerealella): BPT 2295 was one of 11 rice varieties sourced from ARS Bapatla and tested for field incidence and susceptibility in stored rice, but the digest reports no result specific to BPT 2295, so no resistance is claimed for this pest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bastar Dhan-1 (variety_name) / Bastar Dhan- 1 (IET 26624) (seednet_variety_name), Rice (PADDY (DHAN))

Search coverage: four web_search queries were run: (1) variety, release, maturity, yield and stress; (2) breeder and institution; (3) research papers and parentage; (4) seed availability. No search returned a Seednet portal page, so I could not check the Seednet name directly. Queries used both "Bastar Dhan-1" and "IET 26624". Most results named other varieties or other places and were discarded under the strict relevance rule.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searches returned no variety-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Bastar Dhan-1 or IET 26624. Results on tolerance concerned other varieties (e.g., CR Dhan 801) and were discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No blast, bacterial blight, brown spot, stem borer or gall midge reaction was reported for Bastar Dhan-1 or IET 26624.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: IGKV advised farmers in Chhattisgarh's Bastar region, after a delayed monsoon, to consider short- and medium-duration paddy varieties of 125–130 days, and Bastar Dhan-1 is named in that list alongside other varieties -- https://newsriveting.com/adopt-lehi-method-amid-heavy-rainfall-chhattisgarh-agri-scientists-urge-paddy-farmers/ (news report; this is an advisory, not a trial result or a release notification)
No multi-location trial, yield, or maturity data from an official source was found for Bastar Dhan-1.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. The parentage "Rastic BR 240/Chander" and the code IET 26624 did not appear in any result. Pages on Bastar landraces and InDel diversity studies do not name this variety and were excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The variety's institution is recorded as Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur, Chhattisgarh. No result named a breeder or lead scientist for Bastar Dhan-1. Only institution-level information was found: the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding at IGKV Raipur, which maintains rice germplasm -- https://igkv.ac.in/__files/JAI/1/Journal_pub_1__uctfbwn0aq54uzg3dmwcx50h_202204051610516PM046.pdf (department affiliation shown in a journal article; not a variety-specific source)

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder contact was found. Institute-level postal address only, taken from a journal affiliation line: Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Raipur-492012, Chhattisgarh, India -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0005260 (institute address, not a variety-specific contact). No official email, phone or IGKV contact page URL was found in the search results.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, thesis, AICRP report or conference item naming Bastar Dhan-1 or IET 26624 was returned. Papers on IGKV rice breeding and Bastar landraces were excluded because they do not name this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. No NSC, Chhattisgarh state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing named Bastar Dhan-1. The seed-dealer and mandi-price results named only generic paddy.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Chhattisgarh -- supported only by the input record and by the IGKV advisory above, which places Bastar Dhan-1 in a Chhattisgarh/Bastar context -- https://newsriveting.com/adopt-lehi-method-amid-heavy-rainfall-chhattisgarh-agri-scientists-urge-paddy-farmers/ . No official release notification or CSC minute was found.

Gaps to fill: check the Seednet portal entry for "Bastar Dhan- 1 (IET 26624)" directly, the CSC/CVRC release notification for 2020, the IGKV varietal release list, and KrishiKosh for theses on Bastar Dhan-1.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bheema/Dheera (MTU 1140; IET 23933), rice

Name note: The CSC-style name "Bheema/Dheera" and the Seednet name "BHEEMA/DHEERA (MTU 1140)" both appear in the notification and registration sources below, so I treated them as one variety. No Seednet portal page appeared in any of the four searches, so Seednet-specific fields (including the parentage "MTU 5249 / PLA 8572") are unverified.

Search coverage: four web_search calls were run (variety, breeder/institute, research papers, contacts/seed). Seed-availability results were weak, so that heading is marked accordingly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as flood tolerant, non-lodging, high yielding, 145 days, with 2 weeks dormancy and 2 weeks anaerobic germination, in the minikit-testing list of a 2015 IIRR newsletter -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Described as suitable for semi-deep water, with submergence tolerance and a 152-day maturity (the entry is for "Bheema (Dheera) (MTU 1140) (IET 23933)") -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- Named as flood and submergence tolerant, and as a known anaerobic germination tolerant genotype, in a PCA study of 107 rice genotypes; that study cites Girijarani et al. (2014) for the anaerobic germination tolerance -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339207840_Principal_component_analysis_for_anaerobic_germination_traits_in_rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Same genotype (number 17, MTU 1140) reported as flood and submergence tolerant in a 2020 IJPAB/IJCS paper -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2020/vol8issue1/PartAC/8-1-242-344.pdf
- Rated "moderately tolerant" to salinity at the germination stage in a salinity screen of restorer lines (the paper title covers restorer lines; the MTU 1140 rating is from that screen) -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue1/PartG/10-1-60-239.pdf
- Drought, heat and water-stress tolerance: No evidence found for this variety in the search results.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to brown plant hopper and moderately resistant to brown spot (rice-garud listing) -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- Described as tolerant to BPH in the 2015 IIRR minikit list -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Blast and bacterial blight reaction: No evidence found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Eight new crop varieties including Bheema (MTU 1140) were recorded for the 2016-17 ANGRAU release year -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/Annual%20Report%20%20-%202%200%201%206%20-%201%207_compressed%20(1).pdf
- Yield: rice-garud listing gives "yield 60.0 kg/ha" (this is almost certainly a unit or transcription error; a plausible value is 60 q/ha, but this is unverified) -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- Minikit (on-farm multiplication) testing noted in the 2015 IIRR newsletter -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Adoption: a 2022 ANGRAU-contributed review says the variety is popularly grown for submergence tolerance in West Bengal on more than 40,000 ha (area figure is from that review, not a dated survey) -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- Multi-location trial results, yield tables by location: No evidence found.
- Duration conflict: 145 days (IIRR 2015 minikit entry) versus 152 days (rice-garud listing).

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Breeding-line code: MTU 1140; variety code IET 23933 -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- Parentage "MTU 5249 / PLA 8572" (Vajram / PLA8572): No evidence found in the search results. The Vajram name appears only in an ANGRAU review that credits MTU 5249 with BPH tolerance (1986), not as this variety's parent -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- Breeding method and QTL/marker work specific to MTU 1140: No evidence found.
- Genome resources (genotype, SSR profile): No evidence found for this variety.

seednet_fields.Parentage: The proposed variety has been developed from a cross between Gobindabhog x Shatabdi (IET 4786)
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Irrigated medium land; This variety is rfeocmmedned for both Boro, both Kharif. Suitable for both for P-deficient and sufficient soil.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: •	Suitable for the replacement of satabdi (IET 4786) •	Non-lodging and non-shattering plant type. •	Responsive to fertilizer dose of N:P2O5:K2O – 100:40:40 kg/ha for kharif and 120:60:60 kg/ha. •	Also suitable for the areas with low phosphate availability like Bankura, Purulia, Birbhum etc. •	Seed rate: 40-45 kg
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: Broad leaf (1.5-1.6 cm), long slender grain.	Narrow leaf (0.70-0.80 cm), small arotomic grain.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Dwarf (less than 90 cm), broad leaf, stiff culm, does not lodge at maturity, long slender grain.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Suitable for P-deficient soil.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Moderately resistant to bacterial leaf blight and leaf blast diseases in WB condition.	Moderately resistant to leaf blight and susceptible to Blast in WB condition.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Moderately field resistance against YSB and BPH.	Moderately field resistant against YSB and susceptible against BPH.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): N:P2O5:K2O :: 100:40:40 (kg/ha) (kharif) N:P2O5:K2O :: 120:60:60 (kg/ha) (Rabi) Basal: ¼ N + Full P2O5 + K2O 1st Topdressing: ½ N at 15-20 DAT 2nd Topdressing: ¼ M + ¼ K2O at panicle initiation stage.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CG Barani Dhan-2 (Rice)

Name checks: variety_name "CG Barani Dhan-2" and seednet_variety_name "CG Barani Dhan-2 (R-RF-105, IET No. 24690)". I ran four searches, and none returned a page that names this variety under either name. Every heading below therefore reports no evidence for either name.

Limitation: the search tool hit its usage limit during my follow-up check, so I could not open the full text of the pages returned. I reviewed only the first 300 characters of each result. A page that mentions this variety deeper in its text could have been missed. Re-running the searches against the Seednet portal, the ICAR/IGKV pages, and KrishiKosh is recommended.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The "variety" search returned a PIB Year-End Review 2021 (Department of Biotechnology) mentioning an unnamed drought-tolerant rice line -- https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1786619&reg=48&lang=2. It does not name CG Barani Dhan-2, so I have not attributed it.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. The parentage given in the brief (IR 84887-B-153-CRA-25-1 / IR74371-51-1-1 / IR 78877-208-B-1-1) was not found in any search result. It is supplied only from the input record and is unverified.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The "breeder" search returned an OSTI/ETDEWEB record for "CR Boro Dhan-2", a different mutant variety, which I have discarded -- https://www.osti.gov/etdeweb/biblio/22131842.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV) contact page, email, phone or address appeared in the results.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The "research" search returned only the same discarded CR Boro Dhan-2 record.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The seed search returned an ICAR Annual Report 2024-25 that mentions drought-resistant rice varieties in general terms, without naming this one -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf. Not attributed.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. The release record gives Chhattisgarh, but no search result confirmed it.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: CR 1009 Sub 1 (Rice)

Names searched: "CR 1009 Sub 1" (variety_name, CSC minutes) and "CR-1009 Sub-1" (seednet_variety_name). The search results used the spaced form "CR 1009 Sub 1" or "CR1009 Sub 1", and no Seednet portal record came back, so all evidence below refers to the CSC-style name.

Search limit note: the search budget ran out during a second batch of calls. I have only the snippets from the first four searches, not the full page texts. Breeder names, institute contact details and seed-dealer information therefore remain unconfirmed. The follow-up items are listed at the end.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Submergence/flood tolerance is the main trait reported for this variety, described as a submergence-tolerant version of CR1009 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601080_Rice_CR1009_Sub_1IET_22187-A_new_flood_tolerant_rice_variety
- Flood tolerance is also named in the paper's keywords and title -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/f5bd/d012d01797414546d665902494f47d602ce9.pdf
- Drought, heat and salinity tolerance: No evidence found in the retrieved snippets.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found in the retrieved snippets for disease or pest resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration of about 155 days, high-yielding semi-dwarf type -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/f5bd/d012d01797414546d665902494f47d602ce9.pdf
- The paper reports no yield penalty for CR 1009 Sub 1 in the snippet, but the comparator and trial data were not captured -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/f5bd/d012d01797414546d665902494f47d602ce9.pdf
- Listed on the TNAU rice technologies page with release year 2015, duration 155 days and submergence tolerance -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/cpbg/rice-technologies-developed/
- Multi-location trial data: No evidence found in the retrieved snippets.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Keywords include MAS (marker-assisted selection) and QTL, indicating a marker-assisted backcross-type development -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/f5bd/d012d01797414546d665902494f47d602ce9.pdf
- Breeding-line code IET 22187 appears in the paper title -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601080_Rice_CR1009_Sub_1IET_22187-A_new_flood_tolerant_rice_variety
- Parentage: the user record says "Unknown". The TNAU table row for CR 1009 Sub1 shows "CR1009 / FR 13 A" in an unlabelled column, and its meaning is not confirmed -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/cpbg/rice-technologies-developed/
- The Sub1 gene donor and the exact introgression method were not confirmed. Genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Released by Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), with the source attributed to the Department of Rice -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601080_Rice_CR1009_Sub_1IET_22187-A_new_flood_tolerant_rice_variety
- TNAU Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics page listing the variety -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/cpbg/rice-technologies-developed/
- Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found in the retrieved snippets.
- Coimbatore station detail: Not confirmed beyond the institution name given in the record.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.
- Institute-level contact: No evidence found in the retrieved snippets. The TNAU page above is the only institutional source; its contact details were not captured.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured (2019). Rice CR1009 Sub 1(IET 22187) - A new flood tolerant rice variety. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding, 10(3): 995-1004 -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/f5bd/d012d01797414546d665902494f47d602ce9.pdf

- AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses and conference papers: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY

RECOMMENDED STATES

official_quote.quote: RESISTANT/MODERATELY RESISTANT TO BLAST AND BLB

disease_resistance.research_summary: Blast: resistant or moderately resistant (CRRI 2010-11 annual report; released-varieties list codes the variety as MR for blast-related entries). Bacterial leaf blight (BLB): resistant (CRRI 2010-11 annual report; CRRI released list). Sheath blight: tolerant (CRRI 2010-11 annual report; released-varieties list code ShBl). Ground-truth data also records resistant/moderately resistant to blast and BLB and tolerant to sheath blight.

official_quote.quote: TOLERANT TO SB, AND BPH

pest_resistance.research_summary: Yellow stem borer: tolerant (CRRI 2010-11 annual report; CRRI released list entry for stem borer). Brown planthopper (BPH): tolerant per ground-truth data and the released-varieties code string (MR-SB, BPH, BL, BLB, ShBl); no further BPH evidence was found in the digest. No evidence found for gall midge, tungro or other pests beyond these codes.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE (evidence refers to "CR Dhan 408 (Chaka Akhi)", the spelling used by the CRRI/NRRI pages; the notified-list entry uses "CR Dhan 408 (Chakaakhi)")
- Tolerates about one week of complete submergence, per the ICAR shallow-lowland bulletin -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf
- A news report says it can grow with less water and survive flood conditions for up to a week, and can withstand high winds; the article attributes this to CRRI scientists -- https://sambadenglish.com/crri-develops-new-varieties-drought-resistant-paddy-odisha/
- Strongly photosensitive, flowering in the first week of the period given in the bulletin (text truncated), and 165 days to flowering in the CRRI table -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf ; https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- No drought-specific trial data for this variety was retrieved; the drought claim in the news article is general, not supported by a trial report.

DISEASE AND PEST (evidence refers to "CR Dhan 408 (Chaka Akhi)")
- Moderately resistant to leaf blast, neck blast, bacterial blight and sheath rot; moderately resistant to stem borer, leaf folder, whitebacked planthopper and whorl maggot -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf
- Released-variety table lists reactions as MR to leaf blast, neck blast, BLB, sheath rot, stem borer, leaf folder and WBPH (no resistance rating scale given) -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- The NRRI varieties analysis includes a CR Dhan 408 row in an infestation/percentage table for pest and disease reactions, but the values did not parse reliably from the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339527323_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI_Yield_Quality_Special_Traits_and_Tolerance_to_Biotic_and_Abiotic_Stresses

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (evidence refers to "CR Dhan 408 (Chaka Akhi)")
- Average yield 4.8 t/ha in Odisha; plant height 130-140 cm; 250-300 panicles per m2; moderate tillering (7-10); test weight 25.6 g -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf
- Duration 160-165 days; long bold grain -- https://sambadenglish.com/crri-develops-new-varieties-drought-resistant-paddy-odisha/ ; https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf
- Quality: head rice about 60%, milling about 68%, intermediate amylose (23.03%), suited to wet rice preparation -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf
- Field trial, multi-location or AICRP results specific to this variety: No evidence found (the research search returned no trial reports).

GENETICS AND QTL (evidence refers to "CR Dhan 408 (Chakaakhi)" and "IET 20265 / CR491-1590-330-2-1")
- Notified-list entry: CR Dhan 408 (Chakaakhi) (IET 20265) (CR491-1590-330-2-1), 2018, S.O. 399(E) dated 24.01.2018, Odisha -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/national-news/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- Parentage CR149-5010-228/T1242 and pedigree line CR491-1590-330-2-1 appear in the NRRI varieties table (the table is partly garbled; the row is identified by the name in the same row) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339527323_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI_Yield_Quality_Special_Traits_and_Tolerance_to_Biotic_and_Abiotic_Stresses
- Also listed under the synonym "Chakaakhhi/AC38687" in the same table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339527323_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI_Yield_Quality_Special_Traits_and_Tolerance_to_Biotic_and_Abiotic_Stresses
- Breeding method, marker/QTL studies and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (evidence refers to "CR Dhan 408 (Chaka Akhi)" and to the institute)
- Breeder or lead scientist names: No evidence found. The "Pradhan" in the news article is quoted as informing the press, not identified as the breeder, so it is not attributed here -- https://sambadenglish.com/crri-develops-new-varieties-drought-resistant-paddy-odisha/
- Developing institution: ICAR-Central Rice Research Institute (CRRI), Cuttack, and the variety appears in CRRI's 1968-2025 list -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- The shallow-lowland bulletin is published by ICAR-National Rice Research Institute, Cuttack, the same Cuttack institute under its later name -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf
- The same release is also tabulated by ICAR-NRRI in its released-varieties page -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/

CONTACT DETAILS (no breeder contact found; institute-level only)
- Institute website: https://crri.icar.gov.in/ (institute home; the research page retrieved is https://crri.icar.gov.in/res_sal_tech.php) -- no email, phone or postal address appeared in the retrieved snippets.
- Institute postal code shown on the bulletin: Cuttack-753006, Odisha -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf
- Address in the user's record ("Director, CRRI, ICAR, Cuttack-6, Orissa") was not verified by any search result.
- Official email and phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown (year not shown). ICAR-NRRI Bulletin No. 34: High yielding rice varieties for rainfed shallow lowland (publisher: ICAR-National Rice Research Institute, Cuttack, pp. 28). Bulletin -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Rice Varieties of NRRI: Yield, Quality, Special Traits and Tolerance to Biotic and Abiotic Stresses. Journal/report not shown in snippet (ResearchGate) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339527323_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI_Yield_Quality_Special_Traits_and_Tolerance_to_Biotic_and_Abiotic_Stresses
- Peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR annual reports, KrishiKosh theses, conference papers specific to this variety: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY (this variety)
- No evidence found for NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer stock of CR Dhan 408. The search returned general Odisha seed-distribution reports and IRRI decentralised seed-production news items that do not name this variety -- https://pc.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2020-03/7.Seed_Distribution_System.pdf ; https://www.irri.org/news-and-events/news/enhancing-decentralized-seed-production-healthier-rice-odisha
- Seednet portal entry for this variety was not retrieved; the 2011-2021 notified-list search was the only seednet-type record found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Released for Odisha, for shallow lowlands -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf ; https://www.krishakjagat.org/national-news/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- Released-variety table records the release year as 2014, while the notified list gives 2018 (S.O. 399(E), 24.01.2018). The CRRI 1968-2025 list gives 2018 -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ ; https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf

Note on names: the CSC release minutes name used here is "CR Dhan 408 (Chakaakhi)" and the Seednet name is "CR Dhan 408 (Chakaakhi) (IET 20265) (CR491-1590-330-2-1)". The notified-list entry carries both codes, so it matches both names. The variety code "IET 2026s" is confirmed as IET 20265 by that list.

drought.details: No evidence found in the digest for drought tolerance specific to this variety. The variety is described as non-lodging and responsive to good management. Earlier aromatic pure-line varieties had a lodging problem after maturity, which the breeding programme aimed to correct. Recommended for irrigated conditions only.

disease_resistance.summary: Leaf blast: moderately resistant (released-varieties table row for CR Dhan 907; popular-varieties entry, provisional; CSC original data). Neck blast: moderately resistant (released-varieties table; CSC original data). Brown spot: moderately resistant (released-varieties table; CSC original data). Sheath rot: moderately resistant (popular-varieties entry, provisional; CSC original data). Sheath blight: not found for this variety in the digest. Gall midge and neck blast resistance in the RB-34 table are not attributed to this variety in the digest and are excluded. The popular-varieties entry is on the same page as this variety's description but adjacent entries are for other varieties, so it is treated as provisional.

pest_resistance.summary: Stem borer: reported as resistant under natural conditions (CSC original data); moderately resistant in the released-varieties table row for CR Dhan 907 and in the popular-varieties entry (provisional). The two sources conflict on the resistance grade. Leaf folder: moderately resistant (released-varieties table; popular-varieties entry, provisional). Whorl maggot and rice thrips: listed as moderately resistant in the popular-varieties entry only (provisional). Gall midge: not attributed to this variety in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield reported as 4.0-5.0 t/ha (popular-varieties entry), 4.0-4.5 t/ha (released-varieties table), and 4.5 t/ha (CRRI release table, 1968-2024). Yield ranges differ across sources.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data were reported beyond AICRIP promotion to a fourth year of multi-location testing.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated late ecology. Original variety data recommends release and cultivation in Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat and Odisha under irrigated conditions. This state list comes from the original variety data, not from the evidence digest.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Photosensitive, semi-dwarf, erect, non-lodging, good tillering, non-shattering, easy threshability. Plant type described as semi-dwarf and high yielding. Grain: short-grain aromatic (non-Basmati), elongation ratio 1.85, medium scent, alkali spreading value 4.5, hard gel consistency, intermediate amylose (24.3%). Reported as the first semi-dwarf, short-grain aromatic (non-Basmati) variety. Digest duration is about 150 days, which conflicts with the 122-day maturity in the original variety data. Seed-production advice: grain from the wet season for consumption; dry-season crop for seed only; seed treatment before dry sowing.
agronomic_details.field_trials: AICRIP multi-location testing: CR 2616 (IET 21044) was promoted to the fourth year of testing on overall performance and quality (2010-11 report). Reported average yields: 4.0-5.0 t/ha, 4.0-4.5 t/ha and 4.5 t/ha across the three cited release tables. No trial-level data (sites, seasons, replicate yields, checks) were found in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CR Sugandh Dhan 907

Names used: "variety_name" = CR Sugandh Dhan 907 (CR 2616-3-3-31 in NRRI lists; IET 21044 (CR 2616-3-3-3-1) in notification lists). "seednet_variety_name" = CR Sugandh Dhan 907 (IET 21044) (CR 2616-3-3-3-1). Some pages write "CR Dhan 907 (Aromatic)" for the same line (same pedigree). The evidence below refers to this variety under both names. I searched by name and did not query seednet.gov.in directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. The variety is described as non-lodging and responsive to good management -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf
- Earlier aromatic pure-line varieties had a lodging problem after maturity, which the breeding programme aimed to fix -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Listed as moderately resistant to leaf blast, sheath rot, stem borer (dead heart and white ear), leaf folder, whorl maggot and rice thrips -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/ (the entry is on the same page as this variety's description, but the adjacent entries are for other varieties, so treat this as provisional)
- Released-varieties table: resistant to neck blast and gall midge, moderately resistant to sheath rot and stem borer -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf
- Released-varieties table: moderately resistant to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot, stem borer and leaf folder -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ (row for CR Dhan 907)
- AICRIP-era table: moderately resistant to leaf blast, neck blast, sheath blight and stem borer in Eastern India (listed as MR-LBl, NBl, BS, ShR) -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2013-14.pdf
- Full CRRI release table: MR to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot, stem borer and leaf folder, with ShR and SB noted -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf (row 98 of the 1968-2019 table)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration about 150 days, late-maturing, irrigated late ecology; reported as first semi-dwarf, short-grain aromatic (non-Basmati) variety -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/ and https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- Yield: average 4.0-5.0 t/ha -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/ ; 4.0-4.5 t/ha -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ ; 4.5 t/ha -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- Plant type: semi-dwarf, high yielding, short grain aromatic (bulletin) -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf
- Grain quality: elongation ratio 1.85, medium scent, alkali spreading value 4.5, hard gel consistency, intermediate amylose (24.3%); grain quality similar to the Dubraj landrace -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf
- Seed-production advice: grain from the wet season for consumption; dry-season crop for seed only; seed treatment before dry sowing -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf
- AICRIP testing: CR 2616 (IET 21044) was promoted to the fourth year of multi-location testing on overall performance and quality -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/2010-11.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: Pusa 44 / Dubraj -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf ; https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/78726
- Breeding method: pedigree selection with marker-assisted support -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf
- Breeding-line codes: IET 21044; CR 2616-3-3-3-1 (also CR 2616-3-3-31) -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf ; https://www.krishakjagat.org/national-news/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- Used as an aromatic donor in crosses at the institute (2013-14 annual report) -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/2013-14.pdf
- No QTL, marker-set or genome-resource evidence found for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Central Rice Research Institute (CRRI), Cuttack, Odisha. Some pages use the NRRI name for the same Cuttack institute -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf ; https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf
- Crop Improvement Division, CRRI, Cuttack, is the division cited for CRRI breeding work -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/275947902_CR_Dhan_407_a_high-yielding_rice_cultivar_released_for_the_rainfed_shallow_lowland_ecosystem_of_eastern_India (for a sister variety; included for division context only)
- Lead breeder: No evidence found. A ResearchGate profile for Pritesh Sundar Roy lists a 2014 article on this variety's development, but the snippet does not confirm his authorship -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Pritesh-Roy
- Institute scale: CRRI has contributed 186 varieties, and its aromatic programme launched in 2006 -- https://icar-crri.in/major-achievements/ and https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute postal address (from the 2010-11 report): Central Rice Research Institute, Indian Council of Agricultural Research, Cuttack (Orissa) 753 006, India -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/2010-11.pdf
- Institute website domain: icar-crri.in (no contact page URL, email or phone found in results) -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Roy, P. S. et al. (2014). Development of CR Sugandh Dhan 907, the first high yielding, semi-dwarf, short-grain aromatic rice in India. Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding (authors not confirmed in the snippet; no DOI found) -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Pritesh-Roy
- Patnaik et al. (2015). Cited in the NRRI bulletin for the marker-assisted pedigree development of this variety. Full title and journal not found -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf
- NRRI Research Bulletin 39: aromatic rice varieties of ICAR-NRRI (year not stated; file dated 2023). Authors not stated -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf
- CRRI Annual Report 2013-14 (crosses using CR Sugandh Dhan 907 as donor). Authors not stated -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2018

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: Rice Research Station, Chinsurah, Hooghly, West Bengal in collaboration with international Rice Research institute, Philippines"
seednet_fields.Parentage:
The proposed variety has been developed from a cross between 1R4630-22-2-5-1-3 and Nona Bokra at lRRl, Philippines.
1.	One of the parents 1R4630-22-2-S-1-3 is a saline as well as submergence resistant line with low yield.
2.	Nona Bokra a well adopted cultivars at coastal saline belt of West Bengal with 113 days to 50% flowering; 163 cm plant height and having the yield range of 3000 to 3600 kg/ha up to 5 dS/m soit EC.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Coastal saline tract of West Bengal up to Soil EC 6 ds/m. Rainfed Shallow Lowland situation (Water depth 30-50 cm) of the coastal saline tract of  West Bengal.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features:
1.	Resistant to lodging and shattering.
2.	Responsive to fertilizer, best effective as 100% RDN as basal for semi deep water situation in this coastal saline belt.
3.	1st week of July is the best time for sowing for
enhancing productivity.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Erect plant type, Erect flag leaf, Medium bold grain straw colour, Awn less panicle and white karnel. Panicle exertion complete, basal leaf sheath colour green.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: The variety is screened in vitro condition through laboratory based technique against salinity at seedling stage in scored 1(resistant) for EC 4 and 3 moderate resistant) for EC and growth and tillering  nearly normal like resistant check AT401 at EC B ds/m.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Showed resistant reactions against Bacterial leaf blight under moderate disease pressure (LSl 4.5) in State Screening Nursery at RRS, Chinsurah. ln normal field condition at Gosaba and Canning no significant diseases were observed by last three years. DRR screening Nursery for Diseases.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: The variety is found to be tolerant for Yellow Stem borer in State Screening Nursery at RRS, Chinsurah. No significant pest was observed under field condition for last three years both in Kharif and boro at Gosaba and Canning
seednet_fields.Average Yield (Kg/Ha): Around 5.0 t/ha up to Soil EC 6 ds/m). Kg/Ha
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Recommended dose of N 70 kg/ha; 35 kg P2O5 and 35 kg K2O / ha.
